### v0.182 changelog (v0.181 → v0.182)

v0.182 is the **types, expressions & serialization revision** — the fourth ruled train of the 2026-07-07 whole-language design review. Where v0.179 settled borrows against *suspension*, v0.180 against *consumption*, and v0.181 the declaration machinery, v0.182 settles the expression-level semantics around them: what narrows and un-narrows a nullable, what may be thrown and caught, which conversions exist, what auto-equality and serialization synthesis actually require, and what the conformance relation enumerates. Every rule below was selected between recorded live alternatives, with the road not taken noted.

- **Narrowing made honest (§7.4, rationale §6.1).** The establishment forms are enumerated normatively (null tests in conditions and guards; boolean composition through `and`/`or`/`not` with three-outcome fact flow; early exits; `is`/pattern tests; assignment from non-nullable or narrowed values — codifying what the compiler already implements beyond the old three-item list), and invalidation closes two holes: **`out`-argument passing** invalidates like `ref` (spec catch-up to #1188), and a **mutably-captured local** — assigned or passed `ref`/`out` inside any lambda of the body — loses its narrowing at any call, function-value invocation, or `await` inside the controlled block (probe-confirmed compile-clean null-deref segfault; the rule is deliberately syntactic, any-lambda-counts, no escape analysis — the v0.75 only-what-implementations-can-check principle). Rationale §6.1's "a local has none of these writers" is qualified to *uncaptured* locals. *Declined:* treating mutably-captured locals like fields (never narrow) — a captured local's writers are visible, so the checker can be precise for the price of one paragraph, and straight-line check-then-use survives. The compiler's missing closure invalidation is filed as the companion soundness issue.
- **Cleanup ordering is one rule (§29.7, §28.10).** §29.7's two bullets — readable, and on two edges literally implemented, as "dispose all `using var`s, then run `finally` clauses" — are replaced by *reverse order of establishment, exactly as if the body had exited at the suspension point*; §28.10 now states the rule once for **every** exit edge. Framed as clarifying an underspecified ordering, not resolving a contradiction — §28.3/§29.6/§29.8 already derived the right order for a careful reader; the load-bearing defect is the **compiler's** return-edge and iterator-dispose-edge inversion (use-after-dispose when a `finally` touches a later-established `using var` resource), filed with priority. This is the §28.3-adjacent ordering clarification the v0.175 changelog left as a revisit note.
- **The throw operand is codified — any class, owned (§31.1, §17.12, §31.5, §31.2.3, C.5).** The rule the owner recorded closing #771 and the compiler enforces is now written: `throw expr` consumes an **owned instance of any class type** — not restricted to `Exception`-derived; primitives, `string`, records, enums, inline arrays, unit, and function values cannot be thrown, nor can `Object`-/interface-typed operands (their referent may be a boxed value) or *borrowed* class references (throw consumes ownership; re-raise with bare `throw`, or chain a snapshot). §31.2.3's "captures any exception" catch-all overpromise is scoped honestly: a bare `Exception` arm captures `Exception`-derived throwables; there is no universal catch-all pattern (the §31.3-area suppress-all sentence and the example's `// catch-all` comment are swept with it). Two compositions land with the rule: **§31.2.1's multi-type binding fallback is repaired** — a mixed list (`Dog | IOException`) has no common base but `Object`, so the old unconditional `Exception` fallback contradicted its own most-specific-common-base definition; the binding form now requires a common base class more specific than `Object` (compile error otherwise; non-binding lists unrestricted; all-`Exception`-derived lists type exactly as before). And **throw joins no consume-site freeze list, reason recorded** (§31.1): `throw x` is an announced kill — the keyword is the announcement, no `owned` marker, the owned-return logic — whose dispose-after-arm sets the disposed flag, giving it exactly the checked-mode backstop whose absence forced v0.180's freeze for silent transfers. *Flagged to the owner, not shipped:* requiring `Exception`-derivation — #771 predates the v0.162 Exception-model completion, whose reporting surface (`CauseChain`, `StackTrace`, unhandled-exception reports) is written in `Exception` vocabulary; until re-ruled, #771 stands.
- **Pattern A awaits route through §28.3's unbound-owned-temporary machinery (§30.5, §30.3, §28.3, C.6).** The admission rule is unified: *the borrow's source is the awaited expression's own location* — a named owning location bounds the borrow by its scope (list unchanged), and an **unbound temporary** bounds it by the full expression, so `Process(await Producer())` is now admitted, the task (and with it the result) disposed at end of full expression after every use, exactly once. `var x := await Producer();` stays rejected — the borrow escapes the expression its source dies with. `Task<T>.Result` moves in lockstep (v0.179's "same rule as `await`" preserved). Governing precedent: rationale §5.23's v0.150 finding that *naming a value changing whether the program compiles* is a refactoring hazard with no safety content. *Declined:* auto-binding the temporary to an anonymous scope-bound slot (would admit the `var`-binding form by silent lifetime extension — the recorded reject-not-extend posture; kept as a liftable, tracked).
- **Auto-equality is storage-only; serialization gets a real construction rule (§9.2, §9.8).** The "non-trivial constructor body" and "side-effecting computed property" disqualifiers are **removed** (with the membership list's "pure function" qualifier): the generated members are defined over auto-property storage only, so no constructor or computed-member behavior can affect them — the clauses protected no invariant while stripping `=` and serialization from exactly the validating-constructor records §9.5 recommends (the internal contradiction, plus §9.8's confused "constructor the auto-equality machinery already relies on" phrase, was the defect — not undecidability: #770's criterion was decidable, and is retired as purposeless, not ill-defined). **Static members are ignored** for eligibility (codifying the compiler; constants and factories no longer disqualify by the letter). The synthesized record `Deserialize` gains its missing construction rule: explicit constructors select by **unique case-insensitive name match** against the serialized components (camelCase parameter ↔ PascalCase component; none/many ⇒ conformance-declaration error naming candidates — validating constructors now *run on wire input*); a constructor-less record constructs at the storage level, the mechanism `with`/`default(T)` already have; the v0.136 class match is clarified as the same case-insensitive comparison. **Records cannot serialize reference-typed components at all** (§9.8): the old clause requiring an `owned` record field demanded what §9.7 categorically forbids, so it admitted nothing — class-, interface-, `Shared<T>`-, and `Weak<T>`-typed serialized components now make a record ineligible in both directions, remedy the sealed-class envelope (proposal 0019's `Envelope` already has this shape); the analogous heap-collection question is recorded open, tracked. **Duplicate enum constant values are specified** (§10.2, §9.8, §19.6): aliases legal, same value = one runtime value, duplicate-valued `case` arms a compile error (unreachable), exhaustiveness by distinct value, serialization writes the first-declared name and reads all.
- **Conformance enumerates all six sources (§14.2, §7.10, C.4).** The "exactly when" list — three clauses that contradicted §10.5, §11.8, and §28.2 — grows to six, preserving existing clause numbering: classes (now including *implicit* `IDisposable`), records (auto-generated members count — `IEquatable<T>`), interfaces, **enums** (§10.5; the probe-confirmed generic-constraint path), **compiler-provided primitive conformances** (§11.8/v0.176 — a distinct clause: primitives are not records), and **type parameters** whose constraints guarantee conformance. `where T: U` gets its missing semantics (subtype assignability after substitution, instantiation-checked, non-null implication, cycle/self-bound rejection), and **overrides/interface implementations inherit constraints** — omission recommended, equivalent restatement legal (same per-parameter set, compared order-insensitively in alias-resolved form, §27.8), a differing clause a compile error (an added constraint would be unenforced at every virtual call; a weakened one advertises admissions dispatch never grants).
- **The conversion catalog closes its gaps (§5.1, §5.2, §5.3, §4.2, §7.7).** *Nullable conversions* stated (value-type wrapping `T → T?`; lifted `S? → T?` wherever `S → T`; one-hop composition). *Explicit-conversion semantics* completed: decimal↔binary-float rounding and failure modes, `float(d)` saturates to `±Infinity` (floating-point narrowing follows §6.3's arithmetic-overflow behavior, as integer narrowing's throw follows §6.1's — a per-family principle, not an asymmetry), `char`→integer as checked code-point narrowing. *Nullable casts* get their general rule (`T?(x)` admitted iff `T(v)` is; null in, null out; §5.2 checks on present values). *Typed-context widening* is corrected to **integer** literal (hex/binary included) and extended to assignment targets and `return` under declared integer types — the declaration already announced the width; accepting the declaration line while rejecting the identical next-line assignment was a naming asymmetry with no safety content. *`??` typing* restated: right operand `T` or `T?`, result nullable iff the right is — the both-nullable fallback chain the old sentence rejected.
- **Primitive-operator edges (§3.5, §7.11, §4.6).** **Ordering on `bool` is removed** (compile error): no ordering was ever defined, the stdlib `Boolean` deliberately declares no `IComparable`, and the compiler's current answer (`true < false` = `True`) matches no candidate semantics — rejection surfaces latent bugs rather than silently flipping them; order-by-flag is `int(b)`. **Ordering on `string?` operands is a compile error** (narrow first — the nullable-use discipline; the compiler currently accepts and segfaults on null). **Unary `+`** is defined (numeric identity; lifts with `-`/`~`). §7.11 gains the **null-reflexivity advisory** (`null = null` true, `null <= null` false — the #486 decision stands, stated so nobody re-derives it the hard way) and the `bool?`/`string?` boundary notes.
- **The Object surface is total and honest (§8.2–§8.5).** `GetType` on a value answers the static type with no observable boxing — defined on move-only inline arrays (borrowed receiver), whose boxing-based reading was undefined. Default `ToString` for inline arrays and unit: the type name (`"[3]int"`, `"()"`). `ReferenceEquals` is defined by **boxing composition** (arguments box first; result is box identity): fresh boxes unequal, boxed `()` interning makes that comparison unspecified, and a null nullable-value argument boxes to the null reference — `true` against `null` — replacing the blanket "always false" that contradicted §8.6. Hash combining for records **must be order-sensitive** (a commutative XOR is non-conforming); the `Pair(1,2)`/`Pair(2,1)` claim is weakened to what is guaranteed.
- **Small rulings, one each:** `Array<T>` **range slicing produces an owned fresh array** (dedicated §28.3 producers row; stdlib §4.4 gains `Slice(r: Range<int>): owned Array<T>` with `arr[r]` as the compiler-recognized equivalent — a method, not an indexer, so §28.6's getters-never-return-owned rule stays exceptionless); **`case`/`when` are primary atoms** — §17.1's level-15 row and A.7's duplicate `ConditionalExpr` listing corrected to the probe-confirmed grammar, with the **true-branch throw parse** noted in §20 (`throw a if c else b` is `throw (a if c else b)`); **`Range<T>`**: open-ended ranges are never `IsEmpty`, computed step 0 constructs, is direction-agreeing for `Contains`/`IsEmpty`, and faults at `GetEnumerator()`; **exhaustiveness**: an unguarded `_`/untyped-`var` arm is the trivially-total proof case (previously omitted), `when`-guarded arms contribute nothing (C.7 bullet), and the enum bullet's "literal pattern" becomes "constant pattern" with `|`-alternatives counting; **`break`/`continue` may not exit a `finally`** (the `return` rule's reasoning verbatim — on the exception edge the jump silently swallows the in-flight exception, probe-confirmed; exits *of the protected block* via `break`/`continue` are legal and now listed among finally-running exits); **§29.12 "modification" is defined** (structural invalidates — add/remove/reposition/reallocate, insert-through-indexer, in-place `Sort`/`Reverse`; element-level writes to existing positions do not, with owning-collection sets still disposing the displaced element per §28.11; §29.2's protocol elision must preserve the fault); **`KeyNotFoundException`** (`: Exception`, stdlib §4.8 — deliberately not under `InvalidOperationException`, so state-fault arms don't swallow lookup faults) and **`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`** (`: ArgumentException`, stdlib §2.5, auto-imported `System`) are finally declared; **generic type parameters are admissible as catch/case pattern types** with substituted-type matching (class-type bound required in catch arms; `where TEx: Exception` idiomatic — the proposal-0022 `Assert.Throws` consumer).

#### Migration

Compile-time, newly **rejected**: ordering operators on `bool` operands (previously miscompiled — `true < false` returned `True`) and on `string?` operands (previously a runtime segfault on null) — convert (`int(b)`) or narrow first; use of a narrowed **mutably-captured** local after a call/invocation/`await` inside the controlled block (previously a compile-clean null-deref) — copy to an uncaptured local; `throw` of a borrowed reference, a non-class value, or an `Object`-/interface-typed operand (aligns the text with #771 enforcement; borrowed/`Object` cases pending compiler alignment); a multi-type catch **binding** whose listed types share no common base class more specific than `Object` (previously typed `Exception` in contradiction with the fallback's own definition; the non-binding form and all-`Exception`-derived lists are unaffected); duplicate-valued enum `case` arms (previously silently unreachable); `break`/`continue` exiting a `finally` (previously swallowed in-flight exceptions); a record declaring `ISerializable`/`IDeserializable` with a class-, interface-, `Shared<T>`-, or `Weak<T>`-typed serialized component (previously specified as an `owned` record field — a form no program could write, so no real program regresses); an `override` or interface implementation declaring a `where` clause differing from the inherited one. Newly **accepted**, no action needed: `Process(await Producer())` and other expression-confined Pattern A awaits/`.Result` reads; validating-constructor and static-member-bearing records regain `=`/`GetHashCode`/`ToString` and serialization synthesis; the both-nullable `a ?? b`; assignment/`return` typed-context widening; unary `+`; duplicate-valued enum constants; `where T: U`; type parameters as catch/case pattern types. Runtime-visible: the return-edge/iterator-edge cleanup-ordering fix affects only programs whose `finally` touched a later-established `using var` resource (previously use-after-dispose, now correct); `ReferenceEquals(nullNullable, null)` is specified `true` (previously unspecified-in-text, `false` in the compiler — a behavior change gated on the compiler fix); enum serialization under aliases and record `Deserialize` constructor selection are pinned to the rules above; everything else codifies intended or implemented behavior — no correct program changes meaning.

### v0.183 changelog (v0.182 → v0.183)

v0.183 is the **small-rulings batch** — many independent, individually small rulings from the 2026-07-07 review's escalation and residue queues. Each was selected between recorded live alternatives; declines and deferrals are recorded where they fall.

- **Extension resolution defined end-to-end (§26.3–§26.5.1, A.4).** Step 1's "matching" is **name-blocking**: any declared instance member of the called name — regardless of arity, applicability, or accessibility — commits resolution to the instance side; a failed committed lookup is a compile error, never an extension fallback (probe-confirmed compiler behavior, ratified: applicability-conditioned fallback would silently re-route calls when signatures or visibility change). Step 2 filters by call-site visibility. Specificity: rule 1 compares **receiver-substituted heads**, rule 2 the **declared heads** (worked example added — `Array<T>` beats `IEnumerable<int>` for an `Array<int>` receiver). §26.4's bare-identifier binding applies at **any nesting depth**; a `T?` argument position is a compile error (bare `T` already unifies with nullable arguments; constrain-to-nullable heads deferred). **Static members in extension blocks are forbidden** (v1 — the compiler accepted them with zero prose backing; module-level methods cover the use). The rule-4 ambiguity remedies are completed (module-level helper) and a first-class disambiguation spelling is deferred with reasons (rationale §18).
- **Lambda rules completed (§27.3, §27.4, A.6).** A block-bodied lambda with no value-carrying `return` is a **procedure lambda**; mixed exits are errors. Target-less return-type inference requires all `return` expressions to share one type — supertype unification declined (hierarchy-edit sensitivity). **#1408 ships:** lambda-parameter record destructuring `(Entry(k, v)) => …` as an irrefutable binding form — exact-type head (head-as-annotation when target-less), naked/discard/nested slots only, no refutable elements, no modifiers; semantics by desugaring to positional-field reads (borrows for class-typed fields, §28.3).
- **Module and alias smalls (§2.2, §27.8, §32.1, A.2).** An import alias may not collide with an **unambiguously imported public bare name** (#1515 — §2.7's order made such an alias dead on arrival; compiler #1489 reduces to this diagnostic). Module-level type aliases are always **module-internal** — no visibility keyword, never import-visible, not exported; exportable aliases deferred to the module-identity family. Public `extern` methods are reachable **only via qualifier** (not import-visible bare names); extern default visibility stated as `internal`.
- **Enums rounded out (§10.4, §10.5, §25.2, §8.5, A.3).** `OperatorDecl` is admitted in enum bodies (#1381 fork (a) — resolving the §25-vs-A.3 self-contradiction in favor of the recorded rationale position). §25.2's co-declaration spelling is fixed (enums declare a plain `GetHashCode(): int`; `override` remains records-only — §10.5 rejects it on enums). New rule: user-declared plain `Equals`/`GetHashCode`/`ToString` on an enum **replace the generated defaults for every consumer** — hash containers, interpolation, boxed virtual dispatch — via compile-time box-vtable wiring (sound because enums are sealed). The enum `ToString` presentation gap is thereby remediable at the type; changing the generated *default* to the constant's name was declined for now (behavior change; needs a raw-value fallback rule; the per-type remedy addresses the recorded complaint).
- **Out-parameter nullability postcondition (§22.4, §7.4, §22.6, A.5; stdlib §1).** A `bool`-returning method may declare `when true`/`when false` on a nullable `out`/`out owned` parameter: a **compiler-checked postcondition** (every stated-constant return path must assign provably non-null) that **narrows the out recipient at call sites** where the result is statically known — the `c!` after a successful Try becomes `c`. Declared-and-checked was chosen over structural inference (no signature silently gains a contract its body wasn't checked against) and over an attribute system (this is the §18 narrow-modifier escape hatch, like `serialized`). The stdlib Try convention carries the clause normatively across the extraction family. This lands the flow-narrowing revision §22.6 and the v0.171 entry deferred.
- **Patterns: `|` alternatives widen (§19.3, A.7).** Range and relational patterns join constants as alternative members (`1..5 | 10`, `< 0 | > 100`) — binding-free pure membership tests, which the recorded constants-only reasoning (types/bindings, exhaustiveness/binding semantics) never targeted; types and bindings stay excluded, and ranges/relationals contribute nothing to static exhaustiveness.
- **`Range<char>` iteration skips the surrogate gap (§16.3).** successor(U+D7FF) = U+E000 (predecessor symmetric); a stride of k is k successor applications, so stepped ranges cross the gap; the documented two-loop workaround is deleted and the `Contains` asymmetry is confined to the gap itself. Reverses v0.78's terminate-at-boundary: both rules yield only valid `char` values (the recorded reason), but terminate silently truncated full-range iteration to ~5% of code points; Rust's `char` stepping is the precedent.
- **Negated membership stays `not (x in c)` (§17.5) — `not in` declined, recorded.** `in` is a plain bool `Contains` call, so negation composes at the cost of one pair of parentheses; `x not in c` would only half-fix the Python-habit hazard; `is not` earns its two tokens as a narrowing type-classifier, which membership is not.
- **Negative constructor magnitudes fault (stdlib §1, §4.4; #1396).** `capacity`/`size`/`length` constructor parameters raise `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when negative (zero remains valid) — the DateTime defined-fault stance over the implementation's silent empty fallback. `Channel<T>(capacity)`'s stricter v0.174 contract (`>= 1`, `ArgumentException`) is unchanged.
- **Doc tags (§34).** `<typeparam>`, `<typeparamref>`, `<paramref>` join the recognized list; unrecognized tags are preserved verbatim — recognition affects rendering only, never compilation.
- **Honesty fixes (§28.3, §28.7).** The two "no carve-outs" disposal claims now name their one recorded exception — move-only inline-array whole-value reassignment (§15.3, #1385) — which v0.180 left textually false while #1385 is open.
- **Future-work records (rationale §18).** Post-condition loops: deferral restated plainly as a decision (payoff vs a reserved word; #745 declined as D-0003 closed the syntax window) instead of the previous about-to-be-decided framing. New entries: multi-consumer channels (the v0.174 "pipeline evidence" condition engaged honestly — evidence acknowledged, deferral now rests solely on §28.13 domain-locality; N-channels round-robin is the sanctioned interim idiom), channel iteration `ReceiveAll(): IOwningAsyncEnumerable<T>`, opt-in `where T: sendable` (engaging §12.5's decline: bounded constraint vocabulary, not pervasive marker traits), exportable type aliases, and extension-call disambiguation syntax.

#### Migration

Compile-time, additive (no existing meaning changes): enum operator declarations, lambda destructuring, range/relational alternatives, the `when true` clause and its narrowing (`!` remains legal where it was), the §34 tags. Compile-time, newly rejected: an import alias colliding with an unambiguously imported bare name (previously legal-but-dead — qualify or rename); `static` members in extension blocks (previously accepted without specification — move to a module-level method or static class); `extension Array<T?>`-style nullable-marked heads (previously an unclear error — now a defined one). Runtime-visible: `Range<char>` iteration now crosses the surrogate gap — code that relied on termination at U+D7FF must bound its range at `'퟿'` explicitly (the two-loop pattern keeps working); negative constructor magnitudes now raise `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (previously empty-container fallback in the reference implementation); an enum's user-declared `ToString`/`GetHashCode`/`Equals` now reach interpolation, hash containers, and boxed dispatch (previously only direct calls — a correctness fix for the §25.2 divergence).

### v0.184 changelog (v0.183 → v0.184)

v0.184 is the **ownership-coherence settlement** — the centerpiece of the 2026-07-11 spec-quality run, answering the owner's named pain point: three surface ways to dispose a local (`using var`; plain `var` + auto-drop; explicit `Dispose()`), with manual dispose-at-end exception-safe unlike in C#. The finding is that the triad is one mechanism with two specializations, already principled and recorded (§5.23) — so the revision consolidates rather than restructures: one normative "Choosing a disposal form" recap (§28.3), repair of the stale pre-affine sentences in §28's own text (five of them, including the unbound-temporaries "three-form contract" sentence and §21.9's remedy list), and rulings closing the seams the v0.179/v0.180 trains left open. Every rule below was selected between recorded live alternatives, with the road not taken noted.

- **Choosing a disposal form (§28.3 recap; §28 preamble/table, §21.9 conformed).** The three-pattern doctrine is now stated once, normatively: `using var` = intent declared + scope pin; plain `var` = movable, auto-dropped with the must-use warning; explicit `Dispose()` = an early/conditional release point — never exception-safety plumbing, because the unwinding edge always discharges owned locals (the recorded §5.23 posture; the C# habit inverts here by design). The pre-affine "reaches an owned location, `using var`, or explicit dispose" contract sentence, the summary table's three-mechanism class row, the "must reach a discharge point" residue, the unbound-temporaries three-form sentence, §21.9's hard-error remedy list, and the category-ordered `finally` sentence are conformed to the five-form affine contract and the v0.182 establishment-order stack (implicit drops are established at declaration; owned-parameter drops at entry; temporaries at production).
- **The discard of a named owned binding is an announced consume (§17.13, §28.3, §21.9, C.3).** `_ := x;` disposes at end of the discard statement, leaves `x` explicitly-disposed, needs no marker (the sink is the announcement — the §31.1 `throw x` logic verbatim), and joins no freeze list (disposed-flag backstop); the freeze's boundary paragraph now names all three announced kills. A discard of a borrow-state operand disposes nothing (stated normatively). The `Task`/`Task<T>` discard rejection is unchanged. *Declined:* a marked `_ := owned x;` form (churns every documented remedy spelling for a sink that is already unmistakable); the borrow reading (falsifies §28.3's and §29.2's remedy lists).
- **The join boundary is recorded; the sibling lints harmonized (§28.2, §28.3, §5.1).** Uses after a *conditional* explicit dispose stay compile errors (owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = maybe-consumed): a recorded, deliberate step past §5.1's runtime-checked posture — per-path tracking exists anyway, the precision is free. §28.2's dominated use-after-dispose warning is promoted from should to must (covering reads, borrows, and consuming uses), so the statically-certain straight-line case is never the silent one. *Declined:* softening the disposed join arm to a warning (surrenders computed precision; splits the join rule's arms).
- **Who may call `Dispose()` (§28.6, §28.2, C.3).** Explicit disposal requires an owned receiver; `Dispose()` through a borrow is a compile error — borrowed locals/parameters (including `this`: no self-dispose), non-owned field reads, call results, catch bindings, pattern bindings, captured owned bindings, owning-collection element borrows. The owned-field admission is by declaring type (class-level privacy symmetry, §13.1). One recorded exception: element borrows from **borrowing-family** collections (the §28.11 transit regime, **keyed on the source expression's static type** — an `IEnumerable<T>`/enumerator/query-typed source produces tracked borrows and stays rejected) may be disposed — the manual form of `DisposeElements()`, §5.3's recorded escape hatch, caller-vouched with the checked-mode backstop; this preserves §28.11's normative asymmetric-ownership idiom (`entry.Value.Dispose()`), which a uniform prohibition would have deleted. §28.6's "double-free" justification is rewritten in owner-liveness terms (under §28.2 idempotence the second dispose is a no-op — the harm is destroying value the owner relies on), and §28.11's setter paragraph drops its "double-dispose" claim for the same reason (an explicit dispose before an owned-field assignment is §28.7's blessed, redundant legacy shape). *Declined:* dispose-through-borrow legal for plain classes (reads §28.6's first bullet out of the spec; leaves `M(s: Stream) s.Dispose()` compiling); a uniform prohibition without the transit exception (breaks the recorded idiom).
- **Closures cannot consume captured owned bindings (§28.3, §27.5, §28.9).** A captured owned binding is borrow-state inside the lambda: assignment, marked transfer, disposal, and every owned-consuming use through the capture are compile errors — generalizing §28.9's recorded move-only posture and keeping the consume-site freeze body-local and decidable (the admitted alternative was a silent drop-on-overwrite kill invisible to the freeze). *Declined:* cross-body freeze analysis (the whole-method closure-invocation analysis the freeze's recorded design deliberately avoids).
- **Trivial-dispose is defined; borrowing collections are trivial-dispose (§28.9, §28 table, §28.11, §17.13, stdlib §4.4).** "Provably a no-op" = runs no user code and frees nothing beyond what the implicit reclaim mechanism frees with the instance; the intrinsic borrowing collections' backing storage is reclaimed with the instance (their `Dispose()` does nothing — the §28 table's "Dispose releases backing storage" row and stdlib §4.4's sentence are conformed), matching §5.9's recorded plain-memory intent and the no-warning behavior every example relies on. `OwningBuffer<T>` stays non-trivial for both element kinds with its real reason stated: a declared destructor over a manually-managed allocation — the user-expressible storage primitive. *Declined:* making backing-storage release a real obligation (reverses §28.9, §17.13, §5.9; ceremony on every dropped `ToArray()` result).
- **Seam rulings, one each:** the **must-use warning covers frame-disposed `owned` parameters** of iterators/async methods, attached at the declaration, suppressed by the `using var r := owned reader;` adoption idiom (§29.8's Echo annotated; uniformity over a body-kind-conditional lint); a method may **return a deferred-activation frame** whose carried borrows are parameter-/receiver-sourced (§28.3 — the caller-side v0.179 classification re-establishes the constraints; iterator methods are the canonical instance; frames over scope-bound locals rejected at the return site; the §28.6 owned-escape rules are explicitly unaffected); **fresh producers of non-trivial-dispose class type are rejected as borrowing-family literal elements** (§15.4 — statically-certain dangle, §9.7's bind-it-first remedy; trivial-dispose elements stay admissible, which keeps §15.4's own nested-literal examples well-formed; `Add`/`Insert` stay under the §28.11 residual-trust regime, asymmetry recorded); **if-expression and expression-position `case`/`when` arm ownership** follows `??`'s recorded v0.180 meet rule, named-owned-binding-arm demotion and no-arm-marker record included (§28.3 producers row + local-read-row conformance; §20/§19.2 cross-refs; §28.10 admission — Guide 01's Pattern B gains its normative backing, the example carrying its `CloneBuffer(): owned Buffer` signature); **`set(owned)` property/indexer assignment is an announced consume** (no RHS marker; §28.11's setter example fixed to declare `set(owned)`; freeze list and producers row conformed); **implicit discharge is synchronous** (§28.12 — an implicit disposal point never awaits; only `await using` runs `DisposeAsync`); **drop-on-overwrite stores are throwable** for §28.8.1's restoration analysis (moved-from/null-targeted stores stay non-throwable, so the build-before-take idioms stand); **operator parameters admit no modifiers** (§25.2/C.10/A.4 — operand positions never consume named owned bindings; the §22.10 over-admit pattern); **move-only scrutinee pattern bindings are borrows** (§19.3, §15.3 — the §28.9 closure reasoning; `move` through the binding rejected); **unbound owned temporaries are unwind-disposed** when their full expression is exited by an exception (§28.3/§28.4/§28.7/C.3 — reverse production order on the establishment stack; the rule §15.4.1 and §28.7 already cited now exists); **§27.7.1's store-once passage rewritten** (the field spelling was rejected by §28.14 bound 3 and ill-formed under §22.8; named-method references and `Subscribe`+`Subscription` are the reliable forms, respelled `this.Clicked +=` in declaring-class framing per §24.4; record-receiver deterministic `-=` recorded as **not expressible in v1**, bound 3 liftable — this supersedes the v0.180 entry's "store-once required there" for record receivers); **§26.1/§26.4/§25.4 extension and conversion examples conformed** to §28.6/§28.3 (`Words()`, `Sort()`, `Map()` declare `owned` returns; `User` pinned as a record).

**Async, iterators, and exceptions (TRAIN-ASYNC).**

- **Yield ownership under the v0.180 discipline (spec §29.2/§28.3/C.3).** The
  yield-operand read of a named owned binding is classified by the declared
  return type: owning iterators consume (announced by the return type, no
  marker — the owned-return parallel) and the consume joins the consume-site
  freeze (the transfer hands the value alive; no disposed-flag backstop
  exists, unlike throw/dispose/discard); borrowing iterators borrow (nothing
  announces a kill; the re-borrow's source is the frame-resident binding —
  disposed on abandonment by §29.7's pass — and the adopt-then-yield spelling
  `using var l := owned line; yield return l;` is the warning-free form).
  §29.2's owned-expression bullets are re-scoped to fresh producers and
  `move` results. Declined: a `yield return owned x;` marker form (grammar
  for a case the ruling covers without syntax; the operand-position marker
  absence stays recorded as liftable) and §29.2's old letter (silent
  consumption of named bindings — the pattern v0.180 abolished). Impl
  divergence was already on file as #1267.
- **Pattern B await joins the announced-kill family (spec §30.5/§28.3/C.6).**
  The await of a named owned OwningTask<T> binding is enumerated as an
  owned-consuming position, exempt from the freeze with the recorded
  throw-precedent reasoning: the keyword+type announce the kill and the
  await's implicit task disposal sets the disposed flag. Pattern A chaining
  `return await <owned source>` (owned parameter or plain owned local; a
  `using var` source is not consumed, only disposal-deferred) is likewise
  unfrozen for a *structural* reason: the outer task cannot dispose the
  chained task before the body (including `finally`) completes.
- **Pattern A borrowed-source chain (spec §30.5/§22.13/C.6; resolves #1533).**
  `return await <borrowed source>` gets the third result-slot kind: a borrow
  through the source, teardown disposes nothing on the link; source-outlives
  is a caller-side residual with the checked-mode backstop, trivially
  discharged for process-lived statics — §22.13(b)'s own `return await _cfg!;`
  idiom now composes with §30.5 instead of contradicting it. Plain owned
  locals and admitted static Task fields join the admitted operand list
  (#1533 answered yes; the freeze already protects the plain-local case; the
  chained result stays under §22.12 rule 4's confine-or-synchronize
  obligation).
- **No ref/out on async or iterator declarations (spec §30.1/§29.3/§30.6,
  C.5/C.6).** State-machine frames outlive the synchronous call; a caller
  stack slot reference cannot be captured into one, and §22.3's out-contract
  has no coherent exit for a first-suspension return. Rejected semantically
  through the shared Param production (the §22.10 pattern); async-lambda
  target types with ref/out slots rejected at the conversion. Declined:
  assign-before-first-suspension (coherent for out only, unsound for ref,
  fragile, no use case; C# rejects both).
- **Memory-model clause (spec §30.13; stdlib §6.2).** Five normative
  happens-before edges — mutex/semaphore release→acquire (incl. FFI threads
  and Shared<Mutex>), channel accept→deliver, spawn→entry +
  settlement→join, task settlement→awaiter/blocking-wait, and static
  publication (admitted-mutable-static store→observing read; static-init
  completion→cross-domain use — the fence that makes §22.13(b)'s cache and
  the borrowed-source chain through it sound on weak hardware) — plus the
  object-specific guarantees cross-referenced in place (CancellationToken
  flag visibility, §30.8; Shared<T> drop→last-drop destruction, §28.13) and
  seq-cst atomics (v0.140). Small by construction: no mutable state is
  reachable from two domains, so no residual racy-access category exists to
  specify.
- **Channel send fault fate (spec §30.15; stdlib §6.9).** A faulting
  Send/SendAsync disposes the item before the exception surfaces; a channel
  never retains an item it did not accept. States the discharge composition
  explicitly because the data loss is on a retryable condition; give-back
  stays deferred with the TrySend RFC.
- **TCS source-owns-task (spec §30.11; stdlib §6.7).** The Task property is a
  borrow of a source-owned task; the task never outlives the source. Disposal
  accounting is by source kind: OwningTCS awaits-through-borrow dispose (the
  source's later disposal is the idempotent no-op); plain-TCS awaits neither
  consume nor dispose (multi-await fan-out stands, §30.4) and the source's
  disposal is the task's single disposal; a never-awaited task is disposed by
  the source — for OwningTCS disposing the still-held result with it (the
  "disposing the source has no effect on the result" paragraph is rewritten
  to say exactly when that is true). Fault-disposal deferral extends across
  awaiters registered at the fault. The §6.7 immediately-faulted example —
  which returned src.Task out of the source's scope, the exact shape the
  v0.75 changelog records as never having typechecked cleanly, and passed an
  exception of unstated provenance to SetException — is rewritten to the
  async-wrapper idiom (throw in an async OwningTask<T> body, §30.9).
  Declined: first-read transfer (a property read that moves) and an
  independently-owned/refcounted task (imports shared ownership).
- **TaskScope not live across yield (spec §30.7; stdlib §6.10).** An `await
  using var` of an IAsyncDisposable-without-destructor class (TaskScope; and
  conservatively, bindings of interface static type — recorded liftable) may
  not be live across a `yield return` in an async iterator: consumer
  abandonment would take §28.12's synchronous fallback, which for a
  no-destructor type skips cancel/join entirely and silently voids §6.10's
  normative quiescence. Declined (recorded as fallback): a degraded
  synchronous destructor (cancel + detached drain, the #1422 shape); an
  async unwind driver stays future work and would lift the restriction
  wholesale.
- **Allocation failure is fatal (spec §31.4/§17.7/§22.13).** Uncatchable
  termination covering new, growth, strings, boxing, and frames; joins
  §22.13's abnormal-termination list; no OutOfMemoryException. Declined:
  catchable OOM (an exception edge on every allocation, unhandleable in
  practice); a named uncatchable OOM type (report label only) — the latter
  flagged as a cosmetic owner choice.
- **Thrown-borrow cross-reference (spec §31.1; Guide 02).** A borrowing field
  inside a thrown instance is §28.3's field-held residual with the
  checked-mode backstop operative through the unwind's disposals; stated as a
  cross-reference, with the base Exception type's CauseChain snapshot named
  as the design precedent. The finding's reject options are recorded as
  declined (constructor-local admission; no interprocedural field-flow;
  same-frame handlers are sound).

Migration: nil expected for the yield rules (no doc example yields a named
owned binding in a borrowing iterator; owning-iterator named-binding yields
were BAD_REJECTed by the impl, so no user code relies on them), nil for
ref/out (never compiled meaningfully), nil for allocation failure and the
memory model (strengthenings of unstated behavior), one-shape break for
TaskScope-across-yield (restructure to a non-yielding helper), and the §6.7
TCS example was never expressible (see the v0.75 record).

**Statics, construction, and parameter passing (same revision, third train — after own and async).**
The statics/constructor half of the 2026-07-11 settlement: the three-way
incoherences in §22.13 and §22.7/§7.9 are resolved with the same
approximation-plus-recorded-bound pattern v0.181 established, and the
parameter-passing cells the spec never filled (out-assignment scope, transfer
model, ref/out operand categories, defaults × ownership) are filled with the
recorded C#-divergences that ownership forces.

- **Observing `this` during construction (§22.7 new subsection; §7.9, §24.4,
  §12.5, C.5).** §7.9's "no non-nullable field is ever observed unset" was
  falsified by a three-line base-ctor-virtual program the compiler accepts and
  segfaults on. Now: a constructor-local definite-assignment gate on synchronous
  `this`-observation (extending §28.8.1's in-ctor precedent; observations in
  base/this-argument position always rejected); virtual-family calls on `this`
  in ctor bodies rejected outside sealed non-abstract classes (the
  template-method footgun, rejected loudly); `this`-capture carved out
  (observation is at invocation — keeps §28.14 form 3 / §24.4's TickObserver
  verbatim); and the derived-mid-construction residual (helper-routed dispatch,
  escapes, construction-time closure invocation) recorded with a defined bound —
  null watermark at allocation, checked-mode `NullReferenceException`, unchecked
  UB — the §28.2 split applied to construction. *Declined:* C#-style defined
  null-observation (defines the footgun; puts null behind a non-nullable type
  as sanctioned behavior); C++ dispatch-as-static-type (silent
  different-method surprise; vtable machinery; recorded as the liftable path);
  the retired v0.123 self-contained-construction discipline as a
  general-language floor (designed for the keyword-model serialization
  eligibility and retired with it in v0.141; cited as historical precedent
  only — v0.183's §9.8 has no such rule).
- **A type's own static initialization is ordinary execution (§22.13, C.11).**
  The v0.181 backstop read literally made every initializer-to-own-helper call
  raise, while the within-type forward-reference rule checked only literal
  initializer expressions — three sentences, three answers for `Name :=
  PickName()`. Now: the backstop keys on innermost-initialization attribution
  (self-touches ordinary; T→U→T raises); the cross-type graph is distinct-types
  only (T ≠ U — without which the static-ctor freedom sentence was a self-cycle
  error); the within-type forward check follows the cross-type graph's own
  statically-resolvable-call walk (deviation from the verdict's same-type-only
  walk, recorded: same machinery, catches the one-hop foreign-helper route);
  and the function-value/virtual/cross-module residual is recorded with the
  same watermark bound. "Partially-initialized statics are never observable"
  is requalified to the backstop's scope — true again.
- **`out` is copy-out-on-normal-return; obligations bind on return paths
  (§22.3, §22.4, §22.6, stdlib §1, C.3).** §22.3's "every exit path" (which the
  spec's own vocabulary includes throw edges in) made virtually every Try body
  ill-formed; §22.6 said return paths; no transfer model was stated anywhere.
  Now: return-path obligation (throw edges carry none); the callee's out
  parameter is a callee-local slot, copied out exactly on normal return —
  exception edges never expose a partial write, an inline out recipient stays
  unassigned, and an assigned-but-unreturned `out owned` value is discharged
  callee-side by the ordinary exception-path discharge: one owner at every
  instant. Composes with §22.4's v0.181 per-path attachment and the v0.183
  `when true` postcondition (both return-path-keyed). *Declined:* write-through
  (C#'s model, chosen there because a GC owes nothing on the exception edge;
  here it would park an owned value in the caller's slot mid-call with no
  attached obligation). Gives #1634 its normative answer.
- **`ref`/`out` operand categories defined (§22.3 new subsection, §17.6,
  A.4 commentary).** The admissible argument category was never stated; the
  implementation already admitted indexer slots (#1302 is a write-back bug in
  the unspecified corner). Now: §17.6's assignable-lvalue categories, reused by
  cross-reference; locals/fields alias, accessor targets are copy-in/copy-out
  with evaluate-once bracketing and write-back on normal return in argument
  textual order (deviation from "unspecified or rejected", recorded: §22.5
  v0.181 made observable order normative-textual, and write-back order should
  not reintroduce the nondeterminism one token to the right); owned-state
  locations and rule-2 mutable statics excluded as recorded v1 bounds
  (liftable — the freeze-at-ref-site design is the lift path).
- **§22.13 pattern (a) rewritten onto the admitted task cache (§22.13, §30.5,
  C.6).** The sanctioned `Config.Current := await LoadConfigAsync();` wrote a
  mutable class-typed static rule 2 rejects (and its RHS had no legal Pattern A
  reading). Pattern (a) is now eager assignment of pattern (b)'s `Task<T>?`
  cache before any spawn — exactly-once with zero new machinery. Two
  composition gaps this surfaced are closed by TRAIN-ASYNC's borrowed-source
  formulation in this same revision (E-A3a–e, to which this train defers): an
  admitted static task field is a named Pattern-A borrow source (process-lived;
  overwrite-never-disposes is what makes the mutable cache's borrow race-proof
  — the v0.181 accepted cost now pays for itself), and chaining from a
  borrowed source transfers nothing (statics are not movable; pattern (b)'s
  own `return await _cfg!` finally has a defined reading). *Recorded loss:* no synchronous-access async-initialized
  class-typed static exists; restoring it is a real design (a third rule-2
  form with store semantics and an enforcement story), declined here because
  rule 2's admission must stay decidable at the declaration.
- **`when true` × #1535(B): deliberate coexistence, recorded on #1535.** The
  v0.183 clause serves every user-authored Try API and is not deletable by any
  stdlib reshaping; fork (B) (nullable-return conversions) stays open per-API
  on stdlib §1(b)'s criterion. Nullable return where the payload carries the
  signal; Try + `when true` where it cannot (§14.4/§7.10 nullable-underlying
  instantiations) or where the bool shape is the idiom.
- **Statics seams, one each:** §24.6's blanket "not synchronized" scoped to
  instance events, the static exception stated (conforming to rule 5, which
  governed since v0.163); the compiler-generated static-event backing field
  admitted under rule 5 and exempt from rules 2/4, with §30.14's
  `EventSource<T>` entry qualified (both superseded by 0035 if it lands);
  rule 4's domain-reachability warning and §22.13's no-`owned` disposal warning
  stated independent and co-firing, `owned` clearing only the latter;
  §28.13's `Shared`-payload synchronized set given a normative four-type
  list, pinned (as of v0.184) as rule 2 form-(i) minus `ChannelSender<T>` with
  the exclusion's reason (senders are minted per producer) and a
  no-silent-growth clause (a later form-(i) joiner needs a separate ruling),
  replacing two same-named different-membership enumerations, with the two
  predicate-restating sites conformed (spec §30.14, stdlib §2.16) and the two
  stdlib "every exit path" restatements conformed (`TryRead*`,
  `Mutex.TryAcquire`; historical changelog entries deliberately untouched);
  §22.9's construction-unwind enumeration extended to step-0 owned capture
  fields on every edge including step-1 throws (whose "no derived state" claim
  was false), with "reverse construction order" corrected to reverse
  declaration order and the parameter-to-capture move stated (no double
  discharge); §22.7's scenario-table row-2 remnant ("or the throwing field
  initializer is preceded by a successful one") deleted; §22.5's owned-default
  cell filled (owned-producing non-trivial-dispose defaults on `owned`
  parameters only, compile error on plain — trivial-dispose defaults free) and
  the evaluation-site freedom pinned as semantically unobservable.
- **Rule 5 honestly narrowed (§22.12, C.11 — interim; #1647).** The v0.180
  capture-free compile-error promise is unenforceable through an
  `IEvent<T>`-typed alias (bypassable member-site reading vs. undecidable
  all-sites reading). Interim, recorded downgrade: the compile error is scoped
  to member-syntax subscription sites; the alias route is a recorded programmer
  obligation joining §30.14's indirect-alias family, surfaced by a should-level
  advisory at the alias-creation site — a value-position use of the member;
  subscribe- and raise-receiver positions never warn. The
  enforceable statement is proposal 0035 §7 S1, owner-gated; nothing here
  forecloses it. *Declined:* an alias restriction (a new member-kind carve-out
  of exactly the genus 0035 proposes deleting, severing legitimate capture-free
  composition with no bridge); minting a proto-S1 type ahead of the owner's Q4.

**Types, generics, and inference (fourth train).** (1) §14.5 NEW — generic-method type-argument inference: exact-agreement structural unification (no common-supertype joins), two-phase lambda participation with the closed-slot admission rule (equal or implicitly converting; exact beats converting at ranking), method references via §27.6's exact-preferred ranking (now stated in §27.6 — its OrderBy(Math.Abs) example was previously underivable), target-typed completion (typed declaration/assignment/return/default/determined-argument contexts — codifies the implemented Empty()-factory idiom); explicit lists all-or-nothing; no constructor inference; per-candidate inference before §22.6 with failed candidates silently inapplicable; non-generic beats generic as the LAST comparison, after the v0.181 defaulted-arity tie-break (implemented behavior; C#'s internal order would let a new optional-parameter overload re-route existing calls). (2) §6.6 — compound assignment: desugaring with the target evaluated once (base, member hops, indexes, getter/setter each once; §17.6 becomes an instance) and the checked narrow-integer write-back (b += 10 ≡ b := byte(b + 10), OverflowException on range, runtime RHS admitted); cross-family results (f += 2.5, b += 1.5) are compile errors; ??= and event +=/-= carve-outs restated. (3) §18.5 — nullable holes render null (no dispatch, alignment applies, type-formattability check against non-nullable T); §8.5/§7.4 conformed. (4) §9.8 — records with heap-collection serialized components are ineligible (record-admissibility: value-shaped components only); the v0.182 open question closes as same-treatment (Deserialize is ownership-invalid per §9.7); positional/body records agree; C.8 conformed. (5) §12.2 — blocked-name set is visible-members-only (private never blocks except nested-in-base; internal blocks in-module; cross-module residual stated: distinct members, lookup selects by static type, selected member dispatches per its own virtual-ness); pure liberalization; C.1 conformed. (6) §11.2/§12.1 — scoped joins the exact-match parameter-modifier lists, both directions, with the caller-contract reasoning recorded; C.1 conformed. (7) §17.14 NEW — constant expressions: the closed sublanguage (literals sans interpolation, const/enum refs incl. wrapper constants, nameof, built-in operators over primitives/string, constant conditional, parentheses; default(T) declined-liftable) with compile-time evaluation under runtime semantics and evaluation faults as compile errors; A.8/A.5 grammar comments, §22.12, §17.9 (phantom 'attribute arguments' removed), §5.1, §10.2, §15.1, C.11 re-pointed. (8) §5.1 — reference conversions stated (identity, class→base, →Object with boxing, type→conformed interface, interface→extended, type-parameter→constraint bound, §12.9 variance), ownership carries through unchanged, co-equal ranking (M(Animal)/M(Object) on Dog stays ambiguous; C#'s better-target refinement declined per rationale §14.5); §20/§22.6 conformed. Migration: newly rejected — partial/excess explicit type-argument lists, generic-constructor inference, cross-family compound assignment (previously crashed codegen), scoped mismatches, fault-at-fold const initializers, record collection components (already rejected by impl), converting-only lambda overload sets (previously a silent pick); newly accepted — invisible-base-member name reuse, nullable holes (already implemented). Runtime-visible: none for correct programs.

#### Migration

Compile-time, newly **rejected**: `Dispose()` (or a discard) through a tracked borrow — a borrowed local/parameter (including `this`), a non-owned field read, a call result, a catch or pattern binding, an owning-collection element borrow, or an element read of an `IEnumerable<T>`/enumerator/query-typed source (previously unaddressed; each is a probable bug — restructure so the owner disposes, use the owning collection's removal forms, or iterate the collection itself for the transit regime); assignment to / transfer from / disposal of a captured owned binding inside a lambda (previously admitted by the compiler — restructure to an `owned`-parameter callback); a fresh-producer element of non-trivial-dispose class type in a borrowing-family collection literal (bind the source first, or use the owning family; trivial-dispose elements — nested collection literals — are unaffected); parameter modifiers on operator parameters (previously parseable, semantics undefined); a returned lazy/enumerable/Task-typed frame carrying a scope-bound local's borrow (materialize instead). Newly **warned**: undischarged `owned` parameters of iterators/async methods (adopt with `using var … := owned …` to silence); straight-line use after a dominating dispose/discard is now a mandatory warning. Newly **accepted / defined**, no action needed: `_ := x;` on a named owned binding now has one meaning (announced consume at end of statement); if-expressions and expression-position `case`/`when` over owned arms are defined owned producers (Guide 01's Pattern B shape); returning parameter-sourced lazy pipelines (`Evens(xs) => xs.Where(IsEven)`) is confirmed legal; `cache.Current := c;` through a `set(owned)` setter consumes without a marker; mid-expression producers are defined to be unwind-disposed (no leak on the exception edge — codifies the only sound reading). Runtime-visible: none for correct programs — borrowing-collection `Dispose()` was already specified trivial in §28.9 (the contrary table row promised work no conforming program could observe); the unwind disposal of expression temporaries codifies the behavior three sections already assumed.

*From the statics train:*
Newly **rejected** (compile-time): `this`-observation in a ctor body before the declaring class's §7.9-strict fields are assigned, and in `base(...)`/`this(...)` argument position always; virtual/override/abstract calls on `this` in ctor bodies of non-sealed (or abstract) classes; a within-type forward static-readonly read routed through statically-resolvable calls; `ref`/`out` arguments over owned-state locations or admitted mutable statics; owned-producing non-trivial-dispose default values on plain parameters; capture-bearing member-syntax static-event subscriptions (already implemented, #1542 — now the stated scope). Newly **defined**, no action for correct programs: `out` copy-out semantics (programs observing a partial `out` write in `catch` were relying on unspecified behavior); accessor-target `ref`/`out` bracketing with textual-order write-back; callee-side discharge of assigned-but-unreturned `out owned` values; the construction/static null-watermark + checked-mode `NullReferenceException` residual bounds; self-static-init as ordinary execution (programs that today survive only because the backstop is unimplemented become sanctioned; the `Boot` forward-read shape becomes a compile error). Newly **warned** (should-level): a `static event` member used as a value (alias creation); receiver positions — subscribe family and raise family alike — never warn. **Doc-only:** pattern (a) rewrite; §24.6/§22.9/§22.7-row-2/§28.13-set/warning-independence edits; the B6/B7 conforming restatements (spec §30.14; stdlib §1, §2.16, `TryRead*`, `Mutex.TryAcquire`).

### v0.185 changelog (v0.184 → v0.185)

v0.185 is the **stdlib-coherence & currency batch** — the library-facing settlement of the 2026-07-11 review plus the cross-cutting currency fixes the four v0.184 trains surfaced. No new language rules; it aligns the standard-library document and a set of stale examples/cross-references with the v0.184 ownership-coherence revision.

**Standard library (TRAIN-STDLIB).**
**Standard library (TRAIN-STDLIB).**

- **A third Try shape is sanctioned; `IParsable` witnessing is bridged (stdlib §1, §2.19; spec §11.8; rationale §11.8 rider).** The pervasive concrete-value-typed Try APIs (§9 `TryParse`, `Convert.TryTo*`, §4.14/§4.15 `TryRead*`, `DateTime`/`DateOnly`/`TimeOnly`/`Guid` `TryParse`) declare `bool` + **non-nullable value-typed out** + `default(T)` on false — a shape §1 claimed did not exist ("exactly two … nullable in every form"). §1 now sanctions it as shape **(c)** and opens "three Try shapes", scoping shape (a)'s nullability + `when true` to **generic/class-typed** payloads (where `T?` is unavoidable because `default` of a non-nullable class is a compile error, spec §17.11); the v0.171 uniformity posture targeted generic extraction slots, not always-value-typed families, so shape (c) is not the pre-v0.171 illegal class form. `IParsable<T>.TryParse` keeps `out value: T?` (user class conformers need it) and the **compiler-provided primitive conformances bridge the out-nullability** — generic `T.TryParse(out v)` through the constraint sees `T?`, a direct `int.TryParse(out i)` sees `int`; §2.19's false "no signatures changed" claim is rewritten to state the bridge, and the ambiguous "§11.8" citation in §1 is dropped from the `when true` list (the parse companions are shape (c), which carries no `when true`). *Declined:* migrating every value-typed out to `T?` (breaking, hostile for parse loops, buys no honesty the bool lacks); constraining the interface out to non-nullable `T` (breaks class conformers).
- **Stream async methods are an override surface (stdlib §7.1/§7.2; spec §12.1).** `ReadAsync`/`WriteAsync` are `async virtual` (modifier order per §11.5) with a documented blocking default (delegating to the abstract sync forms — a §30.12 pool-pin, no I/O backstop); `FileStream` and proposal 0006's streams override with real async I/O; memory-backed streams inherit correctly. The span overloads **and** `ReadAll`/`ReadAllAsync` are **fixed base conveniences** — *not* override points (a subclass overriding the windowed/async forms gets the right behavior through them). Under §12.1 (non-virtual-by-default) the prior declarations forbade any override, making genuinely-async I/O unimplementable and contradicting accepted proposal 0006. The §7.1 code fence that swallowed the windowed-form prose and `SeekOrigin` is repaired as part of the edit. *Declined:* `abstract` (boilerplate on memory streams).
- **Reference-implementation and example repairs (stdlib §2.14, §4.5, §4.9, §4.10, §6.1).** The §4.5 `OwningArray` capacity constructor is respelled in valid §20 postfix-conditional syntax (`capacity if capacity > 0 else 1`) and now faults on negative capacity (§1 #1396) instead of silently clamping. The §4.9 `OwningDictionary` `Add`/`PopValue` loops and the §4.10 `pool.Add` example gain the v0.169/v0.180 transfer markers (the `Add` loop's key test moved before the node transfer to avoid a use-after-move the mechanical marker would introduce). The §2.14 cyclic `Node` example declares its spine as `Shared<Node>` and its back-edge `owned Back: Weak<Node>?` (was a plain owned edge that could not anchor the `Weak` back-edge and tripped §9.8's lint); the §2.14 `Order`/`Invoice` examples gain component-binding primary constructors (the prior constructors bound no owning components — a §9.8 constructor-selection compile error and a §7.9 violation). The §6.1 linked-source idiom binds its `WithCancelAfter` source to a named `using var` (the prior unbound temporary cancelled the link on disposal).
- **Sendability, disposal, retention, and container-contract prose (stdlib §5, §4.4/§4.8/§4.10, §6.3/§6.4/§6.9, §6.5, §6.6, §7.1/§7.2).** §6.3 `Semaphore` and §6.4 atomics are stated **sendable** (the spec delegated this statement to §6.2–§6.4, but §6.3 said nothing); §6.9's "only Mutex + Channel" sentence is widened to the full sendable set. `destructor;` declarations are added to `EventSource`/`AsyncEventSource`, `Channel`/`ChannelSender`, `TaskCompletionSource`/`OwningTaskCompletionSource` (source-owns-task disposal, spec §30.11), and `FileStream` (whose flush-on-dispose contract was previously stated nowhere), and Stream's abstract-disposal caveat is stated — under §1 the absence had meant no-op. §5 states the **callback-taking** lazy operators' callback-retention certification (spec §28.14 named it; §5 had no retention text), explicitly excluding the callback-free lazy operators. §4.4/§4.5/§5 gain a sorting contract (stability per API, total-order comparer, throw-edge element preservation, re-entrancy → `InvalidOperationException`); §4.8/§4.10 gain the store-time key/element stability rule and the `Set`/`OwningSet` iteration-order decision (Set insertion-ordered, OwningSet no guarantee).

**Currency & consistency batch (TRAIN-EDIT).**
**Currency & consistency batch (post-v0.184 seam sweep).** Twenty-two mechanical edits closing stale-text and dangling-reference seams the v0.179/v0.180/v0.183/v0.184 trains left, none of them design changes. §10.6's canonical enum-matching example moves from the retired comma-alternative spelling to `|` (v0.167). §12.6's FileSource.LoadAsync is rewritten to the real `File.ReadAllTextAsync(_path): Task<string>` (removing an invented 1-arg `FileStream` ctor and a `ReadAllAsync`/`Task<string>` type mismatch), and the four remaining 1-arg `FileStream` construction examples (§21.6, §28.10 ×2, §31.2) take the real `(path, FileMode.Open)` ctor. Appendix C.10's enum co-declaration bullet is conformed to §25.2's v0.183 wording (a plain `GetHashCode(): int` on enums, which never carry `override`). §17.6's owned-field `++`/`--` paragraph is rewritten onto §28.7 drop-on-overwrite (result produced first, displaced value disposed implicitly, no warning), replacing pre-v0.161 must-dispose-first/must-warn text. §7.4's 'how narrowing is established' enumeration and §12.1's override modifier-match list each gain the v0.183 `when true`/`when false` out-postcondition (§22.4), which their own prose and §22.4's back-citation already presumed present. §28.3's move-semantics enumeration, discharge-form list, and `??` producers row each gain `throw` (already an announced kill in §31.1 and the freeze boundary, previously unlisted in these three enumerations). Rationale §11.3 is corrected to the `|` catch-alternative spelling; rationale §12.1's awaiter-borrow prose is broadened from 'must be held in `using var`' to the current §30.5 admitted-owning-location set, and 'the only syntactic shape that compiles' becomes 'the canonical shape' (post-v0.89 loosening). The phantom 'module-level method/helper' phrasing — Bezel has no free functions (rationale §11.3: a `public static class` is the free-function surface) — is corrected to 'static method on a static class' at spec §26.3, §26.5 rule 4, and rationale §18. Finally, Appendix C gains three invariants that exist normatively but were unlisted: the §22.4 out-postcondition (C.5), and the §31.2.1 multi-type-catch nearest-common-base-above-Object and generic-catch-arm class-bound rules (C.7). Migration: none — every edit is doc-only currency; no correct program's meaning changes.

### v0.186 changelog (v0.185 → v0.186)

v0.186 is the **shared-state & data-parallelism graduation** — accepted proposals 0003 (`Locked<T>`/`RwLocked<T>`) and 0032 (parallel extensions, stages 0–1.5) land in the normative documents as one composed revision (the two edit the same §22.12/§28.13/§30.12/§30.14 passages; #1703). All open design questions were resolved by delegated rulings recorded here and in §12.8/§12.9; the owner reviews on the tracking issues.

**Data-owning locks (TRAIN-LOCK; proposal 0003 → spec §30.12 "Data-owning locks", §22.12 rule 4, §28.13, §30.13 edge 1, §30.14; stdlib §6.11; rationale §12.8).**

- `Locked<T>`/`RwLocked<T>`: the lock owns its interior; guard `Value` is a guard-sourced borrow (the `Shared.Get()` dispensation), so the `using var` scope is the critical section with zero new lifetime machinery. Interior admission **reuses the sendable derived property** (`T` must be a sendable class type, checked at instantiation) — the precise form of 0003's "transfer-closed interior", no new predicate. Full acquisition surface mirrors `Mutex` (blocking/`Try(timeout)`/`Async(token)`/`TryAsync`), inheriting the v0.179 blocking discipline. Non-reentrancy stated — including `Mutex`'s, previously unstated anywhere — plus the rwlock recursive-read hazard (a second `Read()` may queue behind a waiting writer; fairness unspecified). Locks sendable; guards not. Guard release joins §30.13 edge 1 (rwlock refinement stated in §30.12; the edge's acquisition-form list extended). Guard-across-`await` is a should-level lint, not a ban.
- **Guard-liveness checks (new checking rules, counted).** §28.3's announced-kill carve-out is justified by the killed object's own disposed-flag backstop; a guard kill sets no flag on the *interior* its surviving borrows reference while releasing the lock — so the carve-out does not extend to guards (the §28.14 admission-freeze precedent): explicit `Dispose()`/discard of a guard binding under a live `Value`-sourced borrow is a compile error, and a live guard counts as a live borrow of the lock binding it came from (body-local kills of the lock under a live guard are rejected the same way). Cross-body/cross-domain lock destruction under outstanding guards takes the §28.2 posture, stated normatively: checked-mode deterministic fault (destruction with live guards detected; stale guard access → `DisposedAccessException`), unchecked UB.
- **Read guards are write-restricted (new checking rule, counted; scope stated honestly).** Concurrent cross-domain read guards are the type's point, and Bezel has no read-only borrow — so **within the body holding the guard**, through a `ReadGuard`-sourced borrow every store, `move`, and `ref`/`out` pass is a compile error (expression-site, borrow-provenance-keyed, the v0.184 dispose-through-borrow family; body-local because borrow provenance does not cross calls). The **recorded residual** (§30.14 indirect-alias genus): mutating methods invoked through the read borrow, and any callee reached with the read borrow as a plain argument. *Declined:* deferring `RwLocked`; pure residual trust; per-interior read facades; a const-method vocabulary (§12.5's road; lift path: a read-only view form designed with the frozen-view family).
- **Static membership, recast on v0.184's ground (recorded deviation from 0003's letter).** 0003's "join the rule-2 form-(i) set" predates v0.184's store semantics: a mutable static lock would be *sound* under them, but overwrite-never-disposes would leak a displaced lock plus its whole interior (payload-scaled, unlike the `Task?` cache), and racing first-use stores could transiently fork a registry into two lock instances. No use case demands lock-slot reassignment (mutability lives behind the guards), so the locks join **rule 4's new v0.186 suppression list** — the `static owned readonly` registry, 0003's actual deliverable, is warning-free and exit-disposed — and stay **out of form-(i)** (mutable lock statics rejected). Liftable by separate ruling. Both lock types join §28.13's `Shared`-payload set by separate ruling per its no-silent-growth clause (`Shared<Locked<T>>` is the `Shared<Mutex>` idiom with the state attached).

**Parallel extensions, stages 0–1.5 (TRAIN-PAR; proposal 0032 → spec §30.14 "Data-parallel combinators", §30.15, §28.13, §28.14, §22.12 rule 4, §28.3, §28.11, §30.1; stdlib §4.19, §6.9, §6.12; rationale §12.9).**

- **Stage 0** was already normative (v0.179 async spawn entries; impl tracker #1523) — cross-referenced, not re-landed. Its rider lands now: **`Channel<T>.ReceiveAll()`**, the non-exceptional drain form (`await for` over the §30.7 interfaces; completes normally on drained-and-closed; one consumption in progress — a second `ReceiveAll`, a `ReceiveAll` begun over a pending `Receive`, or interleaved receives raise `InvalidOperationException`; affine per §29.11; abandonment deregisters like `Receive`). Zero new checking rules.
- **Stage 1**: compiler-known `Parallel.Map`/`Reduce`/`ForEach` over a lazy process-wide worker-domain team. The bodies are **spawn positions** — one table extension of the existing call-site category (§28.14's list names them); zero new checking rules (thesis re-verified against the v0.184 capture/freeze changes: capture-free entries are unaffected). Snapshot-at-call (run-to-completion makes it a contract); results in input order; first-fault-wins as `DomainFaultedException` (*declined:* a `ParallelFaultedException` carrying the failing index — message text suffices, a subclass is additive later); moved-in unprocessed items disposed (the channel-close precedent); call→body and body→settlement visibility derived from the §30.13 edges (the "five edges" title stays true). Returns follow the `Domain.Spawn` owned-task convention (noted against §6.7's unmarked `WhenAll` rows — deliberate, not to be silently harmonized). **`Reduce` seed semantics stated plainly** (new): per-worker fold from `seed`, partials combined in an unspecified tree — a non-identity seed is incorporated once per worker; associativity documented, not checked. `degree: int := 0` = `DefaultDegree` (= `ProcessorCount` at team creation, fixed per process); negative raises `ArgumentException`. *Recorded deferrals:* async bodies, class-element `Reduce`, cancellation parameter, user-declared spawn positions.
- **Stage 1.5**: `FrozenArray<T>` (stdlib §4.19) — deeply immutable, fixed-size; `T` restricted to sendable value types and `string` (intrinsic, the `Atomic<T>` style); `From(owned OwningBuffer<T>)` O(1) steal (value-typed only; *declined:* a receiver-consuming `Freeze()`, which would need a receiver-consumption mechanism the language does not have) and copying `From(Array<T>)` (the only string form). Sendable (§30.14 row). **Membership rulings under v0.184's no-silent-growth clause** (the recast of 0032's q4 — no definitional widening of "internally synchronized" is needed or made): joins the §28.13 `Shared`-payload set as its first **deep-immutability** member (reads need no machinery; reclamation synchronization is `Shared<T>`'s own atomic control block — #689, implemented — plus the string-precedent storage tolerance); joins §22.12 rule 4's suppression list; deliberately **not** form-(i) (the same payload-leak ground as the locks). The §28.13 set's relation to form-(i) is restated (minus `ChannelSender<T>`, plus the three v0.186 members). `Parallel.*` gains zero-copy `Shared<FrozenArray<A>>` overloads (one handle cloned per worker).
- **Freeze-time aliasing closed honestly (rulings, counted).** `FrozenArray`'s "no writer can exist" is delivered by named rules plus one named obligation, not by assumption: (1) the consume-site freeze now **states** that a live borrow-bearing-record local (a span) counts as a live local borrow of its carried sources (§28.3 — making normative what §9.7's subjection of record values to §28.3's borrow rules already implied; a span local over a buffer freezes it against `From(owned …)` and every other consume); (2) the v0.180 **domain clause is extended** at its recorded attachment points (§28.3 borrowed-field rule — the single full statement — §28.11's store rule, §30.1's settlement obligation by reference, the §28.3 fields-not-frozen note, §30.14's summary): the caller-side obligation now also covers **consuming a borrowed-from source into a domain-reachable construction** — `FrozenArray<T>.From`, the `Shared<T>`/`Locked<T>`/`RwLocked<T>` constructors, an admitted static store — which is not a domain transfer but publishes the storage cross-domain while the borrow survives (field/slot-sourced consumes are freeze-exempt and dispose nothing, so no conformance mode can catch this route). For pre-v0.186 payload types the newly-named shapes were benign (the payload was itself synchronized).
- **Stage 2 recorded, not landed (rationale §12.9)**: blocked-primary `Parallel.Join` (the awaiting variant recorded as weaker and more novel); `concurrently-readable` (§3.6 form, fork-position-checked; locks/channels/tasks excluded); the fork-extent acquisition guard **widened to cover the new §6.11 locks**; provenance-linear `SplitAt` witnesses with **opaque lending by type** (a lend-span family; the interprocedural body rule declined); `par` as a compiler-known-only contextual modifier (no grammar reservation in this revision); the location-granular §30.14 invariant amendment ratified in principle, pinned verbatim, deliberately *not* applied now (nothing in v0.186 violates the current sentence); the rule-4-statics fork residual sharpened (a confinement-honoring program can newly race through its own forks — the landing must address it explicitly). *Declined, binding:* a `parallel for` statement; move-capturing spawn bodies; user-generic parallel libraries; a runtime send-check. `.AsParallel()` stays a recorded endnote (§29.11 affinity removes PLINQ's hazard class structurally; evidence first).

**FFI v2 graduation (proposal 0033 + the `env` extension).** Accepted proposal 0033 (owner, 2026-07-12) landed in full (its Stages A+B+C), together with the six §32 defect amendments 0033 §0 had routed to earlier trains that shipped without them (routing corrected; re-verified against v0.185), and one owner-requested extension designed at graduation: **capture-bearing call-bounded callbacks (the `env` clause)**, answering the owner's instance-callback question ("marshal an object method that can update the class object it comes from"). §32 grows from a calling convention into an FFI: foreign memory, C-compatible records, boundary `out`/`ref`, symbol aliases and C-variadic imports, typed handles — every addition **trusted but unverified** in §32's existing sense, explicit at the call site, with the dangerous operations named as dangerous and confined behind `import System.Interop`.

- **Foreign memory (§32.12; stdlib §10.5, §10.1–§10.3, §4.14).** `Ptr<T>` — typed, element-scaled, named-methods-only foreign access; `IntPtr` stays opaque *placement*. Pointee set gated per-instantiation; `Ptr<Ptr<U>>` declined (v1); `Ptr<T>` sendability ratified with a cross-domain UB trust bullet (§32.10). `RawBytes.FromForeign` (view or `free(3)`-on-dispose); `CString`/`WString.Pointer`; `OwningBuffer<T>.DangerousPointer()` (value-typed presentation only — the class-typed presentation can never satisfy the gate). The **no-object-address invariant** stated: class references never convert to addresses. *Declined:* Marshal-style untyped reads; checked foreign memory; operator pointer arithmetic (rationale §16.3).
- **C-compatible records (§32.13; §3.6).** New derived-property row + the language's **first representation promise** (target-C-ABI layout, declaration order, ABI padding), scoped to classified records; §3.6's behavior-dispatch reservation gains its single scoped exception, ratified together with the promise (rationale §16.5). By-address admission (`ref`/`out`, `Ptr<R>`); single-integer/pointer-field records pass directly (typed handles — `Sqlite3Db` vs `Sqlite3Stmt` confusion becomes a compile error); wrapper classes remain the lifetime answer (`closes` clause declined, rationale §16.7). By-value structs stay Stage-D-deferred (§32.14). Unions/bitfields declined with recorded workarounds.
- **Boundary `out`/`ref` (§32.5, new sub-block).** Direct address-of-caller-storage semantics, normative (re-entrant callbacks can observe mid-call writes — through statics, derived `Ptr`s, or a captured `ref` argument of the same call); `out`'s definite assignment granted at return with the write trusted (§32.10 bullet); **new compile error**: a callback argument of an extern call may not capture a binding passed `out` to the same call (indeterminate-bits observation, statically checkable). `out owned`/`owned`/string-type `ref`/`out` not admitted, with reasons. Closes the accepted-but-miscompiled modifier surface.
- **RawBytes marshalling pinned (§32.5)** — previously "a pointer-and-length pair" with no C shape: parameter positions occupy **two consecutive C slots** (pointer, then length); `RawBytes` extern returns are **rejected** (no return convention for two slots; wrap via `FromForeign`); `RawBytes?` marshals NULL/0. (0033 §6.2 named this hole; it does not survive the graduation.)
- **Symbol binding (§32.11, repurposed; the old reserved list moves to §32.14 keeping its anchor).** Identifier-is-the-symbol stated; `:= symbol "…"` aliases; §32.3's bare-name derivation promoted to a stated rule; **startup resolution pinned** — every resolution failure surfaces before `Main`, lazy binding conforming only if it preserves that observable failure point, with the fail-fast cost recorded (platform-absent symbols make a linking program fail at startup until 0034-era conditionals exist); `variadic(N)` with the promoted-type compile error and the fixed-arity-binding `%al` UB warning; true varargs declined (rationale §16.6).
- **Callbacks (§32.8).** Exception escape now **aborts with a diagnostic** (was platform-dependent; never unwinds native frames).
