### v0.200 changelog (v0.199 → v0.200)

**The `choice` revision — proposal 0041 graduates: closed nominal sums land as a new type kind (2026-07-19, owner-directed; #2028).** The language gains **choices** (spec §35): value types whose values carry one of a fixed, named set of cases, each with an optional positional payload; qualified construction (`FetchOutcome.Failed(504, "…")`); `case` consumption with positional destructuring, prefix omission, and full static exhaustiveness by case name (no `_` arm when every case is covered — and no generic determination machinery: the discriminant is a name, not a runtime type). The ownership story is a three-way **derived classification** computed from the payloads on §9.7's pattern — **value-like** (ordinary copyable values), **borrow-bearing** (§9.7's lifetime rules verbatim), **owning** (some payload marked `owned`; the value joins §15.3's move-only category, whose extension rationale §5.14 explicitly anticipated). Matching borrows by default (§19.3 unchanged; peeking at an owned outcome is legal and non-consuming); an **owning match** — triggered by a fresh owned temporary scrutinee or the explicit marker `case owned x of` — transfers the selected case's owned payloads into the arm's bindings, with guards observing borrows and transfer at arm selection. All four proposal stages land together: the kind (Core), the owning classification (Extended, on Appendix D.2's move-only row), serialization synthesis for value-like choices (the `$case`-discriminated object form, §9.8; `$case` joins stdlib §2.15's `$`-reserved set), and stdlib **`Result<T, E>`** (§2.20 — the one shipped choice; `Option<T>` is declined, DECLINED.md D-0004: `T?` is Bezel's option type).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation).** No new axioms — the register stays at fourteen. The owning-choice rules derive: payload-slot arguments are K3.3 consumes; the marked owning-match scrutinee joins **K3.4's marked-transfer family** (the K3.4 clause is extended; frozen per K5.1's existing marked-transfers wording, the owning-iterator reasoning — payloads transfer alive, no flag is set); drop-on-overwrite is K3.11 — owning choices deliberately do **not** share axiom A13's inline-array reassignment carve (a choice has no partial states, so the automatic disposal is sound and taken); discharge and auto-drop are K3.14/K3.15; the temporary-scrutinee owning match rides K8.3's `case`-scrutinee boundary unchanged. The §3.6 behavior-dispatch reservation gains its second scoped exception (the choice classification's per-instantiation copy-vs-move/disposal behavior) via rationale §5.15's recorded generalization path — language-performed, structure-derived, no user hook.

**Decided (proposal 0041 §12's Q1–Q12, resolved per its recommendations under the owner's direction):** the `choice` keyword, fully reserved (collision scan clean — zero identifier uses in stdlib, spec, tests, or guides; Q1); the owning-match trigger is the explicit scrutinee marker plus fresh-temporary auto-consume — **not** §30.5's marker-free named-operand consume, because two of the three announced-kill ingredients are absent (a choice is legitimately multiply-inspected; a moved value sets no flag), and not context-keyed consumption, which would make arm binding modes depend on context outside the construct (Q2); guards use the two-phase borrow-then-transfer rule (Q3); equality for borrow-bearing/owning choices is §9.2's use-site error — the record precedent over §15.3's borrowing-equality precedent, with the conflict surfaced and ruled (Q4); owning classification at Extended on the move-only row, accepting the per-instantiation Core/Extended boundary (Q5); `Ok`/`Error` case names (Q6); interface conformance admitted with the owning-conversion rejection (Q7); `default(C)` a compile error for every choice — a sum has no principled zero (Q8); the §3.6 reservation amendment as worded (Q9); owning choices field-admissible in transfer-closed classes but not directly sendable — the move-only exclusion kept uniform (Q10); one-level exhaustiveness counting, multi-level usefulness analysis recorded liftable (Q11); no `Unwrap`/`Map`/`AndThen` — extraction is the owning match's job, and combinators over owned payloads need the deferred ownership-polymorphic function parameters (Q12).

**Declined (recorded in rationale §9.6):** widening `enum` with payloads (the integer-backed enum contract would need an "unless payloads" fork at every joint); class-backed sums as the primary answer (`sealed abstract` remains the open-hierarchy tool); structural/anonymous unions (anti-nominal; collides with D-0002's posture); `Option<T>` (D-0004).

**Section numbering note:** §35 lands after §34 to preserve every existing section number and anchor; its conceptual home in §3.1's kind ordering (between enums and classes) is stated at the section head. Stdlib `Result` is §2.20 for the same reason.

**Migration.** Purely additive: `choice` was unused as an identifier anywhere in the repository; no existing grammar production narrows; no existing type's classification, layout, or rules change; every edit to shared sections is a new clause keyed on a kind no existing program can name. The Try convention and `sealed abstract` hierarchies remain fully supported; the guides now present the choice return as the first tool for expected failure *with information* (Guide 2 §5/§6, Guide 1 §9; pins → v0.200). Spec-ahead-of-impl: the compiler implements none of §35 yet — tracking issues filed at this landing (stage 1: parser/sema/classification/exhaustiveness; stage 2: the owning machinery through the ownership passes; stage 3: serialization synthesis; stage 4: stdlib `Result`).

### v0.201 changelog (v0.200 → v0.201)

**The three-train revision — proposals 0048, 0049, 0050 graduate (2026-07-19, owner-directed; #2035/#2036/#2037).** Three bounded trains, composition-gated as one revision.

**Train 1 — explicit factory ownership (0048; the first axiom retirement).** The v0.60 static-return heuristic is retired: a `static` method or `operator` whose declared return type (nullability stripped) is a class or interface type is now a **compile error at the declaration** unless the signature announces its classification — `owned`, a `Task`-family type, a §29.3/§30.7 iterable or enumerator interface, or a bare type parameter with a non-empty potential source set (spec §28.3 *Factory methods and sourceless returns*, rewritten under its kept heading; producers row, iterator paragraph, borrow-lifetime tendrils, Appendix C.3 updated). Both v0.60 safety-net motives are discharged (the stdlib pass completed — the sweep found **zero** reliant signatures — and the §2.8 artifact model delivers third-party diagnostics at the declaring build); what the retirement closes is the memorized rule and the instance↔static refactor hazard, plus the method-reference laundering seam (`() -> owned Widget` now carries the announcement into function slots). **Kernel: axiom A1 is tombstoned — the budget's first planned decrease, fourteen → thirteen** — with K1.5 and the register updated per the v0.198 tombstone discipline. Migration is the one-token edit the warning has recommended since v0.60; call sites are semantics-preserving by construction (the retired classification already treated these results as owned). Decided per 0048 Q1–Q6: direct-to-error (the warning was the deprecation, ~140 revisions of it); interface-typed returns included; §11.8 abstract statics and operators covered; the two-remedy diagnostic; heading and anchor kept.

**Train 2 — runtime `const` locals and `where T: sendable` (0049 trains A and B; train C is a currency finding).** *(A)* Local `const` admits any initializer, classified by form (new spec §21.1 subsection): a §17.14 constant expression of primitive/`string` type keeps compile-time-constant semantics; anything else is a **runtime const** — a single-assignment binding, excluded from compile-time positions, never an assignable location, never mutably capturable. The ownership ruling: a runtime `const` **rejects every owned-producing initializer** (`const` bindings never change state — not by assignment, consumption, or disposal; owned values bind with `using var`, the declared-disposal form). The payoff is normative in §7.4: a `const` local's narrowing is **never invalidated** — the invalidating forms are all compile errors on a `const` — making the field-copy idiom airtight. *(B)* §14.2 gains **derived-property constraints**, the general rule decided once as rationale §18 asked: properties admitted individually by recorded ruling, satisfaction = the §3.6 computation per instantiation, nothing inferred or propagated, no negated form; **`sendable`** is the admitted set's first member (contextual keyword, B.2), and stdlib §6.8/§6.9 now state in signatures what previously lived in comments (`where A: sendable, class` on the Spawn rows; `Channel<T> where T: sendable`), with the not-sendable diagnostic moving to the user's instantiation site as a component path. §12.5's decline of inference-driven Send/Sync typing stands untouched. *(C)* The mandated `Channel<T>.ReceiveAll` design **already landed in v0.186** — the deferred-list entry was stale, misleading two planning documents; the entry now carries its shipped marker, two behavior-neutral clarification sentences land in §30.15 (cancellation deregisters with the same no-loss guarantee; the consumer role releases on any enumeration-ending edge), and the spec-change checklist gains the same-revision §18-annotation rule this staleness motivated.

**Train 3 — labeled `break` and `continue` (0050).** A `while`, `for`, or `await for` statement may carry a loop label (`scan: for … do … break scan; … end scan;`); `break name;`/`continue name;` target the lexically enclosing labeled loop of the same callable body (spec §21.5, rewritten; §21.3/§21.4 pointers; grammar A.6 `LoopLabel` + closer alternatives; Appendix C bullets). The design is composition: a labeled loop is a **named construct** under §1.6's v0.170 umbrella rule — `end scan;` checked, `end for;` rejected on a labeled loop per the rule's own "otherwise", zero new closer rules; the label rides §29.2's desugaring onto the generated `while` with `continue` targeting the advance point (the increment on counted forms — never skipping an advance); and a labeled jump runs every exited scope's ordinary obligations in the v0.182 reverse-establishment order — **no disposal rule added or altered**. Labels live in their own namespace, do not shadow, and stop at callable boundaries (the lambda-boundary rule for unlabeled forms is codified in the same text). Declined: numeric break levels, labeling non-loops, labeled-block-as-expression (rationale §5.13 untouched), and `goto` (rationale §17.3 amended into the decision record — the decline stands). Decided per 0050 Q1–Q5: strict closers; `await for` included; the lambda-boundary clarification folded; no unused-label lint (a label buys a checked closer even unused).

**Kernel classifications (the v0.198 obligation):** Train 1 deletes axiom A1 (tombstoned). Train 2's `const` borrows enter K2/K5 as ordinary live local borrows (no new producer row); the ownership rejection derives from K1/K3 (a binding that can never discharge must never hold an obligation). Train 3 adds no ownership rule — labeled jumps are new starting points for the existing K3.15 unwind edges. No new axioms; the budget stands at **thirteen**.

**Migration.** Trains 2 and 3 are purely additive (no valid v0.200 program changes meaning; `Identifier ":"` at statement start parsed nothing before). Train 1 is source-breaking with an empty real inventory: every break site has carried the fix-bearing warning since v0.60, the stdlib migration is empty (sweep-verified), and call sites compile unchanged; the one second-order edit is retyping a function-typed slot storing a migrated factory reference. Spec-ahead-of-impl trackers filed at this landing for all three trains.

### v0.202 changelog (v0.201 → v0.202)

**The `pure` revision — proposal 0042 graduates (2026-07-19, owner-directed; #2029).** The language gains **pure members** (new spec §22.15): a declared, compiler-verified member modifier promising that a call writes no storage outside its own frames, performs no I/O, runs no user code through disposal, and touches no concurrency machinery — while remaining free to *read* anything (purity is deliberately not determinism). The closed rule set: reads of anything reachable; frame-local mutation under the value-typed-path root rule; value/record/enum/string construction and operations; defining (never invoking) function values; all control flow with `for` admitted per non-enumerator desugarings (the Range counted loop becomes normative inside pure bodies; `IEnumerable` sources rejected — index loops are the remedy); calls to pure-declared or pure-classified members only. Class construction is excluded except the **throw carve-out** (a trivial-dispose class with a pure constructor as the immediate `throw` operand — the two conditions make every dispose-after-arm inside a pure region provably a no-op); pure constructors carry the **birth-store rule**; auto-getters and qualifying record-synthesized members classify implicitly. Dispatch soundness is three matching rules: purity never dropped at overrides/implementations, may be strengthened (derived-surface-local), monotone down chains. `pure` occupies `async`'s modifier slot (mutually exclusive), is a contextual keyword (B.2), and is Core (new Appendix C.14). The stdlib first wave lands ~145 annotations (Math minus the constraint-dispatched `Min`/`Max`/`Clamp`; the `string` read surface incl. indexers and `operator +`; primitive `Parse`/`ToString`/`CompareTo` families and classification predicates; `Array<T>.Count`/`Capacity` and the `ReadOnlyStringSpan` read surface as index-loop enablers; the built-in exception `()`/`(message)`/`(message, paramName)` constructors as carve-out enablers — `(message, cause)` excluded, its snapshot builds an `Array`).

**Decided (0042 Q1–Q8 per its recommendations):** the throw carve-out ratified (Q1); the v1.5 widening recorded as the trivial-dispose admission variant, one cycle later (Q2); implicit classification of synthesized bodies confirmed (Q3); the `out` relaxation deferred with the `Result`-return alternative weighed against it (Q4); strengthening-only matching ratified (Q5); `pure` contextual (Q6); the enabler annotations ride this wave (Q7); no extern trust tier — to be designed jointly with contracts if ever (Q8).

**Declined (recorded in rationale §9.7 and proposal 0042 §16):** inferred purity (observations silently becoming obligations; body-dependent interfaces); effect polymorphism for v1; attribute-based purity; the strict no-carve-out throw rule; exact-match override purity.

**Migration.** Purely additive: `pure` appears nowhere as an identifier, no rule fires on unannotated code. Adding `pure` to a non-virtual concrete member is non-breaking; to a virtual/interface member, breaking (every override must restate) — the reason `IComparable<T>`/`IEquatable<T>`/`Object` roots stay unannotated. Removing `pure` is a breaking change like removing `owned` from a return. Spec-ahead-of-impl tracker filed at landing.

### v0.203 changelog (v0.202 → v0.203)

**The contracts revision — proposal 0043 graduates, stages 1 + 4 (2026-07-19, owner-directed; #2030).** The language gains **contract clauses** (new spec §22.16): `requires E;` / `ensures E;` between a method's or constructor's signature and body, and `invariant E;` as a class-body member. Clauses are `bool`, pure (the §22.15 discipline expression-wise, with `throw` and `await` additionally rejected), and borrow-only by construction — the guarantee assembled from existing classifications, not a new checker. Fixed evaluation points: `requires` after argument binding, before the constructor chain, declaration order, stop-at-first-failure, **always-on in every build mode** (the `Verify.That` posture — it replaces the always-on prologue idiom; elision-by-proof is the only elision); `ensures` on every normal-completion path, after result and `out`-slot binding, before scope-end disposals, never on throw exits, under **checked-contracts mode** (the §28.2 two-mode shape whose release relaxation is non-evaluation — defined behavior — not UB); `old(E)` desugars to hidden entry bindings under the ordinary §28.3 rules (value copies; class-typed operands as frame-resident borrows with the freeze/backstop composition; shallow, normatively stated, with the projection idiom recommended); `result` is a read-only borrow of the in-flight return value. **One violation exception**: the new built-in `ContractViolationException` (§31.4) — the `ArgumentException`-compatible alternative presented and declined with four reasons (rationale §9.8). **Tier-tracked**: every clause is proven / checked / assumed; discharge sites differ by kind (`ensures`/`invariant` at the declaring body; `requires` at every call site — `static requires` is a strong API demand restricted to caller-visible state); the initial prover floor is constant folds + §22.4's flow prover, with the extended fragment (linear integer arithmetic, null tests, closed-set case analysis incl. `choice`) fixed as the new **Contract proving** Appendix D.2 row so `static` never silently downgrades. **Slot-bound inheritance**: clauses inherited verbatim, never restated; overrides may add `ensures`, may not declare `requires`; multi-root `requires` combines by disjunction, `ensures` by conjunction. **Class invariants land whole** (stage 4): public-boundary instrumentation (public methods and setters entry/exit, most-derived-construction exit of any visibility; getters exempt with the residual recorded), the `this`-reentrancy exemption via checked/unchecked faces (statically decidable, virtual dispatch included), dynamic-class conjunction at dispatch, and the §22.7 composition. **The §22.4 retro-unification**: `when true`/`when false` is normatively a proven `static ensures` clause — the shipped prototype named as the instance it always was; surface form unchanged, zero migration, the caller-side narrowing now explained as proven-ensures consumption. Async methods take `requires` (synchronous prefix — violations surface on the caller's stack) and not `ensures` (the settlement design recorded in proposal 0043 §10.1, staged); iterators, accessors, operators, lambdas, extern: no clauses, each recorded liftable. Five new contextual keywords (`requires`/`ensures`/`invariant`/`old`/`result`; the `result` parameter-name collision resolved by ensures-scoped keyword-wins + call-site-invisible renames). New Appendix C.15. **No stdlib clause wave** (deliberate: converting documented `ArgumentException` prologues changes caught exception types — deferred to an owner decision); stdlib §2.17 gains the one cross-reference row.

**Decided (0043 Q1–Q11 per its recommendations):** the single built-in exception (Q1); no-knob always-on `requires` (Q2); the invariant instrumentation set and `this`-exemption (Q3); multi-root disjunction (Q4); the `when`-clause exact-match override rule retained (Q5); class-typed `old` admitted with the shallow warning (Q6); no stdlib conversions, with the `out result:` renames deferred alongside (Q7); the assumed tier reserved for the joint extern design (Q8); the clause-region marker-wins and final-clause-closes rules (Q9); extension methods in scope (Q10); per-call-site `static requires` discharge (Q11).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** contracts add no ownership rule and no axiom — clause reads are ordinary borrows (K1.5/K2), `old` captures are ordinary frame bindings under K2/K5, `result` is a borrow position, and the moved-from rejection at return edges is K1's state machinery. The budget stands at thirteen.

**Migration.** Purely additive; all five new reserved contexts are positions that do not exist in v0.202 programs. Adding clauses to non-virtual members is behavior-revealing, not behavior-changing; to virtual/interface members, a contract event with the recorded classifications (requires-added = breaking; ensures-added = strengthening; proven→checked = a flagged guarantee demotion). Spec-ahead-of-impl tracker filed at landing. Stages 2 (interface carriage — with 0044) and 3 (the prover) remain.

### v0.204 changelog (v0.203 → v0.204)

**Design change + clarifications, three trains (proposals 0044, 0045's normative deltas, and 0051 Part A graduate).** Spec §2.8.2/§2.8.3/§2.8.6/§8.3/§30.13, Appendix C.13; stdlib §1/§4.9; rationale §9.9, §12.1–§12.2, §12.11.

**Train 1 — contract carriage and the interface delta classification (0044; 0043's stage 2).** The artifact interface now carries, for every described member, its purity modifier and one **contract record** per contract clause (kind, `static` qualifier, canonical clause text, recorded enforcement tier), and per class its `invariant` records (spec §2.8.2, *Contract records*). Clause identity is **textual** with exactly two canonicalizations — comments/whitespace, and parameter/type-parameter positionalization — so a positional-only rename changes no record and any other re-spelling is a different clause. The recorded tier is **declaration-derived** — it is the clause's §22.16 tier: proven for `static`-qualified clauses (including the §22.4 family, which are `static ensures`) and for §22.16's constant-fold prover floor, checked otherwise — never what a compilation opportunistically discharged at a body or call site (as-if, §22.16) — and downstream static proof consumption requires the recorded proven tier. Records join §2.8.3 rule 3's agreement set (staleness backstop), while **type identity never includes them** (a contract delta is one type described inconsistently, not two types — §2.8.3). New **§2.8.6** fixes the normative delta classification: verdicts identical/preserving/widening/breaking, overload-identity member matching, the two-audience slot rule, the contract and signature delta tables (including the closed-world inversions: enum constants, choice cases, sealed-hierarchy leaves), the **layered verdict** for tier demotions (preserving at Core except the §22.4 family; breaking at the D.2 contract-proving level), and contract-opaque degradation. Appendix C.13 gains the agreement and demand-derived-tier invariants; rationale §9.9 records the reasons and the declined alternatives (semantic clause equivalence, redaction, contracts-in-identity, flat verdicts). Decided per 0044 Q1–Q10, following each recommendation with one recorded divergence — Q2's proven-tier set gains §22.16's constant-fold floor, a v0.203 landing 0044 predates: the fold is a declaration fact, so demand-derivation's purpose (body-independence) is preserved and the recorded tier equals the §22.16 tier for every clause. The rest: textual identity with the two canonicalizations (Q1); demand-derived tiers and the proven-tier consumption rule (Q2); the two-level layered verdict (Q3); §2.8.6 placement after §2.8.5 (Q4); §22.4-family detection by record shape, no carriage marker (Q5); contract-opaque degradation, never fabricated empty records (Q7); §22.6 overload identity as the match key, type changes reporting as remove-plus-add (Q10). The diff/extraction verbs and their exit-code surface (Q6/Q8/Q9) are tooling, recorded in proposal 0044 — the spec fixes the verdicts they must report.

**Train 2 — the determinism statement and its two supporting rulings (0045's normative deltas).** Spec §30.13 gains the *Determinism* subsection: a domain's execution is a deterministic function of what its **edges** deliver — scheduling decisions, runtime-mediated world interactions, and FFI boundary events — with exactly two exclusions (elapsed real time; foreign memory beyond declared writebacks). It adds no obligation on programs and no restriction on schedulers; it makes within-domain nondeterminism given fixed edges an implementation defect and is the foundation for record/replay tooling (proposal 0045, whose runtime design remains a tooling lane). Supporting ruling 1 (spec §8.3, decided per 0045 Q1): the identity-based default `GetHashCode` is **assigned on first request** from a per-domain deterministic sequence, never derived from addresses — programs keep only what was already promised (within-run stability), and the no-object-address invariant now extends through hashes. Supporting ruling 2 (stdlib §4.9): `OwningDictionary` iteration order is **deterministic given the operation-and-hash history** while remaining unspecified as an order — a determinism statement, not an order statement. The stdlib conventions (§1) gain the **replay intercept points** paragraph: the members that consult the world are enumerated as interceptable (record-and-substitute is unobservable except through values), everything else is deliberately not interceptable, and every future world-reading addition must declare itself an intercept point in its own section. Rationale §12.11 records the reasons.

**Train 3 — the producer-default guidance flip (0051 Part A; docs-only).** Rationale §12.2's decision tree is rewritten: the fan-out question is asked first (Pattern A when several consumers legitimately read the same result instance, or for chained republication), and **Pattern B (`OwningTask<T>`) is the default for every fresh, single-consumer class result — including plain data — and the when-in-doubt answer**, reversing the "when in doubt, choose Pattern A" guidance recorded through v0.203. The reversal's evidence: the affine model (v0.150) made the un-discharged-result failure mode a caught diagnostic in both patterns, dissolving A's conservatism argument; v0.190's calls-mint ruling equalized the caller's task obligation; B's consumer form is the one-line bind the corpus overwhelmingly writes; and the recorded stdlib surface has exercised the doubt-default toward B universally (no API started at A and widened, while three rulings — v0.184's owned locals, v0.186/v0.190's admissions — spent design budget easing A's consumer tax). The reversibility asymmetry stays recorded (A→B mechanical, B→A breaking); the flip re-weighs the start, with the one-line Pattern-A-façade sibling as the recovery (§12.1 gains the adapter sentence). **No semantics change**: no grammar, spec-rule, stdlib-signature, or compiler delta; spec §30.5's purpose-keyed producer guidance already agrees, and its optional restatement sentence is deliberately not added (0051 Q2, declined as redundant). Part B of 0051 (the `var x := await E;` deferred-disposal candidate rule) is **not adopted** — it remains a study gated on post-flip evidence.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no train touches an ownership rule. Contract records and the classification are interface metadata over declarations (clause expressions were already pure borrow-only reads, v0.203); the determinism statement is derived from serial execution and the recorded edges, minting no new ownership or scheduling rule; identity-hash assignment is runtime object metadata outside the obligation lattice; the guidance flip is docs-only. No new axioms; the budget stands at **thirteen**.

**Migration.** No source change is required or possible: every train is additive or docs-only, and no valid v0.203 program changes meaning. The one observable build event: the first rebuild of a module under a record-carrying implementation changes its interface bytes once (dependents recompile once; thereafter cutoff behavior is strictly better-informed, and pre-carriage artifacts degrade as contract-opaque rather than as empty record sets). Spec-ahead-of-impl trackers filed at this landing (carriage + classification; assigned identity hashes + OwningDictionary determinism; the replay runtime remains proposal 0045's tooling lane).

### v0.205 changelog (v0.204 → v0.205)

**Clarification, docs-only (rationale).** Rationale §5.5, §5.23, §5.26; new §5.27. No spec or stdlib rule changes.

**The standing decline record for binding-form unification (new §5.27).** Prompted by owner review of the binding-form surface, the recurring proposal "fold `using var` into plain `var` — ownership is inferred anyway" was examined against the full v0.204 rule surface, together with its sibling "fold `using var` into `const`" (the v0.201 owned-`const` alternative, revisited from the other direction). Both are declined, and §5.27 records the reasons as the standing answer: the keyword is a declared constraint on the binding's *future* (the A5 pin, the borrow-pin, the must-use-lint boundary), not an inference annotation — inference is total without it and always was; the lint and the keyword are one economy (the v0.150 affine trade presupposes a zero-ceremony declared-intent silencer); the binding forms are a loudness channel for borrowed↔owned API evolution; and "only `var`" is unreachable regardless, since asynchronous disposal cannot be inferred (`await using var`, `out using var`, and `TaskScope`'s await-using-only contract survive any retirement). The `const` seam holds from both directions: owned-`const` hides a real scope-end event behind the keyword whose claim is that nothing ever happens, and a `using var` doing `const`'s job forces pin semantics onto every fixed borrow (a `const` borrow's source-constraint deliberately ends at last use, §21.1). The record concedes with equal weight what the examination confirmed: the keyword adds no safety, the owned-versus-pin RHS dispatch is the area's one genuine reader ambiguity, and the residual `using var`/`const` overlap over inert right-hand sides is steered by diagnostics, not semantics (the vacuous-pin lint, #2073).

**Currency and cross-reference fixes.** §5.5's pre-v0.180 gloss ("`using var` is owned") is updated to the RHS-dispatched reality (owned over an owned producer; a scope-pinned borrow over a borrow, §28.10) — the staleness was flagged in the same review. §5.23's "moving out of a `using var` stays an error" gains the A12 cross-reference at source (the register's one recorded timing carve against the pin). §5.26 stops hardcoding the axiom count in the auditability claim (the register states its own count; the claim is the append/tombstone discipline).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rule changes. §5.27 re-affirms axiom A5 and the v0.201 §21.1/§28.10 division as decided; no new axioms; no derivations change. Implementation trackers filed alongside, not part of this revision: #2071 (unmarked `using var` adoption divergence, spec §28.10 v0.180), #2072 (single classification funnel), #2073 (vacuous-pin lint).

**Migration.** None — doc-only; no program changes meaning and no diagnostic changes in this revision.

Zero semantic delta — every rule keeps its id, its content, and its derivation tags; what changes is how many times each closed set is stated.

K4.2 is now the sole definition site: K3 gains a one-sentence family classification of its twelve rows (stores into announced owned destinations 1–4/12; ownership-taking kills and transfers 5–10, of which 5/8/9/10 are exactly K4.2's kills; displacement 11) with the rows themselves unchanged; K5.3 states the derivation (announced ∧ flag-backstopped ⇒ unfrozen) and points at K4.2 for membership; the freeze sub-block's boundary paragraph references K5.1–K5.4 instead of re-enumerating both placement lists. K5.1 absorbs the one fact that had lived only in the freeze sub-block's enumeration (the unmarked `Task`-family return of a non-`async` body is a frozen transferring kill, per K3.2). ### v0.207 changelog (v0.206 → v0.207)

**Design change — contract-clause surface syntax (proposal 0055 graduates).** Contract clauses are respelled with structural parentheses: `requires(E)` / `ensures(E)` / `static` variants, and the invariant member `invariant(E);` (the `;` there is the ordinary member terminator). A clause's parentheses are clause syntax, not expression tokens; a clause is self-delimiting and carries no terminator of its own. Grammar (A.4): `ContractClause ::= "static"? ("requires" | "ensures") "(" Expression ")"`; `InvariantDecl ::= "static"? "invariant" "(" Expression ")" ";"`; the interface body slots return to the uniform `ContractClause* ";"` — every member ends with `;`, clause-bearing or not — and every `MethodBody` alternative, the lone `;` included, is reachable at any clause count. What this deletes, by design: the body-less-closure rule ("a clause-bearing declaration ends at its last clause's `;`") and its reachability caveats; the redundant-`;` question entirely (a double `;` after clauses is now unspellable — the divergence #2070 reported becomes structurally impossible); the `; =>` seam on expression-bodied members; and the visual identity of clauses with body statements. The marker-wins clause-region entry rule (Appendix B.2) is unchanged. Contract records (§2.8.2) are unchanged: canonical clause text is the clause *expression's* token sequence, and the structural parens are not expression tokens — no artifact-interface migration exists for any clause in the corpus (all unparenthesized; a hypothetical fully-parenthesized v0.203 clause `requires (E);` migrates as `requires((E))` to preserve its record). Alternatives declined and the collision analysis (first-statement calls to a parameter named `requires`; the per-member-kind failure modes) are recorded in proposal 0055 §3/§8. Rules, tiers, evaluation, inheritance, carriage: untouched — this is a surface revision of v0.203's feature.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rule is touched; no kernel deltas.

**Migration.** Source-breaking for v0.203-syntax clauses, mechanically: `requires E;` → `requires(E)`, `ensures E;` → `ensures(E)`, `invariant E;` → `invariant(E);`; a clause-bearing body-less member gains the ordinary `;` terminator its clause list previously subsumed. The conformance corpus carries no clause-bearing cases at this revision (verified); the compiler's #2053 slice-1 parser and its tests are the tracked impl delta (issue filed at this landing; #2070 is superseded — the lenient acceptance it reported is unspellable under this grammar). Spec-ahead-of-impl until that lands.

### v0.208 changelog (v0.207 → v0.208)

**Design change — paren-delimited expression forms (proposal 0057 graduates; supersedes the postfix half of the #1373 ruling).** One principle lands across the expression grammar: **no expression-position compound value form is `end`-closed — each is paren-delimited; `end` closes statement blocks.** Four surfaces:

1. **The conditional** is respelled condition-first as a parenthesized PrimaryAtom — `(if c then a elif c2 then b else d)` — and the Python-style postfix `a if c else b` is retired. `else` is mandatory; every condition and branch derives a full expression, so a bare `throw` branch is admitted anywhere (the v0.182 true-branch parse trap is deleted, not repaired); `elif` chains replace right-nested postfix chaining; the conditional leaves the §17.1 precedence table (`throw expr` keeps the level-15 row) and §20's grouping/precedence paragraphs are deleted. In call- and index-argument position the atom supplies its own parentheses inside the argument list's (`f((if c then a else b))`) — the recorded ergonomic cost.
2. **Expression-position `case`/`when`** become paren atoms — `(case … of arm, …)` / `(when arm, …)` — with Expression-bodied arms only, no `end`, and no named closer. **Statement-position `case`/`when` are unchanged in surface and gain honest grammar**: new A.6 `CaseStmt`/`WhenStmt` productions carry the `end case?;`/`end when?;` forms and the Statement/`do … end` arm bodies that were previously position-gated semantically inside one shared production (statement position had reached statements only as an expression-statement over the atom). §19's preamble and §19.7 (*Termination*) are rewritten to the position-keyed closer story; interior syntax (`of`, `|`-alternatives, guards, the §35.5 `owned` scrutinee marker, trailing comma) is unchanged in both positions.
3. **The record update** is respelled with keyword-attached parentheses: `expr with(Name := value, …)` replaces `expr with Name := value, … end` — the assignment list reads as §22.5's named-argument list, and the suffix chains past its `)`. The `await for` header keeps today's content-based resolution, restated for the new spelling and now explicit (§9.5/§30.7): header-`with` followed by `(` `Identifier` `:=` is the update suffix on the source; any other `with` opens the cancellation clause.
4. **Ownership and semantics are untouched everywhere**: the K7 arm meet, the v0.184 arm rules and producers-table row, K8.3's case-scrutinee boundary ("the whole construct" — closer-agnostic wording, verified), exhaustiveness, `with`'s copy-not-construct semantics, §21.9's per-arm statement-position discard, and the common-type rule all re-key on the same constructs in their new spelling.

Rationale §3.3 is rewritten as the recorded reversal it is: the #1373 ruling's value-first preference is overturned by the same decider — one word order (retiring the #748 erratum class), `elif`, the throw-trap deletion, and a smaller precedence surface outweighing the value-first reading — with the paren delimiter as the genuinely new element that deleted the `end`-noise cost which had sunk the condition-first candidate at that ruling; the boolean-conditioned default-with-override now reading condition-first is the accepted residual cost. Full analysis, declined alternatives (bare Kotlin-style form; whole-expression `with` parens; C ternary re-affirmed), and the critique record are proposal 0057's.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rule changes — §28.3's producers row and §28.10's arm-meet prose are respelled, not re-ruled; no kernel deltas.

**Migration.** Source-breaking, mechanical in shape but not a token substitution: postfix conditionals rewrite to the atom (`x if c else y` → `(if c then x else y)`); bare expression-position `case`/`when` gain the wrapping pair and lose `end` (already-parenthesized ones only lose `end` — a blind `end`→`)` rewrite double-wraps); record updates become `with(…)`. Statement-position `case`/`when` and the statement `if` change nothing. The conformance corpus and the compiler are the tracked impl delta (issue filed at this landing; the corpus migrates **with the parser**, not before, so the conformance suite keeps testing the implementation it gates — the corpus drift already present in `spec_0101.bzl`/`stdlib_0039.bzl` (prefix-if without parens) and the stale A.7 snapshots in `spec_0288/0293.bzl` are noted on that tracker). Guide 01 re-validated (pin → v0.208); Guide 02 carries no affected forms (pin unchanged).

### v0.209 changelog (v0.208 → v0.209)

**Design change — the arm-position transfer marker (proposal 0056 graduates, as narrowed at critique).** The K3.4 marked-transfer family gains two value-producing positions: `owned x` — `x` a local binding or `owned` parameter — is admitted as an **if-expression branch** and as an **expression-`case`/`when` arm result** (the three mutually-exclusive expression-arm families; `when` arms are semantically identical to `case` arms for the meet and were admitted for parity at the composition gate), with **consume-if-selected** semantics: the marked arm is an owned producer for the construct's K7 meet; the binding is consumed on the path where its arm is selected and joins per [K7.4]'s existing maybe-consumed machinery after the construct (per-path scope-end disposal). The consume-site freeze applies unchanged — in particular, a `case` arm result marking the *scrutinee's own binding* is always rejected (the scrutinee borrow is live through the selected arm's completion, K8.3). §28.3's equalization Pattern 2 gains its one-expression form (`var x := (if useFresh then new Stream() else owned cached);`); the unmarked read of a named owned binding in any arm remains a borrow arm (K3.13 — no silent consume), now stated beside its marked counterpart in the producers table, §20, and §19.2.

**Grammar: the marker unifies as an atom.** A.7 gains `MarkedTransfer ::= "owned" Identifier` — a PrimaryAtom, additive since `owned` begins no other expression — with **positional admission enforced semantically**: the entire RHS of a binding or assignment (the v0.180 forms, whose grammar-slot `"owned"?` alternatives are deleted and re-derived as the atom at RHS root, meaning unchanged), an if-expression branch, or an expression-`case`/`when` arm result. Everywhere else — `??` operands, operator operands, guards, argument subexpressions — the atom is a compile error naming A7's narrowed bound. The call-site argument marker and the `case owned x of` scrutinee marker are separate productions, unchanged.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** a **derivation** — K3.4 gains the arm positions; evaluation and joins are K7.1/K7.4 verbatim; the freeze is K5.1/K8.3 verbatim. **Axiom A7 is narrowed, not retired**: its live content shrinks to the `??`-operand and operator-operand positions (the `??` lift is gated on the null-evaluated-transfer ruling proposal 0056 records — the post-state of a marked nullable binding evaluated while `null` is a genuinely new rule, not a derivation; operator operands remain unmotivated). The register stays at **thirteen** live axioms; rationale §5.26's A7 bullet records the narrowing.

**Migration.** Purely additive: no existing program changes meaning; the marked-arm spelling was a parse error through v0.208. Newly accepted: `owned x` in the two arm positions. Newly *expressible*: the one-expression coalesce of named owned locals (`return (if fast <> null then owned fast else owned slow);`) that previously required the statement equalization dance. Diagnostics may now name the marked-arm remedy at mixed-merge and borrow-escape rejections. Spec-ahead-of-impl tracker filed at this landing.

### v0.210 changelog (v0.209 → v0.210)

**Rulings + clarifications + editorial, one train (the 2026-07-21 language-improvement sweep's defect tier).** Spec §3.6/§9.2 (with §35.7), §7.4, §2.8.6, §20, §13.3, §11.5, §28.3 (K7 wording), §30.15, A.4 comments; stdlib §2.14, §6.9; new proposal 0060 (non-normative).

**Ruling — choices join the shared derived-property definitions (the v0.200 residual).** §9.2's admissible-component list gains the value-like auto-equality-bearing choice (recursively, the same list over every case's payload fields — the clause §35.7 had stated only locally); §3.6's auto-equality-bearing and serialization-eligible rows now name value-like choices; the equality-bearing row's record-only carve-out no longer accidentally classifies owning/borrow-bearing choices as equality-bearing (they are not — §35.7's rule, now consistent from every entry point). Strictly a contradiction fix: §35.7's classifications were already normative; §3.6/§9.2 now agree with them.

**Ruling — `not`-composition never establishes type-classification narrowing (codifying implemented behavior, probe-verified).** §7.4's fact-composition bullet now states its scope: the `not`-swap covers **null facts**; a type-classification fact is established only by `is`/`is not` and typed patterns directly — `not (x is T)` has the same truth value as `x is not T` and narrows neither branch, exactly as §17.4 already stated. The tension between the two passages is resolved in §17.4's favor.

**Ruling — the bare-`null` branch types (codifying implemented behavior, probe-verified).** §20: a bare `null` branch target-types to the nullable form of the other branches' common type (`(if c then s else null)` : `string?`); ownership was already §28.3's null-arm absorption; all-`null` arm sets are errors. Companion §7.4 completions: the narrowing-establisher list names the v0.208 atoms (each condition narrows its own branches; `(when …)` arm conditions narrow their arm bodies), and `x ??= expr` with a non-nullable `expr` is an assignment establisher.

**Clarification — the §2.8.6 uniqueness promise closes its two-row hole.** The `ensures`-added row now notes that a §22.4-family-shaped clause (detectable from the record alone) classifies under the `when`-added row, whose stricter slot verdict wins per the audience rule — one delta, one verdict, as §2.8.6 promises.

**Editorial.** K7's clauses 2–3 say "arms" like clause 1 (the meet's operands are arms everywhere). §11.5's canonical modifier order gains `scoped` in `owned`'s slot (mutually exclusive; the grammar always admitted it). The A.4 `pure set` comment names the real mechanism (does not parse — no `pure` slot on `set`); the IndexerDecl closer comment records the shared-production choice IfaceIndexer states structurally. §13.3 records why member visibility is explicit while file scope defaults. stdlib §2.14's `IDeserializable` promotion gate is renamed to its real blocker (the deferred `Self`-return type — static interface members exist since v0.176). The phantom "give-back-protocol RFC" citations in §30.15/stdlib §6.9 now point at a real artifact: **proposal 0060** (a consolidation stub; non-normative, no design decided). Examined and deliberately NOT done: the §28.3 producer-prose version-pin trim — the surveyed pins predominantly carry `derives:` kernel tags or qualifying content, i.e. load-bearing classification, not sediment; recorded here so the sweep finding does not recur.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rule changes; K7's wording edit is terminology only (the meet, its operands, and every verdict are unchanged); the derived-property ruling touches §3.6/§9.2/§35.7 classification, outside the obligation lattice.

Newly *consistent*: a strict §9.2/§3.6 reader now accepts the value-like-choice compositions §35.7 always granted (permissive widening; impl tracker filed for the compiler's §9.2-composition check if it followed the strict reading).

### v0.211 changelog (v0.210 → v0.211)

**Docs-only — the teaching train (the 2026-07-21 sweep's doctrine tier).** Guides 02/03; rationale §12.12; no spec-rule changes.

Guide 2 re-validated (pin → v0.211).

**New Guide 3 — Modeling Data.** The picking rules the reference prose defines but never collects: the five data kinds (enum / record / choice / class / sealed hierarchy) with the practice-boundary calls (enum-vs-choice, record-vs-class, choice-vs-hierarchy, choice-vs-`T?` per the recorded `Option<T>` decline); the three selection atoms with the three-sentence chooser and the arms-bind/exhaustiveness/meet notes; a one-line pointer to Guide 2 §6 as the failure-signal home (no duplication). Registered in the docs gate (`check_docs.sh`); the spec's introduction and CLAUDE.md name it.

**Rationale §12.12 — choosing the concurrency shape.** The structured-by-default doctrine and the fault fork stated once with adjacency: `WhenAll` collects and never cancels laggards; `TaskScope` supervises and cancels siblings; `WhenAny` selects and settles nothing; `FireAndForget` is the visible abandonment; `Domain.Spawn` is an isolation boundary, not a combinator. ### v0.212 changelog (v0.211 → v0.212)

**Design change — `Task.WhenEach` graduates (proposal 0023, accepted 2026-07-07, owner-confirmed 2026-07-21).** Stdlib §6.7 gains the streaming fan-in family: `WhenEach(Array<Task>)`, `WhenEach<T>(Array<Task<T>>)` (Pattern A — elements are already-completed borrowed tasks, delivered in completion order), and `WhenEachOwned<T>(owned OwningArray<OwningTask<T>>): IOwningAsyncEnumerable<OwningTask<T>>` (Pattern B — ownership transfers; unconsumed tasks disposed by the enumerator). The D1–D7 rulings land as drafted: completion-order delivery; faulted/cancelled tasks yielded, not skipped (per-task decisions, unlike `WhenAll`'s first-fault re-raise); observer-not-owner (the returned iterable is a deferred-activation frame carrying the input array's borrow — compiler-tracked, not a programmer promise); token cancellation stops enumeration only; both sequences affine per §29.11. Rationale §12.12's concurrency map gains the combinator.

**The #1813 input seam is documented, not resolved.** v0.190's calls-mint makes the dynamic borrowed-input idiom (`tasks.Add(GetXAsync(url))`) an abandonment — a seam `WhenEach` *shares with the shipped `WhenAll`*. The stdlib text states the discipline (named-binding builds for the borrowing forms; owning forms for dynamic fan-in) and cites #1813, which stays open as the joint input-side redesign for the borrowing family.

### v0.213 changelog (v0.212 → v0.213)

**Design change — axiom A8 (the transit exception) is retired; only owners dispose, with no exception.** The caller-vouched right to dispose element borrows obtained from a borrowing-family collection — and its bulk form, `DisposeElements()` — is deleted. The evidence gate the retirement was conditioned on (#2075) came back empty: the 2026-07 corpus sweep classified all 34 transit-regime occurrences and found zero load-bearing asymmetric clients — every real use was whole-collection-owned (migratable to the owning family's cascade), the values-owned dictionary shape is what `OwningDictionary<K, V>` expresses by construction, and the genuinely inexpressible direction (owned keys, borrowed values) has no client anywhere in the corpus. The kernel's headline rule is now carve-free: `Dispose()` requires an owned receiver (K3.10), through any borrow it is a compile error, full stop. Elements a holder owns belong in owning locations — the owning family cascades; selective or interleaved cleanup takes elements out first (`Drain()`, `move coll[i]`, the `Pop*` family) into owned bindings. Surfaces: spec §28.6 (the transit paragraph replaced by the exception-free rule), §28.9/§28.11 (tables, the BankAccount and asymmetric-dictionary examples rewritten to the owning forms), Appendix C.3; the register — **A8 → tombstone; twelve live axioms, two tombstones**; stdlib §4.x (the `DisposeElements` declarations and prose removed from `ICollection<T>`, `Array<T>`, `LinkedList<T>`, `Dictionary<K, V>`); rationale §5.1/§5.3/§5.26 updated to the retired state; Guide 1's three-one-line-rules paragraph loses its "lone exception" (pin → v0.213). The adversarial design record is the 2026-07-21 kernel review (candidate C8) plus the #2075 sweep, both run before this landing.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** an axiom retirement — no derivation changes; K3.10/K4 stand with strictly less recorded trust. The budget shrinks: twelve live axioms.

**Migration.** Newly **rejected**: explicit `Dispose()` on an element borrow read from a borrowing-family collection (indexer-get, iteration variable, dictionary-entry fields), and any call to the removed `DisposeElements()`. Remedies, per shape: whole-collection ownership → declare the owning-family type and let `Dispose()` cascade; selective disposal → take the element out first. The conformance corpus's transit cases (`spec_0214`/`spec_0215` mirrors) and the #1653 lit acceptance test flip to reject/migrated forms **with the compiler change**, tracked by the impl issue filed at this landing; #2075 closes as decided.

### v0.214 changelog (v0.213 → v0.214)

**Design changes, four trains, one composition-gated revision (proposals 0058/0059 graduate; two rulings).**

**Train 1 — `readonly` nullable fields narrow (0058).** §7.4's blanket field refusal keeps its premise and loses its over-reach: a `readonly` field has no writer outside §22.8's single-assignment window, so flow narrowing now tracks facts about it — keyed on exactly one field off an admitted root (`this`, a type name, a tracked local; any non-final field segment de-tracks the path), never invalidated by calls/`await`s/closures, inapplicable inside the (static or instance) construction window, and composing with §22.7's `this`-escape residual as inherited-not-enlarged (a mid-construction test sees the watermark — no fact — or the single final value). This deletes the copy-to-local ceremony for the injected-optional-dependency shape; mutable fields and properties are unchanged (rationale §6.1 updated). The critique's findings — the unstated single-segment rule, the static-construction window, the §22.7→§22.8 citation, the during-construction monotonicity reliance — are all resolved in the landed text.

**Train 2 — uniform trailing commas (0059).** §1.6 states the rule once — every comma-separated list admits one optional trailing comma before its closer, no exceptions — and Appendix A adds `","?` to all **eighteen** comma-list productions (the critique's exhaustive enumeration; the draft had missed seven, including choice-case payloads, positional patterns, extern parameters, and function-type parameter lists). Purely additive; `|`-alternative lists are not comma lists; no parse carve anywhere (verified: argument/`ref`/`out` lists, `>`/`>>` closers, the `","? ";"` enum/choice tails, single-parameter function types).

**Train 3 — the `hashable` constraint (ruling; the §14.2 one-property-one-decision mechanism).** `where T: hashable` joins the derived-property admitted set, mapping to §3.6's **equality-bearing** property (the property keeps its name; the keyword names the capability site — the hyphenated property name cannot be a source token, and `equatable` was rejected as both colliding with `IEquatable<T>` and misdescribing the property's breadth). Satisfaction is per-instantiation by §3.6 rule 2, carriage pre-exists (§2.8.2/§2.8.6 already name equality-bearing verdicts), and the admission follows the sendable precedent exactly — including landing one revision after v0.210 corrected the property's choice edges, which is deliberate sequencing, not accident. `hashable` joins B.1/B.2 as a contextual keyword.

**Train 4 — `readonly` on properties has one meaning (ruling).** `readonly` is written exactly where shape cannot express read-onlyness — auto-properties and interface properties; on every body-bearing form (expression-bodied properties and indexers, get-only blocks, the choice/enum/extension expression properties — all three grammar slots) it is a compile error, as it is on a setter-declaring block. The stdlib's thirteen decorative uses are stripped in this revision; the two normative documents now agree.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched (narrowing is the nullability system; the rest is surface/constraint machinery).

**Migration.** Newly **accepted**: narrowed reads of nullable `readonly` fields (permissive); trailing commas in the seventeen previously-forbidding lists; `where T: hashable`. Newly **rejected**: `readonly` on body-bearing property forms (thirteen stdlib strips land atomically here; user migration is deletion). Impl trackers filed at this landing.

### v0.215 changelog (v0.214 → v0.215)

**Design changes, two trains (proposals 0062/0063 graduate, critique-gated), plus one v0.214 seam fix.**

**Seam fix.** §14.2's "admitted set of this revision" sentence had not been updated when v0.214 added the `hashable` table row — the two statements contradicted. Fixed: the admitted set is `sendable`, `hashable`.

**Train 1 — the stdlib ergonomics batch (0062).** New **§4.20 `Counter<K>`** — the tally type and the first stdlib user of `where K: hashable`: unit-returning `Increment(key, delta := 1)` (creation-at-delta; the returning-count variant was rejected at design time because the canonical loop would draw §21.9's warning), non-`pure` `CountOf` (it compares via `K`'s equality — the same line that keeps every `Contains` non-pure), `ContainsKey` (present-at-zero vs absent), insertion-ordered `DictionaryEntry<K, int>` iteration, no auto-remove at zero, `Total` may go negative; §4.8's counting note now routes tallies here. Recorded honestly: a constrained-generic extension upsert was viable — the dedicated type is a design choice, and `Dictionary`/`Set` keep their structural key checks. Plus: `string.IndexOf(char|string, startIndex)` (code-point index, `0 ≤ start ≤ Length`, `IndexOf("", start) = start`); `String.Repeat(unit: string, count)`; `String.PadCenter` (odd padding goes right: `"ab".PadCenter(5) = " ab  "`) — with the previously-unstated `Repeat`/`Pad` contracts pinned for the existing members (negative count/width fault; `totalWidth ≤ Length` returns the original); `JsonDeserializer` options-ctor parity for `string` and `ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>` inputs; `Math.DivRem(a, b, out remainder)` for `int`/`long` (returns the quotient; not `pure` — §22.15 admits no `out` on pure members, and the tuple shape 0062 sketched does not exist; recorded); `Environment.GetInt`/`GetBool` (the convenience tier — absent and malformed deliberately conflate to `null`, recorded, the two-step idiom remaining the distinguishing form). **And the #2089 purity pass, corrected at critique**: `pure` lands on the *non-comparing* reads only — `Count` (including the `IReadOnlyCollection<out T>` slot, a **breaking-on-a-slot** purity addition per §2.8.6 forcing every conformer, acceptable at zero users and permanently forbidding caching `Count` implementations), `Capacity`, `Peek`, `First`/`Last`/`FirstNode`/`LastNode`, `FirstKey`/`LastKey` — twenty-six sites. `Contains`/`ContainsKey` stay non-`pure` everywhere, deliberately: they invoke user `Equals`/`GetHashCode`/comparers, which purity does not require of the equality contract; the library's own precedent (`Array.Contains` was never pure) is now the stated rule rather than an accident.

**Train 2 — the fluent-receiver discard exemption (0063, sharpened at graduation).** §21.9's warning now exempts a discarded **method-call** result that is a borrow sourced within the statement's receiver chain **and** of the receiver's static type — the `return this` fluent shape (`sb.Append(x);`), chained calls included. Both conditions are load-bearing (the type test keeps same-source *queries* warned; the method-call scope keeps accessor reads out), the base-typed-fluent case stays conservatively warned, `_ :=` remains, and owned results keep the full regime. The proposal's original source-set-only test was found over-broad at graduation and the sharpening is recorded in the proposal.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched — Train 2 consumes the existing K1.5 classification for a diagnostic; Train 1 is stdlib surface.

**Migration.** Newly accepted: everything in Train 1 (additive), the exempted fluent discards (a warning disappears). Newly required: `pure` on every `Count` conformance (stdlib-internal; zero external users). #2089 closes at this landing; impl trackers filed.

### v0.216 changelog (v0.215 → v0.216)

**Design change — the binding atom graduates (proposal 0061 §1; owner-deferred 2026-07-21, activated on the owner's direction 2026-07-22).** The `(var x := E; body)` atom joins the PrimaryAtom family (spec §17.15; grammar A.7 `BindExpr`): `(` + reserved `var` commits at the second token like the other paren atoms; each clause `var x := E;` (ascription admitted) introduces one single-assignment binding scoped to the later clauses and the body; the body is one full expression supplying the atom's value, type, and ownership classification; `;` is the separator (`in` collides with membership, `=>` with lambdas). The motivating position is the §22.16 contract clause — expression-only and pure, previously recomputing every twice-used subresult — with expression-position `case`/`when` arm bodies second; helper extraction stands as doctrine for multi-statement logic.

**Decisions this graduation fixed** (the proposal recorded the design; these were unstated and are decided here, each in the landed text): (1) clauses type exactly as §21.1 declaration statements — ascription, typed-context widening, bare-`null`-requires-nullable-ascription; (2) a binding is additionally **not an assignable location** (the §21.1 runtime-`const` rule), closing the `do`-bodied-lambda capture hole that "no statements inside the atom" alone leaves open; (3) duplicate names follow the §21.1 nested-scope rule; (4) a clause is a K3.4 *binding form*, so `var y := owned x;` inside an atom is the ordinary marked binding transfer; (5) the **body is not** a K3.4 marked-transfer position — an atom cannot transfer its own binding out as its result (recorded liftable, with A.7's other positional bounds); (6) the atom is not a §17.14 constant expression (all-constant admission recorded liftable); (7) in statement position the atom is an ordinary expression statement under §21.9's discard regime.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** one boundary-enumeration extension — **K8.5**: a binding whose initializer is an owned production is a *named unbound owned temporary* whose boundary is the **atom itself** (disposal at atom completion after the body, reverse clause order; exception-edge parity; K8.4's rejected-never-extended applied at the atom boundary — deliberately *tighter* than the enclosing full expression, so a borrow of an atom binding never outlives the name that made it legible). Everything else derives: clause borrows are K2, clause transfers K3.4, in-atom consumes K3, the atom's own classification is the body's (no join — clauses and body evaluate unconditionally, so no K7 meet arises). No axiom changes; A7's positional bounds gain the two recorded-liftable entries above. Surfaces: spec §17.1 (atom note), §17.15 (new), §19/§20 untouched, §22.16 (clause admission + the motivating example), §28.3 (producers row; named-temporaries paragraph), K8.5, Appendix A.7 (`BindExpr`/`BindClause`, MarkedTransfer commentary), Appendix C.3 (invariant row); rationale §3.12 (new) and the §5.13 addendum (the atom is not a block expression — §5.13's decline stands); no stdlib surface.

**Migration.** Newly **accepted**: the atom everywhere expressions are admitted, contract clauses included. Newly **rejected**: nothing that was previously legal (the form was previously a parse error — additive). Docs-only landing: the compiler does not yet implement §17.15 — the spec-ahead-of-impl delta is tracked by [#2098](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2098), filed at this landing. The proposal file and README flip at this landing: 0061 §1 superseded, §2 stays an evidence-gated study.

"lambda" "(" LambdaParams? ")" (":" Type)? "=>" LambdaBody`; `lambda` joins Appendix B.1's unconditionally reserved set): the reserved keyword commits the parse at its first token — the last major expression form with no committing lead joins the v0.208/v0.216 committed-reading family — and the form gains the one slot the old spelling structurally could not host, an optional **return-type ascription** behaving exactly as a declared method return (§5.1 widening, the v0.159 typed-context literal widening, the §20 null-arm target; a unit ascription spells a procedure lambda; against a target type it must agree under §27.1.1 — never a bridge). Everything else is deliberately unchanged: §27.4 parameter inference and destructuring, §27.5 capture, body classification, and the `->`-types / `=>`-values split. §27.3's divergent-return rule keeps its no-unification posture and gains the ascription as its third named remedy.
