### v0.220 changelog (v0.219 → v0.220)

**Clarification — §18.5's hole delimitation names its `<…>` edge and the decision to keep it ([#2102](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2102), owner-directed).** The 0064 audits surfaced that a multi-argument generic-arguments list at a hole's top level is cut at its comma (`{Cache<int, string>.Default}` — the alignment rule severs it; loud error, wrong-construct diagnostic). Decided: the rule stands as designed. Extending hole nesting to balanced `<…>` was **declined with reasons**: the generic-arguments reading of `<` is a parser-level commitment (§22.12's balanced-scan-plus-continuation rule), and v0.172's hole delimitation is deliberately a lexer-level boundary a tool can implement without a parser — importing the generic scan would destroy that property, and a naive balance-only test would silently re-cut legal holes (`{x < y,8}`, a comparison with an alignment). §18.5 now names the edge next to its existing parenthesization examples, states the remedy (`{(Cache<int, string>.Default)}`), and notes that single-argument forms are unaffected. Behavior is genuinely unchanged — the paragraph documents what the v0.172 rule already did — hence clarification class; the decision record is this entry. #2102 closes at this landing; the impl-side targeted diagnostic (a hole fragment ending mid-`<…>` should name this rule and the paren remedy) is tracked separately.

**Migration.** None — doc-only; the edge always behaved this way.

### v0.221 changelog (v0.220 → v0.221)

**General-language rulings train — eight delegated rulings, critic-gated (2026-07-24; owner-directed landing).** A batch of underspecified/contradictory cases in the module, pattern, serialization, statics, and control-flow sections, each ruled with its own adversarial critique and each shipping a spec-cited regression test at implementation time. One design change (#2133), one warned-admission ruling (#1393), the rest clarifications and one-passage decisions.

**Duplicate plain imports are idempotent (#1788, §2.2).** A duplicate plain `import` of an already-imported module adds nothing and is not diagnosed — an import is a visibility effect, not a declaration, so there is no name to collide (the deduplicate-not-diagnose posture §2.8.1 rule 3 already states for repeated artifact presentation). **Declined:** making it a compile error (breaks mechanical file concatenation and generated code for no soundness gain) and mandating a warning (the spec mandates warnings only where load-bearing; a redundant import is at most a lint). Alias declarations stay the exception — a repeated `import A as X;` is the existing alias-collision error, because an alias *is* a name declaration. The compiler already accepts the plain-import shape; §2.2's alias-vs-alias collision rule the closing sentence cites is unenforced at HEAD, tracked #2179.

**Set/dictionary literal duplicate-handling asymmetry stated (#1789, §15.4).** One passage records, at the set-duplicates paragraph, why a statically-detectable duplicate dictionary key is an *error* while a duplicate set element *collapses* (a duplicate key silently discards a value expression; a duplicate set element discards nothing — collapsing is what a set means), and why sets retain the *first* occurrence while dictionaries take the *last* value (first-retention makes the `Set<T>` insertion-order guarantee coherent; a dictionary literal reads as a sequence of insertions with the indexer's last-write-wins upsert). **Declined:** harmonizing either behavior (both are correct for their type's semantics; harmonizing trades a defensible asymmetry for a regression or a footgun) and putting the note in the rationale (this is a reading aid for two adjacent normative rules — it belongs where the reader is). Neither behavior changes.

**"Leaf type" defined for concrete non-sealed intermediates (#1821, §19.6).** A *leaf type* in the sealed-hierarchy exhaustiveness bullet is **every concrete (non-`abstract`) class in the closed set** — including a concrete class that itself has subclasses, because its exact-runtime-class instances exist; a leaf is *covered* when some unguarded type pattern it is assignable to matches it (subtype matching), so an arm for a concrete intermediate also covers its concrete descendants. Abstract members have no instances and need no arm. **Declined:** the childless-only reading (unsound — a claimed static proof with a reachable `MatchFailureException`) and forbidding concrete non-sealed intermediates (a new restriction on legal declarations to spare a two-sentence definition). The implementation already treats every concrete class as a leaf and counts coverage by assignability; the term was simply undefined.

**Unboxed value scrutinee vs. reference type-test pattern (#1984, §19.3).** A type pattern over an **unboxed value-typed scrutinee** is a **static** test: over a non-nullable value scrutinee a pattern naming its exact type always matches, and a pattern naming any *reference* type (a class, an interface — including one the value type implements — `string`, or `Object`) is a compile error — the pattern could never discriminate at runtime, and matching it would require an implicit boxing conversion, which pattern position never performs. To test a value against an interface it implements, box explicitly via an `Object`-ascribed binding (`var o: Object := p;`) and match `o`. **Declined:** auto-boxing the scrutinee for interface patterns (adds zero discriminating power — the outcome is statically decided — while introducing a hidden heap allocation and owner-less temporary, and creating always-true arms that silently kill later arms) and accept-with-warning. Affirms the shipped #801/#1936 posture; "subtypes match" (§19.3) is scoped to reference-typed scrutinees, not contradicted.

**Value-like choices are record-admissible for serialization (#2120, §9.8 + Appendix C).** A value-like, serialization-eligible choice is record-admissible — as a choice payload field and as a serialized record/class component. The §9.8 record-admissibility list, the component-eligibility list, and Appendix C's mirror are extended to name it. **Declined:** the strict-list reading (contradicts the "value-shaped storage throughout" criterion both list sites already state and §9.2's admission of value-like choices as equality components, and would disable shapes the shipped #2046 suite pins) and a split reading (payload-but-not-component). Clarification class — the criterion is unchanged; the closed enumeration is brought up to date with the v0.200 type it predated. The component-eligibility edit reaches the full component surface (class components and collection elements), matching the implemented behavior. #2046 is confirmed; the one missing pin (choice-typed record component round-trip) lands with the delta.

**Statement-`case` totality extended to bool and sealed hierarchies (#2133, §21.7 — design change).** A statement-position `case` counts as exiting on every path — a callable may end with it, no trailing `return` — when (i) §19.6 proves it exhaustive by a **closed-value-space** proof (irrefutable-arm, choice, bool, or sealed-hierarchy bullet, or their nullable composition with an explicit `null` arm) and (ii) every arm's body diverges. The irrefutable-arm clause covers both `_` **and** an unguarded untyped `var` binding, closing the match over **any** scrutinee kind — the `var`-spelled catch-all is newly granted here (previously only `_`), an expansion beyond the filed bool+sealed question, adopted because §19.6 states the two spellings as one proof and granting one and not the other repeats the same asymmetry this ruling rejects. The **enum** constants-coverage proof never grants totality (a non-constant cast `E(n)` yields a raw value matching no declared constant — the no-match edge stays reachable). The proven-dead no-match edge is lowered as a defined trap (`MatchFailureException`/abort), so the grant's soundness never rests on the exhaustiveness computation alone. This supersedes the v0.196 N6 posture ("totality must not key on the exhaustiveness proof") exactly for closed-value-space proofs. **Declined:** affirming N6 for bool/sealed (preserves an indefensible bool-vs-choice asymmetry #2129 created, and keeps the silent cross-module fall-through failure mode for sealed matches), a bool-only/sealed-split extension, and extending to enums (unsound). Presupposes #1821's leaf definition (same revision). The sealed grant improves the cross-module failure mode: an upstream leaf addition now surfaces as a loud §21.7 error on recompile rather than a silent fall-through.

**Mutable value statics admitted with a warning (#1393, §22.12 rule 2 — warned-admission ruling).** Rule 2 gains two admitted forms beyond the v0.181 warning-free pair: **form (iii)**, a mutable static of primitive/enum type (nullable forms included) or — fields only — a plain heap-free inline array of recursively form-(iii) element type, admitted with rule 4's declaration-site warning; and **form (iv)**, a mutable owning-inline-array static field (`[N owned]T?`/`[N owned]T`), the admission §22.13/§11.7 already made in v0.181, named inside rule 2 so its "exactly two forms" sentence and that disposal machinery agree, likewise warned. Form (iii) is the violation-tolerant category (no reference content, so ignoring the warning risks stale/torn values, never memory unsafety) and carries none of the store-semantics triple and no memory-model publication edge; form (iv)'s obligation violation is full UB (rule 4's class), which is why it is warned not silent. **Declined with reasons, liftable only by later recorded ruling:** mutable statics of `string`(-bearing), record, choice, and value-builtin types, plain inline arrays of any other element type, and inline-array-typed auto-properties stay compile errors — a mutable string static's overwrite forces either a cross-domain reclamation race (UAF) or an unbounded never-release leak, and torn record reads fabricate invariant-violating values (a hazard bare heap-free inline arrays lack). Also declined: full enforcement with an `AtomicInteger` migration (contradicts the rule-4 and §22.13 warning-not-error precedents and taxes single-domain programs that cannot race), silent admission (falsifies §30.14 with no named obligation), and scoping the error to domain-spawning programs (a whole-program property against the decidability principle). Rationale §12.7 gains the recording; §30.14's residual sentence and the rationale's fork-closure residual now name the form-(iii)/(iv) statics.

**Chain-head member vs type resolves by position, not meaning (#2125, §2.7).** Inside a type's body a bare name that could denote an accessible enclosing-type member or a same-named type resolves by the name's **syntactic position**: a **chain head** (`Color.Red`, `Registry<int>.M()`) consults members *last, after aliases* (a type wins the head, so the `property Color: Color` self-naming idiom survives cross-module); **every other head** — a value read, an assignment target, a bare callee (explicit method type arguments included), a `?.`/`!`-continued head — consults members *between local scope and the module's declarations* (a member wins). A shadowed member stays reachable by `this.`/type qualification; a shadowed type via module qualification. The compiler **warns** when a chain head resolves to a type shadowing a same-named enclosing-type member of a *different* declared type (suppressed when the member's type is the resolved type or an instantiation of the resolved generic). **Declined:** C#'s Color-Color dual-meaning rule (backtracking on semantic failure — against §2.7's recorded "leftmost-first, type-wins, no backtracking" design) and uniform member-first or type-first (each breaks a pinned idiom). Ratifies the shipped #2097/#2126 behavior across the whole head surface; the mandated warning is the one new obligation.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules touched — #1393's forms hold no references and mint no disposal obligation (form (iv)'s disposal is the existing §22.13 exit-pass machinery, v0.181); the rest is name resolution, patterns, serialization eligibility, and control-flow totality.

**Migration.** Newly **accepted**: duplicate plain imports (#1788); exhaustive all-diverging bool/sealed statement-`case`s without trailing returns, and all-diverging `var`-catch-all case statements (#2133); value-like choices as serialized record/class components and choice payload fields (#2120). Newly **warned** (once enforcement lands): mutable primitive/enum/heap-free-inline-array statics and owning-inline-array static fields (#1393 forms (iii)/(iv)) — warnings are inert to the AOT harness, so the counter idiom (~800 corpus declarations) keeps compiling; and a chain head resolving to a different-typed shadowing type (#2125). Newly **rejected** (once enforcement lands): mutable statics of `string`(-bearing), record, choice, value-builtin, function-typed, generic-parameter-typed, and residual inline-array types (#1393 — previously silently admitted, none in the corpus outside test scaffolding); an upstream leaf added to a closed hierarchy relied on by a total sealed `case` statement turns into a §21.7 error on recompile (#2133, intended — leaf addition is already §2.8.6-breaking). Doc-only / behavior-unchanged: #1789, #1821, #1984, #2125's resolution order (the warning is the only new behavior). Spec-ahead-of-impl deltas and the per-ruling regression pins are tracked by the impl issues named in each ruling record (#1393 enforcement; #2179 alias-collision; #1936/§19.3 diagnostic; #2125 shadowing warning; #2133/#2129 stmtAlwaysExits; the #2120 record-component pin). The conformance corpus carries no example flips from this train (no rejected shape is a committed case); example-touching migrations are enumerated per ruling.

### v0.222 changelog (v0.221 → v0.222)

**Standard-library rulings train — nine delegated rulings, critic-gated (2026-07-24; owner-directed landing).** A batch of stdlib-surface decisions: reflection/metadata contracts, span-pipeline completions, collection-family coherence, one handle-API shape conversion, and one async-input seam resolution. Mostly additive; two design-shaped changes (the `Owning{Stack,Queue}` demotion and the `Weak<T>.TryUpgrade` conversion), each with the migration stated below. The spec-side companions (§17.10, §28.11, §28.13, §30.15, Appendix C) land atomically with their stdlib halves.

**`char` gains `IParsable<char>` witnesses; `bool` stays out (#1792, stdlib §9.5 + §2.19).** §9.5 `Char` declares `Parse(s: string): char` / `TryParse` with **one-code-point** semantics — `Parse` yields the sole code point of a length-1 string and raises `FormatException` for every other input (empty, multi-code-point; no whitespace tolerance, no escape recognition — escapes are source-lexical), `TryParse` returning `false` where `Parse` raises with the out slot `'\0'`. These are the previously-missing §2.19 `IParsable<char>` conformance witnesses (the witnessing sentence was false for `char`). `bool` stays out of §2.19 — recorded: its `Parse`/`TryParse` are plain static members, the constraint's clients are generic scalar-parsing paths, and a later admission would be a compatible widening. **Declined:** calling char's witnesses compiler-intrinsics with no declared members (leaves "which strings parse" undefined and contradicts the shipped direct `char.Parse` surface) and admitting `bool` (no use case, an existing exclusion pin). The implementation already ships these semantics; the direct-`char.TryParse` sema gap is tracked.

**Reflection metadata contracts pinned before the renderer exists (#1805/#1812, stdlib §2.13 + §2.4 + spec §17.10).** `Type.EnumNames`/`EnumValues` and `Environment.CommandLineArgs` retype from `Array<T>` to **`IReadOnlyList<T>`** read-only views over the cached process-lived storage (#1805): the entire mutation surface is removed at compile time, the handed-out object is a **dedicated view class** (the §4.8/§4.9 `Keys`/`Values` shape, backing included) so a §12.7 downcast (`view as Array<string>`) cannot recover mutation — it yields `null`. And `Type.Name`/`FullName` gain a **normative byte-exact rendering contract** (#1812): the canonical source-level type expression, `Name` unqualified / `FullName` module-qualified, recursing uniformly through generic arguments, inline-array elements, and function-type components; keyword-aliased types render as their lowercase keyword in both; **top-level nullability is erased at reification** (no `Type` for a nullable form; `typeof(T)` at `T = U?` returns `typeof(U)`), while nullability *inside* a composite renders. The §17.10 identity paragraph is amended in the same revision (mandatory companion): substitution distinctness scoped "up to top-level nullability", the `U?`→`U` reification stated where the contradicted promise lived. **Declined:** `Array<T>` + a documented programming-error caution (a removable process-wide-corruption hazard), `FrozenArray<T>` (over-commits storage), bare-head `Name` for generics and System-qualified primitives (collide `Type` identities, contradict the diagnostic surface), and distinct nullable `Type` tokens (witness-free). Both surfaces are unimplemented (reflection deferred, #487) — the ruling binds the future implementation at zero migration cost.

**`Channel<T>.Close()` — receiver-initiated graceful close (#1807, stdlib §6.9 + spec §30.15).** A new `Close()` on `Channel<T>` puts the channel in the same closed state as last-sender dispose: buffered items remain receivable, an active `ReceiveAll` completes normally after the tail, subsequent `Send`/`SendAsync` fault with `ChannelClosedException` (disposing the offered item first, the v0.184 rule; a pending `SendAsync`'s item is disposed and its task faulted), and the call is idempotent. No give-back — the failed-send edge keeps its recorded dispose posture; the give-back family stays deferred to proposal 0060. Additive; no kernel surface, zero axiom spend.

**Span-pipeline decode/consume completions (#1809/#1810, stdlib §3.1/§3.2/§4.14/§9.1–§9.3).** `Encoding.GetString` gains `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` and `ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>` source overloads (#1809 — same fault model, BOM only at the span start, empty span → `""`, call-bounded borrow), completing the v0.165 span-destination encode pair in the decode direction on both byte-span families. And the span *consumption* family lands (#1810): `ReadOnlySpan<T>.ToArray(): owned Array<T>` for **non-borrow-bearing value T** (a borrow-bearing element type is rejected at the call site per §3.6 rule 2 — the exclusion keeps the escape analysis honest without cross-call borrow-source propagation; class-typed T is deliberately absent — consume with `move span[i]`); numeric `Parse`/`TryParse(ReadOnlyStringSpan)` on `Int32` (and the analogous pairs on `Double`/`Float`/`Decimal`, the "others have analogous shapes" sentence carrying the rest of the integer tower) — identical contract to the string forms, no substring materialized, `IParsable<T>` unchanged; and `StringBuilder.Append(ReadOnlyStringSpan)`. Additive; both rulings note live over-accept miscompiles the impl fix must repair (span-`GetString` malformed IR; `int.Parse(span)` wrong answer; `sb.Append(span)` malformed IR).

**`OwningStack<T>`/`OwningQueue<T>` demoted to `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`; borrowing forms regain `Clear()` (#1811, stdlib §4.11 + spec §28.11 + Appendix C — design-shaped).** The owning twins conform to `IReadOnlyCollection<T>` only, completing for them what v0.165 (#1354) did for the borrowing forms — `Add`/`Remove`/`IsReadOnly` had no LIFO/FIFO semantics and owning `Remove`'s dispose-the-removed contract would make middle-removal irreversible; owned ingress is `Push`/`Enqueue`, egress `Pop`/`Dequeue`/`Try*`/`Drain`, bulk disposal `Clear`, plus an explicit `Contains` (the v0.165 pattern). The borrowing `Stack<T>`/`Queue<T>` regain `Clear()` (lost collaterally in the v0.165 demotion): it drops references and disposes nothing (borrowing-family rule). The spec §28.11 owning-collections bullet, the owning-signature survey intro, and Appendix C's owned-element invariant are scoped so their `Add`/`Remove`/indexer ascriptions no longer over-claim the demoted twins. **Declined:** keeping the `IOwningCollection<T>` conformance (its `Add`/`Remove` are semantically empty on order-disciplined collections). No kernel change — a surface reshape inside axiom A9's columns; zero axiom spend.

**`Weak<T>.TryUpgrade` converted from Try shape (a) to shape (b) (#1535, stdlib §2.16 + §1 + spec §28.13 — breaking on the out-parameter form).** `TryUpgrade(out owned s: Shared<T>?): bool` becomes `TryUpgrade(): owned Shared<T>?` — the handle payload is statically non-nullable at every instantiation, so the bool carried no information and null alone signals failure (the `Mutex.TryAcquire` acquisition idiom). The §1 convention moves `Weak<T>.TryUpgrade` from the shape-(a) enumeration to the shape-(b) sentence. **Declined:** freezing the status quo (leaves the stdlib's one standing violation of its own §1 taxonomy), renaming to `Upgrade` (an unprefixed null-signaling fallible API would be a one-method convention), and converting `Channel<T>.TryReceive` too (self-defeating). No kernel change — the ruling moves one API between two existing K-derived surfaces; the `out owned` derivation stays in force for every remaining `out owned` surface. **Migration:** `if w.TryUpgrade(out using var s) then …` → `using var s := w.TryUpgrade(); if s <> null then …`. Breaking for callers of the out-parameter form; no other Try API changes shape.

**WhenEach/WhenAll borrowing-input seam resolved-and-closed (#1813, stdlib §6.7).** The v0.212 landing's two spellings — named task bindings for statically-known borrowed fan-in, the owning family (`OwningArray<Task<T>>`/`WhenAllOwned`/`WhenEachOwned`) for dynamic fan-in — are the **complete** input-side story for `WhenEach` and `WhenAll` alike. A borrowing-family dynamic-build facility is **declined** as a design goal: a fresh mint's obligation must have a holder, and in dynamic fan-in the only candidate holder is the collection itself, which is exactly the owning family. The §6.7 bullet's "#1813 remains tracked" tail is replaced with the resolution; #1813 stays open only as this delta's landing tracker. **Declined:** keeping it open pending proposal 0060's give-back work (tracks nothing actionable), a borrowed-build facility with compiler-extended temporary lifetime (an invisible ownership transfer against the reject-not-extend posture), and owning-semantics overloads on borrowing types (still holderless). No kernel budget spent; the admitted-but-hazardous `Add(fresh-mint)` shape stays a recorded K2.3-second-arm admission (impl gaps #1881/#1655).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rules changed — #1807's `Close()` consumes/borrows/returns nothing beyond an ordinary receiver borrow; #1811 is a surface reshape inside A9; #1535 moves one API between existing K-derived surfaces; #1810's `ToArray` is a source-free owned production (borrow-bearing elements excluded at the call site); the rest is metadata and additive value-type surface. Axiom register unchanged: twelve live axioms, two tombstones.

**Migration.** Newly **rejected** (breaking): callers of `Weak<T>.TryUpgrade(out owned s)` migrate to the nullable-return form (#1535); `OwningStack<T>`/`OwningQueue<T>` `Add`/`Remove`/`IsReadOnly` and their `IOwningCollection<T>`-typed assignment become member-not-found/conformance errors once enforcement lands (#1811). Newly **accepted / additive**: `char.Parse`/`TryParse` (#1792); `Channel<T>.Close()` (#1807); `Encoding.GetString` span overloads (#1809); `ReadOnlySpan<T>.ToArray`, numeric span `Parse`/`TryParse`, `StringBuilder.Append(ReadOnlyStringSpan)` (#1810); borrowing `Stack<T>`/`Queue<T>` `.Clear()` and owning-twin `Contains` (#1811). **Retype / contract** (source-compatible for reads, mutation removed): `Type.EnumNames`/`EnumValues`, `Environment.CommandLineArgs` → `IReadOnlyList<T>` (#1805); `Type.Name`/`FullName` rendering pinned (#1812) — both unimplemented, binding future work. Conformance-corpus note: the §2.13 mirrors (`spec_0083`/`stdlib_0012`/`stdlib_0013`) and §2.4 mirror (`stdlib_0003`) carry the `Array<...>` typing and update **with** the reflection implementation (`stdlib_0013`'s `.Length`→`.Count` drift noted); no committed case flips at this landing. Spec-ahead-of-impl deltas and per-ruling regression pins are tracked by the impl issues each ruling names (span-consumption over-accepts; `char.TryParse` sema gap; `Channel.Close`; the demotion enforcement; the `TryUpgrade` retarget; #1881/#1655 for the WhenEach input gaps).

### v0.223 changelog (v0.222 → v0.223)

**Ownership/async-kernel rulings train — one composition-gated revision (2026-07-24; owner-directed landing).** Seven delegated, critic-gated rulings in the §28/§30 family, landed together and cross-checked at the seams (the composition gate of the spec-change process): the two ownership-kernel contradictions #2043/#2042, the launder-family fences #1802/#1819/#1820, the terminal-move defect #1814, the discard-await admission #1826, and the iterable-interface frame-ownership ruling #1787. Every ruling states its kernel classification; the axiom register is unchanged — **twelve live axioms, two tombstones** — every ruling a derivation, no axiom added or retired.

**§28.6 owned-field store/argument prohibitions reconciled to §28.3's one rule (#2043 kernel ruling).** §28.6's two pre-history absolutes — "an owned field's value may not be assigned to a non-owned field of any other class" and the argument-tail "may not store the reference in a long-lived location" — were surviving corollaries of a premise the spec **repealed at v0.142** (erratum #717, when §28.3's blanket no-borrow-in-fields rule was found to contradict §28.5's own `_owner` back-reference and §9.8's serialization synthesis). They are rewritten to route the case through §28.3's borrowed-field store rule: an owned field's value reaches another object's non-owned class-typed field only as a **borrow**, classified by the holder's kind (receiver- and parameter-rooted paths admissible, scope-bound-local- and temporary-rooted rejected), carrying §28.3's recorded K4.3 trust and K4.1 backstop, with the obligation stated sharply for the owned-field case (the storing side vouches for the field's *current value*, which drop-on-overwrite or `move` may end before the holder). The argument sentence becomes an ordinary parameter-sourced-borrow statement (store admitted only where §28.3 admits it — the §28.5 idiom); transfer takes the explicit `owned`/`move` forms. The transfer bullet (D3 rider) is tightened, and Appendix C.3's "of another object" tail is dropped. **Declined — Option 1 (keep categorical, record as a new axiom A15):** no soundness gain (same backstop, no leak/double-free delta), unenforceable at the callee seam without repealing v0.142, launderable through one call or one alias, and its recorded reason would have to argue against the project's own v0.142/v0.180/v0.186 record. Kernel: derivation K1.5/K9.1 + K2.3 + K4.3/K4.1; no axiom. **Zero compiler delta, zero test flip** — the compiler has never implemented the categorical sentences.

**§30.5 await-operand admission extended to task field-paths of non-`this` objects (#2042 kernel ruling).** The Pattern A operand list's field bullet — previously "an `owned` field of `this`" only — is generalized to **a task-typed field path rooted at any live object** (`await b._t` where `b` is a borrowed local/parameter; a plain task-typed borrow field), and the list preface's non-exhaustiveness is made principled: its closure is K2's named-location taxonomy (a task-typed storage read through any field path rooted at a live object, plus a borrowed alias of any admitted operand). The source set is the path (K2.1/K2.2), carrying the existing frame-held/true-task-outlives-use residuals — no new trust clause. **Declined — reject and close the enumeration:** contradicts v0.95's recorded reframing of the list as non-exhaustive and the #1533/#1800 precedent line, and is incoherent (one alias `var tt := b._t; await tt` is already admitted by the v0.193 plain-borrowed-local bullet — a direct-form reject would police spelling, not lifetimes). Kernel: derivation K1.5 + K2 named-location + K2.1/K2.2 + existing K4.3 residuals; no axiom. The owned-field-path shape is already compiler-accepted; the plain-borrow-field sub-case is the tracked impl delta (with a probe-found pre-existing displacement-backstop leak, orthogonal, tracked separately). Composition with #2043 was gate-checked over a shared object graph and composes cleanly.

**Terminal `return move x.f;` has no dispensation; the §28.6 example is fixed (#1814).** The field-restoration rule (§28.8.1/K9.2) is stated to admit **no terminal-move dispensation**: a `return move x.f;` with no restoring assignment before the exit is rejected, the return edge being itself an unrestored exit. The §28.6 `TakeTransactions` example (which returned on the very line it moved, contradicting its own comment) is rewritten to the build-before-take shape; Guide 1 §6's mirror rides the same fix. **Declined — sanction the terminal return (option a):** unsound — moved-from is per-method-body-static with no runtime representation for a non-nullable field, so the receiver's destructor would double-free the transferred value and later methods would read a hole (the K9.4 reasoning that already bans static-field moves). Kernel: pure derivation K9.1–K9.5, no axiom. The compiler already enforces the reject; the corrected positive example is gated on a pre-existing owning-collection-field `move` miscompile (impl tracker filed).

**`_ := await t;` is an owned-consuming context for a Pattern B task (#1826, §30.5).** The explicit discard `_ := await t;` is admitted for an `OwningTask<T>` await — the discard is a K3 owned-consuming position (§17.13, elevated to the announced-kill family at v0.184), disposing the awaited result at the end of the statement as an unbound owned temporary, the end-of-statement counterpart of `using var _ := await t;`. §30.5's "an `await` whose result is discarded" is reworded to mean the *silent* bare-statement `await t;`, which stays a compile error. **Declined:** keeping the reject (contradicts §30.5's own "the contexts are K3's owned-consuming positions", §17.13's universal discard-disposal contract, and K4.2's closed announced-kill set — a carve with no soundness content), and relaxing the bare-statement form (that IS the silent owned-result drop the error exists to prevent). Kernel: derivation K1.5 + K3.9/K4.2 + K8.1; A6 untouched.

**Static-getter borrow admission widened across the admissible static field forms (#1819, §28.3/§28.6/Appendix C).** §28.3's callee-side static-getter admission — previously "a bare read of a `static` `owned` field" — is widened to any admissible static class-/interface-typed field (`owned`, §22.13-exempt `readonly` without `owned`, or a §22.12-rule-2 admitted mutable static), all three process-lived to exit; a new *Static field access `T.f`* producers row (the caller-side twin of `T.P`) is added. The stdlib's own `Encoding.UTF8/…` singletons (declared `readonly`, not `static owned`) were admission-orphaned by the `owned`-only wording; this closes the letter-vs-implementation gap (the compiler's getter paths never inspected the field's ownedness). **Declined:** ruling the absence (would invalidate the §22.13 singleton pattern and flip an existing accept pin), and re-admitting static *methods* (the v0.196/v0.201 signature-indistinguishable-from-factory reason is field-form-independent and stands). Kernel: derivation K1.5 + K2 + K2.4; A4 preserved. Zero behavior change.

**Calls-mint laundering through function slots fenced (#1802 + #1820, §28.3/§27.1.1/§27.6).** The v0.194 bare-type-parameter rule's recorded residual — a `Task`-family value laundered through a `Wrap<T>(f: () -> T): T` slot at `T = Task<int>`, mint seen as a lend, a leak — is discharged for the `Task`-family arm by three coordinated fences (#1802/#1820), all announcement-coherence: (a) calls-mint substitutions are **inadmissible** at bare-parameter function slots (per-instantiation, §3.6 rules 2/4); (b) §27.1.1 makes `Task`-family return slots announcement-bearing (exact-match, no cross-family covariance) and the same boundary governs method-reference formation; (c) a new *Concrete-slot function bodies* callee-side rule (#1820) rejects a minting lambda under a concrete class/interface slot (the `Wrap<Object>(lambda() => Work())` route the first two cannot see). #1820 also classifies function-value invocations of concrete class/interface slots as **borrows** carrying {the function value} ∪ {plain reference-typed arguments}, and fences two formation defects: a property reference over a `Task`-family-typed property, and a static-iterable-factory reference bridged to a non-iterable slot. **A narrowed residual stays recorded** (inherited by #1787): a static iterable factory in a bare-parameter or retyped slot at an iterable substitution still launders the iterator convention's caller-owned frame — outside axiom A2's calls-mint family by A2's own recorded reason, so the family-keyed fence never captures it. **Declined:** accept-as-documented-residual (violates leak-freedom and K1's one-classification rule; the sibling route already reaches a live two-owners pairing), post-substitution keying (the recorded v0.190 decline), and the capture-set-transitive-source option (wrong axis — container ownership, not carried sources). Kernel: derivation K1 + K2.4 + K6.3 under A2; no axiom.

**Iterable-interface frame ownership — signature-keyed, `owned`-announced at instance/extension callees (#1787, §28.3/§28.6/§29.2/§29.3/A2).** An iterable-interface call result carries a disposal obligation **iff its signature announces a caller-owned frame** (a static iterable return — the iterator convention, unchanged — or an `owned`-marked instance/extension return) or it is a stdlib affine deferred producer (§29.11). At the **non-owning heads** an *unmarked* instance/extension return is the stored-collection view (a receiver-sourced borrow, no obligation); a *fresh frame* (an iterator body, a composed operator result) through an unmarked instance/extension return is a compile error with declare-`owned` the remedy — the protocol's own `GetEnumerator(): owned IEnumerator<T>` spelling generalized. The **owning heads** take **no unmarked instance/extension spelling at all** (the #1660 declaration-site reject, preserved — a borrowed owning view would drain receiver-owned elements through a no-obligation result, and double-frees under interface dispatch). Calls-mint is **not** extended to iterables (axiom A2 stands, its register reason extended). §28.3's `Evens` composed-frame example and §29.3's `Squares` example are marked `static` to stay valid under the new rule; Guide 1's mirror aligns. **Declined:** extending calls-mint to iterables (reverses A2 and rationale §12.10's explicit warning), body-keyed classification (undecidable at interface-dispatch/function-value sites, violates K2.4), blessing the impl's pragmatic frame-freeing (a hidden ownership channel), and ruling drain-through-borrow semantics for a borrowed owning view (every candidate answer silently consumes receiver-owned elements or reinvents an obligation-splitting mechanism the kernel lacks — declined-not-foreclosed). Kernel: derivation K1.5 + K2.4 + K3.2 + K1.7/K2.3 + K6.2 + K3.13; A2 preserved.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** every ruling is a derivation over the K1–K9 register with its existing K4-posture residuals; no axiom is added or retired (twelve live, two tombstones). §28.6 now states leak prevention purely as K9.1 + K1.7 + the fresh-store rejection and delegates every borrow-storability question to §28.3's single rule; §30.5's operand list is closed under K2's named-location taxonomy.

**Migration.** Newly **accepted** (doc-side; the compiler already accepts the shapes noted): an owned-field bare read stored into another object's non-owned field via §28.3's admitted forms (#2043); `await b._t` over an owned task field-path of a non-`this` object (#2042 — the plain-borrow-field sub-case is the tracked impl delta); `_ := await t;` for a Pattern B task (#1826); static getters re-exposing `readonly`/admitted-mutable static class-typed fields (#1819). Newly **rejected**: a terminal `return move x.f;` with no restoring assignment (#1814 — already enforced); calls-mint (`Task`-family) substitutions/retypings/lambda-bodies laundering through function slots classified as lends (#1802/#1820 — silent leaks or a live two-owners pairing today; remedies: family-shaped `() -> Task<T>` slots, statement-form collection builds, `owned T` factory slots); a fresh iterable frame returned through an unmarked instance/extension iterable return, and an unmarked instance/extension owning-head return (#1787 — remedy: declare `owned`, or expose the stored view at the concrete type / non-owning interface). Doc example fixes: the §28.6 `TakeTransactions`, §28.3 `Evens`, §29.3 `Squares` examples and Guide 1's mirrors. The conformance corpus carries no committed-case flips from this train (verified per ruling); the spec-ahead-of-impl deltas and the per-ruling lit/gtest regression pins are tracked by the impl issues each ruling record names (the §30.5 plain-field await widening; the stale §28.3 diagnostic parenthetical; the owning-`Task`-field displacement leak; the #1802/#1820 fence enforcement coordinated as one unit; the #1787 iterable-return re-keying, preserving the #1660 pins; the #1814 owning-collection-field `move` miscompile gating the corrected example).

### v0.224 changelog (v0.223 → v0.224)

**Design change — named-destructure patterns (proposal 0065 graduates; owner-directed 2026-07-24).** Spec §19.3 gains the named-destructure pattern form `T(Prop = Pattern, …)` — named slots inside the existing destructure parentheses, the by-name completion of the pattern grammar that per-slot `|` alternatives (v0.167) began. Zero new tokens, one new grammar list shape, no new ownership or kernel rule. The direction was the delegated, critic-gated ruling on #1409 (accepting the `=` spelling and fixing the v1 restrictions); this revision writes that acceptance into the normative documents in full.

**The form and its resolution.** A destructuring pattern's parenthesized slot list may now be written **by name** — each slot `Identifier "=" Pattern` — as an alternative to the positional list; the two forms may not be mixed in one pattern (v1). The slot `Identifier` resolves against the pattern's type by kind: a **record**'s stored positional-field/body auto-properties (§9.1/§9.2 — computed record properties are not v1 targets, mirroring `with`); a **choice case**'s payload field names (§35.1/§35.5, prefix-omission unchanged); or a **class**'s **public readable instance properties**, stored or computed, declared or inherited (§23) — the by-name match surface positional destructuring deliberately never gave classes (§5.17's class-*deconstruction* decline is about extraction and disposal, untouched here — a property read transfers nothing). Unknown/duplicate/write-only/indexer/static/non-property names are compile errors at the pattern; enums, primitives, and interface-typed heads have no named-destructure form in v1. Matching is type-test-first (a named pattern never matches `null`, §19.5), then per-slot reads in textual order with short-circuit; a class-property slot read *runs the getter* during matching, in §19.4's deterministic first-match order. Each slot RHS is a full `AltPattern` (bindings, `_`, constants, ranges, relationals, per-slot `|`, type tests, nested destructurings — named or positional — recursively); a naked identifier after `=` is a constant-or-type reference, never a binding (bindings are spelled `var w`); a constant slot is the `=` equality test under the slot type's `=` (§8.4), and a non-`=`-bearing slot type in constant position is a compile error. Every named-slot binding is a **borrow** (§19.3 verbatim); an **owning match** (§35.5) does not transfer through a named slot — a named-matched owned payload is borrowed during the arm and disposed at construct completion, exactly as a discarded slot.

**Exhaustiveness (§19.6).** An unguarded named-destructure arm `T(N1 = p1, …)` contributes to static exhaustiveness exactly where an unguarded arm covering `T` by the existing rules would — a sealed-hierarchy leaf's type pattern (including a determined generic instantiation) or a choice case's all-slots-irrefutable destructure — **iff every named slot is irrefutable** (a binding or `_`); any refutable slot contributes nothing, one level deep, with no per-property value-space analysis. A sealed hierarchy is thus matchable exhaustively with no `_` arm by all-irrefutable named-destructure arms, exactly as by bare type patterns.

**Grammar and invariants.** Appendix A.7's destructuring production becomes `QualifiedName "(" (PositionalPatternList | NamedPatternList) ")"`, with new `NamedPatternList`/`NamedSlot` productions (the two-token `Identifier "="` commit, the `=`-is-not-a-relop collision note, the naked-identifier reading); Appendix C.7 gains one invariant bullet (a slot list is positional or named, never mixed; named slots resolve per the record/choice/class taxonomy). Rationale gains §3.14 recording the `=` spelling and the declined brace (§5.16 no-`{}`) and `:=` forks.

**Declined (carried from the proposal, not reopened):** the C#-style brace form `Rect { Width: var w }` (§5.16's confined-`{}` posture; a redundant second destructure surface); the `:=` spelling (assignment reads false in interrogation position — the `:=`/`=` construction/matching asymmetry is load-bearing); positional+named mixing in v1 (arity/coverage complication; liftable, call-site precedent exists); naked-identifier bindings in named slots (a silent binding directly after `=` would invert the interrogation reading and flip on a `const`). The liftables (mixing, computed record properties, interface heads, privileged-site visibility, lambda-parameter named destructuring) stay recorded in proposal 0065.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no ownership rule changes and no new kernel rule — named-slot bindings are K2 borrows sourced from the scrutinee, adding no K3 consuming position; getters cannot mint (§28.6), so no slot read carries an obligation. Axiom register unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones).

**Migration.** Purely additive — `=` inside a destructure slot is a parse error today, so no existing program changes meaning; the conformance corpus carries no flips and no pins are retired. Newly **expressible**: named-destructure patterns over records, choice-case payloads, and class public readable properties, and the `_`-free sealed-hierarchy match via all-irrefutable named-destructure arms. The feature is spec-ahead-of-impl: the compiler parses none of the named form yet, and an implementation tracker — "impl: named-destructure patterns `T(Prop = Pattern)` (§19.3/§19.6, v0.224, proposal 0065)", sequenced after the R0 drain and the #2079 v0.207+ syntax catch-up family it shares pattern grammar with — is filed at this landing (#1409 remains the design tracker). Guide 03's revalidation-pin example is a graduation-time follow-up, not part of this normative landing.

### v0.225 changelog (v0.224 → v0.225)

**Design change — method-local `record`/`enum` declarations (proposal 0066 graduates; owner-directed 2026-07-24).** Spec §21.10 admits `record` and `enum` declarations as **body-scoped statements** — a shape used once (a projection's result record, a small closed constant set scoped to one algorithm) may live next to its single use instead of at module or class level. This is the **named remedy the anonymous-types decline** (the proposals' DECLINED.md D-0002) already committed to; the direction was the delegated, critic-gated ruling on #1405 (four scope rulings fixed). No stdlib change, no new kernel rule; §9 (records) and §10 (enums) are referenced, not amended — a local type is an ordinary nominal type.

**The form.** Appendix A.6's `Statement` gains one alternative, `LocalTypeDecl ::= RecordDecl | EnumDecl`, reusing the A.3 productions with two semantically-checked restrictions: the `Visibility?` slot must be empty (a local type has no access surface — deliberately opposite to §11.6 nested types, where the keyword is *required*) and the `GenericParams?` slot must be empty (v1). `record`/`enum` are reserved and begin no other statement, so the reading is a token-one commit and no existing program changes meaning. `LocalTypeDecl` is admitted wherever a `Statement` is (method/constructor/destructor/accessor bodies, lambda `do`-bodies, `do … end` blocks, loop bodies, statement-position arm bodies).

**The four scope rulings (§21.10).** (a) **Strict body scope** — the name is in scope from its declaration to the innermost enclosing block's end, like a local variable (§21.6); order-significant (no forward references, hence no mutually-recursive local types); no signature positions (a compile error naming the rule — the name is not in scope at any member signature); no shadowing of a visible type name and no clash with another same-body declaration. Escape via boxing is admitted only as far as §8.6 already goes: a **non-borrow-bearing** local record implementing an interface may return boxed through it (the `private`-nested-type precedent; self-contained because records carry no disposal), while a **borrow-bearing** local record keeps §8.6's call-bounded-box-only rejection unchanged — the case that stops a `record View(Cell: Widget)` over a `using var` widget from dangling. (b) **No reference to an enclosing generic parameter** in v1 (a compile error) — it would make identity, §9.2 equality synthesis, and §9.8 serialization synthesis per-instantiation; a welcome consequence is instantiation-independent identity, so a public generic's carried body holds the local type as ordinary body content (§2.8.2). (c) **One grammar anchor** — `LocalTypeDecl` as above, empty visibility, no shadowing. (d) **`enum` included, `choice` excluded** (and `class`/`interface` excluded) — choices carry classification/coverage/owning-match machinery and classes carry ownership/destructor/§28 disposal surface, both real kernel-engaging admissions for no recorded need. Appendix C.1 gains one type-register bullet; a cross-reference sentence is added near §11.6.

**Semantics.** The local type is an ordinary nominal record/enum: per-declaration identity (two same-shaped local records in different methods are distinct types — no structural unification, the discipline D-0002 declined), §9.2 auto-equality, §9.5 `with`, §8.5 auto-`ToString`, §9.8 serialization eligibility by field types, §9.6 interface implementation, the §3.6 derived type properties, and — for a local `enum` — the whole §10 surface including `case` matching with prefix omission and enum-scrutinee exhaustiveness inside the scope. Rationale gains §9.10 graduating the D-0002 remedy record from the declined register's prose; DECLINED.md D-0002's remedy paragraph now points at the landed sections.

**Declined (carried from the proposal, not reopened):** enclosing generic-parameter capture in v1 (per-instantiation identity/synthesis, §2.8.2 artifact machinery, the #428 cross-module-generics posture — disproportionate to concrete-field projections; **liftable** with that cost named); local `choice` (heavier classification/coverage/owning-match surface, no motivating case — liftable with evidence); type shadowing of outer type names (a readability trap — collision is an error instead); local `class`/`interface` (genuinely new kernel-engaging surface — out of scope, would need its own proposal); unqualified escape-via-boxing (would admit the §8.6-rejected dangling box — the admitted form is qualified to non-borrow-bearing records). Anonymous types stay declined (D-0002 reopening bar unchanged); this feature is their remedy, not their re-admission.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no new kernel rule — local records/enums are value types (records cannot own heap resources or implement `IDisposable`, §9.7; enums are constants), so no ownership/disposal/borrow rule changes and K1–K9 are untouched; a borrow-bearing local record engages the existing §9.7/§8.6/§28.3 borrow machinery (K2 bounding) exactly as a module-level record does, adding none and lifting none. The v1 cut excludes `choice`/`class` precisely because those would add genuinely new kernel-engaging surface. Axiom register unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones).

**Migration.** Purely additive — `record`/`enum` at statement position is a parse error today, so no existing program changes meaning; the conformance corpus carries no flips, and the ruling's grep found no pin asserting the rejection as a named rule. Newly **expressible**: body-local record/enum declarations for projections and small constant sets next to their single use. The feature is spec-ahead-of-impl (symbol collection has no body-scoped type space yet): an implementation tracker — "impl: method-local record/enum declarations (`LocalTypeDecl`) — body-scoped type space in symbol collection (§21.10, v0.225, proposal 0066)", queued after the R0 drain and the R1 stdlib waves — is filed at this landing (#1405 remains the design tracker).

### v0.226 changelog (v0.225 → v0.226)

**Editorial — the specification no longer narrates its own revision history.** This revision is a documentation-only sweep of `Bezel_Language_Spec.md`: the inline provenance tags that had accreted on normative sentences — the `(v0.NNN)` revision markers and the `#NNNN` issue references appended to rules — are removed, and the two retired sections (§22.11 object-initializer blocks, §24 events) and the §28 axiom register are de-narrated. **Zero normative change and zero migration:** not one rule, grammar production, `<a id>` anchor, or section number moved, and no program changes meaning. History is not lost — it lives, as it always has, in this changelog; the spec now points here rather than retelling it.

**What was removed.** The spec carried 998 `v0.NNN` mentions and 127 `#NNNN` references; after the sweep 10 `v0.NNN` remain — nine that name changelog entries this text points at, plus the one §22.11 retirement marker — and no `#NNNN` remain. Gone are the `(v0.184)`/`(v0.184, #1533)`/`(#1660)` markers that dated or attributed a rule and the "since v0.181"/"as of v0.187"/"codifying implemented behavior"/"recorded decline" narration fragments. Where a provenance tag sat inside a parenthetical that also carried a live cross-reference (`([§9.5], v0.188)`, `(v0.196, below)`), only the provenance was stripped and the reference kept; every deletion fixed its own surrounding punctuation so the sentence reads cleanly.

**What was kept, because it is load-bearing rather than history.** Section headings retain their retirement markers where retention is deliberate for citation stability — `## 24. Events (retired member kind)`, `### 22.11 Object initializer blocks (retired v0.188)`. Sentences that *point at* this changelog as the decision record keep the pointer, and with it the version that names the entry. Conformance and "this revision" language is untouched.

**Retired sections and the axiom register.** §22.11 and §24 keep their headings and anchors — so `§22.12+` and `[§24]` citations stay stable — and a one-line statement of the current rule; the historical definition is replaced by a pointer to this changelog. The axiom register (§28) keeps every axiom **number** stable: A1–A14 are a deliberate stable-numbering policy cited across the spec, the rationale, and proposal 0046, and **no axiom was renumbered**. The two tombstone rows (A1, A8) are reduced to a bare "retired; see the changelog" one-liner, and the version/issue provenance is stripped from the live rows' cells; the retirement reasons live in the v0.201 and v0.213 changelog entries where they always were.

**Migration.** None. Editorial only; the conformance corpus is unaffected and no pin changes. The companion documents' revision headers move to v0.226 with the spec; the standard-library, rationale, and guide texts are unchanged this revision.

(the relative clause had lost its antecedent — the same reduction the sweep itself applied to the parallel §22.13 note); §9.7's contentless "; the precedent" dropped; §30.7's referent-less "the family's machinery" restated as "that driver is deferred future work, not foreclosed" (no issue number reintroduced — the sweep removed those deliberately); §28.13's Sendability bullet's orphaned "joins form-(i) at but" re-tensed to "is in form-(i) but" (no pin restored: the bullet was deliberately de-tagged); Appendix C.4's "(this bullet previously omitted the last three sources)" deleted outright.
