### v0.237 changelog (v0.236 → v0.237)

**Rationale front matter rewritten (owner-directed 2026-08-04) — the intro and §1 "The big picture."** Editorial, rationale-only: the spec and stdlib are textually unchanged (headers move in lockstep; the changelog gains this entry). Readers hit these pages first, and the owner directed a rewrite to the standard the rest of the document holds.

- **The intro** no longer names any other programming language. It now states the document's role in the project's own terms — the recorded form of "why doesn't Bezel just do Y?", with each answer naming the alternative, what it would buy, and why it was declined — plus the decisions-recorded-with-reasoning discipline and the settled-convention carve-out, without attribution.
- **§1** drops the three-things-at-once framing sentence and reframes around two commitments: the performance of a compiled language (native code, no collector, costs that follow from the source) and memory management that is predictable and checked — single ownership of resource-holding objects with the `owned`/`using var` spellings named, disposal exactly once, and the price triaged with the pre-rewrite's quantifiers kept: *most* mistakes rejected at compile time, *most* of the remainder deterministic `DisposedAccessException` faults in checked disposal mode, the *few* individually-recorded trust admissions named as such (spec §28.3), and unchecked release builds stated plainly as undefined behavior (spec §28.2). The no-ceremony tier (strings, boxed values, function values, resource-free classes) is noted with linked pointers to §4/§5.9. The Rust comparison compresses to the recorded form: the ownership model bears some similarity, deliberately — and differs in how much the checker demands (no lifetime annotations, no exclusive-writer rule; data-race freedom comes from serial domains with transfer or immutable sharing at their boundaries, §12) — yielding more freedom in how code is written without the common pitfalls of manual management. The named-language inheritance paragraph is retired; the closing keeps and extends the document's framing sentence (each chapter records what a stricter rule would buy, what it would cost, and why the balance landed where it did). The train's adversarial pass drove the final shape: the dichotomy a draft stated exhaustively was re-hedged to the spec's own triage, and the draft's mechanism claims (no background collector activity) were dropped as unsupported by §28's scoping.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** none — rationale prose only; no normative text touched.

**Migration.** Doc-only; no program changes meaning. No grammar, anchor, or section moves — the §1 anchor, heading, and Contents list are unchanged (the intro contains no anchors of its own). The guides are untouched and keep their pins; the conformance corpus is untouched.

### v0.238 changelog (v0.237 → v0.238)

**Silent tracking — trivial-dispose becomes a ceremony property, not a lifetime regime (proposal 0077 stage 1; owner-ruled 2026-08-04, Q1–Q4 as recommended).** The trivial-dispose feature bundled two separable exemptions: the **ceremony** exemption (no `using var`, no must-use warning, cosmetic discard — what v0.61/v0.66 argued for and every user-facing surface teaches) and the **tracking** exemption (references to trivial instances could outlive any static bound, memory reclaimed by an implementation-defined runtime mechanism). This revision keeps the first verbatim and retracts the second: every trivial-dispose instance now has exactly one statically-known owner at every point — the K1 classification it already carried, now load-bearing — and the compiler inserts a **flag-setting free** (logical disposal plus reclamation, no user code) at that owner's release point, so checked disposal mode backstops trivial dangles exactly as non-trivial ones. **No runtime lifetime mechanism exists for user-defined classes at all** — the no-GC claim becomes unconditional for every class a user can write; the runtime-managed trio (`string`, boxed values, function values) is untouched. The retraction resolves the docs' recorded internal split (§9.7's "lifetime that ends at the construction expression" vs. the mechanism sentences — resolved in §9.7's favor) and aligns the spec with the implementation's architecture, which never built the mechanism (the 0077 audits). This **completes v0.66's option-B direction** rather than reversing it: the mechanism was the honesty device that let "tighten the discard" avoid "embrace runtime-managed class instances — it's GC-shaped"; removing the last mechanism finishes that motion. The v0.66 entry, like all pinned history, is unedited.

- **§28 preamble, §28.2, §28.3 (K1.6), §28.12.** The mechanism paragraph is replaced: the exemption is ceremony-not-lifetime, the free is compiler-inserted at the tracked owner's release point, and the no-GC statement strengthens to unconditional. K1.6 rewrites to the empty-*user-visible*-content form: discharge is never demanded *of the program*; the borrow half of the machinery is demanded everywhere. §28.2 defines the inserted free as logical disposal (flag) + reclamation with its costs stated (per-instance flag word; live flag test and quarantine latitude in checked mode only; unchecked builds pay nothing) — a **mandatory companion**: without it the retraction would create the language's only un-backstopped dangling class. §28.3's unbound-temporaries subsection states that trivial temporaries are freed at the same K8 boundary; §28.12 ties the free to the logical/physical split; §28.4's post-disposal reclamation sentence drops its refcount/region parenthetical.
- **§15.4 — the literal-tree ownership rule** replaces the fresh-trivial-producer carve-out (the tracking exemption's one real ergonomic pillar, v0.184's reliance). The fresh nodes of a collection literal form an **aggregate per maximal borrowing-family subtree**, owned by whatever owns the subtree's root (receiving binding, K8 temporary, owning slot, `owned` parameter/return/field, static storage) and freed — all nodes, one obligation — at that owner's release point; membership fixed at construction, borrowed elements never members. Six edge resolutions land with it: call-argument literals owned by the K8 temporary (the §22.14 variadic idiom survives untouched), returned literals legal through `owned` returns only (§15.4's `return` sentence gains the explicit owned-return requirement), owning-family boundaries yield (no double owner), drop-on-overwrite frees the displaced aggregate under a **per-aggregate conservative freeze** (**Q3 as recommended** — cheap, coarse, and revisable: per-node tracking would only *admit more*, so the widening path is recorded, and coarse freezes keep the implementation's sole-owner proofs simple), `Add` is not a literal position, and field-initializer trees require `owned` fields (uniform with §28.6's fresh-store rule).
- **Q1 (Add-position fresh trivial nodes): option (i), uniform admission, with the targeted lint on.** `coll.Add(new Trivial())` and `groups.Add("odds", [1, 3, 5])` stay admissible — rejection cannot be scoped by signature (`coll.Add(new X())` and `sink.Consume(new X())` are indistinguishable plain-parameter calls), and the recorded reason for §15.4's literal-only asymmetry ("an opaque callee's signature does not announce retention") is type-agnostic — but the shape now joins the recorded hazard for non-trivial arguments and draws a **normative warning** at fresh trivial-dispose arguments in `Add`/`Insert`/indexer-set position on borrowing collections: under the retained no-warning rule the shape would otherwise compile with zero diagnostics while the compiler knows the argument dies at its K8 boundary — a statically-certain dangle emitted silently. The lint is the ceremony exemption's counterpart, not its erosion (the program stays accepted; no `using var` demanded); the documented remedy is the owning family, its costs stated in rationale §5.28. Recorded follow-on, not taken: the same lint shape would serve the non-trivial fresh-`Task`-slot trap (#1813).
- **Q2 (the definition amendment): accepted.** "No `owned` fields" becomes "no `owned` fields of **non-trivial-dispose** type", recursive and per-instantiation, and the definition prose becomes "disposal provably runs no user code and releases only memory" — the synthesized cascade over `owned` trivial fields frees memory and runs no user code, so wrapper types keep the ceremony exemption for holding what the free-cascade handles without user code (the c1 resolution's fresh-store `owned` requirement made this necessary). Conformed in lockstep: §3.6's property-table row, §28.9's definition and generic subsection (`OwningBox<T>` is now the worked per-instantiation example; the owning family stays non-trivial at every instantiation via `OwningBuffer<T>`'s destructor), §22.10's primary-ctor capture note, §22.13's static-field warning parenthetical, Appendix C.3, and the §28 preamble. Interface carriage (§2.8.2) and delta classification (§2.8.6) are unchanged in mechanism — verdict-*gained* is preserving, which is the amendment's only direction of effect on existing types.
- **§28.6 — the three ambiguities (c1–c3) resolved as errors, uniform with the letter:** fresh trivial into a plain field = error (declare `owned`; under Q2 the holder's classification survives), fresh trivial from a getter = the A4 error, fresh trivial through a non-`owned` instance return = error (statics already announced). §17.13 respells the trivial discard as freed-at-end-of-statement (identical timing to the non-trivial case, no user code). §22.5's trivial plain-parameter default survives **by re-derivation, caller-side**: the materialized default is an unbound owned temporary of the *calling statement's* full expression, freed at its K8 boundary, the plain parameter a call-bounded borrow — the "fresh into the call's frame" wording is amended to name the caller-side owner (under a callee-frame reading the value would die at callee return and the residual would be strictly worse), and the trivial/non-trivial unification this derivation enables is recorded as a liftable widening, not taken. §30.14 gains the **moved-obligation clause**: a moved sendable trivial instance's free obligation transfers with the move — single owner at all times, no cross-domain bookkeeping (the mechanism's hardest corner, deleted); trivial-sourced borrows join the domain-clause residuals verbatim, and the channel-internal disposal sites need no separate clause because disposal of a trivial item *is* the flag-setting free. §28.11 and the §28 summary table respell backing storage as a **single-allocation layout fact** released by the instance's one free (v0.184's declined alternative — real backing-storage ceremony — stays declined; only the free point becomes static); §22.15/§31.4/Appendix C.14 take the one-line re-derivation note for the pure-throw carve-out (dispose-after-arm = the flag-setting free); Appendix C.3's three invariants conform.
- **Q4 (staging): fixes land ahead.** #2654 (spec-contrary must-use warning on trivial `new`), #2655 (abandonment-shape leaks), and #2660 (nested-literal lowering ICE) are conformance bugs identical under every ruling and proceed independently as stage 2, with #2656's escape-coverage pins riding the #2654 lane; #2655's literal-element fix was reasoned conforming under both the old and new readings on the premise that today's sema rejects every escape, so no accepted program observes the free. *(Stage-2 record, added before this entry landed: the lanes falsified that premise for element-**read** borrows — `outer.Add(xs[0])` slips the store rule that rejects the named-binding spelling, [#2672](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2672) — so the literal-element free was correctly deferred to [#2676](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2676) under the standing leak-over-UAF preference, with #2672 as its prerequisite. The spec semantics this entry lands are unaffected: the element-read escape is a shape §28.11's store rule already rejects by its letter, and #2672 is the implementation catching up to it.)* Stage 1 therefore documents semantics the implementation already exhibits in architecture.
- **Stdlib, rationale, guides.** Stdlib §1 states the compiler-freed rule and the **intrinsic-backing device** (composite trivial-dispose types — the borrowing collections, the sorted forms, `Counter<K>` — hold backing as part of the instance's single allocation, the compiler-known device whose user-expressible spelling is `owned` trivial fields — the c6 resolution); §4.4/§4.17/§4.18/§4.20 wordings conform. Rationale §5.9 is rewritten to the ceremony-only story with the v0.61/v0.66 steps re-scoped to ceremony; §1 and §4's intro now scope the unspecified-mechanism statement to the trio explicitly; new **§5.28** is the decision record — the owner's objection, the two-exemption analysis, the literal-tree rule's design choices, the Q1/Q2 reasoning, and the declined alternatives (the layered runtime; acyclicity restriction, declined for non-locality — a global type-reference-graph property breaks §3.6's computed-from-structure basis; uniform loud ceremony; an opt-out marker). Guide 1 §2 promotes "ceremony only, never lifetime" to its thesis and teaches the compiler-freed story plus the Add-shape caution; Guide 5 §1's backing-storage parenthetical conforms. Both guides' trivial-dispose content was re-traced; their pins move to v0.238.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** this revision rewrites kernel text — K1.6 — and the classification is: **an exemption narrowed, no axiom spent.** K1.6's tracking half is deleted; the behavior now demanded of trivial-dispose values is the existing K1–K9 machinery applied to classifications those values already carried, with the free's placements being K3/K8's existing release points and the backstop K4.1's existing machinery — a derivation, not new content. The literal-tree ownership rule is a **derivation** (K1 fresh-productions-owned + K2.3 bounded escape + K3 discharge + K8 boundaries) with one recorded granularity choice (Q3's per-aggregate freeze, K5's freeze applied at aggregate grain); the Q1 admission extends the existing K4.3-residual/K4.1-backstop posture recorded at §15.4/§28.11 and adds a lint, not a rule. Q2 amends a §3.6 derived-property definition, outside the kernel. The axiom register is unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones).

**Migration.** Newly **warned** (the one behavior change): a fresh trivial-dispose argument in `Add`/`Insert`/indexer-set position on a borrowing collection (`groups.Add("odds", [1, 3, 5]);`, `coll.Add(new Box());`) — previously silent and mechanism-backed, now an admitted, warned, checked-mode-backstopped dangle; remedies are bind-first or the owning family. Newly **rejected**: fresh trivial-dispose values stored into plain fields, returned from getters, or returned through non-`owned` instance returns (c1–c3 — previously ambiguous, decided by the letter of the existing rules), and a returned collection literal through a non-`owned` instance return (§15.4's explicit owned-return requirement). Newly **admitted** (Q2's widening): a class whose only `owned` fields are of trivial-dispose type is now itself trivial-dispose — a verdict *gained*, preserving under §2.8.6. Newly **defined**: aggregate lifetimes for literal trees, K8-boundary frees for trivial temporaries, the flag-setting free with checked-mode backstop, the caller-side owner of §22.5 trivial defaults, and §30.14's moved-obligation transfer. Everything else is doc-only wording (backing-storage respells, the preamble, C.3/C.14 conformances). Doc corpus: the docs audit found every normative example already binds its trivial trees; the §15.4 nested-literal examples are the literal-tree rule's motivating corpus and stay well-formed verbatim. Conformance corpus: no flips — verified by grep at landing (no `Add(new …)` shape exists; `spec_0060`, the §15.4 literals mirror, is saved by the rule and is skip-listed besides). No grammar production changes (Appendix A untouched); no anchor or section number moves. Spec-ahead-of-impl: the compiler is already a silent-tracking implementation in architecture (0077's audit); the deltas are the stage-2 conformance trackers filed before this landing, of which [#2654](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2654) (warning gate), [#2656](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2656) (trivial-variant escape coverage), [#2660](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2660) (nested-literal lowering), and [#2655](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2655)'s bare-statement and builtin-discard frees landed ahead of this entry, as Q4 directed; the literal-element free is deferred to [#2676](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2676) behind the element-read store-rule gap [#2672](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2672) (the Q4 note above), and the Q1 lint and the full literal-tree aggregate semantics ride that retry with spec-cited regression tests per `tests/README.md`; #2332's parked general question is answered by this revision (no trivial carve exists — the escape checks are demanded) and closes with a citation at landing. Proposal 0077 flips to superseded (stage 1 graduated; stage 2 = implementation conformance) and the README queue row moves with it. Guides 1 and 5 re-validated; pins move to v0.238; Guides 2/3/4/6 are untouched and keep their pins (Guide 4's §2 fresh-task trap is unchanged — it becomes the teaching precedent the recorded #1813 follow-on cites).

**Gate round (same train).** The adversarial pass caught two ill-formed inline examples in the newly-written text and one definitional gap, all fixed before landing: the literal-tree blockquote's conditional-element illustration and the lint's remedy example both used bare collection literals in positions §15.4's own no-standalone-type rule rejects (the illustration respelled with `new`-expression arms; the remedy gains its target-type annotation — and the general fact that conditional *literal* elements are unwritable, §20 having no branch target-typing, is recorded as a §20-side liftable, not resolved here); Q2's recursive definition gains its fixed-point convention — **coinductive**, mirroring the sentence sendability already states for its own recursive `owned` references (§30.14) — so `owned Next: Node?` self-reference is trivial-dispose-preserving by rule, not by implementation choice. Completeness repairs in step: the API-surface flip list gains Q2's fourth route (an owned field's declared type itself flipping, propagating across modules); §15.4's fresh-producer enumeration names nested non-trivial literals explicitly; the owning-target paragraph and §28.9's bullet 1 gain cross-references to the literal-tree rule and the store-position lint respectively; rationale §5.28's declined-alternative 2 gains the direction-and-boundedness sentence distinguishing it from Q2.

### v0.239 changelog (v0.238 → v0.239)

**Rationale §5.28 gains declined-alternative 5: uniform silence (owner-directed 2026-08-04).** Editorial, rationale-only: the spec and stdlib are textually unchanged (headers move in lockstep; the changelog gains this entry). The owner posed the mirror of v0.238's alternative 3 directly — if trivial-dispose only drops ceremony, why not drop the ceremony for destructor-bearing classes too? — and v0.238's own decision record had no entry for it. The recorded decline: ceremony is provably not a tracking tax (every class is tracked; silence would leak nothing), so what it is, is the **announcement of observable disposal effects** — which makes the trivial-dispose criterion (disposal provably runs no user code) the *maximal* ceremony exemption: extending silence past it announces effects nowhere. The entry records the supporting material: complexity was never the line (effect-free classes of any size are already ceremony-free; the owned-resource wrapper keeps its announcement because the cascade fires the effect at its drop point); the silent-RAII precedent retrofitted selective must-use ceremony back in by hand where Bezel derives it from structure; and the per-site one-token spellings are the sanctioned local silences, each an announcement itself.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** none — rationale prose only; no normative text touched.

**Migration.** Doc-only; no program changes meaning. No grammar, anchor, or section moves; the guides are untouched and keep their pins; the conformance corpus is untouched.

### v0.240 changelog (v0.239 → v0.240)

**The ceremony-announces-effects principle gains its wider presence (owner-directed 2026-08-04).** v0.239 recorded the full argument in rationale §5.28; the owner ruled it worth surfacing where readers actually meet the ceremony. Two placements, honoring the documents' division of labor — the spec says *what* and points at *why*; the guide teaches the posture:

- **Spec §28.9** gains one principle sentence at the exemption's definition: the ceremony announces observable disposal *effects*, a trivial-dispose class's disposal has none to announce, and that is why the exemption's boundary is exactly the runs-no-user-code line and extends no further (pointer to rationale §5.28). No rule changes; the sentence names the boundary's reason, not a new boundary.
- **Guide 1 §2** teaches it in both homes: the four-spellings paragraph's "how loudly" now says what loudness is for (disposing a resource is an effect — a file closes, a lock releases — and the spellings mark where effects fire), and the trivial-dispose block's lead-in states the contrapositive (a class whose disposal provably has no effects has nothing to announce, rationale §5.28). Guide 1's revalidation pin moves to v0.240 — a guide change riding a normative train carries the pin move, per the 2026-07-30 process ruling; §2's four-spellings paragraph and trivial-dispose block were re-traced against the landed text. The stdlib and rationale are textually unchanged (headers move in lockstep).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** none — one explanatory sentence in §28.9's prose and guide teaching; no rule text touched.

**Migration.** Doc-only; no program changes meaning. No grammar, anchor, or section moves; the conformance corpus is untouched.

### v0.241 changelog (v0.240 → v0.241)

**The 2026-08-11 weekly spec-question sweep — seventeen questions from seventeen issues, owner-ruled 2026-08-11, all as recommended.** Two prepared resolution reports (a typing/casts/grammar/ToString cluster and an ownership/stdlib/indexer cluster) were accepted verbatim; this revision lands every accepted ruling as document text. The common thread is degenerate-corner closure: universal quantifiers meeting shapes they cannot serve (`as` at targets with no informative result type, `new` on builtins with no declared constructor, a discard marker after a modifier that reads its operand), silent divergences between the letter and the implementation (constant narrowing's source-type gate, the default `ToString`'s undefined "qualified", the spec's own three stray `owned` spellings), and one real ordering gap (`finally` establishment). Every rejection lands in the forbid→allow-compatible direction; every admission is derived from standing text.

- **Spec §5.1 — constant narrowing is value-based, site-complete ([#2741](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2741), rider [#2652](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2652)).** The constant-narrowing paragraph now states the value-based reading: the source may be a compile-time constant of **any** integer type, the target any integer type whose range contains the value, **across signedness** (`const N: long := 8; var b: byte := N;`; a `uint` constant where `int` is expected); the never-implicit signed/unsigned bullet is scoped to non-constant expressions (the section's own flagship `var b: byte := 50;` was always a cross-signedness constant conversion). The site population is stated with no position carve-out — initializers, assignments, call arguments, returns, record positional arguments, collection-literal elements, default arguments — with participation in §22.6 applicability and the nullable lifting. This ratifies the reading [#2925](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2925) implemented for the site population, closing #2652's silent-decision complaint; the source-type widening (exact-`int` → any integer constant, including `uint` → `int`) is compiler catch-up tracked on #2741.
- **Spec §17.4 — one paragraph, two degenerate-target arms ([#2911](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2911), [#2962](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2962)).** `as` requires its result type `T?` to exist and be informative. An inline-array target is rejected (§15.1 admits no nullable inline-array form, so the operator's contract is unsatisfiable; the measured alternative was a failed cast manufacturing an all-zero array); the unit target is rejected (`x is ()` carries strictly more information; `()?` stays a well-formed type). The remedy in both arms is the `is` test with §12.7 narrowing (copy-out for inline arrays). Generic reach is per-instantiation under §3.6 rule 2: `x as T` at an inline-array or unit substitution is rejected at the instantiation site. §15.1's no-nullable-form paragraph gains the consequent cross-reference.
- **Spec §8.5 — the qualified-name pin and universality, one amendment train ([#2934](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2934), [#2661](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2661)).** "Qualified name" for the class, enum, and non-auto-equality body-record defaults is pinned to stdlib §2.13's `Type.FullName` rendering (module-path-qualified; generic instantiations per §2.13 rule 3) — the default and `FullName` are one rendering contract, giving the language a single canonical renderer instead of two grown independently. The record heads' unqualified spelling is recorded as deliberate (a record rendering identifies itself by shape; a bare class/enum default is only a name). And the defaults are stated **universal**: generated for every type of the applicable kind, stdlib records included (the span family's positional default; `Range<T>` — a compiler-intrinsic *body* record, not a positional one — the auto-equality body-record default, its auto-properties rendered; the gate corrected the first draft's misclassification), components rendering by their own `ToString` dispatch, `null` components per §18.5, the whole rendering a call-bounded borrow (§9.7 unaffected) — closing [#2311](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2311)'s diagnose-without-ruling deferral, under which four behaviours coexisted (user records worked, spans deferred, `$"{sp}"` yielded `""`, `Range<int>.ToString()` dropped the statement). Stdlib §4.14 gains the matching note that the span records carry the §8.5/§9.1 generated members like any record.
- **Spec §15.3/§15.4.1/§30.11-pattern example + Appendix A.4 — the `owned` parameter spelling is single-form ([#3028](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3028)).** The three stray post-colon spellings — §15.4.1's own normative `FromCollectionLiteral(elements: owned OwningArray<T>)` signature, §15.3's `(x: owned V)` prose, and the §30.11 pattern example's `lambda(loaded: owned Resource)` — are fixed to the pre-identifier form the grammar has always defined (`owned elements: …`, `(owned x: V)`, `lambda(owned loaded: …)`). A.4's `Param` production gains the comment recording the rule: `owned` precedes the identifier in every named-declaration position (`Param`, `LambdaParam` via `FuncParamMods`, `FieldDecl`, `CaseField`, `StaticReadonlyDecl`); the pre-`Type` spelling exists only where no identifier exists (return types, `FunctionType` slots). The corpus was decisive — 51 stdlib and ~832 test occurrences pre-identifier, zero post-colon outside verbatim copies of the spec's stray lines. This **reverts the [#3027](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3027) parser relaxation** (which had ratified the drift): the compiler-side revert to a targeted diagnostic is tracked on #3028.
- **Spec §20 — the branch target-typing gap becomes a recorded decline ([#3042](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3042)).** One sentence in the common-type paragraph: no branch-level target-typing exists beyond the bare-`null` rule — a target-requiring branch form (collection literal, `new()` shorthand, bare case construction) is a compile error even in a target-typed position; remedy statement-form or typed arms. This settles the v0.238 gate round's "§20-side liftable" record in normative text, aligned with §35.3's identical decline for choice-case constructions in return-operand branch positions; the reopening bar and any eventual rule's three sub-questions (position set, arm agreement, §22.6/§28.3 interactions) are recorded on the issue. No compiler change — this ratifies implemented behavior.
- **Spec §17.7 — standard-library builtins have a closed constructor surface ([#2994](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2994)).** `new T(...)` on a builtin resolves only against a declared constructor: `Guid` and `IntPtr`/`UIntPtr` declare none and admit no `new` at any argument list (diagnostic names the declared producers — `Guid.Empty`/`Guid.NewGuid()`/`default(Guid)`; `IntPtr.Zero`/`default(IntPtr)`); the record-shaped reserved builtins (`ExceptionInfo`, `ReadOnlyStringSpan`) reject the undeclared parameterless form exactly as an identically-shaped user record would — which makes the [#2434](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2434) zero-fill degrade's null-`string` records unspellable. §14.2's generic-body `new T()` ≡ `default(T)` equivalence is explicitly unaffected. Stdlib §2.6 gains the one-line insurance note on `Guid`. Compiler-side rejection arm tracked on #2994.
- **Spec §23.5 + A.4 — index arguments are positional-only ([#2758](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2758)).** A Restrictions bullet rejects the named-argument form at the index position (the implementation had bound positionally and silently discarded the name — a silent wrong binding on multi-parameter indexers); indexer parameters may not declare default values, so §22.5's named-binding machinery is never reached, and indexer parameter names are declaration-internal (consistent with §23.4's type-list-only overloading). A.4's `Argument` comment records the shared-production rejection. The issue's other three sub-parts (`ref`/`out`/`owned` index arguments, `_`) were already settled by standing text and are deliberately not restated.
- **Spec §28.10/§31.2 — a `try`'s own `finally` is established at entry to the protected block ([#2892](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2892), Reading A).** Body-declared owned locals and `using var`s (established later) dispose **before** the `finally` on every exit edge, exactly as the desugared nested `try`/`finally` disposes them; cleanups established before the `try` run after it. §31.2 carries the echo. Reading A is what the reverse-establishment stack model forces (see the kernel note below); the historical [#1263](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1263) behavior rested on a pre-v0.182 sentence that most naturally read as the enclosing-local case, which both readings agree on.
- **Spec §15.4 — a dictionary-literal key is an element expression ([#2678](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2678)).** One clarifying sentence in the dictionary-literal paragraph, scoped to `Dictionary<K, V>` (the issue's shape; an `OwningDictionary`'s key positions are left to standing text — the gate caught the first draft's unscoped over-reach): the borrowing-family admission reaches key position, a fresh trivial-dispose key joins the literal tree as a fresh node exactly as a value-position node, and a class-typed key's equality contract is §8.3's default (identity) unless declared otherwise. Every sub-question had a standing answer (§4.8's equality-bearing constraint, §8.3's assigned identity hash, §4.8's stability-while-stored paragraph, §15.4's key-and-value-positions sentence); only the lowering is missing, tracked on #2678.
- **Spec §28.9 — accessor faces are lend-only, uniformly ([#2704](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2704); ratifies [#2694](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2694), rejects [#2703](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2703)'s direction).** A property or indexer read is a lend for every declared type kind — A4's rule for class/interface types, the same face for runtime-managed types: a getter never transfers a reclamation obligation, and §23.3's two accessor body spellings are semantically indistinguishable at every read site (the measured state had them disagreeing, with the statement-bodied producer form leaking per read). Fresh runtime-managed productions in getter bodies stay admissible; the implementation reclaims them — how is unspecified, per the section's lifecycle carve.
- **Spec §17.13 + A.4 — `ref _` is not a discard ([#2679](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2679) part B).** The discard composes with `out` only; after `ref`, `_` is an ordinary identifier per the three-position rule — it must resolve, and an unresolved `_` is the ordinary unknown-identifier error (an `out` parameter is pure output, so receive-and-ignore is coherent; a `ref` parameter reads its incoming value, which a discard could not supply). A.4's `ArgExpression` comment extends accordingly. The parser's `isDiscard` flag after `ref` was a parser bug, not a spec gap; the fix is tracked on #2679.
- **Spec §32.5 — the `owned`-parameter ban is extern-scoped ([#2732](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2732)).** The not-admitted bullet gains the scoping parenthetical: outside `extern` signatures the FFI-boundary classes are ordinary non-trivial-dispose classes, and an ordinary Bezel method may declare `owned c: CString` per §28.1. Ruling-only in substance (the type-kind chain was already in the text; comment 2 on the issue showed the reading was losable); unblocks the #2732 leak fix as its comment 1 laid out.
- **Spec §21.9 — the unused-result hard error extends to interface-typed results ([#3041](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3041)).** An interface's conformance set is open, so trivial-dispose is unprovable across modules; an interface-typed owned result is treated as possibly-non-trivial-dispose and dropping it unused is a hard error, not a warning — the previous scoping had the more abstract face carrying the weaker guard, so narrowing a return type to an interface silently weakened callers' protection. Every directed remedy is valid for interfaces (§17.13's interface discard disposes the runtime type). Compiler-side severity arm rides [#2680](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2680)'s recorded under-rejection work.
- **Stdlib §4.14/§4.15/§3.3 — `Slice(r: Range<int>)` on the five span-shaped types ([#2662](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2662)).** Declared at every declaration site of `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, `ArraySpan<T>`, `ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>` — closing the accepted-and-never-lowered form (silent wrong value 0) — and, for uniformity, on `ReadOnlyStringSpan` (the report flagged leaving it out as silent asymmetry; included). The contract is the view semantics: normalization against `Length` per spec §16.3's endpoint rules, `IndexOutOfRangeException` on out-of-range endpoints, empty range → empty span, equivalent to `Slice(start, length)` after normalization — same view, lifetime, and access mode as the receiver; the normalization validates eagerly, like the `AsSpan(r)` factories and unlike the v0.195 no-check direct constructors, an asymmetry the text states. The `AsSpan(r)` factories already took ranges; a span could be constructed by range but not sub-viewed by one. **Declined, recorded here:** a `span[r]` indexer form — `arr[r]` stays §15.6's compiler-recognized special equivalence on `Array<T>` only. Lowering tracked on #2662.
- **Stdlib §2.8/§2.9 — the comparison-interface findability note ([#2765](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2765)).** Primitives and `string` conform to `IComparable<T>`/`IEquatable<T>` at their own type only; both interfaces are invariant; no `IComparable<Object>`/`IEquatable<Object>` view exists — object-keyed equality is `Object.Equals` (§8.3). Ruling-only in substance: conformance is nominal and declared, and `string`/`string?` are distinct types, so all three questioned conversions (`IEquatable<Object>`, `IComparable<Object>`, `IComparable<string?>`) were already unlicensed; no new prohibition on nullable type arguments is written (a user `class C: IComparable<C?>` stays admissible). The conversion-predicate fix is tracked on #2765.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no axiom is spent and the register is unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones). Most items are derivations or clarifications of existing rules — degenerate-corner subtractions from universal quantifiers, term pinning, scope statements. [#2892](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2892)'s establishment-point sentence is a **derivation forced by the reverse-establishment stack model**: §28.3's established-at-declaration rule composed with §28.10's using-var-compiles-to-try/finally equivalence places a body-declared local's disposal inside the protected block, and Reading B admits no establishment-point formulation at all (ranking a finally at its clause's textual position inverts nesting for nested finallys; keeping it would require a category-ordered phase, the construct v0.182 abolished). [#2704](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2704) applies axiom A4 and the v0.190 calls-mint/storage-lends doctrine to the one storage face the text had not named. [#3041](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3041) extends an existing ceremony row under the v0.76 unknowability reasoning (unprovable ⇒ conservative), which a warn-only interface row had been applying in the lax direction.

**Migration.** Newly **rejected**: `as` at inline-array and unit targets (previously a silent wrong value / raw pointer; remedy `is` + copy-out, `is ()`); `new` on no-constructor builtins and the undeclared parameterless form on record-shaped reserved builtins (`new Guid()` → `Guid.Empty`/`default(Guid)` — mechanical, loud); named index arguments (`d[key := "k"]` — strictly bug-revealing, the name was silently ignored); `ref _` (both call paths, including the long-standing ordinary-call acceptance — a parser bug by the ruling, the three-position rule already excluded it; strictly bug-revealing, the written slot was unreadable); the three `string` → `IEquatable<Object>`/`IComparable<Object>`/`IComparable<string?>` conversions (already unlicensed by standing text — the rejection is the implementation catching up; removes the #2752 trap arm at its root); the post-colon `owned` parameter spelling (never grammatical — it existed only in the spec's own stray examples; **reverts the #3027 parser relaxation** — compiler-side revert-to-diagnostic tracked on [#3028](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3028)); and unused owned **interface-typed** results escalate warning → hard error — including lazy-query statement drops (`xs.Where(p);` as a bare statement), a deliberate inclusion: the statement provably does nothing. Newly **defined / changed observable behavior**: the `finally` establishment point (Reading A) — this **flips implemented, pinned behavior** for body-declared locals (the #1263 family's orderings); the spec text is the ruling and compiler catch-up is tracked on [#2892](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2892) for the local lanes (enclosing-resource orderings, #1567/#1598, survive); and the qualified-name default `ToString` for classes, enums, and non-auto-equality body records — flips observable rendering of every default class/enum line (the compiler renders unqualified today; catch-up on [#2934](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2934)), with the stdlib records gaining their defaults (the spans' positional form; `Range<T>`'s auto-equality body-record form) per [#2661](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2661)/[#2311](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2311); and the lend-only accessor face extended to runtime-managed types — no source-level change, but the two §23.3 getter spellings must agree and the statement-bodied getter's per-read leak disappears (compiler catch-up on [#2704](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2704)). Newly **admitted**: value-based constant narrowing across signedness (any integer-typed constant source, `uint`-constant → `int` included — source-gate widening tracked on [#2741](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2741), with [#2985](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2985)'s constant-aware applicability becoming required work); nested collection literals as dictionary **keys** (currently an ICE; lowering tracked on [#2678](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2678)); and `Slice(r: Range<int>)` on the five span-shaped types (lowering on [#2662](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2662)). **Doc-only records**: the §20 branch-target-typing decline (settling the v0.238-recorded §20-side liftable, [#3042](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3042) the lift tracker); the §32.5 extern-scoping parenthetical ([#2732](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2732)); the §2.8/§2.9 findability note ([#2765](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2765)). No grammar production changes — the A.4 additions are comments only; no anchor or section number moves. Guides untouched; all six keep their pins. Conformance corpus: `spec_0062`/`spec_0256` mirror the fixed stray `owned` lines and follow the docs fix (tracked with [#3028](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3028), `spec_0061` re-evaluated there); no other corpus flips. Spec-ahead-of-impl: every compiler-side flip above is tracked on its issue for the implementation lanes, each fix shipping a spec-cited regression test per `tests/README.md`.

**Gate round (same train).** The adversarial pass caught one misclassification in the newly-written text and four consistency defects, all fixed before landing: §8.5's universality sentence had listed `Range<T>` among the positional records (it is a compiler-intrinsic *body* record; its default is the auto-equality bullet — the two forms' output shapes coincide, but the cited rule was wrong, and the implementation lane would have been pointed at the wrong bullet); §21.9's per-arm lead-in still enumerated the old two-kind hard-error row ("non-trivial-dispose / `Task`") two lines above the amended three-kind row; the `Slice(Range)` contract stated equivalence to `Slice(start, length)` without stating the eager-validation asymmetry against §4.14's recorded v0.195 no-check rule; the §15.4 key sentence was unscoped and over-reached to `OwningDictionary` (where "exactly as a value-position node" would demand the owned key stdlib §4.9 forbids, and the literal-tree owner list covers no such node); and A.4's `ArgExpression` comment said the compiler "rejects `_` after `ref`" where §17.13's new sentence makes it an ordinary identifier that must resolve. Completeness repairs in step: the Migration section gained #2704's accessor-face item; §17.13's write-once corollary is scoped to assignment syntax (a `ref` argument can still write a declared `var _` location); `LambdaParam` joins the A.4 single-form enumeration (one of the three fixed strays *was* a lambda parameter); the closed-constructor-surface category is defined inline (any type the standard-library document declares); `Guid.Empty` is stated to be the all-zero value `default(Guid)` produces; §8.5's borrow claim is hedged for §8.6's boxed-receiver call-bounded copy; and `IndexerDecl`'s A.4 comment records the default-value over-admission alongside the existing `static` one.

### v0.242 changelog (v0.241 → v0.242)

**The elegance-review graduation program, train 1 of 6 — the checked-posture cluster (proposals 0078, 0079, and all eight items of 0086; owner-ruled 2026-08-11, all proposals accepted, all questions as recommended).** The common thread is making the checked posture total: the three places where a built-in operation, handed an out-of-domain input, silently computed something else — an integer-to-enum cast minting an unnameable "raw" value, a shift count reduced modulo the width, a computed-zero range step deferred to `GetEnumerator()` — now fault at the earliest point, under **one fault-type ruling decided jointly at all three sites** (0078 Q1 / 0079 Q2 / 0086 item 1's rider): a compile error when the operand is a §17.14 constant, `OverflowException` at runtime otherwise — no new exception type, no `ArgumentException` at expression sites that have no `ParamName` referent. Alongside the three rule changes, the 0086 consistency batch lands `mod=`, respells `sealed abstract` as the dedicated modifier `closed`, unifies the derived-property vocabulary on **hashable**, and records four made-but-unrecorded decisions in the rationale.

- **Spec §5.3/§5.4/§9.8/§10.4/§17.11/§19.6/§21.7/§28.8.1, Appendix C.1/C.7 — checked enum conversions (proposal 0078, [#3044](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3044); Q1–Q5 as recommended).** `E(n)` is checked against the declared constants: a constant operand equal to no declared constant is a compile error at the cast site (extending the former out-of-range constant error — the range check is subsumed, since out-of-range is a fortiori undeclared); a non-constant undeclared value raises `OverflowException` (Q1). *There is no value of an enum type that is not equal to a declared constant.* The branch tier is the **compiler-provided per-enum static member `FromUnderlyingOrNull(value: U): E?`** (Q2 — the stdlib §1 `*OrNull` tier's exact shape, a recorded deviation from the review's `TryFromUnderlying` sketch), declared in §10.4's static surface and documented at stdlib §9.9. The Q3 rider escalates §17.11's no-zero-constant `default(E)` warning to a **compile error** (covering `new T()` at such substitutions, §14.2, and default-initialized enum storage), closing the last producer of an undeclared value. §19.6's enum bullet gains the restored guarantee: *a statically exhaustive enum `case` cannot raise `MatchFailureException`*. **§21.7's enum row flips (Q5): the constants-coverage proof now grants statement-`case` totality** — the recorded disqualifier ("a non-constant cast `E(n)` produces a raw value") is repealed with the rule that repealed it, and the enum bullet joins condition (i)'s closed-value-space list. §10.4's `Name` example loses its defusing paragraph — the defensive `_ => "Unknown"` advice deletes with the hazard, and §10.4 now states the property's `case` is total. No unchecked entry point ships (Q4 — no flags idiom exists in the language, library, or corpus; `FromUnderlyingUnchecked` is recorded liftable behind flags-workload evidence, in the proposal and rationale §9.12, the new decision record). §5.3's nullable-cast composition carries the check by its existing sentence, with one added cross-reference; §17.14 needs no enum-cast change (enum casts were never constant expressions).
- **Spec §6.5/§6.6/§17.14, Appendix C.1 — shift counts: out-of-domain counts fault instead of silently masking (proposal 0079, [#3045](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3045); Q1–Q3 as recommended).** The count's domain is `0..width−1` of the **left operand's type**; a count outside it — negative, or ≥ width — is a compile error when constant and `OverflowException` at runtime (Q1/Q2). Discarding shifted-out bits stays silent and is stated as *the operation, exactly as `&` discards bits*. Deliberate modular counts are spelled visibly — `v << (k & 31)` / `& 63` — with the precedence note that the parentheses are already mandatory. The constant-count diagnostic for a negative count carries the direction-confusion note (Q3): a negative count does not reverse the shift — use the opposite operator. `<<=`/`>>=` inherit the fault through §6.6's desugaring. §17.14's evaluation list replaces "shift-count masking" with the domain fault: `const F := 1 << 64;` was a silent fold to `1` and is now a compile error, joining overflow and division by zero. User `operator <<`/`>>` overloads are untouched (§25 defines its own contracts). Rationale §14.7 is the decision record, with the precedent survey (Rust checked/Go/Zig/Swift — the post-C trend is uniformly away from silent masking) and the honest codegen note: the backend's unconditional count mask becomes one predicted compare+branch, and in-domain constant counts drop the check entirely.
- **Spec §16.3/§16.4/§16.6 — range step validated at construction (proposal 0086 item 1, [#3052](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3052); Q1 with the fault-type rider).** A computed step of zero faults **at the range expression** with the shared ruling's fault type (`OverflowException` — the drafted `ArgumentException` placeholder folded into the joint ruling: a range expression is no more a method boundary than a shift or a cast); the compile error widens from the literal to any constant-folded zero step (`step (2-2)`, `step K` — §17.14's posture). Since range expressions are the sole producer of `Range<T>` values (compiler-intrinsic record, no declared constructor, §17.7's closed-constructor-surface rule; the `Range<char>` deserialization path validates identically), **no zero-step `Range<T>` value can exist**: §16.3's direction-agreeing zero-step parenthetical, §16.4's at-`GetEnumerator` clause, and §16.6's equal-bounds step-0 sentence all delete — the limbo state they described is unconstructible.
- **Spec §6.6/§17.1/§17.2, Appendix A.6/C.10, §25.1 — `mod=` (item 2, Q2).** A.6's `AssignOp` gains the token (longest-match lexing: `mod` immediately followed by `=`; `x mod = y` stays a syntax error); §6.6's operator list, §17.1's assignment row, and the §25.1/C.10 not-user-overloadable lists gain it; §17.2's defense bullet ("`mod` is uncommon in compound forms") deletes. Semantics are §6.6's desugaring verbatim — target evaluated once, checked write-back, `DivideByZeroException` per §6.1, overload pass-through per §25.2 — no special case needed. The corpus honesty note stands in the proposal: zero real `x := x mod c` sites existed; uniformity won on rule-shape, not demand.
- **Spec §11.7/§12.5, Appendix A.3/B.1/C.1, and a docs-wide respell — `closed` replaces `sealed abstract` (item 3, Q3 — the batch's lowest-confidence recommendation, taken).** §11.7 defines the dedicated modifier: a `closed` class cannot be instantiated and cannot be subclassed outside its declaring module; it may declare abstract members without the `abstract` modifier (`closed` subsumes it — §12.5's must-be-abstract rule and C.1's row gain the rider), and combining `closed` with `abstract`, `sealed`, or `static` is a compile error, as is the former pair spelling — the diagnostic names `closed`. `closed` joins B.1's unconditionally-reserved list and A.3's `Modifier` production. All **26** `sealed abstract` occurrences across the normative documents respell (spec 16, rationale 8, Guide 03's 2 — the changelog's 10 are pinned history and stand); rationale §9.5 shrinks to the rename record (the "read the pair, not the words" defense retires with the pair). The **86 test-side occurrences are compiler-lane** migration, tracked with #3052's implementation work — a mechanical two-token respell.
- **Spec §2.8.2/§3.6/§8.3/§9.2/§9.8/§14.2/§19.3/§21.10/§35.7, Appendix C.1, stdlib §4/§5 — one name for the property: `hashable` (item 4, Q4).** The §3.6 row renames — **hashable (formerly *equality-bearing*)**, the parenthetical kept one revision for findability — and the ~39 `equality-bearing` occurrences across spec/stdlib/rationale respell mechanically, the compound `auto-equality-bearing` becoming **auto-hashable** with its §3.6 row (§9.2's mentions are all the compound form; the bare feature name "auto-equality" for the synthesized members keeps its spelling). §14.2's inline apology ("the keyword names the capability site, the property keeps its §3.6 name") deletes — the seam it recorded is gone; §14.2 still defers to §3.6 for the definition. The `hashable` keyword itself was already the B.2 contextual spelling; nothing changes at the constraint site.
- **Spec §2.7 — the enclosing-member decision table (item 6, Q6).** The drafted six-row table (head shape → member rank → effect, warning row included) lands after the paragraph's first sentence; presentation only — the prose keeps every normative definition, and the table was checked against each prose clause at landing.
- **Rationale records (items 5, 7, 8 — Q5/Q7/Q8; drafted text landed).** New §11.5: enum-prefix omission is a pattern-position affordance, deliberately not an expression-position one (patterns are scrutinee-typed, expressions are position-resolved; Swift's leading-dot machinery declined for the saving of one qualifier). New §11.6: `is` does not bind — the three-construct decomposition (`is`/`as`/`case`), the C# scoping swamp declined, the tight-scoped `is T name` variant pre-committed as the only acceptable lift; spec §12.7 gains the one-line pointer. §5.16 gains the value-element collection-literal inference decline (the literal-tree ownership rule is load-bearing; container choice is a silent decision; the annotation stays meaningful — with the reopening bar recorded).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** this train is **outside the ownership kernel** — no K-rule is touched, no axiom is spent, and the register is unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones). The three fault-site changes are §5/§6/§16 value-domain rules; the §21.7 totality flip is a §19/§21 pattern-rule change — a statement-exit grant keyed to an exhaustiveness proof, whose soundness note (the defined-trap lowering) already covers the enum grant unchanged — not a K-rule; `mod=` rides §6.6's existing desugaring, `closed` is a spelling, `hashable` a vocabulary unification, and items 5–8 are rationale prose.

**Migration.** Newly **rejected**: a constant `E(n)` equal to no declared constant (previously accepted, minting a raw value); `default(E)`, `new T()` at such substitutions, and default-initialized enum-typed storage for an enum with no zero-valued constant (previously a warning; remedy: declare the zero constant); constant out-of-domain shift counts — `1 << 33`, `x << -1`, `<<=` forms, and constant-expression folds (previously silently masked); a constant-folded zero range step (`step (2-2)`, `step K`) — previously a runtime fault at `GetEnumerator()`, now a compile error (§17.14's posture); and the `sealed abstract` spelling (respelled `closed`; the diagnostic names the new modifier). Newly **defined / changed observable behavior**: a runtime `E(n)` on an undeclared value raises `OverflowException` (previously produced a raw value — every enum value is now a declared value, and §19.6/§21.7's enum guarantees rest on it); a runtime out-of-domain shift count raises `OverflowException` (previously masked — in-domain shifts are bit-for-bit unchanged); a computed-zero range step faults at the range expression (previously `ArgumentException` at `GetEnumerator()` — strictly earlier, and strictly more programs fault: a constructed-but-never-iterated zero-step range now faults); statement-position enum `case` with constants coverage counts as exiting on every path (no trailing `return` needed — previously required). Newly **admitted**: `mod=`; the per-enum `FromUnderlyingOrNull` member (fresh name, zero collisions at v0.241); the `closed` modifier (one new reserved word — B.1). **Doc-only**: the `hashable` respell (~39 sites; the §3.6 row carries the one-revision findability parenthetical), the §2.7 table, the §12.7 pointer, and the rationale records (§9.12, §14.7, §11.5, §11.6, §5.16's append). The §5.4 out-of-range anchor is retained (repointed at the merged rule, earlier in §5.4) so pinned citations resolve; no anchor was deleted; new anchors added for the new sections. **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** compiler catch-up is tracked on [#3044](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3044)/[#3045](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3045)/[#3052](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3052), each fix shipping a spec-cited regression test per `tests/README.md`. The flip sets the proposals enumerate: 0079's four masking-pin files (`numeric_shift_nan_char_513_test.cpp`, `int_arithmetic_test.cpp`, `compound_assign_test.cpp`, `dict_compound_wider_rhs_2161_test.cpp` — constant-count pins invert to sema/lit rejections, variable-count pins to runtime-fault tests; no other test relies on masking); 0078's one flags-shaped artifact (the #2162 enum-operator-overload sema test) compiles and passes unchanged — its compositions land on declared values — while the raw-union pattern it exemplifies forecloses at runtime for undeclared unions; the `enum_cast_const_range_859` family's accepted/rejected verdicts survive (its accepted casts name declared constants), as does conformance mirror `spec_0005.bzl`; the `range_literal_step_zero_1628` lit family keeps its verdicts, with the runtime-computed case's fault moving to construction (the test gains its runtime assertion in the compiler lane); and the tests' 86 `sealed abstract` sites are the compiler-lane respell noted above. Guide 3 re-validated: its two `sealed abstract` sites respell, and §2's `_`-arm teaching was checked against the new enum reality — consistent, and now unconditionally true (0078's listed raw-value caveat had no referent at v0.241; nothing deleted); its pin moves to v0.242. Guides 1/2/4/5/6 are untouched and keep their pins. Proposals 0078/0079/0086 flip to superseded — graduated this revision — and their README rows move with them.

### v0.243 changelog (v0.242 → v0.243)

**The elegance-review graduation program, train B — the throwable re-ruling and the statically-certain-hazard lints (proposals 0080, 0081, and 0088 stage 1; owner-ruled 2026-08-11, all proposals accepted, all questions as recommended; directive "implement all into the spec and docs").** The train's common thread is loud-where-certain: the one silent hole in the catch-all closes (every throwable now derives from `Exception`, discharging the owner-review flag §31.1 had carried since v0.182), and the two guide-taught abandonment traps whose hazard the compiler can prove become normative warnings under the v0.238 Q1 doctrine — a statically-certain hazard emitted silently is the one place the language's silence stops being honest. 0088 contributes its cheap stage only: the concrete-selector cliff is recorded in the rationale and the `sourced` design stays shelved, evidence-gated.

- **Spec §31.1/§31.2.1/§31.2.3/§31.2.5/§17.12/§31.5/§22.15, Appendix C.5 — every throw operand is `Exception`-derived (proposal 0080, [#3046](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3046); Q1–Q3 as recommended).** §31.1 now requires the operand's static type, nullability not admitted, to be `Exception` or a class deriving from it; `Object`- and interface-typed operands stay rejected with the sharpened reason (no interface derives from `Exception`). The five permissive-ruling artifacts delete: §31.1's hedged parenthetical and owner-review flag (the catch-dispatch sentence now states that a bare `Exception` arm catches every catchable throwable — §31.4's uncatchable `StackOverflowException` the sole carve — and every throwable carries the §31.4 reporting surface); §31.2.1's `Object`-base binding carve (the simplified rule: the bound name types as the nearest common base, always `Exception`-family — the `Object` case is unreachable under single inheritance); §31.2.3's no-universal-catch-all caveat (a bare `Exception` arm at the end **is the catch-all**; the sole residual carve is the uncatchable `StackOverflowException`, §31.4 — a liveness fact, not a typing one); §31.2.5's suppression asterisk ("suppress all catchable exceptions" — no non-`Exception` carve); and §22.15's carve-out parenthetical (now stating the requirement subtracts nothing from the carve-out's reachable set — `Exception` and every built-in are trivial-dispose). The consequential tightening is stated, not implied (Q1: **error**, not warning): a catch arm naming a non-`Exception`-family class type is a compile error (**provably dead** — or, for `Object`, universally matching, the catch-all's own job), and the generic arm-parameter rule requires an **`Exception`-derived class bound** (`where TEx: Exception` — the formerly idiomatic form is now the required one), rejected at the generic declaration exactly where the class-bound check already sat. §17.12, §31.5, and Appendix C.5 reword their operand-type conditions in step. The ownership seam is untouched — verified clause-by-clause against the v0.242 text per the proposal's §3: K3.8/K4.2's announced-kill status, the moved-from machinery, the exception-ownership rules and both dispose-after-arm exemptions, and the pure-throw carve-out's trivial-dispose ground are all base-class-blind. Rationale gains **§11.7**, the decision record, beside §11.3's `catch`-is-`case` record (Q3). Stdlib: no changes (§2.17's hierarchy already complies). The docs corpus was already clean (all 50 normative-doc `throw new` sites are `Exception`-family — proposal §4); a beyond-the-deletion-list sweep for survivals ("not only `Exception`", "any class", throwable mentions) found §31.2.3's example comment ("catch-all for Exception-derived throwables"), tightened to "the catch-all", and Appendix C.7's two catch-arm entries — the `Object`-base binding carve and the class-type generic bound — rewritten to the simplified binding rule and the `Exception`-derived bound.
- **Spec §15.4/§28.11/§30.10 — lint A: fresh non-trivial stores on borrowing collections (proposal 0081, [#3047](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3047); Q1/Q4 as recommended).** §15.4's existing fresh-trivial store lint extends to the **full fresh-unbound-owned-temporary set of class type** (Q1 — not task-only, which would have left the non-trivial/non-task middle band as the only undiagnosed fresh store): a `new` expression, a collection literal, an `owned`-returning call result, a `move` result, or a `Task`-family call result in `Add`/`Insert`/indexer-set position (key and value positions alike) on a borrowing-family collection **must warn**, the hazard stated per family — trivial-dispose: the compiler's free and a retained dangling reference; `Task`-family: the task's disposal — the operation *abandoned*, its owned result disposed on arrival (§30.5) — with the slot dangling besides (#1813's trap); other non-trivial: the value's disposal and the dangling slot. The remedies are the named-holder binding and the owning family (`Task.WhenAllOwned` for dynamic fan-in, stdlib §6.7). The admission itself is unchanged — the literal-only-rejection asymmetry, the K4.3 residual, and program acceptance are all invariant. Q4: one lint, one paragraph — §15.4 carries the rule, §28.11's store paragraph cross-references it (its fresh-argument sentence generalized from trivial-dispose to the full set), §30.10's abandonment-idioms paragraph gains the boundary sentence (a borrowing slot is not a third abandonment idiom).
- **Spec §29.11, stdlib §5 — lint B: class-element terminal accessors over minting pipelines (proposal 0081, [#3047](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3047); Q3/Q4 as recommended).** A stdlib §5 class-element terminal accessor or no-selector aggregation (`First`/`Last`/`Single`/`ElementAt` with the `*OrNull` and predicate forms, `Min()`/`Max()`) **must warn** iff the receiver's statically-tracked provenance — §29.11's own single-consumption flow trace, followed through the deferred operators — roots at a **directly-called same-compilation-unit iterator with at least one enumerator-owned fresh yield** (§29.2's classification): the returned borrow is dead on arrival, the element having been disposed with the terminal's internal enumerator (Guide 5's trap #4). All-fresh yields state the fault as certain; mixed yields state "may not survive". The must-not-fire shapes are normative in §29.11's predicate: concrete-collection roots, materializer results (the trace stops at `ToArray()`'s owned result), statically-untracked interface-typed receivers, cross-module iterators, and value/`string`/runtime-managed elements all stay silent; `Aggregate`'s seed leg never participates. **Q3: same-unit-only in v1, recorded liftable** — carrying yield classification in the artifact interface (§2.8.2) is the recorded widening, not taken; the checked-mode backstop remains the cross-module guard. Stdlib §5's accessor contract carries the one-sentence must-warn pointer at the classification it rides. **Q2 (shared with lint A): no per-site suppression spelling** — binding-first and materialize-first are the suppressions, each converting the program from hazardous to sound; project-level lint tuning stays the only knob. Rationale §5.28's Q1 record flips its follow-on from "not taken" to **taken at v0.243** and gains the second-and-third-instances paragraph, so the three lints — the v0.238 trivial-store lint, A, and B — read as one doctrine with one design shape. Zero existing corpus sites fire either lint (proposal §1.4/§2.4) — the diagnostics' entire effect is on future code.
- **Rationale §5.7 — the concrete-selector cliff, recorded (proposal 0088 **stage 1 only**, [#3054](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3054); Q1/Q2 as recommended).** §5.7 gains the cliff paragraph: the concrete selector signature (`static method Pick(a: Res, b: Res): Res`) is unwritable while the semantically identical generic twin compiles under the bare-type-parameter rule — the two-owners argument for the rejection preserved in full — and the sanctioned remedy is to **generify**, a fact the declaration-site diagnostic is directed to name (compiler-lane). The announcement gap is a **recorded liftable, not taken**: the `sourced` return-marker design stays in proposal 0088, gated on the first real concrete-selector want (the 0051 Part B evidence posture); auto-detection stays declined on the record's own grounds. **No spec rule changes**; the proposal does not flip to superseded — it stays accepted with stage 1 graduated.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no axiom is spent and the register is unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones). 0080 is **§31-side typing** — one subtype-check precondition at the throw site plus two dead-shape rejections at arms and bounds; the clause-by-clause verification above confirms zero contact with any K-rule, freeze list, or axiom (the announced-kill clause, K4.2's set, and the dispose-after-arm machinery are quantified over owned class instances, never over base classes). 0081's two lints **extend a K-adjacent recorded posture** — the v0.238 Q1 lint, whose K4.3-residual/K4.1-backstop admission they leave verbatim — and add **no rule**: both are normative warnings keyed on classifications the kernel machinery already computes (K8 boundaries and the calls-mint family for A; §29.11's provenance trace and §29.2's yield classification for B), and neither changes what compiles. 0088 stage 1 is rationale prose.

**Migration.** Newly **rejected** (0080): `throw` of a class not deriving from `Exception` — the diagnostic names the remedy (derive the class from `Exception`, one token at the declaration, or throw an `Exception`-derived wrapper); a catch arm naming a non-`Exception`-family class type (provably dead — or, naming `Object`, universally matching, the bare `Exception` arm's job; delete the arm or fix the type); a generic catch-arm parameter bounded by a class outside the `Exception` family (remedy `where TEx: Exception` or a derived bound). Newly **warned** (0081, both families with zero existing corpus hits): fresh unbound owned temporaries of class type — the `Task` family included — in `Add`/`Insert`/indexer-set position on borrowing-family collections (§15.4); class-element terminal accessors whose receiver provenance roots at a same-unit fresh-yield iterator (§29.11, stdlib §5). Newly **defined**: §31.2.1's simplified multi-type binding rule — for every program that remains accepted it types identically (all-`Exception` lists already resolved to their nearest common base); the `Object`-fallback rejection becomes unreachable rather than repealed-with-changed-behavior. **Doc-only**: §31.2.3/§31.2.5/§22.15/§17.12/§31.5/C.5 deletions and rewordings; §28.11/§30.10's cross-reference sentences; the rationale records (§11.7 new; §5.7's cliff paragraph; §5.28's taken-follow-on and doctrine paragraphs); 0088 stage 1 in its entirety (the remedy diagnostic is compiler-lane). No grammar production changes (Appendix A untouched); no anchor or section number moves (one new anchor, rationale §11.7). Docs corpus: clean — every normative `throw new` site was already `Exception`-family; no example changes. Guides: Guide 4 §2 and Guide 5 §6 now teach their traps as *warned* (the diagnostic and its remedies), re-traced against the landed lint text; their pins move to v0.243. Guide 2 was verified per the proposal — zero non-`Exception` teachings exist, nothing to delete — and keeps its pin, as do Guides 1/3/6. **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** [#3046](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3046) — the throw-site subtype check, the dead-arm and `Exception`-bound errors, and the simplified binding typing, plus the test-corpus migration the proposal measured: **224 sites across 38 files** in total, of which the two deliberate permissive-rule pin files hold ~9, leaving **~215 incidental sites** (`class E end E;` → `class E: Exception end E;`, mechanical and semantics-preserving) to land **ahead of the rule flip as a no-op commit** (Q2 — the 0077-Q4 staging pattern, compiler-lane), and the **two deliberate permissive-rule pin files flip polarity** into regression tests *for* the new rule (`tests/sema/catch_multitype_no_common_base_v182_test.cpp`, the `Object`-base carve pin, and `tests/lit/sema/sema_throw_operand_type__non_exception_class_ok_31_1.bzl`, the any-class-ok pin); [#3047](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3047) — lint A (S: widen the warned type set over the existing store-position/K8 classifications, per-family texts) and lint B (M: the §29.11-trace/§29.2-classification join and the compiler-known accessor keying), with the fire/silent test matrix from the proposal's must-not-fire tables (the materialized receiver foremost); [#3054](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3054) — stage 1's declaration-site remedy diagnostic (XS: the plain-parameter shape test selecting selector-vs-factory remedies). Each fix ships a spec-cited regression test per `tests/README.md`. Proposals 0080 and 0081 flip to **superseded — graduated v0.243**; 0088's status becomes **accepted — stage 1 graduated v0.243, stage 2 owner-gated**; the README rows move with them.
