### v0.244 changelog (v0.243 → v0.244)

**The elegance-review graduation program, train C — the reserved discard, `equality skip`, and the pure-body `for` widening (proposals 0083, 0084, and 0085; owner-ruled 2026-08-11, all proposals accepted, all questions as recommended).** The train's common thread is deleting indefensible corners by reusing machinery the language already has: the `_` token stops being two things (a discard in three positions, an identifier everywhere else — the split that produced a readable-but-never-assignable binding and the v0.241 `ref _` ruling) and becomes one thing everywhere; record auto-equality gains the per-member escape its sibling synthesis package has had since v0.117, so a cache field stops costing the five-member road; and §22.15 rule 5 extends to concrete array and string sources the exact normative-elision move it had already made once for `Range<T>`, taking the index-loop tax off the most common loop shape in the language.

- **Spec §1.3/§17.13/§21.1/§21.4/§21.5/§22.4/§27.3/§28.10, Appendix A.1/A.4/A.6/A.7/B.1, Appendix C.1 — `_` is reserved: always a discard or wildcard, never a declarable or readable name (proposal 0083, [#3049](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3049); Q1–Q4 as recommended).** §1.3's "valid identifier name everywhere it appears as a name" sentence deletes; the bare token is reserved (A.1's `Identifier` production splits — `Letter IdentCont* | "_" IdentCont+` — so it never matches the bare token; B.1 carries the punctuation-like reservation note — not a keyword in the word sense, B.3's discipline applied permanently). **§17.13 shrinks** (measured heading-to-heading: 108 lines at v0.243, 97 at v0.244 — and that is *after* absorbing the new ignore-forms and rejected-positions paragraphs and the anonymous-binding subsection): the write-once corollary, the `var _ := 5; Console.WriteLine(_);` worked example, the binding-vs-discard recap's third form, and the v0.241 `ref _` resolution paragraph all delete — `ref _` is now an unconditional compile error ("a `ref` argument reads its operand, which a discard cannot supply"), the #2679 corner deleted rather than ruled. The per-position landings: `var _ := e;` and `const _ := e;` are compile errors with the two-remedy diagnostic (`_ := e;` end-of-statement, or `using var _ := e;` scope-end — §21.1, §17.13's rejected-positions list); `out var _` errors pointing at `out _`, which is unchanged (§22.4); declarations named `_` — method/constructor parameters foremost (**Q2: error**, parameter names are call-site-addressable API surface, §22.5, carried by the artifact interface), fields, properties, methods, types, modules, enum constants, choice cases, loop labels (§21.5's label sentence conformed), aliases — all error; expression-position `_` errors (nothing can bind it). **Newly defined as true ignores** (binding nothing): lambda parameters — `lambda(_, _) => 0` legal, the slot still contributing to the function type, no modifier or annotation composing (§27.3, A.7's new `LambdaParam` alternative) — and `for var _` (§21.4, A.6), with owning-iteration disposal per §29.2 unchanged (the unbound element disposed per iteration exactly as a bound-but-unused one). **Q3: `using var _` kept and redefined as the anonymous owning binding** (§17.13's new subsection, §28.10, A.6): scope-end disposal timing unchanged, no name bound, `_` not in scope after it — the one `_` form that owns storage; adoption (`using var _ := owned x;`) composes. **Q4: ascribed ignores rejected** — one rule everywhere, "a bare ignore takes its type from context, never an annotation" (`out _`'s existing rule, extended to `for var _: T` and lambda ignores; A.6/A.7 grammar comments record the over-admit-and-reject or structural exclusion per site). A.4's `ArgExpression` comment retires its "ordinary identifier elsewhere" clause (the `"_"` alternative is now the only reading in argument position); A.4's `Param` comment records the parameter rejection and the lambda contrast. The discard statement, `out _`, pattern/`when` wildcards, announced-consume semantics, and the type-keyed legality list (Task rejection included) are all **untouched** — the proposal moves the boundary of what `_` can be, not what discards do. Rationale §3.2 is conformed and gains the decision record: its closing line — "`_` is a sink, not a binding. It cannot be read." — becomes true as written (the spec's own worked example had falsified it). Guides: swept for `var _`/discard teaching — **none teaches `var _`** (the proposal's corpus table predicted this; verified), and every guide `_ := x;` teaching survives unchanged; no guide pins move for 0083.
- **Spec §9.1/§9.2/§9.3/§9.8/§35.7/§3.6, Appendix A.3/A.4/B.1/B.2/C.1 — `equality skip`: per-member exclusion from record auto-equality, mirroring `serialized skip` (proposal 0084, [#3050](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3050); Q1–Q4 as recommended).** The grammar is one production beside its sibling — `EqualityClause ::= "equality" "skip"` (A.3), attached at `PositionalField`, the auto-property alternative of `PropertyDecl` (fixed order `SerializedClause? EqualityClause?`, each at most once), **`FieldDecl`** (the point of the proposal: an explicit field is §9.2's disqualifier, and the clause is what un-disqualifies it), and `CaseField` (**Q2: choice payload fields included** — §35.7 already defers to §9.2's list, and not extending would have minted a fresh asymmetry); not on `EnumConstant` (not a component), not on `ChoiceCase` (the discriminant — skipping it is incoherent), and a compile error on computed properties, methods, statics, and class fields (§9.8's inert-annotation discipline). `equality` joins B.1/B.2 as a contextual keyword — exactly `serialized`'s row; only the `skip` form exists (no rename, no `optional` — the vocabulary is one word, closed). §9.2's new subsection carries the normative statement: a skipped storage component is removed from the membership computation — out of `=`/`<>`, `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, exempt from the admissible-component requirement, unable to disqualify — while every other role (storage, `with` target, `ToString` rendering — **Q4: renderings are not contracts, one clause one effect** — and serialization participation) is untouched. **The eligibility-gate sub-choice as landed (Q1, §2 consequence 2):** where §9.8 reuses §9.2's membership conditions for can-synthesis-run eligibility, a member skipped by *either* package's clause is structurally absent — which is what keeps a record with an equality-skipped explicit cache field serialization-eligible with no second clause — while **participation never crosses** (`equality skip` does not hide a member from the wire; `serialized skip` does not change what `=` compares; §9.8's interaction rule states both). The gate is **one-directional** — §9.8's serialization gate reads both packages' skips; the equality package's own gate reads `equality skip` only, a `serialized skip` never rescuing an equality-inadmissible component (gate-corrected at landing; the gate-round record below). The override disqualifier stays unrescuable (the author who takes over equality takes over all of it; the clause on such a record is meaningful, not an error); hashing coherence holds by construction (the generated `=` and `GetHashCode` compute over the same reduced set — §8.3's contract cannot break); **Q3: all-members-skipped is defined with no diagnostic**, taking §9.2's zero-auto-property semantics verbatim. §9.3 admits the clause on positional fields, and §9.1's "all positional fields" equality/hash bullets are conformed to the participating set; §3.6's auto-hashable row notes the post-skip membership computation and rule 3 gains the breaking-change reach (adding or removing the clause on a public member flips comparison and hash results — the artifact interface carries it as it carries `serialized` clauses). Rationale: §18's "Asymmetric record auto-equality customization" deferral resolves with the shipped pointer, and §7.5 is the new decision record (the gate choice, the declined alternatives — type-level lists, visibility-keyed auto-exclusion, other spellings, custom-equality clauses — and the corpus honesty note: no workaround debt existed; the all-or-nothing rule deterred the shape rather than taxing it). Guide 3 gains the cache-field idiom lines; its pin moves to v0.244.
- **Spec §22.15/§29.2 — pure-body `for` over concretely-typed arrays and strings: §29.2's elision becomes normative (proposal 0085, [#3051](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3051); Q1–Q4 as recommended).** Rule 5's amendment lands as drafted: over a source whose **static type at the body's own check site** is concretely `Array<T>`, `OwningArray<T>`, **class-typed `OwningBuffer<T>` (Q1: included — the one §4.14 family member on the protocol path; excluding it would be a one-type hole)**, or `string`, §29.2's admitted protocol elision is **the normative semantics inside a pure body**: the compiler emits the direct indexed loop — a bounds read and per-element reads, rule-1 material — and constructs no enumerator; iteration-variable type and state are §29.2's for the elided form (value copy for value elements and `string`; element borrow for class-typed elements — `OwningArray<T>` default iteration stays borrowing). **Q4: the bounds read is framed neutrally** — an intrinsic length fact of the concrete layout, exactly as the counted loop's endpoints; where an implementation lowers it as the accessor call, that lowering is admissible exactly where the accessor is `pure`-declared (`string.Length`/indexer, `Array<T>`/`OwningArray<T>` `Count`), and elsewhere (`OwningBuffer<T>.Length`, the element indexers) the intrinsic-layout reading is the only admissible lowering (gate-corrected; the record below). **Q2: generic sources stay rejected** — a type-parameter-typed source, even one every instantiation substitutes at a concrete sequence type, errors at the declaration: §22.15's checking discipline is single-pass over bodies ("checked once, at its declaration"), and per-instantiation loop admission would make body-statement admissibility substitution-dependent — a checker-architecture change for one loop form; interface-typed sources (`IEnumerable<T>` included) stay rejected on the elision's own condition, with the remedy at both rejected source kinds being a concretely-typed source — no index-loop spelling is available inside a pure body at such sources (gate-corrected; the record below). The §29.12 structural-modification fault is preserved by the elision as everywhere — and inside a pure region it is statically unreachable (no admitted operation can structurally modify a collection), so an implementation may omit the check there with no observable difference. Spans were verified already admitted (rule 5's existing text; nothing restated); **Q3: `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` stays rejected**, deferred to its severable stdlib-contract issue (its lowering is index-shaped but through interface-dispatched accessors not `pure`-declared — a §4.16 contract question, per the proposal's direction). §29.2's closing paragraph carries the one-sentence pure-body cross-reference. Rationale §9.7 gains the one-paragraph record (the `Range<T>` template, the decisive single-pass argument, the deferred neighbors). Guide 6 §6's "the rule that surprises people" passage is rewritten — the everyday `for var c in text` now compiles in the `CountOf` example, and the index-loop teaching is retired (the generic-source remedy is a concretely-typed source; the record below); Guide 6's pin moves to v0.244, its §6 re-traced against the landed rule text.

### v0.245 changelog (v0.244 → v0.245)

**The elegance-review graduation program, train D — the statics vocabulary and the generic-leaves retirement (proposals 0087 and 0089; owner-ruled 2026-08-11, all proposals accepted, all questions as recommended).** The train's common thread is deleting presentation debt whose defense had expired: the three curated mutable-statics lists — related in normative text by prose set arithmetic ("this set is form-(i) *minus* … *minus* … *plus* the three members") — become three one-line derivations from four per-type stdlib facts, with all thirty memberships proven identical before landing; and §19.6's generic-leaves determination rule — two pages of §19's hardest text serving zero organic corpus uses since choices re-homed the value-shaped sum — retires by deletion, with the reopening shape pinned.

- **Spec §22.12 rules 2(i)/2(iii)/4, §28.13, §22.13, §30.12, §32.8, Appendix C.11; stdlib §1, §2.16, §4.19, §6.2–§6.5, §6.9, §6.11; rationale §12.13 (new) and §12.8's presentation note; Guide 4 §8; `scripts/check_docs.sh` — the statics-and-sharing taxonomy re-derived from per-type facts (proposal 0087, [#3053](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3053); Q1–Q4 as recommended).** Four orthogonal per-type facts, defined once at stdlib §1 and declared on a **Facts** line at each of the ten types any list mentioned — **synchronized** (internally synchronized *and* safe to reach from every domain), **immutable** (deeply immutable after construction), **self-distributing** (has its own sanctioned distribution channel), **displacement-unbounded** (a stranded overwrite-displaced value is payload-scaled) — replace the three curated lists as the normative carrier, and the sets become derived views: **form (i)** = synchronized ∧ ¬displacement-unbounded; **rule 4's warning-suppression set** (historically the *suppression list*) = synchronized ∨ immutable; **§28.13's `Shared`-payload synchronized set** = (synchronized ∨ immutable) ∧ ¬self-distributing. §28.13's minus/minus/plus set-arithmetic sentence and its "this seven-type enumeration is normative" sentence retire; rule 4's "deliberately not form-(i)" justification collapses into the **displacement-unbounded** grants at the type fact lines, which keep the recorded reasons (the lock plus its entire interior; the whole array; the `Task?`-cache-acceptance contrast; no-use-case-for-reassignment). **Q1:** the four names as proposed — `displacement-unbounded` kept, naming the exact recorded cost. **Q2:** the no-silent-growth clause transformed, not weakened — sets grow only by **fact rulings**, each stating the facts it grants and confronting every derived-set consequence in its record; the old vice-versa protection is carried structurally by the two facts that ever made the sets diverge. **Q3:** `scripts/check_docs.sh` gains check 3b — recomputing the spec's three membership parentheticals from the stdlib fact lines, cross-checking the three formulas at every carrier (stdlib §1's symbolic statements and the spec's prose statements against the script's own derivations) and the full fact-line roster (the ten typed lines plus the named none-declaring types), and failing the docs gate on divergence — landed with this train, negative-tested. **Q4:** informative membership parentheticals kept beside each formula (tagged per set: "derived membership (form-(i))/(warning-suppression)/(shared-payload), informative — currently …", each closing with the machine-checked pointer to check 3b), so the reader needs no second document open. The review critic's three-fact conjecture is recorded refuted: without the fourth fact the data-owning locks would silently join form (i) — a behavior change; the fourth fact is what keeps the re-derivation exact. The **reproduction table is the evidence core, re-verified against the landed v0.244 text at graduation: all thirty memberships (ten types × three sets) identical — zero delta.** Rule 2(iii)'s cross-reference re-aims at the fact ("the payload-scaled cost the displacement-unbounded fact names"); §22.13's and §30.12's set references conform (warning-suppression set; the locks' memberships carried by their fact grants); C.11's two statics rows conform to the fact vocabulary; Guide 4 §8 teaches the four facts and three formulas — strictly less to hold in mind than three lists; rationale §12.13 is the decision record. A future admission becomes one fact ruling instead of three coordinated list edits, with the exclusion questions (self-distributing? displacement-unbounded?) posed by the vocabulary itself at granting time.
- **Spec §19.6 (the "Generic leaves" determination subsection deletes; the sealed-hierarchy bullet's generic clause shrinks), §35.6, Appendix C.7; rationale §8.2, §9.6 — the generic-leaves determination rule retires by deletion (proposal 0089, [#3055](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3055); Q1–Q4 as recommended: retire; deletion in one revision, no deprecation window — there are no users to serve one; the existential pattern as the recorded reopening shape; the §35.6 steering).** The v0.196 rule — per-leaf root-instantiation matching under exact invariant identity, constraint filtering, the exempt/determined/undetermined classification, three-valued rigid-parameter identity, the §7.10 `?`-pre-image split, the census prohibition: ~42 dense spec lines plus worked examples — deletes; the replacement subsection ("Generic hierarchies: leaf coverage is not attempted", the anchor retained) states the blanket rule: when a closed hierarchy's root or any leaf is generic, the compiler attempts no leaf-inhabitation analysis against the scrutinee type — no arrangement of type-pattern arms is a static proof, including the ground-leaf sub-case (every leaf non-generic and named) the retired rule's exempt classification did discharge — the `case` is completable only by an irrefutable arm (an unguarded `_` or unguarded untyped `var`), and the warning names the hierarchy and prescribes the `_` arm and — for value-shaped sums — a `choice`, whose exhaustiveness is counted by case name and needs no `_` (Q4's steering, subsumed into the replacement text; §35.6 carries the pointer back). This is the previously-rejected blanket reading adopted **with its rejection's premise expired**, said explicitly rather than in silent contradiction of the v0.196 reasoning (rationale §8.2): the recorded defense — "regresses the determined shape, the canonical sealed-match idiom" — lost its inhabitant when v0.200's choices re-homed the value-shaped sum and the canonical `Result` became a choice (stdlib §2.20); the determined shape's flagship no longer exists as a class hierarchy anywhere in the tree. **Q3:** the recorded reopening shape is the **existential pattern** — a type pattern matching a generic leaf at *any* instantiation, which would make generic-leaf coverage expressible with no determination computation — pinned in the replacement text and rationale §8.2 so a future re-ask starts there, not at restoring determination (the full design stays in git history and the pinned v0.196 entry). The §21.7 consequence was **re-derived against the v0.242-restructured totality rule and vanishes by flow-through**: condition (i) consumes §19.6's proofs, the sealed-hierarchy proof now simply never completes for a generic hierarchy, and the demanded irrefutable arm re-grants totality through the irrefutable-arm bullet — no §21.7 text change was needed. §19.6's choice bullet and §35.6 drop their "determination" phrasing (generic choices need no per-instantiation analysis); the named-destructure paragraph drops its determined-instantiation parenthetical; C.7 — which carried no determination row (verified end-to-end) — gains the new invariant row for the blanket rule.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** no axiom is spent and the register is unchanged (twelve live, two tombstones). **0087 is doc-structural with a proven zero-delta reproduction** — no rule of conduct changes anywhere: the store-semantics triple, the ownership-discharge exemption, every warning text, and every membership are preserved verbatim or restated; the only normative movement is which sentences *carry* the memberships (fact lines plus formulas instead of curated enumerations), and the thirty-membership reproduction was re-verified against the landed v0.244 text before this entry was written. **0089 deletes a §19-side pattern-exhaustiveness rule — outside the kernel:** the affected surface is `case` coverage analysis and §21.7 reachability, not ownership; the owning-match machinery (the K5 freeze, §35.5's triggers), the discard rules, and every K row were checked and none cites the determination rule or the deleted subsection. Honest note: 0089 does change what compiles (below) — it is normative retirement with compiler catch-up, not doc-structural.

**Migration.** **0087 — behavior-invariant, prominently: zero programs change meaning.** No warning appears or disappears, no store semantics move, no membership changes — the fact lines are a *restatement* of rulings already recorded, proven by the 10×3 reproduction table (thirty of thirty identical, re-verified at graduation). Compiler: **no changes required or permitted** ([#1393](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1393)'s enforcement remains correct as-is); [#3053](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3053) carries no compiler work — the check_docs.sh derivation check (Q3) is this train's own deliverable, landed here. Newly rejected/warned/accepted (0087): nothing. **0089 — newly warned:** an exhaustive `case` with no irrefutable arm over a closed hierarchy whose root or any leaf is generic — previously provable in the determined shape *and* in the exempt ground-leaf sub-case (a generic root whose every leaf is non-generic and named, discharged by the retired rule's exempt classification) — now draws the non-exhaustiveness warning in expression position. **Newly rejected (0089):** a callable ending with a statement-`case` over such a hierarchy that relied on §21.7's totality grant now draws the existing missing-return diagnostic (remedy: the `_` arm, which then carries the return or throw). **Zero organic corpus uses** (the study's §4 evidence, re-verified at graduation under both the `sealed abstract` and landed `closed` spellings): the stdlib has no generic — or any — closed class hierarchy (its closed sums are choices and enums); the docs had exactly one generic closed root outside pinned history (§19.6's own deleted example); the guides have none; the only users are the rule's own spec-derived test family — **six files, which flip per the study's enumeration**: `tests/sema/case_exhaustiveness_test.cpp` (the #1816/#1862/#1874 determination suite — determined-shape acceptances become warning-expectation tests; the rigidity and `?`-split distinctions retire with the rule), `tests/sema/case_type_test_instantiation_1913_test.cpp`, `tests/codegen/generic_type_test_arg_1843_test.cpp`, `tests/codegen/result_stdlib_2047_test.cpp` (a pre-choice name-collision test, not a determination user — verify-only), `tests/lit/sema/case_exhaust_generic_leaf_1816__qmark_split_undetermined_warning_spec_19_6_7_10.bzl` (retires with the distinction it pins), and `tests/lit/sema/sema_ret_path__exhaustive_generic_case_stmt_no_trailing_return_total_spec_21_7_11_7.bzl` (flips to demand the irrefutable arm). Runtime behavior: unchanged everywhere — the deleted proof was sound, and arm selection never depended on it. **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** [#3055](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3055) — delete the ~1,000-line determination machinery in `src/sema/ExprTypecheck.cpp` (the helper family at ~648–1450: ground-type walk, tri-state component matching, the `?`-split solver, ground-solution constraint checking, obligation formatting; the exhaustiveness-checker integration at ~2030–2260), replace it with the not-attempted-with-remedy classification (a few lines; the warning text naming the hierarchy, the `_` remedy, and the choice steering is the new surface), and remove the §21.7 checker arm that consumed determined-leaf proofs; the six test files flip as enumerated, each shipping spec-cited per `tests/README.md`. **Doc-only:** the §35.6 rewording; the §32.8 set-reference conforms; rationale §8.2's decision record, §9.6's two retirement annotations, §12.8's presentation note, and the new §12.13; Guide 4 §8's fact-vocabulary rewrite (its pin moves to v0.245; the other guides are untouched and keep their pins); the C.7 row addition and C.11 row conforms; the stdlib fact lines and §1 vocabulary. Anchors: none deleted (`sec-exhaustiveness-generic-leaves` is retained on the replacement subsection; new anchors `sec-statics-and-sharing-facts` in the stdlib and `sec-statics-facts-vocabulary` in the rationale); no section numbers move. Proposals 0087 and 0089 flip to **superseded — graduated v0.245**; the README rows move with them.

<a id="sec-v0-246-changelog"></a>
### v0.246 changelog (v0.245 → v0.246)

**The elegance-review graduation program, train E — the transfer-marker unification (proposal 0090, [#3056](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3056); owner-ruled 2026-08-11: adopt via hard flip, Q1–Q6 as recommended). The largest train of the program, and deliberately spelling-only: `move x` becomes the single consume action at every named location, and `owned` becomes purely declarative.** Through v0.245 the reader learned a three-way spelling rule split by location kind — `owned` for bindings (`M(owned x)`, `var y := owned x;`, `case owned x of`, arm-result `owned x`), `move` for fields and slots (`move x.f`, `move coll[i]`), nothing at announced targets — while the same token `owned` meant *state* at every declaration and *action* at every marker site: `TakeOwnership(owned resource)` was, character for character, a callee describing its parameter's obligation in one file and a caller performing an invalidation in another. The study's reading-model argument — the cost the v0.169 record never weighed, which is what licensed reopening it — is now the rule: after this revision `owned` appears **only** where a slot is described (parameters, fields, returns, `out owned var x`, function-type slots, choice payloads, `[N owned]`, `static owned readonly` — every declaration position, untouched) and `move` **only** where an action occurs, location-uniform: binding, field, or slot — "transfer out, leave moved-from."

- **Spec §14.4/§17.13/§17.15/§19.2/§20/§21.1/§22.3/§22.6/§22.16/§25, §28.3 (K3.4, K3.13, axiom A7's register row, the producers rows, *Move semantics for owned locals*, the freeze and must-use passages), §28.8.1, §28.10, §28.11, §29.2, §29.8, §30.1, §30.5, §30.7, §30.11, §30.14/§30.15, §35.3, §35.5, Appendix A.4/A.6/A.7, Appendix C.3/C.7; stdlib §2.20, §4.9, §4.10, §4.19, §6.7, §6.9; rationale §3.10 (reversal record), §3.14 (note), §5.10 (note), §5.11, §5.26 (A7), §9.4; Guides 1–6 — the unified design as accepted (0090 §2), worked position by position.** **Q1 (adopt, hard flip):** the identifier-operand form joins `MoveExpr` — alternative (c), a bare `Identifier` naming a local binding or `owned` parameter, exactly the old `MarkedTransfer` operand class — with the positional-admission commentary transferred verbatim (RHS root of a binding or assignment, a BindExpr clause's RHS included; an argument root — `M(move x)` parses through the plain `ArgExpression` path, the marker now part of the argument expression; a `case` scrutinee root; an if-expression branch; an expression-`case`/`when` arm result). The `MarkedTransfer ::= "owned" Identifier` production is **deleted**, the bare-`owned` `ArgModifiers` alternative is **deleted**, and the `"owned"?` scrutinee slot of `CaseStmt`/`CaseExpr` is **deleted** — `case move x of` is an ordinary scrutinee expression, §35.5's trigger 2 re-keyed to the identifier-operand `MoveExpr`. `scoped` stays an argument modifier (it marks a lending mode, not an action — the asymmetry is stated at §22.3 and in A.4's comment, not hidden). **Q2 (announced targets, rejected-as-redundant):** `return move x;` under an `owned` return, `throw move x`, `_ := move x;`, owned-field/`set(owned)` stores, a Pattern B `await move t`, owning `yield return move x;` are errors naming the announcement — one spelling per site, the same discipline that already rejected the marker on borrows and fresh producers; K3.13's announced set is unchanged. **Q3 (no alias window):** the old spellings leave the grammar in the same revision — zero external users, and the one-time cost is the lowest it will ever be. **Q4 (A7 sequencing):** the flip ships with the A7 positions still rejected; the `??`-operand lift stays gated on 0056's null-evaluated-transfer ruling, sequenced after the flip so that rule, if ever adopted, lands in the unified spelling and is never written twice. **Q5:** `out owned var x` stays `owned` — it *declares* a fresh owned binding at the call site, a declaration position inside an argument list, `owned p: T`'s coherent mirror. **Q6:** `M(move x)` at a non-`owned` parameter position stays an error with the diagnostic naming the borrow default (a transcription of the current rule — the check moves from the argument-modifier path into expression classification). §30.5's Pattern-B-await paragraph is conformed to the rewritten A7 row — the stale "the same as arm positions" comparison (arm positions have carried the K3.4 marker since v0.209) deletes, the paragraph now grounding the no-marker fact in K3.13's announcement and Q2's policy — **resolving [#3060](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3060) in this train**, as that issue anticipated. §29.2's yield note re-aims its liftable-bound comparison at `??`-operand position (axiom A7) for the same reason. The v0.244 anonymous adoption respells with its family: `using var _ := move x;` (§17.13, §28.10; the drift-verified inventory correction — K3.4's row now names the variant parenthetically as a cross-reference to the already-normative v0.244 position, not a new position). Rationale §3.10 gains the reversal record with the new evidence named (the v0.169 grounds each answered: the reserved slot is deleted rather than filled; the coherent mirror is declaration ↔ declaration; relaxing MoveExpr's operand restriction is the point — §5.10's three explicitness reasons are field-agnostic); §5.10 gains the superseded-locals note; §5.26's A7 record and §9.4's owning-match record are conformed. Guides: Guide 1's §1 teaching now states the clean split ("`owned` describes a slot; `move` performs the action") and every guide example respells; all six guide pins move to v0.246.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no axiom is spent, no axiom is narrowed or widened, and the doctrine is unchanged — the register's twelve-live/two-tombstone census stands.** What changed in the register is **one row's wording, of the same axiom**: A7's rejected positions are identical before and after (`??`-operand, operator-operand), and what the rewrite changes is the *grounds* — the old row's "keeps no-silent-consume uniform where no marker spelling exists" was about to become false (the unified marker *parses* in those positions), so the row now states its content as the purely semantic recorded rejection the study flagged as a mandatory consequence (0090 §5). Nothing is spent: no admission is made, no backstop is invoked, and the liftable bound (the gated `??` half, the unmotivated operator half) is carried forward verbatim. K3.13's announcement doctrine — announcement by declaration or keyword, no silent consume, fresh producers unmarked — is untouched; only the action's spelling in its parenthetical changed (`owned x` → `move x`). K3.4's family list respells and gains a parenthetical naming the anonymous-adoption variant — a cross-reference to §17.13/§28.10's existing v0.244 rule, not a new consume position. Q2's announced-target rejection is stated in *Move semantics for owned locals* as a new sentence. At most of its targets it rejects spellings that never had a reading (identifier-operand `move` did not parse before this train, and the old marker had no admission at those sites); at one target family it retires **compiling programs** — v0.245's whole-RHS admission let a marked owned-slot/`set(owned)` store compile (`arr[0] := owned b;`), and Q2 closes the position outright, so the migration section below carries it as the fifth newly-rejected family with a drop-the-marker fix. No kernel rule, join, freeze placement, or disposal point moves. The acceptance test the study set — every K-tagged rule reads unchanged with "the marker" re-pointed — was applied section by section in this train.

**Migration.** Newly **rejected** (the hard flip, no alias window — Q3): every old `owned`-marker consume spelling — `M(owned x)` at call sites, `var y := owned x;` / `y := owned x;` / `using var y := owned x;` (the anonymous `using var _ := owned x;` included), `case owned x of`, and arm-position `owned x` — each a parse-level rejection after the grammar deletions, with the fix-it naming the mechanical one-token respell to `move` (`"this call consumes x; write M(move x)"` and its per-position siblings). A **fifth family carries a different fix**: the marker on an owned-slot/`set(owned)` store — `arr[0] := owned b;`, `d["k"] := owned b;` — **compiled at v0.245** (the whole-RHS admission; three passing corpus lines, `tests/codegen/excluded_owning_collection_throw_leak_1970_test.cpp:335`/`:393`/`:424`) and is newly rejected under Q2's announced-target rule; the migration is to **drop the marker** (`arr[0] := b;` — the slot is the announcement), **not** to respell it `move` — stated here explicitly for [#3056](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3056)'s corpus rewrite, whose regex families must route this family to marker deletion. Newly **defined**: the identifier-operand `MoveExpr` and its positional admission — semantics identical to the forms it replaces, verbatim, including polymorphic-null adoption, state-match, drop-on-overwrite, the K5.1 freeze at the scrutinee, and 0056's consume-if-selected arm semantics. Adjacent to the newly-defined form, one seam **re-settled** in the semantics-preserving direction rather than newly ruled: the named-argument seam — a move-rooted argument is positional-only (§22.5), `M(item := move x)` a compile error naming the rule — carries the v0.245 rejection of `M(item := owned x)` over to the new spelling unchanged (admitting the named form would have made `owned` parameter names call-site API surface, an unruled new decision this train does not take). **Unchanged**: every declaration-position `owned` (parameters, fields, returns, function-type slots, choice payloads, `[N owned]`, `static owned readonly`, and `out owned var x` per Q5); `move x.f` / `move coll[i]`; every announced and implicit consume position (unmarked, per Q2); the A7 rejections (per Q4); the non-`owned`-position rejection (per Q6); all kernel rules and every disposal point and diagnostic *semantics*. **Doc-only:** the marker respell and the marker-naming prose across spec/stdlib/rationale/guides — measured at this train's parent: **167** old-spelling lines under the study's four regex families across the ten normative documents, **28** of them inside pinned changelog entries (history, never retroactively edited), **139** respelled, and **~220** total lines changed in the nine living documents (respelled lines plus the prose, grammar-comment, and code-comment lines around them); the study's ~196-line docs ceiling is not reproduced by this measurement and stands as the study's own pinned figure; the #3060 resolution in §30.5; rationale §3.10's reversal record, §3.14's and §5.10's notes, §5.26's A7 conform; Appendix B is untouched (`move` and `owned` were both already unconditionally reserved, and no B note keys on the marker spelling). Anchors: none deleted; no section numbers move; the deleted `"owned"?` scrutinee slots and the bare-`owned` `ArgModifiers` alternative carry tombstone comments at their sites, and `MarkedTransfer` is absorbed into `MoveExpr`, whose comment carries the record — no separate tombstone at its old site. **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** compiler catch-up is tracked on [#3056](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3056) — parser (identifier-operand `MoveExpr`; the three deletions), sema (positional admission transferred; every "write `M(owned x)`" fix-it respelled), and the four-regex-family test-corpus rewrite (~633 lines at the study's ceiling) landed as its own commit so behavioral diffs stay clean, with spec-cited regression tests per `tests/README.md` at each K3.4 position and argument position in the new spelling, the announced-target rejections (Q2), the A7 rejections with the reworded diagnostic, and `case move x of` freeze/moved-from traces. One inventory note for the compiler lane: 6 test lines spell the anonymous adoption `using var _ := owned x;` — respelled with the rest of the K3.4 family; no [#3049](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3049) overlap arises (that migration's target, the bare `var _ :=` binding, appears with the marker on zero test lines).

**Open questions recorded (owner-confirmed; question-only, not ruled, no design here — queued for owner ruling post-landing):** **(E-f1)** the §22.6 owned-overload ban and the stdlib's Try-pair dual naming (`Append`/`AppendOwned`, `FromResult`/`FromOwnedResult`): re-examination is now open because the marker premise shifted — `M(move x)` vs `M(x)` is visibly distinct at every call site with no declaration-token ambiguity left, and §3.10's own record conceded the marker satisfies §22.6's carve-out criterion; lifting would drag stdlib renames and resolution rules with it, which is exactly why it is a question and not a rider on this train. **(E-f2)** the §3.14 named-destructure no-transfer liftable: proposal 0065's record marks a transfer-through-named-slots form "liftable later" (its Q2), and the unified marker gives named slots a natural transfer spelling for the first time — where at v0.224 a marked named slot would have deepened the very conflation this train removed; 0090 carries the position as gap G5. Both are recorded in the rationale beside their home records (§3.10, §3.14).

Proposal 0090 flips to **superseded — graduated v0.246**; the README row moves with it, carrying one line per open question so both stay findable.

### v0.247 changelog (v0.246 → v0.247)

**Guide revalidation pass (program-closing, 2026-08-11) — all six guides re-traced against the v0.242–v0.246 elegance-graduation program.** The five trains' per-guide edits carried the teaching content; this pass swept the residue: every code example and every normative teaching claim in Guides 1–6 re-traced against the spec and stdlib at v0.246 — checked enum conversions and `default(E)`, shift domains, `closed`, the hashable vocabulary, range-step construction faults, `mod=`, `Exception`-derived throwables and the dead-arm rejections, the two statically-certain-hazard lints, the reserved `_`, `equality skip` and the one-directional gate, pure-body `for` elision, the statics fact vocabulary, generic-leaves not-attempted, and the full `move`/`owned` unification. The three companion normative documents are textually unchanged (headers move in lockstep; the changelog gains this entry). Three residue defects found; three fixed:

- **Guide 1 (Memory and Ownership) — one fix.** Re-traced in full: the §1 slot/action split, §2's four disposal spellings and the trivial-dispose teaching (the §15.4 store lint included), §4's producers, §5's `owned` fields, §6's factory and transfer returns, §7's `move` on fields, §8's branch joins, §9's idioms, and the quick reference — every `move` spelling verified at a v0.246-admitted position, every announced target verified unmarked. The fix: §8's `??` paragraph still advised coalescing two named owned locals "with `owned` transfers" — the retired marker vocabulary, a spelling that no longer parses after the v0.246 grammar deletions; it now advises `move` transfers and points at Pattern B's own marked-arm teaching.
- **Guide 2 (Errors and Nullability) — clean.** Re-traced in full: nullability and narrowing (§1), the `*OrNull` tier and Try shapes (§2), choice returns, declared-result target-typing and the combinators (§3), the exception machinery (§4 — verified against the v0.243 `Exception`-derived rule: no non-`Exception` teaching exists, and the uncatchable-`StackOverflowException` carve is stated as §31.4 has it), the caught-borrow rule (§5), automatic cleanup (§6), and the §7 table. The §3 owning-match adopt idiom already spells `move c`. No edits.
- **Guide 3 (Modeling Data) — one fix.** Re-traced in full: the five-kinds table, the worked declarations, the boundary calls (the `closed` spelling verified against §11.7; the v0.244 `equality skip` cache-field idiom verified against §9.2's own example, spelling-identical), and the §2 selection rules (arm-position `move x` verified). The fix: the §2 exhaustiveness bullet and §1's choice-vs-hierarchy boundary call taught closed-hierarchy `case` exhaustiveness with no mention of v0.245's generic carve — under §19.6's replacement subsection a `case` over a hierarchy whose root or any leaf is generic gets no leaf-coverage analysis and is completable only by an irrefutable arm. §2 now carries the carve and the value-shaped-sum-as-`choice` steering in §19.6's own terms; §1's boundary call is qualified to non-generic hierarchies and points at it. *(Gate round, same train: the Guide 1 fix gained the marked-arm expression form and the A7 no-marker clause; Guide 4's `Task?`-cache sentence gained its "warning-free" qualifier — a pre-window imprecision taken while the file was open.)*
- **Guide 4 (Concurrency) — clean.** Re-traced in full: domains (§1), task ownership (§2 — the v0.243 fresh-store lint taught as warned, verified against §15.4's landed text), the two task patterns (§3), `TaskScope`/`Parallel` (§4 — `WhenAllOwned(move tasks)` at the v0.246 spelling), sendability and `Domain.Spawn` (§5), channels (§6), data-owning locks (§7), statics (§8 — the four facts and three formulas verified against §22.12/§28.13, and the guide's membership enumerations checked against the spec's machine-checked parentheticals: form (i) and the warning-suppression set both agree), cancellation (§9), and the table. No edits.

No edits.
- **Guide 6 (Contracts and Purity) — one fix.** Re-traced in full: the clause grammar (§1), the `requires` boundary (§2 — `TryAdd(move session)` at the v0.246 spelling), `ensures`/`old` (§3), invariants (§4), declared purity (§5), the pure signature and body (§6 — the v0.244 `for`-elision teaching verified against §22.15 rule 5 as landed, the no-index-loop-workaround remedy included; `a mod b` untouched by `mod=`), what `pure` buys (§7), and `Debug.Assert` (§8). The fix is a stamp, not a rule: §8's surface claim carried its v0.236 verification stamp; the surface was re-verified unchanged at this pass (stdlib §8 is `Stopwatch` and `Debug`, nothing richer) and the stamp moves to v0.247 so the "ships today" claim names the revision at which it was last checked.

### v0.248 changelog (v0.247 → v0.248)

**Two spec-example defect fixes (owner-filed, spec-defect: [#3067](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3067), [#3069](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3069)).** Example-only: no rule changes; the stdlib and rationale are textually unchanged (headers move in lockstep; the changelog gains this entry).

- **§32.8 Callbacks: the `qsort`/`qsort_r` extern parameter renamed `base` → `basePtr` ([#3067](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3067)).** Both §32.8 extern examples declared a parameter named `base` — an unconditionally reserved word (Appendix B.1 lists `base` in its reserved list; §12.3 gives it its meaning), so the spec's own examples did not parse under the spec's own grammar. The rename keeps the C-side name visible per the issue's suggested shape: the `qsort` parameter line carries `// C: void *base`, and `qsort_r`'s existing C-signature comment now names the parameter (`void *base`). The same defect class was repaired on the stdlib side at v0.56 (five signatures moved off `base`/`type` to `base_`/`radix`/`style`, citing B.1); these two spec examples were the last declared uses of `base` as an identifier anywhere in the ten documents (swept this revision — zero remain outside pinned changelog history). §32.8's prose never refers to the parameter by name, so no prose conforms were needed.
- **§28.10 `using var`: the `do ... end` example's phantom `fs.ReadCount()` replaced with the declared read ([#3069](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3069)).** The dispose-before-return example called `FileStream.ReadCount()`, which no stdlib document declares (the sole occurrence in the docs tree — a rule-2 violation standing since the example was written). Per the issue's recommendation (1), the example now computes its `result: int` with the surface `FileStream` actually has: `FileStream` declares only constructors, `Path`, and its destructor (stdlib §7.2), so the int-returning read is the inherited windowed `Stream.Read(buffer, offset, count): int` (stdlib §7.1) — the stdlib's own canonical read shape, called as `fs.Read(buffer, 0, buffer.Count)` over a `using var buffer := new Array<byte>(4096, 0)` (the sized ctor, stdlib §4.4 — the same buffer line §28.10's first example already uses). The teaching is preserved exactly: a value computed inside the `do` block while `fs` is live, used after disposal via the interpolated write; the added `buffer` line teaches nothing new to the section (its first example established it).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation):** none — example-only; no normative rule text touched.

**Migration.** Doc-only; no program changes meaning. No grammar, anchor, or section moves; the guides are untouched and keep their pins (neither `ReadCount` nor a declared-`base` shape appears in any guide — verified this revision). The conformance corpus flips two rows and conforms one case text: **spec_0225** (the §28.10 block, the corpus's one FAIL at v0.247, interim-reclassified `blocked-on-#3069` by the implementation run) returns live as `fragment`/`compiles` and **passes** against the recorded v0.247 oracle (`build/bezelc` 2026-08-04, probed through the harness's own wrap path); **spec_0291** (the §32.8 `qsort` block) sheds `skip:doc-defect` — the fixed block parses past the old blocker, and the probe surfaces the block's next and final blocker, the elided `// ...` comparator body failing definite-return, so the row is now `skip:signature-listing` with the probe finding recorded in its notes; **spec_0292**'s case text is conformed to the renamed `qsort_r` block (verbatim-extraction consistency; its `skip:not-implemented` class is untouched). Gate baseline for the run lane: v0.247 shipped at PASS 137 / FAIL 1 / SKIP 429; the interim reclassification moved it to 137/0/430; this revision's expected figures are **PASS 138 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 429** — the first gate cycle after this lands is the acceptance run for the flip.

### v0.249 changelog (v0.248 → v0.249)

**The elegance program's deferred final train lands: proposal 0082, the Pattern A scoped await-bind (graduation train F; [#3048](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3048); owner-ruled 2026-08-11 — Q1 run-the-measurement, Q2 `const` included, Q3 `.Result` lockstep, Q4 the teaching diagnostics as normative recommended-message text, Q5 the larger question kept fenced).** The train was held by 0051 Part B's adoption gate and every criterion is now answered on the record: **C1** measured 7/11 = 63.6% of strict Pattern A await sites in the bound-task-awaited-once shape (threshold ≥25%; 44.0% under the relaxed population; the one failing compound reading flagged, not adopted; a small population — 11 strict sites corpus-wide); **C2** satisfied on the letter via #2042, with the spirit-reading caveat recorded (on that reading C2 rests on the elegance review's finding alone, which the acceptance already weighs); **C3 PASSED by the stage-1 prototype, with caveat (a) recorded where this entry cites it** — *measured*: everything downstream of the trigger needs nothing (0 lines changed in `src/ownership`, `src/sema`, `src/runtime`; the hidden slot **is** the §28.10 cleanup-stack entry and nothing else; checked-disposal mode unchanged; generated-code ASan/LSan clean; the establishment-order and early-return equivalences against the hand-written two-line form held, and the per-iteration-loop and exception-edge properties held on the one-line form); *reasoned, not measured*: the production trigger is front-end plumbing — one synthetic local symbol plus a statement splice — priced by architecture argument, not by the prototype. The stdlib is textually unchanged (header moves in lockstep).

- **Spec §30.5, consumer-side — the scoped await-bind (the admission).** A local declaration `var x := await E;` or `const x := await E;` whose initializer full expression is exactly the await, where `E` is an unbound owned temporary of static type `Task<T>` for class T (§28.3's classification, computed at every await site already), no longer disposes the temporary at its K8 boundary: the compiler binds it to a hidden scope-pinned slot — established on §28.10's establishment-ordered cleanup stack at the declaration, disposed at the innermost enclosing block's end on every exit edge, exactly as a hand-written `using var` at the same line — and `x` is an ordinary borrowed local sourced by that slot, which no program text can read, move, re-await, or dispose. The desugaring is literal (`var x := await E;` ⇒ `using var $t := E; var x := await $t;`, `$t` inexpressible). Qualification is the classification, not a syntax list: direct producer calls and the conditional producer (K7.1 arm-meet) qualify; named operands do not engage (they were already governed); compositions do not qualify (the initializer must be exactly the await). The near-misses stay rejected with Q4's two teaching diagnostics (normative recommended-message text: the `using var`-bind text and the existing-local text), and the error-participation wording ("the result borrowed by `cfg` is owned by the awaited task pinned at line N, disposed at the end of that block") is adopted as normative recommended-message text; inlay surfaces stay non-normative. Worked in the spec text: establishment order against neighbouring `using var`s, early return, exception unwinding (K3.15 edge parity), two binds per scope, per-iteration loop-body pinning, the impossibility of a second award (name the task to award twice), the consume-site freeze's empty surface, and the unchanged §28.2 checked-mode backstop.
- **`.Result` lockstep (Q3).** Stated in the same §30.5 subsection and conformed in §30.3: a fresh `var`/`const` declaration whose initializer is exactly a completed-task `.Result` read of a fresh producer desugars to the same hidden slot — await and `.Result` continue to move in lockstep (the v0.182 precedent).
- **Spec §28.3 / §28.10 — the one-paragraph anchors.** §28.3's *Unbound owned temporaries* gains the pinned-slot paragraph: the admitted bind's initializer is **not** an unbound temporary of that section — the compiler binds it, and the ordinary named-location machinery governs from there; the classification is unchanged, the consequence at that one declaration form re-pointed. §28.10 gains the compiler-introduced-slot sentence: same establishment-ordered cleanup stack, same ordering as a hand-written `using var` at the same line.
- **Appendix C.6 reworded.** The bare-bind row — previously "`var x := await Producer();` … remains rejected" — now states the desugaring admission (both spellings, `.Result` in lockstep) and enumerates the escape family that remains rejected (a `using var` bind, an existing-local assignment, a class-typed-member composition, a store, a non-chained return).
- **Rationale §5.24 — the second recorded bounded stretch.** The parallel paragraph its `case`-scrutinee entry's template anticipated: one construct, one desugaring (prototyped as macro-expansion into today's language), one bound (the innermost enclosing block); the honest asymmetry stated — the scrutinee stretch was forced, this one is elective and therefore waited on the gate; the conceded invisible-lifetime cost recorded; the close repeated in parallel — everywhere else reject-not-extend stands, and Bezel still has no general lifetime-extension mechanism.
- **Rationale §12.2 — the conceded cost repaid.** Reason 3 of the v0.204 when-in-doubt flip (the one-line `var` bind of a Pattern A await is a compile error) gains the v0.249 parenthetical: the consumer tax is repaid at the everyday site; naming the task remains the two-line form; the pattern choice stays the producer's.
- **Guide 4 §3 — the teaching inverts.** "The compile error newcomers hit" becomes the feature's teaching example: the one-line bind now works and is shown desugaring to the two-line form, which stays taught as the shape for naming the task (multi-award, holding); the two near-miss rejections are summarized with their teaching diagnostics; the §3 table's Pattern A consumer row updates. Guide 4's pin moves to v0.249.
- **§22.13 pattern (a) example — left as-is, noted.** `return Run(await AppConfig.GetConfig());` keeps the confined form: 0082's interactions clause leaves §22.13(b) and the §30.5 chained kinds untouched and directs no respelling. Under the new admission the natural two-statement spelling (`var cfg := await AppConfig.GetConfig(); return Run(cfg);`) becomes writable — recorded as a doc-improvement liftable, not taken this train.
- **HEAD soundness bugs, each one sentence where this revision's text touches its surface.** The confined form §30.5's principle paragraph continues to admit (`Process(await Producer())`) is memory-unsafe at HEAD — codegen frees the anonymous task at the await instead of the K8 boundary ([#3070](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3070)); the scoped bind is immune by construction — the task becomes a named `using var` slot — which strengthens the proposal's §0 observation that the two-line shape is the one that actually works today, now the desugaring target. The borrow-outlives-source enforcement gap for Pattern A result borrows ([#3071](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3071)) applies to the one-line and two-line spellings equally — the prototype reproduced it identically in both — so 0082 introduces no new exposure, and §30.5's "every §28.3 borrow rule applies to `x` unchanged" reads stronger than HEAD enforces until #3071 closes.
- **Q5 stays fenced (verified this revision).** The larger A3 question — whether class-typed `Task<T>` earns Pattern A's three-kind result-slot machinery at all — is neither advanced nor foreclosed by this train: it remains a future numbered proposal against §30.5's producer taxonomy and rationale §12.1–§12.2, with the A3 register row as the recorded extension point. Axiom A3 is untouched.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no new kernel rule, no new axiom.** The admission re-points one §30.5 surface rejection into a desugaring whose target is today's language: the hidden slot is a K2.1 named location riding §28.10's establishment-ordered cleanup stack (K3.15 edge parity). K8.4's reject-not-extend posture is untouched — no unbound temporary remains once the compiler binds, so the kernel's boundary is not stretched; the operand is reclassified by binding (rationale §5.24's "stretch" is the reader's-eye account, the kernel's account is the desugaring). K5 has nothing to guard: no user-visible binding exists, and the slot is a `using var`, non-movable per axiom A5. K7.1 supplies the conditional producer's arm-meet. The C3 prototype is the mechanical witness: the flagged build's only semantic content was an AST-to-AST splice ahead of an unmodified front-end.

**Migration.**

A **pure widening for the `var` spelling**: the rule fires only on today's errors, so no accepted program changes meaning or timing. **For the `const` spelling the pure-widening claim holds only after [#3074](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3074)** (filed by this run): HEAD's §30.5 await check never walks `LocalConstDecl`, so `const x := await Producer();` is today mis-accepted silently and dangles. The compiler sequence is therefore ordered: fix #3074 first (make `const` reject exactly as `var` does), then implement the admission for both spellings.

The rest of C swept for contact: C.3's unbound-owned-temporary and `using var` rows remain true unchanged — the admitted bind's initializer is compiler-bound (hence not an unbound temporary), and the slot is a `using var` no program text can name, move, or reassign; of C.6's other async rows, the Pattern B announced-kill and task-family-production rows have no contact, and the deferred-activation-escape row does make contact — the hidden slot binds the task, which is exactly the escape that row rejects when a plain argument is an unbound owned temporary, so `var x := await SumAsync(Nums(3));` does not qualify for the admission and stays rejected by the argument rule, the carve-out recorded in §30.5's qualification list; no other row states or depends on the retired rejection.

<a id="sec-v0-250-changelog"></a>
### v0.250 changelog (v0.249 → v0.250)

**The Train E follow-ons land as one train: proposals 0091 (the owned-overload lift, E-f1) and 0092 (named-destructure transfer, E-f2) graduate ([#3086](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3086), [#3087](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3087); resolved 2026-08-12 under the owner's delegation — "Please work to resolve all questions the right way as you see fit. Once resolved, graduate both proposals into the docs" — all fifteen questions, 0091 Q1–Q9 and 0092 Q1–Q6, as recommended).** These are the two open questions the v0.246 graduation recorded owner-confirmed and queued; both extend the unified marker's reach with one invariant intact — `move`'s operand is always the location being emptied. The surfaces are disjoint: 0091 adds no operand kind (the marker's argument-root reading becomes resolution-significant), and 0092 adds the payload field, a field (the pattern-slot analog of `move x.f`).

- **0091 — the §22.6 owned-overload lift ([#3086](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3086)).** The ordinary-parameter ban paragraph is replaced by the **ownership-mode applicability rule**: two same-name members may differ by `owned` on ordinary parameters, and at a pair position the argument's ownership classification completes applicability by four exhaustive clauses — an owned production (per the §28.3 producers table, which stays the normative list; its position-classified owned-local-read row is superseded at pair positions by the marker discipline) reaches the `owned` candidate; a borrow the plain one; a context-typed production (`null`, or a null-producing `default` form), a no-classification argument (K1.6), and a bottom-typed `throw` argument keep both applicable and fall to the ordinary ambiguity rule, whose diagnostic names the real remedies (bind-first, or `M(move x)` — the explicit cast is inexpressible at identical parameter types). The clauses apply per position and compose conjunctively: the `owned` member is reached only when every marked position receives an owned production, and a mixed call leaves no candidate — the diagnostic names the positions and their conflicting classifications, the remedy a third member declaring the mixture. The predicate is measured on **substituted** signatures after per-candidate inference; **no ranking changes** — the marker participates in applicability, never the better-than relation — and a move-rooted argument's positional-only status (§22.5) is restated as the pair's named-argument asymmetry. Pairs are guarded at the declaration by the **erasure test**: every differing position must be a class type, an interface type, or a type parameter whose constraints exclude every §28.1-erasing and move-only-value substitution, decided by §14.2's conformance computation — an interface bound qualifying only when its conforming set excludes the erasing substitutions **by language rule**, not merely among the types visible at the declaration (conformance to an ordinary user-declared interface is open-world — a downstream record, enum, or choice may list it, §14.2 rules 2/4/7 — so no declaration-site computation can exclude them): `where T: SomeClass` and `where T: IDisposable` qualify (the `IDisposable` family is closed by §8.7 and inherited by extension); `where T: class`, `where T: IComparable<int>`, and every ordinary user-declared interface bound do not; a failing pair is §11.3's clash at the second declaration. The `out owned` and `scoped` ban halves **stand, re-grounded** (the retired "no resolution-by-call-site-form rule" sentence could not survive the lift): `scoped` on the markerless function-typed operand kind, `out owned` on its recorded binding-form costs plus the operation-distinct corpus observation (`TryGetValue` leaves where `TryPopValue` removes). Conforming edits: §22.3 (the marker's applicability role), §11.3 (the clash rule reads the new distinguishability), §2.8.6 (ordinary-parameter `owned` joins the overload-identity matching key; a plain↔`owned` flip now reports as removal+addition, verdict breaking either way; the member-added row's caveat records the applicability re-route beside the ranking one), §30.10 (the owning aggregator row respells with the stdlib merge; the `FromResult` class-`T` diagnostic's referent is **unchanged**), Appendix C.1 (the never-distinguishes invariant row narrows), and a worked Registry example; **no grammar delta** (the marker is already part of the argument expression — verified). Stdlib: §6.7's `WhenAllOwned`/`WhenEachOwned` become **`WhenAll`/`WhenEach` overloads** (exact signatures kept, names merged) and §1 gains the convention sentences (the argument-side `Owned`-suffix convention retires where a pair is declarable; return-side `Owned` names — `ParseOwned`, `FromOwnedResult` — stay; stdlib pairs do not default the marked position). Rationale §3.10 gains the lift record with the ruled-question reasoning (the erasure test over a whitelist; substituted over declared signatures; ambiguity over route-to-plain at unclassified arguments; the merge over admit-but-don't-rename; category (i)'s investigated-and-withdrawn disposition). Guide 4's two helper lines respell.
- **0092 — the marked named slot ([#3087](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3087)).** §19.3's *Named destructuring* gains the transfer form: `move N = var x`, the marker on the **source** — the payload field, the location being emptied — admitted exactly when the match is an owning match (either trigger), `N` names an `owned`-marked payload field (v1), and the RHS is a top-level binding (`var x`, v1); any number of slots in one list may be marked, per-slot and composing. The "a named slot never transfers" sentence **narrows to unmarked slots**, and the closing remedy sentence **widens** to name both spellings (the positional destructure, or the marked named slot) — here and at §35.5's case-patterns bullet. The rejection taxonomy lands with remedies: borrowing match (mark the scrutinee or match the temporary); value/`string`/runtime-managed payload; **move-only value payload** (v1 — the diagnostic names the liftable; the underlying positional-transfer gap is filed as spec defect [#3094](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3094)); record/class heads by derivation (no obligation-bearing slot can exist there); and the `move N = _` diagnostic under §17.13's sanctioned-forms obligation ("a discarded payload is already disposed at construct completion — drop the marker, or bind with `var x` to transfer"). §35.5's owning-match section states that the marked slot rides borrow-during-trial/transfer-on-selection and the existing disposal traces unchanged — the marker changes routing within the already-consumed value, never whether or when it is consumed — and §35.4's no-per-slot-moved-from sentence gains the storage-model reconciliation parenthetical. §19.6: a marked slot is an irrefutable binding, contributing as `N = var x` does. Appendix A.7: `NamedSlot ::= ("move")? Identifier "=" AltPattern`, with the three-token commit note (`move Identifier "="`; the pre-empted `move`-rooted pattern-bound forms were already §28.8.1-rejected). Appendix C.7 gains the invariant row and the existing named-slot row narrows to unmarked. Rationale §3.14's v0.246 note resolves into the decision record, carrying the corrected Q1 comparison honestly (the unmarked-symmetry rival declined on the per-slot peek alone, its flip of the landed borrow trace acknowledged as definition-text-only), the declined receiver-side spellings, Q3's kernel-cost rejection of a disposing `move N = _`, and Q6's per-slot composition. Guide 3 gains the by-name extraction example (spec-cited §19.3/§35.5, v0.250). **No stdlib change; no new tokens.**

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no new kernel rule, no new axiom — for either proposal.** 0091 adds **no K rule**: the applicability rule *reads* existing classification facts — K1.5 (fresh productions are owned), K1.6 (the no-obligation kinds), K3.13's no-silent-consume totality with §22.3's marker (which is what makes the marked/unmarked split decidable from the argument alone), and the §28.3 producers table — as an applicability filter; no consume position, disposal point, join, or freeze moves, and Appendix C.1's "`owned` never distinguishes" invariant row narrows (ordinary `owned` distinguishes under the declaration guard; `out owned` and `scoped` never do). 0092 is its proposal's §3 derivation table, restated as landed: **one admission** — a second slot spelling routing a payload the construct already owns — **plus its rejection set**; the consume itself stays the owning match's scrutinee consume (K8.3 / K3.4), transfer-at-selection, arm-binding life, remainder disposal, and the K5.1 freeze are §35.5's existing machinery verbatim; **K3's consume enumeration gains no row**, and axiom A7 is untouched — a `NamedSlot`'s `move` is pattern grammar, not an expression-position `MoveExpr`.

**Migration.**

- **Newly defined:** pair declarability under the erasure-test declaration guard; the four-clause ownership-mode applicability rule (§22.6); the marked named slot `move N = var x` with its admission conditions and rejection taxonomy (§19.3/§35.5; grammar A.7).
- **Newly rejected:** nothing that exists. 0091's guard rejects a subset of the declarations the pre-v0.250 ban already rejected wholesale (every pair was undeclarable; the guard admits some and keeps rejecting the erasure-collapsing rest). 0092's marked slot does not parse at v0.249, and the `move`-rooted pattern-bound forms its three-token commit pre-empts parse today only to be rejected by §28.8.1's positional-admission list — no accepted program changes meaning.
