- **Nothing flips:** no existing program changes meaning. 0091: the ban made pairs undeclarable, so no pair exists anywhere — the lift changes the meaning of zero declarations and zero calls, and single-member call sites resolve exactly as today. 0092: every landed spelling keeps its meaning — the unmarked named slot's owning-match borrow trace is preserved verbatim, and the named-destructure form has zero behavioral corpus at v0.249 (unimplemented; [#1409](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1409)).
- **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** 0091's compiler catch-up is [#3086](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3086), sequenced **behind [#3056](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3056)'s marker respell** — resolution keys on the very marker the test corpus is still adopting. The non-mechanical re-keying of the name-keyed `WhenAll`/`WhenEach` recognition (47 `src/` occurrences, re-verified this revision, plus the `bz_task_when_all_owned` runtime-symbol surface) and the gtest-corpus helper renames live there: the **49 test-corpus `*Owned` helper lines (29 `WhenAllOwned` + 21 `WhenEachOwned` occurrences outside the conformance corpus, re-verified this revision)** are deliberately **not** respelled in this train, because the compiler recognizes the helpers by name — renaming tests ahead of the re-keying would break them for nothing; they ride #3086. The 5 pre-#3056 `case owned` test lines likewise ride #3056. 0092's catch-up is [#3087](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3087), behind #3056 and with/behind [#1409](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1409) (the named-destructure implementation itself — there is no shipped named-slot parser to amend); [#3094](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3094)'s eventual ruling gates only its move-only liftable, not the v1.
- **Appendix C sweep (the standing lesson):** C.1's "`owned` never distinguishes" invariant row narrows to the guard-shaped statement (ordinary `owned` distinguishes where the declaration guard admits the pair — an interface bound qualifying only by language-rule closure; `out owned` and `scoped` never do) and C.7 gains the marked-named-slot invariant row, its existing named-slot row narrowing to unmarked slots — the two rows this train's edits carry. The rest of C swept for contact: C.1's marker-aware override- and interface-matching rows are unchanged (signature matching already read `owned`); C.2 has no contact; C.3 has no contact — a `NamedSlot`'s `move` is pattern grammar, not an expression-position `MoveExpr` (the kernel note above), so no consume or discharge row engages; C.5, C.6, and the remaining sections are untouched; and D.2 is unchanged.
- **Guides:** Guide 4's two owning-helper lines respell to the merged names and Guide 3 gains the by-name extraction example; both pins move to v0.250. Guides 1, 5, and 6 are textually untouched and keep their pins — swept for echo sites this revision (old helper names, `AppendOwned`, ban restatements, named-slot transfer claims): one echo site found and reworded — Guide 2's accessor dual-naming sentence, which over-generalized the distinct-names convention past the operation-distinct pairs it still governs (its rewording scopes the names to operation-distinct pairs and teaches ownership-only duals as same-name overloads, the marker telling, stdlib §1); Guide 2's pin moves to v0.250 with it.
- **Conformance corpus:** six stdlib case texts conform verbatim to the renamed doc blocks (stdlib_0108/0109/0111/0112/0114/0115); **stdlib_0112** — the owning-aggregator implementation sketch, a live row — re-verified **PASS** against the recorded oracle (`build/bezelc` 2026-08-04) after the rename (the case declares its own method; nothing name-keyed engages at HEAD). Three hand-added rows carry the train's new blocks (ids provisional; renumbered at the next regeneration): **spec_0321** (§22.6's Registry pair — `skip:mixed` by the first-reported-blocker rule, the #3086 docs-ahead fact carried in the note), **spec_0322** (§19.3's marked-slot example — `blocked-on-#1409`, the probe-verified first blocker: named destructure is unimplemented), **guide3_0002** (Guide 3's example — `skip:mixed`, the #1409/#3087 fact in the note). Gate figures move from PASS 137 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 430 to **PASS 137 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 433** — verified by a full sweep against the recorded oracle this revision.
- **Bookkeeping:** proposals 0091 and 0092 flip to **superseded — graduated v0.250**; the README rows move with them; [#3086](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3086)/[#3087](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3087) join the catch-up run sequence after [#3056](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3056) (`catchup-run-sequence-2026-08-12.md`). Anchors: none deleted; no section numbers move (stdlib §6.7's subsection anchor ids are unchanged under the retitled headings).

**Gate round (same train).** One adversarial pass; verdict ship-after-fixes, every finding applied before landing. The blocker: the drafted declaration guard's interface-bound arm was **open-world** — "qualifies exactly when no value-kind or runtime-managed type conforms to the named interface" is not decidable at the declaration as claimed, because conformance to an ordinary user-declared interface is open (a record, enum, or choice in any downstream module may list it, §14.2 rules 2/4/7, under §2.8 separate compilation): module B adds a value-kind conformer after module A admitted the pair, §28.1 erases, the pair collapses, and the guard's own declined per-instantiation errors leave nowhere to report it — the biconditional fails. The repair narrows the arm to **closure by language rule**: an interface bound qualifies exactly when its conforming set excludes every value-kind and runtime-managed type as a matter of language rule — today the `IDisposable` family, closed by §8.7 and inherited by every extending interface — never as a fact about the types visible at the declaration, so an ordinary user-declared interface bound never qualifies; conformed at §22.6, Appendix C.1, rationale §3.10 (which now records *why* the arm narrows — open-world conformance defeats declaration-site computation), and this entry, with both worked examples, the lit dispositions, and Q6's declaration-site stance intact. The four majors, each fixed in place: stdlib §1's convention bullet had misfiled `Task.FromOwnedResult` as a return-side `Owned` name — it marks its *parameter*, and it stands because its would-be pair fails the guard (category (i)'s withdrawal), so the return-side list is the `ParseOwned` family alone; §22.6's "four exhaustive clauses" was false as drafted — null-producing `default` forms (grouped with the null literal by the producers table) fell through clause (3)'s null-literal scoping, now widened to every context-typed production, and bottom-typed `throw` arguments, carrying no K1 classification, gained their both-applicable sentence; §2.8.6's member-added delta row named only **ranking** re-routes where the train adds an **applicability** re-route — adding the `owned` member beside a plain one re-routes every owned-production argument (a fresh `new`, an `owned`-returning call, a `Task`-family call) from call-bounded borrow to ownership transfer at unchanged call sites — and the row now records both halves; and §22.6's applicability rule never stated multi-position composition though the guard quantifies over every differing position — the clauses now compose conjunctively, a mixed call leaving no candidate, with the positions-naming diagnostic and the third-member remedy. One proposal-body claim was **refuted** by the round: 0091 consequence 5's "its re-route caveat is moot at a pair" — the applicability re-route above is precisely the non-moot case; the body is pinned, and the correction lives in §2.8.6's amended row and this paragraph. No §4(ii)-adjacent claim fell — the merge program's grounds were probed and stood. Eleven minors in step, among them: the producers-table circularity disclaimer at clause (1) (the owned-local-read row is position-classified and superseded at pair positions by the marker discipline); the pair exception in §22.6's ambiguity remedy (the explicit cast is inexpressible at identical parameter types); the type-distinguished re-teaching of the `WhenAll`/`WhenEach` merge at Guide 4 and stdlib §1 (the merged pair resolves by parameter type, §22.3's marker announcing the consuming form — not by the ownership-mode clauses); A.7's `NamedSlot` note trimmed to §28.8.1's actual reach (the identifier-operand `move x`); the Guide 2 echo rewording above; the Appendix C sweep bullet above; and the conformance-manifest slug and note conforms (stdlib_0111–0113; spec_0321's #3056 docs-ahead fact).

<a id="sec-v0-251-changelog"></a>
### v0.251 changelog (v0.250 → v0.251)

**One spec-defect resolution (owner-directed 2026-08-12 — "propose the resolution and resolve 3094"; spec-defect [#3094](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3094)): move-only value payloads gain binding semantics in choice matches — interpretation 1, transfer like `owned`.** At v0.250 a choice case's payload of move-only value type (§15.3 — an owning inline array, or a nested owning choice) made the choice owning (§35.4 rule 1) and disposed correctly when discarded (§35.4's recursive active-case disposal), but *binding* one had no defined semantics on either match form: §35.5 transferred `owned` payloads and copied value payloads, and a move-only value payload can do neither. The ruling completes the rule on both forms. **Borrowing match:** a positional or unmarked-named binding of such a payload is a **borrow** — §19.3's move-only scrutinee rule applied at the slot; reads through the binding are admitted, consuming operations through it (`move b[i]`) rejected. **Owning match:** the payload **transfers into its binding at arm selection exactly as an `owned` payload does** — K3.12 already moves a move-only value into every owning location it flows to, and §28.1's marker is admitted-but-redundant on such a field, so the marked and unmarked field spellings behave identically; the binding is then a move-only owned local of the arm body's scope under §15.3's standard rules, and §35.5's "value payloads bind as copies" narrows to *copyable* value payloads. Discarded and unlisted move-only slots dispose at construct completion — the half that was already defined. **Nested destructuring** through a move-only *choice* payload (the one nested move-only shape with a pattern surface) routes recursively in an owning match through the slots that transfer — a positional slot, and any pattern nested within one; a nested pattern beneath an unmarked named slot routes nothing at any depth, and a marked named slot cannot carry one (condition (iii)) — inner bindings receiving their payloads at selection, the un-bound remainder at every level disposing at construct completion. §35.5's "nested destructuring of an owned payload does not arise" claim is corrected: a class-typed owned payload destructures only in the *named* form (§19.3, since v0.224; interface heads stay barred in v1) and routes nothing — each nested named slot a getter read, a borrow minting no obligation (§28.6), the payload disposed at construct completion exactly as a discarded slot. **The marked named slot widens:** §19.3's condition (ii) becomes "an `owned`-marked payload field or a payload field of move-only value type", the rejection taxonomy's move-only arm (the one naming [#3094](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3094) as the recorded liftable) retires, and its copyable-payload arm states why move-only values are not in it (they *do* carry an obligation). This executes 0092 Q2's move-only liftable at exactly its recorded bar — its own defect issue, its own ruling — and dissolves a latent v0.250 contradiction, recorded honestly in rationale §3.14: §28.1 admits the redundant `owned` marker on a move-only value field, so a redundantly-marked field (`Fetched(owned data: [4 owned]Connection?)`) satisfied marked-slot condition (ii) while the move-only rejection arm rejected the same slot — two rules claiming one declaration; the admission is the only resolution that needs no second carve. Edits: spec §35.5 (both match subsections, the case-patterns named-slot bullet, one new worked example — an owning match over an inline-array payload), §19.3 (the unmarked borrow reading's payload-kind list, condition (ii), the rejection taxonomy), §15.3 (the pattern-binding bullet gains the owning-match transfer sentence), §35.3 (the construction-side payload-argument sentence names the move-only value-move), §35.4 (the storage-model reconciliation parenthetical covers recursively-reached payloads), Appendix C.7 (the marked-named-slot invariant row widens; the unmarked-slot sentence follows); rationale §3.14 (the decision record, appended to the v0.250 marked-named-slot record it resolves). The stdlib is textually unchanged (header moves in lockstep). No grammar delta to the *production* — A.7's `NamedSlot` already carries the optional `move`, positional slots are patterns, and the widened admission is semantic — verified this revision; A.7's `NamedSlot` *comment*, which restated condition (ii) in its v0.250 form, needed and received the conform (v0.250; widened v0.251).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no new kernel rule, no new axiom.** The transfer is K3.12 composed with §35.5's existing transfer-at-selection: the consume remains the scrutinee's — K8.3 for the fresh-temporary trigger, K3.4 for the marked scrutinee — and the payload transfer is routing within that one consume, the same account v0.250 gave the marked named slot. ### v0.252 changelog (v0.251 → v0.252)

**Two spec-defect resolutions in one train (owner-directed 2026-08-12 — "resolve and push both 3110 and 3111 resolutions", the rulings posted verbatim on the issues; spec-defects [#3110](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3110) and [#3111](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3111), both filed by the v0.251 adversarial gate as adjacent observations): borrow-lifetime obligations re-key from the classification label to the borrow-carrying census, and the enumeration silences on the move-only payload position resolve payload-kind-generically.** At v0.251, §35.4's borrow-lifetime paragraph was scoped to "**Borrow-bearing choices**" — the rule-2 classification label, which the cascade reaches only when rule 1 does not fire — so an *owning* choice carrying a plain class- or interface-typed payload beside its owned one (`Loaded(owned response: Response, log: Logger)` — owning by rule 1, `log` a carried borrow) escaped every §9.7 rule: as written, such a value constructed over a borrow of a scoped local could outlive the source with no rule violated ([#3110](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3110)). The ruling names the condition and re-keys every §9.7-derived constraint onto it. **The census:** a choice **carries borrows** iff any case has a borrow-carrying payload field, under §9.7's definition with its transitivity clause reading the census itself at a nested choice payload — §35.4 rule 2's condition, freed of its "otherwise" and of its label-keyed transitivity (the two differ only at a nested owning-choice payload, which rule 2 never meets); ### v0.253 changelog (v0.252 → v0.253)

**One spec-defect resolution (owner-directed 2026-08-12 — "Please also resolve and push 3113", the ruling posted verbatim on the issue; spec-defect [#3113](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3113), filed by the v0.252 train lane and sharpened by its gate): §22.16's `old(E)` capture taxonomy gains its third arm — a move-only value operand is rejected at the contract clause, interpretation 1.** At v0.252 the taxonomy had two arms: copyable operands captured by copy, class- and interface-typed operands captured as a frame-resident borrow. A **move-only value operand** ([§15.3](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-move-only-value-types) — an owning inline array or an owning-classified choice) fit neither, and the gate's sharpening made the gap worse than undefined: §22.16's own desugaring account ("a hidden entry binding equivalent to `var __oldN := E;`", every user-binding rule governing the hidden one) meets §15.3's local-to-local rule as a **move** (K3.12), so a literal reading had the contract clause silently *consume* the operand at entry — a parameter or field moved-from for the entire body, a contract position mutating the state it exists to observe. The ruling adopts interpretation 1: such an operand is a **compile error at the contract clause**, the diagnostic naming the **copyable-projection** remedy — an element- or payload-derived copyable value (`old(pool[i] <> null)` over an owning inline array's nullable slots, a `pure` member's value read through a borrowed element) or, for an owning choice, a `pure` choice method's result over the borrowed receiver (§35.2's `this` borrow; clause calls to pure members per §22.15) — or, universally available, a borrowing-match projection over the operand, `old((case c of …))`, consuming nothing (§35.5) and needing no member on the choice (gate round, below: the pure-method route is real in the language but empty for stdlib `Result`, whose members are deliberately non-pure — stdlib §2.20 — which is why the projection route is named beside it). The two rescues fail on their own terms, recorded in the rationale: a borrow observes **post-state** (an `old` that is silently not old — §19.3/§28.9's borrow adoptions are no precedent, scrutinee and capture positions observing current state by design), and an element-wise snapshot is heavy machinery still undefined wherever an element is itself owned (the copy would mint a second owner). The desugaring account is **conformed, not contradicted**: the hidden-binding sentence now states the binding is a **copy** (or the reference arm's §28.3 unmarked borrow), never a consume — precisely why the move-only operand is rejected rather than desugared; the rejection arm preempts the silent move. Scope is exactly the move-only kinds: copyable values, records, enums, `string`, and value-like and borrow-bearing choices keep arm 1, which function-typed operands now join expressly — previously in no arm, the gate round's completion below; the copy is a reference copy for the runtime-managed kinds (§28.9) — (for a borrow-carrying operand the hidden binding is governed like any user-written binding by §22.16's every-rule sentence — the v0.252 census obligations apply to it with no new text); class- and interface-typed operands keep arm 2. Nothing else moves. Edits: spec §22.16 (the `old(E)` paragraph: the desugaring copy clause, the third arm, the remedy sentence — inline prose spans, the section's convention at this altitude; no fenced example added — and, gate round, the borrow-only paragraph's consumed-inputs idiom sentence), Appendix C.15 (the `old` bullet's capture summary conforms — the one Appendix C edit), Appendix D.2 (the Move-only value types row gains the §22.16 site — gate round); rationale §9.8 (the decision record, appended to the v0.203 contracts record whose section owns §22.16's history). The stdlib is textually unchanged (header moves in lockstep). No grammar delta — the rejection is semantic; A's `ContractClause` production and B.2's `old` contextual-keyword row are untouched — verified this revision.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no new kernel rule, no new axiom.** The rejection is a use-site admissibility rule in contract position, grounded on K3.12's no-copy: every store of a move-only value into an owning location is a move, so the one binding the desugaring may introduce (a capture that does not consume) is the one binding §15.3 cannot supply for such an operand. K3's consume enumeration gains no row (nothing new consumes — the rule exists to prevent a consume), K4.2's announced-kill set is untouched, and the freeze, liveness, and disposal machinery is unreferenced.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected:** nothing that exists. At v0.252 `old(E)` over a move-only value operand had no sound reading — the stated copy arm is the operation §15.3 forbids, and the literal desugaring was a silent K3.12 move at entry; zero users. The form is now a stated compile error with a named remedy.
- **Newly warned:** nothing — the shallow-capture warning on a dereferenced class-typed `old` capture predates this revision, untouched.

### v0.254 changelog (v0.253 → v0.254)

**One spec-defect resolution (owner-directed 2026-08-12 — "Please also resolve 3117", the ruling posted verbatim on the issue; spec-defect [#3117](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3117), owner-filed): §12.7's narrowing gains its boxed-location semantics — the read stated affirmatively, the write rejected, interpretation 2 on the aliasing ground.** [§12.7](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-type-tests-is-is-not-as) narrows the tested carrier itself, and says so flatly; at a carrier whose **declared** storage is `Object`, an interface, or the nullable form of either and whose tested type is a **value type**, that binding names a [§8.6](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-boxing) **box**, and v0.253's text defined neither direction of access through it. The read direction had been fixed compiler-side a revision earlier ([#3090](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3090) — the narrowed read produces the boxed value, which is what §17.4's inline-array remedy `if o is [3]int then var a: [3]int := o; end;` needs to work at all), but no spec text said so; the write direction was left entirely to the implementation, which routes `lvalueAddr` to the box payload for reads and writes alike and therefore accepts `o[0] := 9` de facto — measured `9` through `o`, `4` through the `a` the box was copied from. **Both directions are now stated.** *Reads* through the narrowed binding read the box's payload (the #3090 semantics, affirmative): `o[0]` reads the payload's element, and `var b: [3]int := o;` copies the payload out under §3.2's value-copy rule — in neither case the `a` it was copied from. *A write whose store would land in the box is a compile error*, and the rule keys on **where the store lands**, not on the statement form, so it names the **three position families** that can produce one: **(i)** an assignment, compound assignment, or `++`/`--` targeting an lvalue chain that extends the binding with a `.` or `[…]` hop (`o[0] := 9`, `o.X := 5`, `o[0] += 1`); **(ii)** such a chain passed as a `ref`/`out` argument — [§22.3](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-ref-and-out-argument-locations)'s assignable-storage-location categories admit `ref o[0]` and `out o.X`, and the callee's write reaches the payload whether it aliases the location directly or is written back through the accessor bracket (the `Swap` shape, observable through `o2`); and **(iii)** the binding, or such a chain, passed as an inline-array argument at an `extern` parameter, which [§32.5](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-ffi-compatible-types)/[§15.1.3](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-inline-array-ffi) pass **by address** — native writes land in the payload exactly as a Bezel write would. The **bare-binding** compound and `++`/`--` forms are *not* rejected: §6.6 makes `o += 1` equivalent to `o := o + 1`, whose store targets the declared location and mints a fresh box, so they are the equivalence at work rather than an exception to it (below). The carriers are [§7.4](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-narrowing-applies-to-locals-only)'s throughout — a local or a `readonly` field, instance or `static`, off an admitted root — and the declared type may be `Object`, an interface, or the nullable form of either. **The primary ground is aliasing, not the discarded copy**: `Object` is a class and an interface is a reference type (§3.1, [§8.1](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-definition)), so such a variable carries the standard reference semantics [§3.2](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-reference-vs-value-types) defines, and `var o2: Object := o;` shares the box and such a write is heap mutation observable through every other reference to it — aliased mutation of a value, exactly what value-copy semantics ([§3.2](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-reference-vs-value-types)) exists to exclude; interpretation 1 (write the payload — what the compiler does today) is locally self-consistent and globally unsound against the value model. **The second ground is the runtime-managed kind's own premise**: boxed values are runtime-managed (§8.6/[§28.9](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-runtime-managed-types)) and §9.7/§35.4 treat runtime-managed payloads as classification-neutral — no borrow tracking, no lifetime constraints — with immutable shared referents doing the work; a writable box payload would demand borrow and freeze machinery for the one kind defined by never needing any. **The [§23.5](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-properties-and-indexers-restrictions) family is the secondary, reader-facing ground** and the diagnostic's register ("would modify a discarded copy"), recorded with its imperfection stated: there the copy is discarded and the write unobservable, here the box persists and the write *is* observable through the writing binding — which is why the aliasing ground is primary. The **diagnostic** names §8.6 (boxing copied the value; the box is shared) and the copy-out/mutate/re-box spelling `var b: [3]int := o; b[0] := 9; o := b;`. That final `o := b` is expressly **not** a write through the narrowing: it stores to the declared `Object`/interface location, boxing its right-hand side under [§5.1](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-implicit-conversions) into a **fresh** box (boxed `()`, which an implementation may intern, is the one licensed exception — §8.6's unit-boxing clause, the carve §8.4 already writes into its own fresh-box claim) that leaves every other reference to the old one untouched, and — being a reassignment of the narrowed variable — invalidates the narrowing for the remainder of the controlled block, exactly as §12.7's existing sentence says; the remedy therefore makes visible the box mint interpretation 1 hid. Narrowing to a **reference** type is untouched (no box; ordinary reference-type writes) — the case §12.7's own `Dog` example shows. **The normative home is §12.7**, where the narrowing is defined and where the rule is a use-site admissibility condition on a narrowed binding; §8.6 carries the *premise* (a box's payload is fixed at boxing; a value enters by being copied in and leaves by being read out — a narrowed read, an unboxing `as`, a typed-pattern binding over a boxed scrutinee (§19.3), or the call-bounded receiver copy a call on the box takes (§8.5)) and cross-references §12.7 for the shapes that could appear to write one, in any of the positions §12.7 enumerates. That premise is stated as **no operation *this revision defines*** writes the payload, not as a flat impossibility: the open question of #3124 below (a mutating member on a boxed receiver) is left open by the wording rather than decided by it. Edits: spec §12.7 (the new **Narrowing at an `Object` or interface location** paragraph, placed at the end of the narrowing enumeration — inline code spans, no fenced block, the section's terse voice), §8.6 (the payload-fixed-at-boxing clause on the opening paragraph, with the read-out enumeration and the #3124 parenthetical), §28.9 (the boxed-value-types bullet gains the immutable-shared-reference clause — the ruling's premise stated where the kind is defined), Appendix C.1 (one invariant row); rationale §11.6 (the decision record, appended to the v0.242 `is`-does-not-bind record whose section owns §12.7's history). The stdlib is textually unchanged (header moves in lockstep). No grammar delta — the rule is semantic lvalue admissibility; Appendix A.6's `LValue` production already restricts the chain's base to `Identifier`/`this` and is untouched, and A.5's types are unaffected — verified this revision.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no new kernel rule, no new axiom.** A use-site lvalue admissibility rule, grounded on the value-copy principle ([§3.2](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-reference-vs-value-types)) and §28.9's immutable-referent premise. K3's consume enumeration gains no row (nothing new consumes — a box payload was never an owned location), K4.2's announced-kill set is untouched, and the freeze, liveness, and disposal machinery is unreferenced: boxed values are runtime-managed and carry no obligation in either direction.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected — and, uniquely for this train, rejected *against the current compiler*:** every write that lands in the box of a §12.7 value-narrowed carrier at an `Object`/interface (or `Object?`/`I?`) location, in each of the three position families — the lvalue-chain statements (`o[0] := 9`, `o.X := 5`, and their compound and `++`/`--` forms), such a chain in a `ref`/`out` argument (`Swap(ref o[0], ref o[1])`), and the binding or such a chain as a by-address inline-array argument at an `extern` parameter. The **bare-binding** compound and `++`/`--` forms (`o += 1`, `o++`) are **not** in this list: their §6.6/§17.6 expansion stores to the declared location and mints a fresh box, so they stay admitted (see the gate-round paragraph below, which corrected the ruling's letter here). At v0.253 these had **no defined spec semantics**, but they **are accepted by `build/bezelc` today** (interpretation 1 de facto: #3090's read fix routes `lvalueAddr` to the box payload, and that address serves reads and writes alike). This is stated honestly as **impl-ahead-of-spec, now corrected**: the compiler accepts what v0.254 rejects, and the sema rejection is the catch-up. Zero users, and the behavior change for a program relying on the accident is the measured one (`9` becomes a compile error).
- **Newly defined:** the **read** semantics of a value-typed §12.7 narrowing at an `Object`/interface location — the narrowed read reads the box's payload, element-wise or copied out whole — stated affirmatively for the first time (#3090 landed it in codegen at v0.252 with no spec text behind it); and, at §8.6/§28.9, the **box payload's immutability** (fixed at boxing; no operation *this revision defines* writes it), the premise the ruling's second ground leans on, with §8.6's read-out enumeration completed (narrowed read, unboxing `as`, typed-pattern binding over a boxed scrutinee, call-bounded receiver copy).
- **Newly warned:** nothing.
- **Nothing flips:** no *defined* semantics existed to flip — v0.253 said nothing about either direction — and every other narrowing is unchanged: narrowing to a reference type (§12.7's own `Dog` example), `is null`/`is not null`, the `is not T` else-branch narrowing, and §7.4's nullability narrowing all behave exactly as before. Whole-value assignment to the narrowed binding (`o := b`) remains admitted, boxing under §5.1 and invalidating the narrowing — and so, by §6.6's equivalence, do its compound and `++`/`--` spellings (`o += 1`, `o++`). The one behavior change is the measured accident above, which no defined rule sanctioned.
- **Impl catch-up:** the rejection belongs in **sema**; #3090's codegen path stays as it is (the issue's own note, confirmed by the ruling). [#3117](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3117) **stays open** after the docs land as the compiler-catch-up tracker, gaining the `bug` label (the [#3086](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3086)/[#3087](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3087) pattern); the spec side closes with this revision's merge, recorded on the issue. The catch-up owes **three** rejections, not one — the lvalue-chain statements, the `ref`/`out` argument position, and the by-address `extern` inline-array argument — and must leave the bare-binding compound and `++`/`--` forms accepted. Cite spec §12.7, v0.254, and #3117 in the rejection tests.
- **Appendix C sweep (the standing lesson):** C.1 gains one invariant row (the write rejection in its three position families, the read direction, and the fresh-box carve), placed beside the existing boxing row. C.1's **narrowing row** is *contacted, not amended*: it states §7.4's carrier rule (locals and `readonly` fields, one field off an admitted root), which the new row now cites for its own carriers rather than restating — the earlier no-contact claim on that row was wrong and is corrected here; the row's own text needs no change, since the carrier rule it states is exactly the one the new row rides. Verified genuinely no-contact: C.1's other boxing row (borrow-bearing/borrow-carrying boxing and the move-only exclusion — lifetime constraints on *forming* a box and on where it may then be stored, orthogonal to writing through one, and the distinction §12.7's second ground now states explicitly); C.3 (a boxed payload carries no disposal obligation in either direction); C.5, C.7, C.10, C.14, C.15; D.2 carries no boxing or narrowing feature row — type tests, boxing, and `Object` are Core throughout, so the rule ships at Core with no D.2 or D.3 delta.
- **Guides:** none of the six carries boxing or type-narrowing-at-`Object` teaching (swept by grep: Guide 2's and Guide 6's narrowing passages are §7.4 *nullability* narrowing; Guide 3 §2's is `case` pattern narrowing; no guide shows a write through any narrowed binding). No guide is edited; every pin keeps.
- **Conformance corpus:** textually unchanged — the rule and its remedy are stated with inline code spans, §12.7's convention at this altitude and the v0.252/v0.253 precedent, so no fenced block is added, no case is added, and the manifest↔cases bijection is untouched. (A fenced rejection example was considered and declined: at HEAD the compiler *accepts* the write, so the case would be an `error`-class row that fails the gate, and the README's convention would park it as `skip` + `blocked-on-#3117` — a permanent skip bought at the cost of bloating a deliberately terse section.) Expected gate figures stay **PASS 137 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 434** (the v0.251 baseline).
- **Bookkeeping:** [#3117](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3117)'s **spec side** closes as resolved-at-v0.254; the issue itself stays open as the sema-rejection tracker per the ruling. [#3090](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3090) is cited as compiler-side context and is untouched by this revision. Anchors: none added or deleted; no section numbers move.

**One verification recorded, not resolved (the ruling's scope check, item 6).** Whether a value-type *member* can mutate `this` through a **boxed receiver** — a method call rather than an lvalue chain, reached either by §12.7 narrowing or by ordinary interface dispatch on a variable holding a boxed value, which needs no narrowing at all — was checked against §9/§10/§15/§26/§35's actual member semantics. For three of the four value kinds the answer is no, and the spec correctly states nothing: a **choice** declares no instance fields or storage-backed properties and only expression-bodied read-only properties, with `this` a borrow of the receiver value ([§35.2](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-choice-members)); an **enum**'s instance state is its underlying constant, under §10.4's identical member list and §10.5's restrictions; **inline arrays** declare no members and cannot be extended ([§26.2](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-what-can-be-extended)). The residue is the **mutable body record**: [§9.4](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-mutability) admits a settable property in the body form and nothing forbids a record method from assigning one, so `o.Bump()` on a narrowed boxed receiver — and `i.Bump()` on an `i: IBump` holding a boxed record, the same call with no narrowing anywhere in it — is a constructible shape, but its meaning turns on whether a value-typed receiver's `this` aliases the receiver's storage or a copy of it, which **no section states generally**, for records or for value types (§35.2 states it for choices; §26.7 states it for extension receivers; §28.3's producer table classifies `this` for ownership, not for value-receiver binding; the nearest text is §8.5's parenthetical that a boxed receiver's rendering takes a **call-bounded copy** — said of the `ToString` path and generalized to no other member). Both readings are unsound in the ways this ruling rejects — an alias reproduces the aliased mutation, a copy reproduces the silently-dropped write of interpretation 3 — and a narrowing-site rejection has nothing to key on: the language has no mutating-member classification, and the interface-dispatch route has no narrowing site to key on at all. Per the ruling's own conditional and CLAUDE.md's decline-with-reasons rule, v0.254 **states nothing** about member calls at a boxed receiver; the underspecification of value-receiver `this` binding is a distinct defect with its own issue and its own ruling to come — filed as [#3124](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3124) at this landing — recorded here and in rationale §11.6 rather than settled as a side effect of this train.

**Gate round (same train).** One adversarial pass; verdict ship-after-fixes, every finding applied before landing. **One blocker.** The drafted rule enumerated *statement* forms, and two further positions store into the same box: a **`ref`/`out` argument** naming a chain off the narrowed binding — §22.3's assignable-storage-location categories admit `ref o[0]` and `out o.X`, and the callee's write lands in the payload whether it aliases the location or is written back through the accessor bracket, the `Swap` counterexample observable through `o2` — and an **inline-array argument at an `extern` parameter**, which §32.5/§15.1.3 pass **by address**, so native writes land there too. Both falsified §8.6's newly-written "no operation writes it" the moment it was written. The rule now names all **three position families** and keys explicitly on *where the store lands* rather than on statement shape, conformed at C.1's row, §8.6's sentence, and the Newly-rejected bullet. The FFI arm is not a separate defect deferred to its own issue: it is this ruling's own any-write principle meeting an Extended-tier feature, and a rule that stops at the statement forms would be false as stated. **Three majors.** The first: §8.6's flat "no operation writes it" decided the residue below by fiat — interpretation 1 of #3124 (a value-receiver `this` that aliases the receiver's storage) would have `o.Bump()`, or plain `i.Bump()`, write the box — so the premise now reads "no operation *this revision defines* writes it", with the open question named in a parenthetical, at §8.6 and at §28.9's bullet. The second: the **bare-binding compound and `++`/`--` forms** were rejected on a false ground — §6.6 makes `o += 1` *equivalent* to `o := o + 1`, and that passage's own `o := b` ruling says such a store targets the declared location, mints a fresh box under §5.1, and invalidates the narrowing. Resolved by **admitting** them: they fall on the legal side of the where-the-store-lands line the ruling itself draws, and rejecting sugar whose normative expansion is legal would carve §6.6's equivalence for no semantic gain. They are dropped from every rejected-list carrier (§12.7, C.1, the Newly-rejected bullet) and §12.7 gains the clarifying sentence; chain-rooted compounds (`o[0] += 1`, `o.X++`) remain rejected, their store landing in the box. This is recorded plainly as a **gate-corrected refinement of the ruling's letter** — which said "compound assignment, increment/decrement alike" — adopted because it is what the ruling's own stated principle yields; it is noted in #3117's closing comment as well as here. The third: the passage said "variable" where §7.4 narrows **locals *and* `readonly` fields** — `this._f`, `TypeName._s`, `local._f`, including `static readonly`, the most-aliased carrier of the set — so §12.7 and C.1 now name §7.4's carriers, folding in the nullable declared forms (`Object?`, `I?`) the drafted text also omitted, and the sweep bullet's no-contact claim on C.1's narrowing row is corrected to contacted-by-citation. **Minors in step:** the standard-reference-semantics claim was cited to §3.1 at four carriers when the text is §3.2's (§3.1/§8.1 carry only `Object`'s class kind); "no borrow tracking or lifetime constraint attends one" over-claimed against §8.6's own borrow-bearing-record clause and now distinguishes the *payload* from *forming* a box and placing it; the fresh-box claim gains the boxed-`()` interning carve, the carve §8.4 already writes into its own fresh-box claim; §8.6's read-out enumeration gains the typed-pattern binding over a boxed scrutinee (§19.3) and the call-bounded receiver copy (§8.5); "the spec nowhere states" softened against that same §8.5 parenthetical, which states the call-bounded copy for the `ToString` path and generalizes it to nothing; and the reads sentence now says what a read *does* — `o[0]` reads the payload's element, `var b: [3]int := o;` copies the payload out under §3.2's value-copy rule. **Round close:** the residue paragraphs here and in rationale §11.6 widen from "a narrowed boxed receiver" to a boxed receiver reached by narrowing **or by ordinary interface dispatch** — `i.Bump()` on an `i: IBump` holding a boxed record involves no narrowing at all, so a narrowing-site rejection has nothing to key on there even in principle, which is #3124's actual breadth. Every finding reproduced at the fix pass; none was declined.

### v0.255 changelog (v0.254 → v0.255)

**Four spec-question resolutions in one batch train (resolved 2026-08-18 under the owner's delegation — "there are a few open spec questions from the last week. Please find them, resolve them cleanly, gate them and merge them to master. I trust your judgement." — the rulings posted verbatim on the issues, never per-question owner calls): [#3240](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3240), [#3131](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3131), [#3085](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3085), and [#3124](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3124).** The common thread is one-carrier conforms and uniform readings over special cases: a throwable inventory that already separated raise-capable from analysis-throwable gains its missing member and trades a literal carve-out for a desugaring principle; a per-type rendering sentence and a general storage rule are re-scoped to the one type where they diverge; a general-sounding `using var` claim restates as the position-specific rule it always stood in for; and the value-receiver binding question v0.254 promised its own ruling gets it — the uniform borrow reading, closing the boxed-receiver write route v0.254 could not key on.

- **Spec §28.8.1 — `new` is not analysis-throwable, and compound spellings classify through their desugarings ([#3240](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3240), surfaced by [#3080](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3080); Reading A).** The exception-edge inventory gains the explicit sentence: `new T(...)` joins the stated raise-capable-but-not-analysis-throwable family (`!` throwable only when the target is null; `as` not at all) — a throwing constructor completes no object, so the restoration analysis loses nothing on that edge, and the partially-constructed-object hazard is §22.9/§28.3/§28.6's territory. The common idiom `var old := move _r; _r := new Res();` is expressly legal — the reading the section's own `Wrong` example always encoded (its error names only the false branch) — with the argument carve stated (`new Res(Fetch())` still carries `Fetch()`'s edge). And the non-throwable list's compound-assignment carve-out (whose literal neither-LHS-nor-RHS wording made `x /= 0` non-throwable against the throwable list two paragraphs down) is replaced by alike-classifies-alike: a compound assignment (and `++`/`--`) is throwable **exactly when its §6.6/§17.6 desugared form is** — catching `/=`, `mod=`, *and* checked-arithmetic `+=`, the case the issue's list-patch would have missed — with the bullet's drop-on-overwrite condition applied to the write-back, and no second enumeration to drift. Rationale §5.10 carries the decision record.
- **Spec §8.5/§9.2, stdlib §9.8 — all six `Range` components render; §9.2's storage rule is scoped to the declaration surface ([#3131](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3131)).** §8.5's per-type sentence now says "its auto-properties" means the **declared** surface — all six of stdlib §9.8's properties, not the intrinsic's four-slot storage layout — with the derived pair (`IsOpenEnded`, `IsEmpty`) recomputed by the same §16.3 rules member reads use, so component and member read cannot disagree; the rider is pinned (an open-ended range renders `IsEmpty: False`, agreeing with `r.IsEmpty` under §16.3's never-empty rule). §9.2's "always over storage, never over derived values" gains its scoping sentence: the rule is about the declaration surface — for user records storage and declared auto-properties coincide and the derived tier is exactly the expression-bodied spelling; a compiler-intrinsic body record's plain-declared properties are its auto-property surface even where the implementation stores fewer slots. Four- and six-component equality coincide (the derived pair is a function of the stored four), stated at both carriers. stdlib §9.8 gains the one-sentence pointer at the declaration site. The bullet now states the rule it stood in for: the **await-result borrow specifically** may not flow into a `using var` binding — the list's own recorded K1 ground rejects the owning reading (a borrow cannot assume the obligation the spelling announces), and the pin reading announces a scope the result cannot carry independently, its lifetime being the task's own ("disposing the task disposes the result") — with the cross-reference to §28.10's general borrow-pin admission so the two rules read as visibly different rules. - **Spec §9.4 (new subsection), §9.6, §11.2, §23.4, §23.5, §35.2, §35.8, §26.7, §8.5, §8.6, §28.9, Appendix C.1/C.5 — value receivers are borrows; stores landing in the receiver's own storage are rejected at the member body ([#3124](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3124); interpretations 2/3 combined; discharges the v0.254 residue promise).** §9.4's new **Value receivers are borrows** subsection is the normative home: in every value-kind instance member body (records the live case; choices, enums, and extension receivers already read identically; inline arrays have no members) `this` binds a **borrow of the receiver value** — the reading §35.2, §26.7, §19.3, §28.9, and §28.3's `this` producers row already stated piecewise — and a store landing in the **receiver's own storage** (explicit `this.X := e`, bare `X := e` resolving to the receiver, an inline-array-field chain `this._arr[i] := e`) is a **compile error at the member body**, the diagnostic naming the `with` update idiom (§9.5). The rule keys on where the store lands, never on the chain's root (§12.7's position families at the `this` root: desugared compound/`++`/`--` forms, `ref`/`out` arguments, by-address `extern` inline-array arguments) — so a chain hopping through a class- or interface-typed member **leaves the receiver** (§9.7: record reference fields are borrows) and its store is legal, the sound **mediating** shape: stdlib §4.14/§4.15's span indexer setters (`Buffer[Start + i] := value`, `Source[Start + i] := value`) stay declarable (the gate round's blocker, below). Two boundaries stated at landing: **constructor bodies are initialization, not receiver positions** (§9.2's own canonical form assigns `Width := width;`), and the rejection covers **author-written accessor bodies** — a block-form setter storing its backing field through implicit `this` is the same store by another spelling, so a receiver-storing setter cannot be declared on a value kind (a mediating-shape setter can, §23.4), and a value kind cannot conform to an interface declaring a **settable** property or indexer member at all (conformance rejected at the declaration, **blanket** — stated at §9.6, echoed at §11.2 and §35.8 and C.1's enum row; the deliberate simplification recorded with its cost and lift in rationale §9.13). That conformance rejection — not a vacuity — closes the boxed case: receiver-writing members exist on value kinds (the **synthesized auto-property setter** is one, invoked as an accessor — §6.6's once-each accounting, §22.15's never-pure classification, §22.16's setter instrumentation), but a box's dispatch faces are `Object` and the conformed interfaces, and neither carries a settable member, whether reached by §12.7 narrowing or unmarked interface dispatch. External stores through a named binding's lvalue chain (`r.X := 5` on a settable auto-property) remain legal — the synthesized setter's store is the assignment's own store, announced at the call site; the rule governs author-written bodies. §35.2 now cites the general rule (satisfied by construction), §26.7 applies it to value-kind extension receivers, §8.5's boxed-receiver **call-bounded copy** parenthetical conforms to the borrow reading (observably indistinguishable for an immutable payload; the one-off copy claim retires), §8.6's premise firms from "no operation *this revision defines* writes it" to "no operation writes it" with the v0.254 #3124 parenthetical resolved in place, §28.9's boxed bullet follows, §23.4's record-indexer sentence and §23.5's write-back remedy conform (gate round), and C.5 gains the invariant row. **Gate round (same train).** One adversarial pass; verdict ship-after-fixes, every finding applied before landing. **One blocker.** §9.4's drafted rule keyed the rejection on the lvalue chain's `this` root, and that key rejects the standard library's own records: stdlib §4.14/§4.15's `Span<T>`/`ArraySpan<T>` indexer setters store `Buffer[Start + i] := value` / `Source[Start + i] := value` — chains rooted at `this` whose stores land in the *borrowed heap buffer*, not in the receiver, because a hop through a class- or interface-typed member leaves the value (§9.7: record reference fields are borrows). The rule now keys on the store landing in the **receiver's own storage** — `this.X := e`, bare `X := e`, an inline-array-field chain, in each spelling (desugared compounds and `++`/`--`, `ref`/`out` arguments, by-address `extern`) — with the class-hop **mediating** store named legal as the span setters' shape, the answer to what a record accessor body can do; C.5's row conforms identically. **Five majors.** (1) The settable-interface-conformance arm had an unmeasured flip set: two further green accepting tests flip on it alone, outside the 33 — named in the Newly-rejected bullet — and the stdlib is verified clean of the shape (`IList`/`IOwningList` class-only implementers; `IReadOnlySpan`'s indexer get-only). (2) The vacuity ground was false and its §23.1 cite wrong: the synthesized auto-property setter *is* a receiver-writing member body invoked as an accessor (§6.6's once-each accounting, §22.15's never-pure classification, §22.16's setter instrumentation, §9.5's never-invokes-setters contrast); the closure that holds is the **conformance rejection** — `Object` declares no settable member and no conformable interface may, so no member reachable through a box writes any receiver — conformed at §9.4, this entry, and rationale §9.13's second ground, with external `r.X := 5` legal because the rule governs author-written bodies. (3) The conformance rejection was stated in no conformance-governing section: §9.6's first sentence now carries the exclusion, with one-clause echoes at §11.2's matching rules and §35.8, and the carve appended to C.1's enum-conformance row. (4) §23.4's record-indexer sentence was stale — neither necessary nor sufficient post-v0.255, and misfitting the span records (combined-form, no mutable properties): it now states the mediating form, and §23.5's write-back remedy gains the record carve. (5) The blanket-vs-keyed form of the conformance rejection had been decided silently: the blanket form **stays**, recorded in rationale §9.13 as a deliberate simplification — the keyed form is decidable at the same declaration site, the cost (foreclosing the sound mediating conformance shape) is named, no stdlib interface needs it today, and the keyed form is the recorded lift, no other rule moving. **Minors in step:** rationale §9.13's uniformity ground acknowledges the §28.3 `this`-row widening (the pinned v0.254 entry read the row as ownership-only; this ruling reads the unqualified row as stating both, no competing classification existing); §28.8.1's hoisted-`new` sentence drops the invented call-edges-near-them justification (stylistic uniformity — none of the compiling examples has a call edge between the move and the restoration for the hoist to guard); §30.5's may-not-flow derives clause now licenses both of the restated bullet's grounds (K1 for the owning readings; the task-bounded result lifetime for the pin reading); §8.5's §9.4 link retargets to the subsection anchor, matching the other four carriers; §9.4 gains the one-sentence placement note (homed in the Records chapter, governing all four value kinds and extension receivers); and the #3085 bullet above notes that proposals 0082 and 0051 retain the retired §30.5 general claim in proposed diagnostic text as pinned history — not edited — the live diagnostic already position-specific. **Round close:** the gate **confirmed the accessor-arm rejection itself**: `record_iface_property_conformance_2416`'s accept control and the two ARC conformance tests measure the boxed write-through route live in today's compiler, so the arm rejects real, reachable behavior, not a hypothetical. Every finding reproduced at the fix pass; none was declined.

### v0.256 changelog (v0.255 → v0.256)

**The review-program defect train (seven edits in one batch; ruled under the owner's 2026-08-18 delegation — the review program's basket A: its C10 ruling executed whole, and C1's fence-first sequencing executed here, the unification itself riding proposal 0096): [#3245](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3245) and [#3246](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3246), plus five smaller recorded defects.** The source is the owner-commissioned 2026-08-18 review batch — the **RAII comparative review** (whose two passes converged independently on #3245 as the top spec-clarity defect) and the **back-of-book elegance review** (whose highest-value finding is #3246's self-admitted leak) — with the smaller items drawn from the same program's defect basket. The common thread is stated-versus-implied: a load-bearing negative the spec never stated (#3245), a leak the spec itself admitted as "a leak until that issue classifies or fences it" (#3246), an exceptions list one member short (§13.3), a grammar comment contradicting a landed ruling (A.4), a false same-set claim (§19.3), a flagship example drawing the warning its own section teaches how to avoid (§10.4), and a rationale ground a later revision falsified (§9.9).

- **Spec §22.9/§28.4 — the throwing class's destructor body does not run on constructor unwind; one raw resource per owning wrapper ([#3245](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3245), per the program's C10 ruling).** §22.9's lead had cited "the [§28.4] pass" for construction unwinding while §28.4's pass's step 1 *runs the destructor body* and §22.9's own bullets enumerate only owned-field disposal plus the base chain — two observably different readings, the implementation long shipping one, no text or test pinning it. The negative is now explicit at §22.9: on every unwind edge except the fully-initialized `this(...)`-chaining-body throw, only already-completed owned fields (captures included) and the base subobject's `Dispose()` run — the base chain's full sequence, its destructor body included, because the base *completed* — and the throwing class's own destructor body **never** runs, on §7.9's ground (never-observed-unset is issued only at constructor completion; a mid-unwind destructor body would be the forbidden observer; matches C++). §28.4 gains the companion teaching where destructors are taught: the destructor body runs on disposal, never on construction unwind, so a raw resource is protected only from constructor completion — the discipline is **one raw resource per owning wrapper**, acquired as the constructor's final act, with richer classes composing wrappers as `owned` fields (§22.9 covers those on every edge; the composite then needs no destructor, §28.5). The flagship `FileStream` example was **verified conforming and left byte-identical** — acquisition is its constructor's last statement; the prose now says why that matters — rather than restructured into a wrapper-plus-factory shape (the single-class form *is* the wrapper the discipline prescribes). Rationale §5.29 is the decision record. **#3245 stays open** for the compiler-side regression test pinning the negative (derived destructor body does not run on ctor-throw; base's does) — the spec side lands here, the test is compiler-lane work.
- **Spec §28.3/§27.1.1/§27.6 — the static-iterable-factory function-value leak closes by the mirrored fence ([#3246](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3246); C1's sequencing: the narrow fence lands first).** The two recorded-residual paragraphs — §28.3's producers-row parenthetical and the bare-type-parameter rule's *"one narrowed residual stays recorded"* italic, each carrying the verbatim "a leak until that issue classifies or fences it" — **retire**, replaced by the fence's statements. The fence mirrors the v0.223 Task fence in its own voice: (a) §28.3's calls-mint exclusion gains its iterable twin — a member with a function type whose **return slot is a bare type parameter** anywhere within a parameter's declared type is **inadmissible at an instantiation substituting one of the §29.3/§30.7 iterable or enumerator interfaces or a lazy query**, rejected per instantiation (§3.6 rules 2/4), the diagnostic naming the sound spellings (a family-shaped slot `f: () -> IEnumerable<T>`, a concrete function type, statement-form consumption); (b) §27.1.1 makes **iterable-interface return slots announcement-bearing** exactly as `Task`-family slots are — usable only where the target's return slot is also in the family, covariance within the family under the ordinary reference-conversion rule, never across the boundary — closing the typed-intermediate retyping route (§27.6's formation fence keeps its callee-kind keying; formed values obey the new boundary whatever their origin); (c) §27.6's recorded-seam sentence conforms (the routes it could not see are now fenced where they arise). The fence is deliberately **broader than the leak** — iterable mints are callee-kind-keyed and a function slot erases the callee kind, so sound instance-callee inhabitants are conservatively rejected: the identical conservatism, and identical named workarounds, the Task fence accepted. Classifying the slot was impossible in either direction (mint double-disposes stored views; lend leaks minted frames — the impossibility that is A2's reason to exist), and the family is **not** extended: axiom A2 is untouched, the fence being admissibility, never classification. **The larger A2-unification question — whether frame-producing iterable returns join calls-mint wholesale, retiring the split — proceeds separately as proposal 0096 (the program's C1 direction; accepted, awaiting its graduation train, and subsuming this fence at graduation); this fence is the minimal soundness closure and is right under either outcome, which is why it lands first.** Rationale §12.10 gains the closure record beside the fence records it completes. **#3246 stays open** for the sema arm (the exclusion and the §27.1.1 boundary are spec-ahead-of-impl).
- **Spec §13.3 — the "three exceptions" visibility list gains its fourth.** `invariant` members carry no visibility keyword (A.4's `InvariantDecl` has no `Visibility` slot; §22.16) — the recorded §13.3/§22.16 contradiction closes with the list extended and renumbered ("four exceptions"), and Appendix C.2's mirror row conforms.
- **Appendix A.4 — the `ExpressionPropertyDecl` comment conforms to §23.2's one-meaning ruling.** The stale *"`readonly` … is permitted for consistency"* comment said the opposite of the landed rule; it now states the slot as a shared-production over-admission rejected semantically (§23.2: `readonly` is written exactly where shape cannot express read-onlyness). A comment edit only — no production changes.
- **Spec §19.3 — the named-slot record-target set is made truthfully the same set `with` takes: public explicit fields join it.** The sentence claimed "the same targets `with` takes (§9.5)" while §9.5's set includes **public fields** and §19.3's bullet named only the two property kinds — and a record's explicit field was neither admitted nor named in the rejection list. Verified sound and admitted (the drafter-verified choice the charter left open, taken as admission rather than claim-drop): the slot read is the same storage read the record's other named slots already perform ("a record field copy/borrow", §19.3's own matching text), the ownership paragraph applies verbatim, explicit record fields inhabit the same type domain as auto-properties (no `owned`, no move-only — §9.7/§15.3), and the marked-slot rejection for record heads survives by the same derivation (records carry no obligation-bearing slot). The rejection list gains the completing arms (a record method; a non-`public` explicit field). Zero migration: named destructuring is unimplemented ([#1409](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1409)); no accepted program changes meaning.
- **Spec §10.4 — the flagship enum example respells `Array<Priority>` → `FrozenArray<Priority>`.** As written, `public static readonly All: Array<Priority>` draws §22.12 rule 4's declaration-site sharing warning — the flagship example taught the shape its own chapter warns about. It now reads `public static owned readonly All: FrozenArray<Priority> := FrozenArray<Priority>.From([Low, Medium, High]);` — the warning-suppression set's sanctioned spelling (verified against stdlib §4.19: `From(items: Array<T>)` is the copying construction form, `Priority` a sendable value type, `owned` enrolling the singleton in §22.13's exit disposal per §10.4's own prose), with one sentence pointing at the statics-and-sharing facts vocabulary (stdlib §1) at the site that already teaches enum statics. **Impl note (conformed at the gate round):** the cpp replicating site — `tests/codegen/enum_property_restrictions_2499_test.cpp` — is **deliberately not edited by this docs train**: `FrozenArray<T>` is not yet declared in the compiler (comment-only in `src/` today), so its respell rides the compiler lane's FrozenArray catch-up. ### v0.258 changelog (v0.257 → v0.258)

**The iterable announcement unification: proposal [0096](proposals/0096-iterable-announcement-unification.md) graduates, ruled under the owner's 2026-08-18 delegation.** Calls-mint extends to the iterable/enumerator family: a call whose declared, pre-substitution return type is **mint-announcing** — a `Task`-family type or an iterable-family type (the eight §29.3/§30.7 iterable and enumerator interface heads, or a lazy query) — produces a caller-owned frame at **every callee kind**, and reads of storage of such types remain borrows of their storage. **Axiom A2's task/iterable split retires to a register tombstone**; the stored-collection-view idiom respells as a **property** (`Items(): IEnumerable<Item> => return _items;` → `public readonly property Items: IEnumerable<Item> => _items;` — the exact v0.190 stored-task precedent, by the exact remedy, axiom A4's lend-only accessor guarantee becoming load-bearing); the v0.223 owning-head declaration-site rejection and its `Drain()`/`ReceiveAll()` §29.11 affine carve retire (the carve's ground never fit its occupant — proposal 0096 §3's three-filings/unsound-remedy/closed-list record); and the v0.256 narrow fence ([#3246](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3246)) is **subsumed** — its landed text removed, not amended. The licensing evidence is the proposal's fence-accretion ledger: four fences for one seam, ~1,900 words of announcement-coherence machinery at v0.256, none of it needed by the family that mints — now none of it needed at all.

- **Spec §28.3 — one calls-mint rule for both families.** *Task-family calls produce owned frames* is replaced by ***Calls mint for the mint-announcing families*** (derives K6.2 + K6.3; no axiom): the `Task`-family paragraph's caller- and callee-side machinery generalized — fresh-or-owned-frame on every return path of a non-`async`, non-iterator body, `null` under a nullable declared type, the call-bounded plain-function-parameter carve stated for both families, borrow returns rejected with the property/field/slot/concrete-type remedy named. The producers table's method-call row and function-value-invocation row conform — the iterable-typed function slot's invocation classification, the row's deliberately-open question since v0.223, is **closed as a mint**. *Iterator and iterable returns* shrinks to the unified statement (unmarked at every callee kind; `owned` is admissible emphasis); the whole *Iterable-interface returns at instance and extension callees* paragraph (v0.223) **deletes**, its anchor (`sec-iterable-instance-returns`) removed and every referrer re-pointed. K6.3 reads *Containers: calls mint, storage lends* with no family qualifier; K3.2/K3.13, the K4 kill table's row 3, and K5.1 fold the unmarked iterable-family return into the target-announced consume set (iterable-family in a non-iterator body, §29.5 barring plain `return` in iterator bodies). §29.3 and §30.7 state the unmarked convention at every callee kind; §29.2's fresh-source sentence reads "an iterable-family-returning call at any callee kind". §28.14's *Call-bounded × deferred activation* shape (2) generalizes in step (gate round): the consume-to-K6.1-bound obligation on the frame minted by invoking a call-bounded callback is now stated for both families — a task awaited to settlement, an iterator or query frame enumerated or disposed, none of them storable, returnable, or otherwise escapable — closing the dangling citation §28.3's both-family carve had placed on a task-only §28.14(2); the synchronous-callee rejection stays task-only (a synchronous body consumes an iterable frame by enumerating or disposing it).
- **The v0.256 fence comes back out (obligated cleanup; supersedes [#3246](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3246)).** §28.3's parallel iterable-substitutions exclusion paragraph (~744 words) and its **conservatism-reach paragraph** (~264 words — the one naming `Select<U>`, `Aggregate<TAccum>`, `Zip<U, R>` (on `R`), `GroupBy<TKey>`, and both `ToDictionary` overloads as newly rejected at iterable-head substitutions) **delete**; §27.1.1's iterable bullet **merges into the `Task` bullet** as one *mint-announcing return slots are announcement-bearing* rule, its conservatism clauses ("the sound instance-callee inhabitants included…"; the callee-kind-keyed formation split) deleted; §27.6's formation bar generalizes to any mint-announcing callee at any callee kind, its instance carve-out sentence and its normatively-recorded open question deleted, and the property-reference rejection extends to iterable-typed properties (the stored-view property face may not be laundered into a minting slot); Appendix C.3's v0.256 row is re-derived (the `Task`-family per-substitution exclusion stands unchanged; the iterable family carries none). A **drafting call, recorded:** the proposal's inhabitant-side closure (0096 §6 item 5) is drafted as §27.1.1's boundary being read against the target slot's **declared, pre-substitution** type — a bare-type-parameter slot is not announcement-bearing, so a family-returning formed value cannot inhabit it even where the substitution makes the types coincide; for the `Task` family the member's parameter-position instantiation is already excluded, so at parameter loci the reading newly bites only at iterable substitutions — at the field/property storage locus it moves a `Task`-family verdict too, the Newly-rejected bullet below recording it (gate round). This is the mechanism by which the six stdlib §5 members' iterable-head substitutions become **legal again** while the laundering routes stay closed; the proposal's summary line "entries 2, 3, and 4 generalize (one word each)" was not applied to entry 2's excluded-substitution set, which its own §2 bullet 3 and §8 contradict ("no per-substitution rejection left standing for the iterable family"; "un-rejecting what v0.256's fence rejected") — the detailed claims were followed, the tension recorded here for the gate.
- **`Drain()`/`ReceiveAll()` re-ground as ordinary minting members.** §21.1's runtime-`const` rejection parenthetical re-grounds (the two members leave the affine classification for the ordinary owned-production one; the lazy query's affinity rides the minted frame); §29.11 gains the layered reconciliation — the lazy query is an ordinary minted caller-owned frame whose **container obligation** the standard rules discharge, while the single-consumption rule governs the orthogonal **enumeration right** (layered, not identified — the gate round replaced the train's first draft, which had identified the consumption point with the obligation's discharge; drafting seam Q1 resolved as *inside* the family, the proposal's recommendation); §30.15's "the enumerator is affine" respells to the single-pass/channel-invariant grounding with the fresh-drain-frame identity stated. **Stdlib:** §1's two-family bullet states the unified rule; §4.5's `Drain()` **fresh-frame contract** supersedes the v0.195 return-the-receiver form (`Drain()` mints a small drain-view frame — the `for` desugaring's `using var __source` disposes the frame at loop end, and the frame must not *be* the collection; observable drain semantics unchanged), §4.13 states it family-wide; §6.9 gains the positive `ReceiveAll()` frame-identity statement (a fresh drain enumerable over the channel; the at-most-one-consumption rule is the channel's single-consumer invariant, not a frame-identity fact — the previously-silent identity, stated rather than inherited); §5's intro states the operators' unmarked extension declarations as the ordinary minting spelling. §14.4's `OwningCache.Drain()` example — the member the v0.223 remedy was unsound at — is untouched and becomes coherent: `_items.Drain()` is now a fresh minted frame, transferable through the `owned` return.
- **The lazy-query/derived-interface seam, drafted and flagged.** With the §29.11 carve deleted, `OrderBy`/`ThenBy`'s results (declared `IOrderedEnumerable<T>`, outside the eight heads) need a stated classification: drafted as the same minting members **by their lazy-query kind** (compiler-known, as §29.11's provenance tracking already is), while the derived interfaces stay outside every declared-type-keyed boundary (the static-announcement rule, §27.1.1, §27.6) — the derived-interface **slot** dispositions at §27.1.1/§27.6 are preserved verdict-for-verdict (the quartet's direct call moves borrow → mint; the Behavior-change bullet below records it — gate round). A drafting call the proposal did not enumerate, taken as the minimal reading that leaves the slot dispositions standing; flagged for the gate, which closed its formation leak at §27.6 (the lazy-query-kind bar; the gate-round paragraph below).
- **§29.1 — the self-returning enumerator, stated (drafting seam Q2; the Q2 recommendation replaced at the gate round).** A class implementing both `IEnumerable<T>` and `IEnumerator<T>` may return `this` from `GetEnumerator()`; §29.1 now records the shape as a **recorded seam of the owned-marker protocol spelling**, not an exemption: the protocol's declared `owned IEnumerator<T>` return means the caller takes ownership at every call whatever the implementation body does — a receiver-borrow reading is not available through interface dispatch, where the body is invisible, so the classification stays uniform — and an implementation handing back its receiver must keep exactly-once itself, which the shipped compiler does by wrapping the result and resolving the alias at runtime (v0.235, #2384). The unification neither creates nor widens the seam — it is the protocol spelling's, not the calls-mint rule's — and whether the protocol should carry a static receiver-returning form is recorded as open defect [#3255](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3255), not decided here. (The proposal's Q2 recommendation — a receiver-borrow special case with the desugaring's bindings read as §28.10 pins — was refuted at the gate as undecidable through dispatch and contradicting the shipped wrap; the gate-round paragraph below carries the finding.)
- **§28.6 and the axiom register.** §28.6's method-return exclusion generalizes from `Task`-family-typed fields to mint-announcing-typed fields (the stored-view property face named in place; the owning-head-specific sentence deleted with its ground); the fresh-value parenthetical covers both families. **Register arithmetic, measured at this train's HEAD (obligated):** before the edit, twelve live axioms (A2–A7, A9–A14) and two tombstones (A1, A8); after, **eleven live and three tombstones** (A1, A2, A8) — the register lead, rationale §5.26's opening, and this entry all state the measured numbers; proposal 0101's A13 retirement has not graduated, so no coordination adjustment applies.
- **Rationale.** §5.26's A2 row takes the tombstone form of its shipped siblings; §12.10 gains the **reversal record** — the fence-accretion ledger named as the new evidence, the closure record's "classifying the slot is impossible in either direction" confronted (the impossibility was conditional on the stored-view spelling; the property respell removes the lend-face inhabitant), the v0.190 "not later 'fixed' by copying this ruling blindly" warning honored by the ledger being exactly what it demanded, the alternatives re-declined (marker / narrow repair / stop-at-the-fence), and `Drain()`'s fresh-frame cost stated — and the v0.256 paragraph's forward pointer at proposal 0096 is rewritten as the backward-looking record (a record that points forward at a reversal is stale the moment the reversal lands).
**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no new kernel rule, no new axiom — one axiom retired.** The unified rule is a pure derivation: K6.2 (announcement by declared type) + K6.3 (the frame minted at the call), with K1.7/K2.3 rejecting the storage re-exposure and K3.13 keeping no-silent-consume (the unmarked mint-announcing return joins K3.2's target-announced set; the kill table's row 3 and K5.1 read it off). **A2 retires to a tombstone in the shipped A1/A8 form** — no replacement axiom is minted, and the register's tombstone-pointing prose is left as-is (its prose-vs-instances defect — "points at the retiring revision's changelog entry" versus the generic changelog link both shipped tombstones use — is 0096 §2's recorded coordinator item, deliberately not taken here).
