### v0.259 changelog (v0.258 → v0.259)

**The 0097–0099 graduation train: proposals [0097](proposals/0097-superseded-exception-snapshots.md) (charter ruling C3 — superseded-exception snapshots), [0098](proposals/0098-stdlib-surface-program.md) (charter ruling C7 — the stdlib surface program), and [0099](proposals/0099-scope-guard.md) (charter ruling C5 — `ScopeGuard` and the `defer`/`errdefer` decline) graduate as one revision, ruled under the owner's 2026-08-18 delegation.** Three independent programs, one train: a diagnostics recovery that spends zero new ownership rules (the superseded exception's diagnosis is snapshotted onto the machinery `CauseChain` has used since v0.162 — later-wins kept, the confrontation with primary-wins recorded); a stdlib truth-and-surface pass (one phantom member declared, one shadowing rename, one 14→2 overload collapse with its blocked twin honestly recorded, two document-wide §1 conventions, three repairs, one evidence-gated decline); and the errdefer idiom as an ordinary library type whose whole design is that **no compiler support is required**, beside the recorded decline of the statement forms. Each proposal's semantic content is the contract; the drafting was re-read against this train's HEAD, where v0.257's vocabulary (the three announcement senses, the K5 criterion's derivations) and v0.258's calls-mint unification had moved several quoted passages — the HEAD adaptations are recorded per bullet.

- **Spec §31.2/§31.4 and the supersession sites — the superseded exception is recorded before it is dropped (0097).** `Exception` gains one additive property, `SupersededChain: Array<ExceptionInfo>` (§31.4, beside `CauseChain` — no new type, no new constructor, runtime-populated exactly as `StackTrace` is), and §31.2 gains the **record-before-drop rule**: at the instant of supersession, before the superseded exception is disposed (or, for the two owner-owned instances, dropped from the in-flight slot undisposed), the runtime appends, first, every entry of the superseded exception's own `SupersededChain` and, last, its `ExceptionInfo` snapshot — type name, `Message`, `StackTrace` — keeping the chain **chronological, earliest-superseded first** (supersession has no causal depth, only time — the deliberate ordering contrast with `CauseChain`'s outermost-cause-first, stated in §31.4 so the two chains are not read as parallel orderings). §31.2.1's throwing `when` guard and §28.4's multi-value cleanup pass take the rule by cross-reference (site 3 is the N−1-losses case, now one flat chain), and **§22.9 joins the cross-reference set** — v0.256 identified the construction unwind as §28.4's owned-field pass run partially, so its multi-disposal edges carry the same clause. The *before* is the rule's whole safety content (a snapshot after disposal reads a disposed instance — `DisposedAccessException` checked, UB unchecked), and the append is **best-effort, by deliberate carve-out from §17.7's fatal-allocation rule, stated on both sides**: a mid-unwind allocation failure silently drops the entry and the supersession proceeds as at v0.258 — `SupersededChain` is diagnostic data, never a correctness surface. §31.1's reporting-surface and copy-the-data-out sentences, the uncaught-exception report (§33.3), and the FFI-boundary abort each gain the chain beside `CauseChain` — **HEAD adaptation:** the abort's print sentence lives in §32.8's callback rules, not §32.9 as the proposal's target list had it; the §32.8 carrier was edited. A recorded loss, deliberate: a superseded exception's own `CauseChain` is not carried (`ExceptionInfo` has no slot for a nested chain; widening a shipped public record was declined). One boundary flagged, not ruled: **§22.13's exit-time static-disposal pass** is a multi-disposal pass §28.4 does not enumerate, running with an uncaught exception explicitly contemplated — what a throwing exit-time disposer does is stated nowhere, the silence predates this train, and §22.13 now says so explicitly (recorded open; [#3258](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3258) tracks the open questions).
- **Rationale §11.8 — the confrontation, recorded (0097).** Primary-wins (the Java try-with-resources shape) is declined with its costs named — a second live exception (§31.4's own `InnerException` decline arriving through the supersession door), a change to the single in-flight-slot model, and an arbitrary "first disposer is primary" at §28.4's pass — while the thing the flip was argued *for*, the diagnostics, is what the snapshot delivers. The precedents are cited honestly: Java added the *list*, not the priority; Python's `__context__` **is** later-wins-plus-context, precisely this model with a live carrier where Bezel's is a snapshot, the same difference §31.4 already chose for causes. Reopening bar: field evidence that upstream `catch` arms match on cleanup failures often enough to matter — the one gain the snapshot does not provide, and one a future primary-wins could add over the same chain.
- **Stdlib §5 — `ElementAtOrNull` declared; the warning set enumerates it (0098 i).** Four normative texts (spec §29.11's warning member set, stdlib §5 twice, Guide 05) had named `ElementAt`'s `*OrNull` form; the stdlib never declared it — a normative enumeration carrying a phantom member (vacuous to implement, false in the way that misleads). Declared: `ElementAtOrNull(index: int): T?` — null when the index is out of range, no predicate form (an index has no predicate analogue — the four texts' "and predicate forms" continues to distribute over `First`/`Last`/`Single` only). Spec §29.11's warning set is now enumerated explicitly (`First`/`FirstOrNull`/…/`ElementAt`/`ElementAtOrNull`), the new member a warning-set member for exactly `ElementAt`'s reason (a borrow of the element under §28.3's bare-type-parameter rule); the §7.10 nullable-conflation caveat is inherited from the tier's existing sentence, nothing new written.
- **Stdlib §4.10 — `OwningSet<T>.Take`/`TryTake` → `Pop`/`TryPop` (0098 ii; breaking rename, zero external users, hard flip, no alias — the 0090 Q3/0091 precedent).** The ground is measured shadowing: under spec §26.5 rule 1 the instance `Take(query)` made LINQ's `Take(count)` unreachable on set receivers by name, forever. The rename un-shadows it (`set.Take(2)` now resolves to the lazy operator — the rename's whole point) and joins the family the documents already teach (`OwningStack`/`OwningQueue` spell `Pop`/`TryPop`; the set's forms differ by the query arity). `OwningDictionary.PopValue`/`TryPopValue` **stay, with the reason now stated at §4.9**: the `Value` suffix carries information (the egress transfers the value and consumes the key as a query) — a naming-carries-information ground, not an exception. The **`TryPopAt` gap is recorded at §4.5** with the band reasoning on both sides (positional egress throwing-only while its first/last specializations carry Try forms; the surface currently asserts neither resolution), not closed. Old names left the stdlib in this same revision; every doc carrier conformed — spec §28.3's producer example and §28.11's ownership-out list, stdlib §1's Try-convention roster and §6.11's guard-escape list, rationale §5.7's two carriers, Guides 02/04/05.
- **Stdlib §5/§5.1 — `Sum` migrates to `INumber<U>`; `Average` recorded blocked (0098 iii, the honest split; drafting seam Q1 resolved as recommended).** The stated reason for 28 per-type aggregation overloads — "no generic numeric constraint in this version" — had been false since v0.176. `Sum`'s 14 collapse to two constrained generics (`Sum<U>(selector: (T) -> U): owned U where U: INumber<U>`; `Sum(): owned T where T: INumber<T>` — spec §11.8's own accumulator shape, its ownership already verified at every substitution by §28.3's resolved note, `owned` erased at value substitutions per §28.1). `Average`'s 14 **stay**, blocked primarily on the result-type mapping (five of seven forms deliberately widen to `double` while `float`/`decimal` keep their own types — no constraint expresses that; a single `Average<U>(): U` truncates integer averages, a single `(): double` loses `decimal`), secondarily on the constraint-shape cost of the now-expressible division (`ISteppable<U>.Step(U.Zero(), count)` reaches the count at the price of a second, meaning-stretched constraint on every conformer) — recorded at §5 with the associated-result-type gap named as what it awaits. **HEAD adaptation, a conform the proposal did not flag:** spec §22.6's *Implicit conversions and tie-breaking* used the per-type `Sum` selector family as its worked example for lambda-return ranking; with that family gone the example is re-keyed to `Average` — the family that deliberately keeps the per-type overloads and now exercises the rule — with a parenthetical recording the v0.259 move (the generic `Sum`'s return slot *binds* rather than ranks).
- **Stdlib §1 — two document-wide conventions land in one pass (0098 iv + v(b); drafting seam Q2 resolved as recommended — §1, not spec §31).** The **exception-safety post-state band**: a mutator that re-enters user code (comparators, `Equals`/`GetHashCode`, caller-supplied predicates/selectors/keys) leaves, on a throw, a receiver that is **valid and usable** with every element intact and none half-transferred — on an owning container the dispose-exactly-once obligation preserved for every element — while the contents are otherwise unspecified: the **basic guarantee, not the strong** (structurally unavailable on the owning family — a shadow copy is the value copy §4.5 says cannot exist), stated once as a library promise the language rules make statable rather than force (§28.4's multi-value cleanup, §28.7's drop-on-overwrite carry the exactly-once accounting; the per-member discharge is the gate-round softening), with §4.4's sorting contract remaining the stronger member-specific instance. The **block-by-name note**: spec §26.5 rule 1 commits to instance members by name, so where a collection declares `Count`, `Contains`, `First`, `Last`, `Reverse`, or `ToArray`, the same-named §5 operator is unreachable on that receiver — `arr.Count(pred)` does not resolve to LINQ; `coll.Where(pred).Count()` composes (`Where` is shadowed nowhere). **`CountWhere` is declined in the same note, evidence-gated (0098's one decline):** it fixes one name of six, the composition is idiomatic, no corpus use or filed issue evidences the friction, and the recorded general remedy is rationale §18's extension-call-disambiguation deferral; the reopening bar (field evidence on `Count`/`Contains` specifically) is stated with it. **Truth repairs beside them:** §9.7's LINQ-applicability claim narrowed by the measured four blocked names on `Array<T>`; §5's `Reverse` note's §26.4→§26.5 mis-cite fixed (§26.4 has no rules).
- **Stdlib §2.21 — `ScopeGuard`, the errdefer idiom as a library type (0099; requires no compiler support, stated at the top of its section).** `public class ScopeGuard` with `constructor(scoped action: () -> ())`, idempotent `Dismiss()`, `IsDismissed`, and a destructor that invokes the action unless dismissed — landed exactly as drafted. Every element verified against HEAD: `scoped` is **required** (§28.14's call-bounded default forbids storing a plain callback; the guard's field is the admitted `scoped`-field-of-the-bounding-object shape) and its spelling **mandatory** (§22.10 rejects `scoped` on primary-constructor parameters — the explicit-constructor form is the only admitted shape until that recorded bound lifts); the bounding object resolves by **form 1** (constructor call → constructed object), so `using var g := new ScopeGuard(…)` admits capture-bearing lambdas whose local sources are declared before `g` — the natural acquire-then-arm order — while any other binding, plain `var` included, admits capture-free only; **quiescence is satisfied by construction** (the action runs *in* the destructor, during disposal, never after — §2.21 is the normative statement §28.14 asks of compiler-known types); the **K5.7 freeze is taught before it bites**, with the `do … end` remedy for the build-guard-commit-transfer-out shape, plus the method-reference-on-`this` and field remedies. Facts: an explicit `— none` line with its ground (the §6.9 `Channel<T>` precedent). Deliberate absences recorded: no dismissed-initial-state constructor, no `owned`-taking form (a guard's job is the *action*; a value's undo is its owner's disposal), no `AsyncScopeGuard` (a `() -> Task` action's invocation from a synchronous disposal path is exactly what §28.14 rejects). The composition with 0097 is stated where the reader needs it: a guard action throwing on an exception edge is a §28.4 supersession the new chain records. §2.10 gains the one-line cross-reference. **Verification items (0099 §6) re-checked at HEAD:** spec §2.3's `System` roster is explicitly representative-not-exhaustive, so no spec §2.3 edit arises; `IsDismissed` lands **unmarked** — §2, `ScopeGuard`'s own module, leaves `readonly property` getters uniformly unmarked (measured within §2: **65 unmarked, 0 `pure`-marked** — the stronger ground than the document-wide 125-vs-31 figure, whose marked set is the collections' `Count`/`Capacity` family outside §2; same verdict), so the drafted declaration is no outlier and stands verbatim.
- **Rationale §17.11 — language-level `defer`/`errdefer`, declined with grounds and a reopening bar (0099).** Three grounds, one per half: the value half is redundant under affine ownership (disposal is attached to values; the tighter scope is `do … end`; a `defer` would be a second spelling for one obligation); the ordering half already exists on the single establishment-ordered cleanup stack (`finally`, §31.2); and the failure half needs an "are we unwinding?" primitive the language deliberately lacks — D's `scope(failure)` and C++'s `std::uncaught_exceptions()` name it — whose addition would make meaning depend on ambient unwind state where nothing names an exception. The commit-flag guard is the sanctioned spelling, packaged as `ScopeGuard`; reopening requires both field evidence of systematic misuse *and* a designed uncaught-exception predicate. Guide 01 gains the teaching section (*Cleanup that must not run on the success path*, new §10 — the flag version first, the guard beside it, the freeze taught with the rejected-then-repaired transfer-out example, the when-not-to-reach-for-it rule, the pointer to the decline; Quick reference renumbers §10→§11, with zero cross-document references to the old number, verified).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no new kernel rule, no new axiom — no rule content anywhere in the train.** 0097's whole delta is a value-record copy into a field of an object the runtime already owns at a point the runtime already controls: `ExceptionInfo` is a three-string record (no disposal obligation, §28.9), the carrier duplicates `CauseChain`'s shape on the same class, the superseded instance is never retained (the identical move §31.4 makes for `cause`, for the identical stated reason), §31.1's arm-lifetime rules and the two owner-owned exemptions are untouched, and no constructor's purity classification changes (the chain is runtime-populated, like `StackTrace`). 0098 is a surface program: the rename, the declaration, and the collapse touch no K rule (the block-by-name note restates §26.5 rule 1; the exception-safety band states what §28.4/§28.7 make statable as a library promise; `Sum`'s generics ride §11.8 dispatch and §28.1 erasure as already ratified). 0099 spends none of axiom A11's liftables — `ScopeGuard` is a *client* of §28.14's ratified forms (form 1, the `using var` admission, the K5.7 freeze, the quiescence obligation), arguably the storage-bounded design's first ordinary-user-facing one, and its §2.21 statement is the normative quiescence declaration §28.14 already provides for.

**Migration.** Doc-only at this train: the compiler, runtime, and test migrations below are **recorded as outstanding**, not performed — the coordinator files the tracking issues after the train.

- **Newly defined:** `Exception.SupersededChain: Array<ExceptionInfo>` with the §31.2 record-before-drop rule (ordering clause, best-effort clause, the two owner-owned superseding-side clauses (self-supersession records nothing; the chain is per raise, cleared on an owner's re-raise), and the two-chains-independence statement); `ElementAtOrNull` (stdlib §5); the two `INumber`-constrained `Sum` forms; stdlib §1's exception-safety band and block-by-name note; stdlib §2.21 `ScopeGuard` (four members, the no-facts line); rationale §11.8 and §17.11 (decision records).
- **Newly rejected:** the old `OwningSet<T>.Take`/`TryTake` spellings (renamed; hard flip, no alias, zero external users). Nothing else — `defer`/`errdefer` and `CountWhere` were never in the language or library, so their declines reject no program.
- **Newly accepted:** `set.Take(2)` resolving to LINQ on an `OwningSet<T>` receiver (the un-shadowing — the rename's whole point, needing its own pin); `xs.ElementAtOrNull(i)` (previously a resolution error the documents said could not happen); `Sum()`/`Sum(selector)` at every `INumber<T>` conformer the per-type set did not cover — the narrow primitives `byte`/`sbyte`/`short`/`ushort` (a no-selector `Sum()` did not exist for them, and every selector call returning one was permanently ambiguous under §22.6's co-equal-conversions rule — now binding at the element's own type, overflow-checked in it) and every **user** `INumber<T>` conformer, the pre-1.0 point of the migration.
- **Newly warned:** nothing new in kind — `ElementAtOrNull` joins §29.11's existing terminal-accessor provenance warning set, drawing the v0.243 warning under the same predicate as `ElementAt`; the gate round sweeps `MinOrNull()`/`MaxOrNull()` into the same enumeration by `Min()`/`Max()`'s own reasoning (no-selector aggregations returning `T?`, the element borrow unchanged).
- **Behavior change on legal programs:** none observable except through 0097's additions — the uncaught-exception report (§33.3), the FFI-boundary abort (§32.8), and `ToString()` (§31.4 — the rendering promise `CauseChain` already carried, now stated for the new chain) render one more chain, and a `catch` arm can now read a `SupersededChain` that was previously not there to read. No exception's identity, no disposal timing, no control flow changes; `Sum` calls that resolved at v0.258 keep their result types and values.
- **Interface carriage:** one member added to a public built-in type (`Exception` — §2.8's existing member-added/widening row); the stdlib artifact deltas are the rename (breaking, zero users), the removed 14 `Sum` overloads, and the added members.

### v0.260 changelog (v0.259 → v0.260)

**The 0100–0102 graduation train: proposals [0100](proposals/0100-the-body-seam-examined-and-closed.md) (charter ruling C12 — the body seam, examined and closed), [0101](proposals/0101-a13-retirement-study.md) (charter ruling C11 — the A13 retirement study, conducted to its conclusion), and [0102](proposals/0102-small-records.md) (charter rulings C4/C2/C6/C8 plus the riding small records) graduate as one revision, ruled under the owner's 2026-08-18 delegation.** One provenance is distinct and stated first: **0100's seam ruling is the owner's own** — a mid-turn 2026-08-18 direction (*"what if we do nothing? And also accept an empty line as a separator between contracts and statements?"*, clarified *"i meant it as a convention"*) — so the bare-open keep, the blank-line convention, and the floor land on the owner's direction, the proposal being its permanent record; the rest of the train lands under the standing delegation. Three programs: the body seam closes with **no token added** (a style convention, a keyword reservation, and a decline record written in full); the register's one recorded exactly-once carve-out **retires** — the study was conducted, both blockers confronted, and the outcome is adoption of the proposal's **Rule B**, not its recommended Rule A, on measured HEAD evidence the recommendation did not have; and the §22.5 named-move exclusion — a vestige of a production v0.246 deleted — **lifts**, with five small records landing beside it. Every quoted passage was re-read at this train's HEAD (v0.259) and the drafted text adapted to the live vocabulary; the HEAD adaptations are recorded per bullet.

- **Spec §22.16 — the blank-line separator lands as a recommended, non-normative style convention (0100; the owner's own ruling).** The *Clause granularity is semantic* note's recommended-style sentence extends by one clause: where a member's clause region is followed by a body, a blank line between the last clause and the first body statement — *the promises above the gap, the doing below it* — with the disclaimer stated in the same breath: both recommendations are style only, no implementation consults the layout, and a member without them means exactly what one with them means. **No obligation on user code arises anywhere.** The convention is explicitly not parse-significant, permanently: [#744](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/744) removed the language's only newline-significant rule and rationale §3.1 forbids structure from layout, and the parser never needs the blank line because the floor (next bullet) closes the stealing half of the seam grammatically — the load-bearing composition of the ruling. **The docs adopt their own convention** at a measured **10 adjacency sites** (2 in the spec — §22.16's own `Account` example — and 8 in Guide 06; re-measured at this HEAD by the proposal's methodology, reproducing the proposal's v0.255 figure exactly; the study's earlier ~19 counted clause-bearing fences including abstract and interface members, which have no body and no seam). `scripts/check_docs.sh` gains the docs-only style check — **landed as check 3d**, an adaptation recorded here: the proposal specified "check 5" against v0.255's five checks, but v0.257 added the §3.6 TABLE check (3c) in the interim, so the new check takes the next slot in the lettered series — scanning every fenced block of the **nine non-changelog documents** (a second recorded deviation, the 0095-Q4 shape: implemented as the nine-document literal list check 1 already carries, rather than a six-document contract-bearing subset that would drift as guides gain or lose contract examples — the superset a no-op wherever no clause-bearing fence exists), failing on any clause-region→body adjacency without the blank line, naming document, line, and member; skipped by `--quick` like check 4, and deliberately not wired into `gate.sh`/`agent_check.sh` (docs gate, not compiler gate). Mutation-tested at landing: removing a landed blank line and injecting a fresh violating member each fail the check naming the site; `end`-followed, arrow-bodied, and body-less clause regions do not trip it.
- **Spec Appendix B — the floor: `requires`, `ensures`, `invariant` become unconditionally reserved (0100).** B.1 takes its three edits in one subsection — the three words join the **Unconditionally reserved** list (with a dated parenthetical carrying the ground), leave the **Contextual** list, and leave B.1's opening-paragraph roster (which repeats the list and would otherwise disagree with it); B.2 deletes **two rows**, not three (`requires`/`ensures` shared one; `invariant` had its own), and B.2's closing reserved-everywhere note (`when`/`where`/`with`/`yield`) gains the three words with the simplification's ground: the end of a clause region is now a fact about the *token*, so proposal 0055 §3's **first-statement collision is impossible** — nothing can be named `requires` any more, and the clause region can never absorb a statement at any member kind. `old` and `result` **stay contextual**, with the reason recorded in the same note (clause-interior names, common vocabulary, marker-wins rows already seamless). A.4's clause-region commentary conforms — the "keyword reading always wins there (the B.2 env rule)" comparison is replaced by the unconditional statement, since after reservation there is no identifier reading to win against. Corpus cost re-verified at this HEAD: **exactly one** identifier-position use of any of the three words exists — `tests/parser/contract_clauses_2053_test.cpp :: requires_as_parameter_name_not_a_marker_spec_22_16` (`method M(requires: int): int => requires;`) — which flips to a negative test (recorded for the compiler lane below, not edited by this doc-only train); a second grep hit is prose in a lit-test comment.
- **The decline record and the rationale §3.1 third-category note (0100).** Proposal 0100 is the permanent, standing-alone record of the whole exploration — the reader looks *there*, this entry only indexes it: mandatory `do` declined on migration size (a five-figure corpus insertion — ~5,249 existing `do` tokens against ~24,000–31,000 member-body openings, the proposal's measurement — to mark a seam that occurs at 10 sites in the normative corpus), with `does` recorded as the runner-up so a future revisiting starts from the pair; optional and conditional `do` declined (the v0.246 one-spelling-per-site owner-ruled precedent; conditional-on-clauses makes adding a contract a breaking body edit); `:` declined on collision with type ascription; `;` declined because it reverses 0055's structural-parentheses ruling; the `=`-family and novel symbols declined; the contract-free bare opening **examined and kept** (the Lua precedent, the signature as the frame, `end <Name>` naming the extent); and the six-language survey's conclusion — every language that marks this seam marks it with a token it already required everywhere, and Bezel has no such token. The reopening bar is field evidence from external users, admitting the token space again but never the layout route. Rationale §3.1 (*Always semicolons*) gains the **third-category note**: a contract clause carries no terminator not because a semicolon would be Pascal-wrong but because the clause's structural parentheses already delimit it — the Ada rule is about statements and blocks, a self-delimiting clause is neither, and the `invariant` member (a member, keeping its `;`) is the check on the reading. The **0055 §3 diagnostic obligation is restated as live, re-scoped** (Migration ledger below): the diagnostic-quality half — a non-abstract member parsing body-less *while carrying clauses* should draw a note naming the likely clause-region confusion — survives reservation and remains unimplemented; the parenthesize-or-rename remedy half is obsolete (nothing can be named `requires`), the note's content becoming "the clause region ended where the writer thought it had not" — and one HEAD adaptation recorded here (gate round): 0100 §4.2's closing "keeps 0055's remedy sentence" had nothing to keep — §22.16 at this HEAD carries no such sentence, the 0055 note having never landed in spec text — so the restatement lands as this ledger's record, with no §22.16 edit made or needed.
- **Spec §15.3/§15.1.1/§28.7/§28.4/§28.3/§22.12/§35.4, the axiom register, Appendix C.3, rationale §5.26 — axiom A13 retires: owning-inline-array whole-value reassignment takes per-slot drop-on-overwrite (0101; the study conducted, concluding in Rule B).** The study was directed with its outcome not pre-committed, and the conclusion reached is **retirement by the proposal's Rule B** — *each live slot of the displaced value is disposed, reverse slot order, RHS-first, moved-from slots skipped* — **not the recommended Rule A** (reassignment-as-exit-edge with restoration required first). The reasoning chain, recorded in full because it departs from the recommendation: **(1)** the recorded blocker's premise is refuted at HEAD by the shipped implementation — moved-from *does* have a runtime representation for owning inline arrays (`move a[i]` nulls the slot in the alloca; `lowerMoveFromCollectionSlot`, #747), so "a per-slot flag the type does not have" is false: the slot pointer is the flag, at no width cost, invisible at the non-nullable form because restoration guarantees no observable null. **(2)** The mechanism is not merely reusable but **already shipped**: `Emitter::lowerOwningInlineArrayReassign` (`src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Stmts.cpp`, measured at this HEAD) has implemented exactly Rule B since the #1385 fix — reverse slot order, RHS-first on the main path, null-guard skipping moved-from slots, sharing `emitDisposeAndReclaim` with the scope-end pass — pinned by a dedicated ASan-swept behavior test (`move_only_inline_array_reassign_drop_on_overwrite_1385_test.cpp`) whose header cites a "§28.7 v0.215" extension **that never landed in any spec revision** (the v0.215 entry carries no such change): the implementation has been ahead of the spec, §15.3's "those slots leak" has been false of the reference compiler, the shipped #1549 warning has warned of a leak that no longer happens, and #1385's closed-completed state — which the proposal read as a consolidation close with the work not done — is explained: the codegen work *was* done, without the spec amendment. This resolves the spec/implementation disagreement by amending the spec through the delegated study, per the repository's own rule that such divergences are resolved as recorded decisions. **(3)** The proposal's grounds for preferring A over B do not survive these facts: B does not degenerate to A's conservative edge (no static precision is needed — the runtime state is exact, so B rejects *nothing*, where A newly rejects the moved-from-at-store and every non-constant-index case); B needs no per-store-site slot list; and the "second, weaker notion of restored" is actually the landed rule itself — §28.7's K3.11 clause already words drop-on-overwrite as *"if the previous value is live (non-null and not moved-from), it is disposed"*, so Rule B is that clause's exact per-slot transcription, and the displaced value's restoration obligations are discharged by the kill on **K9.3's existing no-future-read ground** (the destructor-body exemption's), the proposal's "legal at the store, illegal three lines later for the same slot" scenario dissolving because the displaced value's slot states do not survive the store. **(4)** Rule A's residual costs are real and unpurchased: at `[N owned]T` it forces constructing fresh values into holes solely for the pass to dispose them instantly. **(5)** The payoff is identical under B: *every owned value is disposed exactly once on every path* now holds **without qualification** — the §28.3 claim's parenthetical rewritten, its disposal-table footnote reduced to the one `Task` carve-out, §28.7's carve sentence replaced by the two-kind statement, §15.3's asymmetry sentence deleted and its *Whole-value reassignment* bullet rewritten as the rule (self-assignment ruled a well-defined no-op — the RHS move empties the location first; per-slot states travel with a moved whole value), §15.1.1 naming the overwrite as the pass's third run point, §35.4's contrast clause conformed, and the K5.2 consume-site freeze applying to the reassignment as to every consume. **A study finding beyond the proposal's target list:** the never-dispose-at-overwrite behavior **survives at §22.12 form-(iv) static fields, re-grounded** — §22.13's static-overwrite posture ("a racing first use may still hold a displaced value") governs every admitted mutable static, class-typed and inline-array alike, so the static residue is an instance of a recorded *rule*, not an axiom, and the pre-v0.260 reassignment warning survives at exactly that form (the one place displaced slots genuinely persist to process exit); A13 therefore retires with no replacement axiom minted. **Gate item 2 stated, not derived** (§28.7 *Ordering and exceptions*): the per-slot pass is a §28.4 multi-value cleanup — a throwing slot disposer does not stop it, later throws supersede with the superseded exceptions recorded on `SupersededChain` (the v0.259/0097 composition, cross-cited as the two proposals directed), the store is abandoned, the RHS value unwinds as an unbound owned temporary, and disposed slots are left empty so the unwinding discharge observes only empty slots — the emptiness an unobservable state of the abandoned store's unwind, stated with its [§15.1.1](Bezel_Language_Spec.md#sec-owning-inline-arrays) reconciliation (gate round); and §28.4's own multi-value-cleanup list gains the pass as an enumerated member — the enumeration a §28.7 membership assertion must resolve against, the [#3258](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3258) drift class caught at this train's gate round rather than left for that issue's list-exhaustiveness question to find. **Register arithmetic, measured before and after the edit:** eleven live axioms and three tombstones (A1, A2, A8) before; **ten live and four tombstones** after — the register lead, rationale §5.26's opening (which gains "A13 retired v0.260" in its dated roster), and this entry state the measured numbers; the A13 tombstone takes the shipped A1/A2/A8 row form, and §5.26's A13 entry takes the prose tombstone form carrying the study record. Appendix C.3's drop-on-overwrite row gains the per-slot statement with the static-posture pointer; its owning-choice row drops the now-vestigial "for choices" contrast qualifier. ### v0.262 changelog (v0.261 → v0.262)

**The 0103/0104/0105 ruling train: the owner's 2026-08-19 rulings ("resolve all questions, I agree with your resolutions") land the recommended resolutions of proposals [0103](proposals/0103-shared-value-generics-study.md), [0104](proposals/0104-witness-abi-open-questions.md), and [0105](proposals/0105-body-locality-invariant.md), and of issues [#3269](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3269) and [#3270](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3270), as one revision.** Four trains, one entry: two rulings (a new §14 rule; a §22.12 classification), one clarification (§3.6's scope sentence), one rationale amendment (§10) — plus one process-only landing riding the same push (the spec-change-process §9 checklist line, 0105's). Every insertion point and every cited § was re-read at this train's HEAD (v0.261).

- **Spec §14.6 — polymorphic recursion is rejected at the declaration (ruling; [#3270](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3270), proposal 0104 §4).** Decided: a new subsection at the end of §14 (anchor `sec-recursive-instantiation`) defines the static **instantiation-request graph** — each generic type and each generic member a node, a non-generic member's edges attached to its declaring type's node, one edge per instantiation a declaration's compilation must request, arising from generic calls, generic-type instantiations, base-clause references, and field, choice-payload, and signature types, with override bodies contributing their edges to the overridden member's node and a type's node reaching its own generic members only at requested instantiation sites — and rules that within a strongly-connected component every edge must substitute each target parameter with a bare type parameter in scope at the source declaration (its own or an enclosing declaration's) or a closed type; any other in-SCC substitution — an argument containing an in-scope parameter other than as the bare argument itself, the nullable form `T?` included (`F<Pair<T, T>>` on the call route; a `Node<Pair<T, T>>?` field on the data route) — is a compile error at the declaration holding the edge, the diagnostic naming the cycle and the growing argument. Same-key recursion (`F<T>` calling `F<T>`) and bare-parameter permutation cycles (`F<T, U>` calling `F<U, T>`) stay legal; cross-module cycles are checked over §2.8.3 rule 1's compilation closure. Why: 0104 §4.1 found v0.261 silent on recursive generic instantiation — the absence audited against four near-misses (§14.2's bound cycles, §27.8's alias rule, §12.10's inheritance cycles, §35.1's value self-containment) — and the silence untenable: a monomorphizing implementation cannot terminate on the expanding shape while a witness implementation could compile and run it, so program admissibility would depend on codegen strategy, exactly what §11.8's semantics-not-strategy posture forbids; and bezelc today neither rejects nor terminates on the shape (machinery-derived, 0104 §4.2 — no depth bound, no cross-key cycle detection). Declined, with reasons (0104 §4.3): an instantiation-site depth limit (acceptance keyed to an implementation-defined knob; unusable under §2.8.2 clause 2's external-instantiation obligation; the diagnostic lands deep in an importer's chain instead of at the defect); accept-and-support (AOT-unavailable, and it would mandate exactly the runtime metadata cache whose absence the 0103 record names as the design's structural advantage); rejection only at the instantiation site (an exported generic that no argument can instantiate would compile silently — a lie of a public surface). The known over-rejections are recorded, not hidden — three: a dynamically-unreachable growing edge still rejects (the bounded set is the requested closure, not the executed one); an in-SCC `F<T?>` edge rejects even though §7.10's nullable collapse would in fact bound that closure (`T?` is neither a bare parameter nor closed); and a mixed cycle a closed edge would in fact bound (`F<T>` calling `G<int>` while `G<U>` calls `F<Box<U>>`) rejects, the condition being per-edge over the component — deliberately stronger than closure-boundedness, and decidable edge-by-edge at the declaration.
- **Spec §22.12 — readonly bare-parameter statics classified per instantiation (ruling; [#3269](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3269)).** Decided: a `static readonly` field or auto-property whose declared type is a bare generic parameter (`T`, `T?`) is admitted at the declaration and classified **per instantiation, after substitution** — a substitution within rule 3's immutable content is unrestricted; a class-type substitution takes rule 4's warning unless the substituted class is in the warning-suppression set; any other substitution (an interface, function-type, or non-sendable value-kind substitution among them) takes rule 4's warning treatment at that instantiation; a nullable substituted form classifies as its underlying type — with the diagnostic at the instantiation site, naming the offending type argument (§3.6 rule 2's diagnostic pattern). Rule 4's opening now names auto-properties beside fields, keeping the new paragraph's routing honest against rule 4's own words. The pre-existing concrete-typed residual — interface- and owning-choice-typed readonly statics, which rules 3–4 classify at no concrete type either — is out of this train's scope, recorded and tracked in [#3273](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3273), filed at this landing. The paragraph lands inside rule 4 (the readonly rules' home), leaving rule 2's numbering and its mutable-arm declaration-site error untouched; the `const` arm is stated as impossible under any substitution (`const` requires a primitive value type or `string`, which no bare parameter ever is — §22.12's existing type requirement, verified before citing). Why: rule 2's closing sentence bans the *mutable* bare-parameter static, while rules 3–4 admit readonly statics by concrete type kind and never addressed the bare-`T` readonly — the near-miss 0103 §3.1's statics row named; per-instantiation classification is §3.6 rule 2's standing discipline for every substitution-dependent verdict, so the ruling extends the existing pattern rather than minting one. Declined: classifying at the declaration in either direction — blanket admission ignores the class-typed substitutions rule 4 exists to warn on; blanket rejection would ban `static readonly` of `T` at every immutable substitution for the sake of the ones the warning already covers.
- **Spec §3.6 — the reservation's scope stated (clarification; 0103 Q5, owner-ruled 2026-08-19).** One sentence appended to the behavior-dispatch reservation paragraph: the reservation bounds the **user-facing surface** — what user code may condition on — not an implementation's realization strategy for generics, which §11.8 leaves open so long as the observable binding is unchanged. This records the ruled answer to 0103's Q5 in its §1.4's terms: the shared-codegen alternatives compose with the reservation rather than contradicting a recorded position — while remaining deferred behind 0103 §7 item 4's triggers, which the ruling leaves reachable but unfired.
- **Rationale §10 — the strategy sentence's standing recorded (amendment; 0103 Q3).** Two sentences appended to the specialize-values/share-references paragraph, pinned (v0.262): the sentence records strategy *intent*, not a decline — a third point of the space, unboxed sharing at value substitutions through a per-instantiation witness descriptor, was examined and priced (proposals 0103/0104, 2026-08-19) and stands available under §11.8's stated latitude — and the surviving reason the intent stands is codegen quality at value substitutions (indirect dispatch, not boxing). §11.8's appositive ("rationale §10's recorded strategy does both…") needed no edit and got none: §10 still records the same intent; what the amendment adds is its standing.
- **Process §9 — the body-locality checklist line lands (process-only; 0105, accepted by the owner 2026-08-19 answering the strengthened Q7 — mint now, 0105 §6 item 2 the recorded reason for not waiting on the streaming tier).** The spec-change-process §9 checklist gains one line in the kernel-classification line's shape: every ruling states its body-locality classification — **local**, **fact-discharged** (naming the per-body facts), **carve-out** (generic instantiation, confined to its two clauses), or **invariant amendment** (explicit, with the recorded reason) — citing proposal 0105 §1, which stays the invariant's carrier (the per-body-fact refinement confirmed as the canonical reading, 0105 Q1). No normative document is edited by that landing (0105's landing (b)); escalation to a normative anchor keys to 0103 §7 item 4's trigger (iii) (0105 Q2).

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): no contact** — no train touches §28/§30.5; no axiom moves (ten live + four tombstones stand as at v0.261). **Body-locality classification (this train's own new obligation, applied to itself):** §14.6 is **fact-discharged** — the cross-declaration verdict factors through each body's instantiation-request edge set, a per-body fact computed at that body's own single check and closed over the graph (0105 §1's §22.13-shaped discharge); §22.12's readonly classification is the generic-instantiation **carve-out**'s clause (i) — a declaration-computable fact evaluated against the substitution; the §3.6 sentence and the §10 amendment add no compile-time rule (**local**, vacuously).

**Gate round (same train).** One adversarial pass; verdict ship-after-fixes — one blocker, five importants, four minors, every finding applied before landing, none declined. **The blocker (with the first important as its sharpest consequence):** §14.6's node granularity and edge attribution were undefined, and the two available readings disagreed on a realistic shape — `Matrix<T>` with `method Widen<U>(): Matrix<Pair<T, U>>` is legal under member-level nodes (no `Matrix→Widen` edge exists unless requested, so the constructed `Widen→Matrix` edge is cross-SCC) and rejected under type-level nodes — while the drafted "bare type parameter of the source declaration" stranded the ordinary bounded shape of a generic method constructing its enclosing type at the enclosing parameter. Fixed with the member-level definition: each generic type and each generic member is a node; a non-generic member's edges attach to its declaring type's node; a type's node carries an edge to one of its own generic members only at a requested instantiation site, never implicitly; and the bare-parameter category re-scoped to parameters **in scope at** the source declaration (its own or an enclosing declaration's), the error clause keyed to the in-scope-parameter test rather than the undefined term "constructed type" — under which `Widen` and the enclosing-parameter edge stay legal and both growing routes still reject. **The other importants:** the must-clause/error-clause trichotomy closed explicitly (any other in-SCC substitution — `T?` included — is the error) with the nullable-form conservatism added to the over-rejection record; the per-edge-over-the-component approximation acknowledged in §14.6's own text and recorded as the third over-rejection (bounded mixed cycles still reject); §22.12's two-arm enumeration made total with the residual arm (any substitution matching neither rule 3's immutable content nor a class type takes rule 4's warning treatment at that instantiation) — the enumeration had reopened, at interface, function-type, and non-sendable value-kind substitutions, exactly the gap #3269 was filed to close; and 0104's Status and README rows reworded from "#3270 ruled and closed" to "ruled here; closed at the v0.262 landing", the closure being the push-time step, not a review-time fact. **Minors in step:** the nullable-substituted-form clause (classifies as its underlying type); rule 4's opening extended to name auto-properties, which the new paragraph routes through it; the newly-warned Migration clause added (the §5 template names the category; the classification mints real new warning sites); and the pre-existing concrete-typed readonly residual (interface- and owning-choice-typed statics, unclassified by rules 3–4 even non-generically) recorded as out of this train's scope and tracked in [#3273](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3273), filed at this landing. The critique also verified, and this entry records: the edge enumeration matches 0104 §4.3 exactly; the doc-corpus hunt found no existing declaration §14.6 newly rejects (`Tree<T>`-with-`Array<Tree<T>>`, `Pair<K,V>` iteration, `GroupBy`, and `Task.WhenAll<T>` are all cross-SCC); and the composition of the four trains holds, with one positive interaction worth keeping — §14.6's bound is what makes §22.12's per-instantiation obligation finite. Both checkers re-run green after the fixes at the same baselines; no fix touched a fenced example.

### v0.263 changelog (v0.262 → v0.263)

**The 0106 slate: the owner's 2026-08-20 ruling ("act on proposal 0106's slate — record the declines and land the two cheap rulings") lands the two stdlib rulings and the recording train of proposal [0106](proposals/0106-language-lessons-survey.md) §9 as one revision.** Four trains, one entry: two **rulings** (a stdlib purity marker; a stdlib fact grant, the only one with live derived-set consequences), one **recording train** of five decline records plus four register-hygiene items, and one **process-only** train in `spec-change-process.md`. Every insertion point and every cited § was re-read at this train's HEAD (v0.262); two of the brief's own citations were corrected against the current headings before use (the `CancellationTokenSource` fact line lives in stdlib §6.1, not §6.8 — §6.8 is `Domain`, and it carries one of the sentences the ruling amends).

- **Stdlib §9.8 — `Range<T>.Contains` is `pure` (ruling; 0106 §6.4 slate item iii).** Decided: `Contains` carries the `pure` marker in both declarations of the intrinsic (stdlib §9.8 and its restatement at spec §16.3), with the stdlib prose stating the contract. **Admissibility verified before the marker was written, against §22.15's rules for a runtime-provided body:** the parameter is a copyable value type at every admitted `T` (the integer types and `char`, §16.3's intrinsic restriction) and is neither `ref`, `out`, `owned`, `scoped`, nor move-only; the return is `bool`, so neither the owned-class-return nor the move-only-return rejection applies; the member is not `async`, not an iterator, not a destructor, not `extern`; and the body §16.3 specifies — nonempty-under-iteration conjoined with `min(Start, End) <= v <= max(Start, End)`, the inclusive bound excluded when `IsEndInclusive` is false, an open endpoint imposing no bound — reads the receiver's components and compares them, writing no storage outside the frame, allocating nothing, touching no task, domain, channel, event, or synchronization object, and **raising nothing at all** (§16.4 makes a zero-step `Range<T>` value non-existent, so no operation needs that case), which discharges §22.15's intrinsic-purity requirement that any exception from a pure intrinsic be trivial-dispose — vacuously, there being none. What it unblocks: `requires(port in 0..65535)`, the readable spelling of a range precondition, which §22.16 admits as a clause expression under §22.15's calls-to-pure-members rule; the `in` operator invokes `Contains` (§17.5), and range construction is already admitted pure-body material. **Ruled narrowly, and the rest named rather than swept along.** `GetEnumerator` **cannot** ride — §22.15 rejects an `owned` class-typed return outright — and that is recorded in the stdlib text rather than left to be rediscovered. **The six declared properties are ruled, not deferred (owner-ruled 2026-08-20).** The question an earlier draft of this entry left open — does classification-by-rule reach a storage-backed auto-property of a compiler-intrinsic record? — decides itself once the classification rule's own premise is read: *Members classified by rule* makes an auto-property getter pure **because the synthesized body is a backing-field read**, so it reaches exactly those properties for which that premise holds. `Start`, `End`, `Step` and `IsEndInclusive` read stored slots: they are **pure by classification**, no marker is needed, and one would be the redundant spelling §22.15 rejects on an auto-property declaration — so `requires(r.Step > 0)` compiles today, and always did. `IsOpenEnded` and `IsEmpty` are **recomputed** by the intrinsic (§16.3), so the premise fails for them, classification does not reach them, and they fall to the intrinsic-purity paragraph — where the marker is not merely admitted but **required**, since a checker would otherwise trust a runtime-provided computation carrying no stated contract at all. Both now carry it, and `requires(r.IsEmpty)` is served. **The coherence argument that settles it:** §16.3's normative formula makes `Contains` read `IsEmpty`, so this revision's own `Contains` marker rested on a contract `IsEmpty` did not state; marking `IsEmpty` is what makes the pair consistent rather than a second favour. **Admissibility verified before the markers were written:** `IsOpenEnded` is a null test over two slots; `IsEmpty` is a bound comparison over the four stored components with no zero-step case reachable (§16.4) — both read the receiver, allocate nothing, call nothing outside the fragment, and raise nothing, discharging the trivial-dispose requirement vacuously as `Contains` does. §9.2's auto-property *surface* keeps exactly the job it had, fixing the generated members and deciding no purity; §22.15's intrinsic paragraph gains the general rule so the next compiler-intrinsic record does not re-litigate this — the declared surface does not decide purity, a recomputed property takes the marker, a stored-slot read is classified. *Declined:* marking all six alike, which would either write a redundant-and-rejected marker on four or leave two runtime computations uncontracted; and deferring the four to an issue, now that the premise reading resolves them on the text.
- **Stdlib §6.1 — `CancellationTokenSource` granted the synchronized and displacement-unbounded facts; a published source is signal-only (ruling; 0106 §7.5.1 slate item ii).** Decided: the type gains a **Facts** line declaring **synchronized** and **displacement-unbounded**, and a record confronting each derived-set consequence, per stdlib §1's fact discipline ("a fact ruling states the facts it grants and confronts each derived-set consequence in its record") and §28.13's growth clause, which was written to receive exactly this. **The consequence the ruling is for:** the type joins §28.13's `Shared`-payload synchronized set — it is not self-distributing, having no sanctioned distribution channel of its own — so **`Shared<CancellationTokenSource>` is sendable**, a cloned handle crosses as a spawn argument or channel element, and the source is disposed once by whichever domain drops the last handle. The type itself gains no sendability. **The novelty that shapes the whole ruling:** `CancellationTokenSource` is the **first member of the `Shared`-payload set that is not itself sendable** — the other seven each cross on their own as well as behind a handle. Set membership keys on a type's facts, not on its sendability, and this is the first case where the two come apart. It matters because disposal of this payload runs **registered callbacks**, which are function values, and §30.14 states that "function-typed values are never sendable: their captures are borrows of the origin domain's scopes" — where every prior member's last-handle disposal runs only a destructor over state the disposing domain could legitimately have held (`Locked<T>`'s interior, the nearest shape, must be a *sendable class*). **What was landed, and what it replaces.** An earlier draft of this ruling stated `Register`'s confinement as a programmer obligation. That was wrong and is not what landed: **four** callback paths cross a domain boundary, and an obligation reaches only the first — a foreign domain calling `Cancel()`; the **last-handle drop**, which performs a full `Cancel()` on the disposing domain's thread and is a runtime race no obedient program can steer; a **linked child**, whose own callbacks fire transitively when a published parent is cancelled from anywhere; and a **process-global static**, on which any domain may call `Token` and then `Register`, a path this same revision opens by admitting the type to §22.12 rule 4's warning-suppression set. Two of the four are invisible at the site that would have to honour an obligation. What landed instead is a rule enforced at runtime: a source becomes **published** at three points — `new Shared<CancellationTokenSource>(owned source)`, a `static readonly`/`static owned readonly` field of the type, and a linked child of a published parent (publication does not propagate child-to-parent, cancellation running only parent-to-child) — and on a published source **`Register` raises `InvalidOperationException`**, while **publishing a source that already holds live registrations raises** at the publishing operation, which is what makes the register-then-share order immaterial. A published source is therefore **signal-only**, and every fire path is closed structurally rather than by enumeration: `Cancel`, `CancelAfter`, the `WithCancelAfter` deadline, cancel-on-dispose, and linked propagation all remain safe from any domain because the registration list is empty, so no fire path can run a foreign closure — including one an enumeration would miss. **The alternative design, confronted and not adopted:** a **runtime-checked domain affinity** — the source records its registering domain and a foreign `Register` raises — is the option the §30.12 precedent points at, and it fails on the *firing* half rather than the registering half. To close the four paths it must also govern who may fire, and each way out is worse than the disease: barring cross-domain `Cancel` destroys the grant's entire purpose (a shutdown coordinator cancelling another domain's work); admitting it only when no registrations exist makes a cancel's success depend on what an unrelated domain did, a race in the contract itself; and skipping the callbacks on a foreign last-handle drop would silently defeat the cleanup `Register` exists to run. Signal-only is the same idea taken to the point where it is sound: rather than policing every fire path, it empties the set they fire. *Also declined:* **queueing a foreign callback to its registering domain** — it breaks the guarantee `Register` exists to give, since disposal runs pending callbacks *before* severing the list, which is §28.14's quiescence (no stored callback is invoked after disposal completes), and a queued callback cannot be known to have run when disposal returns, or ever, that domain being possibly complete already (§33.3); **rejecting the registration statically** — `Register` is declared on `CancellationToken`, a freely-copyable record passed, stored in async frames, and copied without ceremony, so the check would need a whole-program value-provenance analysis over token values with no existing carrier to ride, where Bezel's per-value analyses (ownership, borrow liveness, definite assignment, narrowing) are method-local. Declined on that cost. **An earlier draft declined it by appeal to §3.6's closing rule; that appeal is withdrawn as a non-sequitur** — §3.6 governs *structural classifications of types*, and provenance is by the argument's own premise not one, so §3.6 forbids nothing here. **On the §30.12 precedent, precisely:** what is shared with the blocking acquisitions is the *runtime* layer — a member-level restriction on a synchronized type, enforced by an `InvalidOperationException` at the call. What is **not** shared is §30.12's lexical layer, and deliberately: a blocking acquire inside an `async` method is a syntactic property a compiler can see, while publication is a property of the receiver's history, so there is no lexical form to reject. The earlier draft cited this precedent for an *unenforced* obligation, which inverted it. **The recorded cost:** a program may today hold a `static readonly CancellationTokenSource` and `Register` on it, and in a single-domain program nothing is wrong with that; under this rule it raises. The over-rejection is deliberate and recorded in the stdlib text — a static is reachable from every domain by construction, the property cannot be narrowed to "reachable from a *second* domain" without observing the whole program, and the alternative is a hazard that first appears when a program later spawns a domain. The remedy is one line: poll, or hold the source domain-locally. **The source-outlives obligation, now spanning domains:** §30.8's obligation (the source must outlive the settlement of every task observing one of its tokens) gains a clause — under sharing it binds each observing domain and is discharged by that domain holding a live handle, the handle keeping the source alive where the borrow does not (§28.13). That is *stronger* than the intra-domain case, which rests on scope ordering. **The two other derived sets:** the **synchronized** fact puts the type in §22.12 rule 4's warning-suppression set, so a `static readonly` source is admitted warning-free — and suppressing that warning is right *because* the residual is now checked: rule 4 asks the programmer to confine the instance or ensure its internal synchronization, the fact discharges the second disjunct across the state-and-signal surface, and the part confinement was still protecting is excluded by a raise rather than by a reminder. The **displacement-unbounded** fact keeps the type *out* of rule 2's form-(i) set, so a **mutable** static stays rejected; that fact is granted on its own evidence, not by analogy to `Locked<T>` — overwrite-never-disposes would strand a source with its whole registration list and its registrations in every parent, and, worse than a payload-scaled leak, the stranded source can no longer be signalled, leaving every token still observing it waiting on a cancellation that cannot arrive. **Five** now-false or now-incomplete sentences were amended in the same edit rather than left to contradict the ruling: stdlib §6.1's "linking is intra-domain", stdlib §6.8's "there is no built-in cross-domain cancellation", spec §30.8's parenthetical saying the same, spec §30.14's closing "cancellation does not cross domains in this revision", and rationale §12.6's "a sendable cancellation primitive can be added later" — the last being the site the other four defer to, and the one describing the primitive this ruling delivers. Cross-domain linking is admitted with its transitive path stated rather than waved past: the link's own edge touches only the parent's synchronized state, but the child it feeds would run the child's callbacks on the cancelling domain's thread, which is why publication propagates to the linked child.
- **The recording train — five declines, each landed where its context lives (0106 §9, Q3, Q6).** *(a)* **Units of measure at the type-level-erased pole** — a new rationale §18 entry, recorded §18-style per that section's allocator-entry placement rule (what stands in the way is unbuilt machinery, not a rejected idea): its two prerequisites are §18 deferrals of its own (associated types; const generics), §14.6 removes the *normalizing* encoding (an expanding in-component instantiation shape) while the non-recursive phantom encoding escapes that rule only by degenerating into hand-declared identities, and the consequences past the type system are priced (§9.8 would see only the underlying `double`, §32.13's typed-handle admission excludes `double` single-field records, §2.8.2 identity would carry a fragile unit-expression argument). The entry records **all three poles** and declines exactly one: value-carried units need no language change and ship today in their single-dimension case as `TimeSpan`, whose producers, readouts, and dimensionally-split operators are the shape; doing nothing is the honest status quo elsewhere. *(b)* **Contract-carrying type aliases** — rationale §17.12, a rejection rather than a deferral: aliases see through (§27.8), so the feature would buy range safety and not the nominal distinctness a services language needs; no conversion boundary exists to check at (§25.4), so the check would be the parallel mechanism §3.6's closing rule forbids; and aliases are module-internal, so the guarantee would stop at the boundary where validation matters most. *(c)* **Bit-syntax patterns** — rationale §11.9, beside the pattern-matching entries, declining the *pattern-position* half only, on the pattern system's own three grounds (a binding whose type is computed inside the pattern; no exhaustiveness account for width alternatives; a borrow-producing binder, which no pattern kind is); the reader direction is untouched and is proposal 0109, filed separately. *(d)* **Forcible domain teardown** — **judged, and no new decline minted**: rationale §12.4 already contains the refuting sentence, but it predates domains and never says whether a domain boundary changes the answer, so the fix is to extend the existing record rather than open a second one. §12.4 gains the extension — a domain is not a safer unit to interrupt than a thread, §30.13's run-to-completion makes it less safe, and the recovery need is routed to cross-domain cancellation and to §12.14 — and the decline index points at §12.4 for the domain form. *(e)* **Ambient authority** — the owner-ratified decline-with-reasons of 2026-08-20, homed at **rationale §17.13**. On the home: the brief suggested a home near the stdlib-design or FFI discussions; §17 was chosen instead because §17 *is* the explicit-rejection register (the first of the five decline homes the index names), this is an explicit rejection, and the FFI adjacency is a cross-reference rather than a subject — the entry carries the supply-chain-era note (a linked artifact reaches every ambient entry point its imports name; the legibility that exists is module-level, the non-auto-imported `System.Interop` audit marker) and points at §16/§32.10 for the boundary, which is where the reasoning needed the FFI, not where the record belongs. Its reopening bar is deliberately narrow: not ocap in general, which is a different language, but a **capability-scoped stdlib profile** on real multi-tenant or plugin-host demand.
- **Register hygiene — four items (0106 §1.4, §5.5, §7.4, §3.3/§7.5.3).** *(f)* Proposal 0008's declined-alternatives register gains item 10, **typed modular arithmetic**, converted from adjacency to an explicit decline: it answers item 1's legibility objection *better* than item 1's own candidate did, so it is declined on **cost** — a new arithmetic type kind needs its own conversion rules against a fixed integer surface with no user-defined conversions to extend, its own `INumber<T>` question, its own literal and constant-folding behavior, and its own FFI classification — with a reopening bar keyed to whole *regions* of wrapping arithmetic. *(g)* `DECLINED.md`'s **Part 2 register is renumbered**, the one sanctioned amendment below that line: D-0004's three stacked declined-paragraphs become **D-0005** (value-form try expression), **D-0006** (comprehensions), and **D-0007** (delegation-by-forwarding sugar), with the three index rows that cited "recorded under D-0004" re-pointed to the new numbers. No word of the existing reasoning was deleted or rewritten; the split did require three additions, made because splitting one paragraph into standalone entries leaves both halves broken without them — D-0005's opening said "two paren-atom candidates" and then listed one (now: the first of two, naming D-0006), D-0005 lost its reopening bar when the shared closing sentence went to D-0006 (now restated in both), and D-0006 opened mid-sentence with no `Declined` lead of the kind every other entry carries (now supplied). `DECLINED.md`'s own "unchanged below this line" sentence is reworded to record the amendment rather than deny it; D-0004 keeps `Option<T>` alone. **D-0008** is added for **newtype deriving** (GND / Nim `distinct` borrowing), recorded explicitly rather than by adjacency and on D-0007's ground *extended*: both are implicit method promotion at the one-field case, but GND derives a conformance by representational coercion where Kotlin `by` forwards to a stored delegate, and a conformance so derived asserts interchangeability with the wrapped type — the very claim a distinct wrapper exists to deny. *(h)* The **no-poisoning** record lands at **rationale §12.8**, not spec §30.12: 0106 §7.4 asks for the sentence without naming its home, and the *why* of a deliberate absence — with lock poisoning as the declined alternative — is rationale material, while the spec states rules and this adds none. It records that a throwing guard holder releases by unwind and poisons nothing, because the interior is unaliasable behind a scoped guard and the class invariant re-evaluated at the next public entry is a detector with content where a poison flag carries only "someone threw" — with the asymmetry 0106 asks be stated: invariants are never evaluated on throw paths, and checked-contracts mode is not the release default, so in a default build that detector is off. *(i)* **Rationale §12.14** is new — the error-kernel doctrine and the process-supervision posture, beside §12.12's shape map: it states the doctrine (push fallible work outward; keep irreplaceable state in a unit that must not fail), notes that the sendable rules already push programs this way, names the recovery-unit fork, and records that **Bezel's posture is the OS process**, cross-citing §31.4's fatal band, §33.3's exit code 70, and §22.13's watchdog caveat. It deliberately does **not** decline in-process supervision; it shrinks the target.
- **Process-only — `spec-change-process.md` (0106 §4.4, §2.5; no normative-document surface).** The **warn→deny ratchet** lands as 0106 scoped it: one row in §2's change-class table (a **Ratchet** class — tightening an existing diagnostic against programs that compile today — taking the ruling-class gate plus a stated ramp) and one line in §5's Migration-note requirement (the note must give both ends of the promotion, since the Migration categories record one revision's end state while a promotion is a two-revision fact). And a new §10 records **Oberon's periodic subtraction review** as standing practice — a cadence over *shipped* surface whose only question is what to delete, output a proposal or nothing, deliberately not a §9 checklist line, since attaching it to revisions is what made every removal so far incidental to another errand. The cadence is **every twenty revisions**, owner-ruled 2026-08-20 and revision-counted rather than calendar-counted (the project's revision pace, not the calendar, accumulates the surface a pass reviews); the clock starts here, so the first pass is due at v0.283.

**Kernel classification (the v0.198 obligation): contact, no movement.** The `CancellationTokenSource` grant touches §28.13, but only as a **derivation**: the section already defines the `Shared`-payload set by a normative formula over stdlib §1's facts and already carries the growth clause that admits a new member by fact ruling, so the set grows by the mechanism it defines. No kernel rule changes, no axiom is added, extended, or retired — ten live axioms and four tombstones stand as at v0.262. **Body-locality classification (0105 §1, applied to every train):** Ruling 1 is **local** — §22.15 admits a call site "by the *declaration* of the statically named member, never by inspecting its body", and the modifier travels on the imported declaration (§2.8.2), so no body consults another body; Ruling 2 is **local** likewise — the facts are declaration-level trust grants on a compiler-known type and every derived-set verdict is computed from the types a body names; the publication rule adds no compile-time rule of any kind, being a runtime property of a receiver checked at the call (the shape §30.12's blocking-acquisition guard already has), so it mints no cross-body information and no body consults another; the five decline records, the register hygiene, and the process train add no compile-time rule at all (**local**, vacuously).

**Migration.**

- **Newly defined:** `Range<T>.Contains`, `IsOpenEnded` and `IsEmpty` are `pure` (stdlib §9.8, spec §16.3) — a stated contract binding the implementation. What newly compiles: a contract clause containing a range test, `requires(port in 0..65535)` and its kin, previously rejected because §22.15's calls-to-pure-members rule reaches neither an unmarked intrinsic nor pure-classification (which covers synthesized bodies only). Nothing that compiled before stops compiling: `pure` constrains the member's body and contract, never overload selection (§22.6), and §22.15's never-drop dispatch rule — an override or interface implementation of a pure member must restate `pure` — reaches nothing here, `Range<T>` being a sealed record (§9.2) whose `Contains` implements no interface member.
- **Newly admitted (fact-derived):** `Shared<CancellationTokenSource>` is **sendable** — a cloned handle may cross a domain boundary as a spawn argument, a channel element, or a task result (§28.13, §30.14) — and a `static readonly` / `static owned readonly` `CancellationTokenSource` is admitted **warning-free** (§22.12 rule 4's warning-suppression set). Both are widenings: no program that compiled at v0.262 is rejected by either, and one class of declaration-site warning stops firing.
- **Still rejected, deliberately:** a **mutable** static `CancellationTokenSource` (the **displacement-unbounded** fact keeps the type out of §22.12 rule 2's form (i)); the bare source crossing a domain boundary (the type gains no sendability of its own); and `CancellationToken` crossing at all (a borrow-bearing record, unchanged).
- **Spec-editorial issue candidates, named not filed** (both surfaced by this train's own tracing, neither in its scope): whether §22.15's declaration-level return rule, which reads "an **`owned` class-typed return is rejected**", is meant to read "class- or interface-typed" — the substance is unaffected either way, the pure body separately prohibiting calls returning `owned` class instances, which is the rule stdlib §9.8 now cites for `GetEnumerator`; the second candidate this train named — whether classification-by-rule reaches a storage-backed auto-property of a compiler-intrinsic record — was ruled at this landing instead of filed (Ruling 1), so it is withdrawn from this list.
- **Newly rejected (at runtime):** `Register` on a **published** `CancellationTokenSource` raises `InvalidOperationException`, and so does publishing a source that already holds live registrations (stdlib §6.1). Publication is `Shared` construction, a `static readonly`/`static owned readonly` field of the type, or being the linked child of a published parent. Two migration facts, stated plainly. *One shape that compiles today now faults:* a program holding a process-global `static readonly CancellationTokenSource` and registering callbacks on it — legal at v0.262, and harmless in a single-domain program — now raises at the `Register`. This is the ruling's recorded over-rejection, taken deliberately (a static is reachable from every domain by construction, and the narrower property is not observable without the whole program); the remedy is one line — poll `IsCancellationRequested`/`ThrowIfCancellationRequested`, or hold the source in domain-local storage. *Everything else is new ground:* no source could be shared at all before this revision, so the `Shared` and linked-child publication paths reject nothing that previously existed.
- **Newly obliged (not compiler-checked):** the source-outlives obligation binds each observing domain, discharged by that domain holding a live handle (stdlib §6.1, spec §30.8) — joining §30.14's recorded trust obligations, with no compile-time check and no checked-mode backstop, stated as such. The `Register` confinement is deliberately **not** on this list: it was on it in an earlier draft of this ruling, and the four paths above are why it is now enforced instead.
- **Doc-only:** the seven rationale records this revision lands — §11.9, §12.4's extension, §12.6's v0.263 clause, §12.8's no-poisoning paragraph, §12.14, §17.12, §17.13, and §18's units entry (eight, counting §12.6, which is an amendment of a falsified sentence rather than a decline record) — together with proposal 0008's register item 10 and `DECLINED.md`'s renumbering and index rows.
- **Process-only:** `spec-change-process.md`'s Ratchet row, the Migration-note ramp line, and §10's subtraction review. No normative-document surface, no conformance surface.
- **Unchanged:** `Range<T>`'s four storage-backed properties (pure by classification, marker rejected as redundant — the ruling states their status without changing their declarations), its remaining members, and every rule of §16; §22.15's rules themselves (this revision applies them, it does not amend them); §28.13's and §22.12's formulas, which are untouched — what moves is the informative membership parentheticals, §22.12 rule 4's prose naming the members outside form (i) ("three" → "four"), and Appendix C.11's restating row; §28.14's quiescence and bounding forms, cited but not amended; rationale §12.4's original text, which gains a paragraph and loses no word.
- **Guides:** untouched — no idiom is retired, so no guide teaches anything stale; all six keep their pins (01 v0.259, 02 v0.259, 03 v0.250, 04 v0.261, 05 v0.261, 06 v0.260). One follow-up is named rather than taken: 0106 §3.3 reads Guide 04 §6's actor idiom as recommending the domain owning entangled state as the home for serialized work, which §12.14's doctrine now cuts against; the guide edit is outside this train's brief and is left for a guide pass, which is unversioned under §5's guide-only rule.
