### v0.278 changelog (v0.277 → v0.278)

**Proposal [0117](proposals/0117-import-asymmetry.md) graduates: a type's standard surface now follows the type.** §2.3 makes 26 standard-library type names visible in every file with no `import`, and §2.8.3 rule 2 lets a program *call* the public members of a value whose module it never imported. Against both, §26.5 rule 2 scoped extension-member candidacy to *"the current module and all imported modules"* — so a program could hold an `IEnumerable<T>` and call its instance members with no import at all, while `xs.Where(p)` required `import System.Collections.Linq;`, a module naming **neither the receiver's type nor the receiver's module** (`import System.Collections.Generic;` did not help). §2.3 now auto-imports that module and states the invariant that generates the entry: **where the standard library declares an extension over an always-available type, its module is auto-imported.**

**Three facts about the rule's standing decided this, not a design argument — and each reverses an assumption it is natural to start from.**

- **It was never argued.** The standard library's *"(v0.195)"* citation dated the **sentence**, not the rule: that changelog entry is a stdlib contract sweep containing nothing about extensions or imports. The nearest recorded reason is §2.8.3's decline of *everything-without-import*, argued about **bare names** — and extension members are not bare names; they are reached through a receiver whose type the reader already holds. The drafting began intending to *defend* the gate on the argument C# and Rust make for it, and there was no decision here to defend. Importing another language's reasoning to fill that gap is precisely the failure this project's process exists to prevent.
- **The compiler never enforced it for the standard library.** §5's operators are compiler builtins matched by name; the import set is not consulted for them. **Forty-three test files call `.Where(` with no import and pass the real compile-link-run path** — 35 `.cpp` and 8 `.bzl`, measured at this revision's HEAD and at 0117's pinned `c7574a8e`; recipe: `for f in $(grep -rl '\.Where(' tests/); do grep -q 'import System.Collections.Linq' "$f" || echo "$f"; done | wc -l`. *(A first draft said thirty-four, a number no recorded recipe reproduces.)* The gate *is* implemented, correctly and per-module, for user-declared cross-module extensions — just not at the only place the defect existed.
- **The specification's own examples did not follow it.** **Six** fenced examples call §5 operators with no import — §14.5, §21.10, §27.4 (×2) and §27.6 (×2); Guide 01 uses `xs.Where(p)` normatively and never mentions the import, as does Guide 05, which additionally states the retired requirement twice; and `tests/conformance/cases/spec_0172.bzl` records the un-imported form as **compiling**. *(A first draft of this entry said "eight … two of them inside §26". The gate falsified both halves: the count is six, and §26's two fences do not call a §5 operator at all — they declare their own `First`, which makes them a **cost** of this revision rather than evidence for it. See the gate round.)*

**So the question was never whether to relax a rule — it was which of two things the project already does should be written down.** That reframing is what disqualified the option that looks conservative. Keeping the rule and correcting the documents would have meant **enforcing** an unargued restriction: 34 failing test files, nine document sites to edit, a conformance case to reclassify, and new compiler work, for a benefit no record states. Ratifying practice instead makes those nine sites correct **without editing them**.

**What it costs, in full.** Two names enter the bare-name space — `IGrouping<TKey, T>` and `IOrderedEnumerable<T>`, §5's only public named declarations, everything else in the module being a nameless `extension` block. Zero new bare-name ambiguities in the standard library, and zero new §26.5 rule-4 ambiguities: the only other stdlib extension blocks are over the span families, with disjoint heads. Instance shadowing is untouched — §26.5 rule 1 decides instance-vs-extension by **name**, before imports matter, so the six names the standard library records as blocked (`Count`, `Contains`, `First`, `Last`, `Reverse`, `ToArray`) stay exactly as blocked.

**The gate is kept where it earns its keep, and that is the substance of the invariant.** An extension injects member names onto a type its author did not write; §26.5 rule 4's ambiguity remedy — *remove or narrow a conflicting import* — is the language's only tool for choosing between two such blocks. That hazard is real for third-party modules and absent for the standard library, which is singular, compiler-known, and cannot collide with itself. **User extensions stay import-gated, unchanged.** Every comparable language draws the line in the same place after shipping the opposite first: C# made `using System.Linq` implicit in the default template a decade on; Rust puts `Iterator` in the prelude while requiring `use` for other traits; Kotlin auto-imports its collections.

**The cost that is accepted rather than answered.** §2.3 has **no opt-out**, and Bezel's extension blocks are **nameless** (§26.1) — so unlike C#, where a colliding extension is still callable through its static class, a user block declaring a member named `Where` over `IEnumerable<T>` has no qualified spelling and no import to remove. Renaming is the only remedy. Three bounds, two of which survived the gate. The escape did not work before either, since the gate was unenforced; and the failure is §26.5 rule 4's ambiguity diagnostic naming every origin, not a silent wrong answer. **The third — that the affected population is zero — was false, and the gate found the instance in the specification's own chapter.** §26.5.1's second worked example declares two blocks over `IEnumerable<T>` both spelling `First()`, which §5 also declares and `Array<T>` does not (it declares four of the six blocked names, not `First`), so the auto-import made §5 a **third** equally-specific candidate in the example that exists to teach two-way ambiguity. The example's member is renamed to `Pick`, and §26.5.1 now states the general consequence rule 4's remedy list did not reach: **against an auto-imported standard-library candidate, *narrow an import* is not available**, which leaves renaming. That is the accepted cost, no longer hypothetical — a user block over `IEnumerable<T>` must avoid §5's member names. Two general fixes are recorded and deliberately **not** taken — a **provenance** tiebreak ranking a user block above a compiler-known one (provenance, *not* the auto-ranked specificity rationale §17.10 deleted), or an import-suppression form on §2.3 — because neither is designable without knowing which of them a real collision wants. `DECLINED.md` carries both, the second with a bar of **one real collision**.

**Gate round (adversarial composition gate, same revision).** One pass; verdict **BLOCK** — nine blocking findings and ten non-blocking, all applied. `check_docs.sh` saw none of them. The decision survived; **the sweep and the evidence did not**, and that split is the round's lesson.

- **The auto-import added a third candidate to §26.5.1's own ambiguity example.** Its two blocks both spell `First()`; §5 declares `First()` over `IEnumerable<T>`; `Array<T>` declares four of the six blocked names and **not** `First` — so rule 1 does not commit, extension search runs, and the example that exists to teach a *two*-way tie acquired a third arm, in the corpus case `spec_0175.bzl` too. This falsified *"zero new §26.5 rule-4 ambiguities"* and *"the affected population is zero"*, which were the bounds on the accepted D3 cost. Repaired in both halves: the example's member is renamed to `Pick` (the name the sema test suite already uses for it), and rule 4's remedy list now states that *narrow an import* cannot reach an auto-imported block.
- **Four prose sites still asserted the retired requirement** — Guide 05 twice (the *collections* guide, whose pin the entry claimed did not need to move), the code-generation reference twice more than the two the entry counted, and the standard library's own §9.6 saying *"(§5, import required)"* two thousand lines from the §5 header that now says the opposite.
- **The two measured numbers this revision rests on were both wrong.** *"Eight fenced examples, two of them inside §26"* is **six**, none in §26 — and the §26 pair are not examples of the violation at all but the collision above, so the rhetorically strongest half of the evidence was exactly backwards. *"Thirty-four test files"* is **43**, under a recipe that had never been recorded. Both appeared in four landed artifacts including a `DECLINED.md` reopening bar, which is a record future readers re-derive from.
- **§2.8.3 rule 2's new sentence keyed the gate to the wrong module** — to *"a value whose module is unimported"* rather than to the extension block's own declaring module. It was added deliberately *"because nothing else announces it"*, so it was the one place a reader would learn the rule, and it stated the rule backwards, implying the false converse that importing the receiver's module would help.
- **The changelog shipped an unfilled `GATE_ROUND_PLACEHOLDER`** — this paragraph, and the second revision running. v0.277 recorded the same defect one entry above.

Non-blocking, all applied: the standard library conditioned `OwningArray<T>.ToArray()`'s resolution on the import; §5's heading lacked the *(auto-imported)* marker its two siblings carry, so the stdlib and the code-generation reference disagreed in presentation; the code-generation reference's transcription pin still read v0.268 directly above the table this revision rewrote; *"roughly fifty member names"* is 42 names and ≈60 overloads; and *"26 standard-library type names"* drops the qualifier — it is 26 **non-auto-imported** names, since §2.3 also makes the whole of `System` and `System.Text` visible.

**One item recorded rather than fixed.** The gate reads `ExprTC::lookupExtensionMember` as never admitting §5's builtins to the candidate vector, so the compiler would report *two* candidates where the specification now implies three. That is a spec-ahead-of-implementation delta on the very rule this revision writes, filed as [#3343](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3343) rather than asserted — no build was available to settle it.

**Migration.**

- **Newly accepted: two bare names in every file** — though only one of them is implemented. `IGrouping` is a real builtin; `IOrderedEnumerable` exists in `src/` only in comments and `tests/conformance/manifest.tsv` skips its case as `skip:stdlib-unresolved`, so that name is document-only and this revision widens the scope of a pre-existing gap rather than creating one. Also newly reachable: **42 distinct member names** (≈60 overloads) on `IEnumerable<T>` receivers, **at the document level only** — the compiler already admitted them. §2.8.6 class: **widening**.
- **Newly rejected: nothing.**
- **Behaviour change in the compiler: none.** That is this revision's unusual property and its strongest practical argument: it changes what the documents claim, to match what the implementation has always done.
- **Newly defined:** §2.3's auto-imported-extension-module invariant; §2.8.3 rule 2's statement of its own exception, which nothing previously announced.
- **Unchanged:** every ownership rule and every kernel rule; the axiom register stands at eleven axioms and four tombstones. **Kernel classification: no contact.** **Body-locality classification: not applicable** — the change is to a visibility list and states no compile-time rule over bodies.
- **Deltas filed, not asserted.** [#3341](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3341) records that the import gate was not applied to the standard library — under this revision that becomes correct by construction, and the issue closes as a documentation matter rather than an implementation one. [#3342](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3342) is unrelated to this decision and deliberately does not ride it: `arr.Count(pred)` resolves to the §5 operator on an `Array<T>` receiver, which §26.5 rule 1 and the standard library's own worked example say the instance `Count` blocks. **No build was available in this run**, so every compiler claim is a read of the source plus the passing test corpus, and is marked as such.
- **Guides:** Guide 01's normative `xs.Where(p)` becomes correct without editing, and keeps its pin. **Guide 05 did not** — it stated the retired requirement twice, in its opening paragraph and in its §5 section, so it is edited and re-pinned to v0.278. The first draft of this entry asserted all six were untouched, having inspected one. **`Bezel_For_Code_Generation.md`:** edited and re-pinned — its module table and §5.5's heading both stated the import requirement.
- **Conformance corpus:** **zero rows deleted, zero reclassified.** `spec_0172.bzl`, which records the un-imported form as compiling, becomes correct rather than anomalous. Eight spec fences and one guide example become conforming with no edit.

### v0.279 changelog (v0.278 → v0.279)

**Clarification-class revision: two withdrawn-draft residues retracted, no rule changes.** Both defects were found by the 2026-08-25 elegance-and-simplicity review and verified against the recorded decisions before filing ([#3366](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3366), [#3367](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3367)).

**§22.8/§23.1/Appendix C no longer contradict each other on `readonly` auto-properties (#3366).** v0.271's first draft extended the single-assignment rule to auto-properties; the composition gate withdrew the extension (the narrowing is that entry's own headline, with test evidence), but **three** sites of the draft survived: §22.8's checkable-form paragraph still said the rule "travels unchanged to a `readonly` auto-property", §23.1 asserted the extension and the non-extension in one sentence, and Appendix C.5's invariant row said "`readonly` field **or auto-property**" — the third found not by the review but by this revision's own confirmation gate, and the worst of the three, since the invariant list is what implementers read for the checkable form. All three are retracted; the operative rule — single-assignment governs `readonly` **fields**, the auto-property case undecided with the extension declined (`DECLINED.md`, *Extending §22.8's single-assignment rule to `readonly` auto-properties*) — is unchanged. §22.8's scope statement also drops its inline implementation narration; the reasons live in the decline record.

- **The pinned v0.271 entry carries the same residue, recorded here rather than edited there:** its Migration note's "Newly rejected: one shape … a `readonly` auto-property written both by its initializer and by a constructor body" block is first-draft residue, contradicted by the same entry's body ("nothing newly rejected"; "the auto-property delta … does not exist, the rule having been narrowed to fields"). The body blocks are authoritative; nothing was newly rejected at v0.271 beyond what its body states.

**The standard library's member-access import claims are corrected (#3367).** §2.4 (`Environment.Variables()`) and §2.10 (`Type`'s enum-metadata views) said that calling members of a returned value requires importing the value's type's module — the claim §2.8.3 rule 2 refutes. (This is a *different* claim from the extension-member import gate the v0.278 sweep corrected; rule 2's one stated exception. The first draft of this entry conflated the two.) Both now state the naming/use distinction: member access needs no import; spelling the type's name in source does. The confirmation gate found one further residue of the v0.278 sweep itself: §3.0's `Split` tokenizer example still read "(§5, import required)" — a site the v0.278 gate-round text claimed corrected, though its commit did not touch this document; it now reads "(§5, auto-imported)". These were the last such sites in the normative documents; proposal 0014 (an under-review draft pinned to v0.177) carries the member-access phrasing and is re-verified at graduation per the proposal-pin rule, not edited here.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected: nothing. Newly accepted: nothing.** All fixes conform the text to decisions already landed (v0.271's narrowing; v0.278's rule-2 statement and auto-import). Appendix C.5's row, as it stood, would have rejected initializer-plus-constructor-body on a `readonly` auto-property — the shape `tests/module/xmod_record_body_ctor_field_store_3207_test.cpp` pins twice as compiling; scoping the row to fields *removes* a phantom rejection the rest of the spec never made.
- **Gate round (clarification-class confirmation, one reviewer).** Verdict on the first draft: **FAIL** — two blocking findings, both applied: the Appendix C.5 residue above (the draft claimed the contradiction closed with two sites fixed; a third decided the open question), and the "v0.278 gate corrected three sibling sites" evidence claim, which conflated the extension-gate sweep with this revision's member-access claim. Non-blocking, applied: the §3.0 residue; the decline-record citation is by row subject, not row number.
- **Doc-only:** all seven edits. No compiler contact; no conformance-corpus contact; no guide contact (swept — neither defect's phrasing appears in the guides or the code-generation reference).
- **Kernel classification: no contact.** **Body-locality classification: not applicable** — no compile-time rule is added or altered.

### v0.280 changelog (v0.279 → v0.280)

**Statement-hygiene revision (clarification class): the rules are unchanged; how they are stated is not.** The 2026-08-25 elegance review's verdict on the spec outside §28 was that its dominant defect is prose inflation and multi-site restatement, not special-casing. This revision is the editorial batch that verdict licensed: three drafting trains (consolidations, decompositions, reader orientation), each edit traced against its section's own examples with identical accept/reject verdicts required, composed and adversarially gated as one edit set. Net effect on the spec: **−372 words** (`wc -w`, v0.279 → this text; the drafting lanes' own tokenizer measured −820 before the gate's restorations) with zero semantic change. §28 is untouched — its rewrite is proposal 0118's graduation, not this revision.

**Consolidations (one definition site per rule).** §2.7's name-resolution **table** is now the normative statement; the ~400-word prose twin shrinks to its non-tabular residue (tie-breaks and temporal clauses, qualification remedies, the chain-head-preemption note, the `Buffer<int>` example, the §11.6/§19.8 non-reordering scope). `throw` is defined once (§17.12); §21.8 and §31.5 keep their headings and anchors as statement-spelling and pointer stubs. *Closed-value-space* is defined in §19.6 with each proof family's closure ground stated there — the enum family's producer argument (checked casts, §9.8 deserialization, §17.11's zero-constant) moved in from §21.7, which now cites the definition instead of re-enumerating it. The two-package skip model (participation vs. eligibility; equality vs. serialization) is one 2×2 table in §9.2 with three citing sites; §35.7 keeps its choice-only value-like gate. `Range<T>`'s declared-surface rendering is §9.2's rule, read out by §8.5 citing the v0.255 ruling (#3131, rationale §9.3). §7.11's ordering-rejects-absence argument lives in §7.11; the §4.6/§6.6/§16.6/§17.5 satellites state their operation shapes and defer the reasoning, keeping their non-derivable facts (§16.6's pattern-kind keying; §17.5's nullable-`Contains` admission). §13.3's four visibility-keyword exceptions are one principle (member kinds user code can never invoke or name carry no visibility keyword), cited from Appendix C.2. §26.5's rule-4 remedy list is stated once. §17.4 covers `is`/`is not`/`as` ownership in one place; §12.7's ownership paragraph points at it.

**Decompositions (same words' worth of rule, readable).** §17.13's per-type discard bullets collapse to one rule — an owned result is an unbound owned temporary, disposed at end of statement — plus the `Task` exception; the ceremony exemption, the freed-not-disposed wording for trivial-dispose classes, the `Task.FireAndForget` diagnostic-naming requirement, and the move-only slot-disposal order are preserved verbatim. §29.11's provenance warning, §22.6's ownership-applicability paragraph, §12.7's boxed-location-write paragraph, §22.16's `old(E)` paragraph, and §20's fused paragraph are decomposed under run-in heads (§29.11's silent-roots prose becomes a table), with no anchor added, moved, or removed. §30.5's two "(recommended-message text, normative)" labels are resolved: the diagnostics' **content requirements** are normative, the quoted texts are recommended wordings — an interpretive resolution of the v0.249 label, disclosed here.

**Reader orientation (additions that state no rule).** §22.6 opens with an eight-step road-map of the overload-resolution pipeline, each line naming and citing its owning section, the stage order proven from the spec's own relative-order sentences. §2.3's always-available names are one table (family, members, shadowability), the §3.4 non-shadowable exception now a visible column; the `System.Interop` ruling (v0.265) and the v0.278 auto-imported-extension-module invariant are retained verbatim. Appendix A gains an index table of the eight shared-production over-admissions with their rejecting sections. §23.5 names the accessor principle — **accessor read faces are lend-only; transfer-out is a method** (axiom A4's wording) — and §29.1's `TakeCurrent()` cites it. §15.5 states the `Length`/`Count` rule as a rule (fixed extent ⇒ `Length`; resizable ⇒ `Count`). §18.5's alignment wording matches the grammar ("an integer, optionally negated").

**History extraction (process §7 enforcement).** Ten superseded-state narrations removed from §22.3/§22.5/§22.6/§22.16/§29.11/§30.5; each is carried by the v0.249, v0.250, v0.253, v0.259, v0.260, v0.265, or v0.268 entry, except one restated here as its history's home: **v0.268's predicate widening made a same-unit adopt-then-yield iterator warn where its cross-module twin stays silent — a widening of v0.243's same-unit/cross-module gap**; the spec now states only the current asymmetry.

**Gate round (adversarial composition gate, one pass).** Verdict **BLOCK** — three blocking findings, all applied: the Appendix A over-admit table had *replaced* the preamble's whitespace-and-comments sentence rather than sitting beside it (restored); the first draft of §23.5's named principle ("accessors never transfer ownership") was false as stated — `set(owned)` and `move coll[i]` are accessor-face transfers — and is re-worded to axiom A4's directional form; and the code-generation reference's claim that `CancellationTokenSource` is auto-imported contradicted §2.3 at the exact surface this revision restates (two CG sites corrected, pin moved). Non-blocking, applied: §17.13's lead now keys on ownership classification rather than "the static type"; §21.7's enum-producer enumeration moved into §19.6 rather than deleted. ### v0.281 changelog (v0.280 → v0.281)

**Proposal [0118](proposals/0118-kernel-absorption-completion.md) graduates: the kernel absorption is complete — one definition site per ownership rule.** v0.198's kernel (K1–K9) committed §28 to the factoring "kernel principle, derivation, or recorded axiom"; v0.199's tag pass classified every block but left 56 DERIVED blocks carrying their full prose. This revision finishes the migration the kernel began, honoring 0046 §13's decline of the unaudited one-shot rewrite as constraints: three drafting lanes over disjoint regions, per-lane deleted-sentence → covering-statement audit tables, an independent kernel-diff verification, and the composition gate — the whole record committed as [`0118-audit-v0.281.md`](proposals/0118-audit-v0.281.md). The verification's verdict: **nothing missing** — 112 independently-sampled rule sentences and all 72 cells of the new consume table verified covered; five divergences found and closed before landing (below). **Intended semantic delta zero, held** — apart from three corrected-in-passing items this entry records explicitly.

**The structural changes.**

- **The consume table** (§28.3, new anchor `sec-consume-table`): K3's twelve-position list, K4's kill table, and K5's placement list were three projections of one relation; they are now one table — position × marker spelling × subject (binding vs slot) × post-state × frozen? × disposal moment × kernel tag. K4 keeps its posture clauses, K5 its two-conjunct criterion, two recorded failure shapes, and one override. The freeze criterion, stated at five sites inside §28.3, is stated once. The producers table's call rows collapse to one row pointing at the announcement table; `move coll[i]`'s admitted-type enumeration lives once, in §28.11.
- **Absorption.** §28.6/§28.7/§28.8's tagged restatements are corollary citations plus their genuinely-new content and every example; §28.11's per-family prose collapses onto its two tables (each deleted member signature verified present in stdlib §4); §28.13/§28.14 keep the machine-checked rosters the SETS/FACTS checks anchor on and shed the grounds narration around them; the §28 intro is a short orientation paragraph. §28.1's ~500-word single-sentence type requirement, K1's ~450-word statement, the calls-mint flow, and the move-semantics paragraph are restructured into numbered clauses, operative wording preserved.
- **A glossary and a router** (§28.3 head / §28 head): the role/classification split, drop vs removes, and the four announcement terms defined once; the router names the API-consumer subset (the Guide 01 set) and the API-author surface, states no rule.

**Terminology (the old→new table).** *target-announced* → **marker-free position**; *borrow-consuming position* → **borrowing position**; *owner* as the obligation-holding role → **holder** (*owned* remains the classification); *drop* is reserved for disposal-carrying discard — §28.11's non-owned operation-table cells now say **removes**. Sweep counts: spec 15 sites + 5 hyphenless variants outside §28, rationale 9, code-generation reference 4, Guide 01 3, stdlib 1. Kept as history: two "(formerly *target-announced*)" notes plus the glossary's own, and one "(then *target-announced*)" in the rationale. Out-of-scope survivors, named so they are not later mistaken for misses: §31.4's "dropped from the in-flight slot" (task abandonment, not element removal), stdlib §4's two `Clear()` comments and Guide 05's "drops the reference; disposes nothing" (each states "disposes nothing" inline — the glossary's reservation is scoped to §28 and its satellites). Grep-trail note: `src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp` already used "marker-free" in an unrelated sense ("marker-free constructs") before this revision. The compiler's own stale spellings — one user-visible diagnostic ("the announced consume", `PureChecker.cpp:852`) and nine comment sites — are filed as [#3371](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3371), not edited here.

1. §28.6 said owning collections "have no value-copy materializers at all … not part of the surface on a borrow or otherwise" — false since **v0.266** ([#3286](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3286)): they *declare* none, and stdlib §4.5 states the reachable-by-extension forms and their lifetime obligation. The text now uses the declared-surface framing. Acceptance unchanged (resolution is §26.5's business).

### v0.282 changelog (v0.281 → v0.282)

**Proposal [0119](proposals/0119-stdlib-symmetry-batch.md) graduates: the stdlib symmetry batch.** Three verified residues of the 2026-08-25 stdlib elegance review — each checked against `DECLINED.md`, the rationale, the changelog, and every prior proposal before it was proposed, so nothing here re-decides a recorded question.

**1. `TryAdd` for the dictionaries; `SortedDictionary` regains the duplicate-is-a-bug tier.** The three sets carried §1's shape-(d) `TryAdd`; no dictionary did, and the absence was recorded nowhere — the one entry in the code-generation reference's not-exists list with no principled ground. New members: `Dictionary<K, V>.TryAdd(key, value): bool` and `SortedDictionary<K, V>.TryAdd(key, value): bool` (`false`, no mutation, on a present key); `OwningDictionary<K, V>.TryAdd(key, owned value): bool` with the `OwningSet<T>.TryAdd` contract verbatim — on `false` the passed value is disposed, since the caller relinquished it at the call site. `SortedDictionary` also gains throwing `Add(key, value)`: it had been indexer-write-only, so the *duplicate-is-a-bug* stance existed on the sorted set and not the sorted map; the sorted map now carries §4.8's three insert stances (throwing `Add`, `TryAdd`, indexer upsert); `SortedSet`'s own stances — silent-discard `Add`, `TryAdd` — are unchanged, and the first draft's claim that the map now matches the *set* was a gate finding, corrected here and in §4.17's comment. The argument is the sets' precedent and `OwningDictionary.Add`'s dispose-on-duplicate cost (the pre-check remedy is two hash lookups); the sets' *other* recorded ground — §11.2 return-type conformance on an inherited interface `Add` — does **not** transfer (`Dictionary.Add` is not an override) and is deliberately not cited. `Keys`/`Values` on `SortedDictionary` stay absent, now with the reason recorded in §4.17 and a `DECLINED.md` row (reopening bar: a use the entry iteration cannot serve).

**2. The window-parameter convention, recorded and enforced.** Three spellings of "a sub-range" coexisted — `(start, length)` on spans/`Substring`/`StringBuilder.Remove`, `(offset, count)`/`(index, count)` on `Stream`/`Encoding`, and `String.From(buffer, start, count)` mixing the families inside one signature, with `Substring(startIndex, length)` beside `Remove(startIndex, count)` in the same type. §1 now records the rule: windows are **`(start, length)`** (`startIndex` standing as the string family's spelling of the start), with the **`Stream` byte-window family** the one recorded exception (`(offset, count)` kept for C-family muscle memory). Renamed to the convention — rename-only, no arity or semantics change: `String.From(buffer, start, length)`, `String.Remove(startIndex, length)`, `Encoding.GetString(bytes, start, length)`. Parameter names are API surface (named arguments, spec §22.5): the renames are free before external users exist, which is the whole argument for doing them now. `RawBytes.CopyTo(destination, destOffset)` is untouched — a write position, not a window.

**3. The comparer-injection ruling (doc-only).** The hash containers take `constructor(comparer: IEqualityComparer<K>)`; the sorted containers refuse ordering comparers on the recorded single-order ground — and neither text cited the other, with the sorted family's principle, read alone, indicting the hash family's constructors. Rationale §17.14 now records the reconciliation: an `IEqualityComparer<K>` carries **both** facets a hash container consults as one object, so injection relocates identity *whole* — no observable facet can disagree with another; an ordering comparer would *split* identity between the instance's order and the type's equality, directly observable in `Contains`/`TryAdd` since sorted identity **is** `CompareTo`-equality. The single-order rule's real content is *identity must not fork*; the constructors satisfy it. Both postures stand; stdlib §4.8/§4.17 cite the record; `DECLINED.md`'s sorted-comparer row points at it. No API change.

**Gate round (adversarial critique, one pass).** Verdict on the first draft: **REFUTED** — seven blocking findings, all applied. The sharpest three: the comparer record landed as a *second* rationale §17.12, its anchor hijacking the contract-carrying-type-aliases section's (moved to §17.14, all citations renumbered — the collision would have silently re-pointed two existing `DECLINED.md` rows); §4.17's new comment claimed the restored tier matches *SortedSet*, whose `Add` in fact discards silently — the true referent is `Dictionary` §4.8, a defect originating in proposal 0119 §1 itself and noted at its status flip; and the entry's own Migration note said "six new members" while enumerating four. Also applied: the code-generation reference's §5.11 not-exists line still denying `TryAdd`, its `SortedDictionary` listing omitting the new members it announced in prose 26 lines below, stdlib §1's shape-(d) enumeration under-listing its own sites, and the three conformance transcriptions. Non-blocking, applied: §17.14's "no observable facet can disagree" claim qualified (K's own `Equals` stays observable via `DictionaryEntry` record equality — the claim is about the container's lookups); the named-argument-users claim corrected to what the gate's check actually found (zero).

**Migration.**

- **Newly accepted (document level):** the four new members (three `TryAdd`s and `SortedDictionary.Add`); three renamed parameter spellings at named-argument call sites (`length:` where `count:`/`index:` were). **Newly rejected:** named-argument call sites spelling the old parameter names (`count:` on `String.From`/`String.Remove`/`Encoding.GetString`) — positional call sites are unaffected, and **no named-argument call site of the renamed members is known**: the four grep candidates in the tracking issue are signature *transcriptions* (conformance-case declarations), not calls.
- **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** the compiler declares none of the four members and knows the old parameter names; filed as the catch-up issues at this landing (see the tracking issue). No language-spec rule changes; **kernel classification: no contact** (the owning `TryAdd`'s dispose-on-false is the recorded §4.10 contract applied to an existing member shape). **Body-locality: not applicable.**
- **Doc-only:** stdlib (§1 convention, six members, two prose records), rationale (§17.14), code-generation reference (nine updates — the §4.8/§4.9/§4.17 listings, the shape-(d) table, the §5.11 not-exists line, the sorted-collections line, and the §5 transcription pin; header pin → v0.282), `DECLINED.md` (one row updated, one added). Guides: no contact (no idiom taught changes; swept — no guide spells the renamed parameters as named arguments, and the guides' `TryAdd` mentions are the sets'). ### v0.283 changelog (v0.282 → v0.283)

**Proposal [0120](proposals/0120-unit-type-record.md) graduates: the unit type's existence is recorded, and the no-value boundary becomes a rule.** The 2026-08-26 investigation (occurrence census, design-space study, keyword-syntax parse study) found that nothing anywhere motivated `()`'s existence — no rationale entry, no decline row — while the census showed it load-bearing at exactly three places (function-type returns: 57 occurrences across spec, stdlib, and the code-generation reference and 273 in tests — 43 and 241 matching *lines* respectively, both counting units stated here because the first draft mixed them; the `EventSource<()>` no-payload idiom, proposal 0035; the `catch Exception => ()` suppression arm) and invisible everywhere else (§22.1's procedure form spells no return clause; zero unit locals, fields, patterns, or payloads exist in idiomatic use). Rationale §3.15 now records: why unit exists (one function-type grammar — `Retry<T>(op: () -> T)` takes a no-result operation with no twin member, the split C#'s `Action`/`Func` cannot escape; the thin-wrapper instantiation; the typed statement calculus), and the **no-value boundary rule** — a no-value variant earns a dedicated type when its rules differ by arity (`Task` beside `Task<T>`: Pattern A/B, result lifetime), and is an instantiation at `()` when none do (`EventSource<()>`). The language's Task-vs-Event hybrid is thereby principled, not accidental.

**The keyword-led function-type direction is deferred with its design worked, not declined.** The owner's direction — a keyword-led function type on the `lambda` precedent, the result clause elidable as method declarations elide it, the type arrow possibly retired — was studied to a settled parse verdict: `lambda(T)` / `lambda(K): V` is LL-resolvable in the current parser's own terms (`Parser::parseType()`, one-token lookahead, greedy `:` consumption; two `as`/`is`-embedded corners close by precedented mandatory parenthesization). The deferral is cost-shaped: the respelling pessimizes the ~85% result-bearing majority of function types to save the ~15% unit minority, deletes no parse ambiguity (proposal 0064's strongest ground does not transfer to types), and migrates the whole function-type surface (~263 occurrences across spec, stdlib, code-generation reference, and guides + ~1,792 in tests, plus ~8 in the unpinned rationale). Proposal 0120 §5 carries the full design as the reopening's starting point; the `DECLINED.md` row states the three reopening conditions, the third of which is an owner call that the pre-1.0 window warrants the uniformity on its own — the register holds the aesthetics decision open rather than foreclosing it.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected: nothing. Newly accepted: nothing. No spec or stdlib text changes** — the revision adds one rationale section and three `DECLINED.md` rows (the `void` removal, rejected with the member-bifurcation reason and an evidence bar; the boundary moves in either direction, rejected with the rule as the record; the keyword respelling, deferred with conditions).
- **Kernel classification: no contact. Body-locality: not applicable. Conformance corpus: no contact. Guides: no contact. Code-generation reference: no contact, pin unmoved** (v0.282, 1 behind — no surface it transcribes changed).
- **Gate round (adversarial critique, one pass).** Verdict on the first draft: **REFUTED IN PART** — four blocking findings, all applied; the decisions survived, one stated principle did not. The substantive one: the boundary rule's first draft grounded the `Task`/`Task<T>` split in arity-sensitive rules, misreading §30.5 — Pattern A/B keys on the result's *kind*, and a `Task<()>` would differ from `Task` by nothing — so the recorded rule is now **frequency-shaped** (dedicated type where the no-value case is pervasive; instantiation where it is the minority; satellites follow their family head), and the boundary row's reopening bar was rewritten, the first draft's bar having been met by current spec text on day one. Mechanical: the `deferred` row sat in the `rejected` group and two rows were mis-alphabetized; the new rationale section had been inserted under §4's anchor (the same anchor-hijack class the v0.282 gate caught — twice is a pattern worth a mechanical check); and the census figures conflated two counting units and two document scopes, restated above with both stated. Non-blocking, applied: `Task<()>` appears in *two* parser tests (the proposal's census corrected); the §5 follow-set gains `)`/`?`; the migration figure names the rationale's own sites.
- **Standing note:** v0.283 is the due point of the first process-§10 subtraction review (clock started v0.263; `DangerousPointer` is routed to it). Per §10 it is its own pass with its own output, deliberately not attached to any revision — it has not run yet and is now due.

### v0.285 changelog (v0.284 → v0.285)

**Ruling: §35.2's boxable-classifications clause scopes replacement, not declarability ([#3335](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3335) — reading (1)).** v0.276's composition gate had surfaced a three-way tension: §35.7 offers every non-auto-hashable choice the §25.2 operator rescue, §25.2 obliges `Equals(T)`/`GetHashCode` to take it, and §35.2's carry-over sentence — "for the boxable classifications" — could be read as denying those members to **owning** choices (borrow-bearing choices are boxable, §35.8, so even the strict reading denied them nothing), making an owning choice that overloads `=` unrescuable. The ruling adopts the reading the issue itself identified as the likely intent: the clause is about **taking over `Object`'s virtuals**, which only a boxable value can be dispatched through; it says nothing about *declaring* the plain members, which dispatch statically on a choice anyway. One sentence lands in §35.2 stating it: the members are declarable on every classification, replace nothing where no box exists, and §25.2's obligation is dischargeable everywhere. The alternatives' costs were as the issue recorded — reading (2) would have needed three scope edits and a compiler guard for an unrescuable form with no diagnostic; the population was zero at v0.276; since then, #3333's own test fixtures declare choice equality operators — including an **owning** choice with the full four-member surface that sema already accepts — which is live evidence *for* this reading, not against it. **Gate round (adversarial critique, one pass): SOUND-WITH-CORRECTIONS**, all applied — the entry's first draft said the strict reading denied members to borrow-bearing choices too (false; they box); its population claim was two revisions stale; and, decisively, the ruling sentence's final clause had blessed the operator rescue on move-only choices without noticing that §25.2's never-consume operand rule and §15.3's by-value-move parameter rule give those comparison positions no consistent binding — the clause now claims *declarability* only, and the binding question is filed as its own spec defect ([#3560](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3560)) rather than settled as a side effect. Corrected in passing on the gate's flag: the code-generation reference's operator line still said "records and enums may overload" `=`, omitting choices — stale since v0.276 — now "records, enums, and choices"; CG pin → v0.285.

**Migration.** Newly rejected: nothing. ### v0.286 changelog (v0.285 → v0.286)

**Ruling: the comparison positions of a move-only type bind borrows ([#3560](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3560)).** v0.285's declarability ruling surfaced a collision its own gate caught: §25.2 promises operator operands "never consume a named owned binding," while §15.3's parameter rule passes a move-only value by value-move — so an owning choice's obliged `Equals(other: C)` read under §15.3 would destroy its right operand, and `a = b` had no consistent passing at all. The ruling extends the borrow reading: **operator operand positions and the comparison surface's `Equals(T)` parameter bind borrows of move-only values**, with §19.3's discipline through the borrow (reads and non-destructive matches admitted, consuming operations rejected) and both operands live after. The definition site is §25.2 (the operand bullet + one sentence on the co-declaration clause, keyed on member shape rather than co-declaration since v0.285 made a lone `Equals(T)` declarable); §15.3's parameter bullet and §35.2's v0.285 sentence are cites.

**Why the borrow reading, and not a carve-free §15.3:** the research pass counted **eight** existing borrow-of-move-only position families — the value receiver (§9.4/§35.2), the match scrutinee (§19.3), payload bindings (§35.5, v0.251), closure capture, indexing, iteration variables, owning-match guard trials, and — decisively — **the intrinsic move-only equality itself**, which §15.3 already specifies as "borrowing comparison (reads each slot without moving)." The ruling makes user-declared comparison do what the language's own comparison does; the alternative (value-move operands) would make `a = b` consume both sides, violating §25.2's stated guarantee and every reader's expectation of equality. Scope is exact: user-declared operators and `Equals(T)` on **owning choices** — move-only records do not exist (§15.3) and owning inline arrays have no operator surface (§9.4/§25.2), so no other kind reaches these positions. The accepted limit is stated in place: a non-comparison operator (`+` on a choice, say) cannot transfer an operand's payload into its result.

**Adjacency kept, not amended:** §22.15's rejection of move-only `pure`-member parameters (v0.234) rests partly on the by-value-move ground this ruling carves at comparison positions; that rule **stands unchanged** — this ruling reaches operator operands and `Equals(T)` only, and the §22.15 question is recorded as liftable on its own evidence, not re-opened here.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected: nothing. Newly accepted: nothing the compiler doesn't already do** — source reads show sema's operator resolution has no move-only-aware operand logic and the ownership pass marks no owning-choice moved-from state, so today's compiler *silently borrows both operands*: this ruling pins the behavior-by-omission as the rule and gives #3333's implementation its binding semantics (the in-body consuming-operations rejection and the end-to-end double-dispose question are the impl deltas, noted on [#3333](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3333); no build was available — all compiler claims are source reads).
- **Kernel classification: derivation** — operator operands and the `Equals(T)` parameter are borrowing positions (K3.13's unmarked-read rule; the §28.3 borrowing-positions list); no kill is added, no axiom touched, the consume table unchanged.
- **Body-locality: local** — the binding is decided at the call site from declared types; no cross-body facts.
- **Doc-only:** seven spec edits, one code-generation-reference line + pin (→ v0.286), one `DECLINED.md` row. Guides/stdlib/corpus: no contact (the only owning-choice operator declaration anywhere is #3333's fixture, whose trivial bodies embody this reading).
- **Gate round (adversarial critique, one pass): SOUND-WITH-CORRECTIONS** — two blocking findings, both process obligations, applied: the §22.15 liftable deferral this entry mints needed its `DECLINED.md` row in the same commit, and the ownership-rule change bound the code-generation-reference update + pin move the first draft skipped ("CG: no contact" was checklist-false even though nothing in CG was falsified). Every technical attack failed, with the reasoning worth keeping: a temporary operand (`MakeHandle() = x`) is an unbound owned temporary whose K8 boundary outlives the call-bounded operand borrow; a moved-from operand is caught by §15.3's may-not-read rule (a borrow is a read); §6.6's compound-assignment accounting completes the operation before the store, so the operand borrow never overlaps the drop-on-overwrite; and the compiler's own disposal pass comments the same conclusion ("The operands stay borrowed, so there is no double-free"). Non-blocking, applied: the elective-`Merge(other: C)` boundary stated outright; axiom A7's Notes cell updated (its "operator half a use case" arrived here and resolved toward never-consume); §28.3's unbound-temporary use-list names operator operands; §22.15 carries the cross-note. The kernel-classification's load-bearing leg is §28.3's borrowing-positions line ("a borrow of the value through indexing or equality comparison"), the K3.13 leg being class-typed-scoped — noted per the gate.

### v0.287 changelog (v0.286 → v0.287)

**Editorial and clarification batch — no rule changes.** Seventeen items, each editorial or clarification class (process §2), landed as one revision: eight incidental defects from the 2026-09 elegance review ([`docs/proposals/elegance-review-2026-09.md`](proposals/elegance-review-2026-09.md)), four issues from the week's survey, three from the older-issue triage, and two proposal-0122 §3 presentation items. Every clarification was checked to be rule-preserving; where an item turned out to decide a case it was **held back**, and those are recorded at the end of this entry rather than landed under a lighter gate than they need.

- **Appendix C.4 lists choices under `where T: value` (editorial; [#3806](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3806)).** C.4's substitution list for `value` now reads "records, enums, choices (§35), primitives, inline arrays …", matching §14.2's normative table, which admitted choices when §35 landed.
- **§2.3 no longer lists `IDisposable`/`IAsyncDisposable` twice (editorial; [#3808](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3808)).** The two names leave the `System` row's representative list; the dedicated *Disposal interfaces* row is their home.
- **§9.4's inline-array parenthetical says what it meant (editorial; [#3809](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3809)).** "inline arrays declare no members (§26.2)" contradicted §15.1.2's four members; it now reads "inline arrays have no member bodies: their fixed surface is compiler-provided (§15.1.2) and admits no extension (§26.2)" — the reason the value-receiver rule has no inline-array case.
- **Appendix A's over-admission index records `old` and `result` (editorial; [#3810](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3810)).** One row: both forms parse through the shared expression productions in any clause (`result` as an `Identifier`, `old(E)` as an `Identifier` with a call suffix) and are restricted by §22.16 — `result` a compile error in unit-typed, constructor, `requires`, and `invariant` clauses; `old(E)` meaningful only in a method's `ensures` and rejected in an invariant member. No `ContractExpression` production was added: that would be a restriction-restating production of the kind 0122 L12 argues against.
- **§29.6 states the ground of each `yield`-placement rule (clarification; [#3816](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3816)).** No rationale section carried one (topic search: `finally`, `yield` — none), so the grounds are stated in place. A catch arm holds a borrow of the in-flight exception, disposed once the arm completes (§31.1, K3.8), and the language keeps one exception in flight (rationale §11.8) — a suspension there would hold that exception across consumer code that may raise its own, and a disposal of the suspended enumerator would end the arm without completing it. A `finally` runs to completion on every exit, including the enumerator's disposal, which §29.7 performs by running pending `finally` blocks with no consumer left to resume one. The `try`-with-`catch` rule follows: the arm is reachable from every point of the body, so a suspension in the body would carry an established handler across consumer code, and the frame carries pending `finally` cleanup and nothing else — which is why the `finally`-only form is admitted. Stated as grounds, not as new rules; the three bullets are unchanged.
- **§29.2 names the yielded borrowing-literal case (clarification; [#3706](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3706)).** One sentence in the yield-ownership preamble: a borrowing-family collection literal bound to a body local and yielded from a borrowing iterator (`var xs: Array<int> := [1, 2, 3]; yield return xs;`) is the unmarked-read-is-a-borrow case already stated there and in §28.3's borrowing-positions list — the iterator frame owns the literal (an owned body local, released at its scope end under §28.3), the consumer borrows. #3706's missing scope-end free is therefore an implementation gap, not an open ruling; the field-store half (`b.Items := xs`) is §28.3 clause 1's existing rejection. Nothing new is decided.
- **§22.13's forward-reference rule names `static readonly` auto-properties (clarification; [#3774](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3774)).** §23.1 already places a `static readonly` auto-property's backing store in the declaring type's own static initialization and §22.12 rule 4 names auto-properties beside fields, so the rule's extension to them was implied, not stated; one sentence states it, "as F and as G alike". The compiler's check is field-only on both ends (#3774's finding) — the issue stays open as the implementation tracker for this sentence.
- **§14.6 records the fourth known over-rejection (clarification; [#3407](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3407)).** The v0.262 entry listed three deliberate over-rejections; the shape #3407 found — an in-SCC edge whose argument is constructed over an *enclosing declaration's* parameter (`M<Pair<X, X>>` inside `Holder<X>`'s generic member `M<T>`), rejected although `X` is fixed for the instantiation and the edge cannot expand — is the fourth, and is now stated in §14.6's *Consequences* paragraph with its ground (the rule reads the argument's shape alone, never which parameters are fixed relative to which component) and the mechanical workaround. Reading (1) of the issue, as it recommends: the status quo is intended; the list of three is now four; no behaviour changes.
- **§14.6's stale compiler-status note is gone (editorial; [#3408](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3408)).** "*(Compiler status: not yet enforced — tracked #3271.)*" was false at v0.286: both halves of the §14.6 check run (`checkExpandingInstantiationEdges` and `checkExpandingGenericMemberEdges`, `src/sema/TypeResolution.cpp`). §22.12's sibling note (#2331) is untouched — its arm is still unenforced.
- **Stdlib §9.8's example and §4.4's prose drop the stale `import System.Collections.Linq;` (editorial; [#3818](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3818)).** The module has been auto-imported since v0.278 (§2.3's invariant; stdlib §5 names this exact failure mode). The same stale line headed three spec examples — §16.5's range composition, §26.4's extension example (with a comment giving the import as the reason), §27.6's method-reference example — and is removed from those too, as the same defect.
- **Stdlib §2.13 carries a ⚠ implementation-state marker (honesty machinery; [#3819](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3819)).** In the #3557 form. The evidence is a source read, not the probe #3819 asks for: no build exists in this environment, so `typeof(int).BaseType` was **not** run. Losslessness in the admitting direction holds as 0122 states (`Member` ⊇ the old alternation via `FieldDecl`/`ConstDecl`/`PropertyDecl`), but the over-admission index row the shape needs would have to cite a rejecting section for every form `Member` newly admits on an enum or choice body, and for **static fields other than an initialized `static readonly`** none exists: the old grammar rejects a mutable or uninitialized static field on an enum (`StaticReadonlyDecl` requires `readonly` and an initializer), §10.4's admitted list rejects them only by omission (with §35.2's "exactly" making the list exhaustive for choices), §10.4's own next paragraph says "Enum statics carry the full class-static surface rules", and the compiler admits every `static` field on an enum body (`Resolver::checkEnumRestrictions`, `src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp` — only `!static` fields are rejected; the parser already parses the full `Member` grammar for both bodies, `Parser_Decls.cpp`). Routed to the rulings train as a question: *does an enum/choice body admit the full class-static field surface (the compiler's reading and §10.4's "full class-static surface rules" sentence), or exactly §10.4's list (the grammar's reading and §35.2's "exactly")?* — a tracking issue is filed with this entry. `EnumMember`'s bespoke alternation and `StaticReadonlyDecl`/`StaticConstDecl` stay until then.

Each answer changes an extent. The union family is determinable; the subsets are not, without deciding. Routed to the rulings train with those three questions; a tracking issue is filed with this entry.

### v0.288 changelog (v0.287 → v0.288)

The rulings train: nine issue rulings, seven rulings and clarifications from proposal 0122 §2 (L5–L11), two rulings from the older-issue triage, and 0122 L12's held-back body. Every item records what was decided, what was declined, and why; the normative text states only the resulting rule.

**Ruling: "parameter-sourced" means a plain (non-`owned`) parameter in the borrowed-field and collection store admissions ([#3753](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3753)).** §28.3 clause 2 and §28.11 admitted "parameter-sourced" borrows unqualified; read literally an `owned` parameter qualified, although §28.3's own *Auto-drop (affine)* disposes it at the method's end — a statically certain dangle (five store shapes measured rc=0 → SIGSEGV before fix #3746). Both sentences now say *plain* parameter and state that an `owned` parameter is scope-bound. Declined: the literal reading (admits a certain dangle against clause 1's own premise), and admitting the store under K4.1's backstop (the residual-trust clause is for cases the compiler cannot compare; here it can). Kernel: derivation (K2.3 with K3.14). Body-locality: local. Impl already matches (#3746).

**Ruling: reads in a convenience constructor's chaining position ([#3585](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3585)).** §22.10 now states that a primary-constructor parameter is not in scope in a `this(...)` argument, and that no field or auto-property of the not-yet-constructed `this` may be read from the chaining position (§12.8 and §22.8 cross-cite it): the chaining call's arguments run before the chained-to constructor's step 0 and step 2, so no such slot has a value. Declined: leaving the rule derived from §22.10's scope list (enforced since `7132f69`, stated nowhere), and admitting the read with the null watermark (a read of unassigned storage — #3562's SIGSEGV). The parameter half is implemented (#3583); the field half is a spec-ahead-of-impl delta, tracked. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local.

**Ruling: a §7.4 narrowing reaches compound assignment and `++`/`--` ([#3686](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3686)).** §6.6 and §17.6 keyed their nullable-operand rejection on "the static type" without saying whether that is the declared or the narrowed type; §7.11 says narrowed, and fix #3298 read the compound forms off the declared type — accepting `n := n + 1` and rejecting `n += 1` for the same narrowed `n`. §7.11's own reading governs — the compound forms inherit the base operator's rule ("rejected with them"), which is narrowing-keyed — so both sections now read the static type after §7.4's narrowing, and the store leaves the narrowing in place; §6.6's narrow-integer write-back stays the one deliberate place where `b += 10` and `b := b + 10` differ (a typing rule, not a nullability one). Declined: the declared-type reading (makes the compound forms the one place where narrowing is invisible, for no semantic gain — rationale §6.4's recorded posture against the compound-only rejection). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. Spec-ahead-of-impl, tracked.

**Ruling: §15.4 stands — the dictionary literal targets only `Dictionary<K, V>`/`OwningDictionary<K, V>` ([#3517](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3517)).** The compiler's `SortedDictionary<K, V>` admission is impl-ahead-of-spec and is to be removed (with it the backing leak's only path). Declined here: widening §15.4's target set silently — whether the two fresh-store whitelists should be widened is #3489's proposal question and stays one (reopening bar: a proposal). No normative text change; `DECLINED.md` row added; one code-generation-reference line.

**Ruling: `FullName` and §8.5's default `ToString` render the enclosing-type path; `Name` stays the identifier ([#3542](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3542)).** For a nested type, `Type.FullName` is the declaring module, then every enclosing type outermost first, then the identifier (`"M.Outer.Inner"`), because the enclosing path is part of the type's identity (§2.8.3 rule 3); `Type.Name` renders `"Inner"`; §8.5's default `ToString` uses `FullName`'s rendering and keeps doing so. Stated at stdlib §2.13 rule 1, spec §8.5 and §11.6. Declined: `Name` carrying the enclosing path (rule 1 makes `Name` the identifier), and leaving `FullName` module-only (the reported ambiguity). Spec-ahead-of-impl (the default renders `module.name` today; `FullName` is unimplemented — #3819's marker sits beside the corrected contract), tracked.

**Clarification (ruling-shaped): §14.2's register-cost sentence and `DECLINED.md`'s restatement were stale against §2.3's v0.278 invariant ([#3811](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3811)).** The invariant governs: a standard-library extension over an always-available type auto-imports its module. Both sentences now state the residual cost that actually exists — the invariant imports the extension's *whole* home module. Declined: carving the invariant to modules already on the list (re-creates the hazard the invariant exists to close). With 0122 L3 at v0.289 the residual disappears for `System.Collections.Generic`; that revision retires the clause.

**Ruling: §30.11's callback admission is a named carve beside §28.14 (axiom A10), not a derived instance; the retirement trigger is a real condition ([#3813](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3813), closes [#1509](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1509)).** On §30.11's own example §28.14's forms resolve the receiver `dev`, a parameter, which admits no capture-bearing argument — so the "derived instance" claims at §30.11 and §28.14 were false and are deleted; the four-condition admission is stated as the carve it is, and A10's register row and cross-references say so. The trigger "until the standard library's signatures migrate to `scoped`" named no signature (stdlib §6.6 declares none; the registration callee in the pattern is user code) and is replaced: at a registration site whose callback parameter is `scoped`, §28.14 applies and the carve is not consulted; the four-condition shape governs registration through a plain function-typed parameter. Not taken: re-expressing a stdlib registration parameter as `scoped` and retiring the text — there is no such signature to migrate; the per-site condition is that design, available today. #1509 closes: the migration it tracked does not exist. Kernel: A10's description corrected, no new axiom. Body-locality: local.

**Ruling: the undocumented `Single` resolver arm is deleted ([#3812](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3812)).** §3.4 pairs `float` with `System.Float`; stdlib §9.2 says no `Single` type exists; the v0.2xx rename entry records that the name "never existed in the stdlib". The compiler's `Single → float` arm (and the `Single` reservation riding on it) is impl-ahead-of-spec and goes. Declined: documenting `Single` as a second alias — a newly minted duplicate against the recorded "tolerate inherited duplicates, mint no new ones" posture (`DECLINED.md`'s stdlib duplicate-spelling row; rationale §15.x), which would also have to enlarge §3.4's reserved set. No normative text change; `DECLINED.md` row added; tracked (two #884/#1081 test cases flip).

**Ruling: the §2.3 import gate for `System.IO` and `System.Threading` stays as spec ([#3807](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3807)).** 0122 L3 (v0.289) ratifies practice for `System.Collections.Generic`; the other two modules are not ratified — `System.Threading` is an Extended feature (D.2) whose visibility interacts with D.3's absent-not-stubbed rule, and `System.IO`'s import line is the file-level effect convention §2.3 already keeps for `System.Interop`. #3807 remains the impl-catch-up tracker for those two. Declined: ratifying all three (reopenable by a proposal that prices the Extended-feature interaction).

**Ruling (0122 L5): §4.2's typed-context widening is folded into §5.1's constant narrowing — target-typed integer constants.** An unsuffixed literal beyond `int`'s range has no standalone type and is admitted exactly where constant narrowing admits an integer constant, at the declared integer target it fits — §5.1's position list is now the only list (§4.2's own five positions were a strict subset that omitted collection-literal elements, record positional arguments, default arguments and enum constant values). Rider ruled: it participates in overload applicability on constant-narrowing's terms — `f(3_000_000_000)` selects `f(long)` over `f(double)`, the constant being admitted at integer targets only; an oversized literal at a non-integer target stays the error it was. Newly defined: the four positions above and the applicability case. The term "typed-context widening" is retired at its four other carriers (§20's binding atom, §18.1, §27.3's return ascription, rationale §9.11). Two of [#3821](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3821)'s three readings are settled for §4.2 **by this ruling and explicitly**: §4.2's "parameter" position is both the call argument and the default argument (listed separately), and a lambda's return-type ascription is a written integer target (§27.3); §17.7's and §35.3's own lists are untouched, so #3821 stays open for them. Declined: keeping two lists. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. Spec-ahead-of-impl at the newly-defined positions, tracked.

**Clarification (0122 L6, closes [#3815](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3815)): K5.4 is a consequence of the freeze criterion, not an override of it.** (i) holds — §30.5 already asserted the form is the keyword — and (ii) holds by its intact-referent disjunct: the outer task cannot dispose the chained task before the body, `finally` blocks included, completes, so every borrow that survives the kill finds its referent intact and disposal-tracked. K5 clause 1's reason for the family-1 freeze is restated to match (their surviving borrows' referents are neither flagged nor guaranteed intact). The "override" wording, K4's hedge and K3.6's "none — the form announces" Spelling cell (which read as *not* keyword-visible under K4's own recipe while §30.5 said the form *is*) are gone; K3.6's Spelling cell reads `return await` — the form is the keyword. Kernel: derivation restated; register untouched. Zero semantic delta.

**Ruling (0122 L7, Option B): one source spelling for the `out p: T? when true` postcondition.** §22.16 keeps the `static ensures` reading as the clause's *meaning* and no longer offers it as an equally-legal spelling; a hand-written `static ensures(not result or p <> null)` is an ordinary static postcondition that narrows nothing at the call site — which is what the compiler does (the narrowing is keyed on the `when` clause; `static ensures` reaches sema only as a parser comment). §12.1's exact-match override rule (0043 Q5) stands; §2.8.6's sub-row reads the meaning, not a spelling equivalence; across a module boundary the clause is carried by the parameter's postcondition modifier, not by a contract record (a hand-written clause of the same canonical text yields the same §2.8.2 record and grants no narrowing). Newly rejected in the spec's own terms: an override or interface implementation that spelled a `when` postcondition as a hand-written `static ensures` clause — formerly "the same declaration", now a dropped clause under §12.1/§11.2 (zero implementation delta: the compiler never implemented the equivalence). Declined: Option A (inherit the clause and reject a restatement — mints a restatement error the spec states for no clause kind, with a migration, for no semantic gain); `DECLINED.md` row. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. Doc-only in effect.

**Ruling (0122 L8): the anonymous `using var _ := <Task-family>;` is rejected with the discard.** Nothing can await an unnamed binding, so the form is the discard's abandonment one scope later, inside axiom A6's reach; §17.13's remedy list loses the anonymous entry, and the named `using var t := call();` idiom (§30.10) is untouched. The #1667 record's three-way severity table now reads: error — `_ := task;` and `using var _ := task;`; warning — a fresh task into a borrowing slot (§15.4); silent and blessed — `Task.FireAndForget(t)` and the named `using var t`. The named form's distinction is reviewability, not behaviour: a name is what a later `await` needs, and an un-awaited named binding stays §30.10's legal idiom. The rejection is keyed on the binding's type at the site under K2.4's pre-substitution keying, so a bare type parameter is not `Task`-shaped. Declined: S2-03 option (a), admit the discard and warn on every un-awaited drop (a permanent unsuppressible warning on §30.10's own legal idiom — rationale §5.28); `DECLINED.md` row. Kernel: axiom extension (A6's reach; row reworded). Body-locality: local. Spec-ahead-of-impl (the compiler's own `_ := task` diagnostic offers the anonymous form as a remedy), tracked.

**Clarification (0122 L9): the enum→integer cast is defined for every integer target.** §5.4: `I(e)` is `I(U(e))` — to the underlying type, then §5.2's checked conversion; `U(e)` is the round-trip-safe spelling. The two cases the old text covered reproduce exactly; `long(p)` on a `byte`-backed enum, undefined before, is now defined. Rationale §9.12 records it. Implementation status unverified at the new targets — a probe is filed rather than an absence asserted.

**Clarification (0122 L10): `Int32` and its PascalCase siblings are ratified in the enum underlying-type position.** §3.4's keyword-only exception and A.3's token-class disambiguation go; §10.3 states the one-list rule (the first item is the underlying type iff it resolves to one of the eight integer types, decided semantically), which is what the parser and sema already do. Declined: enforcing the keyword restriction (unargued, never enforced, against v0.184's one-type ruling). Impl-ahead-of-spec, ratified; the over-admission index gains a row.

**Ruling (0122 L11): `override` admitted on enum and choice bodies for the `Object`-virtual surface; the plain spelling stays.** The stated ground for the old rejection (no chain, no `base`) is equally true of records, which admit `override`; parity is restored at exactly the members §10.5 names, with the record admission (§9.2) as the reference — whether `override` reaches `Equals(T)` follows the record rule and is not decided here. §25.2's and C.10's three-way fork collapses to "spelled `override` or plain on all three kinds". Declined: rejecting the plain spelling (refuted by a lit-pinned record ACCEPT). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. Spec-ahead-of-impl (sema rejects `override` on every enum method; one lit test pins it), tracked.

**Ruling: `DisposeAsync` supersedes a destructor body per class along the reclamation chain ([#3492](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3492)).** §28.12 step 2 now says at which levels the destructor body runs under `await using`: skipped where the level declares or overrides `DisposeAsync`, run where it does not — a base whose only cleanup is its destructor is cleaned up as on the synchronous path. Fix #3470 implemented this reading (the issue's Reading A). Accepted cost, stated in the text: where a base level declares `DisposeAsync`, chaining to `base.DisposeAsync()` is the override's obligation — an override that does not chain forgoes that level's asynchronous cleanup and its destructor body alike, the asymmetry with the synchronous path's unconditional destructor chain. Declined: destructor-free reclamation at every level once any `DisposeAsync` ran (silently drops a base level's only cleanup); `DECLINED.md` row. Kernel: no contact. The overridden-base case needs one test, tracked.

**Ruling: §15.4's fresh-store must-warn is keyed on the borrowing position and reaches `OwningDictionary<K, V>`'s key slot ([#3429](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3429)).** An owning map owns its values and not its keys, so a fresh class-typed key dangles at its K8 boundary exactly as a `Dictionary` key does; the warning now names the position, with the bind-first remedy (the owning-family remedy is unavailable for a key, and the bound key is admitted only where §28.11's store rule admits it); §28.11's own description of the owning map ("its keys are value-like") and its store-rule scope are amended to say so, and §15.4's `Dictionary`-only literal-site scope is left deliberately unextended. Scope kept: the literal-site hard error is not extended to an `OwningDictionary` literal's key position (a newly-rejected program is a design change; recorded as an open question). Declined: leaving the key slot unwarned as the #3395 negative control pinned. Kernel: derivation (K8 + K2.3). Body-locality: local. Spec-ahead-of-impl, tracked.

**Ruling + editorial (0122 L12): Appendix A's enum/choice body productions collapse into `Member`; §10.4's admitted-member list is made exhaustive and is the rule.** v0.287 landed the two zero-over-admission pieces and held the body back because the old grammar was the only text rejecting a mutable static field, an uninitialized `static readonly`, a `static` property, or a static constructor on an enum body — §10.4's list rejected them only by omission, its "full class-static surface rules" sentence read the other way, and the compiler admits all four. Ruled (owner-delegated): the list is the rule — §10.4 now says *exactly … and no others*, writes *instance* on the property item, and re-scopes the statics sentence; §35.2 carries it over unchanged; `EnumDecl`/`ChoiceDecl` take `Member` and the over-admission index gains the row (net −5 productions with v0.287's pieces). Newly rejected by the text: mutable/`scoped` static fields, `static` properties, static constructors on enum and choice bodies (all admitted by the compiler today — spec-ahead-of-impl, tracked; one lit-pinned ACCEPT flips). Newly defined: an uninitialized `static readonly` field (admitted by the list, only the retired grammar required the initializer; the compiler accepts it). Declined: ratifying the compiler's full class-static surface (would import §22.12's mutable-static rules into a value kind for no recorded need; reopen on a real program). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. Corpus: `spec_0320`/`spec_0321` (Appendix A transcriptions) need a re-sync, not edited here (#1380).

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected:** an override or interface implementation spelling a `when` postcondition as a hand-written `static ensures` clause (L7); `using var _ := <Task-family expression>;` and `await using var _ := …;` (L8; replacement `Task.FireAndForget(e)` or a named `using var t := e;`); reading a primary-constructor parameter, or any field/auto-property of `this`, in a `this(...)`/`base(...)` argument (#3585; the parameter half already rejects); a borrow of an `owned` parameter stored into a field or a longer-lived collection (#3753; already rejects since #3746); `SortedDictionary<K, V>` as a dictionary-literal target and the `Single` type name (#3517, #3812 — impl-ahead removals, spec text unchanged); a mutable or `scoped` static field, a `static` property, or a static constructor on an enum or choice body (L12 — admitted by the compiler today).
- **Newly accepted / defined:** `n += 1` and `n++` on a §7.4-narrowed nullable local (#3686); `override` on an enum's or choice's `Equals`/`GetHashCode`/`ToString` (L11); oversized unsuffixed literals at collection-literal elements, record positional arguments, default arguments and enum constant values, and their overload applicability (L5); `I(e)` for every integer target `I` (L9); `enum E: Int32` and siblings (L10 — already accepted by the compiler); `FullName`/default-`ToString` rendering `"M.Outer.Inner"` for nested types (#3542); an uninitialized `static readonly` field on an enum or choice body (L12).
- **Newly warned:** a fresh class-typed key stored into an `OwningDictionary<K, V>` (`od[new K()] := v`, `od.Add(new K(), v)`) — #3429.
- **Doc-only:** L6 (K5.4 restated), L7's normative text (the compiler already narrows on the clause only; the override case above is newly rejected in the spec's terms with zero implementation delta), #3811 (the register-cost sentence), #3813/#1509 (the carve's status and trigger), #3492 (the per-class rule fix #3470 implements), #3807 (the gate affirmed).
- **Ramps:** none (no ratchet in this revision).
- **Kernel:** #3753 derivation (K2.3 + K3.14); L6 derivation restated; L8 axiom extension (A6's row reworded); #3813 A10's row corrected; #3429 derivation (K8 + K2.3); no new axiom, no tombstone, consume table: K3.6's Spelling and Frozen cells reworded, no row added.
- **Body-locality:** local for every compile-time rule this revision adds or alters (#3753, #3585, #3686, L5, L7, L8, L10, L11, L12, #3429); not applicable to #3542, #3811, #3813, #3492.
- **Documents touched:** spec (59 old→new substrings), stdlib (2), rationale (6), code-generation reference (12 + pin → v0.288), Guide 06 (1 prose line, pin unchanged), `DECLINED.md` (1 row corrected + 6 rows added).
- **Deferred, on the record:** 0122 L17 — v0.287 routed it here with three questions; they are filed as #3821 and are not decided by this revision beyond the two §4.2/§27.3 readings L5 settles explicitly above; §17.7 and §35.3 keep their own lists.
- **Issues resolved by this revision:** #3753, #3585, #3686, #3517 (ruling; impl delta re-tracked), #3542, #3811, #3813, #1509, #3812 (ruling; impl delta re-tracked), #3815, #3492, #3429; #3807 stays open as the `System.IO`/`System.Threading` impl tracker; #1667's asymmetry record is answered by L8's severity table.
- **Gate round:** the edit set passed an adversarial critique (8 blocking, 12 corrections, 10 notes — all resolved or declined with reasons before landing); `scripts/check_docs.sh` and `scripts/check_proposals.sh` clean at landing.
- **Tracking issues filed:** one per spec-ahead-of-impl delta above, filed at the landing.
