### v0.289 changelog (v0.288 → v0.289)

**Proposal [0122](proposals/0122-language-simplification-batch-2026-09.md) §1 graduates: four language design changes land (owner-accepted 2026-09-04 — "I agree with all proposals, please implement them as spec revisions on main"), and the proposal is superseded.** This is a **design-change landing, not a ratchet**: none of the four rejections below was scheduled by an earlier revision, so there is no ramp to state — each is newly rejected at v0.289 on the record this entry gives. The trains are the elegance review's language docket ([elegance-review-2026-09.md](proposals/elegance-review-2026-09.md)): L5–L11 landed at v0.288 as rulings; L13, L18 and L12's two zero-over-admission pieces landed at v0.287 as editorials and L12's body at v0.288; L17 was deferred on the record at v0.288 (its three questions are [#3821](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3821)) and is withdrawn from the proposal at this graduation, the questions staying open there; the presentation items L14–L16 follow at v0.291.

**L1 — the `when` construct is deleted, in both positions.** The scrutinee-less condition dispatch — the `(when c1 => a, c2 => b, _ => z)` atom and the `when … end when?;` statement — is gone from §19, Appendix A.6/A.7 (`WhenExpr`, `WhenArm`, `WhenStmt`), and every mention (§4.1, §7, §8.7, §17.2, §17.13, §17.15, §20, §21.7, §21.9, §22.15, §28.3's K7/A7/producers row/borrowing-positions list and K3.4's consume-table row, K8.2's boundary sentence, §28.10, and §1.6's closer list — the last three found by the landing's whole-document sweep, not by the edit set; the §9.6 and §10.5 examples now use the conditional atom). It was provably the `if`/`elif` chain — `(if c1 then a elif c2 then b else z)`: the same §20 common-type fold §19 already delegated to, the same textual-order evaluation, the same K7 meet — and the *weaker* spelling: §21.7 grants a trailing `if`/`elif`/`else` whose every branch exits the every-exit-path rule, and gave a trailing `when` nothing, while `when` carried two productions, a never-statically-exhaustive rule, a per-arm discard clause, a precedence note, a disambiguation sentence, and a third role for one token. The record had only ever weighed it against a scrutinee-less `case` (rationale §11.1, v0.144), and proposal 0057 re-spelled it in the train that made `elif` first-class without asking the question; `D:210`/`D:211`/`D:412`/`D:482` are adjacent and silent on `when`-vs-`elif`. **Declined:** keeping both (the asymmetry above); retiring `if`/`elif` instead (`if` is the statement's word order, the two-way pick, and the form with the grant); a deprecation window (no external users — the v0.217 precedent); migrating an `_`-less form to `else throw new MatchFailureException()` (§31.4 names that exception's producer as `case`; the corpus has no `_`-less instance). **`when` stays reserved** (B.1 unchanged; B.2 now names its two surviving positions — the arm guard and the `when true`/`when false` clause v0.288's L7 kept — and states that a `when`-led expression or statement is a syntax error). Rationale §11.1 is rewritten as the retirement record. **Kernel: no contact** (the producers row loses a word; the meet is unchanged). **Body-locality: not applicable.**

**L2 — `out owned var x` is deleted; `out var x` adopts.** The last use-site `owned` v0.246 left standing is gone from §22.3, §22.4, §22.5, §22.6, Appendix A.4 `ArgModifiers` and the code-generation reference. `out var x` now declares a fresh local that **adopts** the classification the resolved parameter announces — a borrow against `out`, an owned local under the standard discharge rules (must-use warning included) against `out owned` — which is §28.3's adoption clause (v0.270, K1.7 + K3.11) applied to one more fresh producer: `var x := Factory();` already adopted owned from the callee's declaration with no site marker, and an `out owned` result is the same situation. `out using var x` stays as the scope-bound owned form, accepted only against `out owned`; `out _` is unchanged in §22.6 and §22.3's `out owned` list now also names it, closing that list's "exactly the inline forms" contradiction with §22.6's discard paragraph. **One case the proposal left to the landing, decided here:** a *pre-declared local* passed as plain `out x` is admitted against `out owned` exactly when it is in one of §28.3's two adoptable states (uninitialized, or polymorphic-null) and adopts owned on every normal-return path — the callee's `false` path leaves an owned local holding `null`, as `out owned var x` did, K7 meeting owned with owned at the join; the adoption happens **once**, the local being state-matched from the call's normal return, so a second `out x` on it — a loop back edge included — is rejected until the value is discharged, which makes the pre-declared form §22.6's *single-use* disambiguation remedy and leaves the loop shape to the inline forms; no field, indexer slot, or property target is admitted at `out owned` (an owned-state location §22.3 bars, or a borrowing location §28.6 rejects — the categories §28.3's adoption clause cannot reach are exactly the ones §22.3 already excludes). This resolves a v0.286 contradiction: §22.3 admitted only the inline forms against `out owned`, while §22.6's own remedy for an ambiguous inline inference was "pre-declare a typed local and pass plain `out x`". `D:137` is strengthened, not eroded: §22.6's ground that an `out` half of resolution "would require a dedicated `out _` ambiguity remedy (the discard is compatible with both members of such a pair)" now covers `out var` as well. **Declined:** keeping the spelling as a visual cue (`var x := Factory()` lacks it already, and the rule contradicted the habit the reference teaches beside it); `out move var x` (`move` marks invalidation; nothing is invalidated); folding `out using var` in (rationale §5.27's four reasons stand). The v0.93 ground — "the resulting value's ownership would have nowhere to go" — predates the adoption clause that gives it exactly somewhere to go; 0090 Q5 ruled the token, not the form's existence; `D:137` (no `out owned` overload lift) is untouched. **Kernel classification: derivation** — K1.7 + K3.11 (adoption), K7 at the join, K3.15 for the normal-return-only attachment; the register stands at eleven axioms and four tombstones; no consume-table row changes. **Body-locality: local.** Rationale §3.10 carries the record; Appendix C.3 gains the row.

**L3 — `System.Collections.Generic` is auto-imported.** §2.3's table gains the module row and loses the two hand-hoisted rows (`Array<T>`/`OwningArray<T>` and the fourteen iteration and collection interfaces arrive with their module; `Object`/`Type` stay in the core row); stdlib §4 carries the *(auto-imported)* marker its siblings carry; the §14.2 sorting row's "home module" cost sentence (v0.288's #3811 rewrite) is deleted, the contradiction with §2.3's own invariant closed. The decision is the v0.278 method, applied to the collection module: the rule was **unenforced** (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Names.cpp:130–135` says so beside `KeyNotFoundException`), **unfollowed** (84 `.bzl` test files used a §4 type, 4 carried the import; 216 embedded programs; the specification's own fences — ten uses, two imports; no guide carried the line), and **unargued** (no decline record; proposals 0025/0111 restate it without a reason). **The cost, at full strength, is written into the §2.3 row itself:** twenty-nine names — `LinkedList`, `LinkedListNode`, `OwningLinkedList`, `Dictionary`, `OwningDictionary`, `DictionaryEntry`, `DrainedEntry`, `Set`, `OwningSet`, `Stack`, `OwningStack`, `Queue`, `OwningQueue`, `OwningBuffer`, `Span`, `ReadOnlySpan`, `BitReader`, `BitWriter`, `ArraySpan`, `ReadOnlyArraySpan`, `ArrayBitReader`, `ArrayBitWriter`, `IReadOnlySpan`, `SortedDictionary`, `SortedSet`, `FrozenArray`, `Counter`, `IEqualityComparer`, `KeyNotFoundException` (every `public class|record|interface` stdlib §4 declares, the `FrameBuffer` example excluded — 46 declarations at v0.288, re-measured at landing; the proposal's "roughly twenty-two" and a first draft's twenty-three both undercounted, and `BitReader`/`BitWriter`/`LinkedListNode` are the generic-sounding names most likely to collide) — enter every file's bare-name space with no opt-out (`D:220`); §2.2's current-module shadowing absorbs every in-tree user type of those names (`Counter`, `Span`, `SortedSet`), and a future user module *exporting* one makes the bare name ambiguous wherever both are imported. That is the ground on which the owner could have declined, and the change was accepted at that price. **Declined:** enforcing the gate (new compiler work plus edits at every site above, for a benefit no record states); hoisting more names row by row (the shape that produced the §14.2/§2.3 contradiction); an opt-out (not designable without a real collision — `D:220` stands). §2.3's extension-module invariant is untouched and still names one module. **Newly rejected: nothing.** An explicit `import System.Collections.Generic;` remains legal and redundant, as `import System.Collections.Linq;` has been since v0.278 — no redundant-import diagnostic exists and none is added. **Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: not applicable.**

**L4 — `++`/`--` leave the overloadable operator set.** §25.1's unary list, Appendix A.4's `OpToken`, §25.2's postfix-only bullet, §25.3's `Counter` example and §17.6's four overloaded-operand passages (the `T.operator++(x)` desugaring, the reference-type paragraph, the owned-field drop-on-overwrite paragraph, the indexer-slot overload sentence and the `Array<MyClass>`/`OwningArray<MyClass>` admission paragraph) are gone. `x++` is defined on exactly the operands §6.6's compound form admits for `+= 1` — an integer type, a floating-point type, `decimal`, or `char` (`c++` is `c := char(c + 1)` under §5.2's code-point rules; `char++` compiled before and compiles after, and the operand set is stated by reference to §6.6 so that §17.6 and §6.6 stay one rule) — and any other operand is a compile error; an `operator ++`/`operator --` declaration is a **syntax error at the token** (it left `OpToken`; §25.1's bullet says why, and no over-admission-index row is owed — the shape L1 uses for `when`); a type advances by `x := x + 1` under its own `operator +` (§25.2's declaring-type rule admits `operator +(c: Counter, n: int)`) or by a named method, the posture §25.1 takes for `not` and the shape the standard library's own `ISteppable<T>.Step` takes (no stdlib static interface declared `++`; no stdlib conformance is foreclosed). The overload was a second desugaring with an ownership corner — a fresh owned `++` result into a borrowing slot — that arose nowhere else, and rationale §14.1 had only defended statement-hood. **This is the re-measure `D:157` invites each subtraction pass, filed against that row:** the shared `OpToken`/`IfaceStaticOperator` cost is real and is paid here; the other two grounds — the compound-assignment desugar, §14.4's `~` argument — do not reach `++`/`--`, so **the binary bitwise keep stands unchanged on its own grounds** and the row records the pass. Stated honestly: the weakest of the four, landed because the bar asked for the measurement. **Declined:** keeping it for value kinds only (keeps the second desugaring and the `OpToken` cost for the one case `c := c + 1` already covers). **Kernel: no contact** (§17.6's drop-on-overwrite paragraph was an instance of §28.7, deleted with its trigger). **Body-locality: local.** Rationale §14.1 carries the record; Appendix C.10 gains the row. v0.288's #3686 sentence (a §7.4 narrowing reaches `++`/`--` through the desugaring) is kept in §17.6 and now follows the operand rule and the two rejection grounds.

**Gate round (adversarial critique, one pass, 2026-09-04): LAND-WITH-CORRECTIONS — six blocking findings, ten corrections, twelve notes; every one applied or declined with a reason, none dropped.** The four designs survived every attack: the `if`/`elif` equivalence and the totality asymmetry hold on the text (§21.7's grant is keyed to §19.6's scrutinee-typed registry, so a `_` arm never rescued `when`); the adoption-clause derivation holds; the auto-import evidence reproduces; the `D:157` re-measure is honestly filed against the indexed row; every `old` block re-located uniquely after v0.287 landed mid-round. What failed was completeness. **Blocking, all applied:** (B1) the first draft's §17.6 operand rule said "built-in numeric" and would have rejected `char++`, which §6.6 admits (`c += 1` is `c := char(c + 1)`), the compiler accepts, and three tests pin — the rule is now stated by reference to §6.6's admitted set, `char` included; (B2) the §2.3 cost row was short by six names (`LinkedListNode`, `DrainedEntry`, `BitReader`, `BitWriter`, `ArrayBitReader`, `ArrayBitWriter`) — the price is twenty-nine, not twenty-three, and is corrected at every carrier; (B3–B5) four surviving sites of retired forms — §22.5's `out owned var x`, §31.4's `KeyNotFoundException` import sentence, rationale §3.3's and the code-generation reference §4.4's `(when …)` — are edited; (B6) §22.3's category list admitted a pre-declared "recipient" where only a *local* has an adoptable state — restricted, with the field/slot/property exclusion stated in §22.3, §22.4 and C.3. **Corrections, all applied:** the #1336 try-convention remedy string is pinned by two lit rows and is reworded at the catch-up ([#3842](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3842)), not mechanically renamed; the L3 decline row takes the `declined-at-proposal` class of its v0.278 precedent; the `DECLINED.md` index-size line was stale since v0.278 and is re-measured; the `operator ++` rejection is a syntax error at the token (no over-admission row), and the Migration note says `char` stays and the enum-overload case is the one the operand rule newly rejects; the pre-declared form's single-use boundary and its `false`-path adoption are stated (§22.4); `out _`'s addition to §22.3's list is recorded as the contradiction fix it is. The critic's reading of the pre-declared sub-decision — admission restricted to a local in an adoptable state, every other category rejected by §22.3/§28.6 — is the one adopted. **Composition with v0.288 (landed between the critique and this landing):** three shared lines were re-targeted at landing — §17.6's paragraph (the #3686 narrowing sentence kept, the L4 rule applied as three within-line substitutions), §14.2's cost sentence (#3811's rewrite deleted outright), and the code-generation reference's pin; every other `old` applied unchanged (109 fragments, each unique).

### v0.290 changelog (v0.289 → v0.290)

**The stdlib regularization train — proposal 0123 graduates (owner-accepted 2026-09-04, whole: "I agree with all proposals, please implement them as spec revisions on main"; [`docs/proposals/0123-stdlib-regularization-batch-2026-09.md`](proposals/0123-stdlib-regularization-batch-2026-09.md)).** Ten items, one revision: four regularizations (R1, R2, R4, R6f — rulings and one signature change), three removals (R3, R5, R6a/b/g — design-change landings), one generalization (R7), two editorials (R9, R10) and three of R8's four presentation halves; every removal carries its `DECLINED.md` row, every compiler delta its tracking issue, and the S3-03 refutation (`CopyFrom`/`MoveFrom`) is re-affirmed in rationale §5.15 rather than re-litigated. Decisions taken at the landing plan and recorded here: R5 **Option B**, R3 **removal** (not the editorial fallback), R1's `Debug.Assert` **Reading 1**. This is a **design-change landing, not a ratchet**: none of the rejections below was scheduled by a prior revision, so there is no ramp to state — each is newly rejected at v0.290 on the record this entry gives.

- **R1 — nine overload pairs are one `:=`-defaulted signature each (ruling; stdlib §1, §2.2, §2.15, §4.4, §6.7, §7.2, §7.4, §8.2, §9.6).** `Task.Delay(ms | duration, token := CancellationToken.None)`, `Directory.Delete(path, recursive := false)`, `PadLeft/PadRight/PadCenter(totalWidth, paddingChar := ' ')`, `FileStream(path, mode, access := FileAccess.ReadWrite)`, `BinaryDeserializer(input, ignoreUnknownFields := false)` and `Binary.Parse<T>`/`ParseOwned<T>(input, ignoreUnknownFields := false)` on both span families, `Debug.Assert(condition, message := "")`, `Math.Round(x, digits := 0)`, `String.IndexOf(value, startIndex := 0)`, `Array<T>.IndexOf(item, startIndex := 0)` — thirteen rows fewer, every parameter name kept (§1: names are API surface). *Why:* the document already spelled the shape with §22.5 defaults (seventeen `token := CancellationToken.None` sites; `Increment(key, delta := 1)`), every default here is a literal or a constant, and replacing a pair with one candidate re-routes no call (§22.6's defaulted-arity reasoning). Each default is exactly what the dropped shorter overload did: `recursive := false` and `access := FileAccess.ReadWrite` were stated in prose, `ignoreUnknownFields := false` is §2.16's strict default, `startIndex := 0` is the one-argument search, `paddingChar := ' '` is evidenced by §9.6's own worked example (`"ab".PadCenter(5) = " ab  "`), and `Round(x) ≡ Round(x, 0)` is what the merged row now states. *Alternatives:* leave the pairs (the v0.215 `PadCenter` pair had no stated reason) — rejected; `Debug.Assert(cond, message: string? := null)` (Reading 2) — rejected, a nullable minted to encode absence when the runtime already reports an empty message as none (`bz_debug_assert_fail`, `len > 0`). §1 states the rule and the **three shapes that keep a pair**: forms differing by parameter type or `owned` (the duals); an interface-required member beside its `ignoreCase` twin (`CompareTo`/`Equals`, fixed by §11.2's exact match); and an omitted argument with **no nameable default** — the to-the-end window forms (`Slice`, `AsSpan`, `AsReadOnlySpan`, `Substring`, `String.Remove`, whose shorter form means the remainder, not a default) and the §2.15 JSON facade's `options: JsonOptions`, which is exactly the record-typed option `DECLINED.md`'s options-as-defaults decline is about — so that decline is named as the reason the `Json` pairs stay, not waved past. The `Binary.Parse<T>(ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>, ignoreUnknownFields)` gap the document recorded against itself closes. Incidental repair: the Pad contract comment said "all five Pad forms" over six rows; it now says "all three Pad members".
- **R2 — `Counter<K>` spells key membership `Contains(key)` (ruling; stdlib §4.20, §1).** `key in tally` now resolves through spec §17.5's structural lookup; `ContainsKey` on the three dictionaries is the inherited alias (rationale §15.x) and §1 records that it is not minted on new types; §4.20's prose sentence naming the member was found by the landing's retired-name sweep, not the edit set, and respelled with it. *Alternative:* a second name beside the first — rejected on 0074 §7's line (a new duplicate serves no arriving habit). One consequence stated honestly: an instance `Contains` commits resolution by name (spec §26.5 rule 1), so §5's `IEnumerable<T>` extension `Contains(value: T)` is shadowed on a `Counter<K>` receiver — `tally.Contains(entry)` no longer resolves (0 sites; the same shadowing the three dictionaries already carry). Absence check: the stdlib `Counter<K>` has no compiler implementation at all (`"Counter"` → 0 in `src/`; every `Counter<` in `tests/` is a user fixture), so the rename is free and rides the type's own tracker ([#3848](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3848)).
- **R3 — the array family's two cross-mode `SequenceEqual` concretes are retired (design change; stdlib §4.15).** `ArraySpan<T>.SequenceEqual(ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>)` and `ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>.SequenceEqual(ArraySpan<T>)` were v0.107 residue shipped before `IReadOnlySpan` (v0.108) and never retired when the interface form arrived — not a contradiction resolved but a legacy removed; a cross-mode call resolves to the interface overload under §8.6's call-bounded boxing, the rule §4.14 already states for `Span<T>`. *Alternative not taken:* keep them with a recorded direct-dispatch sentence. Zero call-site migration; the codegen's direct cross-mode arm is now an optimisation, not a declared overload ([#3849](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3849)).
- **R4 — `Math.Sign<T>(x: T): int where T: INumber<T>`; `Abs` stays (design change; stdlib §2.2).** One generic replaces four `pure` per-type overloads by the principle that retired `Sum`'s; the return type is `int` at every substitution, and NaN yields `0` (both `<` tests false — the codegen's existing `FCmp` behaviour, now the rule and listed below as newly defined). *Costs stated:* `pure` is lost until `INumber<T>`'s members are pure-declared (`deferred` row); a `char` argument is newly rejected (0 sites). *Why `Abs` stays:* §5.1's widening means `Abs<T>` would change `Math.Abs(shortVal)`'s result type from `int` to `short` — the result-type mapping `DECLINED.md`'s `Average` row records as blocked; `rejected` row.
- **R5 — the windowed `Encoding.GetString(bytes, start, length)` is retired; `String.From`'s window stays with its reason in §1 (design change, Option B; stdlib §3.2, §1).** Subsumed since v0.222 by `GetString(bytes: ReadOnlyArraySpan<byte>)` under §4.14's slice-first rule: `GetString(bytes.AsReadOnlySpan(start, length))`. The stale "`index`/`count` overload" sentence ([#3817](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3817)) died with the row. §1's window paragraph keeps its v0.282 rename frame (the three members renamed then were exactly three; the convention's instances are many more) and now records why `String.From(buffer, start, length)` keeps its window — `Array<char>` has no span-shaped route to `string`; Option A (mint `From(ReadOnlyArraySpan<char>)`, retire both) is `deferred` — a regularization batch does not mint a member to make a deletion possible. The catch-up ([#3851](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3851)) retires the **call form** only: the four `bz_encoding_*_get_string(arr, index, count)` runtime entries stay, because the surviving one-argument `GetString(bytes)` lowers through them with a synthesised full window.
- **R6 — four .NET-heritage duals (design change for a/b/g; ruling for f; stdlib §2.13, §8.1, §9.6; spec §17.10, §3.4).** By rationale §15.x's arrival ground measured at 0074 §7's bar: **(a)** `Type.Implements(iface)` retired from **both** documents and from rationale §18's delivered-member list — `iface.IsAssignableFrom(t)` is the one spelling; 0 call sites, 0 compiler arms (the lattice is unimplemented; [#3819](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3819)'s marker roster shrinks by it). **(b)** `Stopwatch.Restart()` retired — `Reset(); Start();` (1 test site; four lines in the live proposal 0016 respelled); §8.1 now states what `Reset` does — stops the stopwatch and zeroes `Elapsed` — a contract the section had not written, taken from the runtime's own `Stopwatch.Reset()` (`src/runtime/bezel_runtime_time.cpp:877`, source read: `running = 0; elapsed_ns = 0`), and `Reset(); Start();` is byte-for-byte what `bz_stopwatch_restart` did. **(f)** the static `String.Compare(a, b[, ignoreCase])` becomes the instance `CompareTo(other, ignoreCase)` beside `Equals(other, ignoreCase)`; §9.6's existing ordinal-with-`ignoreCase` note governs the new member's ordering, so no new contract sentence is owed; the #2581 nullable-argument gate travels to the instance spelling ([#3853](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3853) carries the test over). **(g)** `String.IsNullOrEmpty` retired — `s = null or s.IsEmpty` (`IsEmpty`, v0.231); spec §3.4's static-access example respelled to `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace`. *Keeps, recorded (`rejected` row):* `ElapsedMilliseconds` (19/6/7), `IsCancellationRequested` (reason in place), `Decimal.Zero`/`One` (21 in `tests/`).
- **R7 — the byte read tier is one `extension IReadOnlySpan<byte>` (design change, declaration-only; stdlib §4.14, §4.15, §4.16; spec §8.6).** 128 declared `Read*`/`TryRead*` members become 32: §26.2 admits interface heads (the document's own `extension IEnumerable<T>` precedent), §26.5 rule 2 reaches every conformer, and the receiver box is call-bounded — **spec §8.6 now says so for the receiver of an interface-headed extension call in one clause** (the gate found the mechanism was being inferred from the argument-side sentence rather than stated; §4.16's new *Extensions on the interface* paragraph cites the clause instead of asserting it), and the bodies read `Length` and the indexer and return values. The write tier stays per writable span (no writable interface); the bit tier's records store their span and stay mirrored; rationale §5.15's v0.103 byte-accessor record now names the interface-declared read tier. *Recorded honestly:* the accessors are not `pure`, and this pins the tier behind `DECLINED.md`'s pure-body `for` over `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` (`deferred`) and its sibling `rejected` row (interface-typed sources can never satisfy the elision's "see the type concretely"); the deferral's row now names the dependent. The `Stream.Write`/`File.WriteAllBytes(IReadOnlySpan<byte>)` widening the same move enables is `deferred`, not bundled. Migration: zero at any call.
- **R8 — presentation (editorial; stdlib §1, §4.4/§4.5, §6.8).** §1's 517-word Try bullet is a four-row table with its residual rules beneath (every statement preserved member for member; the one loss is the "(v0.184 wording;" landing pin, dropped deliberately; the GFM table ends the list item, so the bullets after it render as a second list); §6.8's nine async `Spawn` rows are elided under a marker comment that states the twin rule exactly — on the marker's own terms, since §1's elision convention covers interface-required members only and no new convention is minted by an editorial; §4.4/§4.5's `Sort()` listings drop the compiler-state narration (process §7 — it belongs in [#3325](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3325)) and keep the §14.2 statement. **The §4.14 double-listing consolidation is deferred to v0.291** (the presentation train): a section-wide restructure R7 also edits, not expressible as verifiable `old→new` in one revision with it. **[#1668](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1668)'s semantic sweep ran here (the v0.184 obligation):** the three *releases the backing storage* phrasings — stdlib §4.14 `OwningBuffer<T>` (*Disposal*, value-typed `T`), §4.19 `FrozenArray<T>` (the `destructor;` comment and its *Disposal* paragraph) — sit on owned buffers with non-trivial dispose and stand; the three in-fence `Dispose()` calls — `item!.Dispose()` on a `move`d owned local in `OwningArray<T>.Clear`, `_storage.Dispose()` on the owned buffer being replaced in `Grow`, `chain.Dispose()` on a `move`d owned entry node in `OwningDictionary<K, V>.PopValue` — are owned-receiver disposals; the prose sweep for disposal-through-a-borrow found only the rules that forbid it (§4's "element disposal is never performed by or through a borrowing collection"; `Array<T>.Dispose()` is a no-op; `Get()`'s borrow-lifetime error). Residue: none; no fix; closed.
- **R9 — the recorded-misfit flag on `TextReader.Read(): int` (editorial; stdlib §7.4).** §1's failure-signal rule requires it; the sentinel stands (0006's ruling), the `char?` change is `rejected` with the member's own graduation as the bar.

**Migration.**

A declared type takes the first row that names it and otherwise the first row that describes it; `string`, a reference type (§3.1), has its own row in the reference-kinded table above the class-type row, so it takes rule 3's verdicts and never the class-type row's warning; the `const` column decides nothing the `const` paragraph after rule 5 does not — a non-nullable primitive or `string` is `ok`, and an enum and every nullable form show `—`. The audit enumerates all 73 statements of the previous text and places each — a verdict, obligation or mechanism in the spec, its ground in exactly one rationale home, a pointer where the two meet — and maps every cell back; four ground paragraphs repeat their rule clause only as a lead-in, and the audit lists them; nothing is dropped and nothing is decided. Two kinds of text leave the normative prose without a rationale home: three history clauses ("since v0.260 … no per-kind carve remaining", "pre-v0.260", "historically the *suppression list*"), whose rule content stays verbatim (process §7; the old name stays recorded at rationale §12.8 and here), and the two compiler-status parentheticals, which were **stale** — the bare-generic-parameter arms they described as unenforced are enforced for a generic type's statics (`32db958`; `src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:11008–11024` and the auto-property twin at `:11057`ff; `tests/sema/static_readonly_bare_t_3272_test.cpp`; #3272 closed), a spec-asserted absence the compiler contradicted (process §5 item 3b); the generic-*method* arm is not demonstrable by source read (`isBareEnclosingTypeParam` at `:10214–10222` tests the enclosing type's parameters only) and is left as a question on #2331. Nothing admits it, so rule 3 now separates the two forms: "`static readonly` of **immutable content** — value types of sendable-value category, `string`, enums — and `const` (a primitive value type or `string`, the requirement stated after rule 5) are unrestricted"; Appendix C.11 and Guide 04 say the same; the table's `enum` row reads `const: —` accordingly. **Decided:** an enum-typed `const` (class-level or enum-body) is a compile error under the `const` type requirement; an enum-typed `static readonly` is rule 3's shared-immutable content, unrestricted. **Declined:** widening the `const` requirement to enum types — it would need §17.14 to fold enum operands, which its literal-rooted sublanguage deliberately does not, and the `static readonly` spelling already carries the use case warning-free (one `DECLINED.md` index row). **Class: clarification** (states a rule the `const` paragraph already implied and consolidates four texts); under process §2's stricter-gate rule it is gated as a ruling would be if a reviewer reads rule 3's old wording as having admitted the form — the decision, alternative and grounds are recorded here to ruling shape so the stricter gate costs nothing more. **Implementation (process §5 item 3b):** the compiler rejects an explicitly-typed non-primitive `const` at `src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:1023–1031` ("const `X` must have a primitive value type or `string` (§22.12)"; `tests/lit/sema/sema_enum__const_member_non_primitive_rejected_1564_22_12.bzl`, `sema_const__named_type_const_diagnoses.bzl`), enum types included by the `Kind::Primitive` test. ### v0.292 changelog (v0.291 → v0.292)

**Rulings and record closure: the §14.5/§22.6/§27.3 inference edge set ([#1695](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1695)), §16.3's `Range<T>` restriction against `ISteppable<T>` ([#1508](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1508)), the unbounded tier declined with reasons ([#1427](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1427)), a status memo for the Stage-2 fork-join gate ([#1725](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1725), open), and two stdlib corrections.** Four one-sentence rulings, one ruling that retires a recorded follow-up, one runtime-contract ruling, one editorial, one decline-register sharpening, one supporting record.

- **§14.5/§22.6/§27.3 — the edge set decided (rulings; #1695).** Of the six edges the tracking issue lists, two were already decided by the text and get no new rule: constraints as inference sources (*Constraints*, "recorded as liftable"; `DECLINED.md` *Type-argument inference powers*) and partial explicit lists (*Explicit lists are all-or-nothing*; the same row). Cyclic lambda dependencies were likewise decided (phase 2's fail-and-direct sentence). Four are ruled, each the smallest reading that decides the case without a join or a guess (rationale §10): **(1) a non-unique interface instantiation makes the candidate inapplicable** — an argument reaching both `I<int>` and `I<string>` against `p: I<X>` is never resolved by choice (*Agreement*); remedy a cast or explicit type arguments. **(2) A collection-literal lambda body contributes no return binding** — the literal has no standalone type (§15.4), so its substituted return position must be closed at the lambda's turn in phase 2 and admit a literal (an `IEnumerable<U>` position admits none), else the lambda is a compile error at the body; the remedy is a block body with a typed local. At an overloaded call such a position ranks *converting, never exact* (§22.6 *Lambda-literal arguments*, one sentence added), so two candidates that differ only there are the ordinary ambiguity. **(3) A nested lambda is an expression of its enclosing body** — typed under §27.3/§27.4 against the target its own position supplies and never re-entering phase 2; its parameter positions bind nothing of the enclosing call's type parameters. **(4) A lambda literal at a target-typed non-call position** (a declared function-typed local or field initializer, an assignment, a `return` against a declared function-typed return) **is admitted under the argument-position rule** — parameters from the target, inferred return type equal to or implicitly converting (§5.1) to the target's return slot — stated in **§27.3** (*Admission at a target-typed non-call position*), where the non-call contexts live, cross-citing §14.5 phase 2 and §22.6; §27.1.1's closing sentence names it as the one other site-typed bridge beside method-reference formation. An *ascribed* lambda is judged as a value's, so an ascription narrows what the position admits (`lambda(x): int => x * 2` at `(int) -> long` is rejected where the unascribed form is admitted). **Declined:** phase-2 re-entry for nested lambdas (it would need an agreement rule the section does not have); inferring a literal's container/element type from the body (rationale §5.16's uniform target-derived rule); deferring a literal-bodied lambda until a later argument or phase 3 closes its slot (a second pass phase 2 does not have); choosing among instantiations; and restricting the non-call literal to §27.1.1's value rule — the literal is typed at the site, so the compiler bridges the conversion as at a call argument and at method-reference formation, while a formed value has no adapter (two `DECLINED.md` rows). **Compiler:** (2) and (3) are the implemented readings (`src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Exprs.cpp:8815-8866` rejects the open and interface cases outright; `ExprTypecheck_impl.hpp:596-606`, `:679-693`); (4) is the typed-local reading `ExprTypecheck_impl.hpp:596-606` records, its other positions probes; (1) is the spec's intended reading and **not** what the compiler does — `unifyArgSubst` (`ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp:1047-1052`) recurses component-wise on arity with no generic-head check and no ancestor walk, so it binds `X := int` at that non-unique argument today and compiles the call (and mis-binds `C<string>: I<int>` at `p: I<X>` to `X := string`), a defect tracked as [#3861](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3861). The issue closes; its remaining implementation half is [#3858](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3858).
- **§16.3 — `ISteppable<T>` conformance is necessary, not sufficient; the recorded follow-up is retired, not discharged (ruling; #1508).** §16.3 said replacing the compiler-intrinsic element restriction with a `where T: ISteppable<T>` clause was "compiler surgery with no user-visible effect". It is not: the compiler-provided conformers are the whole numeric tower and `char` (stdlib §2.19; `src/sema/TypeRef.hpp:123-145`), the restriction admits nine (`src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Exprs.cpp:10396-10411`), and `ISteppable<T>` is user-conformable — the clause would admit `float`, `double`, `decimal`, and every user conformer. **Decided (reading (i)):** the nine types stand; conformance to `ISteppable<T>` is necessary but not sufficient; the restriction is intrinsic and is not a spelling of the constraint. §11.8's *What this unblocks* drops the `Range<T>` clause and says why; stdlib §9.8, stdlib §2.19's conformance sentence and rationale §18's static-interface-members entry say the same. **Declined (reading (ii)):** genuine de-intrinsicking — a widening, therefore a design change needing a proposal, recorded `deferred` with the five questions the intrinsic rule settles by fiat (borrow-bearing `Start`/`End` at class-typed `T`; `Contains`'s `min`/`max`/`<=` over an interface with only `<`; representable-range termination; `int`-shaped slicing and `case` ranges; `Range<char>`'s surrogate gap). **Nothing widens and nothing narrows**; the diagnostics pinned at `tests/sema/range_intrinsic_element_type_3247_test.cpp` are unchanged. The issue closes; the predicate's comments align under [#3859](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3859) (text only).
- **§28.14 — the unbounded tier: declined with reasons, bar sharpened (#1427 closes).** Not a rule change. The tier stays deferred; the bar moves from "until evidence demands it" to a predicate on both `DECLINED.md` rows: a corpus program that must return a composed function value capturing received callbacks with no bounding object to make it a `scoped` store — no `using var` local, no `this`-owned registration, no deferred-activation frame — together with a stated rule for `unbounded` in §27.1 function-type identity and in §28.14's method-reference formation bar. Measured 2026-09-05: the only `Compose` in the tree is the negative test `tests/ownership/call_bounded_2814_test.cpp:283`; no stdlib member composes callbacks into a returned function value; the one dependent want (proposal 0035's user-`Subscribe` row) shipped `SharedEventSource<T>` as its stand-in. §28.14's *Known v1 limitation* sentence now points at the row instead of stating the bar inline.
- **Stage-2 fork-join gate — a status memo, no normative change (#1725 stays open).** `docs/proposals/fork-join-gate-status-2026-09.md` (README supporting-records row; `DECLINED.md`'s fork-join row points at it) records the five dependencies verified at v0.291: dependency 1 is blocked on proposal 0027 never graduating (`SplitSpans` is nowhere in the stdlib); 2 is unlanded and its flagship sentence has two carriers (§30.14 and §30.13's memory-model close) the amendment must reconcile; 3 and 5 are unlanded — 5's home exists, §30.13's five-edge happens-before list, where the clause is a sixth edge; 4 is recorded-not-discharged; `Parallel` is wholly unimplemented (#3557). One correction to the gate's framing: items 1–3 and 6 of a landing are design changes under process §2, so "ruling-class revision" holds only for exactly 0032's recorded Stage 2. The memo asks the owner to sequence 0027's graduation first or re-scope the gate.
- **Stdlib §6.7 — the Task-discard sentence completed (editorial).** "`FireAndForget` is the only supported way to discard a `Task`" grounded the rule on the discard statement alone and named "the two legal patterns"; it now also names v0.288's rejected anonymous binding `using var _ := …;`/`await using var _ := …;` and says the legal `using var` is the **named** one (§17.13, axiom A6, Guide 01 and Guide 04 already agreed; a completeness gap the Guide 01 revalidation found).
- **Stdlib §2.5 — `DateTime` range faults are `OverflowException` (ruling; proposal 0076 §5's M9 row discharged).** The `Add*` family, `Add`/`Subtract`, and `FromTicks` raised `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` "when the result falls outside `MinValue..MaxValue`" — blame on the argument for a data-dependent condition (0076 §5: "Band blur … Blame semantics attached to a data condition"). They now raise `OverflowException`: the condition is an overflow of the tick domain, §31.4's `OverflowException` class ("a value outside the destination type's or operation's domain … checked narrowings"), which `TimeSpan`'s own arithmetic already raises; it is re-classified from the band-1 defect surface its `Argument*` label implied (stdlib §1: "A defect surface is never a recovery surface") to band 4's catchable fault; the constructors' component validation stays `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. The sentence now names `DateTime.FromTicks` (`TimeSpan.FromTicks` accepts every `long`) and `Subtract(span: TimeSpan)` (`Subtract(other: DateTime)` yields an unbounded `TimeSpan`). **Declined:** keeping the argument-blamed type (one `DECLINED.md` row). `FromTicks` is the borderline — there the datum is the argument — and takes the same answer: the argument is a valid `long`, and what fails is the checked narrowing into the tick domain. **Compiler:** raises neither today — `Add`/`Add*` lower to a wrapping add (`src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Calls.cpp:12596-12617`), `FromTicks` is the identity (`:11959`) — tracked as [#3860](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3860).

### v0.293 changelog (v0.292 → v0.293)

**Proposal [0124](proposals/0124-enum-name-parse.md) graduates (design change; owner-directed 2026-09-04): the string→enum name surface, [#2244](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2244).** Every enum `E` now carries **three** compiler-provided static members where v0.242 gave it one — beside `FromUnderlyingOrNull(value: U): E?`, the pair `FromNameOrNull(name: string): E?` and `NameOf(value: E): string` (spec §10.4; stdlib §9.9), unoverridable by a member **or a declared constant** (the constant case is what the compiler already enforced for `FromUnderlyingOrNull`; the text catches up). The two are the directions of **one table, the enum's declared-identifier table** — the bare constant name as written — the table §17.9's `nameof(E.A)` folds at compile time and stdlib §2.13's `Type.EnumNames` lists, so `E.NameOf(E.A) = nameof(E.A)` for every written constant and `NameOf` extends the operator to a runtime value (§17.9 says so in one sentence). `FromNameOrNull` matches exactly (ordinal, case-sensitive, nothing trimmed; a digit string names no constant because no identifier begins with one) and returns `null` otherwise; `NameOf` is total because every enum value is a declared value (§5.4). Under duplicate constant values (§10.2) `NameOf` yields the first-declared identifier and `FromNameOrNull` accepts every declared identifier, so §10.4 states the round-trip laws **up to aliasing** — `E.FromNameOrNull(E.NameOf(v)) = v` always; `E.NameOf(E.FromNameOrNull(s)!) = s` unless `s` names an alias. A `serialized "<name>"` rename (§9.8) is the **encoded form only** — the synthesized `Serialize`/`Deserialize` read it, and `NameOf`/`FromNameOrNull`, like `nameof` and `EnumNames`, never see it; §9.8 now says so where it names its table. The §18 boundary: a compile-time constant of one declaration consulted for a constant of a statically known type, not member reflection (rationale §5.18's "closed, stateless, ownership-free" enum introspection, and less of it than `EnumNames`). §10.4's example replaces its hand-written `Parse`-over-`case` with a three-line delegation (`Priority.FromNameOrNull(text) ?? throw new ArgumentException(…)`) — the sanctioned way to a user-declared throwing tier — and keeps its `Name` property for the exhaustiveness rule it teaches, saying so. §8.5 points at `NameOf` for the one-line `ToString` opt-in; §5.4's "the compiler-provided static member" becomes "a". Stdlib §2.13 no longer calls `EnumNames`/`EnumValues` "the building blocks for enum-to-string formatting, string-to-enum parsing" — they list the identifiers the enum's own members read, so a validation list built from them matches the parse surface exactly. The surface keeps the matching rule #2244's sketch asked for (declared constant names, ordinal, no numeric strings) and departs from it on shape: per-enum statics, not the generic `Enum.Parse<E>`.

**Why the identifier, and not the serialized name or both:** three surfaces must agree — `nameof`, `EnumNames`, `NameOf` — and only the identifier table lets them; the serialized name is by §9.8's own words the encoded form and already round-trips through the serializers; matching it here would let a JSON-motivated rename silently re-key a configuration parse. The cost accepted: a boundary wanting a renamed constant's wire spelling deserializes it. **Why per-enum static, not `Enum.Parse<E>`:** §14.2 has no `enum` constraint and `where E: value` over-admits; the per-enum device is shipped, enforced and implemented (#3044). What that gives up — reach from generic code, since no constraint carries the enum domain — is recorded as the reopening trigger. **Why band 2 only:** the precedent shipped without a throwing twin; the name axis has no assert *tier* — `?? throw` is the idiom, and a compiler-provided thrower must choose one exception for every program; shape (c) has no honest `default(E)` on an enum without a zero constant (§17.11). **Why a static `NameOf` and not `Name`/`ToString`:** `Name` collides with §10.4's own example and would be the first compiler-provided instance member on enums; §8.5's default is a separate rule with its own blast radius. Three `DECLINED.md` rows (*Enum name-parse alternatives*, *Enum name-parse tiers*, *Enum name-parse over the serialized-name table*), each with a reopening bar. Rationale §9.12 carries the decision record (*The name tier*).

**Adjacency kept, not amended:** §8.5's enum `ToString` default; `Type.EnumNames`/`EnumValues` (#3819, still spec-ahead-of-impl); the §27.6 method-reference form of the compiler-provided tier (unspecified for all three members, as the compiler already treats `FromUnderlyingOrNull`); §9.8's uniqueness clause's reach over enum constants (a reading question, filed — not load-bearing here); `DECLINED.md`'s deferred `FromUnderlyingUnchecked` and flags-enum rows (rationale §9.12: no flags idiom exists, so `NameOf` has nothing undefined to answer).

**Migration.**

- **Newly defined:** `E.FromNameOrNull(name: string): E?` and `E.NameOf(value: E): string` on every enum, at every nesting depth; §17.9's `nameof`/`NameOf` identity. **Newly rejected:** a user-declared enum member **or constant** named `FromNameOrNull` or `NameOf` — no enum in `src/`, `tests/`, `docs/` or the corpus declares either (the `docs/` hits for `NameOf` are Appendix A.7's `NameOfExpr` production; the `src/` hits are C++ identifiers); the constant clause also names, for `FromUnderlyingOrNull`, what the compiler already rejects (impl-ahead-of-spec, closed by this text). Newly warned: nothing. No existing program changes meaning: `ToString`, serialization and `nameof` are untouched.
- **Spec-ahead-of-impl ([#3862](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3862)):** the compiler provides `FromUnderlyingOrNull` only. The catch-up is one arm beside each existing arm — the declaration reject (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:676-684`, members and constants, nested), call typing (`src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp:1926-1960`), the no-`MethodSymbol` callee exemption (`:19749-19753`), and lowering (`src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Calls2.cpp:4255`, siblings of `tryLowerEnumFromUnderlyingOrNull` over the constants' **identifiers** in declaration order — not `enumConstantWireNames`, which is §9.8's table) — plus the comment refresh in the four files that quote §9.8's rewritten sentence. **Filed separately:** whether §9.8 `:1613`'s uniqueness clause reaches enum constants, and whether sema enforces it (no diagnostic located by reading).
- **Compiler claims are source reads** — no build exists in the authoring environment; every `src/` citation above was read at `dc0b60d`, not run.
- **Kernel classification: no contact** (§28/§30.5 untouched). **Body-locality: local** — the declaration reject is a declaration-site check; call typing is ordinary applicability at the call site; no cross-body fact is consumed.
- **Diagnostic couplings:** none — the `"may not declare a member named"` diagnostic (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:679`, pinned by the three `from_underlying_or_null_3044__*` lit rows and `enum_restrictions_nested_3601_test.cpp`) is unchanged; the new names get new diagnostics.
- **Doc-only:** 7 spec edits (§5.4 one word, §8.5 one clause, §9.8 one sentence, §10.4 the example's `Parse`, the `Name` paragraph's sentence, the tier block, §17.9 one sentence), 5 stdlib edits (§2.13 one sentence; §9.9 heading, lead, signatures, the name-pair paragraph), 1 rationale paragraph (§9.12), 3 code-generation-reference edits + pin (→ v0.293: §3.3's fence comment, §5.1's tier list, §5.11's `Enum.*` absences), 3 `DECLINED.md` rows, the README row (Live → Graduated), the proposal's status flip, gap-map row 32 annotated. Guides: no contact (Guide 03 teaches `enum` vs `choice` and cites no boundary member; its pin stays at v0.289). Corpus: `spec_0032`, `spec_0033`, `stdlib_0150`, `codegen_0003` hand-updated (#1380); the new §10.4 usage fence is not added (one case short; `EXTRACT` 511 → 512).
- **Composition with v0.292** (§14.5, §16, §27.3, §28.14; stdlib :4193): no shared section, no shared line; the four headers, the code-generation pin and this entry's parenthetical are the six v0.292-dependent sites, taken after it. Every `old` unique at v0.291 on the first sweep (22 of 22, headers included).
- **Issues this revision resolves:** [#2244](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2244) closes with the citation (spec §10.4, v0.293). **Tracking issues filed:** [#3862](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3862) (the compiler catch-up above); [#3863](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3863) (the §9.8 uniqueness-reach question).
- **Gate round (adversarial critique, one pass, 2026-09-05): LAND-WITH-CORRECTIONS — 5 blocking, 12 corrections, 11 notes; every one applied or declined with a reason, none dropped.** What bit: the second round-trip law was false under §10.2's duplicate values (`Legacy := 1, Current := 1` refuted it in the same paragraph) and is now stated up to aliasing; the surface as drafted read the *serialized*-name table, which made "a digit string names no constant" false (`serialized "2"` is legal), left `nameof`/`NameOf` disagreeing on every renamed enum, and rested law (1) on a §9.8 uniqueness clause whose reach over enum constants the spec does not state — resolved together by the coordinator's decision for the declared-identifier table, under which the digit-string claim is true by construction, `nameof`, `EnumNames` and `NameOf` read one table (§17.9 now says so), and well-definedness follows from identifier uniqueness (the §9.8 question is filed, not asserted); the gate bullet itself had been drafted as "pending" with predictions in it. Corrections: §2.13's rewritten sentence had recommended building a validation list from a table the parser did not read; the `Enum.Parse<E>` decline omitted its rival's one advantage (generic reach) and now records it as the reopening trigger; the reserved names' reach over declared constants was unstated while the compiler already enforced it; the metavariable `E` sat inside copyable code; two `§9.8` anchors in one sentence; a cited line span overreached; the absence claim was refutable on a literal grep. The attacks that failed: `NameOf` totality (§5.4 plus §17.11's rider close every producer of an undeclared value), the flags case (rationale §9.12), the corpus (all four cases `skip`), and the mechanical set (every `old` unique, both gates green, `+1` extraction fragment exactly as predicted).

### v0.294 changelog (v0.293 → v0.294)

**Proposal [0125](proposals/0125-static-interface-promotions.md) Part A graduates (design change; owner-accepted 2026-09-05): the user-defined sequence-literal protocol becomes interface-based, [#1506](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1506).** §15.4.1's by-name opt-in — *"declaring a static method named exactly `FromCollectionLiteral` with one of two recognized signatures"* — is replaced by conformance (§12.7) to one of two static-member interfaces (§11.8), `ICollectionLiteralTarget<TSelf, T>` (borrowing form, `ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>` carrier) and `IOwningCollectionLiteralTarget<TSelf, T>` (owning form, `owned OwningArray<T>` carrier), defined in stdlib §2.19. A class is a **sequence-literal target** exactly when it conforms at `TSelf` = itself; a type parameter constrained to conform is one inside its declaring body; an interface never is. The member's name and signature are unchanged — the promotion costs each conformer one clause in its class header. The ten built-in sequence collections declare the same conformance in their own standard-library declarations (stdlib §4.4–§4.11) and each lists `FromCollectionLiteral` as a member, so §15.4's target list is now *derived* from declarations (its bullets restate them) rather than curated; at a built-in target the literal is still constructed directly under §15.4's element-order rules — §15.4.1's materialize-then-call *Lowering* governs the other targets, and a built-in's listed factory produces the same value the literal produces. Bezel therefore has **two** recognition categories, not three: interface-based (iteration, §29.1; collection literals, §15.4.1) and the single structural-dispatch rule for `Contains`/`in` (§17.5).

**Why explicit conformance, and not an implicit one inferred from the factory:** an implicit rule would be a second structural-dispatch rule beside `Contains` — the thing §17.5 and rationale §5.16 (*One opt-in path, not two*) both guard by name, and which `DECLINED.md`'s duck-typed-enrollment row already declines — and it would buy nothing: the compiler would still look up a name, and `TSelf.FromCollectionLiteral(…)` would stay unreachable through a constraint because nothing would declare the constraint satisfied. §12.7 states conformance nominally in every clause but the `IDisposable` carve-out, so an inferred conformance would be a new kind of conformance, not a use of the existing one. §11.8's *"both signatures were chosen for zero-source-change promotion"* is corrected on the same ground: the promise holds of the **member**, never of the **header**.

**Why the built-ins declare nominally, and not by a compiler-provided conformance:** §12.7 clause 5's compiler-provided device is scoped to primitives, so a class cannot use it without a new implicit case this revision declines to add; and a member callable on a type's own name that appears in no standard-library listing is exactly the invented-API class #1424 removed once (`int.Zero()`). Declaring the conformance and listing the factory keeps both rules: `Array<int>.FromCollectionLiteral(span)` is a **declared** member.

**A recorded decline reopened, with its evidence stated:** `DECLINED.md`'s row *"A `ToArray()` on `ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>`, riding the v0.272 collection-literal carrier fix"* (`rejected`, v0.272; bar *"a stdlib pass that takes it on its own merits"*) declined the value `ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>` → `owned Array<T>` on *"surface is debt"* and *while-we're-at-it* grounds. This revision supplies that value as `Array<T>.FromCollectionLiteral(elements: ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>): owned Array<T>`, and nine siblings. The new evidence against the stated reasons is structural: a nominal conformance to a static-interface member **requires a declared witness** — §11.8: *"A conforming type declares `class Meters: INumber<Meters>` and supplies the static members with exact signatures (the §11.2 matching rule, applied to statics)"*; *"a runtime type conforms only by declaring the full member set, statics included"* — and neither §11.8 nor §12.7 has a witness-less form. The members are the unavoidable cost of the promotion the owner directed (#3247, #1506), not a convenience riding a fix; the alternative (built-ins conforming with no callable member) was priced and declined as a new conformance kind. The row is amended in place — its `ToArray()` spelling stays declined as a dual — and the reasoning is registered as `DECLINED.md` D-0009. The ten members are recorded on the revision's **cost** side as well as its gain side.

**Adjacency kept, not amended:** the dictionary-literal form (`[k: v]`) stays outside the protocol and both dictionaries conform to neither interface; inline arrays are unchanged (§15.1, not nominal types); `SortedDictionary<K, V>`'s dictionary-form admission remains the impl-ahead delta tracked at [#3831](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3831); §15.4's `:2960` owning-target sentence takes no edit (its enumerated list serves the dictionary value-position parenthetical); §14.2's conditionally-admitted-member register, §3.6's derived-type-property table and the statics-and-sharing fact sets have no contact — *sequence-literal target* is declaration-derived, not structure-derived, and adds no §3.6 row.

**Migration.**

- **Newly required: a conformance clause on every user conformer.** A class that keeps a bare `FromCollectionLiteral` and declares neither interface is no longer a sequence-literal target. In-tree: **17 declaration sites in 4 test files** — `tests/sema/collection_literal_factory_conjuncts_3032_test.cpp` (10), `tests/parser/param_post_colon_owned_3027_test.cpp` (3), `tests/codegen/collection_literal_user_type_fcl_2957_test.cpp` (2), `tests/sema/collection_literal_dict_form_target_3031_test.cpp` (2) — plus one corpus case (`tests/conformance/cases/spec_0075.bzl`). **External users: none.** No ramp is owed: this is a design change, not a Ratchet (process §2 — nothing scheduled the tightening), so there are no two ends to state; what is owed is the diagnostic below.
- **Newly defined:** the declaration-site diagnostic — a class declaring a `public static FromCollectionLiteral` matching either interface member at `TSelf` = the class while conforming to neither is a compile error naming the missing conformance and its remedy (*add `: ICollectionLiteralTarget<C, T>` / `: IOwningCollectionLiteralTarget<C, T>` to the class header*); `TSelf.FromCollectionLiteral(…)` through a constraint; a constrained type parameter as a literal target; the ten built-in factories callable directly by name (stdlib §4.4–§4.11); `is`/`as` against either interface `true` for those ten types (§11.8's static-member interfaces are ordinary types) — a new runtime-observable fact.
- **Newly rejected:** conformance to either interface by a value kind (record, choice, enum) — the erasure of §11.8 would otherwise admit one silently; a class declaring both conformances on itself, or one of them at two element types; an interface type as a target (unchanged in effect — the compiler already declined it, `isCollectionLiteralInterfaceTarget`).
- **Newly accepted (the retired conjunct diagnostics):** a `FromCollectionLiteral` that is non-`public`, non-`static`, inherited, extension-supplied, or of a non-matching return type, on a class declaring no conformance, is no longer rejected at its declaration — it is an ordinary member of a type that is simply not a target, and the three §15.4.1 conjunct diagnostics that used to name it are retired into §11.2 conformance matching (which reaches it only once a conformance is declared) plus the declaration-site diagnostic above.
- **Diagnostic couplings (the reason the test track moves with the compiler, not with this revision):** `tests/sema/collection_literal_factory_conjuncts_3032_test.cpp` pins the three retired §15.4.1 sentences verbatim (*"must be `public`"*, *"must return `owned C<T>`"*, *"exactly one may be declared"*) and states that its predicates are selective on that wording; it is **re-authored**, not clause-patched, against §11.2 conformance diagnostics and the new declaration-site diagnostic, and its cells have successors only once each declares the conformance (its non-`public`-without-conformance cell has none — that program is newly accepted). The other three files take one header clause per site.
- **Spec-ahead-of-impl.** Prerequisite [#3857](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3857) (the compiler never received v0.272's `ReadOnlySpan<T>` → `ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>` carrier rename: `src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:1625`, `src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Setup.cpp:31450`) lands first. The promotion's own catch-up is filed as [#3866](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3866): synthesize the conformance and the listed member on the ten built-in `TypeSymbol`s (today *"null `decl` and empty members"*); re-key `isCollectionLiteralAdmissibleTarget` and the empty-literal predicate (`src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp:503-530`, `:573-592`) to a conformance query at `TSelf` = target, class-only, plus the type-parameter case; retire `checkCollectionLiteralFactoryConjuncts` (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:1576-1751`) into §11.2 matching while keeping the value-kind and own-declared-dual rejections and adding the declaration-site diagnostic; keep the built-ins' direct intrinsic construction at a literal and add a callable static body for their listed factory; re-author `_3032` and clause the other three files; add spec-cited tests for the non-target conformance at `TSelf ≠ C`, the derived class declaring its own, the interface non-target, the type-parameter target, and the migration diagnostic.
- **Compiler claims are source reads** — no build exists in the authoring environment; every `src/` and `tests/` citation above was read, not run.
- **Kernel classification: derivation** — no §28/§30.5 rule moves. §15.4's D4 borrowing-family and nested-fresh-producer clauses are re-keyed from *"a user-defined type whose `FromCollectionLiteral` declares the borrowing form"* to *"every borrowing-form target"* / *"any sequence-literal target"*, the same set under the new predicate; v0.272's derivation (K1/K2.3/K4.3 through §28.11's borrow column) stands unchanged, no kill is added, the consume table and the axiom register are untouched. **Body-locality: local** — a declaration-site check on the conformer plus a use-site predicate over the target's declared conformances (for a type parameter, over the constraints in scope in the same body); no cross-body fact is consumed.
- **Doc-only:** 13 spec edits (§11.8's follow-up sentence; §15.4's target bullet, sequence-form sentence and two D4 clauses; §15.4.1's opt-in paragraph, both form headings, the conjunct paragraph, *Lowering* with its built-in carve, *Recognition category* and the `RingBuffer` example header; §17.5's taxonomy sentence), 20 stdlib edits (§2.19 heading, opening, producer markers and the new interface pair; §4.3's roster sentence; ten conformance declarations over eleven §4.4–§4.11 header lines with eleven members — ten listed signatures and `OwningArray<T>`'s reference-implementation body; §2.14 `:732`, `:747`, `:769`), 8 rationale edits (§5.16 four, §5.19 two, §18 two), one code-generation-reference §5-index line **and its pin (→ v0.294** — required by process §9 because the stdlib surface changed; the pin was one revision behind, inside the gate's allowance), seven new `DECLINED.md` index rows, two corrected rows (the dual-shape row's carrier; the `ToArray()` row's amendment) and one register entry (D-0009). Guides: no contact (none mentions the protocol).
- **Editorial repairs carried, not dropped silently:** §15.4.1's conjunct paragraph still named the retired `ReadOnlySpan<T>` as an element-type carrier (v0.272 replaced it), and `DECLINED.md`'s dual-shape row carried the same stale carrier; both now read `ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>`. Stdlib `:747` and `:769` called a `Self` type *"separately deferred"* while `DECLINED.md` records it `rejected` with no reopening bar; both sentences now name the decline. Stdlib §2.14 `:732` taught that `FromCollectionLiteral` is recognized by name; it now says so in the past tense, dated.
- **Corpus (#1380):** no case is deleted. `spec_0075` (the `RingBuffer` example) gains the header clause and is re-transcribed by hand; `spec_0073`/`spec_0074` are unchanged (the two form code blocks stay as `C<T>`-spelled witness listings — only their prose headings move); the §2.19 interface pair adds one new `stdlib_NNNN` row, `skip:signature-listing`; the ten §4 listing rows and `OwningArray<T>`'s reference-implementation row are re-transcribed. Every row keeps its `skip` status until the compiler catch-up lands.
- **Part B ([#1507](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1507)) is deferred, not landed.** `IDeserializable` stays the marker interface it is. The recorded design — `IDeserializable<TOut>` with `static Deserialize(d: IDeserializer): owned TOut`, no recurrence, and an admissibility clause on `TOut` (`C` or `Shared<C>` for a class, `V` for a value kind) — fits all three return shapes §2.14 and §9.8 state, the shared-node entry `owned Shared<C>` (§9.8, *Synthesized `Deserialize`*) included, as `TOut = Shared<C>`. It sits in proposal 0125 §3 behind a three-item bar that is about cost and two unverified obligations, not about any gap in the spec: an owner decision on the 621-occurrence breaking header change across 90 files (one hard revision, or a ramp — and a ramp needs a ruling that a bare and a generic `IDeserializable` may coexist by arity); the §9.8 synthesis generator learning to emit `Deserialize` as an interface-member witness; and `class Node: IDeserializable<Shared<Node>>` verified admissible as a conformance header under §11.2/§11.8/§12.7 as written, with the `TOut` clause ruled. Separately, the `owned Shared<C>` entry shape is spec-ahead-of-impl (sema types every `Deserialize` as returning the declaring type; codegen mints no `Shared` entry) and is filed as [#3867](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3867) — a tracking item, not a deferral ground. §11.8's follow-up sentence and stdlib §2.14 now say exactly that.
- **Issues this revision resolves:** [#1506](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1506) closes with the citation (spec §15.4.1, stdlib §2.19, v0.294); [#1507](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1507) is re-pointed at proposal 0125 Part B and its bar. **Tracking issues:** [#3857](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3857) (prerequisite, open); [#3866](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3866) (this revision's catch-up); [#3867](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3867) (the `owned Shared<C>` entry shape); [#3831](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3831) (the `SortedDictionary` dictionary-form delta, cited not re-filed).

What bit: the built-ins conformed to nothing under §12.7's own definition, and the edit-set never touched it (fixed by nominal declaration per type, not by a new implicit case); the direct built-in call would have re-created the #1424 invented API (fixed by listing the factory in all ten sections); the in-tree break was claimed as three declaration sites and measured as seventeen, ten of them pinning diagnostics this revision deletes; an interface conformer was an admitted-but-unconstructible target; the uniqueness rule over-rejected a derived class that declares its own conformance; two form blocks and the *Lowering* sentence kept name-keyed text no edit reached; the migration had no declaration-site signal — the exact silent non-opt-in #3857 documents as a bug; and the code-generation pin move was called optional. Pass 2 — 5 blocking, 11 corrections, 5 notes; it confirmed each pass-1 resolution against the tree and ran both gates green on the applied set, and it bit five more times: pass 1's own C1 had injected a **false absence** about §9.8's `owned Shared<C>` shape into the record (the shape is at `:1546` in both trees; reverted, and Part B re-grounded on cost and two unverified obligations); the ten declared factories reopened `DECLINED.md`'s `ToArray()` row without naming it (named, evidenced, amended, registered as D-0009); the re-keyed §15.4.1 *Lowering* governed `Array<T>` circularly (carved); stdlib §2.14 still taught by-name recognition (retired, dated); and this changelog entry itself was missing.

### v0.295 changelog (v0.294 → v0.295)

**Ruling (owner-directed 2026-09-08, [#4085](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4085)): a call through a function-typed value admits no named argument (§27.1).** The named form `Identifier := expr` at an invocation whose callee is a function-typed value — a parameter, local, or field of function type, or any expression of one — is a compile error naming §27.1, the treatment §23.5 already gives an index position. §27.1 said the names a function type may carry are *documentation only* and that *calls are positional*, but nothing about the call-site syntax; the compiler accepted the form and bound it by textual position, discarding the name — `caller(b := 2, a := 100)` against `(a: int, b: int) -> int` ran as `caller(2, 100)`, a silent swap with no diagnostic.

**Why rejection, and not one of the two bindings.** *Binding by name* would make the names load-bearing at the call while §27.1's own statement that the named and unnamed forms are the same type lets any assignment — exact-match, or §27.1.1's identity-preserving retyping — drop or relabel them — `var g: (b: int, a: int) -> int := f;` is the same value under other labels, and `g(a := 1, b := 2)` would reach `f` as `(2, 1)` — and there is nothing for a name to do that position cannot: a function type declares no defaults, so §22.5's named-binding machinery, whose purpose is skipping and reordering around defaults, is never reached (§23.5's own reasoning). *Order-checked labels* — the name admitted only where it equals the declared name at that position, the reading the owner first proposed — were weighed and declined: they would turn documentation-only names into a compatibility contract, since a retyping to the unnamed form or a rename in the function type would break every call site that spelled them. Both are `DECLINED.md` rows.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected:** the named form at a function-value invocation. Out-of-tree this is not *strictly* bug-revealing, unlike v0.241's index-position twin: a call whose names happen to agree with position (`caller(a := 100, b := 2)`) compiles and behaves correctly today and stops compiling — the cost #4085 states and this ruling accepts, on the ground that the name is unenforceable either way. In-tree: no test program or documentation example writes one — the only hits are the two parser round-trip renders in `tests/parser/arg_modifiers_test.cpp:84,104` (`f(name := "x", …)` with no declared `f`), which exercise the shared A.4 grammar and are unaffected, because the rejection is semantic, exactly as at the index position. Newly warned: nothing. No existing program changes meaning.
- **Spec-ahead-of-impl ([#4085](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4085) stays open as the tracker):** the compiler accepts the form. In `src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp`, the function-value call check (the `#1093 / §5.1` block, `:3745-3793` at `511e576`; the guard at `:3767-3773`) marks any call carrying a named, modifier or discard argument `simple = false` and *defers* it — so a named argument also skips the arity report and the `checkAssignable` loop that the positional form gets, both inside `if (simple)` — and lowering binds by position — that half is #4085's measured run (exit `52` = `Sub(2, 100)`), not a source read. The catch-up is one arm: reject a named argument at a function-typed callee with the §27.1 diagnostic, the shape of #2758's index-position arm (`ExprTC::checkIndexArgsPositional`, `src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Exprs.cpp:1007`, its named-argument half at `:1055-1073`, invoked at `:8210`), plus a lit row and a behavior test pinning that `caller(b := 2, a := 100)` is rejected, not swapped.
- **Compiler claims are source reads** — no build exists in the authoring environment; the sema citations were read at `511e576`, not run.
- **Kernel classification: no contact** (§28/§30.5 untouched). **Body-locality: local** — a call-site check on the argument form.
- **Diagnostic couplings:** none — the diagnostic is new; §23.5's `"index arguments are positional-only"` text and its pins are unchanged.
- **Doc-only:** 4 spec edits (§27.1 one paragraph; §22.5 one sentence; §27.7 one sentence; Appendix A.4's `Argument` comment one clause), 1 code-generation-reference edit + pin (→ v0.295: §7.1 one WRONG/right pair), 2 `DECLINED.md` rows (`rejected`). Stdlib, rationale, guides: no contact (companion headers only). Corpus (#1380): no action — the spec paragraph carries no code block; the two code-generation-reference §7.1 blocks that gain a line are the committed `codegen_0043`/`codegen_0044` cases, both `skip:literal-listing` in `tests/conformance/manifest.tsv` (never compiled), and #1380 forbids regenerating the corpus as a side effect of a docs edit.
- **Issues:** [#4085](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4085) is answered by this ruling and remains open as the compiler tracker.
- **Gate round (adversarial critique, one pass, 2026-09-08): LAND-WITH-CORRECTIONS — 4 blocking, 6 corrections, 9 notes; every one applied or declined with a reason, none dropped.** The central argument survived refutation: §27.1.1's assignability bullets key on slots, never on a name, and §27.1's same-type statement is the licence to drop or relabel. What bit: two source citations pointed at the wrong code (the `simple` guard is at `:3767-3773`, the index-position arm is `checkIndexArgsPositional` at `:1007`); §22.5's first draft enumerated the admitting sites and so closed choice-case construction (§35.3, *as to a parameter list*) by omission — reworded to the two exclusions, with that site left open as it was; the rule as drafted did not reach the null-conditional invocation `e?(…)` over a nullable function type (§27.2) — now named, with a pointer from §27.7 (note N1 taken); the retyping ground cited §27.1.1 where §27.1 is the authority; the migration under-reported that in-order named calls, correct today, stop compiling; the corpus note asserted an absence two `skip:literal-listing` cases disprove; and the code-generation pair did not show `caller` to be a function value. Declined: N2 (a comment on A.4's `FuncParamType` — the `Argument` comment already carries the cross-reference).
