### v0.296 changelog (v0.295 → v0.296)

**Rulings train: how a method-reference argument ranks at an overloaded callee ([#4088](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4088)), a parameter-count mismatch at a function-typed slot ([#4089](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4089)), an `async` lambda's wrapper at a return slot with a free type parameter ([#4090](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4090)), a result-discarding lambda at a procedure slot (found in §22.6 while ruling #4088), and the written-declared-type position family named once ([#3821](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3821)).** Four rulings (one folded from §22.6's own text), one clarification riding the second, one editorial that names a family once; no design change.

- **§22.6/§27.6/§14.5 — a method-reference argument ranks as a lambda literal does (ruling; #4088).** §22.6 spelled exact-versus-converting for lambda literals only; §27.6's exact-preferred ranking runs the other way (which overload of the *reference* is selected against one target — Appendix C.1's "mirrored"). **Decided:** a method-reference argument is formed per candidate against that candidate's (substituted) parameter type and ranks at the callee as a lambda literal does — *applicable* when formation succeeds under §27.6's criteria (signature equality, or a formation-site adapter for a §5.1 conversion at a parameter or return slot — `Task<Todo?>` at a `Task` slot is the ordinary derived-to-base reference conversion — with modifier slots exact and §27.1.1's family boundary respected), *exact* when the selected signature equals the slot slot for slot after substitution, *converting* otherwise; where §27.6's exact-preferred ranking finds no unique winner against a candidate's slot, formation fails at that candidate and it drops out — §27.6's ambiguity is reported only at a single target; where two candidates are exact at a reference position the explicit-cast remedy is inexpressible, and the diagnostic names the reference remedies (an explicit type-argument list, or a lambda spelling the overload). Stated as a new §22.6 paragraph (*Method-reference arguments*), cross-cited from §27.6's exact-preferred paragraph and from §14.5 phase 2's method-reference sentence; §22.6's no-candidates sentence now names the four ways a candidate is unreachable. The issue's case resolves: `Get<A, R>(route, (A) -> Task<R>)` is exact for `GetById: (int) -> Task<Todo?>` and `Get<A>(route, (A) -> Task, status := 204)` converts, so the first is unambiguously better before the defaulted-arity tie-break is reached. **Declined:** ranking every reference position as converting/co-equal because "a reference has no static type", and ranking it exact whenever formation succeeds — both discard the information §27.6 already computes in the mirror direction (one `DECLINED.md` row). **Folded in from the same section (incidental, ruled here):** §22.6 said only that at a procedure slot "§27.3's value/procedure classification decides", and §27.3 admits, for procedure lambdas, an expression body "whose result is discarded" — a target-driven form whose applicability and rank at an overloaded call were unstated. Decided: an expression-bodied lambda whose body is not of type `()` is applicable at a `-> ()` slot as that result-discarding form and ranks *converting* there; a unit-typed body or a `: ()` ascription is exact; a block-bodied lambda that returns a value is inapplicable — `M(f: () -> ())` beside `M(f: () -> int)` on `M(lambda() => 42)` resolves to the second; for an `async` lambda at a `-> Task` slot §30.6's closed-slot conformance decides instead (a valued body does not conform to `Task`). The discarded result is under §21.9's expression-statement regime, stated at §27.3's sentence — a warning for a copyable, `string`, runtime-managed or trivial-dispose result, the hard error directing to `_ :=`/`using var _ :=` in a block body for a non-trivial-dispose class, interface-typed or `Task`-family result (§17.13) — so no owned production is dropped silently and §28 is not amended. Declined: inapplicable-unless-unit, and ranking the discarding bridge exact (one `DECLINED.md` row).
- **§14.5/§22.6/§27.1.1 — a parameter-count mismatch at a function-typed slot makes the candidate inapplicable (ruling; #4089), and §27.1.1 says its rules presuppose equal counts (clarification).** §14.5's function-typed bullet said "unifies component-wise" and never "arity". **Decided:** unification over a function type of a different parameter count reaches nothing — an inference failure, so the candidate drops out under *Interaction with overloading*, never an error at that candidate; the same at a non-generic candidate for a function-typed value, a lambda literal, or a method reference (§22.6, its own paragraph *Parameter count at a function-typed position*). §27.1.1's opening sentence now states what its slot-wise bullets presupposed and the compiler has always enforced (`src/sema/ExprTypecheck.cpp:4363-4367`, "Arity mismatch is never assignable (§27.1.1), formation or not"; the lit pin `tests/lit/sema/function_type_assignability_1544__arity_mismatch_rejected_spec_27_1_1.bzl`). **Declined:** a hard error at the candidate (one `DECLINED.md` row) — it would make an overload family keyed on function-typed arity (0002 §3; stdlib §6.8's `Domain.Spawn` forms) unusable by design.
- **§30.6 — an `async` lambda's wrapper comes from its ascription, else a closed target slot, else its own body; at a free `Task<R>` slot a fresh-owned-class body is inapplicable (ruling; #4090).** §30.6 deferred to §30.1's list of admissible declared types, which names no source for a lambda's wrapper. **Decided (reading (b) of the two the issue weighed):** (1) an ascription names the wrapper; (2) any closed function-typed target's return slot names it — a closed head binds nothing, so reading it is reading a declared type, not an inference — and the body conforms under §30.1/§30.5 as an `async` method's body conforms to its declared type: a fresh owned class result is admitted under `Task<C>` (Pattern A, kind 1) and under `OwningTask<C>` (Pattern B) alike, so the target decides, a valued body does not conform to a plain `Task`, and two closed overload candidates differing only in the wrapper are both exact and fall to the ambiguity, remedied by an ascription; (3) with no target, or a return slot still holding a free type parameter, the body alone decides by §30.6's own sentence, and that type unifies against the slot under §14.5 phase 2: `OwningTask<C>` reaches no instantiation of `Task<T>` (§30.3, v0.295: siblings under `Task`), so the `Task<R>` candidate is inapplicable and an `OwningTask<C>`-slotted sibling applies. The head of a free slot is never read as the wrapper. Consequence for proposal 0002: its raw arm `Get<A>(route, (A) -> OwningTask<HttpResponse>)` is *uniquely* applicable to `async lambda(req: HttpRequest) => Http.Text("ok")` without the classic non-generic member's help; that member stays for the unannotated `async lambda(req) => …` (its parameter needs a closed slot) — 0002 §3's listing comment, §7 Q3 and §9(f) item 3 take a companion edit at the proposal's next pass. **Declined:** target-directed selection at a free slot (a target-directed inference §14.5 does not have; it would make one body's wrapper depend on the candidate under trial) and a blanket explicit-type-argument requirement at such slots (over-rejects the value-typed body that binds `R` cleanly) — one `DECLINED.md` row.
- **§17.7/§4.2/§5.1/§35.3/§14.5 — the written-declared-type positions named once, subsets by reference (editorial; #3821 closes).** §17.7 gains the family (anchor `sec-written-declared-type-positions`): (i) typed field initializer, (ii) typed local initializer (binding-atom clauses included), (iii) default parameter value, (iv) typed assignment target, (v) the declared-result positions of §35.3 as that section defines them (the `async` result-type reading included), and (vi) an argument at a determined parameter type. The three readings #3821 held open: **reading 1** — the narrow one, which the issue itself offered and proposal 0122 L17 specified: §17.7's return position is the `return e;` statement alone, stated explicitly as excluding an expression body and an ascribed lambda's return (the case reading takes all three; this shorthand takes only the statement) — no extent moves, and the wide reading is recorded `deferred` (§22.2 and §27.3 define the declared-result equivalence for §35.3's case reading, not for this shorthand, so widening is a design change); **reading 2** — already settled by v0.288 L5 (§4.2's "parameter" is the call argument and the default argument), restated by reference with §4.2's and §5.1's lists kept **open** — illustrative, "the governing rule remains §5.1's"; **reading 3** — corrected: §17.7's subset is (i), (ii), (iii) and the `return` statement of (v), excluding typed assignment targets *and* argument positions, exactly as §14.5's derivation clause ("§17.7's `new()`-shorthand contexts, extended by typed assignments and determined argument positions") has said all along — 0122's "all but argument position" was the error. §14.5 keeps its own list and its derivation clause, annotated by reference (no widening); §35.3 names its subset as group (v) alone. Proposal 0122's L17 — withdrawn at graduation as an editorial with "§14.5 stays out; no widening; no extent changes" — is superseded by this editorial, which lands the family it proposed on exactly those terms. Widening the shorthand to assignment targets or arguments is the second `deferred` row (rationale §9.11's evidence bar); rationale §9.11 and `DECLINED.md`'s `Ok(3)`-at-a-typed-local deferral are unaffected — the case reading's extent does not move.

**Migration.**

### v0.297 changelog (v0.296 → v0.297)

**Three rulings and one editorial: value kinds admit no dispatch modifier — records join enums and choices, and all three now say *member* ([#4061](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4061)); §9.8's serialized-name uniqueness reaches enum constants and choice cases ([#3863](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3863)); §31.1's *may outlive the arm* is defined as §28.3's rule with the arm as the source's scope ([#3569](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3569), open as the implementation tracker); §22.7's rule 1 says *declaring type* ([#4069](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4069)).**

- **§9.2 — dispatch modifiers on record members (ruling; #4061).** §10.5 states, for enums, that methods "may not be declared `virtual`, `abstract`, or `sealed override`", that `override` is admitted "only on the `Object`-virtual members … with the same admission a record body has for them", and why — "implicitly sealed (no inheritance) and have no virtual-dispatch surface of their own, so the dispatch modifiers carry no meaning". §9.6 says "Records are implicitly sealed" and §9 stated no rule; the compiler accepts `public virtual method Peek()` on a record with no diagnostic (the issue's measured repro). **Decided:** a record member may not be declared `virtual`, `abstract`, or `sealed override`; `override` is admitted only on `Equals` (the `Equals(Object?)` spelling and the co-declared `Equals(T)`), `GetHashCode`, and `ToString` and rejected on every other member, whatever its kind — its own §9.2 subsection (*Dispatch modifiers*, anchor `sec-record-dispatch-modifiers`, placed before the equality subsection), with one clause in §9.6, one sentence in §10.5 and one clause in §35.2 so the three value kinds state one rule, and one row in Appendix A's over-admission index (the grammar's shared `Member` production admits the tokens; §9.2 rejects them). **Made true for the other two kinds in the same revision:** §10.5's "Enum methods" and §35.2's "Choice methods" now read *members*, and Appendix A's enum/choice row names every member and non-trio `override` — an enum's or choice's expression-bodied property (§10.4, §35.2) was grammar-admitted and unreached by the method-keyed sentences, so `public virtual property Name: string => …` on an enum was accepted-and-inert, the posture this ruling declines. Bare `sealed` on any member was already §12.4's error; the rule adds `sealed override`. **Declined:** admitting the modifiers as inert, or with a warning (`DECLINED.md`) — an inert modifier is the inert-looking-but-load-bearing annotation §9.8 and §9.2 already refuse, and a warning would be a third posture where enums and choices reject.
- **§9.8 — serialized-name uniqueness reaches enum constants and choice cases (ruling; #3863).** The clause read "unique among the serialized names of the type's **components**" while the subsection's opening distinguishes components from enum members, so `enum E  A serialized "x", B serialized "x"; end E;` was undecided. **Decided:** the clause reaches enum constants and choice cases — a serialized name is the rename where declared and the identifier otherwise, so a rename equal to another member's identifier collides too — because its purpose does: two constants under one wire name make the read direction ambiguous. Its scope is stated with it: a choice's payload fields are unique within their **case** (two cases' payload fields never share a wire object — the pre-edit clause was silent on this, and the subsection's lead-in now names choice cases and payload fields among the clause's positions), an enum's constants among themselves, a choice's cases among themselves; names are compared **ordinally** (the constructor-matching rule beside it is case-insensitive, and the two are now told apart). Not relaxed for same-valued aliases (§10.2): the write side already uses the first-declared name, so the second alias's rename could never be written. **Declined:** the component-only reading with a first-declared-wins read, and the alias carve (`DECLINED.md`).
- **§31.1 — which closures *may outlive the arm* (ruling; #3569 stays open).** §31.1 said the catch binding "may not be … captured by a closure that may outlive the arm" and defined "may outlive" nowhere; fix #3546's lambda-body driver over-approximated it syntactically, rejecting a returned closure over the binding anywhere in a lambda body. **Decided:** the term is §28.3's closure-capture rule read with the arm body as the source's scope — a closure over the binding may outlive the arm exactly when its **value** can leave the arm (returned from the method, or from a lambda whose own value can leave the arm, recursively; assigned to a binding declared outside the arm — an enclosing block's local, an `out`/`ref` parameter — or stored in an instance or static field or a collection reachable beyond the arm; passed to a `scoped` position whose bounding object (§28.14) outlives the arm, or to a deferred-activation callee whose frame leaves the arm; captured by such a closure; or reaching a position §30.11, §30.14 or §32.8 governs by its own capture rule) — and, **in particular**, a closure is confined to the arm exactly under §28.3's three admitted forms: immediate invocation, a `using var` local of function type declared inside the arm (§28.9), or an argument to a call-bounded parameter (§28.14), at any lambda nesting depth. **A closure bound to a plain local is not admitted — §28.3's list is closed and §31.1 adds no fourth form.** Consequence stated honestly: #3569's `over1.bzl` *as written* (`var mk`/`var g`) stays rejected — on §28.3's authority, not the pre-pass's — and its `using var` spelling (the paragraph's worked example) is the admitted one. **Declined:** the syntactic reading as the rule, a blanket rejection, and the plain-local fourth form stated in §31.1 alone — the last a §28.3 widening, a design change needing a §6 proposal (`DECLINED.md`). The compiler's pre-pass is recorded as a **conservative implementation** of the rule (it accepts nothing the rule rejects) with its narrowing tracked at #3569; the compiler's *admission* of plain-local-bound closures over borrows in general is the separate impl-ahead-of-spec delta below.
- **§22.7 — *declaring type* in rule 1 (editorial; #4069).** The *Observing `this` during construction* subsection said "the declaring class" three times where rule 1 (the observation gate) is generic across the type kinds with a §7.9 obligation — records included, as fixes #4001/#4014 established against §9.4's *Constructor bodies are not receiver positions* — and only rule 2 (virtual dispatch) is class-only. Rule 1's two occurrences now read "the declaring type", rule 2's stays, the lead-in sentence says which rule reaches which kind (rule 3 as stated, for both), and the three restatements of rule 1 move with it — Appendix C.5's row, §22.16's constructor-`requires` sentence (constructor-only records carry such clauses, §9.9), and §22.10's chaining-position sentence (a record constructor may `this(...)`-chain; the compiler's `runRecordConstructor` seeds the chain) — and §12.8's "`this(...)` chains to another constructor in the same class" now says *type*, its `base(...)` wording staying class-only.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected (in the spec's terms):** `virtual`, `abstract`, or `sealed override` on any record member, and `override` on a record member outside `Equals`/`GetHashCode`/`ToString` — **programs the compiler accepts today** (`virtual` measured by #4061; non-trio `override` by source read: `checkHidingAndOverride` walks `Class` kinds only, `src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:4927`); `virtual`/`abstract`/`sealed override`, and non-trio `override`, on an enum's or a choice's expression-bodied **property** — accepted today, since `checkEnumRestrictions` and `checkChoiceDispatchModifiers` test `MethodSymbol` only (`:846`, `:982`); a serialized-name collision among an enum's constants or a choice's cases — likewise accepted today (no §9.8 uniqueness check exists for any kind; the only uniqueness check in the serialization pass is the `polymorphic` registry's, `:10053-10078`). In-tree: two test rows in `tests/sema/record_ctor_this_observation_gate_4014_test.cpp` (`:351-370`, `:376-395`) declare `public virtual method Peek()` on a record — one asserts the program is *accepted and runs*; and `tests/lit/sema/sema_record_base_restrictions__record_extends_abstract_class_diagnoses.bzl:8` declares a non-trio `override method Compute()` on a record (its `CHECK` rows are unanchored searches for the §9.6 diagnostic, so the row survives a second diagnostic). All three are re-authored under the tracking issue below. No documentation example carries a dispatch modifier on a value-kind member. **Newly accepted (in the spec's terms):** a closure over a catch binding confined to the arm under §28.3's three forms — `using var`-bound, immediately invoked, or call-bounded — inside any nesting of lambdas: the compiler's pre-pass rejects the returned-from-a-lambda spelling today (#3569); and a closure over the binding passed to a **builtin or standard-library** call-bounded position (including a deferred-activation callee whose frame is consumed inside the arm): `verifiedCallBoundedFormalAt` trusts user-authored callees only (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:17920-17923`, `if (!formals.methSym || !args) return false;`; the legacy-rejection note at `:4295-4299`), so the compiler treats these as escaping. **Newly defined:** §31.1's escape test; §9.8's serialized-name definition (rename or identifier), its per-case scope, and its ordinal comparison. **Newly warned:** nothing.
- **Impl-ahead-of-spec (process §5 item 3b):** the compiler admits a capture-bearing closure over a **borrow** bound to a **plain** local at the same or a deeper block than the source — `checkBorrowStoreEscape` flags a plain-local target only when its block *strictly encloses* the source's (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:7226-7233`: "A target at the same or a deeper block dies no later than the source, so it is not an escape"; `:7254-7262`), and `hasLambda` there only chooses the diagnostic's wording — while §28.3's closure-capture bullet admits three forms and a plain local is none of them. This is general to every borrow (a borrowed local or parameter, a catch binding), not catch-specific; the two catch-arm "clean control" rows `tests/ownership/catch_escape_test.cpp:333-345` and `:581-597` (`var f := lambda() => Use(ex); n := f();`) pin the divergent admission. Tracked as [#4154](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4154) — the owner's call whether the closed list is enforced or reopened by proposal; this revision states the list as it stands.
- **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** (1) records — `checkEnumRestrictions` (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:754-878`, gated `TypeDeclKind::Enum` at `:769`) and `checkChoiceDispatchModifiers` (`:977-1001`, gated `Choice`) each carry the dispatch-modifier sub-check with the trio predicate `isObjectVirtualReplacementMember` (`:746-752`), over `MethodSymbol` only; no record twin exists, and the record-only checks at `:1495-1560` reject `abstract record` and destructors, not member modifiers — the catch-up is one helper the three kinds call, over methods, properties and indexers, walked by `forEachTypeAndNested` (not the module-children loop `checkRecordRestrictions` uses, `:1491-1493` — the #3601 nested-type hole), tracked as [#4152](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4152) (whether `abstract` on a record member already draws the §12.5 obligation loop's "does not implement" report — that loop walks records beside classes, `:5388-5416` — is a probe, not asserted). (2) §9.8 uniqueness — no check for components, enum constants, or choice cases; the enum read is a first-match chain in declaration order (`src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Serialization.cpp:1759-1800`), so a collision silently resolves to the first-declared constant today — tracked as [#4153](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4153). (3) §31.1 — three drivers feed the pre-pass: `checkLambdaBodyEscapes` (`src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:8329-8336`), `checkLambdaBodyEscapesExpr` (`:8340`, the `=> E` sibling) and `checkOneLambdaBodyEscapes` (`:8385-8417`), whose header comment (`:8284-8328`; "⚠ DELIBERATELY CONSERVATIVE" at `:8303`, "Issue 3569 tracks narrowing this" at `:8318`) records the over-approximation; every lambda-body `return` goes through `scanCatchBorrowClosureReturns` (`:8706-8710`) into `checkClosureEscapesOnReturn` (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:4273`, the §31.1 leg at `:4426-4445`) with `EscapeScope::LambdaBody`; the assignment channel is `checkBorrowStoreEscape`'s `Dest::OuterLocal` arm (`:6873`, `:7444-7475`). The name the issue cites, `checkCatchBorrowClosureEscapesInOneLambda`, was #3546's and was renamed by #3564/#3565 (`57e2faf`). #3569 stays open as the tracker: narrow the three drivers to lambdas whose own value escapes, so the `using var` spelling compiles; the `var` spelling then owes #4154's rejection, not this one's.
- **Compiler claims are source reads** — no build exists in the authoring environment; every `src/` and `tests/` citation above was read at `5693331`, not run.
- **Kernel classification:** §9.2/§9.8/§22.7 — no contact. §31.1 — **derivation**: the new paragraph instantiates §28.3's closure-capture bullet (*Borrow lifetime rules*, an instance of K2.3's bounded-escape rule over K2.1's source, here the runtime's in-flight exception with the arm body as its scope) and §28.14's bounding-object forms, and adds no capture form; no kill is added, the consume table and the axiom register are untouched. **Body-locality: local** for all three rules — §9.2 and §9.8 read the declaration; §31.1's escape test is one body's flow (K5's "body-local by construction" clause), a callee's retention being read off its signature (`scoped`, a deferred-activation return type), never its body. §22.7: not applicable (editorial).
- **Diagnostic couplings:** none of the pinned strings move. `"enums dispatch statically (§10.5)"` (3 lit rows under `tests/lit/sema/sema_enum*`; the gtest twin they cite, `tests/sema/enum_restrictions_test.cpp`, no longer exists — ported to lit) and `"choices dispatch statically (§35.2)"` are unchanged; the record diagnostic is new text. `"returned closure captures the caught exception"` (`tests/ownership/catch_escape_test.cpp`, 7 rows; `tests/ownership/localdecl_bare_const_arms_3591_test.cpp`) is unchanged. The pinned row `catch_escape_closure.lambda_confined_to_arm_over_rejected_known_3569_31_1` (`catch_escape_test.cpp:621-655`) **does not flip**: its program (`var mk`/`var g`) stays rejected by §28.3's closed list — its comment ("FLIPS to `BEZEL_EXPECT_FALSE`" when #3569 lands) is re-authored to say the verdict is right and the reason wrong, and a sibling row with the `using var` spelling is added expecting acceptance once #3569 lands; the two clean-control rows at `:333` and `:581` are re-labelled as #4154's pins. §22.7's `"cannot observe `this`"` is unchanged. ### v0.298 changelog (v0.297 → v0.298)

**Design change, graduated by owner ruling: a closure is a borrow-carrying value, admitted wherever such a value is admitted — §28.3's closed three-form closure-capture list is replaced by the source-set rule ([#4154](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4154); proposal 0126, ruled under the owner's 2026-09-10 delegation: "rule on #4154 without regarding the implementation; the implementation will change to match").** One rule replaces one list at four carriers; the storage and return sinks that were never open stay closed; §31.1's confined-closure paragraph is restated under it, with #3569's program as written as its worked example.

- **§28.3 — the closure bullet becomes the source-set rule (design change; #4154 closes).** Through v0.297 the bullet read "A borrowed local may not be captured by a closure that may outlive the borrow's source. Capture is permitted for closures that are immediately invoked, closures bound to a `using var` local of function type, and closures passed as an argument to a function-typed parameter"; §28.14 restated "three escape forms", §28.9 said the `using var` on a function-typed local "serves only the §28.3 capture-scoping and non-reassignability roles", and the code-generation reference taught the same closed list. **Decided:** the headline sentence stays as the definition site of *may outlive*; whether a closure may is decided by its **source set**, read off provenance — a lambda literal or method reference contributes the sources of the borrows it captures (a borrowed local or parameter its source, an owned local its enclosing scope, a captured function value its own set transitively, a bound receiver as a capture; a lambda's captures include the outward-resolving free bindings of every lambda nested in its body); a local or parameter the union of the sets it is traced to, a plain function-typed parameter's set being unannounced (K2.4) and so call-bounded as before; **invoking** a function value yields a value carrying the invoked value's set (a lambda's body can return a closure only over what the lambda captures, its own locals being scope-bound; a method's function-typed return is borrow-free by construction, so a method call's result carries the empty set); a field or collection read the empty set (those holders admit only capture-free values); anything else untraceable an unannounced source. Every §28.3 borrow rule then applies by that set with no closure-specific list: bound to a local (plain `var` or `using var`) whose scope does not strictly enclose any source's scope, back edges included (an initializer is admitted by construction; each assignment to a plain function-typed local is checked on its own, a later read carrying the union); immediately invoked; captured by another closure transitively; passed to a function-typed parameter under §28.14's tiers; and — **while its source set is non-empty — not stored in a field, in any collection, or through an `out`/`ref` parameter, and not returned from the method**, on K2.4's ground (a function type announces no source set, so no holder outside the body can re-establish it and no caller bound it — the ground §28.14 already states for a received callback), the only storage route for a capture-bearing closure staying §28.14's `scoped` admission. A `return` inside a lambda leaves only that lambda: a closure returned there over an outer binding carries only sources the enclosing value already carries. The former three forms are consequences, not a list; `using var` on a function-typed local keeps the non-reassignability role only (§28.9 — what §28.10 had said all along: "the only effect is the reassignability restriction"); §28.14's lead names the general admission and defines the argument form's two variants, its *v1 admission bounds* item 3 keeping the narrower verifiable-argument list at `scoped` call sites; the method-reference bullet names its source set (`obj`'s); the borrow-return bullets' item 5 points at the closure bullet for a returned function value's carried borrows; *Deferred-activation callees*' traced-forms list gains the invocation form and its read-from-elsewhere clause says *a method call's result*. **Grounds:** uniformity (the local-scope bullet already decides every other borrow-holding local by structural scope comparison; §28.9 already framed the closure as a borrow-carrier); soundness unchanged (the sinks stay closed, so §28.3's capture-set contribution — "borrow-free by construction" — rationale §5.25, §28.14's asymmetry and the v0.177 record stay true verbatim); ergonomics (a local helper lambda over a borrow needs no `using var`); and the compiler implemented the scope comparison and the invocation provenance all along (below). **History:** the bullet as first written (2026-05-28) admitted closures "immediately invoked or whose lifetime is statically bounded by the borrow's source", naming the `using var` local and the extension parameter as instances; v0.177's rewrite enumerated the instances and dropped the criterion; §28.14 (v0.175) and §28.9 (v0.178) restated the enumeration; no changelog or rationale entry records a reason for excluding the plain local. **Declined:** the closed list with `using var` as the sole capture-scoping marker, and widening it by a fourth form only (one `DECLINED.md` row; rationale §4.2 carries the dated record; the v0.297 row *Syntactic reading of §31.1's …* is re-pointed at proposal 0126 — what it still declines is a §31.1-only statement of the admission); and, at the gate round, opening the storage/return sinks to a function value whose sources satisfy the object-borrow rules (proposal 0126 §2).
- **§31.1 — the confined forms restated (consequence).** The v0.297 paragraph's "exactly when the closure's value can leave the arm" test is unchanged; its "in particular" sentence now says a closure over the binding is confined to the arm whenever its value stays inside it under §28.3's rule — as it does when immediately invoked, bound to an arm-local (plain or `using var`), or passed to a call-bounded parameter, among other in-arm holders, at any lambda depth — and the sentences "§28.3's list is closed, and this section adds no fourth form" and "The same program with `var mk`/`var g` is rejected" are gone. The worked example is #3569's program as written (`var mk := lambda(): () -> int => do return lambda() => Use(ex); end; var g := mk(); total := g() + g();`), traced clause by clause: `mk`'s lambda carries `{ex}` through its nested lambda's free binding; `mk` is an arm-local — admitted; `mk()`'s result carries `{ex}` by the invocation clause and is bound to the arm-local `g` — admitted; `g()` is an immediate invocation; the counter-example `outer := mk();` into a local declared before the `try` is rejected by the local-scope bullet.

**Migration.**

- **Newly accepted (in the spec's terms):** a capture-bearing closure over a borrow bound to a **plain** local at the same or a deeper block than every source — the local helper lambda `var f := lambda() => Use(b); f();` over any borrowed local, parameter, or catch binding `b`; reassignment of such a local, each assignment checked on its own; a capture-bearing closure captured by another closure bound the same way; the result of invoking such a closure bound to a local (`var g := mk();`); and #3569's `over1.bzl` as written (the §31.1 example). Every one of these the compiler admits today except the last (below). **Newly rejected:** nothing — no program the v0.297 text admitted is rejected: the three forms are among the rule's consequences, and the storage and return sinks were closed to capture-bearing function values before ("admit a borrow-capturing closure into none of those locations", §28.3 *Deferred-activation callees*; "may not be stored at all", §28.14) and stay closed, a closure over `this` returned or field-stored included. **Newly defined:** the closure's source set and its provenance clauses (traced local, invocation result, field/collection read, unannounced), the sink rule's K2.4 ground, and the return-from-a-lambda clause. **Newly warned:** nothing.
- **Compiler status — the compiler is ahead of the old text and conforms to the new one for the general rule.** The only plain-local check is `checkBorrowStoreEscape`'s block-depth comparison (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:7226-7233`: "A target at the same or a deeper block dies no later than the source, so it is not an escape"; `depthOf` and the `td < sd` test at `:7255-7263`; `hasLambda` at `:7247-7255` chooses only the diagnostic's wording), which is the local-scope bullet applied to the closure's holder; the field, `out`/`ref`, and return sinks are the rules the 3744/3564 rows pin; the invocation-provenance clause is what fix #3702 implemented for the method-return leg (`:4310-4318` — `return mk();` "escaped the method through Mk()'s own return (a use-after-dispose measured as a SIGSEGV)"; #3702 closed 2026-09-04, its open half — whether the lambda's own value escapes — answered normatively here by the invocation clause and the local-scope bullet). Pinned rows that are now conformance pins rather than divergence pins: `tests/lit/ownership/closure_escape_outer_local_861__{same_scope_closure_accepted,inner_block_target_accepted}.bzl` (plain-local binding at the same or a deeper block admitted), `…_861__{escape_to_method_scope_local,escape_from_doubly_nested_block}_rejected.bzl` (assignment to an enclosing-block local rejected — the #861 SIGSEGV repro), `lambda_body_escape_3727__*`, `lambda_body_escape_3743__*` (the same inside lambda bodies), `lambda_body_escape_3744__{owned_local_closure_stored_into_field,owned_local_written_through_ref_param}_rejected.bzl` (the field and `ref` sinks), `lambda_body_escape_3564__owned_local_returned_closure_rejected.bzl` (a closure over a lambda-body-local returned from that lambda), and the catch-arm controls `tests/ownership/catch_escape_test.cpp:333-345`, `:581-597` (v0.297's "impl-ahead-of-spec" label on them is withdrawn). `…_3564__exprbody_lambda_over_method_local_accepted.bzl` is accepted *through an un-run check* — its own comment and `Ownership.cpp:8390-8399` say the lambda-body pre-pass clears its map rather than deciding the escape — so it corroborates the return-from-a-lambda clause's verdict without pinning the rule. #4154's probe — whether a `LocalDecl` initializer reaches the depth test — is moot: an initializer can never cross scopes. **What the compiler still owes is #3569's alone:** the catch-arm pre-pass — `checkLambdaBodyEscapes` (`src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:8329`), `checkLambdaBodyEscapesExpr` (`:8340`), `checkOneLambdaBodyEscapes` (`:8385`; the header comment `:8284-8328` records the over-approximation, quotes the §31.1 example at `:8309-8313`, and names the issue at `:8318`) — still rejects the returned-from-a-lambda shape syntactically, so the §31.1 example is rejected today with "returned closure captures the caught exception `ex`". No new tracking issue is filed. One probe rides with #3569, recorded because the text's rejection may be unimplemented: whether the method-level return leg (`checkClosureEscapesOnReturn`, `Ownership_Checks.cpp:4272`) rejects a closure over `this` returned through a plain function-typed return — it walks identifier captures resolved through `states_` and the catch-borrow flag, and the file has no `ThisExpr` handling, so the rejection §28.3 has always stated (*Deferred-activation callees*: none of those locations admits a borrow-capturing closure) is likely not enforced there; a pre-existing delta, not one this revision creates, owed its own issue if the probe confirms it.
- **Compiler claims are source reads** — no build exists in the authoring environment; every `src/` and `tests/` citation above was read at `bbd37bf`, not run.
- **Kernel classification: derivation** — the closure bullet becomes an explicit instance of K2.1 (a holder bounded by its weakest source), K2.2 (union under composition: the producers-table row *Captured borrow inside a closure* already classifies each capture as a re-borrow of the captured binding's source, and a holder of several is bounded by all), K2.3 (bounded escape — every sink the bullet names is the list's existing rule), and K2.4 (a function type announces no source set → the storage/return sinks stay closed and a received callback is call-bounded); no kernel text moves, no kill is added, the consume table and the axiom register — A5 (`using var` as scope pin: the pin is §28.10's borrow-pin over a borrow initializer, which a function value is not) and A11 (§28.14's forms) included — are untouched. **Body-locality: local** — the rule reads one body's scopes, its flow-traced provenance, and the callee signatures at its call sites (K5's "body-local by construction" clause), never a callee's body.
- **Diagnostic couplings:** no pinned string moves — `"closure capturing `rr` is assigned to `f`, which outlives it"` (`Ownership_Checks.cpp:7506-7508`; the `_861`, `_3727`, `_3743` and the `_2144`/`_2180` record/choice lit rows), `"returned closure captures `r` whose source is disposed at scope end"` (`_3564`), `"borrow of `r` stored into a field would outlive its source"` (`_3743`, `_3744`), `"returned closure captures the caught exception"` (`Ownership_Checks.cpp:4439-4440`; `catch_escape_test.cpp`, 7 rows; `localdecl_bare_const_arms_3591_test.cpp`) are unchanged. The pinned row `catch_escape_closure.lambda_confined_to_arm_over_rejected_known_3569_31_1` (`catch_escape_test.cpp:637-655`) now pins an over-rejection the spec no longer licenses: it keeps `BEZEL_EXPECT_TRUE` until #3569 lands and then **flips** to `BEZEL_EXPECT_FALSE` — its original comment (`:621-636`) was right, and v0.297's instruction to re-author it as "right verdict, §28.3's reason" is withdrawn; the `using var`-spelled sibling v0.297 asked for is still worth adding (both spellings expect acceptance). The `:333`/`:581` controls are re-labelled as §28.3 v0.298 pins. **Spec-quote couplings** (comments citing the deleted sentence as authority, re-authored when next touched): `tests/ownership/lambda_body_escape_test.cpp:40`, `:466` (its row binds a closure to a plain local and cited "immediately invoked" — now grounded in the local-scope bullet), `tests/lit/ownership/lambda_body_escape_3564__owned_local_closure_invoked_in_lambda_accepted.bzl:6`.
- **Doc-only:** 8 spec edits at 4 sites (§28.3: the closure bullet's head, the method-reference bullet's clause, the borrow-return item 5's clause, *Deferred-activation callees*' traced-forms list and read-from-elsewhere clause; §28.9 one clause; §28.14 the lead paragraph's first two sentences; §31.1 one paragraph with its fenced example rewritten in place), 1 code-generation-reference bullet (§4.4) + pin (→ **v0.298**), 1 rationale paragraph (§4.2, dated), 1 `DECLINED.md` row added (`rejected`) and 1 amended (two cells of the v0.297 §31.1 row), proposal 0126 created with its README ledger row (graduated table). Stdlib: companion header only. Fences: §31.1's one fence edited in place (EXTRACT count unchanged at 514). Guides: no contact — no guide teaches the closed list; Guide 02 §5's "capture it in a closure that outlives the arm" is the general rule; no pin moves. Corpus (#1380): no case transcribes the closed list or §31.1's v0.297 fence (the corpus predates it), so nothing is re-transcribed; the next regeneration should note that §31.1's fence is now a reject-today program (the #3569 pre-pass) on the extraction path — `blocked-on-#3569`, not a failure.
- **Issues:** [#4154](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4154) closes with the citation (spec §28.3, v0.298; proposal 0126); [#3569](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3569) receives a corrected comment — its v0.297 comment said the `var` spelling is rejected by §28.3, which this revision reverses — and stays open as the pre-pass tracker; [#3702](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3702) (closed) receives a loop-closing comment naming the invocation clause as the normative answer to its open half; no new issue is filed.
- **Gate round (adversarial critique, one pass, 2026-09-10): LAND-WITH-CORRECTIONS — 3 blocking, 12 corrections, 7 notes; every blocking and correction applied, every note applied or recorded, none dropped.** Blocking: the first draft's sink clause ("unless every source satisfies the corresponding rule") admitted a capture-bearing closure into a plain field, a collection, or a function-typed return whenever its captures were receiver- or parameter-sourced — falsifying §28.3's own capture-set contribution ("borrow-free by construction"), rationale §5.25, §28.14's recorded asymmetry and the v0.177 record (resolved, the coordinator's call: the sinks stay closed to every function value with a non-empty source set, on K2.4's ground; a closure over `this` returned or field-stored is a rejection, as before); the source set was defined only for values the body authors — nothing said what the result of invoking a function value carries, so §31.1's example rested on an unstated step and, read at its smallest, `outer := mk();` into a local declared outside the arm would have been admitted — a use-after-free v0.297 rejected and #3702 had measured as a SIGSEGV (resolved: the headline sentence restored as the definition site of *may outlive*; a provenance rule — traced local, invocation result carrying the invoked value's set, field/collection read empty, otherwise unannounced — with the nested-lambda capture premise stated; *Deferred-activation callees*' traced-forms list gains the invocation form; the example re-traced clause by clause with the counter-example named); the Migration's "Newly rejected: nothing / no new tracker" and two probes recorded admissions the text could not support (resolved: with the sinks closed the two are rejections and the entry is honest; the one surviving probe — whether the method-level return leg enforces the `this` rejection — is recorded as pre-existing and routed to #3569). Corrections applied: revision narration removed from three normative sentences (bare `v0.298` pins); §31.1's "in particular" sentence no longer reads exhaustive ("as it does when … among other in-arm holders") and the vacuous scope qualifier is gone; the caller-side clause stated once; the owned-local contribution cites the producers row and the K2.1/K2.2 gloss is correct; §28.14's *v1 admission bounds* item 3 named as the narrower `scoped`-site list; one sink form; three test *comments* quoting the deleted sentence recorded as spec-quote couplings; the `_3564` expression-body row restated as accepted through an un-run check and #3702 given its loop-closing comment; the `DECLINED.md` bar cell leads with its bar; four line citations corrected (`:4439-4440`, `:4272`, `:7255-7263`, `:8309-8313`; `hasLambda :7247-7255`; rationale anchors `R:894`/`R:934`); the recorded grep restated so it reproduces.
