### v0.299 changelog (v0.298 → v0.299)

**A defect train: seventeen issues resolved and three findings withdrawn with reasons — and the finding-set is what an *executable* reading of the documents turned up, every one of the fifty-two issues in this family having been raised while writing the rule-keyed conformance corpus (`tests/conformance/rules`, landed separately, indexed by [#4383](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4383)) from the documents themselves. Five rulings decide cases the documents answered two ways: the non-auto-hashable use-site error is **per member** ([#4396](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4396)); a `serialized skip` component still binds its constructor parameter, and a nested record or choice component must declare the conformance itself ([#4398](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4398)); the trivial-dispose ceremony exemption is over the **obligation**, at every holder form ([#4400](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4400)); §28.10's borrow-pin drops *"not disposed"* ([#4413](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4413)); and the local half of definite assignment is keyed on **defaultable**, not on nullability ([#4362](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4362)). Two further rulings settle §29.7's completed state as the machine's own bookkeeping and make a second `Dispose()` a stated warning ([#4399](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4399)), and state at one width the rejection of bare `sealed` on a member ([#4374](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4374)).**

- **§9.2 — the non-auto-hashable use-site error is *per member*, and a declaration of that member lifts it (ruling; [#4396](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4396) closes).** Four passages disagreed, not the three the issue named. §9.2's use-site paragraph carved out *"without a user-defined override"*; Appendix C.1 stated the error unconditionally; §25.2's *"rather than the inherited box-identity one"* read as though the inherited member were simply reachable; and the fourth sat **inside §9.2 itself** — the second disqualifier's parenthetical swept the direct calls into the operator clause (*"`=`/`<>` (and the direct `.Equals`/`.GetHashCode` calls above) are a compile error unless the author also declares the `operator =`/`<>` overloads"*), a bullet reached only when the author *has* declared an override, so it said the override does not lift the error. **Decided: §9.2's per-member reading wins.** The error fires per member and does not fire for a member the record declares itself; the escape is a *declaration* of that member in either spelling, `override` or plain. **Grounds:** the losing reading makes §9.2's own recommended remedy inert — a record that follows the three-member instruction and stops short of the operator overloads would carry three members no record-typed receiver could ever call; the error's stated purpose is to stop a silent reference-equality fallthrough, which a declared member forecloses; body text governs an index of it; and the shipped compiler has always read it per member (below). **Losing text:** C.1's row gains the per-member clause and keeps its `Object`-receiver sentence; §9.2's disqualifier-2 parenthetical keeps the operator condition for `=`/`<>` alone and hands the direct calls to the use-site rule; §25.2 names the receiver that reaches the box-identity member; §9.3's combined-form sentence and §35.2's choice use-site sentence are re-pointed at the per-member rule. **Declined:** the unconditional reading — it would reject the shipped accept-control and strand §9.2's own remedy; reading the escape as the `override` spelling alone — §9.2's *Dispatch modifiers* subsection admits `override` on these members without requiring it, and the accept-control declares them plain; and deciding per-*signature* granularity, which no passage and no corpus case turns on (recorded below). **Body-locality: local** — the rule reads the receiver's own declaration surface at the call site and no other body. **Kernel: no contact.**
- **§9.8 — a `serialized skip` component binds its constructor parameter with `default(T)`, and a nested record or choice component must declare the conformance (ruling; [#4398](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4398) closes).** **Gap 1:** *Synthesized `Deserialize`* step 2 searched for the constructor *"whose parameter list binds exactly the serialized components"* while the `serialized skip` clause says the skipped component's `default(T)` is *"supplie[d] … to the constructor"* and the eligibility rule says a skipped field *"is no longer a serialized component"* — so a checker written from step 2 rejects every record that mixes `serialized skip` with an explicit constructor, at the conformance declaration. **Decided:** step 2 binds the record's components, the serialized ones *together with* every `serialized skip` one, which binds its `default(T)`. **Gap 2:** the component row defined the property structurally, so a record or choice shaped eligibly but declaring neither interface satisfied it on its face — while the synthesized bodies reach *"the nested value's `Serialize(s)`"* and *"the nested type's `Deserialize`"*, members only the conformance supplies. **Decided:** a record or choice component must itself declare `ISerializable`/`IDeserializable`, exactly as the **class** row in the same list already required; enums stay exempt, being always eligible and encoded as a name string rather than by a member call. **Grounds:** it is the only reading with a member to call; §3.6's own row already defines the property as *"records, enums, and value-like choices for which `Serialize`/`Deserialize` are synthesized"* and §9.8's opening makes synthesis conditional on the declaration, so the property was declaration-sensitive at its definition site and §9.8's structural restatement is the passage that drifted; and the alternative would make a type's wire form a consequence of another type's declaration, against §9.8's *"Declaring the conformance is the opt-in"*. **Term split, at the gate:** because the component predicate and the type-level property had been sharing one name while gap 2 gives them different content, the component rows are renamed **admissible as a serialized component** and *serialization-eligible* is left to the type-level property; §9.8's positional-record, body-record, class-eligibility and choice-eligibility sentences and Appendix C's `Shared<T>`/`Weak<T>` row move with the term, changing no rule. **Declined:** synthesizing an un-opted-in component's encoding at its use site. **Body-locality: local** — the check reads the component type's own inheritance clause at the enclosing type's conformance declaration. **Kernel: no contact.**
- **§28.9 — the ceremony exemption is over the obligation, not over the `new` expression (ruling; [#4400](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4400) closes).** Through v0.298 the first exemption bullet read *"A `new` expression of a trivial-dispose class type whose result is not stored in an `owned` location or `using var` does not produce the standard ownership-discharge warning"*, while §28.3's *Must-use warning*, §29.2's owning-iteration-variable clauses, §29.8's frame-disposal sentence, §30.1's `IOwningAsyncEnumerable` bullet and Appendix C.3's row all stated the warning with no trivial-dispose condition — so whether an `owned` parameter or an owning iteration variable of trivial-dispose type warned was undecided. **Decided:** no must-use / auto-drop diagnostic attaches to a trivial-dispose value at **any** holder form the warning attaches to — a plain-`var` owned local, an undischarged `owned` parameter (method, iterator, async), an owning iteration variable, and the unbound `new` result as before; the auto-drop itself is unconditional at every one of them. **The key was amended at the gate, and it is the load-bearing half:** the classification is read from the **produced type** where the drop site's value has a statically-known producer (a `new` expression, an `owned`-returning call — *statically-known producer* being §28.3's own notion, whose producers table already classifies every initializer), and from the **declared type** otherwise. An interface-typed binding is never exempt, its conformance set being open across modules (§21.9). **Grounds:** §28.9's own stated principle — *"a trivial-dispose class's disposal has none to announce"* — is about the obligation; its API-surface paragraph describes the flip as an instance that *"was freed silently now draws the must-use auto-drop warning"*, a claim about bindings; and **Appendix C.3 already stated the broad rule twice** (*"A trivial-dispose class has its discharge performed by the compiler — no warning"*; *"trivial-dispose values freed by the compiler with no demand on the program"*), as do Guide 01's opening and the code-generation reference. **Declined:** the narrow reading with §29.2 and §29.8 restated as explicitly unconditional — it would make §28.9's principle false at the positions where a trivial-dispose value most often sits, and contradict two normative Appendix C rows; and the draft's declared-type-only key, which would have exempted `var b: Base := new Derived();` at a trivial-dispose `Base` over a destructor-bearing `Derived` — the one shape the compiler was written to get right, and the direction that makes the exemption **type**-keyed where K1.6 states it of the **value**. **Kernel classification: derivation** — K1.6 (the empty *user-visible* obligation content §28.9 already cites as its derivation) + K3.14 (the affinity lint, whose kernel line now names the exemption); no kernel text moves, no kill is added, the consume table and the axiom register are untouched. **Body-locality: local** — the rule consumes the static type at the drop site and its §3.6-rule-2 derived property, and no per-body fact from any other body.
- **§28.10 — the borrow-pin drops "not disposed" (ruling; [#4413](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4413) closes).** The pin's sentence read *"the source must remain live (not moved, not disposed)"* while §28.3's consume-site freeze, §28.6's *Who may call `Dispose()`* and the consume table's K3.9 row all make disposing an owned binding under live borrows legal — the site-announced kill under its flag backstop. **This one is settled by a recorded decline, not by judgment.** Rationale §5.1's v0.180 record declines *"freezing explicit `Dispose()` too"* and records **one** exception, §28.14's storage admission; §28.3's *Diagnostics* names that same admission as *"the one exception"*; and K5's criterion says conjunct (ii) *"fails in exactly two recorded shapes, and in no other"*. §28.10's clause was therefore a second, undeclared exception to a closed set, and **keeping it would have been the design change**, not dropping it. **Decided:** the pin extends the borrow's *liveness* and the freeze then governs — the frozen kills (a move, a transfer, a reassignment of the binding) stay compile errors, the site-announced kills stay unfrozen, so an explicit `Dispose()` of the source is permitted and a later read through the pin raises `DisposedAccessException` in checked mode. **Declined:** making the pin a third recorded shape — it would reopen a closed enumeration for a case that has an admissible backstop (the kill flags the very object the pinned borrow references), which is exactly the criterion-(ii) test; if the owner intends `using var` to carry a *static* disposal guarantee the edit inverts and K5's enumeration opens to three with a recorded reason, but every piece of text read points the other way. **Kernel classification: derivation** — K5 (the freeze criterion) + K4.2/K5.3 (site-announced kills unfrozen) + K4.1 (the backstop); the two-recorded-shapes enumeration stays closed, and stopping §28.10 from silently adding a third is the edit's whole purpose. **Body-locality: local** (K5.5's body-local backward dataflow).
- **§7.9 / §21.1 — the local half of definite assignment is keyed on *defaultable*, not on nullability (ruling; [#4362](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4362) closes).** §7.9's lead sentence and §21.1's restatement split on **non-nullable** while §7.9's own *Default initialization* subsection splits on **defaultable** — and `int` is both, so `var count: int;` followed by a read was a compile error under one sentence and `0` under the other, the parenthetical illustrating only the nullable half on which the two agreed. **Decided: defaultable.** A local of defaultable type declared without an initializer holds that type's default from its declaration; a local of non-defaultable type must be assigned before it is read — the same predicate §7.9 already applies to fields. **Grounds:** *Default initialization* is the section's full statement of the split and the two restatements are one-liners; the defaultable reading is the one §15.1's *Initialization* subsection prints for locals (`var counts: [10]int; // 10 zeros`), §15.1.1's `var pool: [16 owned]Connection?;` prints for a move-only local, and §9.9's *"a `Port`-typed field **or local** declared with no initializer … are compile errors"* presupposes; and no non-nullable reference type is defaultable, so §7.9's never-observed-unset guarantee is untouched. §21.1's own `var balance: decimal;` is now described correctly by the sentence beneath it; *Default initialization*'s parenthetical gains a value-typed instance; §28.3's ownership-state bullet and its *Adoption* paragraph split the no-initializer declaration on the same predicate (at a defaultable `T` the declaration is the initialization, and the nullable case joins the polymorphic-null state); §28.8's dominance sentence and Appendix C.1's two rows say *non-defaultable*. **Declined:** strict-for-all-locals — it contradicts §15.1's *Initialization* subsection and would newly reject §15.1.1's own worked example, making it a design change rather than a defect fix; a nullability-keyed local rule beside a defaultability-keyed field rule — a second predicate for no gain, still needing an inline-array carve-out; and a warning on reading a never-assigned defaultable local, a new diagnostic not a defect train's business. **Body-locality: local** — one body's control flow and each local's declared-type property. **Kernel: no contact** (§28.3's two bullets restate §7.9's split at the classification, adding no rule).
- **§29.7 / §28.2 — the completed state is bookkeeping, and a second `Dispose()` warns (ruling; [#4399](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4399) closes).** §29.7 read *"subsequent `MoveNext()` returns `false`"*, which §28.2 makes unobservable: checked mode raises `DisposedAccessException` on any instance member access on a disposed instance, carving out exactly one member, a further `Dispose()`. **Decided (a):** the clause describes the state machine's own bookkeeping — nothing resumes and no suspended body runs again — and is not a post-disposal guarantee to the consumer; a post-disposal `MoveNext()` is an ordinary §28.2 member access, so no conforming program observes what a completed machine would answer, while a second `Dispose()` *is* observable and is the no-op §28.2's contract keeps callable. **Decided (b), the second-order gap:** §28.2's *"a further `Dispose()` remains a no-op, not an error, in both modes"* is the **runtime** contract and suppresses no diagnostic — a second `Dispose()` is a use of the binding (K3.9's **explicitly-disposed** post-state already says *"straight-line use afterward is §28.2's mandatory use-after-dispose warning"*) and draws the warning; the warning-free spelling of idempotence is one explicit disposal, an auto-drop and a `using var`'s scope-end disposal not being repeat calls. **Declined:** adding `MoveNext`/`MoveNextAsync` as a second §28.2 carve-out — the single carve-out exists because the disposal contract must keep `Dispose()` callable, and a per-member post-disposal allowlist is machinery the section does not have. **Kernel classification: derivation** — K3.9 + K4.2 + K7.4. **Body-locality: local** (straight-line dominance in one body).
- **§12.4 / §11.5 — bare `sealed` on a member is a compile error, whatever the member's kind or dispatch modifier (ruling; [#4374](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4374) closes).** §11.5 said `sealed` alone *"does not appear on individual members"* — a statement about the grammar — while §12.4 said it *"may not appear on a non-virtual, non-override member"* — a semantic rejection whose qualification presupposes a member-position form and left `public sealed virtual method M()` unaddressed. **Decided:** on a member, `sealed` appears only as the compound `sealed override`; a declaration carrying `sealed` without `override` is a compile error at every member kind and beside every other dispatch modifier, and a `sealed override` still satisfies §12.1's override-matching. **Grounds:** §9.2's *Dispatch modifiers* subsection (v0.297) already reads *"Bare `sealed` on any member is already §12.4's error"* and cites §12.4 for a rule §12.4 did not state at that width; §26.3's extension-member exclusion and §32.1's `extern` exclusion both enumerate bare `sealed` as a rejected modifier; and the literal reading of §12.4's sentence makes it redundant with §12.1. **Declined:** correcting §12.4 in the other direction and leaving §11.5 as written — it would oblige edits in five places and a diagnostic change to preserve a grammar production no one has been reading. **Recorded residual, its own issue:** A.4's `VirtualKind ::= "abstract" | "virtual" | "sealed"? "override"` derives bare `sealed` at member position nowhere, so five sections speak of it as a *rejected modifier* while the grammar makes it underivable; the new text says *"is a compile error"* without naming a phase, which is true either way, and whether A.4 gains an over-admission alternative is filed rather than decided. **Riding in the same edit-set, named rather than buried:** §11.7's `closed` paragraph carried *"(Through v0.241 the semantics were spelled as the modifier pair `sealed abstract`; that spelling is rejected, the diagnostic naming `closed`.)"*, and stdlib §5's opening carried *"(Through v0.277 this paragraph required `import System.Collections.Linq;` …)"* — two instances of the history narration in normative text that process §7 names as a recurring defect. Both now state the rule alone; the history is here, which is the one place it belongs. Appendix C.1's `sealed abstract` row is unchanged and already stated it.
- **§22.7 — the chaining position rejects a direct field read, whatever the field's type (clarification; [#4390](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4390) closes).** Rule 1 carved direct field and auto-property reads out of the *observation* set (*"they keep their existing definite-assignment rules"*) and then rejected, in the chaining position, *"any observation of `this` there"* — a premise about **fields** with a conclusion about **observations**, the bridge having just been removed. On `public constructor() this(_x, 0); end constructor;` with a defaultable `_x: int`, §22.7 read alone admits the program. The rule that rejects it lives in **§22.10** and **§12.8**, with §22.8 restating it — and both of the first two cite §22.7 as its ground, §12.8 in so many words (*"the field half is §22.7's ground"*), which §22.7 did not supply. Rule 1's chaining clause now carries its own field arm: the carve-out notwithstanding, a direct read of any field or auto-property of `this` is a compile error there too, **whatever the field's type**, and the only reads a chaining argument may make are of the constructor's own parameters, constants, and statics. **Both halves survive, and the trace says why:** clause A is load-bearing in the constructor *body* — without it no constructor could assign its own fields, every first `_x := v;` being an observation at an unsatisfied gate — while clause B's own premise (*"no field of the declaring type is yet assigned"*) is exactly the ground for the field arm it never drew. **Composition note:** the clause says *whatever the field's type* precisely so that #4362's defaultable ruling and this one cannot be composed into an admission. **Body-locality: local.**
- **§17.2 — the range-with-bitwise bullet drops the remedy that does not type, and the mandatory-parenthesization rule states its scope (clarification; [#4369](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4369) closes).** The bullet offered two spellings for `mask & 0..n`, and one of them, `mask & (0..n)`, resolves the category mix into an expression with no intrinsic operand pairing — `&` is defined on the integer types (§3.5, §6.5) and `Range<T>` declares no operators (§25.1) — so a reader taking the offered remedy hit a second, unrelated error. `(mask & 0)..n` both parses and types and is now the only one shown. The section's closing paragraph gains the rule's scope: the check is **syntactic**, reading operator categories and parenthesization and never operand types, so a listed mix is rejected whether or not some grouping of it would type; a parenthesization restores a *parse*, and the result is then subject to the ordinary operand rules. The bitwise-with-logical remedy is named as the shape — `(flags & MASK) <> 0 and ready` supplies the `bool` operand `and` requires. **Declined:** re-illustrating the bitwise-with-logical mix with operands that pair, so the parenthesization requirement is the first rule violated (the issue's critique comment) — §17's operand tables admit no such intrinsic pairing, and the only well-typed instance needs a user-declared `operator &` with a `bool` result, a two-declaration example inside a precedence-notes bullet. The consequence is recorded rather than engineered away: for the two mixes whose operands do not pair, no reject case can isolate §17.2, and the scope sentence is what makes that a documented property of a syntax rule rather than a hole. (One `DECLINED.md` row owed, below.)
- **§15.1.1 / §28.5 — an owning-inline-array field is disposed by the generated `Dispose()`, and needs no user-written destructor (clarification; [#4375](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4375) closes).** §15.1.1 said *"for class fields, the enclosing class's destructor invokes the disposal"* while §28.4's generated `Dispose()` does it at **step 2** and §28.5 says such a class *"needs no destructor"*; the two reconcile only by reading §15.1.1's "destructor" as the generated teardown path, which the word means nowhere else in §28. A reader working from §15.1.1 alone writes one, and a declared destructor is not inert — §22.9's construction-unwind rule and §28.4's one-raw-resource-per-owning-wrapper discipline both key on whether a class declares one. §15.1.1 now names §28.4 step 2 and states the negative; **§28.5's own owning-inline-array bullet carried the same misnomer** four lines above its *"needs no destructor"* sentence and is corrected with it. **Kernel: no contact** — the edit names an existing §28.4 step in place of a wrong mechanism word; the obligation and its discharge point are unchanged.
- **§9.7 / stdlib §4.14 — the null-source form is unreachable for spans (clarification; [#4387](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4387) closes).** §9.7 admits a borrow-bearing record into a static field only in the null-source form (every reference-typed field, and every reference-typed slot of every inline-array field, `null`), and into a class instance field on the same definition; `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, `ArraySpan<T>` and `ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>` each declare a **non-nullable** `Buffer`/`Source`, so no span value has that form and neither admission is reachable for them. Both documents now state the consequence rather than leaving it to a cross-document derivation, with the remedy (store the source, re-derive the span at the use site). `ReadOnlyStringSpan` is unaffected — its only reference-typed field is a runtime-managed `string`, so it is not a borrow-bearing record and is outside the rule entirely. **No rule changes.**
- **§28.6 — the no-escape example becomes reachable (editorial; [#4365](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4365) closes).** `LeakTransactions` illustrated the escape rule with `return move _transactions;`, which §28.8.1's field-restoration rule rejects first as a terminal move — the section half-noticed this in its own prose without withdrawing the example. The body is now `return new OwningArray<Transaction>();`, the **fresh-producer** arm of the very same §28.6 bullet (*"a freshly-produced owning value … returned through a non-`owned` return is likewise an error"*), which no earlier rule reaches. **Declined:** the take-restore-return shape, which would have left the moved field's value at a plain class-typed return and so behind the announcement table's row-4 borrow escape — trading one over-determined example for another. **Residual recorded rather than deleted:** §28.6's **moved-field** arm is normatively stated and **diagnostically unreachable**, standing behind two earlier rejections (§28.8.1's terminal-move rule and the announcement table's row 4); it stays stated, and this entry is its record. The corpus case `tests/conformance/cases/spec_0208.bzl` is hand-synced with the fence (#1380), its `reject` verdict unchanged.
- **§29.12 — the remove-during-iteration example discards its `bool` (editorial; [#4401](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4401) closes).** `transactions.Remove(t);` drew §21.9's discarded-result warning (`Array<T>.Remove(item: T): bool`, stdlib §4.4; the fluent-receiver exemption requires the result type to equal the receiver's), so the spec's own canonical idiom warned. Now `_ := transactions.Remove(t);`, with the reason in the comment. **Sweep:** every bare expression statement of a `bool`-returning collection member across the documents was checked; one other instance exists, Guide 05 §3's `ledger.Remove(t);`, corrected in the same commit as a guide-only fix (no pin move). `RemoveAt` (Guides 06, 07) and `Set<T>.Add` return `()` and are clean.
- **§9.2 — the member list is the equality package's membership set, not an admission list (editorial; [#4363](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4363) closes).** The opening sentence read as exhaustive. **No rule changes:** §9.3 already says a member *"outside the §9.2 list … suppresses the auto-generated equality members — the declaration itself stays legal"*, §9.4 restates it, §9.5 makes *"public fields"* a `with` target, and §9.2's own first disqualifier and its worked `equality skip` example are both written over an explicit field. The sentence now says which set it is stating. **Declined:** treating it as a ruling — §9.3 has already decided it — and the argument the issue was filed on, from the *silence* of Appendix A's over-admission index, is **withdrawn**: that row was itself incomplete (next bullet), so its silence carried nothing either way.
- **Appendix A — the over-admission index's record-body row gains destructors and `invariant` (editorial; [#4395](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4395) closes).** The row listed only the dispatch modifiers; `DestructorDecl` and `InvariantDecl` are `Member` alternatives that `RecordBody ::= Member*` admits and that §9.7 (*"Records cannot have destructors"*) and §22.16/C.15 (*"`invariant` members appear only in classes"*) reject. The enum-or-choice row directly above already names both, so the record row's silence read as an admission; the citations mirror that row's shape. **Declined:** adding an `owned`-field row in the same pass — a modifier on a field rather than a `Member` alternative the record body newly admits, not named by the issue, and a widening better decided deliberately (recorded).
- **§9.1 and §9.2 — the generated-member lists gain `Equals` (clarification; [#4406](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4406) closes).** §9.1 listed the primary constructor, the properties, value equality, `GetHashCode` and `ToString`; §9.2 listed *"`=`, `<>`, `GetHashCode`, and `ToString`"*. Four passages already state the generated `Equals`: §8.3's kind table has a *Default `Equals`* column with positional- and body-record rows, §14.2 clause 2 names *"the synthesized `Equals(T)`"* as what satisfies `IEquatable<T>` (which is what makes a bodyless `record Point(X: int, Y: int): IEquatable<Point>;` legal), §9.2's `equality skip` clause enumerates *"`Equals(T)`/`Equals(Object?)`"* among the generated members, and §25.2 says both *"continue to exist"*. Generation is stated unconditionally. **Declined:** attaching the `IEquatable<T>` condition to *generation* — §9.2's use-site parenthetical qualifies which calls the error covers, not which members exist; whether that parenthetical is itself accurate is recorded below, not decided here.
- **§2.3, stdlib §5 and the code-generation reference — one import surface, stated the same way in every document (clarification; [#4412](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4412) closes).** §2.3's table has always made the `Task` family always-available, while §2.3's own closing paragraph enumerated the `System.Threading` exemptions as *"`Subscription`, `CancellationToken`, or any of the six event types"* — an enumeration its *"and the other threading types"* closes, so read strictly it made `Task` import-requiring and every `async` method's declared return type an unnameable one (§2.8.3 rule 2 puts a return type in the *naming* half). **The table is the rule**, and the paragraph now says so: the exemption sentence names the Task family and the participation sentence above it names the reason. The code-generation reference's §5.0 row, which had taken the paragraph's side, gains the same clause; its §5.6 declaration comment `public class CancellationTokenSource   // auto-imported` — contradicting that document twice over and §2.3, which names `CancellationTokenSource` as import-requiring — now reads `// NOT auto — needs the import`; and its §6 tallying idiom drops the stale `(with import System.Collections.Linq;)`, the fifth and last copy of the line v0.287 swept from the spec and the stdlib ([#3818](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3818)). **Stdlib chapter 5's heading gains the `(auto-imported)` marker** its three auto-imported siblings carry and its own first line has asserted since v0.278; the Contents entry moves with it, the heading slug being what the table of contents links by. The marker is machine-readable and is being read — `tests/conformance/rules/names.py` derives module membership from these headings and had to special-case this chapter against a hardcoded list, which the marker retires. **Nothing decided:** each part is a second text catching up to a rule a first text already states.
- **The code-generation reference — one wrong line, four misleading ones, and one sentence in §19.2 ([#4371](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4371) closes, two of its seven items withdrawn; [#4382](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4382) closes as mostly withdrawn).** **One was wrong, not merely misleading:** §4.2 said `ref`/`out` are forbidden *"on lambdas"*, where §30.1, Appendix A.4's over-admission index and §27.1 all say *`async` lambdas* — A.7's `LambdaParam ::= FuncParamMods? Identifier …` admits the modifier, `(ref int) -> ()` is a legal function type that must have an inhabitant, and the same §4.2 list names lambda parameters as an `owned`-admissible position; the line now names `async` lambdas and shows the admitted ordinary one. **Four clarifications:** §3.3's *Method, arrow, unit* row said *"(assignment body only with no declared return type)"*, read by two lanes as "only an assignment is admitted there" — §22.2 makes the assignment an *addition*, admitted only where there is no declared return type, and the row now says which; §3.3's enum block said `ToString()` *"renders the TYPE name"*, one glance from C#'s constant name, and now says *qualified* type name, never the constant's, `NameOf` being that; §4.2's Task-discard line conflated discarding the **task** (rejected) with discarding an **awaited result** (`_ := await t;`, a Pattern B owned-consuming position §30.5 admits); and §7.2 gains the generic static factory `Make<T>(): T where T: new()`, §28.3 row 6's rejection, beside the concrete `Create(host): Connection` it already carried. **In the spec:** §19.2's first bullet read *"This is the only form valid in expression-position `case`"*, which reads equally as "valid only in expression position" and cost one lane twenty files' worth of edits before A.7's `ArmBody` settled it; it now says *"Valid in both positions, and the **only** form an expression-position `case` admits"*, the parallel its two sibling bullets already use. **#4382 is largely withdrawn:** its central claim — that §31.4's exception surface is in neither derived index — is false against the current text. §5's block headed *Exceptions (spec §31.4)* has carried `Message`, `StackTrace`, `CauseChain`, `SupersededChain`, the three constructors, `ExceptionInfo` and `ArgumentException.ParamName` **since the document's first commit (`2a65e27a`, 2026-08-20), twenty-six days before the issue was filed**, and that is the treatment the issue proposes. Two narrow gaps are real and close here: `TypeInitializationException.InnerException: Exception?` — §31.4's one built-in live reference, declared in stdlib §2.17 — was absent while the hierarchy line's correctly-qualified *"No user `InnerException`"* sat three words from the type that has one; and §5.12's `pure` inventory named only `Exception`'s and `ArgumentException`'s pure constructors where §31.4 gives **every** built-in exception's `()` and `(message)` forms, which is the set §22.15's throw carve-out consumes. §31.4 and stdlib §2.17 are unchanged and were already complete. **#4371's two withdrawn items:** §4.3's announcement table does state row 6's declaration-site rejection (and the `where T: new()` gloss the issue quotes is spec §14.2's, not the reference's), and §5.2's `Result<T, E>` entry already carries stdlib §2.20's conditionally-admitted framing and the sentence *"Owning instantiations carry none of the four members"*.
- **[#4381](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4381) — withdrawn in full, no edit.** (1) The zero-auto-property `with` error was said to have no spelling. It has: A.7's suffix is `"with" "(" InitAssign ("," InitAssign)* ","? ")"` and `InitAssign`'s left side is any identifier, so `r with(Anything := 1)` parses on such a record and §9.2's sentence is the authority that rejects it — the premise conflated *legal* with *parseable*, and a compile error's trigger need not be an otherwise-accepted program. The residual (the diagnostic can never be *isolated* from §9.5's own target-list rejection) is not a defect, and neither proposed remedy is available at this gate: an empty `with()` is a grammar change and so a design change, and a "this case cannot be typed" note would be normative text asserting a falsehood. (2) The third auto-equality disqualifier's non-isolability was said to be worth recording. It is already recorded, in the disqualifier's own bullet — *"by that rule the two disqualifiers always fire together, so this bullet decides nothing on its own for a conforming record"* — with its cause (§25.2's co-declaration forcing `override GetHashCode`, which is disqualifier 2) named in the same clause. A third statement would be redundancy, not clarity.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected (in the spec's terms):** a record or choice declaring `: ISerializable`/`: IDeserializable` one of whose components is a structurally-eligible record or choice that declares **neither** interface — a compile error at the conformance declaration, naming the component (#4398 gap 2). **The shipped compiler already rejects it** (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:10115-10119` for a record component, `:10154-10156` for a choice; the predicate's header comment states it as doctrine at `:9913-9915`), so no program that compiles today stops compiling. Also newly rejected in the spec's terms, and likewise already rejected by the compiler: bare `sealed` beside `virtual` or `abstract` on a member — outside §12.4's v0.298 sentence, inside §11.5's clause (#4374).
- **Newly accepted (in the spec's terms):** a direct `.Equals(…)`/`.GetHashCode()` call on a non-auto-hashable body record that declares that member itself and declares no `operator =`/`<>` overloads (#4396); a record mixing `serialized skip` with an explicit constructor, which a step-2-literal checker would have rejected (#4398 gap 1); and an explicit `Dispose()` of a source pinned by a `using var` borrow-pin — `using var pin := w; w.Dispose();` — previously rejected on §28.10's literal wording and admitted by §28.3/§28.6 all along (#4413). **All three the shipped compiler already accepts**, so these are impl-ahead-of-spec silences being retired, not deltas being created.
- **Newly defined:** the per-member scope of §9.2's use-site error and the `override`-or-plain escape; that a `serialized skip` component binds its constructor parameter with `default(T)`, that a nested record or choice serialization component must declare the conformance, and that enums need not; the term *admissible as a serialized component* as distinct from the type-level *serialization-eligible*; the trivial-dispose exemption's scope (over the obligation, at every holder form, keyed produced-type-where-known and declared-type otherwise, interfaces never exempt); §28.10's pin as the consume-site freeze's liveness reading; §29.7's completed state as bookkeeping and the status of a post-disposal `MoveNext()`; the local half of §7.9's defaultable split; §22.7's chaining-position field arm; §17.2's rule as syntactic; that §9.2's member list is the equality package's membership set; and the unreachability of §9.7's null-source form for spans.
- **Newly warned:** a second `Dispose()` on the same binding, where the first dominates the use site on every path (§28.2, #4399) — stated normatively for the first time; the compiler already emits it. **No longer warned:** the must-use / auto-drop lint at the holder forms §28.9's amended key exempts — a plain-`var` owned local, an undischarged `owned` parameter (method, iterator, async) and an owning iteration variable of trivial-dispose type (#4400); the auto-drop itself is unaffected at every one of them. **Spec-level loosening:** #4362 admits a read of a defaultable local declared without an initializer, which both v0.298 sentences and the compiler reject today. **No ramp is owed** — this train tightens nothing that was scheduled, and a ramp is a ratchet-class artifact; nothing here is a ratchet.
- **Compiler status — two spec-ahead-of-impl deltas, each owed a tracking issue at landing (process §5 item 3); everything else codifies shipped behaviour.** (1) **#4400:** `MethodOwnership::localIsTrivialDisposeNewBinding` (`src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:6515`) implements the narrow, `new`-keyed reading **deliberately** — its header comment at `:6488-6490` says *"`new` expressions only. The spec sentence names the `new` expression form; a factory call returning `owned T` is not covered by it, so it keeps today's warning"* — and no arm suppresses the lint at an `owned` parameter or an owning iteration variable. **The gate's amended key reduces this delta rather than widening it:** the produced-type arm is exactly what the compiler already does (`:6520-6531`, whose comment names the declared-type key *"the dangerous direction"*), so the catch-up is the reach over holder forms and the declared-type fallback, not a reversal. (2) **#4362:** `src/sema/DefiniteAssignment.cpp`'s `LocalDecl` arm marks a no-initializer local assigned only for `TypeRef::Kind::InlineArray` (`:1122`), so every other defaultable local draws `read of unassigned local` (`:2136-2141`) — including a nullable one, which neither v0.298 sentence rejected; the narrow fix widens that test to the **defaultable** predicate, and the `out var` path's related, narrower `isNonNullableReferenceType` split should end at the same predicate. **Codifying shipped behaviour:** #4396 (`checkEqualityMemberUseSite` is reached only from inside `resolveMemberAccess`'s `if (!member)` block — `src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp:21058` the lookup, `:21207` the block, `:21350` the call, definition at `:22607`; the predicate comment at `src/sema/SymbolCollection.cpp:1878-1880` states it, and `tests/lit/sema/sema_record_equality__ineligible_user_equals_accepted_spec_9_2.bzl` pins the accept); #4398 gap 1 (`TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:10797-10812`, whose comment says skipped components *"still bind a constructor parameter (their value is default(T))"*); #4399 (`markDisposedByName`, `src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:9337`, warns at `:9343-9357` with §28.2 as its cited authority, and calls only the §28.14 `checkScopedFreeze`, never the consume freeze — which is #4413's conformance too);
