### v0.300 changelog (v0.299 → v0.300)

**A question train: the thirty-one `spec-question` issues the rule-corpus effort raised and the documents left undecided — twenty-eight resolved here, two re-classified as *compiler* gaps with no spec edit, and one ruling held out of the train for want of a probe.** Where v0.299's defect train fixed places the documents said two things, this one fixes places they said **nothing**: every issue in the set is a question a conforming implementation could have answered either way, and most of them are stdlib members whose entire specification was their name. The consequential rulings are three — a **compile-time-constant operand** at an explicit conversion the conversion would reject is now a compile error at the conversion site ([#4405](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4405)); a class or record member named **`Dispose`** is a compile error at **any** parameter list ([#4404](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4404)); and a class declaring **no instance constructor** has an implicit public parameterless one that satisfies `where T: new()` ([#4364](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4364)) — and the rest either state a rule the neighbouring text already implied or name a semantics that was carried by a member's name. **Three outcomes are not ordinary resolutions and are stated plainly below:** [#4384](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4384) and [#4386](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4386) are compiler gaps, not spec gaps — #4386's filed premise is refuted, and the real non-conformance is the mirror of the reported one; **half of [#4376](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4376) is withdrawn at the gate**, its adoption ruling standing in full and its must-use-suppression clause reverted; and **[#4380](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4380) lands three of its four parts and stays open for the fourth**, the only edit in its set that newly rejected a program class.

- **§5.2 / §5.3 / §16.3 — a compile-time-constant operand the conversion would reject is a compile error at the conversion site (ruling; [#4405](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4405) closes).** §5.2 said only *"Integer narrowing raises `OverflowException` if the value does not fit"*, a complete rule a conforming implementation can apply to a constant operand without noticing a gap — and this compiler has, for many revisions. Its three siblings do not: §5.1's constant narrowing is a **range error at the site**, §5.4's checked enum cast is a compile error *"AT THE CAST SITE"* for a constant equal to no declared constant and names the parallel outright (*"the same posture as §5.1's constant-narrowing range error"*), §6.5's shift count is *"a **compile error** when the count is a compile-time constant"*, and §17.14 makes a faulting constant expression a compile error wherever it is written. **Decided:** where the operand of an explicit conversion is a compile-time constant whose value would raise `OverflowException` under any rule of §5.2 — integer narrowing, the same-width signedness change, the integer-to-`char` code-point range, the floating-point and `decimal` conversions — the conversion is a compile error at the conversion site, never a deferred runtime fault: `uint(-1)`, `byte(300)`, `char(0xD800)`, `int(1e30)`. **Two bounds ship with the rule:** it reads the **operand** and does not make a conversion expression a constant expression (§17.14's inductive set is unchanged — `const K := byte(1);` is still not a compile-time `const`, so its recorded *casts-are-liftable* bound is untouched), and a conversion that **saturates** rather than raises is unaffected — `float(1e300)` is `Infinity` and `float(0.0 / 0.0)` is `NaN` at a constant operand exactly as at a runtime one. §5.3's nullable cast inherits it through its existing delegation (a present value converts *"by `T(v)` under that conversion's own semantics"*, now including the constant-operand error). **Grounds:** the literal reading would make §5.2 the language's only checked operation that defers a decidable fault, and would leave the primitive cast laxer than the enum cast modelled on it; and the v0.242 record supplies both the reason §5.2 was left behind and the precedent for the direction — that train's scope was the three operations that, handed an out-of-domain input, *"silently computed something else"*, which §5.2's already-raising narrowing was not, while the same train converted a constant-folded runtime fault into a compile error (the zero range step, §16.4) under a ruling-class landing. **Declined:** the literal runtime reading. **Caught at the gate:** §16.3's surrogate paragraph still said `char(0xD800)` *"raises `OverflowException` at runtime per §5.2"* — citing the section this ruling rewrote, which names that exact constant as rejected where it is written; it now states the compile error and keeps the runtime fault for a non-constant operand. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact** (§5 is outside §28/§30.5).
- **§28.2 / stdlib §2.10 — a class or record member named `Dispose` is a compile error, whatever its parameter list (ruling; [#4404](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4404) closes).** §28.2's *"User code does not implement `Dispose()` directly"* stated a fact and no consequence, and no member-collision rule covered it. **Decided:** the §9.3 posture for a body member colliding with a compiler-generated one, keyed on the **name** as §12.2's inherited-member rule is, not on the parameter list — because §22.5's optional parameters make `Dispose(mode: int := 0)` callable as `x.Dispose()` and therefore ambiguous against the generated member, which an arity-keyed rule would admit. On a class the name is the compiler's: the generated `Dispose()` is what `using var` (§28.10), the owned-field cascade (§28.4), the discard (§17.13) and an explicit call (§28.6) all reach, and §28.4 makes it non-overridable, so a user body would never run — the silent trap the rule exists to prevent. Records are covered on §9.7's ground rather than on a collision. **Interfaces are carved out explicitly:** `IDisposable` *is* `method Dispose();`. **Declined:** admit-and-shadow. **The widening from the compiler's arity-keyed rule is the one place this ruling goes past its evidence,** and the record is here: the fallback, if a reviewer holds the constructed `Dispose(mode: int := 0)` case too thin, is the implementation's shape with *"zero parameters"* substituted, and nothing else in this entry moves.
- **§28.6 — an explicit `Dispose()` of an owned field or owning-collection slot demands nothing afterwards (ruling; [#4366](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4366) closes).** §28.6 admitted the receiver and justified it with idioms that all reassign or tear down, leaving the bare early-close shape and the later-read question open. **Decided:** the call is an **early release point**, not a discharge — the slot keeps its reference and its K9 obligation, the containing object's teardown still runs the cascade over it (§28.4 step 2), where the second call is §28.2's no-op; at a **trivial-dispose** slot type the compiler's single free stays at the holder's release point, which §28.9 already fixes as the containing object's teardown, the explicit call having performed logical disposal only; and **no restoration obligation arises**, K9.2's rule being scoped to a `move` and grounded in the hole a moved-from slot leaves. A later field read is the checked-mode backstop, not a static diagnostic: §28.2's use-after-dispose warning is a straight-line rule over a **local**, and this section's admission is by declaring type, so no body-local dominance argument is available. **Declined:** a restoration-like obligation — it preserves no invariant idempotence does not already preserve, and makes a **non-nullable** owned field's early close inexpressible. **Kernel classification: derivation** — K9 + K9.2 read at its own scope + K3.9 + K4.1 + K5.6; no kernel text moves. **Body-locality: local.**
- **§28.10 / §15.3 / §35.4 / §28.3 — an unmarked `using var` over a move-only value *adopts*; the must-use-suppression half is withdrawn (ruling, half-withdrawn at the gate; [#4376](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4376) closes).** §28.10's borrow-pin enumeration named *"an **unmarked** read of a named owned binding"*, which the §28.3 producers table's own definition extends to move-only locals, while §15.3's *Local-to-local assignment* said such a read **moves**. **Decided:** it moves. The pin list is scoped to **class- and interface-typed** bindings, exactly as its first item is already scoped by announcement-table row 8, and a move-only binding has no borrow reading for a pin to pin; the unmarked form therefore adopts, `y` carrying the value's owned slots to the end of *its* block and `x` left moved-from. **Declined:** the pin reading — it has no coherent value semantics, since the pinned binding would have to read by copy and §15.3 forbids copying. **The withdrawn half.** The lane's second ruling said `using var` over a move-only value **suppresses the must-use warning** on the implicit drop, restating what it took to be §28.3's existing suppression sentence. No section defines that warning for owning inline arrays: K1 rule 14 scopes it to a plain-`var` local or an `owned` parameter, K1's *owned* is class- or interface-typed, §35.4 had to **state** it for owning choices (which is evidence it does not follow generally), and §28.10 says in this same revision that the only additional effect on a move-only local is the reassignability restriction. A clarification may not create a diagnostic in a subordinate clause with no rule defining it and no remedy; the clause is reverted and §15.3's *"its only observable consequence is preventing reassignment"* stands, now with *"an unmarked move-only initializer is **adopted**, not pinned"* beside it. **Caught at the gate, separately:** §28.3's *Ownership state of locals* still said an unmarked read of **any** named owned binding is a borrow-pin — the ruling qualified that sentence in three places and missed the fourth. **Kernel classification: derivation** — K3.12 + K3.13's own move-only parenthetical + K1.5, with **A5 read, not extended**: the pin bars moving *out of* a `using var`, and adoption moves *in*. **Body-locality: local.**
- **§15.1.1 / §15.3 / §22.13 / §28.7 — an owning inline array's slots are disposed in reverse slot order at every ending, and a wholly moved-from local owes no restoration (ruling + clarification; [#4388](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4388) closes).** §15.3 pinned **reverse** slot order for the whole-value-reassignment pass and the other endings stated none. **Decided:** reverse slot order at every one of them — one pass over one value cannot have two orders, and every other multi-value disposal in the language is reverse-of-establishment (§28.3's locals and temporaries, §28.4's fields, §28.10's stack, K8.5's atom clauses). The endings are **four**, not three: scope end, the containing class's generated `Dispose()` (§28.4 step 2), whole-value reassignment, and **program exit** for a static field of owning-inline-array type (§22.13) — and §15.1.1's *"for class fields"* is narrowed to *"for **instance** fields"*, without which the fourth ending is redundant with the second. **Declined:** ascending order, whose only argument was that two of the compiler's three passes do it while the third cites the spec for reverse. **The restoration half is a clarification:** K1's moved-from state says *"discharge machinery skips it"* and §28.3's auto-drop runs only on a local *"not in moved-from state"*, so a **wholly** moved-from move-only local is never walked and owes nothing; the per-slot obligation's own stated ground — *"auto-dispose on a moved-from **slot** is not defined"* — is about a pass that still runs, and K9.2's rule for a whole-value `move` out of a **field** is untouched. **Caught at the gate:** §22.13 still said slot order within such an array *"is unobservable (slots are disposed independently)"*, against a rule that is now unconditional; it cites §15.1.1's order. **Kernel classification: derivation** — K9 + K3.15 + K3.14 + K1, the forward-vs-reverse choice settled by uniformity with §15.3's already-pinned pass rather than derived from a kernel clause. **Body-locality: local.**
- **§28.9 / §28.1 / §28.5 / §28.11 / §17.10 / stdlib §2.13 / rationale §4 — `Type` is runtime-managed (ruling; [#4393](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4393) closes).** §28.3's producers table had no `typeof` row, and §17.10 and stdlib §2.13 stated only the interning guarantee, so a `Type` value's ownership classification was undecided. **Decided:** `Type` joins `string`, boxed values and function values — the runtime holds one instance per type for the life of the process, user code never allocates one, and nothing is ever reclaimed, so no holder acquires an obligation: no `Type` expression is an owned production, none lends a borrow, none constrains a lifetime, and **`owned Type` is inadmissible** at every position §28.1 lists. A `Type`-returning member is the announcement table's **row 7** at every callee kind, so a `static` `Type`-returning method may be declared. **Grounds:** the owned reading is unimplementable — `Type` is trivial-dispose, so §28.9's compiler-inserted free would set the disposed flag on the one process-wide token at every `var t := typeof(X);` scope end and fault every other holder in checked mode. **Declined:** the borrow-from-static-storage row the issue offered first — sound, but it keys a receiver-bounded liveness constraint to a process-lived singleton and, through announcement-table row 4's static column, makes a `static` `Type`-returning method unwritable. §28.9's exhaustiveness sentence is unweakened (`Type` is not a class a user can write) and the no-GC claim is untouched (nothing is reclaimed); rationale §4 now names `Type` as the set's **fixed-mechanism** member, distinguishing it from the three whose reclamation is unspecified. **Caught at the gate:** §28.11's element-category table is a **decision** table and `Type` was absent from its runtime-managed row — so `OwningArray<Type>` would have taken owned element slots, against this very ruling. **Kernel classification: derivation** — K1.6's runtime-managed exemption, discharged by the interning guarantee §17.10 and stdlib §2.13 already state, with K2's always-live characterisation; recorded for the record, a reviewer who reads tier **membership** as a grant rather than a derivation would place it under **A10**. **Body-locality: local.**
- **§22.7 / §14.2 — the implicit parameterless constructor is stated, and its two builtin carve-outs land with it (ruling; [#4364](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4364) closes).** No section said a class declaring no constructor has one, while §12.8's inserted `base()` and §11.7's own `closed class Shape` / `sealed class Circle(radius: double): Shape` example both depend on it, and §14.2's `where T: new()` was written over the word *"declares"*. **Decided:** a class that declares **no instance constructor** and no primary-constructor parameter list has an implicit parameterless constructor — `public`, no parameters, an empty body, chaining implicitly per §12.8 — and it satisfies `where T: new()` on the same terms a declared public parameterless one does. Declaring **any** instance constructor suppresses it, a primary-constructor parameter list included; a `static constructor` does not (it is never a chaining or `new` target); a `static` class has none. The rule is stated for the **class** kind: a record's construction surface is §9.1/§9.2's, and the body-record twin (the compiler's #4059, v0.295) is not decided here. **Declined:** no implicit constructor — its only defence was §14.2's wording, and it breaks §11.7's own example. **Caught at the gate, and it is the finding that was not merely a stale sentence:** the ruling as drafted gave a **standard-library builtin** an implicit constructor that §17.7's closed-constructor-surface rule forbids, and let `Subscription` — which declares none — satisfy `where T: new()`, so a generic factory could mint one, which is exactly what §17.7 exists to prevent. Two carve-outs close it: §22.7 excepts a standard-library builtin from the implicit constructor, and §14.2's `new()` arm excepts it from satisfaction. stdlib §2.11 now says in prose that `new Subscription(...)` is a compile error at any argument list. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact.**
- **§12.4 and §35.7 — `virtual` is rejected on a member of a `sealed` class, and §35.7's direct-call exemption is keyed on the members (two rulings; [#4391](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4391) closes, its middle part settled by v0.299).** **(a) §12.4:** a member of a `sealed` class may not be declared `virtual` — the class admits no subclass, so a new virtual slot can never be filled, and an inert modifier that reads as load-bearing misleads every reader of the declaration. This is v0.297's §9.2/§10.5/§35.2 rule for the **implicitly** sealed value kinds, read for the explicitly sealed class, on that ruling's own ground. `override` and `sealed override` are unaffected — they fill a slot an ancestor declared, which is what §12.4's own `sealed override` example and the sealed-derived-class idiom do; `abstract` was already excluded (it requires an `abstract` class, and `abstract`/`sealed` are mutually exclusive class modifiers). *Declined:* admitting it inertly, and warning — the two `DECLINED.md` already records for records. The lane's own self-critique asked for the count v0.297's ruling was landed with, and **the sweep was run: zero occurrences** of a `virtual` member inside a `sealed class` across `tests/`, `docs/` and `examples/`, so the churn this rejection creates is empty in this tree. **(b) §35.7:** the use-site exemption for **direct `Equals`/`GetHashCode` calls** is keyed on the declared **members**, not on the operators — a choice that declares plain `Equals(other: C): bool` and `GetHashCode(): int` admits those calls on **every** classification, owning and borrow-bearing included, because they resolve statically to the declared members, which is what §35.2's *reachable by static dispatch only* says and what §25.2's *"a lone `Equals(T)` on an owning choice takes the same reading"* presupposes; the operator-keyed reading emptied §35.2's v0.285 clause for the entire population it was written for. `=`/`<>` stay keyed on the operators — there is nothing for `a = b` to invoke without one — and the pair grants a **call**, not a property: auto-hashable and **hashable** (§3.6) are unmoved, so an owning choice still keys no hash container. *Declined:* reading §35.2's reachability clause as loose, which leaves a declarable member with no caller. **(c)** The issue's middle part — whether a second `Dispose()` is a *use* — was **settled by v0.299 the other way from this lane's recommendation** (§28.2: it is, and it warns); the recommendation is withdrawn rather than pressed, pressing it after a recorded decision being a design change under process §2's third rule. **Body-locality: local** for both rulings. **Kernel: no contact.**
- **§19.6 / Appendix C.7 — a non-nullable record scrutinee joins the exhaustiveness proof (ruling; [#4372](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4372) closes).** §19.6's proof list named enums, choices, sealed hierarchies and irrefutable arms, and said nothing about a record — while §19.3 already calls a type pattern naming a non-nullable value scrutinee's exact type *always matching*, which is a totality claim §19.6 then refused to consume. **Decided:** a `case` over a non-nullable record scrutinee is statically exhaustive with **no `_` arm** when some unguarded arm is an all-slots-irrefutable destructure for that record type (positional or named), or an exact-type pattern for it. What closes the value space is stated as it is for every other bullet: a record has exactly one shape and is implicitly sealed (§9.6), so covering that shape covers every value. **Coverage is one level deep with no per-slot value-space analysis** — a refutable slot contributes nothing, exactly as a refutable choice-case slot does — and a nullable record scrutinee takes the nullable bullet. The closed-value-space paragraph and the named-destructure clause are conformed in the same stroke, and §21.7's statement-`case` totality grant widens with the registry it is keyed to. **Declined:** closing the list and requiring `_` — it demands a provably dead arm on a match §19.3 already describes as total, and gives a two-case choice a `_`-free match while a one-shape record gets none; rationale §8.2's acceptance of a dead `_` arm was argued for **generic** hierarchies, and its ~1,000-line determination-rule cost argument does not reach a proof that needs no analysis. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact.**
- **§22.5 / C.5 and §9.3 / §22.10 — a parameter binds at most once, and a record's body constructor does not chain (two rulings; [#4389](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4389) and [#4397](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4397) close).** **§22.5:** each supplied argument binds **exactly one** parameter and each parameter is bound by **at most one** supplied argument, so `Log("Failed", message := "Retry")` against `Log(message: string, level: string := "INFO")` is a compile error **at the call**, naming that parameter — *not* an applicability failure, which at an overloaded name would resolve the mistake away rather than diagnose it (§22.6's decline-to-guess stance), and not later-wins, which discards a written argument silently. §22.6 defers the stage to §22.5 by its own road-map sentence and §22.5 never stated it; the compiler has been citing the missing sentence by number. **§9.3:** a record body constructor with a **different** parameter list is **not** required to chain to the primary — §22.10's convenience-constructor rule is a **class** rule and both its grounds (one base call, one capture point) are vacuous for a record, which has no base (§9.6) and no capture fields. Such a constructor initializes the positional storage by **assigning the auto-generated read-only properties**, which §9.1 now makes auto-properties in §23.1's sense, under that section's constructor-assignable context — the spelling §9.2's own example uses — and owes §7.9's obligation on each: a non-defaultable positional field must be assigned on every path, a defaultable one may be left to its default. Chaining with `this(...)` stays available and stays §12.8's. §22.10 gains the one clause that says it is a class rule. *Declined:* extending §22.10 to records — it makes §9.3's differently-parameterized body constructor a pure re-spelling and forecloses the compute-the-arguments shape, with nothing recorded against it, and §22.10's memory-safety ground is a class `new`-site lowering fact the compiler already scopes to classes. **Body-locality: local** for both. **Kernel: no contact.**
- **§14.1 and §11.1 — *instantiation* and *instantiation site* are defined, and a class may implement one generic interface at two instantiations (two rulings; [#4367](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4367) closes, [#4380](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4380) item 4).** **§14.1:** several rules fire *"at the instantiation site"* and no section said which syntactic forms constitute one. **Decided:** an instantiation is the constructed type or member obtained by substituting type arguments, and its site is wherever the program **forms** one — a field, local, parameter or return annotation, a base clause or interface list, a `where` bound, a choice payload, an inline-array element type, a type alias, or a nested type argument, as much as a `new`, a `typeof`/`default` operand, or a generic call at explicit or inferred arguments; `var b: Box<string>;` forms `Box<string>` exactly as `new Box<string>(…)` does, and `G<A>?` forms `G<A>`. §3.6 rule 2's per-instantiation properties, §14.2's constraint checks, §14.4's owning-element restriction, §15.1.1's owning-inline-array element check and §28.5's generic-owned-field check all fire at every such site, and §14.6's instantiation-request graph reads the same forms. *Grounds:* five passages already entail it — §14.4's class-only restriction is stated over a list of five **interface** types and *"rejected at the instantiation site"*, which a `new`-keyed reading could never enforce; §14.6 rejects a never-constructed `Node<Pair<T, T>>?` **field**; §14.2's conditional-member contrast turns on *"`Array<Widget>` is a well-formed type"*; §14.2's bound runs *"at instantiation, after both parameters are substituted"*; and §2.8.2 rule 2 defines instantiation for the artifact interface as substitution at admissible arguments. *Declined:* the `new`-only reading, which leaves §15.1.1's and §28.5's per-instantiation checks siteless at the declarations they govern. **§11.1:** a generic interface may be listed at **two or more instantiations**, directly or through a base class. The class still declares **one** member set and §11.2's matching rule is applied once per obligation under its own substitution, there being no explicit-implementation form — so the class is well-formed exactly when one member set satisfies every obligation, which it does where the obligations' members are §22.6-distinguishable (`CompareTo(int)` beside `CompareTo(string)`) and does not where they differ only in return type, in which case the declarations clash at §11.3. §14.5's non-unique-instantiation clause, which has named this case since v0.292, is **reachable**, not dead. *Declined:* forbidding doubled conformance — it deletes a reachable branch of a standing rule and buys nothing, the indistinguishable cases already being rejected at §11.3. **Body-locality: local** for both — one declaration's written types, its base chain's declarations, and the named interfaces'. **Kernel: n/a.**
- **§28.3's announcement table, §17.6 and §22.3 — `return null;` under `owned T?`, and the parameter as an assignable lvalue (two clarifications; [#4373](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4373) closes).** Row 1's callee-side cell said only *"a fresh or owned value; a borrow is rejected"*, where row 2's already said *"`null` admissible under a nullable declared type"* — an omission, not a rule: K1's polymorphic-null bullet already fixes it (*"A null arm or RHS is compatible with either target, having no value to own"*) and §28.8.1's own worked example `Right2(replace: bool): owned Stream?` opens with `if not replace then return null; end;`, with §22.4's `out owned … when true` example and §7.7's *"owned (or owned-nullable)"* corroborating. The cell now says so. Separately, §17.6's and §22.3's lvalue enumerations both ran *"a mutable local variable, a writable field, an indexer slot, or a property with an accessible setter"* and **omitted the parameter** — accidental on four grounds: §22.3's own `ref`/`out` bar excludes *"an owned local or `owned` parameter"* as an owned-state location, which presupposes that a plain parameter is otherwise admitted; the spec pairs local-and-parameter everywhere else; §22.3 **obliges** the callee to assign every `out` parameter on every normal-completion path, which an unassignable location could not discharge; and §14.1's own `Swap<T>(ref a: T, ref b: T)` body is `a := b; b := temp;`. Both lists name it, with `this` carved explicitly and pointed at §9.4's store rejection and §28.6's borrow receiver. *Declined:* reading the silence as an immutable-parameter rule — no record anywhere states such a decision, and it would be a design change, not a reading. **Kernel: derivation** for the table cell (K1.4's null clause read at K3.2's return position; no kernel text moves, the consume table and axiom register untouched); **n/a** for the lvalue lists. **Body-locality: local**, and vacuous for the cell.
- **§4.2, §16.2, §16.4, Appendix A, §22.1 and §10.3 — six corners of the syntax surface, and a new grammar index (rulings and clarifications; [#4378](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4378) closes, [#4380](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4380) items 1 and 2).** ***Immediate*** in §4.2's boundary carve-out means the operand **after grouping**: parentheses group and introduce no expression of their own (§17.14 admits a parenthesized constant expression as the same expression), so `-(2147483648)` is the carve-out's form and denotes `int.MinValue` exactly as `-2147483648` does, while an intervening **operation** is not — `-(2147483647 + 1)` is §17.14's overflowing constant expression. *Declined:* lexical adjacency, which needs a concept the language has nowhere else and isolates one site from its uniform treatment of grouping. **The fully open `..`** is an ordinary `RangeExpr`, not an index-position-only spelling: both endpoints `null`, `IsOpenEnded` true, `IsEmpty` false, `Contains` holding of every value, never iterable — and, supplying no `T`, admitted **only where a written type supplies one** (a declared `Range<T>` location, an index position, a `Range<T>` parameter), a compile error in an untyped context, on §4.2's own target-typed-constant precedent. *Declined:* index-position-only (no such production exists) and an inferred `int` element type (`Range<char>` is as ordinary). **`step` in a `case` pattern is a syntax error** — A.7's `RangePattern` carries no step clause — and §16.4 now says so rather than leaving the reader to expect §16.4's own diagnostic. That last one earns **Appendix A a new index**: a *grammar-foreclosed-prohibition* table, the mirror of its shared-production over-admission index, listing the three instances verified at this revision (`step` in a pattern; `async` on a constructor, destructor or accessor; `equality skip` on a choice **case**). Like its sibling it states no rule. **An empty method body is legal** (§22.1): A.4's `MethodBody` is `Statement*`, the same production `DestructorDecl` uses, and §21.7 makes falling off the end of a no-return-type method implicit — with the one boundary stated, that an empty body under a **declared return type** is §21.7's every-exit-path error and not an empty-body rule. And **§10.3's colon-list fallback names the underlying-type fact**: for `enum Ratio: double` the rule runs both steps and fails at the second, and the diagnostic *should* report that the type is not one of the eight admissible underlying types, listing them, rather than the literally-failing "not an interface". Appendix D's *Diagnostic identity* paragraph is unchanged and still governs — **a conformance case pins the rejection, not the message**. **Body-locality: local** throughout. **Kernel: n/a.**
- **§21.9, §7.9 and §17.14 — three questions the documents had already answered somewhere else (clarifications; [#4370](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4370), [#4377](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4377), [#4392](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4392) close).** **§21.9's hard error was never `Task`-only:** its own per-arm lead-in names *"the non-trivial-dispose / interface / `Task` hard error"* and its remedy list offers `.Dispose()` and `using var _ :=`, neither of which §17.13 admits over a `Task` — so a `Task`-only reading makes the section's own directed remedies unreachable. The escalation is keyed on the result's **static type**, not on its §28.3 ownership classification, with the fluent-receiver discard the sole exemption; §28.3's must-use *warning* is a different diagnostic at a different site (the implicit drop of a **bound**, undischarged owned local) and the two never met. **Inline-array fields take definite assignment through their element type:** §7.9's *Default initialization* keys on **defaultable** and §17.11 makes an inline array defaultable exactly when its element type is, the owning `[N owned]T?` form named explicitly there — the clause simply never said *"inline array"*, so a rule that was derivable went unstated. A field of `[N]T?`, `[N owned]T?`, or `[N]T` at a defaultable `T` is implicitly slot-defaulted and needs no constructor assignment; `[N]T` at a non-defaultable element type and `[N owned]T` in every form need an initializer or assignment in every constructor. (§9.7 independently bars an `[N owned]…` field on a record, which is why the reported example's second field is rejected for another reason entirely.) **A faulting *local* `const` was already decided — in §21.1:** its *Runtime `const` locals* bullet states that *"an evaluation fault in a form-constant initializer remains a **compile error at the declaration**"*, which is the reported reading at the reported scope. §17.14's *Type restriction* now carries the cross-reference and the one-line derivation — membership in the sublanguage is decided by the **forms** §17.14 lists, not by whether evaluation succeeds, so a faulting initializer fails neither condition and never reaches the runtime-const escape. *Declined:* the evaluation-based reading, which would make §17.14's three worked examples mean different things at different scopes. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact.**
- **§17.13, §30.1 and Appendix C.3 — the discard prohibition is the whole `Task` family, and §30.1's placement rule is grammar-enforced (clarifications; [#4394](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4394) closes).** §17.13's exception bullet is **headed** *"a `Task`-family result may not be discarded"* — a term this specification defines as `Task`, `Task<T>` and `OwningTask<T>` (announcement-table row 2) — while three abbreviations of it named two types: the bullet's own second sentence, the section's closing sentence, and Appendix C.3's invariant. The family is the rule and the abbreviations are corrected, with §30.3's declaration comment supplying the reason (the destructor *"disposes any unconsumed `owned` result"*, which bites hardest on the one family member that has one) and §30.10's *"only supported way to discard a `Task` value"* already covering `OwningTask<T>` by §30.3 subtyping. **The §30.5 seam is stated rather than left implicit:** the rule keys on the **discarded expression's** declared type, so `_ := t;` over an `OwningTask<T>` binding is the error and `_ := await t;` is not — the latter discards the awaited **result**, an owned value in an owned-consuming position (§30.5's Pattern B list), and the task is consumed by the `await`, not abandoned. *Declined:* reading the two-name enumerations as the rule, which would let the one task type carrying an owned result be abandoned by the one form §30.3 names as the prohibition's reason. **§30.1** gains the converse of the `ref`/`out` note two paragraphs below it: A.4 and A.7 admit `async` in the `MethodDecl` and `LambdaExpr` productions only, so `async` on a constructor, destructor, or accessor is a **parse error** and no diagnostic names §30.1's rule — the sentence is stated for the reader, and is now one of Appendix A's three foreclosed prohibitions. **Kernel: derivation** for the §17.13/C.3 edits — the prohibition's footing is unchanged (axiom **A6** and the K3.9/K4.2 site-announced-kill row, as C.3's own citation records); no axiom is extended, no kernel text moves, no consume-table row changes, and §30.5 is cited rather than edited. **Body-locality: local**, and the §30.1 clause adds no compile-time rule at all.
- **Stdlib §2.1 / §2.4 / §3.1 / §7.4 — the line terminator, stated (clarification; [#4402](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4402) and [#4379](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4379) close).** Through v0.299 **no sentence in either document said that `WriteLine` ends a line.** The strings *line terminator* and *newline* appeared twice in the whole corpus — at the `Environment.NewLine` declaration and in the escape table — and every `run` expectation in both conformance corpora rested on the members' **names**. **Decided:** `WriteLine` writes its argument followed by `Environment.NewLine`, the no-argument form the terminator alone; `Write` writes no terminator; `Console.Write` and `Console.WriteLine` **are** `Console.Out.Write`/`WriteLine` — one destination, one interleaving, so a program mixing the two spellings sees them in call order; and `NewLine` is the host platform's terminator (U+000A on Unix-family platforms, U+000D U+000A on Windows), fixed for the process and not varying with the destination written to. `TextWriter` (§7.4) and `StringBuilder.AppendLine` (§3.1) carry the mirrors. A **`null`** argument to a `Write`/`WriteLine` `Object` overload renders as the four characters `null` — spec §18.5's rendering, with no `ToString()` dispatch. **Grounds:** this is what the entire `run` tier already assumed, and what the implementation does; the compiler even cites *stdlib §2.1* as the authority for a terminator §2.1 did not state. **Declined:** fixing the terminator as the literal `"\n"`, which would make `Environment.NewLine` decorative; rendering a null argument as an empty line or as a fault.
- **Stdlib §2.2 / §2.5 / §2.7 / §9.2 / §9.5 / §9.6 — the members whose whole specification was their name (clarification, with the tie and the `From*` conversion ruled; [#4403](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4403) and [#4409](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4409) close).** `Min(a, b)` returns `a` when `a.CompareTo(b) <= 0` and `b` otherwise, `Max` the mirror at `>= 0` — so **a tie returns `a`**, which is the half that decides *which object* a class substitution yields and is what every observable lowering path already returns; `Clamp` returns `low`, `high`, or `value`. A **tick is 100 ns** (10,000,000 to the second, 864,000,000,000 to the day), `From<Unit>(n)` is *n* of that unit computed over ticks in `double` and **truncated toward zero**, carrying the `*` operator's `OverflowException` contract outside the tick range and on `NaN`, and `Total<Unit>` is the whole span in that unit, fraction included. A **seeded `Random`** is deterministic in its seed and its call sequence and reads nothing outside the process; the algorithm stays deliberately unspecified (§1's disclaimer), so a sequence is reproducible within an implementation and across none. The **`Char.Is*` family is defined by Unicode general category** — `IsDigit` is `Nd`, `IsLetter` one of `Lu`/`Ll`/`Lt`/`Lm`/`Lo`, `IsWhiteSpace` the `White_Space` property, and so on — total and never raising, with `ToUpper`/`ToLower` the **simple** case mappings §9.6's `ignoreCase` comparisons already fold under; the `Double`/`Float` `Is*` family reports the operand's **IEEE-754 class** exactly (subnormals and both zeros finite, every NaN payload and sign a NaN); and `IsNullOrWhiteSpace` is `true` for `null`, for `""`, and for an all-whitespace string. **Declined:** ASCII-defined `Char` predicates — which is what ships — because §9.6 already obliges the library to carry Unicode case-folding data, `char` is a full Unicode scalar, and an ASCII rule could never later be widened without changing running programs, where the Unicode rule is an ordinary spec-ahead delta; round-to-nearest-tick and .NET's round-to-the-nearest-millisecond; and specifying `Random`'s generator.
- **Stdlib §9.1 / §9.3 / §2.18 — the two numeric surfaces two conforming implementations could have disagreed on (ruling; [#4408](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4408) and [#4368](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4368) close).** §9.1 fixed the radix set and the input grammar's strictness and never said which characters are digits above radix 10, so `int.Parse("ff", 16)` had two conforming answers. **Decided:** the digits of radix *r* are the first *r* of `0`–`9` then `A`–`Z`; `Parse`/`TryParse` accept **either case**; `ToString(radix)` emits the **lower-case** digits in **sign-and-magnitude** form and takes the same radix set, `ArgumentException` otherwise — so `Parse(n.ToString(r), r) = n` for every value, every integer type and every admitted radix. **Decided:** `decimal`'s no-format `ToString()` (and `G`) is the value's **exact shortest decimal form** — sign, integer digits, and a `.` with fractional digits only where there are any; no exponent, no grouping, **no trailing zeros**, scale not being part of the value — and `MaxValue`/`MinValue` are `±79228162514264337593543950335`. **Grounds:** sign-and-magnitude is the only emission under which the round-trip is total, two's complement making the text depend on the type's width and producing digit strings the `OverflowException` contract then rejects; and the decimal rendering is what spec §4.3's *"straightforward value equality"* already implies and what the runtime's scale normalisation already does. **Declined:** upper-case emission (the `x`/`X` format specifiers already give the caller that choice); two's-complement emission; and .NET's scale-preserving decimal rendering.
- **Stdlib §4.3 / §4.5 / §6.1 / §6.2 / §6.3 / §2.11 / §2.17 / §2.18 and spec §28.11 / §31.4 — the rules that lived somewhere else, or nowhere (clarifications with two ruled points; [#4385](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4385), [#4410](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4410), [#4411](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4411), [#4407](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4407) close).** ***Raises if empty*** now names its type **once for the whole of §4** — `InvalidOperationException`, §1's band 1, the type §4.17/§4.18 and §5 already named for the same condition — with the one seam ruled: `PopAt(index)` is governed by its **index** (`IndexOutOfRangeException`), so `PopFirst`'s `= PopAt(0)` gloss names the position it selects, not the fault it raises. **`Clear()` disposes in `Dispose()`'s order** — reverse-insertion for the ordered families, implementation-defined for the unordered — which spec §28.11's table row and its disposal paragraph now say, and which §4.5's reference implementation is **amended** to do rather than followed. `ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` raises `OperationCanceledException` when cancellation has been requested on the token's source and **returns with no effect otherwise**, `None` never raising. `Mutex`'s **non-reentrancy** (a holder re-acquiring waits on itself, in every acquisition form) and `Semaphore`'s **permit counting** are restated where the types are declared, with the spec §30.12 pointer — locality, not new binding force. `Subscription`'s closed constructor surface moves from a fenced comment into prose; `Guid.FromByteArray`'s comment stops spelling an `ArgumentException` condition with the word §1 reserves for contracts; the seven temporal specifiers render fixed-width zero-padded fields of their own letter count (`yyyy` four, `MM`/`dd`/`HH`/`mm`/`ss` two, `fff` three); and **spec §31.4 states the constructor surface of every declared exception type** — `Exception`'s triad where a declaration shows none, exactly what it shows where it does, under §17.7's closed-constructor-surface rule, which is why `new ArgumentException()` is a compile error and `new FileNotFoundException(path)` is not. **Declined:** naming the empty-egress exception at each of six sites, or in §1 beside band 1 (a per-family rule among cross-family ones); leaving `Clear()`'s order implementation-defined (it is the coverage the issue exists to buy); and **insertion order for `Clear()`**, which is what the runtime helper does and what this document's own reference implementation showed — declined because it would give one collection two disposal orders under two names. **#4411's third part is refuted rather than fixed:** the `async`-body compile error the issue reports as missing is already stated, in stdlib §6.2/§6.3's *Blocking discipline*.
- **[#4384](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4384) and [#4386](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4386) — COMPILER gaps, not spec gaps. No spec edit.** Both were filed as `spec-question`s and neither is one. **#4384:** `bezelc` takes exactly one source file — a second non-flag argument is *"more than one input file given"*, and `--import` names a dependency **artifact**, never a co-compiled source — so neither §2.8.1 rule 2's multi-file module nor §2.5's SCC unit has any expression in the driver's interface. The spec is not silent, vague, or self-contradictory here: §2.4 requires the compiler to take *"all source files belonging to the compilation unit"*, §2.5 requires *"the sources of all SCC members to one compiler invocation"*, §2.6 step 1 parses *"all source files of the compilation unit"* and then declares build-tool integration and project-file format **implementation-defined**. The spec requires an invocation capable of taking several sources and deliberately declines to specify how it is spelled; the driver does not provide one. **The lane declined the fix the issue's own text suggested** — writing into §2.8.1 and §2.5 that *"a compilation is one source file in the current implementation"* — on two independent grounds: it is implementation narration in normative text, which process §7 forbids in terms and which this train has already swept out of two other sections' history; and it would make the normative document track the implementation, the reverse of the project's first rule. The corpus's affected cases are annotated `blocked-on-#4384` rather than reclassified. **#4386: the filed premise is refuted, and that is the useful finding.** The issue asserts that `ensures`/`invariant` are *"unreachable at runtime"* with no way to select checked mode. They are not unreachable: the emitter arms the contract epilogue **whenever a member carries an `ensures` clause or belongs to an invariant class**, reading **no option** — no mode test exists in its body, both call sites are unguarded, and `CodegenOptions` has **no contracts field at all** (a tree-wide grep for one returns nothing). So the compiler behaves as though checked-contracts mode were permanently **on**, and **the real non-conformance is the mirror of the reported one**: there is no *unchecked (release)* mode, which §22.16 makes the **default**. Two consequences ride with it: the three behaviours the issue lists as uncoverable — an `ensures` violation raising `ContractViolationException`, an invariant violation at an instrumentation point, and the value an `old(e)` capture held at a violated postcondition — are writable as `run` cases **today**, with no flag; and a `run` case written against always-on behaviour will **break** when the mode switch lands, so such a case must carry the future flag or be annotated `assumes-always-on-#4386`. **No spec edit is owed either way.** §22.16 already states the mode, its default and its instrumentation points as *"a per-build choice between two conformance modes"* — the identical phrasing §28.2 uses for disposal-checking mode, whose `--checked-disposal` flag the spec has never named — and §2.6 makes the build surface implementation-defined, so naming a switch in §22.16 while §28.2 names none would be a bare asymmetry and naming both would be a new normative CLI surface. Appendix D puts contract clauses in **Core**, so offering the choice is already a Core conformance obligation. Both issues are re-labelled and stay open as compiler tracking items, #4386's with its premise corrected.
- **One ruling was HELD OUT of the train entirely: [#4380](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4380) item 3 — reserving `Equals`, `GetHashCode` and `ToString` against choice case names.** §35.1 routes case-name collision through §11.3 *"with cases counted as members"*, and §11.3 speaks of what a type **declares**, leaving the always-present `Object` virtuals unaddressed; read literally the answer is **classification-dependent** (§35.7 synthesizes `ToString` on a value-like auto-hashable choice, so the name is taken there and free on an owning one), which is a genuine defect. The lane's recommendation was to reserve the three names on every classification — and it was the **only edit in its set that newly rejects a program class**, on a uniformity argument imported to settle a reading rather than on text that points one way. Its author recommended holding it absent a compiler probe (compile `choice C ToString; Other; end C;` at all three classifications and beside a declared `ToString`), which no environment here can run: there is no working build, and no case-vs-member collision check was located in `src/sema/` at all, so the ruling would have landed with its population, its direction and its implementation status all unmeasured. It is excluded; **#4380's other three parts land** (the empty method body, §10.3's diagnostic fact, and doubled generic conformance) and **#4380 stays open for this part**, re-filed as the narrower question it really is: does a choice's member namespace include the `Object` virtual surface for collision purposes, independent of declaration and synthesis? That is a one-line answer and it settles every sibling question after it.

**Migration.**

- **Newly rejected (in the spec's terms).** The consequential one: an explicit conversion with a compile-time-constant operand the conversion would reject, **including in unreachable code** (#4405). That last clause is the honest part and is stated rather than glossed: `if false then var u := uint(-1); end;` compiles today and stops compiling. The rule is not anomalous in that respect — §5.1's constant narrowing, §5.4's constant enum cast, §6.5's constant shift count and §17.14's constant evaluation all reject a faulting constant **wherever it is written**, reachable or not, on identical terms, so §5.2 joining them adds no new posture and every reachable instance faults unconditionally at run time today; what moves is the diagnosis, from the run to the build. Also newly rejected: **a member named `Dispose` at any parameter list on a class or record** (#4404 — widened from the zero-parameter form the compiler rejects); **`virtual` on a member of a `sealed` class** (#4391a — swept across `tests/`, `docs/` and `examples/` at **zero** in-tree occurrences); **`owned Type`** at every position §28.1 lists, and a `Type` element slot claimed as owned in an owning collection (#4393); a **bare `..` in an untyped context** (`var r := ..;`, #4378b — a spelling that had no reading before rather than one that was admitted); and, at the two carve-outs the gate added, **`new Subscription(...)`** at any argument list and a standard-library builtin standing as the substitution for `where T: new()` (#4364, the §17.7 closed-surface rule).
- **Newly accepted (in the spec's terms):** a class declaring **no instance constructor** has an implicit public parameterless one and satisfies `where T: new()` (#4364), excepting the standard-library builtins whose constructor surface §17.7 closes; an expression-position `case` over a **non-nullable record** scrutinee with a total destructure and **no `_` arm**, and with it §21.7's statement-`case` totality grant over such a match (#4372 — the compiler warns today); **`return null;` under an `owned T?` return type** (#4373a — already admitted by K1 and by §28.8.1's own worked example, and already accepted by the compiler); a direct `.Equals(…)` / `.GetHashCode()` call on a choice that declares them and declares no operators, on **every** classification (#4391c — the compiler rejects it today); a **record body constructor that does not chain** to the primary, initializing the positional storage by assigning the auto-generated properties (#4397); a **doubled generic conformance** (`class D: IComparable<int>, IComparable<string>`, #4380 item 4 — already implemented); a **parameter as an assignment target** (#4373b — never in doubt, never stated); and an **empty method body** on an ordinary method (#4380 item 1).
- **Newly defined — most of this train is here**, and the stdlib share of it is semantics that until now was carried by a member's name: `Console`/`TextWriter`/`StringBuilder` line termination, the `Console.Write`/`WriteLine` = `Console.Out.…` identity, `Environment.NewLine`'s value and the rendering of a `null` `Object` argument (#4402, #4379); `Math.Min`/`Max`/`Clamp` and the tie rule (#4403); the 100 ns tick, `From*` and `Total*` (#4403); seeded `Random`'s determinism and the deliberate non-specification of its generator (#4403); the `Char.Is*` family by Unicode general category, `ToUpper`/`ToLower` as the simple mappings, the `Double`/`Float` `Is*` family by IEEE class, and `IsNullOrWhiteSpace` (#4409); `ThrowIfCancellationRequested`'s two halves and `None`'s answer (#4410); the radix digit alphabet, case-insensitive input, lower-case sign-and-magnitude emission and the round-trip it makes total (#4408); `decimal`'s rendering and its bounds (#4368); the empty-egress exception and `PopAt`'s index fault, and `Clear()`'s disposal order (#4385); `Mutex` non-reentrancy and `Semaphore` permits at their declaration sites (#4411); the temporal field widths, `Subscription`'s closed surface and every declared exception type's constructor surface (#4407). In the language: §5.2's constant-operand posture and its two bounds; §28.2's collision consequence and its scope; the post-state of an owned field after an explicit `Dispose()`; move-only adoption under `using var` and the class-and-interface scoping of §28.10's pin enumeration; reverse slot order at all four endings and the absence of a whole-value restoration obligation on a local; `Type`'s tier and every consequence read off it; the implicit parameterless constructor and its `new()` arm; the argument-binding multiplicity rule and its diagnostic class; the record body constructor's non-chaining status and its assignment route, with §7.9's obligation over positional fields (a partially-assigning record constructor now has a stated verdict where it had none); the terms *instantiation* and *instantiation site*; the reading of *immediate* in §4.2's carve-out; the fully open range's typing rule; the `_ := t;` / `_ := await t;` contrast; §30.1's enforcement site; and the inline-array arm of §7.9's defaultable split.
- **Newly warned: nothing.** One diagnostic is narrowed rather than widened — §28.2's use-after-dispose warning is explicitly **not** extended to fields (#4366) — and one claimed narrowing is **withdrawn**: the draft's must-use suppression over a move-only `using var` is reverted, so that lint is exactly where v0.299 left it (#4376). **Observable-behaviour changes without acceptance changes:** an unmarked `using var` over a move-only local now disposes at **its own** block's end, the adoption point (#4376); an owning inline array's scope-end, destructor and program-exit passes now run in reverse slot order (#4388); and an owning collection's `Clear()` now disposes in reverse-insertion rather than insertion order (#4385b). **No ramp is owed** — this train schedules no tightening, and a ramp is a ratchet-class artifact.

The tracking issue must name the test, not just the check: the row flips to a reject with the accepting control retired, and its comment is re-authored rather than re-cited. **(2) #4409** — `src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Calls2.cpp:592-632` lowers the whole `char` classification family onto `<ctype.h>`: `IsDigit`→`isdigit`, `IsLetter`→`isalpha`, `IsLetterOrDigit`→`isalnum`, `IsWhiteSpace`→`isspace`, `IsUpper`/`IsLower`/`IsPunctuation`/`IsControl` likewise, with `ToUpper`/`ToLower` on `toupper`/`tolower`, the argument sign-extended to `i32` and handed straight to libc. That is not merely ASCII-narrow, it is **undefined behaviour**: `char` is a 32-bit Unicode scalar and those functions are defined only for values representable as `unsigned char` or `EOF`, so every operand above U+00FF is UB today. Every `src/` and `tests/` citation above was **re-derived against the current tree** and read, never run; the lane specifications' citations were checked one by one and a substantial share of them had moved — `checkUserDeclaredDispose` by ~250 lines, the §19.6 exhaustiveness dispatch by ~1,400, `localSlot` by 20, the radix emitter by ~57 — because three of the four lanes were authored against an older HEAD. Two lane citations did not survive re-derivation at all and are replaced above rather than carried: `ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp:2240-2308` for the §5.2 conversion arm and `:13489`/`TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:7559` for the implicit constructor.
- **Kernel classification — every §28-touching ruling is a *derivation*; no axiom is named, extended, or added, no kernel text moves, no register row moves, and the consume table is untouched.** #4366: **K9 + K9.2 read at its own scope + K3.9 + K4.1 + K5.6**. #4376: **K3.12 + K3.13's own move-only parenthetical + K1.5**, with **A5 read, not extended** (the pin bars moving *out of* a `using var`; adoption moves *in*). #4388: **K9 + K3.15 + K3.14 + K1**, the forward-vs-reverse choice settled by uniformity with §15.3's already-pinned pass rather than derived. #4393: **K1.6**'s runtime-managed exemption, discharged by the interning guarantee §17.10 and stdlib §2.13 already state, with **K2**'s always-live characterisation — recorded for the record, a reviewer who reads tier *membership* as a grant rather than a derivation would place it under **A10**. #4373a: **K1.4**'s null clause read at K3.2's return position. #4394b: axiom **A6** and the **K3.9/K4.2** site-announced-kill row, unchanged — the clarification names the type set the rule was always stated over. #4404: **K4.1 + K3.9**. Every other ruling in the train is outside §28 and §30.5 and carries no kernel line. **Body-locality: local throughout** — each rule reads one declaration's modifiers or member list, one call's argument list against one signature, one construct's arms, one body's control flow, or one written type and the declarations it names; no per-body fact is consumed from another body, no fact-discharge is taken, no carve-out is added and no invariant is amended. **This train schedules no tightening, so no ramp is owed.**

- **Residual recorded rather than fixed, and open questions recorded rather than decided.** **Residual, pre-existing and not created here:** for `OwningArray<T>`, §28.11's and stdlib §4.3's *"reverse-insertion order"* and **reverse index order** coincide under `Add`-only use and **diverge** the moment `Insert(0, x)` has been called — the term has named the ordered families' disposal order since well before this revision, and §4.5's reference implementation (amended here to reverse index order, `_count - 1 - i`) is the place a reader meets the divergence. #4385b's ruling makes `Clear()` follow `Dispose()`, which is the point; which of the two orders *"reverse-insertion"* denotes after an `Insert` is the older question, and it is recorded, not answered. **Open questions carried forward, each named rather than folded in silently:** `Semaphore(initialCount, maxCount)`'s **`maxCount` has no stated meaning and no reachable effect** — permits are returned only by disposing an acquired token, and the runtime stores the cap and enforces nothing (`src/runtime/bezel_runtime_sync.cpp:440-455`, whose own comment calls it advisory) — so it either validates `initialCount` or should be retired at a subtraction review ([#4417](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4417)); **§9.9's declaration-site rejection of a non-defaultable local against §7.9's read-site rule** ([#4416](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4416)); the **abstract-class / `where T: new()` seam** — §14.2's class arm is written over what a class *declares*, and this revision's implicit-constructor clause now supplies one to a class that declares none, which an `abstract` class also does while being unconstructible; **§22.5's unstated companion** — the section now says a parameter is bound at most **once** and still never says that every **required** parameter must be bound, which the compiler diagnoses and no sentence states; and **§17.13's nullability keying**, where the discard rule says *"the discarded expression's declared type"* and states no stripping rule of its own, while the announcement table's Keying rule strips nullability for its rows — so `_ := someNullableTask;` over a `Task?` escapes the check (`isTaskShapedRef` requires `!t->nullable`, `src/sema/ExprTypecheck.cpp:3166`). ### v0.301 changelog (v0.300 → v0.301)

**The conformance-corpus train.** Every item below was found the same way: a lane tried to write a conformance case for a stated rule and could not, because the documents did not settle the verdict. Lanes were instructed to record the readings and a recommendation instead of embedding a guess in a case, and twenty-two such reports became this revision. The corpus work itself is not normative and is not described here; what follows is only what moved in the documents.

- **§5.4 / Appendix C.1 — a compile-time-constant enum operand at an enum-to-integer cast is a compile error at the cast site (ruling).** §5.4 defines `I(e)` as two steps — to the underlying type, then §5.2's `I(u)` — and #4405 (v0.300) put the constant-operand compile error into §5.2 without sweeping §5.4, whose own prose still promised `OverflowException` unqualified. The section therefore took **both** postures on one question: `E(n)` at a constant `n` was already *"a compile error at the cast site"* while `I(e)` at a constant `e` deferred to run time. **Decided:** §5.2's rule carries through the delegation unchanged, so `int(HttpStatus.Huge)` at `long`-backed `HttpStatus` is rejected where it is written, while a local-variable operand still faults at run time (§17.14 does not admit a local read as constant). §5.2's two bounds ride across with it — the rule reads the **operand**, the cast expression is still **not** a constant expression, and a constant operand the conversion accepts converts as before (`int(Priority.Low)` yields `0`). **Grounds:** one section cannot decide one question two ways; §5.3's general rule *already* cites §5.4 for a constant-operand compile error, a citation only half-true until now; and rationale §9.12 states the design intent outright — the two-step definition exists *"so the checked posture above is applied by the second step rather than restated per spelling."* **Declined:** the literal runtime reading. This is the shape #4405's own gate caught in §16.3, one section further out.
- **§9.7 / §28.3 — the admitted set for a borrow-bearing record return is closed at three forms (ruling).** §9.7 said a borrow-bearing record may not be returned where the return-type rules *"cannot establish a sufficient lifetime"*, and stated no decision procedure: §28.3's announcement table is keyed on class and interface returns, and its row 7 puts value types outside it. The uncovered middle was the standard library's own span shape — an instance method returning a record that borrows the receiver's `owned` field — which stdlib §4.14 works for its types while the language admitted it nowhere. **Decided:** admissible exactly when every borrow carried has a source the caller re-establishes at the call site, closed at **receiver-sourced**, **static-storage-sourced**, and the **null-source** form; rejected at locals, `using var`s, `owned` parameters, unbound temporaries, and a **plain parameter** of the returning method. Rejection is per return expression, never at the declaration. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): admitting parameter-sourced returns, which is not one sentence but a caller-side source-set algebra nothing today announces — a caller of `static method Trim(s: ReadOnlySpan<byte>): ReadOnlySpan<byte>` would bind a span with no source at all, the value-carried form of the asymmetry §28.3 clause 4 already rejects for reference returns. §28.3 gains a cross-reference clause only; row 7's cells are unchanged.
- **§19.3 / §19.6 — named destructuring reaches a class-typed scrutinee (ruling, stating what three sites already said).** §19.6 concluded that a sealed hierarchy is matched exhaustively by named-destructure arms, while its own sealed-hierarchy bullet said class leaves are matched by type-test patterns and §19.3 said classes have no positional-destructuring surface. The reading that would have made §19.6's sentence a leftover was **not available**: named destructuring with a class head is a graduated design change (proposal 0065, v0.224), and rationale §3.14 records that *"a class's public readable properties **are** its encapsulation-respecting match surface."* §19.3's own *Class* slot-resolution bullet, §35.5 and Appendix A.7 already state it. **Decided:** §19.3's restriction is on the **positional** surface only; §19.6's bullet is corrected; the concluding sentence stands unedited.
- **§28.9 — the ceremony exemption is keyed on the produced type where a producer exists, and is a property of a declared class (ruling + clarification).** Two consecutive sentences pointed opposite ways for `var t: IThing := new TrivialThing();`. **Decided:** the produced-type arm decides wherever a statically-known producer exists, in both directions; the interface sentence governs the arm the key selects, which reaches every site with no known producer whose declared type is an interface *and* every producer whose produced type is itself an interface. Separately, the exemption is now stated to be a property of a **declared class**, computed from that declaration and carried in the artifact interface — so it is not defined for a compiler-synthesized frame, and the must-use lint reaches a frame-typed owned local on §28.3's ordinary terms. That second clause settles which of two verdicts §29.11's bound-query warning has.
- **§29.11 / §28.3 — the suppression set is closed, and its fifth member is stated on both sides (ruling).** §29.11 stated only a *suppression* (*"suppressed where the binding's consumption point is statically visible"*), presupposing a warning it never stated, and the condition it named — that the value was used — is none of §28.3's four. A mere use discharges nothing. **Decided:** §29.11 now states the positive half, and §28.3's suppression sentence gains the spent-enumeration-right condition **and** an explicit closure clause, so the two sections name one set rather than four-plus-one. Conditions are not renumbered and no count is asserted.
- **§31.2.3 — an unreachable `catch` arm draws a warning (ruling).** The section said specific types *should* appear first and that non-exhaustiveness draws nothing, and was silent on an arm an earlier unguarded arm already covers. Ruled a **warning**, not an error: an error would newly reject programs the current spec admits with no prior revision having scheduled that tightening, which §2's Ratchet rule makes a design change. §31.2.1's *provably dead* rule is distinguished rather than extended — that is a property of one arm in isolation, decidable from its type, where this is a property of the sequence and is repaired by reordering. The rule is keyed to `catch` arms and deliberately **not** extended to `case` type-pattern arms, where coverage is a per-pattern rather than per-type question; that asymmetry is stated in the text rather than left for a reader to find.
- **stdlib §6.5 / §28.14 — a captured constructor parameter is excluded only where it contributes a borrow source (ruling).** stdlib §6.5 excluded captured constructor parameters flatly, on the ground that *"a constructor parameter is a borrow of a caller local"* — which is false of a value-typed or runtime-managed one. §28.3 assigns the source sets this reads: *"a value-typed capture contributes nothing … a `string` nothing."* **Decided:** the exclusion keys on the borrow source, which is what §28.14's `this` arm already tests. The v0.180 record's parenthetical is narrowed to its own stated reason under v0.298's newer text; it is a changelog entry, not a rationale decline or a `DECLINED.md` row, so §2's design-change trigger does not fire.
- **§8.5 / §35.7 — a choice's `ToString` (clarification + ruling).** The rendering of a choice was pinned nowhere: §35.7 fixed the shape and neither it nor §8.5 said whether the head is qualified, so no `run` case could state its first line. **Decided:** a value-like auto-hashable choice renders with an **unqualified** head; for every other choice **no default is generated** — a statically-known receiver takes §35.7's use-site error, a boxed receiver renders the qualified type name. The second half is a ruling and gated as one. **Declined and recorded:** a synthesized default for the rest, which would have to render owned and borrowed class payloads on the ground §8.5's inline-array bullet already refuses.
- **§21.10 — the member-signature prohibition binds enclosing and sibling declarations (clarification).** The prohibition read unqualified and so appeared to forbid `public method Twin(): Pair` inside a local `record Pair`, on a justification (*"the name is simply not in scope at any signature"*) that is false inside the local type's own body. The decisive ground is the section's own framing: a local type is an ordinary record and *"the sole relaxation is where the declaration may appear"* — the restrictive reading is not a relaxation. §21.10's separate field-type rule is untouched, so a self-typed field remains an error. This narrows the v0.225 entry's stated scope.
- **§15.3 — no must-use warning attaches at an owning inline array's auto-drop (ruling).** §15.3 named no diagnostic either way while the writing reference presupposed one. The reading that both move-only kinds warn is a **recorded decline** — the v0.300 gate withdrew exactly that clause (#4376), with the reopening bar *"a rule, stated somewhere, defining that warning for owning inline arrays"* — so it was unavailable here; the reading that neither warns contradicts §35.4's shipped sentence. The remaining reading is stated directly, and the #4376 row is marked **foreclosed**: the bar is answered in the negative rather than met.
- **Smaller clarifications.** §15.3's call-site spelling at `(owned x: V)` for a move-only `V` (unmarked at both parameter spellings; §22.6's declaration guard already presupposed it, and the owning-match scrutinee is named as the exception). §15.4.1's witness at a value kind is spelled unmarked, which §11.8 already stated generally. §35.4 states the static-field rejection for an owning choice where the classification is defined, and §15.3's citation of *"rule 4's residual"* is corrected — (g) is an exception to the residual, not an instance of it. §28.2's carve-out is stated by admission rather than exclusion: an interface may declare `Dispose()`, the rule reaching classes and records only. §35.7's exemption is per member. §15.4's target contexts name field initializers. §17.11's unit-type row names its source spelling, which Appendix A.5 already admitted. §12.10 no longer names a family of mixed class/interface cycles that cannot exist. §21.9 states that a bare accessor read is an admissible expression statement. §27.3 admits a named unit-typed lambda parameter. Appendix C.10 and §25.1 agree on the diagnostic class of a declared `operator ++`.
- **§30.10 — `Task.Delay`'s cancellation argument is a `:=` default, not an overload pair (editorial currency).** Not a fresh call: v0.290's R1 retired the overload-pair spelling for nine methods and named `Task.Delay` explicitly; the stdlib and the writing reference already carry the defaulted form. §30.10's bullet was the one line that ruling did not sweep, and the sweep found no other — §30.10's remaining overload language is `Task.WhenAll`'s three forms, which the same row's carve-outs legitimately keep.
- **Newly rejected (in the spec's terms):** an enum-to-integer cast whose operand is a declared enum constant outside the target's range; a borrow-bearing record return sourced from a plain parameter; a `ToString()` call on a statically-known non-auto-hashable choice receiver. **Newly warned:** an unreachable `catch` arm. **Newly admitted:** a captured constructor parameter contributing no borrow source; an interface declaring `Dispose()`; a local body record naming itself in its own member signatures; a named unit-typed lambda parameter. **Newly defined:** the unit type's source spelling at `default(())`; a choice's rendering; whether a compiler-synthesized frame is trivial-dispose.
- **Kernel classification — every §28-touching item is a *derivation*.** No axiom is named, extended or added; no kernel text moves; no register row moves; the consume table is untouched. §28.9's key: K1.6, verified value-keyed in the register rather than assumed — K1.6 speaks of *"trivial-dispose class **instances**"* and *"any undischarged trivial-dispose **value**"*, never of a declared type. §29.11/§28.3: K3.14's lint predicate only; the alternative (a new axiom A16) was considered and rejected as disproportionate for a lint that changes no acceptance, and is recorded rather than left silent. §9.7/§28.3: K2.4 + K2.1 + K2.3. stdlib §6.5/§28.14: K2.1 + K2.2 read at A11's admission arms. **Body-locality: local** for every item.
- **One recommendation was refuted at the gate and its opposite landed.** The docket recommended that when a consuming call raises, the caller keeps the obligation and the binding is still owned in the `catch` arm. It contradicts K3.3's consume-table row (post-state *moved-from*, disposal moment *"none here — the callee's"*), §28.8.1's own *"moved-from from the moment of the move expression's evaluation"*, and §22.9's *"One owner at every instant, on every edge"* — under which the caller and the callee's unwind would both hold the obligation, a double dispose. Its stated ground was also wrong: §28.3's exception-path discharge disposes the parameter during unwinding and `CancellationTokenSource` is cancel-on-dispose, so nothing is stranded. **Decided:** transfer completes at call entry; the binding is moved-from on the exception edge as on the normal one; a `catch` arm may not dispose it again. A raise *before* the call is entered leaves the temporary untransferred, and §28.3's unbound-temporary rule already covers it.
- **Compiler status — spec-ahead-of-impl deltas, each owed a tracking issue.** #4405's §5.2 constant-operand rule has **no implementation at all**, so this train widens an existing delta rather than opening one. §28.14's capture reduction is asymmetric between parameters and locals — the parameter branch applies no type filter while the local branch drops value-typed locals — so the compiler today rejects a captured value-typed *parameter* and admits a captured value-typed *local* at the same arm, an asymmetry no document states in either direction. `checkRecordBorrowEscapesOnReturn` rejects only returns rooted at a tracked owned local and leaves a parameter-rooted one to pass, while the caller-side root of `Util.Trim(s)` is the type name and attaches no source — a real use-after-free shape, and the reason §9.7's parameter arm is closed here. Pre-existing and adjacent: §28.2's v0.300 widening to *"whatever its parameter list"* is unimplemented; §35.7's existing exemption admits fewer choices than the spec states; `isBorrowableType` returns false for an inline array, so a captured move-only local is filtered out of an order test §28.9 says applies.
- **Compiler claims are source reads.** No build exists in the authoring environment (clang 18; the compiler needs 21). Every `src/` citation above was read, not run; where a probe would settle a question it is named in the record rather than asserted.
- **Doc-only: 55 edits across 6 files** — 38 in the spec, 7 in the code-generation reference, 4 version headers, 3 in `DECLINED.md` (one row amended, two added), 2 in the stdlib, 1 in the changelog. The code-generation reference moves to v0.301 on both of its pin assertions.
- **Gate rounds.** The five drafting trains ran a shared composition gate over the union of their edits, re-checking every `old` against the combined intermediate state rather than the pristine file; 55/55 applied clean. Three trains corrected the docket that briefed them: §19.3's answer was already recorded, §5.4's supporting evidence was in §5.3 rather than where the docket looked, and §15.4's supporting citation was simply wrong — the real evidence was two corpus cases that already depend on the admission. A separate adversarial pass over the revision's conformance work returned DO-NOT-LAND on three findings, all applied there.
