### v0.302 changelog (v0.301 → v0.302)

**The carried-forward train: every open `spec-defect` and `spec-question` issue on the tracker, plus the four filings v0.300 recommended by name and nobody opened.** v0.300's *Issues* paragraph ends *"Recommended further filings, named above: the abstract-class / `where T: new()` seam; §22.5's unstated every-required-parameter rule; §17.13's nullability keying; and the `OwningArray<T>` reverse-insertion residual"* — and for a whole revision nothing followed. Those four are filed here ([#4439](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4439), [#4440](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4440), [#4441](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4441), [#4442](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4442)) and ruled in the same train, beside the four questions v0.299–v0.301 carried forward ([#4415](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4415), [#4416](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4416), [#4417](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4417), [#4423](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4423)) and the part of [#4380](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4380) v0.300 held out. **Two outcomes are not ordinary resolutions and are stated plainly: [#4429](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4429)'s filed premise is refuted by the very commit that filed it and it takes no spec edit at all; and #4380's held-out ruling lands without the probe it was held for**, because what the probe was to establish is now settled from the text on one side and from a source read on the other — and the source read **corrects v0.300's own record**, which reported that no case-vs-member collision check existed.

- **§9.9 — a constructor-only record's *local* is governed by §7.9, not by a declaration-site rejection (clarification; [#4416](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4416) closes).** §9.9's worked-example prose said *"`default(Port)`, a `Port`-typed field **or local** declared with no initializer … are compile errors"*. That sentence is wrong twice over, and its own section already says so: §9.9's normative bullet states the rejection as *"default initialization of `R`-typed storage (§7.9)"*, which is the right concept. §7.9 rejects a non-defaultable **field** only when it neither carries an initializer nor is assigned in every constructor — a declaration with no initializer is perfectly legal beside a constructor that assigns it — and rejects a non-defaultable **local** only at a read before assignment. §28.3 states the local half a third time (*"`var x: T;` without an initializer at a non-defaultable `T` is **uninitialized**: it holds no value … and may not be read until assigned (§7.9)"*). **Decided:** the example prose now names default initialization of `Port`-typed *storage* and says explicitly that a `Port`-typed local is not among the errors — `var p: Port;` is legal and reading `p` before assignment is not. **Grounds:** two sections and §9.9's own bullet against one example sentence; and the declaration-site reading makes the two-step declare-then-assign shape unwritable for every constructor-only record, which is a real pattern (assign under a condition, assign in a loop) and not something the property was ever meant to forbid. The site split is principled and is now stated: a **field** has no flow to analyse, so its declaration *is* the right site; a local has one. **Declined:** nothing new (the nullability-vs-defaultability keying was already declined at v0.299). **Body-locality: local** — the rule consumes no cross-body information; it is definite assignment as §7.9 already defines it. **Kernel: no contact.** Corpus: `s9_9_0006` is a *field* case whose constructor assigns nothing, so its reject verdict is unchanged and its `constructor-only` diagnostic still names the right property.

- **§14.2 — an `abstract` or `closed` class never satisfies `where T: new()` (ruling; [#4439](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4439) closes).** §14.2's class arm admitted a class that *"declares no instance constructor at all, in which case §22.7's implicit parameterless constructor, which is `public`, satisfies it on the same terms"* — and §12.5 says *"`new` on an abstract or `closed` class is a compile error"*, as does Appendix C. So `abstract class Shape` with no declared constructor satisfied a constraint whose sole purpose, `new T()` in the generic body, the language rejects. §14.2 excludes interfaces explicitly and choices explicitly; abstract and `closed` classes — the third unconstructible kind — were named nowhere in the arm. **Decided:** they never satisfy it, whether they declare a `public` parameterless constructor or take §22.7's implicit one, with the diagnostic at the **instantiation site** — the same footing as the interface exclusion, and the site that names the type the author wrote rather than a `new T()` in a body they may not own. Appendix C.4's constraint row carries the exclusion. **Grounds:** a constraint that guarantees an operation the language forbids is not a constraint; and the seam's *population* is what changed at v0.300 — an abstract class ordinarily declares no constructor, so #4364's implicit-constructor clause moved this from a corner (an abstract class that declares `public constructor()`) to the default shape of every abstract hierarchy. **§22.7's implicit constructor is deliberately untouched:** an abstract or `closed` base needs it as §12.8's inserted `base()` target — the section names the `closed class Shape` / `sealed class Circle(radius: double): Shape` shape as its motivating case — so the exclusion is about the constraint, never about the constructor's existence. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): admitting the substitution and leaving the rejection to `new T()`. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact.**

- **§22.5 — every parameter that declares no default must be bound (clarification; [#4440](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4440) closes).** §22.5 stated the upper bound on binding and never the lower one: *"each parameter is bound by **at most one** supplied argument"*, with no sentence obliging a required parameter to be bound at all. Under the stated rules `Log()` against `Log(message: string, level: string := "INFO")` satisfies §22.5 completely. The compiler has diagnosed it all along and **cites this section while doing it** — `"required parameter \`X\` is not supplied (§22.5)"` (`src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp:11912`) — which is the shape worth fixing: a diagnostic whose authority is a section that does not contain the rule, reached through the one §22.5 binder that serves calls, `new` expressions and record construction alike. **Decided:** the lower bound is stated, with its §22.6 disposition named explicitly, because it is the *opposite* of the at-most-once clause's: a duplicate binding is *"not an applicability failure, so at an overloaded name it is diagnosed rather than resolved away"*, while an **unbound** required parameter makes the candidate **inapplicable**, so a sibling overload still resolves and the error is reported only where no candidate survives. Stating both together is the point — the contrast is what a reader needs. Appendix C.4's row carries it. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact.**

- **§17.13 — the `Task`-family discard prohibition strips nullability (ruling; [#4441](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4441) closes).** §17.13 stated the prohibition over a *family* and no keying rule of its own; it does not mention nullability anywhere. Its neighbour does: §28.3's announcement table carries an explicit **Keying** rule — *"with nullability stripped (`Task?`, `IEnumerable<T>?`, `T?` qualify as their unstripped kinds)"* — so the language strips nullability wherever it keys on the `Task` family for **ownership** and said nothing where it keys on the same family for **abandonment**. **Decided:** the keying strips nullability here too; `_ := someNullableTask;` over a `Task?` is the same compile error, and where the operand may be null the supervised spelling takes the null check with it (`if t <> null then Task.FireAndForget(t); end;`). **Grounds:** §17.13's own sentence says the rule exists because *"disposing a task abandons a running operation — a semantic, not a leak, concern"*, and a non-null `Task?` abandons exactly the operation a `Task` does. A nullable static type changes what may be absent, not what is abandoned when it is present; without the strip, any API returning a nullable task is a supported route around the rule `Task.FireAndForget` exists to enforce. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): the carve-out admitting `Task?` discards. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact** (§17.13's discard is a §28.3-classified consumption, but this clause decides only which static types the §17.13 exception reads, adding no ownership rule). **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** `isTaskShapedRef` requires `!t->nullable` (`src/sema/ExprTypecheck.cpp:3165`) and is what the discard path calls (`:16756`), so a `Task?` discard compiles today; the same predicate gates four other call sites whose strip decision is **not** settled here and must each be taken on its own (notably §30.1's async-readiness use). Issue filed.

- **§28.11 — the ordered owning collections dispose in reverse *storage* order, and "reverse-insertion" is retired (ruling; [#4442](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4442) closes).** §28.11 stated the order twice as *"reverse-insertion"*, stdlib §4.3's v0.300 `Clear()` clause inherited the term — and stdlib §4.5's reference implementation walks `_count - 1 - i`, *"reverse index order"*, a different order the moment the two stop coinciding. `OwningArray` declares `Insert(index, owned item)` and `OwningLinkedList` declares `AddFirst`/`AddBefore`/`AddAfter`, so positional ingress makes them diverge; `OwningArray.Sort` and `Reverse` make one reading **unimplementable**, because these types store elements and not arrival order, so after a sort the insertion order is not recoverable from the collection at all. **Decided:** reverse **storage** order, stated per family — descending index for `OwningArray`, tail-to-head for `OwningLinkedList`, pop order for `OwningStack`, the reverse of dequeue order for `OwningQueue` — with the unordered families implementation-defined as before, and `Clear()` following `Dispose()` as v0.300 ruled. **Grounds:** storage order is observable, computable at every point in a collection's life, and **equal to the old term wherever the old term was well defined** — `OwningStack` and `OwningQueue` have append-only ingress, so nothing changes for them, and an `Add`-only `OwningArray` disposes exactly as before. No program that relied on the stated order changes behaviour. **`Channel<T>` keeps the phrase** (spec §30.15, stdlib §6.9) and is deliberately not swept: a channel is FIFO with no positional ingress, so insertion order *is* its storage order and the term is exact there. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): per-element arrival tracking, which is what an insertion-keyed rule would cost. **Kernel: no contact.**

- **§35.1 — `Equals`, `GetHashCode` and `ToString` are reserved against choice case names on every classification (ruling; [#4380](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4380) closes, its last part).** §35.1 says a case name *"may not collide with any member name of the choice (the §11.3 member rules apply with cases counted as members)"*, and §11.3 speaks of what a type **declares** — leaving the three always-reachable names unaddressed, and the literal answer **classification-dependent**, since §35.7 synthesizes `ToString` on a value-like auto-hashable choice and not on an owning one. v0.300 held this out: its lane recommended reserving all three on a **uniformity** argument, which is an argument imported to settle a reading rather than text that points one way, and it was the only edit in its set that newly rejected a program class. **The ground it lacked arrived in v0.301.** That revision ruled that a non-auto-hashable choice generates no `ToString` default and draws a use-site compile error *"which the author removes **by declaring the member**"*, and made the `Equals`/`GetHashCode` exemption **per declared member** on every classification. So on every classification those three names are the stated **remedy**, and a case holding one of them would put the remedy out of reach for exactly the choices v0.301 addressed. **Decided:** reserved everywhere, on that ground rather than on uniformity. A second, independent consequence is recorded with it: keying the reservation on classification would make §3.6's auto-hashable flip legalize or outlaw a case name as a side effect, which its recorded flip-consequence list does not carry. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): the classification-keyed reading. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact.** **The probe is discharged rather than waived, and it corrects the v0.300 record.** v0.300 reported that *"no case-vs-member collision check was located in `src/sema/` at all"*. There is one: `Resolver::checkTypeDuplicates` (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:4373`) walks `TypeSymbol::members`, and choice cases **are** members — `ChoiceCaseSymbol : MemberSymbol`, pushed at `src/sema/SymbolCollection.cpp:535` with the comment *"choice cases live alongside members, like enum constants"*. So `case ToString;` beside a **declared** `ToString()` is diagnosed today. What is not diagnosed is a case colliding with a **synthesized or inherited** member, which is precisely and only this ruling's delta — a far narrower gap than an absent check, and one whose fix has an obvious home. Issue filed. *(Source reads at `5a01b840`; no build exists in this environment — clang 18, the compiler needs 21 — so these are reads of the code, not runs of it.)*

- **stdlib §6.3 — `maxCount` is a construction-time permit ceiling (ruling; [#4417](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4417) closes).** The two-argument constructor took a parameter with no stated meaning and, as filed, no reachable effect. **Decided:** `new Semaphore(initial, max)` raises `ArgumentException` when `max < 1` or `initial > max`; the one-argument form has no ceiling; and the ceiling needs no run-time enforcement thereafter — which is the fact the section now states rather than leaving a reader to wonder at. A permit is returned **only** by disposing a `SemaphoreToken`, and a token exists only because an acquisition consumed a permit, so the count can never rise above where it started: there is no release-more-than-you-took path, which is the shape a ceiling exists to guard in semaphore APIs that release by count. **Grounds:** of the issue's two readings, validation is the one under which the runtime is merely missing a check rather than storing a dead field, and it is a ruling rather than a public-surface removal. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): retiring the two-argument form at a subtraction review — a declared constructor's removal is a design change needing a proposal (process §6), and the reopening bar names the migration it would owe. **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** the runtime stores `maxCount` and enforces nothing (`src/runtime/bezel_runtime_sync.cpp:438-452`), and its own comment cites *"§6.3 two-arg ctor documents maxCount as a cap"* — which §6.3, until this revision, did not. Issue filed.

- **stdlib §6.10 — "first fault" is first in real time, and concurrent selection is unspecified (ruling; [#4423](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4423) closes).** §6.10 promised that `await Join()` re-raises the **first** fault, and a reader naturally asks *first by what order*. Its own fault-policy bullet answers causally — *"first fault wins and cancels siblings via the scope's token"* — which is a statement about a race, not a selection rule over a set. **Decided:** "first" is first in real time, the fault that triggered the cancellation, and never spawn order; where two children fault concurrently, **which one re-raises is unspecified**. What holds at every arity is what a program can rely on: exactly one child fault re-raises, never an aggregate, and every sibling is cancelled. **Grounds:** spawn order fixes nothing about children already running concurrently, and pinning it would oblige the scope to *order fault delivery* rather than report it — a cost with no beneficiary, since the load-bearing half of the sentence is the no-aggregation posture rationale §13.5 records. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): the spawn-order reading. **Consequence for the corpus:** `l6_10_0005` spawns one faulting child and therefore tests the whole deterministic guarantee; the two-fault case it could not write is now *specified* not to exist, so the case is complete rather than under-claiming, and no expectation may be written over concurrent selection.

- **The code-generation reference's third pin, and the one place it was stale (editorial; [#4415](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4415) closes).** v0.301 gated the document's **citation basis** after it sat 32 revisions behind its own validation line. It left a third assertion loose: section 5's stdlib name index states the revision it was transcribed from, and that line read **v0.282** while the other two read v0.301 — 19 revisions, over the one part of the file whose entire job is exact signatures. A check of the index against every stdlib signature changed since v0.282 found it **substantially current** — the collapsed-overload families (`Task.Delay`, `Directory.Delete`, `Pad*`, `Math.Round`, `IndexOf`, `CompareTo`), the retired `Math` trigonometry and `Math.E`, the retired `Stopwatch.Restart`, `string.IsNullOrEmpty` and static `string.Compare`, the generic `Math.Sign<T>` marked NOT pure, the collection-literal target interfaces and their ten `FromCollectionLiteral` witnesses, `E.NameOf`/`E.FromNameOrNull`, and the `IReadOnlySpan<byte>` byte-accessor extension are all present and correct — with **one residue**: `FileStream` was still listed as the two pre-collapse constructor overloads rather than the single `access: FileAccess := FileAccess.ReadWrite` form. Fixed, the line moved, and `check_docs.sh`'s PIN check extended so all three pins move together or the gate fails. The new check was self-tested by planting v0.290 (it fired) and restoring (clean).

- **Doc-only: 27 edits across 4 documents** (spec §9.9 ×2, §14.2 ×2, §17.13, §22.5, §28 ×2, §28.11 ×2, §35.1, Appendix C ×3; stdlib §4.3, §6.3, §6.10; the code-generation reference ×5; the four version headers), 6 new `DECLINED.md` rows, and one `scripts/check_docs.sh` check. Applied as **one dry-run sequence**, each `old` re-checked against the combined intermediate state rather than the pristine file — clean at both passes, including the two edits that depend on an earlier edit's output (the code-generation reference's transcription line is fixed to v0.301 and then moved to v0.302 by the header pass). `check_docs.sh` passes on all eleven checks.

- **Gate round: four sites were still stating the old rule after the rulings had landed correctly in their own sections** — the shape that produced ten blocking findings across the v0.299 and v0.300 gates and that no mechanical check catches. (1) §14.2's **constraint table** row still read *"Class types with a `public` parameterless constructor"* with no exclusion — the row a reader consults before the prose. (2) Axiom register row **A6** and (3) §28's carve-out parenthetical both named the discard ban over *"`Task`/`Task<T>`"*: two thirds of the family, with no keying, while their own cited section now defines both. (4) Appendix C's choice row stated the case-name collision rule and stopped short of the reserved names. All four fixed in the same commit. **A6's edit is not an axiom amendment:** the axiom's content — abandoning a running operation is a decision, not a disposal — is untouched; the row now names the family and the keying that §17.13, which it already cited, defines. **Kernel: no contact** on that ground.

- **Corpus.** Swept by construct for every verdict-changing ruling — `where T: new()` beside an abstract or `closed` class, a nullable `Task` discard, a choice case named for an `Object` virtual, and any case asserting a disposal order. **No case changes verdict**: the §17.13 cases (`s17_13_0008`, `s17_13_0009`, `s30_5_0005`) discard a non-nullable `Task.Delay(…)` and stay rejects, `l6_9_0009` is the `Channel<T>` case whose "reverse insertion" wording this revision deliberately keeps, and no case in the corpus exercises the abstract-class or reserved-case-name shapes at all. Those three are recorded as **owed coverage**, not written here.

- **Not a resolution: [#4429](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4429) takes no spec edit, its filed premise being false.** It reports that §28.14's capture reduction is asymmetric between parameters and locals *"in a direction no document states"*. §28.14 states it. Clause 1 of its capture-reduction list reads *"a captured value-typed local **or parameter** lives in its heap capture cell"*, and names the case outright: *"a `string`- or `int`-typed constructor parameter captured by a form-3 subscription does not bar the admission"*. That wording is **v0.301's own** (commit `5a01b840`) — the same landing the issue was filed alongside — so the spec has stated the admitting direction since before the issue existed. The asymmetry is therefore a plain implementation bug: the `ParameterSymbol` branch needs the `isBorrowableType` filter the `LocalSymbol` branch already has. Re-labelled, with the premise corrected on the issue.

- **Migration.** Four rulings can reject a program that compiled before, all four of them programs the language did not mean to admit: a `where T: new()` substitution naming an `abstract` or `closed` class (the remedy is a concrete class, or a different constraint); a discard of a nullable `Task`-family value (use `Task.FireAndForget` under a null check, or a named `using var`); a choice case named `Equals`, `GetHashCode` or `ToString` (rename the case); and `new Semaphore(initial, max)` with `max < 1` or `initial > max`, which now raises. §22.5's and §9.9's clarifications reject nothing new — §22.5 states what the compiler already diagnosed, and §9.9 *admits* a shape its example prose had wrongly called an error. §28.11's order changes no behaviour for any collection built by appending alone.

- **Issues.** [#4380](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4380), [#4415](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4415), [#4416](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4416), [#4417](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4417), [#4423](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4423), [#4439](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4439), [#4440](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4440), [#4441](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4441) and [#4442](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4442) close with their citations (spec §9.9, §12.5, §14.2, §17.13, §22.5, §22.6, §28.11, §35.1, §35.7, Appendix C.4; stdlib §4.3, §4.5, §6.3, §6.10, v0.302). **#4380 closes in full**, its first three parts at v0.300 and its fourth here. **[#4429](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4429) does not close and takes no spec edit** — re-labelled from `spec-defect` to a compiler tracking item, with its premise corrected. New issues filed for the four spec-ahead-of-impl deltas above (§17.13's nullable discard, §35.1's synthesized-member collision, §6.3's unenforced `maxCount`, and §14.2's missing abstract test in `groundSatisfiesNew`). The guides remain 7–13 revisions behind and are reported, not failed, by design.

### v0.303 changelog (v0.302 → v0.303)

**The mislabelled train: five spec questions that were open the whole time, filed under `needs-owner-decision`, `spec-tracking`, or no label at all.** v0.302 closed the last `spec-defect` and the last `spec-question` on the tracker, and a sweep of those two labels reported no spec work left. It was wrong — not about the labels, which were accurate, but about what they covered. Every item below was filed by an implementation lane that hit a question it could not answer, followed CLAUDE.md's rule 1 correctly (*"stop and open an issue"*), and reached for the label that described **who had to decide** rather than **what kind of thing it was**. Five of them sat for eight to twelve revisions. **The lesson is recorded rather than just fixed:** a label is an index, and an index that does not cover every entrance gives a clean bill of health it has not earned. The right sweep is over the question — does an implementation need a sentence the documents do not contain? — and the labels are a shortcut to it, never a substitute.

- **§14.1 / Appendix C.1 — a reference to a generic type supplies exactly its declared arity (ruling; [#4181](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4181) closes).** The compiler enforces this at two sites with two different rules, and no normative section states either. The filing checked §11.3, Appendix C.4, all of §14, Appendix C.1 and §3 and found nothing — a search this revision repeated and confirmed: the only neighbouring statements are §2.8.1's *identity* rule (which keys identity on arity without saying a reference must match it) and Appendix C.1's generic-**method** inference bullet (a different subject, as §14.5 says itself). **Decided:** every reference supplies exactly the declared number — class, interface, record, and generic `type` alias alike. There is no raw and no open generic type reference; `Box` bare and `Box<int, string>` are equally compile errors at a `class Box<T>`, each naming the declared arity. **Grounds:** identity is keyed on arity (§2.8.1), so a reference supplying none names no type; and there is nothing at a *type* reference to infer arity from, which is precisely why §14.5's omit-or-supply-in-full rule is scoped to a generic member **call**, which has arguments. The filing's second question — why the two implementation checks differ — resolves as a consequence rather than a recorded asymmetry: the alias check is right and the ordinary-type tolerance is the gap. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): raw and open references. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact.** **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** `resolveNamed`'s arity check is guarded by `!t.genericArgs.empty()` (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Names.cpp:2928`), so a wholly omitted list passes. Issue filed.

- **§26.4 — "any nesting depth" reaches generic argument positions and not a function type's slots (ruling; [#4192](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4192) closes).** §26.4's binding rule applies *"at **any nesting depth** of the extended type's argument positions"*, and both its worked examples nest through further generic arguments. Whether a function type's parameter and return slots count was unstated, and the measured behaviour is that they do not — `extension Array<(T) -> T>` fails at its own declaration with *"unresolved type name `T`"*, before any call-site matching runs. **Decided:** "argument positions" means a **constructed generic type's** argument positions and nothing else; a function type's slots are not among them, and a bare identifier there binds nothing and is a compile error **naming this rule**. **Grounds:** §26.4 says of itself *"this is the only implicit type-parameter binding in the language, so the rule is stated exactly"*, and the section already declines the one alternative that would have made binding depend on anything but syntax (resolving against scope first — *"action at a distance"*). The diagnostic shape is not invented here either: §26.4 already rejects a **nullable-marked** identifier in an argument position *"naming this rule"*, and this is the same kind of near-miss deserving the same treatment. **Deferred and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): admitting function-slot binding, on the same footing as §26.4's own deferred `T?` head — reopenable on a recorded need, which must say how a freshly-bound identifier in a nested function slot interacts with §28.3's mint-announcing rule, that rule reading a **declared** slot type. **Body-locality: local.** **Kernel: no contact.** **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** the diagnostic today is a bare unresolved-name error. Issue filed.

- **§22.16 — an inert `static invariant` must say so (ruling; [#4256](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4256) closes).** §22.16 records `static invariant` as out of scope this revision: *"parses from day one and is useful when the prover fragment lands"*. v0.298's #4206 correctly **refuted** rejecting it, and `Emitter::emitInvariantCheck` excludes it from instrumentation by design. So the accept-and-skip behaviour is right, and the filing did not ask to change it. What it asked about is the silence: `static invariant(false);` compiles with **zero** diagnostics and has zero effect — measured, no `ContractViolationException` at construction exit or at any method boundary — and nothing distinguishes that from a checked predicate at the author's seat. **Decided:** the compiler **must** warn at the clause. **Grounds:** the clause is a prove-time obligation with no prover to discharge it and no run-time stand-in, and it reads exactly like the non-static form that *is* enforced; a contract a reader believes is enforced is worse than no contract. The warning changes no verdict, so it needs none of the rejection authority §22.16 withholds. It is **withdrawn, not silenced**, when the prover fragment lands — stated in the rule itself, so the diagnostic cannot outlive its reason. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): withholding the signal. **Body-locality: local** — it reads one declaration. **Kernel: no contact.** **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** no such warning exists. Issue filed.

- **§28.2 — a dominating kill warns for every use form, a conditional kill errors for every use form (ruling; [#3975](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3975) closes).** Six programs differing only in where the `move` sits got two different verdicts — three §28.2 warnings and three §28.3 errors — over identical program state, decided by whether `checkRead` happened to run before `markMovedByName` and cascade-suppress it. The filing established that both behaviours are individually deliberate and that *"nobody chose the combination"*, and recommended that §28.2 govern. **Decided: it does.** §28.2's list has named *"read, borrowed from, or **consumed**"* together since it was written, and the sentence immediately following pairs the dominating kill with the *conditional* one as the contrast that decides severity — so the split the section draws is between the two **kills**, never between the use forms. Under a dominating kill every use in that list warns, `move x` and an `owned` argument position included; under a conditional kill every one of them is §28.3's error. **Grounds:** the alternative requires narrowing a word §28.2 chose and unwinding the cascade-suppression contract `Poisoned` exists to provide, to buy a severity difference the checked-disposal backstop already covers in both directions — `DisposedAccessException` fires for a disposed read and a disposed consume alike. **Declined and recorded** (`DECLINED.md`): keying the diagnostic on the use form. **Body-locality: local** — it consumes the same dominating-kill fact the rule already computes, adding none. **Kernel: no contact** — K4.2 + K7.4 are cited by the sentence unchanged; this fixes which *diagnostic* a state draws, not the state. **Spec-ahead-of-impl:** rows 4–6 over-reject today. Issue filed.

- **§14.5 — nullability is part of a binding, and the wrapping bullet does not compose into the nested case (clarification; [#4231](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4231) closes its spec half).** The filing asked whether §14.5 phase 1's `X?` nullable-wrapping rule composes when `X` appears **nested** inside a constructed parameter type, since `isFreeGenericTypeVarRef` ignores nullability on both sides. The documents answer it: the wrapping bullet is about the **parameter position's own `?`**, the constructed-type bullet unifies *"component-wise and **invariantly**"*, and the bare-`X` bullet binds to *"the argument's static type"* — which at a nested position is whatever sits there, nullable or not. So `b: Box<Box<X>>` against a `Box<Box<int?>>` argument binds `X` to `int?`, and the probe program in the filing is **correct** rather than suspicious. **The adversarial shape it could not test is also already decided:** *Agreement* requires all bindings of a parameter to be *"the **same type**"*, with two different bindings an inference failure and *"no common supertype and no widened join"* — so an `X` bound `int` at one slot and `int?` at another is an error, not a widening. All three sentences are stated; only their composition was not, and it now is. **Nothing is ruled about the implementation**, which is the half the filing was right to keep open: whether `checkAssignable`'s leniency can accept a program *Agreement* forbids is a question for the adversarial probes the filing names, and this environment cannot run them. #4231 stays open for that, re-scoped.

- **Closed without an edit: [#4205](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4205), resolved at v0.299 and never noticed.** It asked for Appendix A's shared-production over-admissions index to list `invariant` for the record `Member` row alongside the enum/choice row. The row has read *"destructors; `invariant` members … `invariant` by §22.16"* since commit `c8ee8846` — v0.299's defect train swept it in. An issue that describes a real gap, is silently fixed by an adjacent train, and then sits open is its own small failure mode: the same sweep that found the four mislabelled rulings found this one already discharged.

- **Doc-only: 16 edits across 5 documents** (spec §14.1 ×2, §14.5, §22.16 ×2, §26.4, §28.2, Appendix C.1; the code-generation reference ×1 plus its three pins; the four version headers), 4 new `DECLINED.md` rows. Applied as one dry-run composition-gated sequence — 6/6, then 7/7, then 3/3 clean.

- **Gate round: three sites, one of them introduced by this train.** (1) The §14.1 ruling cited **§2.8.1** for the identity-on-arity sentence, which lives in **§2.8.3** — an anchor that resolves and a subsection number that does not hold up, which is #4177's citation-defect pattern exactly, committed here while writing a ruling *about* an uncited rule. Corrected. (2) §22.16's *Discharge sites differ by clause kind* paragraph states what `static invariant` does **when the prover fragment lands**, in the present tense, four paragraphs above the out-of-scope note — so a reader arriving there would take the rejection for live behaviour and the new warning for noise. It now says which revision it describes. (3) The code-generation reference said a later straight-line **read** of an explicitly-disposed binding warns, where §28.2 says *use*; a model copying from it would not learn that a consume is covered, which is the very ambiguity this revision's §28.2 ruling removes. Now states use, with the three forms named. `check_docs.sh` passes on all eleven checks. **Corpus:** no case changes verdict. §22.16's warning is a new diagnostic on a shape no case exercises; §26.4's and §14.1's rejections are error-site and arity shapes the corpus does not cover; §28.2's ruling changes a *severity* the corpus pins nowhere, since no case writes a consume after a dominating `Dispose()`. Four owed-coverage shapes recorded, none written here.

- **Issues.** [#4181](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4181), [#4192](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4192), [#4205](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4205), [#4256](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4256) and [#3975](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3975) close with their citations (spec §2.8.1, §14.1, §14.5, §22.16, §26.4, §27.8, §28.2, §28.3, Appendix A, Appendix C.1, v0.303). **[#4231](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4231) does not close** — its spec half is answered above and it is re-scoped to the implementation probe it names. New issues filed for the four spec-ahead-of-impl deltas. Every implementation claim here is a **source read**, not a run: there is no working build in this environment (clang 18; the compiler needs 21), and where the filings themselves recorded measured behaviour that is cited as theirs, not re-measured.

### v0.304 changelog (v0.303 → v0.304)

**Editorial: the specification's 238 inline revision markers are removed, and its loaded vocabulary with them. No rule changes.** Owner-directed. Two passes over `Bezel_Language_Spec.md` alone; every other document is untouched.

- **Inline revision markers: 238 → 0.** The spec had accumulated a marker at the site of nearly every rule that had ever moved — `(v0.289)`, `(v0.265, [#3278](…))`, `([§16.3](…), v0.292)`, `(v0.250 — ordinary-parameter `owned` distinguishes overloads)`, and a dozen other shapes. **The principle now applied: the specification states the current rule, and this changelog states when it changed.** A reader asking *what is the rule* was being handed a fact about the project's history in the middle of the sentence; a reader asking *when did this change* was never going to find a complete answer inline anyway, because only some rules carried a marker. **Issue links and proposal references sharing a marker's parenthetical are kept** — `(v0.265, [#3278](…))` becomes `([#3278](…))` — because those are provenance a reader can follow, not a label. The document's own version header is untouched, and no `DECLINED.md` row, guide, or companion document was swept.

- **Three historical clauses were rewritten rather than stripped**, because deleting the marker alone would have left a dangling comparative. §B.2's *"`requires`, `ensures`, and `invariant` are unconditionally reserved since v0.260 — previously contextual"* now reads *"are unconditionally reserved rather than contextual"*, keeping the rule and its stated reason (the clause region's statement-stealing collision, proposal 0055 §3) and dropping the history. Its §B.2 twin and §28.7's *"the owning choice has had it since v0.200"* are handled the same way.

- **Loaded and colloquial vocabulary removed.** `footgun` ×4 → *error-prone default* / *behavior* / *problem* / *error-prone*; `blessed` ×1 → *privileged*; *"declined as implicit magic"* → *"declined as implicit binding"*; *"the single most dangerous primitive"* → *"the highest-risk primitive"* (its parenthetical already carries the fact: *it executes, not merely corrupts*); *"it often works until it doesn't"* → *"it may appear to work on one target and fail on another"*; *"clearly-defined source"* → *"well-defined source"*. The filler adverb **`simply` ×16 is deleted outright** — *"is simply not auto-hashable"*, *"the received value is simply dropped"*, *"the next `MoveNext` simply produces the next value"* — every one of which reads more precisely without it, and each of which quietly told the reader the point was obvious.

- **Two candidates were checked and deliberately kept.** *`no-hidden-magic`* stays: the rationale (§5.18 and elsewhere) invokes it repeatedly as a **named principle**, so renaming it in the spec alone would desynchronize the two documents — the word is terminology here, not tone. And **`trivially` ×9 stays** in every instance: *"discharged trivially"*, *"trivially outlives the call"*, *"hold trivially in a Core implementation"* are the technical sense, and each is load-bearing. `just` ×9 likewise stays — *"just below Primary"*, *"positioned just before the first element"*, *"the list just given"* are positional, not minimizing.

- **Second person is now confined to the front matter.** The opening description and the reading guide address a reader on purpose and keep doing so. Three uses that had reached normative text are impersonal now: the unit-type sentinel sentence, §17.13's anonymous-binding guidance, and §30.5's *"You do not need to pin anything"*. Six contractions in normative prose are expanded.

- **Method, and what it caught.** The marker sweep ran as a scripted transform with a line-for-line artifact check, and the check earned itself three times. A blanket empty-parenthesis cleanup **deleted every literal `()` in the document** — the unit type, and every nullary call spelling from `Subscribe()` to `ToString()`; the rule was unnecessary as well as destructive and is gone, with a comment in the script saying why. Twice a rule used `\s+`, which spans newlines, and **swallowed every line between a comma and the next marker** — the second time silently, because the verification compared files line-for-line and two deleted lines had misaligned it into reporting 160 false artifacts. The transform is now same-line-only and line-count-preserving by construction, which is what makes its check meaningful. Three markers wrapped onto their own line inside Appendix A's EBNF comments are hand-edited for that reason, along with 25 other residuals no safe regex reached.

- **Doc-only: 238 marker removals, 28 residual hand edits, 19 vocabulary edits, 16 `simply` deletions, the four version headers and the code-generation reference's three pins.** No rule, verdict, example, or grammar production changes. `check_docs.sh` passes on all eleven checks, with `EXTRACT` at the same 514 fragments before and after; the conformance corpus is untouched at 2,148 cases.

- **Not swept, and why.** `Bezel_Standard_Library.md` carries **552** inline markers and is normative, so the same argument applies to it; it is left for a decision rather than swept on this pass's authority. `Bezel_Design_Rationale.md` carries **800**, and there the markers should probably **stay** — a rationale entry's subject *is* the decision and the revision it was taken at, which is the one document where "when" is the content. The code-generation reference carries 73, most of them teaching when a spelling changed, which is closer to useful than to clutter for a document written to be copied from.

### v0.305 changelog (v0.304 → v0.305)

**Editorial: the standard library's inline revision markers, 552 → 88, and its loaded vocabulary with them. No rule or signature changes.** Owner-directed, the companion pass to v0.304's sweep of the language specification. Every other document is untouched.

- **Markers removed: 464 of 552.** The same principle v0.304 applied to the spec — the document states the current surface, the changelog states when it changed. The stdlib's shapes were messier than the spec's and needed their own rules: the fenced **signature comments** lead with the marker (`// v0.215: returns the quotient`, `// v0.186; address of the buffer`), which the spec never did, and one heading carried three at once. Where a marker was the *whole* comment the comment goes with it, rather than leaving a signature line ending in a bare `//`.

- **Three classes are deliberately kept, and the distinction is the substance of this pass.** (1) **Changelog and rationale citations** — *"see the changelog, v0.140"*, *"the decision record are in the v0.188 changelog entry"*, *"the v0.174 rationale entry"*. There the revision is how a reader *finds* the record, so it is the content and not a label. (2) **Referring uses**, where the revision identifies which thing is meant — *"generalizing the v0.148 ruling"*, *"the v0.195 note said was missing"*. Stripping those leaves a dangling referent (*"the ruling"*, *"the note"*), which is worse than the marker. (3) **Cross-document citations already carrying a section** — `[§28.14](…), v0.273` — lose only the revision; the section number remains and still resolves.

- **What is left, and why it is not an editorial question.** **88 markers remain**, and they are overwhelmingly a different thing from what this pass removed: *sentences whose subject is the history*. `### 4.17 `SortedDictionary<K, V>` (added in v0.136)` and `### 3.4 `ReadOnlyAsciiByteSpan` (retired v0.188)` are **headings** about a type's lifecycle; *"declared `ToArray(): owned Array<T>` from v0.222 (#1810) until v0.277, which **deleted** it"* is a member's biography; *"the category was written at v0.102, before choices existed"*, *"v0.114 establishes the interface vocabulary"*, *"async examples formerly used a hypothetical `HttpClient`; v0.269 rewrote them"* are design-and-editorial narrative. Removing the revision from those does not neutralize them, it makes them incoherent. **The stdlib is carrying a body of rationale-and-changelog content inside a normative document**, and whether it should is a content decision, not an editorial one. It is recorded here and left for a ruling rather than taken on this pass's authority.

- **Vocabulary.** `footgun` → *genuine hazard*; *"not as compiler magic"* → *"not as a compiler intrinsic"* (more precise as well as more neutral); `simply` ×5 deleted. **Two candidates were checked and kept:** the `"no hidden magic"` **principle**, which the rationale names and invokes repeatedly — the same call v0.304 made for the spec — and the **`Dangerous` prefix**, which is an API naming convention, not a tone word.

- **Method.** The three mechanical passes ran under the same line-for-line artifact check and line-count guard v0.304 established, and it caught four rule defects before any of them reached the file: a `\s+` that spans newlines (**the third time that trap has fired in two revisions** — it is now commented at every rule that could hit it); a trailing-comment rule that left dangling `//` on nine signature lines; and two rules ported from the spec sweep that are **wrong here** — `(?<=\S) v0.NNN)` turned *"; unified v0.258)"* into *"unified)"* and *"shape (d) v0.195)"* into *"shape (d))"*, and a broad `the v0.NNN X` rule turned *"generalizing the v0.148 ruling"* into *"generalizing the ruling"*. Both were dropped rather than narrowed, and what they would have mangled is in the kept-class above. A fenced hand-edit batch failed closed on two non-matching targets and wrote nothing, which is the behaviour that makes a batch safe to run at all.

- **Doc-only: 464 marker removals across three mechanical passes, 27 hand edits, 8 vocabulary edits, the four version headers and the code-generation reference's three pins.** No signature, no rule, no example changes. `check_docs.sh` passes on all eleven checks with `EXTRACT` at the same 514 fragments throughout; the conformance corpus is untouched at 2,148 cases.

### v0.306 changelog (v0.305 → v0.306)

**The history and rationale content moves out of the standard library.** Owner-directed, completing what v0.305 identified and deliberately left: the stdlib was carrying design narrative and revision biography inside a normative document. **88 inline revision markers → 10**, and the ten that remain are all one thing — a citation whose target *is* a record.

- **What moved, and where.** Nothing was deleted on the assumption that the record existed elsewhere; each removal was checked against the document that holds it. Three dispositions:
  1. **Stated as the current rule, with the date dropped.** The large majority. *"As of v0.117, a `serialized` clause customizes…"* → *"A `serialized` clause customizes…"*; *"**Identity tokens (specified in v0.139):**"* → *"**Identity tokens:**"*; *"### 4.18 `SortedSet<T>` (added in v0.136)"* → *"### 4.18 `SortedSet<T>`"*. The rule was never in doubt; only its date was in the sentence.
  2. **Deleted, because the record lives in a document whose job it is.** `ReadOnlySpan<T>`'s `ToArray()` biography — *"declared … from v0.222 (#1810) until v0.277, which **deleted** it"* — is a `DECLINED.md` row (*`ToArray()` on a span over class-typed or borrow-bearing elements*, with the member's dates). §4.14 and §4.15 now state the current position (neither family materializes) and point at the row. Likewise the editorial note recording that v0.269 rewrote the spec's async examples off a hypothetical `HttpClient`, and *"the category was written at v0.102, before choices existed"*.
  3. **Moved to the rationale, because the reasoning existed nowhere else.** §4.10's *"The v0.259 rename (`Take`/`TryTake` → `Pop`/`TryPop`)"* paragraph was checked against the rationale and was **not** there. Its content is a real design argument — an instance member blocks a same-named extension **by name** under spec §26.5 rule 1, so an instance `Take(query: T)` made LINQ's `Take(count: int)` permanently unreachable on an `OwningSet<T>` receiver — and it is now **rationale §15.z**, where a reader asking *why is it `Pop`* will look. The stdlib keeps the members and their semantics and loses the migration narrative.

- **The ten kept, and the rule they share.** *"see the changelog, v0.140"*, *"the prior definition and the decision record are in the v0.188 changelog entry"*, *"the v0.174 rationale entry"*, *"Provenance: the v0.186 ruling, rationale §12.8"*, *"declined at v0.274 and the reopening bar its record states (`DECLINED.md`)"*, *"the v0.276 changelog entry's stated cost"*. In every one the revision is **how a reader finds the record**, which is the opposite of a label: delete it and the pointer stops resolving. §3.4's `ReadOnlyAsciiByteSpan` section is kept in full for the same reason it was written — it tells a reader the type does not exist and what to use instead — with only *"(retired v0.188)"* shortened to *"(retired)"* in its heading, the changelog citation in its body left intact.

- **Doc-only: 69 stdlib edits, one paragraph relocated to rationale §15.z, the four version headers and the code-generation reference's three pins.** Applied as two composition-gated sequences (59/59 and 10/10 clean). **No signature, rule, verdict or example changed** — this revision moves prose between documents and states in the present tense what was stated in the past tense. `check_docs.sh` passes on all eleven checks with `EXTRACT` at the same 514 fragments; the conformance corpus is untouched at 2,148 cases.

### v0.307 changelog (v0.306 → v0.307)

**The path-of-least-resistance revision (owner-directed 2026-09-22).** Six items from the 2026-09-22 investigation into making the sound memory-management spelling the shortest one and making the compiler say what it already knows: five graduate here (proposals 0127–0131, two composition-gated trains, one adversarial critique with seven blocking findings, all resolved — `scratch/finalize-A/resolutions.md`, `scratch/finalize-B/resolutions.md` in the landing session's record), and one is recorded as a study (0132). The doctrine each item sits inside is unchanged: static rules only as free precision or where no backstop exists (rationale §5.1), announce at signatures and infer inside bodies (§5.5), and a statically-certain hazard gets a normative warning with no per-site suppression (§5.28). No compiler was available to the landing session; every item is spec-ahead-of-implementation and tracked (below), and every new rule corpus case was written from the document and lands unclassified.

- **§22.10 — a class- or interface-typed `scoped` primary-constructor parameter is admitted (ruling; proposal 0127 graduates; [#4601](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4601)).** The header admits plain, `owned`, and class/interface-typed `scoped` parameters. A body-referenced `scoped` parameter is captured as a compiler-generated **non-owned** private field — exactly §28.14's "direct non-owned field of the bounding object", the constructed object being form 1's bounding object — so the recorded ground for the v1 bound ("the scoped-storage contract needs an explicitly declared field") does not hold for this form: the compiler declares the field. Capture-iff-used, layout stability, the call-site marker `new Box(scoped src)`, the bounding-object forms, the fresh-producer rejection, the plain-`var`-holder rejection and the freeze are unchanged. §28.14's callee-side bullet now states the plain-argument disposition of a `scoped` parameter — an ordinary borrow argument; a store the receiving callee makes is that callee's own §28.3 admission with its residual — of which the base call is an instance. A body reference to the capture is an ordinary receiver-sourced field read (K1.5). **Declined:** lifting the function-typed form with it — its capture field would be a `scoped` field whose never-read-out and quiescence obligations §28.14 states over a *declared* field an author can see and clear; it stays the recorded v1 bound (liftable, design sketched in 0127 §2.1); unconditional capture of a `scoped` parameter; dropping the call-site marker for the primary-constructor spelling. Appendix A.4's over-admission row now lists the function-typed `scoped` parameter beside `ref`/`out` (repairing its omission of `scoped`); Appendix C.5 gains the modifier-set row; the code-generation reference §4.2 and Guide 01 §5's rejected-shapes paragraph re-taught. `DECLINED.md`'s `deferred` row narrowed to the function-typed form. Corpus: `s22_10_0011` re-authored reject → accept (re-bank at the next classification); `s22_10_0016`–`0019`, `s28_14_0019` added.
- **§28.2 — checked disposal mode is the default; unchecked mode is the explicitly selected release relaxation (ruling; proposal 0128 graduates; [#4602](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4602)).** The two-mode structure, the equivalence claim, the implementability and cost paragraphs, the compiler-inserted free, the use-after-dispose warning and K4.1's posture are unchanged word for word; the default flips. Ground: §28.2 already said unchecked mode is the release-build relaxation of the checked semantics, not a different language, and every recorded trust admission in §28 names checked mode's `DisposedAccessException` as its backstop (K4.1) — a default build that omitted it made each of those sentences describe a build the user did not get. §31.4 no longer calls the exception a development aid a build is free to omit. Rationale §5.30 records the decision and **the cost of the default**: checked mode's fault is deterministic only while the disposed flag stays readable through every alias, so a checked build retains per-disposed-instance state for the process's life; the reference compiler today retains the whole disposed block, and a *windowed* quarantine that reuses blocks is declined because it would make K4.1's deterministic fault probabilistic. **Compiler (tracked):** `bezelc` builds checked with no switch; `--unchecked-disposal` selects the relaxation; `--checked-disposal` stays accepted as a no-op; both switches together are a usage error; bounding the per-instance retention to the flag's footprint is the recorded precondition of the CLI flip. The Driver library's `CodegenOptions.checkedDisposal` keeps its `false` zero-value — an embedder chooses explicitly, and the gtest oracles need real frees (AddressSanitizer sees no use-after-free on a quarantined block; `runAotChecked`'s LeakSanitizer would report every quarantined block). **Declined:** the status quo; flipping the library default with the CLI; deleting the relaxation. Corpus: `s28_2_0011` (default build faults), `s28_2_0012` (`--unchecked-disposal`, accept-only).
- **§29.12 / §28.11 — two more statically-certain-hazard lints in rationale §5.28's shape (ruling; proposal 0129 graduates; [#4603](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4603)).** *Lint A* (§29.12): a call to a structural operation on the **same binding** the enclosing `for`/`await for` iterates — the same local or parameter, or the same `this`-rooted owned-field chain — in the loop's own callable body (not a lambda or local type body the loop merely contains), from which the loop's next advance is reachable, **must warn**; a call followed on every path by an exit from the loop (`break`/`return`/a `throw` no in-body `catch` handles/labeled jump) is exempt, a conditional call is warned, a dictionary indexer-set is outside the set, and a modification through a different binding is not traced — chosen, liftable. *Lint B* (§28.11 *Owning collections*): a local holding an element borrow — an indexer-get, a default-iteration variable, or a §29.11-traced class-element accessor result rooted at the collection — used after a **dominating** `Clear()`, `Remove` of the borrow, or `RemoveAt` at the borrow's own index (a constant or an unreassigned local read, with no §29.12 structural operation on the binding between the borrow and the kill) on the same collection binding **must warn**: §28.2's dominating-kill shape with the kill on the collection (K4.2 + K7.4, the source per K2.1). An indexer-set and `OwningDictionary`'s keyed `Remove(k)` are not in the kill set (liftable); a re-taken borrow is clean; a conditional kill stays with the checked-mode backstop. Remedies named in both diagnostics: collect-then-remove; the egress members `Pop`/`PopAt`/`PopValue`; re-take the borrow; mutate after the last use. §28.3's indexer row cross-references the warning; Appendix C.3 gains two rows; stdlib §4.5 one sentence; rationale §5.28 the fourth and fifth instances; the code-generation reference and Guide 05 §2 collect-then-remove paragraph re-taught. `DECLINED.md`: the per-site-suppression row now covers five lints; one `deferred` row records the liftables. Corpus: `s29_12_0005` (warn), `0006`–`0009` (quiet); `s28_11_0008`–`0009` (warn), `0010`–`0012` (quiet); per §5 item 3c, `s29_12_0001` and `s29_12_0004` now carry `warns: yes`.
- **Stdlib §4.21 — `OwningSlotMap<T>` and `SlotHandle` (proposal 0130 graduates; [#4604](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4604)).** An owning collection keyed by generational handles it mints, so that "store a stable key, not a borrow" is the shortest spelling for graph-, cache- and registry-shaped code: `Insert(owned value: T): SlotHandle`; `Contains`/`Get`/`GetOrNull`/`TryGetValue` (borrows sourced from the map); `Remove` (disposes); `PopValue`/`TryPopValue`/`Drain()` (transfer); `Handles()` (an owned `Array<SlotHandle>` snapshot, ascending `Index`); `Clear()`. `SlotHandle` is a compiler-known value record — `Index`, `Generation`, a non-public owner tag; sendable, hashable, defaultable, no public constructor, declaring no serialization conformance; `default(SlotHandle)` denotes a slot of no map and faults like a foreign handle. A slot's generation advances on every vacate (a stale handle reads absent forever); `Insert` reuses the most recently vacated slot; a slot whose generation would exceed `int.MaxValue` is retired; a handle from another map is an `ArgumentException`. `Clear()`/`Dispose()` dispose in descending `Index`; iteration, `Handles()` and `Drain()` visit in ascending `Index`. Conformance: `IEnumerable<T>` + `IOwningEnumerable<T>`, not `IOwningCollection<T>`, not a literal target. The two bare names join §2.3's auto-import row (twenty-nine → thirty-one); §28.11's owning family and §28.9's not-trivial-dispose list name the type; rationale §5.4's "handle-and-table indirection" is thereby a library type — a stored key carries no K4.3 clause. **Declined:** a borrowing twin; foreign handles as a silent miss; a `[h]` indexer (and so `move map[h]`) in v1; `int` handles; insertion-ordered disposal; the name `OwningRegistry`. Distinct from rationale §18's deferred *allocators and arena allocation*: this is a collection, not an allocation mechanism. Corpus: `l4_21_0001`–`0011`.
- **§28.3 *Diagnostics* / K4 clause 3 — the trust-admission report mode (proposal 0131 graduates; [#4605](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4605)).** A per-build diagnostic mode, off by default and selected explicitly (`--report-trust-admissions`): at every site where the compiler makes a K4.3-recorded admission — a parameter-/receiver-/field-path-sourced borrow stored into a non-`owned` field (§28.3); such a borrow stored into a borrowing-family collection or an `OwningDictionary` key slot (§28.11), an unclassified receiver included; a borrow held by a pending frame past its call (§30.1/§30.5 — a frame returned under a mint-announcing type is type-announced, K6.2 + K2.4, and is not reported); a §28.14 form-3/4 registration residual or a user `scoped` field's quiescence obligation — the compiler emits a **warning** naming the rule and clause, the borrow, its source, the holder, the obligation and the static remedies (`scoped`, a `SlotHandle` key, `Shared<T>`, the owning family, awaiting to settlement). A unit that emits no report under the mode carries no recorded trust clause; excluded by text: K4.2's site-announced kills, §22.12's statics obligations, §32.10's documented trust, axiom A10's grants. K4 clause 3 gains one sentence: the recorded set is enumerable and the mode enumerates it. The default build's diagnostics are unchanged. **Declined:** toolchain-only; always-on (a trust admission is the taught back-reference, not a hazard); a third diagnostic class; a per-site acknowledgement marker. Rationale §5.31 records the placements. Corpus: `s28_3_0090`–`0096`.
- **Study 0132 — derived retention (no normative change).** A per-parameter "retains parameter *i* in a `readonly` plain field of `this`" fact computed from the callee body, interface-carried, consumed only by a caller-side statically-certain warning, is sound in exactly the shape `scoped` already makes static for one keyword; the tree writes zero such fields today; rationale §9.7's and proposal 0048's objections are weakened, not answered, by a warning-only consumer. **Recommendation: defer**, with the evidence that would move it (0131's measured count against `scoped` adoption; an implementation probe; a class-level §9.7 ruling) and a reopening bar recorded in the study.

- **Also filed, outside this train:** [#4606](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4606) — the dictionary runtime bumps the modification epoch on a value update of a present key, where §29.12 says the enumerator stays valid (impl-vs-spec, noticed while tracing §29.12).

- **Migration.** *Newly admitted:* class/interface-typed `scoped` in a primary-constructor header. *Newly defined:* the default disposal-checking mode is checked (a program that touches a disposed instance and was built with no switch now faults deterministically where it had undefined behavior — **known cost, disclosed:** a checked build retains per-disposed-instance state until process exit, in the reference compiler today the entire disposed block; bounding that retention is the tracked precondition of the CLI flip); the plain-argument disposition of a `scoped` parameter and the capture-read classification (§28.14); `OwningSlotMap<T>`, `SlotHandle` and the two auto-imported bare names; the trust-admission report mode and its flag. *Newly warned:* lint A and lint B in the default build; under the report mode, every K4.3 site. *Newly rejected:* nothing. *Doc-only:* the A.4/C.3/C.5 rows, §31.4's clause, stdlib §4.3/§4.5 sentences, rationale §5.4/§5.28/§5.30/§5.31, the code-generation reference (§4.1/§4.2/§4.5/§4.6/§5.4/§5.11 and its three pins), Guide 01 §2/§5 and Guide 05 §2/§8 sentences. *Guides:* edited only where a sentence stated a rule this revision changes; their re-validation pins stay at v0.291 (Guide 05 v0.291) because the guides were not re-traced end to end — that full pass is owed separately. *Spec-ahead-of-impl:* every item above, tracked in #4601–#4605. `check_docs.sh` passes on all eleven checks; the rule corpus grows from 2,148 to 2,184 cases (36 new; one re-authored), all new cases unclassified until the next dev-box classification.

### v0.308 changelog (v0.307 → v0.308)

**A clarification train from the 2026-09-29 spec-defect/spec-question docket.** Ten issues. Every edit states a rule the documents already implied, corrects text that misdescribed one, or settles a silence the kernel already decided; no compile-time verdict moves in this revision — the docket's verdict-changing items ride v0.309 with its critique gate. Two premises were refuted by the text and are recorded as such: #4479's citation was correct but ambiguous, and #4457's `.ToArray()` remedy survives as §29.11's re-enumeration remedy (v0.265 withdrew only its liveness use).

- **§31.4 — the cause-chaining example carries the `;` A.4's `CtorChain` requires (editorial; [#4632](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4632)).** `base(msg, cause) end constructor;` → `base(msg, cause); end constructor;`. The grammar, §12.8 and Appendix C already agreed; the example was the one form in the documents that omitted the terminator. The rule-corpus cases authored from it already carry the terminator; none changes here.
- **§9.7 — the static-storage-sourced record return cites its admission unambiguously (editorial; [#4479](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4479)).** "§28.3's clause 2" meant item 2 of *Borrow lifetime rules*' callee-side return list (the static-property-getter admission, whose terms the sentence imports). §28.3 carries three numbered lists, K2's four clauses among them, and the phrase read naturally as K2.2 (*Union under composition*). The sentence now names the list item and adds K2's always-live-source bullet and the `T.f` producers row as the source's authority; the sibling "clause 4" in the same bullet is re-cited the same way. No rule changes.
- **§29.11 — the consumption diagnostic's `.ToArray()` remedy is scoped to what it remedies (clarification; [#4457](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4457)).** The mandate that every static consumption error name "the `.ToArray()` materialization remedy" read as contradicting the section's #2557 sentence ("materializing is not among them"). The two govern different hazards. Materialize-first is the **re-enumeration** remedy over a live backing (paragraph 2, and the reason v0.265 declined rejecting the materializers); #2557 withdrew it only as a **liveness** remedy for the terminal-accessor warning. The mandate now says so in the remedies paragraph's words. What the diagnostic names is unchanged. **Declined:** replacing the named remedy with the liveness remedies. That would drop the remedy from the error it remedies, and it would flip `s29_11_0002`/`0004`/`0006`. The minting-source case, where the re-enumeration remedy itself yields dead borrows, is filed as its own question at landing.
- **§4.3.1, rationale §7.4 — the IEEE-relational justification names the idiom it does not cover (clarification; [#4588](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4588)).** Both sentences said relational operators keep IEEE semantics "so numeric algorithms work as published". That holds for ordering-based algorithms. The canonical NaN self-test `x != x` is an *equality* idiom, and under reflexive `=` its port `x <> x` is `false` for every `x`. Both now say so and name `Double.IsNaN(x)` as the replacement. The semantics are unchanged, since §4.3.1's `NaN = NaN` bullet already decides it. **Deferred:** a warning on a float-typed self-comparison (the issue's option 2). It is a language-surface addition with an open generic-instantiation leg, recorded with its evidence bar in `DECLINED.md`. The code-generation reference's row 3 carries the replacement.
- **§27.8 — the recursive-alias ban is stated for every alias (clarification; [#4783](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4783)).** The ban sat in the *Generic type aliases* subsection and said "A generic alias". The definition it rests on (an alias names *an existing type*; a pure synonym) is not generic-only. The rule now reads: no alias may reference itself, directly or through other aliases, in its aliased type or its `where` clause, which covers `type A := Array<A>;`, `type P := Q; type Q := P;` and `type Sorted<T> := Array<T> where T: Sorted<T>;`. The `where` clause is part of the declaration (A.2 `TypeAliasDecl`), so the last is the same error. **Declined:** routing it to §14.2's self-bound rule, which governs type-parameter bounds, and reading it as an F-bound like §11.8's `where T: INumber<T>`, which names a declared interface whose identity does not depend on its constraint. Body-locality: local. Corpus: `s27_8_0002`'s `rule:` header re-quoted (verdict unchanged).
- **§9.3, §11.1 — "the same parameter list as the primary constructor" is §11.3's clash sense (clarification; [#4775](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4775)).** Both sentences are §11.3's rule applied to the primary. Arity, parameter types, `ref`/`out` and guard-admitted ordinary `owned` distinguish; names and defaults do not. `constructor(x: int, y: int)` beside `record Point(X: int, Y: int)` is rejected, since a names reading would make every `new Point(1, 2)` a §22.6 ambiguity. §9.3 also states the consequence §7.9 already imposes: the auto-generated primary assigns only positional storage, so a non-defaultable body field or auto-property is satisfied only by a field initializer, never by a body constructor. **Declined:** the names reading. Corpus: `s9_3_0002` already states the reading (a banked divergence); `s12_8_0003`'s convenience constructor is given a distinct list so the case isolates its rule.
- **§15.1 — a non-defaultable inline array is initialized under §7.9, and an element store does not assign it (clarification; [#5026](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5026)).** §15.1 said "an explicit initializer is required at declaration", while K1, §28.3, §7.9 and §9.9 (which decides the local/field split for `[8]Port` in terms) all make a non-defaultable local *uninitialized* until assigned, readable only after. §15.1 now defers to §7.9: a local is assigned before first use, at its declaration or by a later whole-array assignment, and a field by an initializer or in every constructor. The array is one variable, so an element store `a[i] := v` into an unassigned local is a use of that local, rejected like a read; the compiler already reports it there. §15.1.1's example comment says the same for the owning form. **Declined:** per-slot definite assignment. **The code-generation reference is corrected:** its constructor-only block marked `var q: Port;` and `var slots: [8]Port;` as errors, contradicting §9.9's local rule. It now shows the read and the element store as the errors.
- **§29.12 — a repositioning through a view is structural (clarification; [#4740](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4740)).** `Reverse()` on an `ArraySpan<T>` or `Span<T>` invalidates an enumerator over the `Array<T>` or `OwningBuffer<T>` it views. The ground is §29.12's own criterion: an operation that repositions entries, with the fault a property of the collection, not of the binding that called it. The views' `Fill`, `CopyFrom`, `CopyTo` and `Span<T>`'s `Clear`/`MoveFrom`/`MoveTo` are element-level writes, because stdlib §4.14/§4.15 define each as per-slot indexer writes, which the next sentence of §29.12 already exempts. The mutation-during-iteration warning is unchanged: a view joins the untraced different-binding list. **Declined:** treating the slot-overwriting members as structural, which would make `s.Fill(v)` fault where the equivalent indexer loop stays valid. **Compiler (tracked):** the span `Reverse` lowering bumps no epoch. Corpus: none affected; the gap is recorded.
- **§15.1.1 — a boxed value in an owning slot is runtime-managed (clarification; [#4477](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4477)).** A slot of an `[N owned]I` inline array can hold a boxed record, because a record at an interface location is boxed (§8.6). §8.6 and §28.9 make that box runtime-managed, with a no-op `Dispose()`, and §9.7 bars a record from carrying disposal work. The auto-dispose pass therefore runs no user code for such a slot, in all four of its endings. **Declined:** rejecting a boxed record at an owning interface slot (it would reject an admissible slot type on the value's classification); treating the wrapper as disposable (contradicts §28.9). Corpus: none affected; the gap is recorded.
- **§28.3 — the borrowed-field residual names its backstops (clarification; [#5028](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5028), [#4880](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4880)).** Clause 3 now states that the named K4.1 backstop is the default build's behaviour. A member access through a stored borrow after its source's disposal raises `DisposedAccessException` (§28.2), and is undefined behavior only under an explicitly selected unchecked build. The trust-admission report (§28.3 *Diagnostics*) names every such store, and a `scoped` parameter (§28.14) makes the bound static. **Not a defect:** a plain parameter's store into a non-owned field whose caller-side source dies first is the K4.3-recorded admission that §28.3 clause 3 and §28.14 ("remains legal with the trust residual") both state. v0.307's proposals 0128 and 0131 set the posture around it. **Declined:** requiring `scoped` for every parameter-sourced field store (contradicts §28.14 and the `rejected` compile-time borrow-liveness row, rationale §5.1); a caller-side retention check (study 0132's recorded deferral). Kernel: derivation (K4.1 + K4.3).

- **Migration.** *Newly defined:* declare-then-assign of a local non-defaultable inline array is admitted (the literal §15.1 sentence read it as rejected; the compiler already admits it); an element store into an unassigned inline-array local is rejected at the store (every reading rejected the program; only the placement is newly stated); `Reverse()` through a span view faults at the backing collection's next advance (runtime only; no compile verdict changes). *Newly rejected:* nothing — §11.3 already rejected a body constructor with the primary's type list, and the compiler already rejects all three recursive-alias shapes with the §27.8 diagnostic. *Doc-only:* #4632, #4479, #4457, #4588, #4783, the #4775 clarifications, #4477's §15.1.1 boxed-slot sentence, #5028's §28.3 clause-3 backstop sentence, §15.1.1's example comment, and the code-generation reference (§2 row 3, the §4.5 iteration paragraph, the §8.4 constructor-only block) with its three pins. *Deferred:* a float self-comparison warning (#4588), recorded in `DECLINED.md` with its evidence bar. *Spec-ahead-of-impl (tracking issues filed at landing):* the compiler accepts a body constructor differing from the primary only by parameter names or default presence (#4775); the span `Reverse` lowering bumps no modification epoch (#4740); #4457's minting-source residual is filed as a question, not an impl delta. The checked default and the trust-admission report #5028 points at remain tracked in #4602 and #4605. *Guides:* no idiom changed; their re-validation pins stay. *Corpus:* the rule corpus stays at 2,185 cases and no verdict flips — `s27_8_0002`'s `rule:` header is re-quoted and `s12_8_0003`'s convenience constructor is given a distinct parameter list; the doc-example cases `spec_0067` and `codegen_0080` are hand-updated to match their edited fences (#1380: never regenerated).
