### v0.317 changelog (v0.316 → v0.317)

**The follow-up train to v0.316.** v0.316 filed thirteen questions its rulings surfaced ([#5478](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5478)–[#5490](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5490)), and the R28 corpus repair filed two more ([#5476](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5476), [#5477](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5477)). This revision rules on all fifteen in seven lanes. Twelve change text: ten rulings and clarifications in the normative documents, and two editorial corrections (a history-narration parenthetical in the spec, and proposal 0022's stated ground for a decline). Three are answered without a text change: #5476 and #5477 by the current text, and #5484 parked for the owner as a design change. At the owner's direction a question a lane surfaced was folded into that lane when it was within reach (same sections, decidable from the text and recorded decisions), and ten such fold-ins land here, each under the issue it was folded into, with one editorial correction the #5478 critique surfaced. Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique (13 blocking and 44 non-blocking findings, all resolved), and the 61 edits were applied as one sequence. A composition check over the union then fixed six seams: §9.2's *Through a type parameter* named no member for a class or other non-record substitution under its second and third kinds; rationale §7.7 did not state the cross-path cost of the kind-2 bridge; rationale §5.24's v0.317 addendum said rule 2 admits a mutable static auto-property only at two forms, which holds for class types only; the code-generation reference and §35.7 said "an owning choice" where §8.3 says a choice owning at every instantiation; and #5485's synchronous-iterator decline had no `DECLINED.md` row. Two critiques reclassified part of a lane as an owner decision, and both edit sets are parked ready to land: #5484 (retiring the setter-`value` shadowing exemption) and #5486's local-inline-array half. Proposal [0133](proposals/0133-set-erasing-positions.md), the design answer to #5375, is now `under-review` after its first critique round; its owner questions are open.

- **§3.6 / §28.3 / §28.8.1 — the "formerly …" notes on renamed terms are removed (editorial; surfaced by the v0.317 composition check).** The §3.6 rows for **hashable** and **auto-hashable**, and the *marker-free position* entries in §28.3, its ownership kernel and §28.8.1, carried the term each name replaced. Normative text states the current rule only; the renames are recorded in their changelog entries. No rule changes.
- **§5.1 / §8.1 — choices are named among the types that reach `Object` by boxing (editorial; folded into [#5479](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5479)).** Both lists predate choices. §5.1's *any type to `Object`* bullet and §8.1's root paragraph now name choices beside records and enums, with owning choices excluded beside owning inline arrays (§35.8).
- **§7.4 / §22.3 — storage inside a narrowed nullable value, and `ref`/`out` chains into it (ruling; [#5478](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5478)).** v0.316 typed a chain rooted at a narrowed variable by its final hop (§22.3) and did not say whether `ref n.X` over a narrowed `n: Pt?` is sound, or whether `n.X` is assignable at all. A new §7.4 paragraph, *Storage inside a narrowed nullable value*, decides both:
  - A member or index chain from `n` that does not leave `n`'s value through a class- or interface-typed member (§9.4's key) names storage inside the value. It is assignable wherever the same chain is on a `Pt` local, so `n.X := 5` stores into `n`'s value and `n` stays non-null.
  - The location exists only while `n` holds a value, so a store to it requires `n` narrowed **at the store**. An assignment stores after its right operand and a compound assignment after locating its target and evaluating its right operand (§6.6), so `n.X += F()` with `n` mutably captured, or `n.X := G(ref n)`, is a compile error.
  - A `ref` argument, or an inline-array argument at an `extern` parameter, can store at any point of the call; an `out` argument stores at its copy-out and an accessor target at its write-back (§22.3), after the callee's code has run. During the call a closure that captured `n`, or another argument naming `n`, can null it before that store, and §7.4's facts hold between operations, not during a call. Such a chain at those positions is therefore a compile error, whose diagnostic names the copy-out `var p: Pt := n; Inc(ref p.X); n := p;`.
  - A chain that leaves the value (`ref n.Owner.Name`) names storage in that object and is admitted.

  §22.3's chain sentence points at the paragraph. **Declined:** defining the write into an absent value's storage, which has no meaning in the language; and rejecting only where the narrowing can be invalidated during the call, which needs a during-the-call fact §7.4 does not have and would also have to account for a `ref`-parameter root. Two `DECLINED.md` rows. The direct-store half (the store checked at the store) is a fold-in under this issue. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. The code-generation reference's `ref`/`out` bullet gains the rejection and its remedy. **Compiler (tracked):** `checkRefOutOperandCategory` has no arm for such a chain, so `ref n.X` is admitted, and sema visits an assignment's target before its right operand, so the compound-assignment case is admitted too. `n.X := 5` already works (fix #416).
- **§8.3 / Appendix C.1 — the `Equals`→`GetHashCode` pairing reads both spellings on an enum or a choice (clarification; folded into [#5479](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5479)).** An enum's or choice's `Object`-slot `Equals` takes its own type, and §10.5 makes `override` and plain spell one member, which fills the slot and replaces the default for every consumer, hash containers included (`Set<E>` reaches the user's `Equals`/`GetHashCode`). A lone plain `Equals` there paired the author's equality with a hash it never saw, which is what §8.3's rule forbids. §8.3 now says the rule reads both spellings of both members: a plain `Equals` obliges `GetHashCode`, and a plain `GetHashCode` discharges the obligation. A choice owning at every instantiation is reached by no boxing and fills no slot, so its declared `Equals` carries no obligation; §35.7's lone-`Equals` example is scoped to it. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. The code-generation reference's equality-operator row states it. **Compiler (tracked):** `checkEqualsHashCodePairing` keys on the `override` spelling only, so it misses a plain lone `Equals`, rejects an `override` lone `Equals` on an always-owning choice, and rejects an `override Equals` beside a plain `GetHashCode`.
- **§8.5 / §8.6 — history narration removed from the boxed-receiver sentences (editorial; [#5482](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5482)).** §8.5's boxed-`ToString` parenthetical told what the sentence once claimed (a call-bounded copy) and why it was dropped, and §8.6's #3124 pin described "the question the parenthetical here left open" (a fold-in under this issue). Both keep only the bare pin; the borrow rule the sentences state is unchanged.
- **§9.2 / Appendix C.1, rationale §7.7 — equality on a `T`-typed operand is read at the substitution, and an instantiation at a type with no equality is rejected (ruling; [#5481](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5481)).** §9.2 rejects a direct `Equals`/`=` on a non-auto-hashable record, and v0.316 defined the boxed path. The third route, `x.Equals(y)` on an unconstrained `T` instantiated at such a record, was unstated. A new paragraph, *Through a type parameter*, states it:
  - Such a use, and `=`/`<>` over `T`-typed operands (§8.4's `Equals`), type-checks once against `Object`'s surface. The body's check fixes each use as one of three kinds: `Equals` against a `T` (with `=`/`<>`), `Equals` against any other argument, and `GetHashCode`.
  - At each instantiation the kind, not the body, is read against the substituted type, nullability stripped (§3.6 rule 2; §35.11), and reaches that type's own member for the kind. At a record that is its declared `Equals(T)`, else its declared `Equals(Object?)` or generated members; at an enum or choice its declared or generated `Equals`; at every other type the member the same use on an operand of that type binds.
  - `Equals` against a non-`T` argument, at a record, enum or choice whose only equality takes its own type, compares a boxed argument's payload by that member and is false for any other argument, `null` included: the bridge an enum's box already performs, and #5479's for a choice.
  - Where the type has no member for the kind, the instantiation is rejected at its site, the diagnostic naming the use, the type argument, the missing member and the `hashable` remedy. Every hashable type has a member for all three kinds, so `where T: hashable` states the requirement in the signature and its constraint failure replaces the interior diagnostic (§14.2).

  §35.7 points `T`-typed `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `=` and `<>` on a choice at the same rule. **Declined:** box identity, because a `T`-typed operand of a value substitution is a value, not a box, so `x.Equals(x)` would turn on the generics strategy §11.8 leaves open (irreflexive under per-call boxing); and a synthesized structural comparison, on v0.316's ground for the boxed path. Two `DECLINED.md` rows: the structural comparison on both paths, which also indexes v0.316's #3908 decline, and box identity on the generic path. The stated costs: an instantiation's validity depends on what the body does with `T`, §14.2's existing model for interior uses and §7.10's for copy demands, so adding such a use to a public generic's body can reject a client's instantiation although §2.8.6 classifies a carried-body change as preserving; and at a record whose only equality is `Equals(T)`, such as `IntPtr`, `x.Equals(o)` through `T` compares the payload of a boxed `o` while the boxed `o.Equals(x)` compares box identity (rationale §7.7). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: carve-out. The per-instantiation work evaluates a per-body fact (the set of use kinds with their sites, fixed at the body's one check; proposal 0103 §2 Class C's equality row) against the substitution's declared and generated members, and selects among them by kind; no body is re-checked. The code-generation reference's *Generics* paragraph states the rule. **Compiler (tracked):** sema has no per-instantiation equality check; codegen's #1091 redirect emits a structural choice comparison with no auto-hashable gate and returns no member for a non-auto-bearing record; the kind-2 bridge at an `Equals(T)`-only record is new work.
- **§9.8 / Appendix C.8, rationale §5.22 — a registry-less class's synthesized `Serialize` raises for a derived instance, and no component is rejected for its static type having derived classes (ruling; [#5488](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5488), [#5489](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5489)).** §9.8 made "a base-class-typed component" without a `polymorphic` registry a compile error but defined the term by a run-time condition, and every class not `sealed` can be a base while §9.8 makes `sealed` irrelevant to serialization. Separately, a derived class declaring components that conforms to `ISerializable` only through a base with a synthesized `Serialize` (§14.2 clause 1) wrote the base's form and dropped its own components. The rule now:
  - The synthesized `Serialize` of a class `C` with no registry of its own writes `C`'s form and raises `SerializationException` when the receiver's run-time type is a class derived from `C`, however the member is reached: as a component's `Serialize`, through a `C`-typed receiver, or as the member a derived class inherits. It is the registry's closed-set rule with `C` the set's one member. A `Weak<T>` or plain borrowing back-edge, written as a `$ref`, never reaches it, and a derived class's own synthesized form writes its inherited components without reaching it.
  - Name lookup selects between a base's and a derived class's synthesized members by the receiver's static type, as between §12.2's distinct members, a type-parameter receiver selecting as its type argument; a call through an `ISerializable` receiver runs the member the run-time class conforms through. A class is a synthesized class, and admissible as a component, only for a serialization interface its own inheritance clause lists.
  - No component is rejected because its static type has, or could have, derived classes (§2.8). An `abstract` or `closed` class with no registry of its own and a synthesized `Serialize`, as a serialized component's type (directly, or under `T?`, `Shared<T>`, or a collection's element, key or value type; a back-edge is admitted), is a compile error at the conformance declaration, and so is such a class declaring `IDeserializable` with no hand-written `Deserialize` (a fold-in under #5488): every non-null value through the member would raise, and `Deserialize` has nothing to construct (§12.5).

  Grounds: §9.8's field-name customization already says adding a component never silently drops it, whether a class has subclasses is not known where a component is declared, and one check in the member covers the base-typed component, the base-typed receiver and the non-redeclaring subclass. It is rationale §5.22's weak-reachability disposition: unrepresentable where a static rule reaches, detected and never silent where the property is per-value. The two restatements of the no-registry error in earlier entries (v0.122; the #659 entry) are not decline records, and #659's own `sealed` sentence removed the rule's only static trigger. **Declined:** a compile error, or a warning, at a derived class that declares components and inherits a synthesized `Serialize` without declaring `ISerializable` (a subclass never serialized would have to become serializable, a non-defaultable non-serializable field only by becoming nullable, and a redeclaring subclass reached through a base-typed receiver would stay unchecked); rejecting a non-`sealed` component type (against §9.8 and the stdlib's `Node` example); rejecting when a derived class exists (not decidable under separate compilation); and writing the run-time type's own form without a discriminator (the static type's `Deserialize` cannot read it). Two `DECLINED.md` rows. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. The code-generation reference's serialization paragraph states the rule. **Compiler (tracked):** `emitClassSerialize` writes the static type's form with no run-time check, and an abstract registry-less class is admitted as a component and with `IDeserializable`.
- **§12.7 — type narrowing shares §7.4's invalidating forms (clarification; [#5480](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5480)).** §12.7 said only "Reassignment within the controlled block invalidates the narrowing". It now cites §7.4's other forms (a `ref` or `out` argument and, for a mutably captured variable, the first operation that can transfer control to user code) and says that any reassignment invalidates the type narrowing whatever the right-hand side's type, while the assignment may still establish §7.4's non-null fact. v0.316's §22.3 bare-variable ruling (#4851) rests on this timing. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. **Compiler:** conforms (`narrowings_` is erased beside `nullNarrowed_` at each form).
- **§14.2 — `where T: value`'s list of nullable value types names no inline array (editorial; surfaced by the [#5478](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5478) critique).** The list named "the nullable form of any record, enum, or inline array", and §15.1 admits no nullable inline-array type (`([3]int)?`). The inline array is dropped from the list.
- **§28.3 — a borrow-bearing value argument contributes its carried borrows at a function-value invocation (ruling; [#5485](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5485)).** Row 4's function-value cell counted reference-typed and, since v0.316, function-typed plain arguments, and said value-typed arguments contribute nothing. But a lambda inhabiting a row-4 slot may return a borrow reached through its own parameter (*Concrete-slot function bodies*), and that parameter may be a borrow-bearing record such as `Ref(Item: Item)` or a span, so `get(r)` with `r := new Ref(x)` returned a borrow of `x` the caller attributed to `get` alone. A borrow-bearing record or inline-array argument, or one of a choice type that holds borrows, now contributes the sources of the borrows it carries, in row 4's cell and in clause 2 of the borrowed-field rule, which gains `_v := get(r)` as a rejected example. This is the count the `ref`/`out` rule and §9.7 already make. **Declined:** rejecting the borrow at the lambda instead, which would reject the ordinary selector `lambda(s) => s.Item` and split the concrete-slot admission from the bare-type-parameter callee side. One `DECLINED.md` row. Kernel: derivation (K2.2 + K2.4). Body-locality: local. The code-generation reference's back-reference line says so. **Compiler (tracked):** `borrowSourceForExpr`'s call arm keys on `calleeMethodDecl`, null for a function value, so a function-value invocation's result is sourced at no argument of any kind (#5376's shapes included).
- **§28.3 *Bare-type-parameter returns* — a borrow-bearing argument or receiver contributes its carried borrows (ruling; folded into [#5485](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5485)).** Caller-side clause 2 said an argument or receiver whose substituted type is a value type contributes no constraint, while the callee side admits a borrow reached through any source parameter, `b: Box<T>` included. Now only a runtime-managed value or a value that carries no borrow contributes nothing; a borrow-bearing record or inline array, or a choice that holds borrows, contributes the sources of the borrows it carries, so `static method Unwrap<T>(b: Box<T>): T => b.V;` over `record Box<T>(V: T)` lends, at `T = Item`, from what `b` carries. Kernel: derivation (K2.2 + K2.4). Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked):** `bareTypeParamCallSourceRoots` admits only class- and interface-typed arguments; the receiver is already counted.
- **§28.3 *Deferred-activation callees* / *Returning a deferred-activation frame* / §29.4 — a borrow-bearing argument's carried borrows ride the frame (ruling; folded into [#5485](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5485)).** §30.1 bans borrow-bearing parameters on the `async` kinds only, so a synchronous iterator may take a span, and its state machine holds the copy, but the frame's listed sources omitted it. The frame now carries the borrows of each plain borrow-bearing record, inline-array or holds-borrows choice argument, in the caller-side list, the callee-side return check and §29.4. A `CancellationToken` is excepted: §30.8 already admits it into `async` frames under a residual obligation that a static count would tighten. **Declined:** banning such parameters on synchronous iterators as §30.1 does on the `async` kinds, which would reject a frame consumed within its source's scope. One `DECLINED.md` row. Kernel: derivation (K2.4 + K6.2). Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked):** the frame's argument scan covers reference-typed plain arguments only.
- **§28.3 / §35.3 / §15.1 / §28.14 / Appendix C, rationale §4.2 — function-typed choice payloads and inline-array slots are fields for the closure bullet (ruling; [#5486](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5486)).** v0.316 made a record's function-typed component a field (#5377). Two holders of the same shape were unstated: a choice payload declared at a function type, which §35.4 leaves classification-neutral, so `Opt.Some(f)` from a call-bounded `f` was freely storable and returnable; and an inline array of function type. A new §28.3 bullet, *Choice payloads and inline-array slots of function type*, makes a function-typed payload, and each slot of a function-typed inline array that is a field, a parameter, a record component or a payload, a field under the closure bullet. A case-construction argument for such a payload (the declared-result form included), each element of a collection literal targeting such an array wherever the literal stands, and an element assignment to such a slot are stores judged at the site: a capture-free value is admitted, and one with a non-empty source set is rejected. A function value read from such a slot, or bound out of such a payload by a pattern, carries the empty set. A local inline array of function type stays a collection under the closure bullet and §28.14's call-bounded default. The keying is on the declared type, so a payload or element declared at a type parameter (`Result<() -> int, E>.Ok(f)`) is not reached; that is #5375's question (proposal 0133). §28.14's list of call-bounded stores names both, and §35.3, §15.1 and Appendix C cross-reference the bullet. **Declined:** classifying the choice or array by what it holds (§3.6 rule 1, as for #5377). One `DECLINED.md` row. Kernel: derivation (K2.4). Body-locality: local. The code-generation reference's closure line names both. **Compiler (tracked):** a case construction is checked as a plain call, and an `IndexExpr` into an inline array is no store destination, so both shapes are admitted. **Parked for the owner:** making the slots of a *local* inline array fields too, which would reject a received callback in `var fs: [1]() -> int := [cb];`. It tightens §28.14's stated permission that a call-bounded callback may live in "a purely local collection", and it is the inline-array instance of the open local-collection question (Migration, *Filed as questions*), so it is decided with that question and with proposal 0133.
- **§28.3 / §23.3 / §22.12 / Appendix C, rationale §5.24 — a static property assignment of a borrow-carrying value is a store into a static (ruling; [#5487](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5487)).** v0.316 (#5387) read an instance-property assignment as a field store and left static properties open. A static auto-property's assignment stores into a static field, which §22.12 rule 2 admits for a class type only at forms (i) and (ii), where a fresh value is discharged into process lifetime; a block-form static setter's `value` is a plain parameter, so a fresh value would be disposed at its full-expression boundary even when the setter stores it. §28.3's *property stores* bullet now reads a static property assignment, not through `set(owned)`, as a store into a non-`owned` static field declared as the property is (its declared type, and `readonly` for a `static readonly` auto-property), whatever the form:
  - A `static readonly` auto-property's assignment in its type's static initialization is the `static readonly` field store, which discharges a fresh value (§22.13).
  - At a settable static property a fresh value is admitted, and is process-lived, only where rule 2 admits a mutable static of that type, even when a block-form setter drops it; such a setter therefore leaves it undisposed until exit, the bounded cost §22.13 accepts for a displaced static. At any other type, where the property can only be block-form, it is §28.6's fresh-store error.
  - A borrow of a scope-bound local or an `owned` parameter is rejected; a class- or interface-typed borrow is admitted where the field-store bullet admits it, under its residual and domain clause; a borrow-bearing record or choice value only in the null-source form.

  §11.8 defers static interface properties, so every site resolves its declaration; the ground is verdict and disposal stability across an auto-to-block rewrite (#5360's), with A4's write-face reading. §23.3, §22.12's *Ownership* store semantics and Appendix C say so. The cost: a block-form static setter of a class type outside rule 2's forms receives no fresh value or scope-bound borrow; the remedy is `set(owned)` or a static method. **Declined:** reading the assignment by accessor form, which changes a client's verdict and its value's disposal point when the form changes; and rejecting every fresh value at a static property, which would withdraw rule 2's store semantics for admitted static auto-properties, the `Task?` cache among them, and §22.13's discharge of a `static readonly` one. Two `DECLINED.md` rows. Kernel: derivation (K2.3, with the field-store bullet's K4.3 residual and §22.13's discharge). Body-locality: local. The code-generation reference's field-store line gains the static sentence. **Compiler (tracked):** the fresh-store check is field-only, so `T.P := new Item()` is unchecked at every static property, and whether a block-form static setter's fresh value is disposed at its boundary is unprobed.
- **§35.7 / Appendix C.1 — a non-auto-hashable choice's boxed `Equals` and `GetHashCode` are decided per member (clarification; [#5479](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5479)).** §35.7 and §35.8 gave only the boxed `ToString`. A new §35.7 sentence is the twin of v0.316's §9.2 record sentence: a boxed receiver reaches, member by member, the choice's declared `Equals(other: C)` or `GetHashCode(): int`, and otherwise the inherited `Object` member, reference equality of the boxes and the box's identity hash (§8.3). A choice's declared `Equals(other: C)` fills the box's `Object` slot in either spelling, because §35.2 carries §10.5's replacement rule to the boxable classifications, where a record's `Equals(T)` does not (§25.2, a record having a separate `Equals(Object?)`). An argument that is not a boxed `C`, `null` included, compares unequal. No structural comparison or hash is synthesized, and a `T`-typed operand is not a boxed receiver (#5481). **Declined:** a structural boxed comparison, on v0.316's ground for records (the `DECLINED.md` row #5481 adds covers both). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked):** the box vtable installs the identity thunks for every non-auto-hashable choice, so a declared `Equals(C)`/`GetHashCode` is never reached through a box (identity with no declared member is already right, fix #3900).
- **Stdlib §2.3 — `Convert.ToString` returns the argument's own `ToString()` text (clarification; [#5490](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5490)).** §2.3 tied the `To*`/`Try*` methods to §9's `Parse` family but gave `ToString` no rule, so §2.18's round-trip form and v0.316's non-finite spellings reached `Convert.ToString` only by assumption; rationale §15.x already calls `Convert` a thin veneer over `Parse`/`ToString`. A new paragraph states that each one-argument `ToString` returns the received value's no-format `ToString()` text, and `ToString(value, toBase)` returns `value.ToString(toBase)`'s: `Convert.ToString(true)` is `"True"` and `Convert.ToString(1.0 / 0.0)` is `"Infinity"`. It also states the consequence of the five-overload surface under spec §22.6: a `float` has one applicable overload and widens, so `Convert.ToString(0.1f)` is `"0.10000000149011612"` where `0.1f.ToString()` is `"0.1"`; a `char`, `sbyte`, `byte`, `short`, `ushort`, `uint` or `ulong` argument converts co-equally to two or more overloads and is ambiguous, with a cast or the value's own `ToString()` as the remedy. A stale `// elision expanded` comment on the `long` overload, a history residue, is removed (a fold-in under this issue). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: not applicable (a run-time library contract). The code-generation reference's `Convert` block gains the equation and the widening example. **Compiler (tracked):** sema types any one-argument `Convert.ToString` as `string` without overload resolution, so `char`, `byte`, `uint`, `ulong`, `string` and nullable arguments are admitted and rendered in their own type, and a `float` renders `"0.1"`.
- **Stdlib §9.1 — an integer's no-format `ToString()` is `ToString(10)`'s text (clarification; folded into [#5490](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5490)).** §9.1 stated the radix rendering and §2.18 every other primitive's no-format form, but not an integer's, which §2.3's new paragraph now leans on. It is `ToString(10)`'s text: a `-` for a negative value, the decimal digits, a single `0` for zero, no leading zeros and no grouping (`(-42).ToString()` is `"-42"`), and an interpolation hole without a format spec uses it (spec §18.5). **Compiler:** conforms.
- **Rationale §15.y, `DECLINED.md`, proposal 0123 — the generic-`Math.Abs` decline's premise corrected; the decision is unchanged (clarification; folded into [#5490](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5490)).** The *`Math.Sign` is one generic* paragraph, the generic-`Abs<T>` row and proposal 0123 §5 item 2 said `Math.Abs(shortVal)` resolves to `Abs(int)` by widening and that a `char` argument to `Math.Sign` was admitted by `char → int`. Spec §22.6 ranks every implicit conversion co-equal, and `short`, `sbyte` and `char` each convert to all four per-type parameter types, so each call was ambiguous, the same rule §2.3's new paragraph states for `Convert.ToString`. The decline now rests on `Math.Abs(floatVal)`, which resolves to `Abs(double)` because `float → double` is its one applicable conversion and would return `float` under a generic; a generic would also admit the `short`/`sbyte` calls that are ambiguous today, and the `Sign` change's `char` cost was nil. The v0.290 entry's R4 bullet is pinned and stays as written; this entry records the correction.
- **Proposal 0022 §5.1, §11 item 2 — the ground for declining `Assert.Equal(Object, Object)` restated (editorial; [#5483](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5483)).** The proposal said a boxed record compares by reference equality and quoted §9.2's pre-v0.316 sentence. An auto-hashable record's box dispatches its generated `Equals(Object?)` (§9.2); the identity fallthrough belongs to records and choices outside the auto-hashable set that declare no equality, the types the generic `where T: hashable` form rejects at the instantiation site with the constraint failure (§14.2). The decline stands; the proposal's currency note records the correction.

  - **§12.1 / §12.2 — `override` of a non-virtual base member (no change; [#5476](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5476)).** §12.1 makes a member non-virtual unless marked `virtual`, and §12.2 makes a same-named derived member a compile error unless it is an `override` of a virtual member. The compiler rejects the form with its §12.1 diagnostic, which the lit suite pins; the issue's own discovery section quotes that rejection. The defect is rule-corpus case `s20_0006`, whose fixture overrode a non-`virtual` `Animal.Speak` and so was rejected before §20 was reached. Its repair (the base method `virtual`, `12.1` added to `cites:`) lands separately with a baseline bank from a built compiler, and is not part of this landing.
  - **§22.12 rule 2 — a mutable `string` static in an evaluation-order probe (no change; [#5477](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5477)).** Rule 2's verdict table gives a mutable `string` static *error (iii)-closed*: the form-(iii) set grows only by recorded ruling, and that cell is declined (rationale §12.15). The compiler's rejection is correct, and the rule leaves room for such a probe through an instance field, a warned primitive static, or output written by each condition. The defect is rule-corpus case `s20_0012`, which kept a mutable `string` static; its repair (each condition writes its letter to standard output, and the case asserts `AB` and `2`) lands separately with the same baseline bank.
  - **Appendix B / §21.1 — whether a setter's implicit `value` keeps its shadowing exemption (parked for the owner; [#5484](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5484)).** The lane's answer is to retire the exemption: a declaration in a setter body may not take the name `value` while the implicit parameter is in scope, with a fresh name or `set(v)` as the remedy, because under `set(owned)` the implicit `value` holds the setter's owned obligation and a same-named local hides it with no qualified spelling (#5267's and #5252's setter rows were defects of that shape). The critique reclassified it as a design change: the permission is stated normative text (Appendix B), and v0.314 and v0.316 each re-affirmed it, so retiring it is a tightening of a stated permission (process §2). The edit set is parked ready to land on the owner's acceptance, and the text is unchanged in this revision.

### v0.318 changelog (v0.317 → v0.318)

**The follow-up train to v0.317.** v0.317 filed eleven questions its rulings surfaced ([#5491](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5491)–[#5501](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5501)). Six carry `needs-owner-decision` as design-change-sized and stay with the owner. This revision rules on the five the text could decide, in two lanes: `generic` ([#5492](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5492), [#5493](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5493), [#5494](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5494)) and `sermisc` ([#5498](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5498), [#5501](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5501)). Four are rulings or clarifications in the normative documents, and #5501 is an editorial correction. One question surfaced while drafting #5492 is folded into it (a choice component of a generated rendering), and Appendix C.1 gains v0.316's synthesized-serialization-member exemption, which it never carried. Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique (4 blocking and 14 non-blocking findings, all resolved), and the 22 edits were applied as one sequence. #5498's draft ruling admitted a derived class's hand-written `Serialize`/`Deserialize` over a base's synthesized one. The critic rejected that draft as a design change: it relaxes §12.2's stated rule and contradicts the recorded member-hiding decline (rationale §8.1). The landed ruling therefore states that the rejection is intended, and the relaxation goes to the owner as a question. A composition check over the union then fixed four seams: the #5493 sentence scoping its rule to user declarations said a standard-library generic type is well-formed wherever its declared constraints admit the arguments, which contradicted §14.4's class-only restriction on the owning collections, named in the same paragraph (spec and rationale); §15.1.2's per-instantiation check reached only a bare type-parameter element, so `[N][M]T` and `[N]Box<T>` comparisons would have fallen to the body's weakest assumption; #5493's list of members a constrained extension block cannot carry left out constructors, destructors, field initializers and settable properties, which §26.3 also excludes (spec and code-generation reference); and the hashable row read "(a) …, and (b) …, and (c) …".

- **§3.6 rule 2 / Appendix C.1, rationale §10 — an interior-use requirement in a member of a generic type belongs to the constructed type (ruling; [#5493](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5493)).** v0.317's §9.2 *Through a type parameter* rejects "the instantiation" at a substitution with no equality, and §7.10's copy demand has the same shape. Neither said, for a member of a generic type, whether the instantiation is the type or a use of the member. §14.1 *Instantiation and its site* answers it: an instantiation is of the declaration that declares the parameter, a type is instantiated by being named, and a rule that fires at the instantiation site fires at every such site. §3.6 rule 2 now says so:
  - A use of a generic type's parameter in any member body, accessor, constructor, initializer or destructor the program declares for the type is a requirement of the constructed type. It is checked at every site that names the type, whether or not the member is reached: `var b: Bag<R>;` is rejected when `Bag<T>.Contains` compares `T` and `R` has no equality, even if `Contains` is never called. A use of a generic method's own parameter is checked at each instantiation of the method.
  - The rule reads user declarations only. A standard-library generic type's member bodies, the span records' Bezel realization included (stdlib §4.14, §4.15), add no requirement of this kind. Such a type is rejected at an instantiation only by its declared constraints and the instantiation-site rules stated for it, such as §14.4's class-only restriction. Otherwise `ArraySpan<R>` and `ReadOnlyArraySpan<R>` would be rejected at every non-hashable `R`, against `Array<T>.AsSpan()`, every built-in's `FromCollectionLiteral(elements: ReadOnlyArraySpan<T>)` and §15.4's literal lowering.
  - A member that should demand more of the type's arguments than the type does is written as a generic method over its own parameter, or in a constrained extension block (`extension Bag<T> where T: hashable`), the form §14.2 names as user-writable for a member present at some instantiations only. A member neither form can carry (an override, an interface implementation, an operator, an indexer, a constructor, a destructor, a field initializer, a settable property; §26.3) makes its use a requirement of the type, stated by a constraint on the type's parameter.

  Appendix C.1's equality bullet and the code-generation reference's *Generics* line point at the rule. **Declined:** checking a member's requirement only where the member is reached. That would be a member present at some instantiations only, conditioned on the enclosing type's arguments, which §14.2 rule 1 reserves to registered standard-library rows and whose declared form (a member `where` naming an enclosing parameter) Appendix C.1 rejects. It would also need its own account of members reached with no visible use (overrides and interface implementations by dispatch, a destructor by disposal). One `DECLINED.md` row. The stated costs: a user collection with one equality-using member is unusable at a non-hashable element type, with no remedy short of `where T: hashable` on the type when that member implements `ICollection<T>.Contains`, where the standard library's `Array<R>` is usable; and a body edit adding such a use rejects every client that names the type, not only those that call the member (§2.8.6's interior-use gap, at a wider reach). The standard library's unconstrained equality-using members (`List<T>.Contains`, the span `IndexOf` family) stay with [#5491](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5491) (owner decision). Read with this ruling, #5491's constrained-block option is what a user library does, and its use-site option is a §14.2 register row per member family. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: carve-out (the per-type fact is the union of the member bodies' interior-use facts, proposal 0103 §2 Class C, evaluated against the substitution at each naming site; no body is re-checked). **Compiler (tracked):** sema has no per-instantiation interior-use check at either granularity (v0.317's #5481 item); this ruling fixes where that check fires for a generic type.
- **§3.6 / §15.1.2 / §9.2 / Appendix C.1 — a nullable type or inline array over a non-hashable type is not hashable, and an inline array has equality only over a hashable element (ruling; [#5494](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5494)).** §3.6's hashable row excluded only records and choices, so `[2]R` and `R?` over a non-hashable record `R` read as hashable. Yet the row defines the property as consistent `Equals`/`GetHashCode`, `[2]R`'s element-wise equality (§15.1.2, §15.3) and hash (§8.3) reach `R`'s missing members, and v0.317's "every hashable S has a member for all three kinds" (§9.2) failed there. The exception list was an omission against three explicit statements of the element condition, not a stated permission.
  - The row gains clause (c): a nullable `T?`, or an inline array of any form whose element type is `T` or `T?`, is excluded where `T` is excluded by (a), (b) or (c) itself, so `[2][2]R` and `([2]R)?` are excluded too.
  - §15.1.2: an inline array whose element type, nullability stripped, is not hashable has no equality. `=`, `<>`, `Equals`, `GetHashCode` and `Contains` (and so `in`) on it are a use-site error naming the element type, with that type's §9.2 or §35.7 remedies, and nothing is synthesized in their place. Where the element type is or contains a type parameter, the check is made at each instantiation (§3.6 rule 2), and `where T: hashable` states it in the signature.
  - §9.2's *Through a type parameter* names §15.1.2's error beside its own and §35.7's, and Appendix C.1 gains the bullet. The code-generation reference's `Dictionary<K, V>` comment says `K?` and `[N]K` are hashable exactly when `K` is.

  The nullable half states what the compiler already does. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local (discharged by the substitution's hashable fact at a type-parameter element). **Compiler (tracked):** `isEqualityBearing` treats every inline array as hashable, the `=`/`<>` use-site gate inspects only record operands, and `emitInlineArrayEquality` compares element-wise with no hashable gate.
- **§8.5 / §35.7, rationale §7.7 — a `T`-typed operand at a choice with no `ToString` renders the qualified type name (ruling; [#5492](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5492)).** §8.5 and §35.7 gave a non-auto-hashable choice two answers: a `ToString()` call at a statically-known receiver type is a use-site error, and a boxed receiver renders the qualified type name. A `T`-typed operand, a receiver or interpolation hole whose static type is a type parameter, is neither. `x.ToString()` or `$"{x}"` in a generic body instantiated at such a choice renders the qualified name, as the box does, and the instantiation is not rejected. For an owning choice the receiver is borrowed, not boxed. A declared `ToString` is reached as before, and the use-site error at the choice's own static type stays. **Declined:** rejecting the instantiation (a fourth kind beside v0.317's three equality kinds). No constraint states a rendering requirement (`hashable` does not imply one: a value-like choice outside auto-hashable only through its homogeneous `=` is hashable and has no generated `ToString`), so the rejection would be an interior diagnostic with no signature-side remedy, the shape §14.2's derived-property paragraph exists to replace, and it would fall on every generic logging or message helper. Unlike box identity on the equality path, the qualified name is a function of the type alone, so it does not depend on how generics are realized (§11.8). The stated cost: `$"{x}"` prints a type name where the author may have wanted the value, and a generic body and a concrete one disagree on whether the same rendering compiles; a choice whose rendering matters declares `ToString`. One `DECLINED.md` row. v0.301's decline of a synthesized case-shaped default is untouched. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked):** codegen reports #2479 for a `T`-typed receiver and on the bare-`T` interpolation path; the concrete-receiver diagnostic stays.
- **§8.5 — a choice component with no `ToString` renders its qualified type name (clarification; folded into [#5492](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5492)).** §8.5's component rule renders each component "as its own `ToString` renders it (virtual dispatch …)". A positional record's field may be a borrow-bearing or inadmissible-payload choice with none, and no user call is written at its static type. Such a component renders the qualified name, as the choice's box does. The same §8.5 sentence states it with #5492, and §35.7 points at both. Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked):** `emitValueToString` falls through to the empty string.
- **§9.8 / §12.2 / Appendix C.1, C.8 — a derived class's hand-written serialization member over a base's synthesized one is a §12.2 hiding declaration (clarification, gated as a ruling; [#5498](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5498)).** v0.316 exempted a derived class's *synthesized* `Serialize`/`Deserialize` from §12.2. #5498 asked whether a member the derived class *hand-writes* over a base's synthesized member is exempt too. It is not, and the rejection is intended: §12.2 blocks the name of any inherited member visible at the derived class's declaration site, §9.8 says such a class inherits the base's synthesized member, and the exemption covers only the members the compiler generates for the derived class's own conformance. For a direction a base synthesizes, the derived class's own member is its synthesized one.
  - §9.8 *Inherited components* states the rule. §9.8's eligibility error no longer lists hand-writing among its remedies for a direction a base class synthesizes.
  - §12.2, Appendix C.1 (which lacked v0.316's exemption, an editorial completion riding here) and C.8 carry both halves: synthesized, exempt; hand-written over a synthesized base member, not.
  - §9.8 *Suppression*'s "always valid regardless of eligibility" waives the conformance declaration's eligibility error, not the hand-written member's standing under §12.2.
  - The code-generation reference's serialization line states the rejection.

  **Not decided here:** admitting such a member. The lane's draft did, with an exception for classes a base's `polymorphic` registry names and an exemption of `base.Serialize(s)` from v0.317's run-time check; the critique reclassified it as a design change, because it relaxes §12.2's stated rule and admits the static-type-selected shadow the member-hiding decline rejects (`DECLINED.md` "Member hiding", rationale §8.1). It is filed for the owner with the draft as its candidate design and the critique's two open soundness points (identity tags under `base.Serialize(s)`, and no read counterpart for a static `Deserialize`). No `DECLINED.md` row: the relaxation is parked, not declined. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked):** a synthesized member has no symbol, so `checkHidingAndOverride` never sees it and admits the hand-written derived member today (from source reading; not probed).
- **§28.3 — row 4's function-value-invocation summary names every contributing argument (editorial; [#5501](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5501)).** The bold summary said "every plain (non-`owned`) reference-typed argument", while its detail also counts function-typed arguments (v0.316) and borrow-bearing record, inline-array and holds-borrows choice arguments (v0.317). It now reads "every plain (non-`owned`) argument that is or can carry a borrow". No rule changes.

- **Migration.** *Newly rejected (spec-ahead-of-impl):*
  - Naming `G<R>` where a member of a user generic type `G<T>` uses `T` in a way `R` does not admit (§9.2's equality kinds, §7.10's copy demand), even when that member is never called: `var b: Bag<R>;` for `class Bag<T>` whose `Contains(x: T)` calls `Equals`, with `R` a record with a class-typed field and no declared equality (#5493).
  - `where T: hashable` at `[N]R`, `Set<[N]R>`, `Dictionary<[N]R, V>` and the `hashable` LINQ block over `[N]R`, for a non-hashable `R`; `=`, `<>`, `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `Contains` and `in` on `[N]R`; an instantiation of a generic body comparing `[N]T` operands at such an `R` (#5494).

  *Newly accepted (spec-ahead-of-impl):*
  - `x.ToString()` and `$"{x}"` on a `T`-typed operand instantiated at a borrow-bearing, owning or inadmissible-payload choice that declares no `ToString`; the compiler rejects both today with the #2479 diagnostic (#5492).

  *Newly stated:*
  - The rendering in that case, and of such a choice as a component of a generated rendering, is the qualified type name; today a component renders the empty string (#5492 and its fold-in).
  - `R?` is not hashable where `R` is not (`Set<R?>`, `where T: hashable` at `R?`); this matches the compiler (#5494).

  - Rationale paragraphs: §7.7 (#5492) and §10 (#5493).

Probe: `[2]R = [2]R` and `Set<[2]R>` for `record R(C: Widget)`. No test flips (the hashable tests use admissible elements only).

The concrete-receiver pins in both files and `nullable_value_tostring_receiver_3481.non_auto_hashable_choice_still_diagnosed_{nullable,non_nullable}` stay.

### v0.319 changelog (v0.318 → v0.319)

**The second follow-up wave.** v0.318 filed six questions its rulings surfaced ([#5503](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5503)–[#5508](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5508)). Two carry `needs-owner-decision` as design-change-sized and stay with the owner ([#5505](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5505), [#5506](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5506)). This revision rules on the four the text could decide, in two lanes: `gen2` ([#5503](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5503), [#5504](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5504)) and `row4` ([#5507](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5507), [#5508](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5508)). Three are rulings or clarifications, and #5508 is an editorial correction. Two questions surfaced while drafting #5507 are folded into it (a deferred-activation frame's sources, and row 5's caller-side exclusion in a generic body). The `gen2` critique also folded in a correction of v0.318's own text: §3.6's hashable clause (c) and §15.1.2 named inline-array forms §15.1 does not admit. Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique (3 blocking and 15 non-blocking findings, all resolved or recorded), and the 21 edits were applied as one sequence. The `row4` critic's blocking finding was a fourth list of row 4's contributing arguments the draft left unamended (the field-store bullet's clause 2, the check that actually reads them at `_v := f(x)`). The `gen2` critic's was that #5504's §3.6 sentence, through §14.1's list of instantiation-site rules, decided the declared-constraint question the lane meant to leave open; the landed sentence excludes declared constraints by name. A composition check over the union then fixed five seams: §35.7's clause said a generic choice "whose type arguments contain a type parameter" where §8.5 says "are or contain"; §35.11's new sentence spoke of "an operand of the choice type", which read as covering a closed instantiation such as `Result<Widget, string>` that §8.5 keeps rejected, and now names type arguments that are or contain a type parameter in scope; Appendix C.1's new clause said "or calls that method" with no method in the bullet to refer to; row 5's caller-side clause 2 carried #5507's parenthetical directly beside its existing one, and the two are merged; and the rationale's #5504 paragraph narrated the compiler's history with #2713 where it needed only the measured fact. The owner has accepted proposal 0133 ([#5375](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5375)); it lands with the other owner decisions in the train that follows as v0.320.

- **§8.5 / §35.7 / §35.11, rationale §7.7 — an operand typed by a generic choice over a type parameter renders the qualified type name where the instantiation has no `ToString` (ruling; [#5503](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5503)).** v0.318 settled a bare `T`-typed operand (#5492). It left open `r: Result<T, E>` in a generic body, whose static type is a choice type while its classification, and so whether it has a generated `ToString`, is decided per instantiation (§35.11).
  - Such an operand now renders as a `T`-typed operand does. At an instantiation that is not auto-hashable and declares no `ToString`, `r.ToString()` and `$"{r}"` render the instantiated type's qualified name (its `FullName` rendering, type arguments recursing), and the instantiation is not rejected.
  - A choice type containing no type parameter (`Result<Widget, string>`) is a statically-known receiver type in a generic body as anywhere else, and keeps §35.7's use-site error. The test is the operand's static type, not its spelling: an inferred local of type `Result<T, E>` renders.
  - §35.11 states that rendering is not among the classification-dependent rules enforced at the instantiation. §35.7's boxed-receiver clause and the code-generation reference's interpolation line name the case.

  **Declined:** rejecting the instantiation. No admitted constraint establishes the classification: `where T: hashable` admits a class `T`, at which `Result<T, E>` is owning, and a record declaring its own equality, which is not an admissible component (§9.2). The rejection would also refuse through `Result<T, E>` the value a bare `T` renders at the same substitution, so a more precise static type would compile in fewer programs. `Result<T, E>` gains no declared `ToString`: rendering its payloads at the owning and borrow-bearing instantiations is the case-shaped default v0.301 declined, and the auto-hashable instantiations already have the generated rendering. One `DECLINED.md` row. The stated cost is #5492's: a generic body and a concrete one disagree on whether the same rendering compiles, and a user generic choice whose rendering matters declares `ToString` (§35.2 admits it at every classification). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked):** codegen specializes the body and reports #2479 at the concrete instantiation for a `C<T>`-typed receiver and hole; the fact that the operand's type contained a type parameter must reach it from sema or be recorded before substitution.
- **§3.6 rule 2 / §14.1 / §9.2 / Appendix C.1, rationale §10 — a requirement reaches the outer declaration through a substitution (ruling; [#5504](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5504)).** v0.318 made an interior-use requirement the constructed type's (#5493). It did not say what happens when the type is named at another declaration's type parameter: `class Outer<T>` holding a `Bag<T>`, or `F<U>` calling `Eq<U>`. Read literally, §9.2's per-kind rule admitted the inner naming, because at a type-parameter substitution the use reached `Object`'s member, and then nothing ever rejected `Outer<R>`.
  - §3.6 rule 2: where a user declaration forms an instantiation at a type argument that is or contains a type parameter in scope, a requirement of that instantiation which the parameter's constraints do not establish (§14.2) is decided not at that site but at the instantiations the declaration's own instantiations form by substitution. This covers an interior use's requirement and an instantiation-site rule's (§14.4, §15.1.1, §28.5). `Outer<R>` is rejected wherever it is named where `Bag<R>` would be, whether or not the member forming it is reached, and `F<R>` at each call where `Eq<R>` would be. It holds through any chain of declarations, with the diagnostic at the first site whose argument decides the requirement, naming the chain.
  - A requirement the parameter's constraints establish is discharged where it is written (`class Outer<T> where T: hashable` holding a `Bag<T>`). A declared `where` constraint is not a requirement of this kind: its satisfaction at such an argument stays §14.2's (filed as a question).
  - §14.1 *Instantiation and its site* states the forming fact: a site whose arguments contain a type parameter forms, at each instantiation of the innermost declaration declaring one, the instantiation its arguments substitute to, and §14.6's request graph reads the same forms.
  - §9.2 *Through a type parameter*: at an `S` that is a type parameter in scope, no constraint of which supplies a member for the use's kind, the use is a use through `S`, read in turn at `S`'s substitutions.
  - Appendix C.1's equality bullet and the code-generation reference's *Generics* line carry one clause each.
  - The rule reads user declarations and instantiations formed by substitution. A standard-library declaration carries nothing (v0.318's rule-2 sentence, unchanged), so `Array<R>` forming `ArraySpan<R>` in its signatures carries no requirement. An override's body reached by dispatch through its base's signature is filed separately.

  **Declined:** deciding the requirement at the inner site. A type parameter has no structure for a property-dependent rule to read, so the inner site would admit it, and one level of wrapping would launder every instantiation-site rule; §14.4's owning-element restriction so laundered (`OwningCache<string>` over `OwningArray<T>`, §14.4's own example) is a measured use-after-free ([#2713](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/2713)). **Also declined:** making the wrapper state the requirement as a constraint of its own. Most of these rules have no admitted constraint to state them (a copyable substitution, §7.10; an admissible `as` target, §17.4; the runtime-managed exclusion of §14.4 and §28.5 short of `IDisposable`), and the rejection would refuse wrappers at their admissible instantiations. Two `DECLINED.md` rows. The stated cost: an edit adding a requirement to a declaration's body or fields rejects clients of every declaration that wraps it, at any depth (§2.8.6's interior-use gap, at a wider reach again; filed as a question). Kernel: no contact (§28.5's per-instantiation check keeps its K1.6 derivation; only the set of sites grows). Body-locality: carve-out, confinement (i): the per-declaration fact is the union of its own interior-use facts and the facts of the instantiations it forms at its parameters, each yielded at its body's single check, composed by substitution fact-through-fact over the §14.6 request graph (the shape proposal 0105 §2 admits for §22.13), with a fixed point within a strongly-connected component; §14.6's bounded instantiation closure keeps the formed set finite, and no body is re-checked. **Compiler (tracked):** the chain is implemented for §14.4's owning element, §15.1.1's owning inline array, §17.4's `as` target and nested declared constraints; hash-container keys are checked one level deep; §28.5's owned field and every generic method's own parameter are not checked through a substitution; and there is no interior-use check at all (v0.317's #5481 item).

That recursive arm reaches only nested inline arrays and nullable inline arrays, which §15.1 does not admit ("Inline arrays may not be elements of inline arrays in the form `[N][M]T`"; "`([3]int)?` is not admitted"), and v0.318's entry glossed it with `[2][2]R` and `([2]R)?`. §15.1.2 likewise gave `[N][M]T` as an example of an element type containing a type parameter.

On every type §15.1 admits this is the same predicate: a directly written `T` is a record, choice, class, interface, primitive, enum, unit or function type, or a type parameter, so "not hashable" is exactly (a) or (b). It still recurses, so it stays right if a substitution can form a nested or nullable inline array.
  - §15.1.2's example is `[N]Pair<T>`.
  - No verdict changes. Whether a substitution can form a nested or nullable inline array (`[N]T` or `T?` at `T = [M]int`) is filed as a question. Body-locality: local.
- **§28.3 — a type-parameter-typed argument contributes in a generic body (clarification, gated as a ruling; [#5507](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5507)).** Row 4's function-value-invocation cell lists the arguments that contribute to the result's source set by kinds known only after substitution, and said nothing of an argument typed by a type parameter. A generic body is checked once, under the weakest assumption its constraints establish (§3.6 rule 2; §28.1 clause 3's class-or-interface assumption).
  - The cell now says that such an argument, or one whose borrow-bearing or holds-borrows classification turns on a type parameter, contributes at every substitution the union of what each substitution its constraints admit would contribute: at a type parameter admitting a class or interface substitution, what a class- or interface-typed argument contributes; under `where T: value`, the sources of the borrows it may carry.

Its wording already said so.

Rejecting a body's flow violations only at class instantiations would be a per-instantiation re-check of a body that no rule designates; rationale §5.7's per-instantiation enforcement is of declaration-keyed rules (row 5's callee side, §28.5's generic field), not of a body's flow. ### v0.320 changelog (v0.319 → v0.320)

**The owner-decision train.** On 2026-10-08 the owner accepted proposal [0133](proposals/0133-set-erasing-positions.md) ([#5375](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5375)) with its §7 recommendations, and accepted every recommendation the coordinator put to them on the open `needs-owner-decision` questions filed by v0.317 and v0.318. This revision lands those decisions, with the three decidable questions v0.319 filed, in four lanes:
- `g0133`: the graduation of proposal 0133 ([#5375](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5375)), with #5486's parked local half ([#5486](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5486)) and [#5499](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5499), which 0133's soundness argument depends on.
- `owner`: [#5484](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5484), [#5500](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5500) and [#5491](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5491), and the declines [#5497](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5497), [#5505](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5505) and [#5506](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5506).
- `misc`: [#5510](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5510), [#5512](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5512) and [#5513](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5513), with a §2.8.6 narration fix.
- `g0134`: the graduation of proposal [0134](proposals/0134-ref-parameters-do-not-narrow.md) ([#5495](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5495)). Proposal 0134 was drafted in this train from the owner's accepted option (ii) and critiqued before graduation (3 blocking and 9 non-blocking findings, all resolved in the proposal).

Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique: 6 blocking and 35 non-blocking findings, all resolved or recorded (`g0133` 3 and 10, `owner` 1 and 9, `misc` 2 and 8, `g0134` 0 and 8). The 114 edits (`g0133` 40, `owner` 31, `misc` 17, `g0134` 26) were applied as one sequence.

The critics' blocking findings were these:
- `g0133`: return-slot covariance still let a function value reach `Object` with no site (`() -> (() -> int)` used as `() -> Object`), so §27.1.1 now states both directions. A `scoped o: Object` parameter had been declared never set-erasing, though `Object` is a class (§3.1). A `yield return` of a function value had been left open, and is now judged as a `return` is.
- `owner`: the new §14.2 bullet called the signature remedy "closed" for every member of the equality search, which is true only for the interface members.
- `misc`: the #5510 records dropped one of the two grounds of v0.319's recorded decline, and its migration list of pinning tests was mostly wrong. The corrected list is 10 lit files and 21 gtest cases, including 7 tests that would go vacuous rather than fail.

A composition check over the union then fixed four seams:
- §23.3 and Appendix B called the setter's implicit `value` "a parameter of the setter like any other", which read against §28.3 and §28.14's empty-set treatment of that parameter. It is now "a parameter of the setter", with §21.1 applying "as to any other parameter".
- §28.14's fan-out sentence read "a purely-local collection (a purely local collection, …)".
- Rationale §10's #5491 paragraph had been placed between the v0.318 and v0.319 paragraphs, where the v0.319 paragraph's "the cost … stated above" pointed at it. It now follows the v0.320 paragraphs.
- Four rationale sentences narrated a superseded state ("no longer take", "resolved … and rendered", "restores", "already read"), and now state the rule conditionally or in the present.

Proposal [0135](proposals/0135-value-receiver-by-copy-when-source-writable.md) ([#5496](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5496), the owner's accepted direction that a value receiver is passed by copy whenever its source may be written) is in the folder. It has been critiqued (round 1: 6 blocking and 10 non-blocking findings). Its move-only half, which the direction leaves open, was settled by the owner-delegated choice of *F* (admit the call in place and close the hazard where a move-only payload is bound), recorded in the proposal's §13; it graduates in the next train after that decision's critique.

- **§28.3 / §28.14 / §27.1.1 / §27.6 / §28.1 / Appendix C, rationale §4.2 — function values at set-erasing positions (graduation of proposal 0133; owner decision; [#5375](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5375)).** A generic body is checked once under §28.1's class-or-interface assumption, so `_v := x` with `x: T` is a parameter-sourced borrow admitted under the field-store bullet's residual. The caller's closure bullet tracks a function value by its source set, and a plain `T` parameter does not carry one. With neither side rejecting, `new Holder<() -> int>(f)` stored a closure over a scope-bound local in a field whose read "carries the empty set". `Object` (`k.Keep(f)` over `Keep(o: Object)`) and a function-typed parameter whose return slot is a bare `T` (`constructor(mk: () -> T)`) erased the set the same way.
  - The closure bullet defines a **set-erasing position**: a position declared `Object`, or a parameter, return slot, `ref`/`out` location, record component, choice payload or inline-array slot declared at a bare type parameter that the instantiation substitutes with a function type. A function value reaches one by implicit conversion, at an argument, an initializer, an assignment, a `return` (a lambda's included), a pattern binding, a collection-literal element or a `with` assignment. It also reaches one through every invocation of an argument bound to a function-typed parameter whose return slot, reached through return slots only, is such a type parameter.
  - At a set-erasing position a function value with a non-empty source set is rejected and a capture-free one is admitted. The receiver of a member `Object` declares (`f.ToString()`, an interpolation hole) is not such a position. A `scoped` parameter of function type is not one either, but a `scoped` parameter declared `Object` is. The check is the caller's, over the callee's declared signature, and the generic body is not re-checked.
  - A function value is not returned from an iterator by `yield return` while its set is non-empty, as for a `return`. An iterator's element type announces no set either.
  - §27.1.1: neither variance rule relates a function-typed slot to an `Object` slot. A function-typed target parameter slot is not contravariant to a value's `Object` slot, and a function-typed value return slot is not covariant to a target's `Object`.
  - Two companion rules close the routes with no conversion at a caller. §28.14's *method-reference formation bar* also rejects a function-typed slot bound to a set-erasing callee parameter, capture-free uses included (`var add := xs.Add;` at `xs: Array<() -> int>`; `var keep: (() -> int) -> () := k.Keep;`), with a lambda as the remedy. A member with a type parameter in a parameter slot of a parameter slot (`Fill(reg: ((T) -> ()) -> ())`) is inadmissible at a function-type substitution of it, beside the `Task`-family exclusion.
  - Row 5's runtime-managed cell states that the result is capture-free at a function-type substitution. The #5377 record-component sentence and the #5486 payload/slot sentence are re-pointed: a component, payload or element declared at a type parameter is a set-erasing position at a function-type substitution. §28.1 clause 3, §28.14's caller-side sentence and extension-method note, and §27.6 cross-reference the rule. Appendix C gains three rows here (set-erasing positions, the widened formation bar, the nested-slot exclusion) and one under #5499.
  - Costs, with remedies:
    - `Console.Write`/`WriteLine(Object)`, `StringBuilder.Append(Object)` and `Equals(Object?)` reject a capture-bearing argument. Use `f = g` to compare, and print a description.
    - `EventSource<T>.Raise` at a function-type payload rejects one. Raise data instead.
    - A selector `Pick<T>(a: T, b: T): T` rejects one. Use `(if c then f else g)`.
    - A received callback is not forwarded to a generic or `Object`-typed utility.
    - `Contains`/`IndexOf`/`Remove` at a function-typed element would find nothing anyway.
  - The owner's answers: no `Raise` allowlist (Q1); the `Object` stdlib sinks stay rejections (Q2); `scoped x: T` stays unwritable and is not the remedy (Q3); row 5's result is capture-free (Q4); one train under the composition gate (Q5); the simple nested-slot rule (Q6).

  **Declined** (owner-accepted with the proposal):
  - an instantiation exclusion keyed on `T`-typed fields (Option 2a);
  - a declaration-site store rejection in generic bodies (Option 3);
  - a K4.3 trust residual for function values (Option 4, on proposal 0126 §2's record);
  - a per-member `Raise` exemption;
  - `ToString`-only stdlib overloads at function types;
  - `scoped x: T` as the remedy;
  - row 5 announcing its arguments' union;
  - lambda-literal slot marking in place of the nested-slot exclusion.

  **Deferred:** a body-keyed exclusion (Option 2b), recorded as a second dependent of proposal 0132's storage fact on the #5374 row; and exempting the return-slot arm where the member's own return is mint-announcing (lazy selectors). Eight `rejected` rows and one `deferred` row, and the *Unbounded retention tier* row gains the `Pick<T>` instance.

  Kernel: derivation (K2.3 + K2.4; the companions K2.4, and K1.6 + K2.4). Body-locality: local, with one carve-out (the nested-slot exclusion, §3.6 rule 2's per-instantiation admissibility). The code-generation reference's closure line, call-bounded line and §7.2 carry the rule. Proposal 0133 is `graduated-v0.320` with a §10 graduation note.

  **Compiler (tracked):** nothing implements the rule. `callBoundedParams_` is seeded with plain function-typed formals only (`Ownership.cpp:480`, `:1740`). The generic body's store is admitted, and the caller side of a bare-`T` or `Object` parameter is unchecked. The formation bar's existing site (`ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp:21516–21559`) checks register positions only.
- **§28.14 / §28.3 / §31.2 (exception arms) / §15.1, rationale §4.2 — no function value in a local collection; frames keep the exemption (owner decision; [#5499](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5499), with [#5486](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5486)'s local half).** §28.14's call-bounded default let a received callback live in "a purely local collection". The closure bullet gives a function value read from any collection the empty set, so `var xs: Array<() -> int> := []; xs.Add(f); _field := xs[0];` stored a call-bounded `f` in a field. `var fs: [1]() -> int := [cb]; _f := fs[0];` did the same through a local inline array.
  - A call-bounded callback is not stored in any collection, a local one included.
  - A deferred-activation frame carrying the callback, or a task minted by invoking it, may still be held in a *purely local* collection: one that is not a parameter, a borrow or a field, nor reached through one. The fan-out idiom `pending.Add(cb()); await Task.WhenAll(pending);` is unchanged.
  - Every slot of a function-typed inline array is a field under the closure bullet, a local array's included (§15.1, §28.3, Appendix C).
  - The exception-arm paragraph's "a collection local to the arm is an arm-local binding" is withdrawn for closures, on the same ground (fold-in).

  **Declined:** tracking a local collection or local inline array as a carrier of its elements' source sets. Its value or reference copies into returns, fields, components, plain arguments and `Object`, none of which announces a set. One `rejected` row. Kernel: derivation (K2.4). Body-locality: local.

  **Compiler (tracked):** `exprReachableBeyondCall` (`Ownership_Checks.cpp:22255`) treats a local root as purely local for every value. `checkRefOutLambdaCaptureOnStore` (`:6430`) has no `IndexExpr` destination into a local inline array.
- **§21.1 / §23.3 / Appendix B / Appendix C.5, rationale §8.1 — a setter's implicit `value` is a parameter under the local-name rules (owner decision; [#5484](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5484)).** v0.314 and v0.316 kept the implicit `value` outside §21.1's *Local names*, because Appendix B said it "may be shadowed inside the setter body". The owner retired that permission, and the set parked at v0.317 lands with its pins retargeted to v0.320.
  - A declaration in a setter body may not take the name `value` while the implicit parameter is in scope. That covers a body-top local, or a nested local, loop variable, arm binding, binding-atom clause, or lambda parameter or slot, in a property's setter or an indexer's.
  - Appendix B says the name is not a true keyword in that role: it is a parameter of the setter, and §21.1's *Local names* applies to it. §23.3 and C.5 say the same, and §23.3 states the `set(x)` spelling, which Appendix A's `SetterParamSpec` already admits.
  - The remedy is a fresh local name, or `set(v)` / `set(owned v)`, which renames the parameter and frees `value` in that setter.

  **Declined:** keeping the exemption at body top and nested, which leaves one parameter outside both rules in the position where an owned obligation most often arrives; and keeping it at body top only, which is the same-scope rebinding v0.314 declines, applied to one parameter. One `rejected` row. Rationale §8.1 gains the paragraph, and its v0.316 sentence points to it. The code-generation reference's setter row names `set(x)` and gains a WRONG line. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local.

  **Compiler (tracked):** sema still exempts a property setter's implicit `value` (`setterImplicitValueExempt_`, `ExprTypecheck.cpp:18132`).
- **Stdlib §2.3, rationale §15.x — `Convert.ToString(value: float)` (owner decision; [#5500](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5500)).** With five one-argument overloads, `Convert.ToString(0.1f)` resolved to `ToString(double)` (§22.6, `float → double` being its one applicable conversion). It rendered `"0.10000000149011612"` where `0.1f.ToString()` is `"0.1"`, silently breaking §2.3's own equation (v0.317, [#5490](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5490)).
  - §2.3 declares `ToString(value: float)`, so the call is an exact match, `Convert.ToString(0.1f)` is `"0.1"`, and the paragraph's widening example is gone.
  - A `char`, `sbyte`, `byte`, `short`, `ushort`, `uint` or `ulong` argument is still a §22.6 ambiguity. `char` stays an error by the owner's direction.

  **Declined:** keeping the five overloads, and the rest of .NET's set. `char` and the narrow integers share `float`'s arrival ground but are declined on cost: each call is a compile error today, not a wrong string, and its remedy is one call. One `rejected` row. The code-generation reference's `Convert` block lists `float`. Kernel: no contact.

- **§14.2 register / stdlib §4 / Appendix C.1, rationale §10 — the standard library's equality search is rejected at the call where the element type has no equality (owner decision; [#5491](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5491)).** The equality search compares an argument with stored elements by `Equals` on an unconstrained element type:
  - `ICollection<T>.Contains`/`Remove(item)` and their `Array<T>` and `LinkedList<T>` implementations;
  - `Stack<T>.Contains` and `Queue<T>.Contains`;
  - `Array<T>.IndexOf`/`LastIndexOf`;
  - `LinkedList<T>.Find`;
  - the span family's `IndexOf`, `Contains` and `SequenceEqual`.

  At a record or choice with no equality the comparison had nothing to reach, and v0.318 had kept standard-library types out of the interior-use rule.
  - A call is admitted only where the element type, nullability stripped, has a member for §9.2's first kind (`Equals` with an argument of that type). Elsewhere it is a compile error at the call, `x in xs` included. The collection type stays well-formed: `Array<R>` is usable, and only its search is refused.
  - In a generic body, a call at an element type involving a type parameter is that body's own comparison, checked at its instantiations as a written `Equals` is. A user `Bag<T>` delegating to `items.Contains(x)` is rejected at `R` as one writing `Equals` is.
  - The members are conditionally admitted. §14.2's register gains a fourth row and a disposition bullet: the row lapses if a member-level condition is admitted, and the bullet states which signature remedies are closed and why. Stdlib §4 gains the paragraph listing the members (anchor `sec-collection-equality-search`), and the §4.4 register comment and both spans' *Search and equality* paragraphs point to it. Appendix C.1's equality bullet gains the clause. The code-generation reference's `Array<T>` block and *Generics* line state the rule. Signatures are unchanged.
  - The family goes past the owner's named list by `LinkedList<T>.Find` and the span `SequenceEqual`, which compare the same way.
  - Remedy: declare equality on the element type (making it `hashable`), or test a key with a predicate (`Any`) or a loop.

  **Declined:** a `hashable` constraint on the members. A constrained block is never consulted for a name the receiver declares (§26.5 rule 1) and cannot carry `ICollection<T>`'s members (§26.3). A member-level `where` is Appendix C.1's declined form. Either would also demand a `GetHashCode` a linear search never calls. Comparing by identity is declined too, as the box identity §9.2 declines. One `rejected` row. The stated cost: a call through `ICollection<R>` is refused even where the implementing class is a user's whose `Contains` does not compare by `Equals`. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local at a concrete element type, and a carve-out (generic instantiation) for the generic-body reading.

- **§9.8 / §12.2, rationale §5.22 — the hand-written serialization edges stay closed (owner decisions; [#5497](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5497), [#5505](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5505), [#5506](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5506)).** No normative text changes.
  - A `serialized skip` or `serialized optional` component's type must be defaultable whatever directions the class declares (#5497). A `Deserialize`-only reading is the direction-dependent eligibility §9.8 declines for a record's collection components and v0.316 declines for a base. The nullable form is the remedy.
  - A derived class's hand-written `Serialize`/`Deserialize` over a base's synthesized member stays a §12.2 hiding declaration (#5505, declined). Admitting it would admit the static-type-selected shadow the member-hiding record declines, and its `base.Serialize(s)` exemption would relax §9.8's run-time type check. The design also left unstated the identity tag a `base.Serialize(s)` of `this` writes, and it has no read counterpart. A hierarchy that needs a form per class hand-writes the base's `Serialize` as `virtual`.
  - A derived class's recognized static `Deserialize` over a base's hand-written one stays rejected (#5506): a static has no `override` escape, and the hierarchy deserializes through one factory. **Deferred**, to be revisited with the `IDeserializable.Deserialize` static-interface promotion ([#1507](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/1507)), under which each class's factory would be its own conformance witness.
