### v0.326 changelog (v0.325 → v0.326)

**Proposal 0136's stage 4, and rulings on v0.325's five bare-type-parameter follow-ups.** This revision lands proposal [0136](proposals/0136-simplification-batch-2026-10.md) §5.4, the re-trace of all seven guides against the current text, and rules on the questions and defects v0.325 filed against §28.3's bare-type-parameter rule, §9.7 and `GetOrAdd`. Six lanes:
- `g1`: Guide 01 (Memory and Ownership).
- `g2`: Guides 02 (Errors and Nullability) and 03 (Modeling Data).
- `g3`: Guide 04 (Concurrency).
- `g4`: Guide 05 (Collections and Iteration).
- `g5`: Guides 06 (Contracts and Purity) and 07 (Style).
- `qd`: [#5616](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5616) (an `owned T` result at a borrow-bearing value substitution, and its lambda), [#5617](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5617) (a constructor call's receiver in the `ref`/`out` count), [#5618](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5618) (a type-parameter-typed argument read per substitution), [#5619](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5619) (`GetOrAdd`'s key and factory result) and [#5620](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5620) (a `where T: value` member at a borrow-bearing substitution).

Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique, and `qd` a second critique of the rule its first critic added: 5 blocking and 42 non-blocking findings, all resolved or recorded (`g1` 1 and 5, `g2` 1 and 5, `g3` 0 and 7, `g4` 0 and 5, `g5` 1 and 4, `qd` 2 and 16). The 124 edits (`g1` 21, `g2` 17, `g3` 23, `g4` 29, `g5` 13, `qd` 21) were applied as one sequence, and a composition check added 17: 11 in the documents (3 spec, 4 code-generation reference, 2 stdlib, 1 rationale, 1 guide), 6 in the proposals folder and the decline index.

**Proposal 0136's stage 4 (§5.4) lands here**, and with it every presentation stage: each guide is re-traced and its pin moves to v0.326. S2-4 still waits on [#5526](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5526), and S2-16 on its name ([#5603](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5603)). The proposal's status line and README row record stage 4 as landed.

The critics' blocking findings were these:
- `g1`: §3's new remedy said a plain return hands out "only" a receiver borrow. That contradicts the guide's own §4 (`Math.Max` is a borrow of its arguments) and §6 (a lazy pipeline over the method's inputs). It is scoped to a method whose return type is a plain class type like `View`.
- `g2`: one claimed defect rested on a false absence. Stdlib §1 names "the §7.10 conflation caveat: §4.8, §4.17, §5", so Guide 02's "(the conflation caveat, stdlib §1/§4.8)" is right and the edit was dropped.
- `g5`: Guide 06 §1's new list of non-defaultable sites said "an `R`-typed field with no initializer". §9.9 rejects only a field that neither carries an initializer nor is assigned in every constructor; the text now says so.
- `qd`:
  - #5616 did not answer the issue's own lambda question. `(Item) -> owned T` at `T = Pair` *is* `(Item) -> Pair` (§27.1), so a lambda admitted at the generic slot reaches a non-generic holder of the concrete type, and row 7 had no function-value cell. Rejecting `Gen<Pair>` alone left the route open. The rule is completed in *Concrete-slot function bodies* (below).
  - The first draft parked #5618 and #5620's reading (i) as needing the owner. Under the owner's 2026-10-08 delegation ("Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues"), both are decided: declined, each with a reopening bar. Neither needs a design.

**Three outcomes the owner should see.**
- **A new rule for lambdas at borrow-bearing return slots.** `qd`'s first critic added it to close #5616, and a second critic attacked it; it stands. A lambda whose return type at the check site is a borrow-bearing record or inline array, or a choice that holds borrows, may return capture-, plain-parameter- or static-storage-sourced carried borrows, never a borrow of its own scope-bound local, `owned` parameter or temporary. Invoking such a function value carries row 4's union. This makes `static method Apply(f: () -> CancellationToken): CancellationToken => f();` a compile error; the bare spelling `Apply<T>(f: () -> T): T` is the remedy. Measured reach: zero sites.
- **#5618 and #5620's reading (i) are declined under the owner's delegation.** `Map<int, Item>` stays rejected (the remedy is `MapI<B>(a: int, …)`), and `Id<T>(a: T): T where T: value => a` stays rejected at `Id<Pair>` (the remedy is the unconstrained declaration). Neither has a measured site.
- **§9.7's per-instantiation reading is ruled for two returns only.** The same ground reaches a `Box<T>` return and a bare-`T` store into an `owned _last: T` field (`Keep<Pair>(new Pair(x))`), which no text decides. Filed as [#5629](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5629), with the recommendation that every §9.7 bullet be read per instantiation.

A composition check over the union then fixed seven seams:
- *Concrete-slot function bodies* said the admission is vacuous at every value check-site type, beside v0.325's callee clause 1 (not vacuous at a borrow-bearing substitution) and `qd`'s new borrow-bearing sentence. The vacuity now covers the value types that carry no borrow.
- §30.2 said a bare `var x := await t;` with a class result "is rejected", while §30.5 admits it under Pattern B, under Pattern A's may-flow list and through the scoped await-bind. §30.2 now defers to §30.5's patterns (`g3`'s critic, Q1; below).
- The code-generation reference's callee-side row for an `owned T` or `where T: value` return at a borrow-bearing substitution listed two of §9.7's three forms; it now names static storage through a static property getter. Its lambda clause named "a record or choice with a class component", and now names inline arrays and interface components.
- The code-generation reference's *Borrow-bearing records* paragraph said such a value "may be **returned** only when every borrow it carries is **receiver-sourced**", against the new lambda admission. It now says "returned from a member". Its caller-side row 1 now says what an `owned T` result is at a value `T`, pointing to row 7.
- Guide 05 called `GetOrAdd` "a read path" only. It now says the key and the factory's result are stores, checked at every call (spec §28.11, #5619).
- §28.11's borrowing-family list omitted `SortedDictionary<K, V>` and `SortedSet<T>`, which stdlib §4 and the code-generation reference's §4.5 name (`g4`'s observation). The list now names them.
- The decline index's v0.325 `deferred` row for #5606 sat in the `rejected` group, though the v0.325 size line counted it as `deferred`. It is moved to its group, and the size line is recomputed.

- **Guides 01–07 — re-traced against v0.326 (guide-only; [proposal 0136 §5.4](proposals/0136-simplification-batch-2026-10.md)).** Every claim, quoted diagnostic, stdlib member and fence was traced against the spec, the stdlib and the code-generation reference. No fence taught a rejected form, and no fence's verdict moves. 35 defects were fixed, in guide prose and two fences (Guide 01's `Timer`, Guide 07's test fence), and the history narration came out: revision pins in prose and in fence comments, "used to", "since v0.NNN", "named `Take` through v0.258". Each pin moves to v0.326.
  - **Guide 01** (pin v0.291; 10 defects). §3's remedy for a borrow-returning method, scoped to a plain-class return (announcement table row 4). §9's `Timer` narrowed a mutable `scoped` field; it now calls `_onTick?()` (§7.4, §7.6, §28.14). §9's capture-verification bound names every unverifiable form, not only a reassigned local (§28.14 bound 3). The opening called a use-after-free "rejected outright"; it is caught in layers, a straight-line use after disposal being a warning (§28.2). Checked disposal is the default build (§28.2). Also: `Math.Max` at a class or interface type argument, `owned` fields at a bare type parameter, the frame-disposed `owned`-parameter warning at a non-trivial-dispose type (§28.9), the `Task`-family discard row and `ScopeGuard`'s `scoped` constructor parameter. 0136 §5.4: §2's four-spellings table and its 437-word trivial-dispose paragraph become pointers (spec §28.3 *Choosing a disposal form*, §28.9; the code-generation reference's §4.1, §4.2 and §4.5), keeping two sentences and the `StringBuilder` example.
  - **Guide 02** (pin v0.291; 3 defects). Narrowing covers non-`ref` parameters and never a `ref` parameter (§7.4). Adding an outcome to a result choice flags an expression-position `case` with a warning, while a statement-position `case` falls through silently (§19.6). `KeyNotFoundException` lives in an auto-imported module (§31.4).
  - **Guide 03** (pin v0.289; 2 defects). Two ways to select over a shape, not three. An `R`-typed local of a constructor-only record is governed by definite assignment, not rejected (§9.9, §7.9).
  - **Guide 04** (pin v0.291; 5 defects). A `closed` class whose module-closed hierarchy is transfer-closed is sendable (§30.14 rule 1). Read-guard reader purity is a data race no conformance mode detects, and both halves of §30.12's obligation are named. A fault re-raises at every await of a `Task<T>` but only the first of an `OwningTask<T>` (§30.4). The scoped await-bind carries the guide's implementation-status note ([#3048](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3048)). 0136 §5.4: §3's Pattern A/B table becomes a pointer to spec §30.5 and the code-generation reference's §4.3 *Awaiting a task* table.
  - **Guide 05** (pin v0.291; 8 defects). `OwningArray<T>` is stdlib §4.5, and "§5's `ToArray()`" names stdlib §5. A drained loop variable of trivial-dispose type draws no must-use warning (§28.9). The mutation-during-iteration warning fires only on the loop's own source binding (§29.12). §6's warning needs a directly-called same-unit iterator, and its silent list adds the iteration variable (§29.11). A span may sit in neither a class's instance fields nor any static field (§9.7). Re-exposing an owning field fails only at a mint-announcing return (§28.3 *Calls mint* clause 6). 0136 §5.4: §1's two-families table and §2's *What the `for` variable is* table become pointers to the code-generation reference's §4.5.
  - **Guide 06** (pin v0.290; 3 defects). §1's non-defaultable sites in §9.9's terms, with the local carve-out. The `Range` purity citation adds §17.5. §9's "rows 1, 4, 5 and 7" no longer matched Guide 02 §7. 0136 §5.4: §9's failure-signal rows become a pointer to Guide 02 §7.
  - **Guide 07** (pin v0.295; 4 defects). §2's test fence declared a method at module level, which `TopDecl` does not admit, and omitted the import a dotted module name needs (§2.1, Appendix A.2); it is now a static test class with the import. The tour measurements are corrected, a §28.3 paraphrase is no longer printed as a quotation, and §6 names the added `Count` property. 0136 §5.4: §1's three-tier naming sentence becomes a pointer to stdlib §1.

  Composition: Guide 05 states #5619's `GetOrAdd` store (above). No guide teaches a form #5616, #5619, #5620 or the lambda rule rejects: no guide example instantiates an `owned T` or `where T: value` member at a borrow-bearing type, or declares a function type returning one.
- **§30.2 — an await whose result is a class (clarification; `g3`'s critic, Q1).** §30.2 said that when the task's result type is a class "the bare assignment shown here is rejected". §30.5 admits `var x := await t;` there: under Pattern B ("A bare `var x := await someTask;` compiles"), as Pattern A's `var` binding, and through the scoped await-bind for a fresh producer. §30.5 is the specific rule, and it governs. §30.2 now says that §30.5's patterns govern which operands an await accepts and where its result may flow. The same pre-v0.90 wording was removed from Appendix C.6 earlier; §30.2 was missed. Verdict impact: none.
- **Stdlib §2.21, rationale §5.31 — editorial.** `ScopeGuard`'s "explicit constructor, not primary" bullet gave the stale ground that §22.10 rejects every `scoped` primary-constructor parameter. Since v0.307, §22.10 rejects only a function-typed one, which `action` is, so the conclusion stands on the current ground. The freeze bullet wrote the rejected transfer-out as `return move conn;`, itself a redundant-marker error under an `owned` return; it reads `return conn;`. The rationale's back-reference citation pointed at Guide 01 §2; the back-reference is taught in §5.
- **§9.7 return bullet, §28.1 clause 3, §28.3 announcement-table row 1, the code-generation reference — an `owned T` result at a borrow-bearing value substitution (ruling; [#5616](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5616)).** Row 1 said that at value substitutions of a bare-type-parameter `owned` return the marker is erased and the result is a plain value, and no rule bounded the borrows that value carries: `owned` parameters are never bare-`T` sources, and row 1 is outside *Bare-type-parameter returns*. Over `record Pair(Item: Item)`, `static method Pass<T>(owned a: T): owned T => a;` called as `return Pass<Pair>(new Pair(x));` handed back a borrow of a scope-bound `x`.
  - **The fix.** At such a substitution the body's returns are held to §9.7's return bullet, a requirement of the body's use of `T` checked at that instantiation (§3.6 rule 2), and a caller reads the result's carried borrows as §9.7's form 1 states: sourced at the receiver expression, none at a static member. `Pass<Pair>` is rejected (its return carries a borrow of an `owned` parameter), and so is `Gen<T>(f: (Item) -> owned T): owned T` returning `f(t)` over its own local, at `Gen<Pair>`. Fresh producers whose results carry no borrow stay admitted, as §28.1 clause 4 requires.
  - **Precedent.** §9.7's own reading of a value return's carried borrows. v0.325's #5607 composition already said that §9.7's plain-parameter rejection does not reach a return *Bare-type-parameter returns* classifies; row 1 is not such a return.

  **Declined:** a caller-side union over the receiver and the `owned` and plain arguments, which leaves `Gen<Pair>` open and needs a new callee-side source list for `owned` returns; and making the member inadmissible at such a substitution, which rejects the fresh producers §28.1 clause 4 keeps. Two `rejected` rows. Kernel: derivation (K2.4, via §9.7). Body-locality: carve-out (generic instantiation, §3.6 rule 2). **Compiler (tracked, [#5630](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5630)):** §9.7's return check (`checkRecordBorrowEscapesOnReturn`, `src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:5993`) gates on the static type of the returned expression, a type parameter in a generic body, and no per-instantiation re-run was located; `Pass<Pair>` is very likely admitted (HYPOTHESIS, probes on the tracker).
- **§28.3 *Concrete-slot function bodies*, the announcement table's rows 1, 7 and 8, stdlib §4.14, the code-generation reference — a lambda at a borrow-bearing return slot, and its invocation (ruling; [#5616](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5616), the issue's lambda question).** Rejecting `Gen<Pair>` does not close the lambda: `(Item) -> owned T` at `T = Pair` is `(Item) -> Pair` (§27.1), so the same function value is invoked by any generic body that does not return the result and by non-generic code holding a concrete `(Item) -> Pair`, where row 7 had no function-value cell.
  - **The rule.** A lambda whose return type at the check site, nullability stripped, is a borrow-bearing record or inline array, or a choice that holds borrows (a concrete such type, or an `owned` or `where T: value` bare-type-parameter slot at such a substitution), may return a value carrying capture-sourced, plain-parameter-sourced or static-storage borrows, never a borrow of its own scope-bound local, `using var` or `owned` parameter, or of a temporary. The check site is the target slot or, with no target, the lambda's ascribed or inferred return type. Invoking a function value of such a type yields a value carrying row 4's union: the function value's source set and what every plain argument contributes.
  - **Consequences.** `var g: (Item) -> Pair := lambda(i) => new Pair(i);` is admitted, and `return g(x);` past a scope-bound `x` is rejected. A named member returning the invocation of its own plain function-typed parameter at such a type is held to §9.7's member forms: `static method Apply(f: () -> CancellationToken): CancellationToken => f();` is rejected, and the bare spelling `Apply<T>(f: () -> T): T` is admitted. Rows 7 and 8 gain their function-value cells, row 1's cell and §28.1 clause 3 point at the rule, and stdlib §4.14 says that `OwningBuffer<T>`'s value-tier `init` results carry `init`'s captures.
  - **Why lambdas and members differ.** A member call (row 7) counts no arguments, so §9.7 rejects a plain-parameter-sourced return; a function-value invocation counts the function value and every plain argument, so a lambda may return what the invocation re-establishes. Row 4 draws the same line for class returns, and v0.317's [#5485](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5485) decline records the posture.

  **Declined:** holding such a lambda to §9.7's member forms. A bound method reference to an instance member already hands back receiver borrows, so the invocation must count the function value anyway, and the member forms would reject `lambda(i) => new Pair(i)` and every capture-carrying `lambda() => new Pair(x)`. One `rejected` row. The decline index's row 150 (v0.324, declining a callee-side rejection of a bare-`T` member's `return f()`) is not contradicted: its ground is that every caller of a bare-`T` member re-establishes the result, and row 1 and row 7 announce no source set. Kernel: derivation (K2.4; K2.2's union). Body-locality: local. **Compiler (probe first, [#5632](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5632)):** unprobed; the invocation half shares #5485's and [#5609](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5609)'s gate (`src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:4756`, keyed on `calleeMethodDecl`).
- **§9.7 return bullet, §28.3 *Bare-type-parameter returns* clause 3, §26.5.1's example — a `where T: value` member at a borrow-bearing substitution (clarification, gated as a ruling; [#5620](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5620)).** A bare-type-parameter return under `where T: value` is row 7's on both sides, so §9.7's return bullet governs it. The bullet is read at each instantiation substituting a borrow-bearing type (§3.6 rule 2: it turns on a derived type property), not at the declaration under the weakest assumption, which would reject §26.5.1's `First` example at every substitution, `int` included. `static method Id<T>(a: T): T where T: value => a;` is admitted at the declaration and at `int`, and rejected at `Id<Pair>`. §26.5.1's `IEnumerable<T> where T: value` `First` is rejected at a borrow-bearing `T`, the copy's borrows being sourced, as the iteration variable is, at the loop's implicit enumerator; its comment says so.

  **Declined:** the declaration reading; and bringing `where T: value` members under *Bare-type-parameter returns* at borrow-bearing substitutions, so that `Id<Pair>` is admitted with a caller union (the issue's reading (i)). Done at borrow-bearing substitutions only, that keys the member's classification on a derived property of the substitution, the post-substitution keying rationale §5.7 declines; done at every substitution, it sends sourceless `where T: value` factories to row 6, where `owned` is itself rejected under `where T: value` (§28.1 clause 5). The unconstrained declaration is the remedy. Two `rejected` rows; reading (i) decided under the owner's 2026-10-08 delegation. Kernel: derivation (K2.4). Body-locality: carve-out (generic instantiation). **Compiler:** as #5616 ([#5630](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5630)).
- **§28.3 *A `ref` or plain `out` location outlives the call* — a constructor call's receiver (clarification, gated as a ruling; [#5617](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5617)).** The count names "the receiver" without saying which object a constructor call's is. It is the object or value constructed, read as the binding or field its result initializes, or, for an unbound result, as an unbound owned temporary bounded to the full expression; in a `this(...)` or `base(...)` chain it is `this`. The callee side already admits a receiver-sourced store into the location, and inside a constructor the receiver is the object under construction, so this is the only reading under which `new Holder(out o)` with `o := _r` is sound. Not adopted: a constructor call with no receiver in the count, which admits `Use(new Holder(out o)); o.Show();` after the temporary is disposed. Kernel: derivation (K2.3 + K2.4), unchanged. Body-locality: local. Verdict impact: none under the sound reading. **Compiler:** the location's caller-side union is not implemented ([#5145](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5145), which gains this probe).
- **§28.3 — a type-parameter-typed argument at a bare-type-parameter function-value invocation, read per substitution (ruling: declined; [#5618](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5618)).** The text stands: a type-parameter-typed argument counts under the weakest assumption its constraints establish (*The sources an argument contributes* item 4), so `Map<A, B>(a: A, f: (A) -> B): B => f(a)` stays rejected at every class `B`, `Map<int, Item>` included. **Declined:** reading the argument's contribution at its own substitution. It is sound but only a precision gain, at zero measured sites, and it would make the callee check run per pair of substitutions rather than per category of the returned parameter, so that a public generic's requirement summary (§2.8.6) turns on pairs. `MapI<B>(a: int, f: (int) -> B): B` is admitted at every `B`. One `rejected` row, with a reopening bar; decided under the owner's 2026-10-08 delegation. No normative text changes.
- **§28.11, stdlib §4.8–§4.9, the code-generation reference — `GetOrAdd` is a store (ruling; [#5619](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5619)).** `Dictionary<K, V>.GetOrAdd(key, factory: (K) -> V): V` invokes its factory on `key` and stores both, but the slot policy's store row named `Add`, `Insert` and the indexer-set only, and the bare-`V` caller count does not reach `key`. At `Dictionary<Item, Item>`, `d.GetOrAdd(k, lambda(kk) => kk)` left `d` holding, and returned, a borrow of `k` that no rule bounded `d` by.
  - **The fix.** `GetOrAdd` is a store at every call, whether or not the key is present: of `key`, and of the factory's result, whose sources are what invoking the factory on `key` carries (row 4's count: the factory's source set and `key`'s contribution). Each is checked against the dictionary under §28.11's store rule, or §9.7's copy rule at a borrow-bearing type. `OwningDictionary.GetOrAdd`'s `key` is stored as its `Add`'s is. The result keeps row 5's bound (the receiver and the factory), now sound up to the store rule's recorded residual, as an indexer read is.
  - **Over-rejection accepted.** Checking the key when it is present rejects `_d.GetOrAdd(localKey, f)` on a field dictionary; the indexer-set with the same key is rejected the same way, and the signature cannot say the key is present.

  **Declined:** counting `key` among the result's bare-`V` sources, which bounds only the returned borrow and leaves the dictionary holding a borrow of `key` past its scope (one `rejected` row). Kernel: derivation (K2.3, with K2.2's union). Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked, [#5631](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5631)):** the store sets at `src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:10642` and `:22274` do not list `GetOrAdd`.

Measured reach: zero sites; every generic `owned T` instantiation in `tests/` is at a class or at a record of value-typed fields.

  - **#5620.** At an instantiation substituting a borrow-bearing type for a `where T: value` returned parameter, a body whose return carries a parameter-, local- or enumerator-sourced borrow: `Id<T>(a: T): T where T: value => a` at `Id<Pair>`, and §26.5.1's `First` at `IEnumerable<Pair>`. Measured reach: zero sites.
  - **#5619.** A `GetOrAdd` call whose key, or whose factory result's sources (the factory's captures, or `key` returned through the factory), fail §28.11's store rule against the dictionary: `_d.GetOrAdd(k, f)` with a scope-bound class-typed `k` and a field-held `_d`; `d.GetOrAdd(1, lambda(i) => x)` past `x`'s scope where `d` outlives `x`; at a borrow-bearing `V`, a copy whose carried sources do not outlive `d`. Measured reach: zero sites; every `GetOrAdd` call in `tests/` and `docs/` keys on a `string` or `int`.

  *Newly accepted:* none.

### v0.327 changelog (v0.326 → v0.327)

**Every open spec decision, decided under the owner's delegation.** On 2026-10-08 the owner directed: "Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them." This revision acts on that direction for every issue that carried `needs-owner-decision`, and for the policy question and the defect filed beside them. Each decision is a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`). A decision that changes what compiles went through a proposal, which graduates here. The decisions:
- **Proposal [0138](proposals/0138-compiler-known-sendability.md)** (the sendability of the compiler-known classes): [#5613](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5613) (a library class admits a user subclass only where its text opens it), [#5614](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5614) (the copy-state ground: `StringBuilder`, `Random`, `Stopwatch` sendable), [#5578](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5578) (`OwningBuffer<T>` at a sendable value element), [#5615](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5615) (`Type` sendable as a shared reference), [#5605](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5605) (a class deriving from a library class is not sendable) and [#5604](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5604) (a retained comparer is recorded trust).
- **Proposal [0139](proposals/0139-mark-the-arm-meet.md)** (the arm-meet is marked too): [#5591](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5591).
- **Proposal [0140](proposals/0140-formation-bar-out-parameters.md)** (the formation bar exempts `out` parameters): [#5526](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5526), with proposal [0136](proposals/0136-simplification-batch-2026-10.md)'s S2-4, which waited on it.
- **Proposal [0141](proposals/0141-dispatched-generic-methods.md)** (dispatched generic methods): [#5509](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5509).
- **Proposal [0142](proposals/0142-static-readonly-static-initialization-only.md)** (a `static readonly` field is assigned only in static initialization): [#5577](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5577).
- **Rulings, no proposal:** [#4454](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4454) (the spec-ahead-of-impl policy, a process amendment), [#5592](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5592) (the asynchronous borrow-pin is admitted), [#5598](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5598) (an enum's or a choice's `Equals` is the own-typed one), [#5603](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5603) (the union is *a value type that holds borrows*; 0136's S2-16), [#5511](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5511) (no nullable inline array is formed by substitution) and [#5554](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5554) (an owning inline array destroyed with its holder is in the disposed state).
- **Ruled by reading, no text moves:** [#5612](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5612) (a lazy query passed as an `IEnumerable<T>` argument stays lazy; a compiler defect, relabelled).

With S2-4 and S2-16 landed, proposal 0136 graduates (v0.323–v0.327). Six lanes:
- `dP`: #4454 and #5612.
- `dU`: proposal 0139 (#5591) and #5592.
- `dE`: proposal 0142 (#5577), #5598 and #5603.
- `dS`: proposal 0138 (#5613, #5614, #5578, #5615, #5605, #5604).
- `dM`: proposal 0140 (#5526), 0136's S2-4 and 0136's graduation.
- `dI`: proposal 0141 (#5509), #5511 and #5554.

Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique: 15 blocking and 46 non-blocking findings, all resolved or recorded (`dP` 1 and 5, `dU` 2 and 8, `dE` 3 and 9, `dS` 2 and 11, `dM` 3 and 7, `dI` 4 and 6). The 162 edits (`dP` 6, `dU` 14, `dE` 43 — 16 of them re-anchored on v0.326's text —, `dS` 54, `dM` 26, `dI` 19) were applied as one sequence, and a composition check added 27: 17 in the documents (2 spec, 2 stdlib, 3 rationale, 1 code-generation reference, 9 guide), 10 in the proposals folder and the decline index.

The critics' blocking findings were these:
- `dP`: the policy's "a spec rule is never marked in spec prose" was false at landing. Spec §14.2's conditional-member register marks `DangerousPointer()` unimplemented on its face, as proposal 0116 §9 R5 requires. A spec text that names a stdlib member is now the stdlib tier.
- `dU`:

**Outcomes the owner should see.**

They pin the compiler's collapse of `([3]int)?` to `[3]int`, a type §15.1 never admitted. The implementing tracker rewrites each to `await Receive()`, which the file's `inline_array_await_receive_spec_30_15` already uses.
- **Two banked controls flip under #5577.** `ctor_type_qualified_static_readonly_assignment_accepted_spec_22_8` and `ctor_bare_static_readonly_assignment_accepted_spec_22_8` (`tests/sema/readonly_per_instance_3316_test.cpp`) assign a `static readonly` field in an instance constructor. They become rejections. No other test, document or corpus case writes the form.
- **#5598 rejects every `Object`-taking `Equals` on an enum or a choice**, `override` or plain: `Equals(o: Object?)` and `Equals(o: Object)` alike, at every choice classification. The issue asked about the `override` spelling only. The plain one is rejected too because it is not inert (above). Measured reach: zero.
- **The compiler-known classes are closed to inheritance.** Only `Encoding`, `Stream`, `TextReader`, `TextWriter` and the exception family (the built-in exceptions and the stdlib's producer-local ones) admit a user subclass. `class E: Mutex`, `: StringBuilder`, `: Array<int>` and `: FileStream` are compile errors, `sealed` written or not. A class deriving from an opened class is never sendable, so **no exception class is sendable**. Measured reach: zero.
- **`Type`, `StringBuilder`, `Random`, `Stopwatch` and `OwningBuffer<T>` at a sendable value element are sendable.** `Type` crosses as a shared reference, as `string` does. The other three cross by move on a new copy-state ground. So do `Array<Type>`, a record or a transfer-closed class with a `Type` field, and `Locked<OwningBuffer<double>>`. The compiler rejects all of them today.
- **A dispatched generic method's body carries no deferred requirement.** An implementation of `method Id<T>(a: T): T where T: value;` that returns `a` is rejected at the implementation, where v0.326's #5620 rule would otherwise wait for a borrow-bearing instantiation. The remedies are #5620's: the unconstrained declaration, or a fresh return. Measured reach: zero.
- **#5603 deviates from the owner-accepted name.** S2-16 accepted `borrow-carrying value`, which collides with four live wider-sense uses (33 spec occurrences). The union is named *a value type that holds borrows* instead, by widening the existing **holds-borrows** property.

- **Spec-change process §5 item 3, §7, §9 — the spec-ahead-of-impl policy (process; [#4454](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4454), ruled under the 2026-10-08 delegation).** The gap between the documents and the compiler is intended. A question is ruled while its context is loaded, and the rule corpus turns each ruling into a test that already exists when the implementation arrives. The backlog is inventory, not a landing condition: a revision never waits for its trackers to be owned or closed, and there is no ceiling or catch-up quota. It is drained in the roadmap's order, soundness first, with the compiler bug-fix phase before stdlib implementation (the owner's direction).
  - **Three legibility rules make it measurable.** Every tracker carries `spec-tracking`. A stdlib surface is told apart by its `⚠` marker (v0.323), and a spec rule by its tracker and its rule-corpus `fail` row, never by a marker in spec prose. A spec text that names a stdlib member, such as §14.2's register row for `DangerousPointer()`, is the stdlib tier. The Migration note names the probe where a delta is unmeasured.
  - §7's *Impl divergence is not a spec defect* gains its converse: a `spec-defect` label on an issue the text already decides is a labelling defect (#5612 below). §9's checklist names the label.
  - **Measured at v0.325:** 103 open `spec-tracking` issues (12 · 8 · 31 · 52 by month filed, July to October) against 6 closed; 12 open trackers titled as catch-up without the label; 219 rule-corpus `fail` rows against 1,966 `pass`.

No compile-time rule changes.
- **§29.11 item 3, stdlib §5 — a lazy query passed as an `IEnumerable<T>` argument (ruling by reading, no doc change; [#5612](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5612)).** The text decides it. The enumeration right transfers into the callee, the argument is a borrow of a frame that stays lazy (stdlib §5: every operator is lazy unless documented otherwise), and a re-enumeration reachable only at run time raises `InvalidOperationException`.
  - The compiler drains the pipeline into an `Array<T>` at the call site (`src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Assign.cpp:9010`, from the argument arms at `:15160` and `LlvmBackend_Calls2.cpp:13486`). That runs the pipeline before the callee is entered: its callbacks run even when the callee never enumerates, its exceptions surface outside the callee's `try`, and a `First()` pays for every element. It also leaves the runtime guard with no subject. The runtime has no re-enumeration guard for a lazy frame at all.
  - So the issue is a compiler defect, filed as a spec defect. `spec-defect` comes off and `spec-tracking`, `codegen` and `iterators` go on; the issue stays open as the tracker. `l5_0003` stays a banked divergence until the fix. [#4692](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/4692) reported the same divergence from the corpus side and is cross-linked.
- **§12.4, Appendix C.1, §31.4, stdlib §1, §3.2, §4.1, §7.1, §7.4, rationale §12.6 — a compiler-known class is closed to inheritance unless its text opens it (design change, [proposal 0138](proposals/0138-compiler-known-sendability.md) §3; [#5613](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5613)).** A compiler-known class is a class of the standard library, or `Exception` and the built-in exception types. It is a valid base class only where the text that declares it says user code may derive from it. Every other one is closed exactly as a `sealed` class is, `sealed` written or not, and a base-type reference to one in a user declaration is a compile error naming §12.4. `Object` is not reached by the rule, nor are the library's own derivations (`FileStream: Stream`, `Task<T>: Task`).

These are the abstract library classes, whose abstract members exist to be supplied, and the exceptions; a concrete class's inherited virtual members do not open it. §31.4 opens the exception family in words, and stdlib §4.1's "extend" now says extension blocks.
  - §12.4 says why. A sendability statement stands for every instance of its type only if no user subclass can hide origin-domain borrows behind a compiler-known static type. That is rationale §12.6's hole, which rule 1 closes for declared classes.

- **§30.14, stdlib §2.7, §3.1, §8.1, rationale §12.13 — the copy-state ground, and three statements on it (design change, [proposal 0138](proposals/0138-compiler-known-sendability.md) §4; [#5614](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5614); lifts v0.325's deferral, [#5606](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5606)).** The **sendable** form's grounds are now four:
  - internally synchronized and reached from several domains by purpose;
  - deeply immutable;
  - a channel endpoint;
  - a holder of copy state only: every member reads and writes that state by value and retains no borrow past its call, and no member exposes an address of its storage.

  `StringBuilder`, `Random` and `Stopwatch` are **sendable** on the fourth ground, and each statement records why its members meet it. `Append(value: Object)` keeps the text, not the object. `AppendFormat`'s `args` and `NextBytes`'s `buffer` are call-bounded. A moved `Random` continues its sequence, and a moved running `Stopwatch` keeps measuring (the clock, not the thread, is the source). v0.325's `deferred` row is annotated as taken and stays as the record.

Kernel: no contact. Its storage is part of the instance and crosses with it, as `Array<double>`'s does.

That is a `DangerousPointer()` result the origin domain keeps after moving the buffer. It is valid until the buffer is disposed, by whichever domain then holds it, and no borrow tracks it.
  - `Locked<OwningBuffer<double>>` becomes an admitted interior by §6.11's unchanged condition.

- **§28.14 *The method-reference formation bar*, §27.6, §28.3, Appendix C.3, rationale §4.2, the code-generation reference — the formation bar exempts `out` parameters, and a function-typed `ref`/`out` location's set after the call (design change, [proposal 0140](proposals/0140-formation-bar-out-parameters.md); [#5526](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5526)).** v0.320's widened bar rejected a formed reference whenever a function-typed slot bound to a set-erasing callee parameter, `out` slots included. So `var tg := d.TryGetValue;` at `d: Dictionary<string, () -> int>` was a compile error while the direct call, and the `g` it fills, were admitted.
  - **The fix.** The bar keys on the slots a caller's value reaches, plain and `ref`, and exempts an `out` parameter. `var put: (ref () -> int) -> () := b.Put;` over `Put<T>(ref x: T)` stays rejected. A call through the formed value passes an `out` parameter a location and no value. What the callee copies out is capture-free: every value of the type parameter's type the generic body can place there arrived through a set-erasing position, a holder, the return-slot arm or another `out`. *Set-erasing positions* states that ground, and that a `ref` argument's current value reaches a `ref` location so declared and is still checked there.
  - **The location's set after the call.** A function-typed `ref` or plain `out` location is a holder the callee may fill only capture-free, so the union of the call's borrows over-approximated it. On the call's normal return an `out` location carries the empty set and a `ref` location its prior set. On an exception exit an `out` recipient keeps its prior value and set (§22.3). `d.TryGetValue(k, out this._g)` is admitted. Class-typed and borrow-bearing locations keep the union and the check.

  **Declined** (three `rejected` rows): keeping the bar uniform over `out`; dropping `out` locations from the set-erasing definition instead (an `out o: Object` location is a real erasure site in a checked callee body); the union at a function-typed location. Kernel: derivation (K2.3 + K2.4). Body-locality: local. **Compiler:** the widened bar is unimplemented ([#5515](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5515)), and so is the location rule's call-site union ([#5145](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5145)). The compiler therefore already admits both newly admitted forms. Both trackers are annotated with the carves.

It has a numbered provenance list: lambda literal, method reference (a static one carries the empty set), plain function-typed parameter, invocation, a read from a field, collection, property or indexer (#5602's clause), and the traced local. It keeps one sink rule and the lambda-`return` clause, and its frame-residence sentence points to §28.14's *Call-bounded × deferred activation*.

  - Row 4's function-value cell reads "the function value's source set ∪ the sources every plain argument contributes".

- **§14.2 *Dispatched generic methods*, §3.6 rule 2, §14.6, Appendix C.1, rationale §10, the code-generation reference — dispatched generic methods (design change, [proposal 0141](proposals/0141-dispatched-generic-methods.md) option D; [#5509](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5509)).** v0.319 scoped #5504's chain to instantiations formed by substitution, and filed the one that dispatch forms. `i.Find<R>(…)` on an interface instantiates `IFinder.Find<R>` and reaches `F.Find<R>`, a body the call site need not see. Across modules that body need not be in the caller's compilation closure (§2.8.3), so §3.6 rule 2's "checked at each instantiation of the method, a call … among them" named a site that cannot read the body. A dispatched generic method is an interface method (instance or static), or a `virtual` or `abstract` method, that declares type parameters of its own, with every override or implementation of one, an inherited witness included. Two rules govern it:
  - **Requirements are decided at the body.** Every body is checked under its constraint set with no deferral. A requirement of its own parameter the set does not establish is a compile error at that body: an equality use, an `as` target at a unit substitution, an owning element, a wrapper or hash key carrying one. The remedy is a constraint on the **declaring** interface or base method, or for `as`, §17.4's `is` test. An inherited witness is checked at the conforming class.
  - **No move-only or inline-array substitution.** The method's type parameters admit no move-only value type and no inline array as a type argument. That is a compile error at the call, through any receiver type, and at the enclosing declaration's instantiations where the argument is or contains a type parameter in scope. So every reachable body reads its parameter as copyable and not an inline array, and copies, boxes, `case` bindings, `[N]T` and `T?` in it need no instantiation.

  §3.6 rule 2 names the case in one sentence, and §14.6's edge attribution now says it decides no requirement. **Declined** (three `rejected` rows): the call-site reading and its link-time variant (unenforceable across modules); a `copyable` constraint in place of the exclusion (explicit at the declaring interface, in a module the implementer may not own, for a program that does not exist, and no constraint would state the inline-array half); checking overrides at the body while leaving a `virtual` body per instantiation at its direct calls. The stated cost: a move-only value or an inline array cannot pass through a dispatched generic method's own type parameter (wrap it in a record or a class). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local; fact-discharged at an inherited witness; the chain is #5504's carve-out. **Compiler (tracked, [#5639](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5639) and [#5640](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5640)):** no interior-use check exists ([#5481](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5481)'s item). The `as` join for a method type parameter (`src/sema/TypeResolution.hpp:247`) fires only at a direct call. `where T: value` admits a move-only or inline-array argument at every generic method.
- **§15.1, §14.2 (the register), Appendix C.1, rationale §5.14, stdlib §1, §6.9, Guide 05 §5, the code-generation reference — no nullable inline array is formed by substitution (ruling; [#5511](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5511)).** v0.322 answered the nested half (#5555): `[N]T` at an inline-array `T` is rejected at the instantiation site. The nullable half stayed open. `T?` under `where T: value`, or the `T?` storage §7.10 recommends for an unconstrained `T`, forms `([3]int)?` at `T = [3]int`, which §15.1 admits for no written type.
  - **The rule holds wherever the form arises.** `T?` at a type parameter substituted by an inline array is a compile error at the instantiation site, through any chain of user declarations. That covers a field, local, parameter or result, a payload or element type, a type argument, and a local the body declares. So is a generic type alias reference whose expansion forms one.
  - **The standard library.** A standard-library declaration carries no requirement at its naming, so `Array<[3]float>` and `Channel<[3]int>` are well-formed, indexed, iterated and sent as any other. A member whose signature forms `T?` at its receiver's element or value type is a conditionally-admitted member where that type argument is an inline array, so §14.2's register gains the row. Its members are `FirstOrNull`, `LastOrNull`, `SingleOrNull`, `ElementAtOrNull`; `Stack<T>.TryPop`/`TryPeek`, `Queue<T>.TryDequeue`/`TryPeek`, `Channel<T>.TryReceive`; `LinkedList<T>.First`/`Last`; and `Dictionary`'s and `SortedDictionary`'s `GetOrNull`/`TryGetValue` at `V`. A call is a compile error naming the remedies: a count or index test, the non-nullable member, or a wrapping record.

  **Declined** (two `rejected` rows): admitting the formed type as a nullable value type no expression spells (it would have no rendering distinct from the element-nullable `[3]int?`, and §17.4's `as` rule rests on its absence); and reading a Try member's `T?` out as a non-nullable `T` assigned `default(T)` at an inline-array element (`[2]string` has no `default`, §17.11). The stated cost: a generic that follows §7.10's advice to store `T?` admits no inline-array argument, and `Channel<[3]int>` loses `TryReceive` (above). Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local; the chain is #5504's carve-out. **Compiler (probe first, then tracked, [#5641](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5641), extending [#5563](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5563)):** `applyBareParamSubst` (`src/sema/SubstArgs.cpp:66–70`) copies the inline-array `TypeRef` and sets `nullable = true` with no diagnostic. `isNullableValueTy` (`src/codegen/LlvmBackend_impl.hpp:5997`) does not list the inline-array kind, so the formed value lowers as the bare `[N x T]`. A class-typed slot's object is flag-backstopped (K4.1), but a boxed value in an interface-typed slot is runtime-managed and carries no flag, so the read reached a released box.
  - §9.4's disposed state is entered by a null store of an owning choice's location, or by the destruction of the holder of either move-only kind (§28.4 step 2's per-slot pass). Checked mode tests it on every read through an in-place `this` or a borrowing-match binding, an owning inline array's slot reads, iteration and compiler-provided operations included, as `DisposedAccessException`.
  - The state is the value's, not its contents': a released box has no flag, and the array's state is what the binding's read tests. A whole-value overwrite is not this case, since it stores a replacement, visible whole. §15.1.1 says it at the pass.

### v0.328 changelog (v0.327 → v0.328)

**The questions v0.326 and v0.327 surfaced, decided under the owner's delegation.** On 2026-10-08 the owner directed: "Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them." v0.327 acted on that direction for every issue that carried `needs-owner-decision`. This revision acts on it for the questions those two revisions' lanes surfaced and did not file, and for the three `spec-question` issues filed beside them. Each decision is a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`). A decision that changes what compiles went through a proposal, which graduates here. The decisions:
- **Proposal [0143](proposals/0143-move-only-field-move-disposed-state.md)** (a whole-value `move` of a move-only field leaves its storage in the disposed state): the v0.327 #5554 critique's filing.
- **Proposal [0144](proposals/0144-await-using-yield-key-object-and-interfaces.md)** (`Object` and every interface join §30.7's `yield return` key): raised by this revision's own ruling on the run-time `DisposeAsync`.
- **Proposal [0145](proposals/0145-taskscope-owned-by-its-await-using-binding.md)** (a `TaskScope` is owned by its `await using var` binding alone): the question 0144 filed.
- **Rulings, no proposal:**
  - [#5629](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5629) (§9.7's bullets are read per instantiation in a generic body);
  - a class field at a bare type parameter is a set-erasing position (the v0.327 `dM` critique);
  - a lambda body is outside the `readonly` assignment window (the v0.327 `dE` lane);
  - the `DisposeAsync` an `await using` awaits is the run-time object's (the v0.327 `dU` lane, under [#5592](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5592));
  - the synchronous fallback is read per level (0144's question);
  - `Type` carries the **immutable** and **self-distributing** facts (proposal 0138 §13);
  - [#5634](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5634) (a method reference over a conditionally-admitted member is rejected where it is formed).
- **Clarifications:** [#5635](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5635) (a dispatched generic method's requirement summary is its constraint set), with two §2.8.6 rows for a member's kind change; Guide 02 §7's typed-exception row.
- **Already landed, no edit:** the other five entries on the run's list. §30.2's await-of-a-class sentence, stdlib §2.21's two bullets and the rationale's Guide 01 citation, and the #5606 decline row's group landed in v0.326. The enum and choice `Equals(Object?)` question was #5598, and the Guide 04 `Type` edits landed with it, both in v0.327.

**Outcomes the owner should see.**
- **Two banked tests flip under #5629, through proposal 0141.** `codegen_5129/named_closure_local_virtual_callee_not_released_no_uaf` and `codegen_5216/lambda_literal_virtual_callee_not_released_no_uaf` override `virtual method Keep<U>(x: U)` with `F := x;` into `public F: Object?` and call at `U = () -> int`.

  - **The declined alternative:** widen 0141's exclusion to value types that hold borrows at every dispatched call. It is sound and has zero measured call sites, and it keeps both tests unchanged. It is declined because it reverses 0141's recorded choice, made a week earlier, and rejects read-only dispatched bodies at ordinary record arguments. Its `rejected` row's bar is a program neither bound serves, or an owner direction; it would then be a proposal amending 0141.

But it closes such a body to every value-type argument, `int` included. `where U: sendable` admits values without borrows but excludes function types and open classes. No constraint means exactly "holds no borrows".

- **Proposal 0145's restrictions are wider than "no upcast".**
  - A `TaskScope` is minted only as the initializer of an `await using var` binding whose static type is `TaskScope`. It is never an `owned` parameter, field, return slot, choice payload or function-type slot, never an owning element or `Shared<T>` payload, and never converted to `Object` or an interface at an owning position.

So `Log(scope)` over `Log<T>(x: T)` is rejected although it passes a borrow. The remedy is a plain parameter of type `TaskScope`. `List<TaskScope>`, a borrowing collection, is rejected too, and its per-instantiation admission is declined with a reopening bar.
  - Measured reach: zero sites.
- **0144's `Object` case is ahead of the compiler.** The compiler already rejects every interface-typed `await using var` live across a `yield return`. It **admits** the `Object`-typed one, because `Object` resolves to a primitive type ref that `awaitUsingYieldSensitive` skips. The interface half flips nothing; the `Object` half is tracked ([#5654](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5654), item 1). Under 0145, a `TaskScope` can no longer be held at `Object` by an `await using var` at all. 0144's key still covers a program's own class without a synchronous fallback held at `Object`.

Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked, [#5654](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5654), three items, each probed before filing):** the `Object` head is admitted (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:20025`; `src/sema/TypeResolution.cpp:127`). A no-destructor class without `IAsyncDisposable`, and a compiler-known head, are over-rejected. An inherited destructor is counted (the next bullet).
- **§28.12, §30.7, Appendix C.3, C.6, stdlib §2.10 — the synchronous fallback is per level (ruling; the question proposal 0144 §5 filed).** §30.7 keyed on a class that "declares no destructor", and §28.12's warning on one "without a destructor". Neither said whether a destructor the class only inherits counts.
  - It does not. An inherited destructor is a base level's cleanup: §28.4's chain runs each level's own body, and §28.12 step 2 supersedes per level. It stands in for nothing declared above it.
  - A class is **without a synchronous fallback** when any level of its chain declares or overrides a non-`abstract` `DisposeAsync` and declares no destructor of its own. So `class Der: Base, IAsyncDisposable`, with only `Base` declaring a destructor, draws §28.12's warning and may not be live across a `yield return`.
  - A class that only inherits a `DisposeAsync` together with the destructor paired with it at that level has its fallback, and is neither warned nor rejected. A literal "declares no destructor" would warn every subclass of a correctly written async-disposable base.
  - An `abstract` `DisposeAsync` performs no cleanup and needs no fallback.
  - §28.12's run-time paragraph, §30.7's class clause and Appendix C.6's row read the defined term, and stdlib §2.10 says the destructor belongs at the level that declares `DisposeAsync`.

  **Declined** (one `rejected` row): the inherits reading, under which `Base`'s destructor would discharge `Der`'s asynchronous cleanup. Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked, item 3 of [#5654](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5654)):** `awaitUsingClassHasSyncDisposeFallback` (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:19990–20013`) returns at the first destructor at any level and admits `Der`. The §28.12 warning is unimplemented (`s28_12_0003`, a banked `fail`), and its implementation takes the per-level fact.
- **Stdlib §6.10, §5.1, Appendix C.6, Guide 04 §4, rationale §12.12, the code-generation reference — a `TaskScope` is owned by its `await using var` binding alone (design change, [proposal 0145](proposals/0145-taskscope-owned-by-its-await-using-binding.md)).** Stdlib §6.10's "consumption is `await using` only" was stated by binding form, which is checkable only while the static type is `TaskScope`. A scope reaching another owning position was discharged on §28.12's implicit synchronous path, which skips the drain while children hold the frame's borrows: an `owned` field, parameter or return slot, an owning element, a `Shared<T>` payload, or an owning position of `Object` or an interface through a §5.1 upcast (`Make(): owned Object` returning `new TaskScope()`, bound by `using var o := Make();`).
  - A `TaskScope` is minted only as the initializer of an `await using var` binding whose static type is `TaskScope`, and that binding owns it alone. A `using var` is never moved out of (§28.10).
  - Every other owning position is a compile error at the site: a plain, `using` or `const` binding; an undisposed drop; any §28.1 `owned` position; an owning element or slot; a `Shared<T>` payload; and an owning position of `Object` or an interface reached by conversion. `TaskScope?` reads as `TaskScope`.
  - `TaskScope` is no type argument, explicit or inferred (§14.1). That also stops `new T()` under `where T: new()` from minting one.
  - Other borrows are unrestricted: a plain parameter at `TaskScope`, `Object` or an interface, a pattern binding, a child's self-capture. No implicit discharge runs on a borrow, and `Dispose()` through one is already a compile error (§28.6), so no borrow reaches a synchronous disposal path.
  - §5.1 now says that a reference conversion into an owning position of the wider type is an owning position of the source's type.

  **Declined** (three `declined-at-proposal` rows): the status quo; a bare conversion ban, which closes only the upcast faces and rejects harmless borrows; and a per-instantiation check admitting `TaskScope` as a type argument. No borrowing collection of scopes exists to admit, and the check would need reject-at-substitution clauses where §28.1 erases `owned T`, plus a `new T()` check. The whole-argument ban is §14.2's existing shape. The degraded synchronous destructor stays `deferred` on its own row, its condition unmet. Kernel: no contact. It is **self-distributing**: `typeof` is the type's own distribution channel, and since `owned Type` is inadmissible, no `Shared<Type>` could exist. **Displacement-unbounded** is not granted, because an overwrite strands nothing.

### v0.329 changelog (v0.328 → v0.329)

**The questions v0.328 filed, decided under the owner's delegation.** On 2026-10-08 the owner directed: "Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them." v0.327 and v0.328 acted on that direction. This revision acts on it for the four issues v0.328's lanes filed, and for one older `spec-question` that the text already decided. Each decision is a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`). A decision that changes what compiles went through a proposal, which graduates here. The decisions:
- **Proposal [0146](proposals/0146-borrow-erasing-positions.md)** (a value that holds borrows reaches no `Object` or interface position other than `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>`): [#5645](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5645), the v0.328 `L1` critique's filing.
- **Proposal [0147](proposals/0147-direct-disposeasync-takes-the-owned-receiver-rule.md)** (a direct `DisposeAsync()` call takes §28.6's owned-receiver rule): [#5646](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5646), the v0.328 `L4` lane's filing.
- **Rulings, no proposal:**
  - [#5647](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5647), a spec defect (§28.12 step 2 skips no destructor at an `abstract` `DisposeAsync` level);
  - the receiver of an extension call headed `Object` is a set-erasing position (decided by reading in the composition check; `N1`'s critique, NB5).
- **Clarifications:** [#5648](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5648) (§14.2's exclusion reaches the calls dispatch can route to an inherited witness, not a base class's own generic method).
- **Decided by reading, no doc change:** [#5628](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5628) (a record's primary constructor is a §22.6 candidate at `new`). It was closed before this revision, and its compiler delta is [#5658](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5658).

Three lanes:
- `N1`: proposal 0146 and #5648.
- `N2`: proposal 0147 and #5647.
- `N3`: #5628.

`N1` and `N2` each passed their author's adversarial pass and an independent critique: 5 blocking and 8 non-blocking findings, all resolved (`N1` 4 and 5, `N2` 1 and 3). `N3` makes no edit and took its author's adversarial pass. The 40 edits (`N1` 19, `N2` 21) were applied as one sequence. A composition check added 15: 10 in the documents (3 spec, 4 stdlib, 1 rationale, 2 code-generation reference) and 5 in the proposals folder and the decline index.

The critics' blocking findings were these:
- `N1`:
  - The receiver admission covered every interface-headed extension call. An extension on `Object` or a user interface reads `this` at the head type and may pass it to a parameter that stores it, so a borrow-bearing record escaped through `p.Leak(k)`. The receiver admission is now a member call or an extension call headed `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>`. The receiver of an extension call headed `Object` or another interface is borrow-erasing.
  - `s as Object` over an `IReadOnlySpan<int>` parameter, and a typed-pattern binding at `Object`, reached a storing `Object` parameter with no conversion at the call. The bullet now names both conversions.
  - The drafted rule said an `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` value **holds borrows**, against §3.6 and §35.4, which define the property for value types only. It now says such a value is **read as holding borrows**, and §3.6's row points there.
  - #5648's clarification left §2.8.6's *becomes a dispatched generic method* row rejecting a call "wherever written", the literal reading #5648 declines. The row now reads "wherever §14.2's exclusion reaches it".
- `N2`:
  - The drafted §28.12 and K3.9 text left the chained `base.DisposeAsync()` inside "a direct `DisposeAsync()` call", the clause that triggers physical reclamation. Read that way, the chain would reclaim the object while the override is still running, and K3.9 would kill a binding that does not exist. The chain is now neither a reclaiming direct call nor a K3.9 position.

**Outcomes the owner should see.**
- **`Console.WriteLine(span)` stops compiling** on a buffer- or array-backed span, and so do `Console.Write`, `TextWriter.Write`/`WriteLine` and `StringBuilder.Append` at their `Object` parameters. The remedy is `Console.WriteLine(span.ToString())` or `Console.WriteLine($"{span}")`. Both print the same text, which `span_interpolation_agrees_with_call` pins, and the diagnostic must name them (0146 §5.4). A record's `Equals(Object?)` called on a borrow-bearing record is rejected the same way; its `Equals(T)` and `=` are the spelling.
- **Five banked tests flip under 0146** when its check lands. Each must be updated in the fixing commit:
  - `span_range_tostring_2661.span_console_argument_renders` (`tests/codegen/span_range_tostring_2661_test.cpp:178`): `Console.WriteLine(sp)` is rejected at the call. The rendering it guarded stays pinned by `span_tostring_in_statement_position` and `span_interpolation_agrees_with_call`.
  - `xmod_imported_span_box_vtable_3358.local_single_module_control`, `.is_string_on_dependency_boxed_span`, `.whole_object_surface_on_dependency_boxed_span` and `.dependency_with_span_box_links_and_runs` (`:150–231`): `var o: Object := irs;` is rejected at the initializer. Three of them also return that box past its `using var` buffer, which v0.328 already rejected and the compiler misses. The cross-module box-vtable linking they guard is to be re-pinned on an admitted shape.
- **The Console allowlist is declined, although it is sound.** Stdlib §2.1, §3.1 and §7.4 state that the `Object` overloads of `Console.Write`/`WriteLine`, `TextWriter.Write`/`WriteLine` and `StringBuilder.Append` render by `ToString()` and keep nothing. Admitting a span there would be sound. It is declined, on three grounds:
  - It is a per-member allowlist that user rendering APIs could not share, which is the ground v0.320 gave for declining `Raise` by name.
  - The closure twin declined the same rendering admission at v0.320, so the two rules would disagree at one position.

- **§8.6, §9.7, §3.6, §28.3, §28.14, Appendix C.3, stdlib §4.16, rationale §4.2, the code-generation reference — borrow-erasing positions: a value that holds borrows reaches no `Object` or interface position other than `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` (design change, [proposal 0146](proposals/0146-borrow-erasing-positions.md); [#5645](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5645)).** §8.6 admitted boxing a borrow-bearing record "for a short-lived interface call (e.g. passing to a method accepting `Object`)". §28.3's field-store residual then admitted the callee's store of a plain `Object` parameter under K4.1's backstop, a backstop a span's buffer window does not have (§9.7's instance-field bullet). `method K(x: Object) F := x;` called with a span, and `b.Keep<Object>(span)` over `Keep<T>(x: T) F := x;`, kept a dangling view with no rejection, no backstop and no recorded clause.
  - **The rule.** A value that holds borrows (§3.6) is converted to `Object` or to an interface type at two positions only. One is the receiver of a member call (§8.6, §9.4) or of an extension call headed `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>`; the other is a position declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>`. Every other conversion is a compile error at the conversion site, checked by the caller over the callee's declared signature, per instantiation (§9.7's *borrow-erasing position* bullet; K2.3 + K2.4, the twin of §28.3's *Set-erasing positions*). That covers:
    - a parameter, plain or `scoped`, declared `Object` or any other interface, or at a bare type parameter the call substitutes with one;
    - a local, a field, a collection slot or literal element, a record component, a choice payload, an inline-array slot, a `ref`/`out` location, and a return;
    - the receiver of an extension call headed `Object` or another interface, whose body reads `this` at the head type;
    - an `as` or typed-pattern binding of an `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` value at such a type.
  - **`IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` values are read as holding borrows.** A value declared at that interface type, nullable or not, is read as holding the borrows of the span it boxes, by declared type. A boxed `ReadOnlyStringSpan` is included. The interface gets no holds-borrows property, which §3.6 keeps for value types; §3.6's row points at the reading. So a callee's parameter of that type cannot be stored in a field (the #4751 compiler leg, now the spec's), returned past its source, captured by an escaping closure, passed at `Object`, or declared on an `async` method. It is the one reference type so read, and stdlib §4.16 says the same of its parameter.
  - Rejected with it, as the set-erasing rule rejects a capture-bearing closure there: `Console.WriteLine(span)` and `StringBuilder.Append(span)`, whose spelling is `span.ToString()` or an interpolation hole, and a record's `Equals(Object?)`, which its `Equals(T)` and `=` replace.

  **Declined** (four `rejected` rows and one `deferred`):
  - a recorded K4.3 trust clause for the store, which would reverse §9.7's no-backstop ground;
  - a callee-side rule forbidding the store of every plain `Object` or interface parameter, which retires §28.3's back-reference idiom and, keyed on an interface's implementers, is not modular (§2.8.3);
  - the Console allowlist and its overload variant (above);
  - `Object` locals with tracked sources.

  The `deferred` row is a user-declared borrow-view interface in `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>`'s role; no program needs one. Kernel: derivation (K2.3 + K2.4). Body-locality: local at the conversion; carve-out, confinement (i), for the type-parameter twin. **Compiler (tracked, [#5659](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5659), five items, probe first):** the conversion is identified by `isBoxingTargetType` (`src/sema/ExprTypecheck.cpp:4434`), and the only borrow checks on it are the boxed-record field store (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:9846–9900`, #4478) and the `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` field store (`:9697–9838`, #4751). §28.14's `scoped` interface clause has no implementing leg.
- **§28.3 *Set-erasing positions*, Appendix C.3, the code-generation reference — the receiver of an extension call headed `Object` is a set-erasing position (clarification, decided by reading in the composition check; `N1`'s critique, NB5).** §28.3 exempted a function value as the receiver of "a member `Object` declares" (`f.ToString()`). Nothing said whether the receiver of an `extension Object` call, which §26.5 rule 2 reaches from a function-typed receiver, is such a position.
  - **It is.** The extension's receiver parameter is declared at the head, which is `Object`, and the body may pass `this` on to a parameter that stores it.
  - A capture-bearing function value there is rejected, and a capture-free one is admitted. This is the closure twin of 0146's receiver clause.

  Kernel: derivation (K2.3 + K2.4). Body-locality: local. **Compiler:** a note on [#5514](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5514), whose caller-side check takes the position.
- **§28.2, §28.6, §28.12, Appendix C.3, kernel K3.9 and K4, stdlib §2.10 and §6.10, the code-generation reference §7.2 — a direct `DisposeAsync()` call takes §28.6's owned-receiver rule (design change, [proposal 0147](proposals/0147-direct-disposeasync-takes-the-owned-receiver-rule.md); [#5646](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5646)).** §28.12 admitted "a direct `DisposeAsync()` call awaited outside `await using` (legal; … reclamation follows exactly as if `await using` had issued it)" with no receiver condition. §28.6 *Who may call `Dispose()`* and K3.9 enumerated `x.Dispose()`, `x?.Dispose()`, `x!.Dispose()` and the discard. So a borrow could await the call and reclaim the heap block of an object its owner still held: a plain parameter, a pattern or `catch` binding, a field read, a getter result, an `IAsyncDisposable`-typed view, or `this` in a `CloseAsync()`-style method. §28.6 closes that hazard for `Dispose()` with no exception.
  - **The rule.** The direct call, in the same three spellings and awaited or not, requires a receiver the caller owns by §28.6's classification. Through a borrow it is a compile error, `this` included.
  - **The chain.** `base.DisposeAsync()` directly in the body of a `DisposeAsync` override (not in a lambda nested in it) is §28.12 step 2's chain, not a disposal of `this`. It is admitted, and it triggers no reclamation of its own.
  - **The post-state.** The call is K3.9's row. The binding is explicitly-disposed afterward, so the scope-end machinery of a `using var` or `await using var` whose `DisposeAsync()` was called directly skips it. A straight-line use afterward, a second explicit call included, is §28.2's use-after-dispose warning. §28.12's "a second call … is a no-op" now says it is the runtime contract. The disposal moment is the call; logical disposal completes at the returned task's terminal state, and reclamation follows there.

  **Declined** (three `declined-at-proposal` rows): the status quo; logical-only disposal through a borrow with reclamation deferred to the owner, which still runs the cleanup out from under the owner and splits §28.12's object-central reclamation by receiver; and a warning in place of the error, since §28.6 is exception-free for the synchronous call. Kernel: derivation (K3.9's row widened by a spelling; no new axiom; eleven positions). Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked, [#5660](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5660), five items, probe first):** the receiver check and the explicitly-disposed bookkeeping match the `Dispose` spelling only (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:2592`, `:2130`, `:2203`, `:2629`, `:4653`; `src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:14085`). `DisposeAsync` on a `TaskScope` receiver is "no member" ([#5657](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5657) item 6).
- **§28.12 step 2 — an `abstract` `DisposeAsync` supersedes no destructor (spec defect, ruling; [#5647](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5647)).** Step 2 skipped a level's destructor "if that level declares or overrides `DisposeAsync`". The same section's definition of *without a synchronous fallback* already read an `abstract` declaration as performing no cleanup. Take `abstract class Base: IAsyncDisposable`, declaring `abstract method DisposeAsync(): Task;` and a destructor, overridden in `Der`. `await using` skipped `Base`'s destructor, and `Der.DisposeAsync` could not chain to an abstract `base.DisposeAsync()`, so `Base`'s cleanup ran on neither path.
  - **Decided:** at each level, the destructor body is skipped only if that level declares or overrides a **non-`abstract`** `DisposeAsync`. An `abstract` level is cleaned up exactly as on the synchronous path.
  - Chaining to `base.DisposeAsync()` is the override's obligation only where the base level declares a non-`abstract` one.
  - So the hierarchy above runs `Der.DisposeAsync`, skips `Der`'s destructor if it declares one, and runs `Base`'s destructor, on both paths.

  **Declined** (one `rejected` row): keying the skip on any `DisposeAsync` declaration, `abstract` included. Kernel: no contact. **Compiler:** the `await using` reclamation chain (`bz$<C>$DisposeReclaim`, `src/codegen/LlvmBackend_Disposal.cpp:529–620`) chains through `emitBaseDisposeChain` (`:6458`), which runs every base level's destructor body (source-read). So for this shape it already runs the abstract base's destructor, once [#3516](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3516)'s abstract-head bug is fixed. The same unconditional chain is the divergence [#3838](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3838) tracks at a non-`abstract` base. Both issues get a note; there is no new tracker.
- **§14.2 *Dispatched generic methods*, §2.8.6, rationale §10 — the exclusion reaches the calls dispatch can route to an inherited witness, not a base class's own generic method (clarification, gated as a ruling; [#5648](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5648)).** Take `class D: B, I`, which uses `B.M<T>`, an ordinary generic method of `B`, as the inherited witness of `I.M<T>`.

  - §2.8.6 says the same of a summary gain's audience. Its *becomes a dispatched generic method* row's "rejected wherever written" now reads "wherever §14.2's exclusion reaches it".
