### v0.330 changelog (v0.329 → v0.330)

**Three defects found by the rule-corpus catch-up, decided under the owner's delegation.** The rule-corpus catch-up that covered the v0.324–v0.329 rulings (commit `8de0292`, 120 cases) found three places where the documents could not be written against: a case that the text required could not be stated, or a program the text printed did not compile. On 2026-10-08 the owner directed: "Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them." This revision decides the three under that direction, each as a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`). None needed a proposal: two resolve contradictions the text already contained, and one corrects a printed example. The decisions:
- **Rulings, no proposal:**
  - [#5664](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5664), a spec defect: §12.2's hiding rule, read against `Object`'s members, blocked every class from implementing `IEquatable<T>`, `IEqualityComparer<T>` and `IFormattable`;
  - [#5665](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5665), a spec defect: §28.14's formation-bar remedy, `lambda(g) => xs.Add(g)`, is itself rejected.
- **Clarification and editorial:** proposal 0143's example did not compile; it is corrected, and §28.8.1 gains a sentence on `finally` restorations.

One lane, `P1`, wrote all three. It passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique: **4 blocking and 8 non-blocking findings**, all resolved. Its 15 edits (4 spec, 2 stdlib, 1 rationale, 4 code-generation reference, 3 in proposal 0143, 1 in the decline index) were applied as one sequence. A composition check added 9: 4 in the documents (2 stdlib, 1 code-generation reference, 1 guide) and 5 in the proposals folder and the decline index.

The critic's blocking findings were these:
- The drafted stdlib §2.9 text said `=` and the hash containers reach `Equals(Object?)` on a class that declares `Equals(T)`, and that §8.3's hash rule does not bind `Equals(T)`. Both were wrong. §8.4 makes `a = b` the call `a.Equals(b)`, §9.2 *Through a type parameter* binds a container's key comparison to the member the same use on a `T`-typed operand binds, and §22.6 resolves both to the exact own-typed overload. §8.3's rule reads every `a.Equals(b)`. Stdlib §2.9 and the code-generation reference now say which member each surface reaches, and that the author overrides `GetHashCode()` to agree.
- The drafted §12.2 said `p.Equals(q)` selects the own-typed overload and `p.Equals(o)` reaches `Object`'s, as a general rule. §22.6 ranks only exact matches, so an argument that converts to both overloads and matches neither exactly is ambiguous: a subclass of `Point`, or a `Point` where the overload is declared at `Point?`. §12.2 now states the ambiguity and its remedy, and that `=`, `<>` and uses through a type parameter are such calls.
- The issue placeholders were links without a `#`, which `check_docs.sh`'s anchor check never examines, so they would have landed silently. They are now fail-loud missing anchors, with a `grep` for the decline index, which the check does not cover.
- The lane asserted that no test flips. A scan found nine `tests/` programs that declare a class member at `Object`'s own signature without `override`, and the standard library's own `StringBuilder` sketch did the same. The nine are listed for the tracker, and `StringBuilder.ToString()` is now spelled `override`.

**Outcomes the owner should see.**
- **`p = d` with a subclass-typed `d` is a compile error** on a class that declares `Equals(T)`, and so is `p.Equals(d)`. The argument converts to both `Point` and `Object?` and matches neither exactly, which is §22.6's ambiguity. The remedy is to bind `d` at `Point` first (`var pp: Point := d;`). Whether `=` on classes should instead bind a fixed member is filed as a question ([#5670](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5670)).
- **`=` and the hash containers use the own-typed `Equals`.** On a class declaring `Equals(T)`, `a.Equals(b)` and `a = b` at `T` operands, and a `Set<T>` or `Dictionary<T, V>` built without a comparer, compare by `Equals(T)` and hash by `GetHashCode()`. `Object`-typed dispatch reaches `Equals(Object?)`. Such a class overrides `GetHashCode()` to agree, because the compiler's pairing check reads `override Equals` only. Whether the compiler should enforce that pairing for a plain own-typed `Equals`, as v0.327 made it for enums and choices, is filed ([#5668](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5668)).
- **Nine compiler tests flip when the tracker lands** ([#5669](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5669)). Each declares a class `ToString()`, `GetHashCode()` or `Equals(other: Object[?])` without `override`, plain or `virtual`, and each must be re-spelled with `override` in the fixing commit. They were already ill-formed under the literal v0.329 §12.2, so no spec verdict moves.
- **`string`'s `Equals` is declared at `string`** (composition check, below). As printed at v0.329, `Equals(other: string?)` beside `override Equals(Object?)` would have made `s.Equals(t)`, `s = t` and every `Set<string>` ambiguous under this revision's §12.2 sentence.

A composition check over the union then fixed four seams:
- **[#5664](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5664) × `string`.** Stdlib §9.6 declared `public pure method Equals(other: string?): bool`, satisfying `IEquatable<string>` under §11.2's nullability widening, beside `override Equals(other: Object?)`. A `string` argument converts to both and matches neither exactly, so by the ambiguity this revision states, `s.Equals(t)`, `s = t` (§8.4) and a `Set<string>`'s key comparison (§9.2) had no unique member. The member is now `Equals(other: string)`, exact at a `string` argument. A `string?` argument reaches the content-based `Equals(Object?)`, which gives the same answer, so no program changes verdict or result. The code-generation reference's `String` listing says the same. Stdlib §2.9 now tells a class to declare `Equals` at `T`, not `T?`.
- **[#5664](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5664) × Guide 07.** Its *A name is never reused down an inheritance chain* paragraph said §12.2 forbids hiding "outright", so that every same-named derived member is an error unless it is an `override`. The paragraph now names the exception for `Object`'s three members at another parameter list.
- **[#5665](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5665) × proposals 0140 and 0133.** Proposal 0140's item 7 quoted the code-generation reference's remedy as "write `lambda(g) => xs.Add(g)`". It is corrected in place to the new reference text, with a one-line note. Proposal 0133 states the old remedy twice (its option 5's §28.14 edit and §4.3's list of costs and remedies). Both sentences keep their text and gain a superseded note, since they record what was landed at v0.320.
- **The decline index.** One `rejected` row records the composition's alternative, and the size line is recomputed (below).

Checked at the seams, with no edit needed:
- **[#5664](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5664) × #5598 (v0.327).** On an enum or a choice the `Object` slot is reached by the own-typed `Equals`; on a class by `override Equals(Object?)`. In both, other parameter lists are ordinary methods, and the rationale paragraph states the parallel. The *Member hiding* and hand-written `Serialize` rows in the decline index are narrowed at `Object`'s signature only, not reopened.
- **Rationale §8.1's opening** ("Bezel rejects same-name members in derived classes outright") stays. The v0.330 paragraph qualifies it, as the v0.184 visibility paragraph already does.
- **Spec §8.4** ("classes customize equality by overriding `Equals`") stays true. Operator overloading of `=` is still refused on classes, and the own-typed overload is an `Equals`.
- **Appendix C.** C.1's hiding row is `P1`'s. No other row restates the hiding rule, the remedy or the restoration discipline.
- **§28.8.1's `finally` sentence × build-before-take.** Rationale §5.10's *exception-path obligation*, the code-generation reference's §28.8.1 note and Guide 01 §7 teach build-before-take, which stays the idiom. The `finally` form is for a read that must follow the move, so none of them is contradicted.
- **The rule corpus.** `s15_1_1_0009` already restores in a `finally`. `s15_1_1_0010`/`0011` and `s9_4_0010` read before the move or restore adjacently. `s28_14_0024` cites the bar's rule sentence, not the remedy. No case states a class `Equals` at a non-`Object` signature as rejected.
- **The guides.** No guide teaches `IEquatable`, `IFormattable` or `IEqualityComparer` on a class, the formation-bar remedy, or a field move with a read before the restoration.
- **`scripts/check_docs.sh`** on the composed tree: ANCHOR fails only on the unfilled placeholder `rationale#UNFILED-P1-ISSUE-1`, and passes once both placeholders are replaced. VERSION, FACTS, TABLE, SETS, REGISTER, STYLE and EXTRACT are clean (523 fragments). The one CITATION advisory, `§4.12`, was already present at v0.329. `scripts/check_proposals.sh` passes (live 48, graduated 99).

- **§12.2, Appendix C.1, rationale §8.1, stdlib §2.9, §3.1 and §9.6, Guide 07, the code-generation reference — `Object`'s virtual members block only their own signature (ruling; [#5664](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5664)).** §12.2 blocked a derived member of any inherited visible name at any signature, and §8.1 gives every class `Equals(Object?)`, `GetHashCode()` and `ToString()`. Read literally, no class could declare `Equals(other: T)`, `Equals(a: T, b: T)`, `GetHashCode(value: T)` or `ToString(format: string)`, so none could implement `IEquatable<T>`, `IEqualityComparer<T>` or `IFormattable`. That contradicted §18.5 and stdlib §2.9, §2.18 and §4.8–§4.10, whose comparer constructors would have had no admissible argument.
  - **The rule.** A class may declare a non-`override` instance member of the three names at any parameter list other than `Object`'s (nullability-widened). It overloads the inherited member at the class and its subclasses, resolved by §22.6:
    - the exact own-typed overload at a `T` argument;
    - `Object`'s member, overridden or not, at an `Object?` argument;
    - §22.6's ambiguity at an argument that converts to both and matches neither exactly (a subclass of `T`, or a `T` where the overload is declared at `T?`), remedied by binding the argument at the intended parameter's type.

    `=` and `<>` (§8.4) and uses through a type parameter (§9.2) are such calls.
  - **Unchanged.** The plain same-signature spelling stays hiding, and `override` stays the only route to the slot. The standard library's `StringBuilder.ToString()` is now spelled `override`.
  - **The admission is `Object`'s alone.** A class's `Equals(T)` blocks the name in its subclasses as any member does. Static members of the three names, `GetType` and `ReferenceEquals` block as before.
  - **What each surface reaches (stdlib §2.9).** `a.Equals(b)`, `a = b` and a comparer-less `Dictionary<T, V>`/`Set<T>` select `Equals(T)` and hash by `GetHashCode()`. The hash containers' key comparison is §9.2's `T`-typed use. `Object`-typed dispatch reaches `Equals(Object?)`. §8.3's hash rule reads every `a.Equals(b)`, so the class overrides `GetHashCode()` to agree; the compiler's pairing check still reads `override Equals` only. The member is declared at `T`, not `T?`, as `string`'s now is (composition).
  - **The accepted residual (rationale §8.1).** `p.Equals(q)` at a `Point` receiver may answer differently from the same call through `Object`. Every typed-equality interface carries that split, and a record whose only `Equals` is `Equals(T)` already has it on its boxed path (§9.2). The author overrides `Equals(Object?)` where the two answers must agree.

  **Declined** (three `rejected` rows):
  - the literal reading, which contradicts four normative statements and leaves stdlib surface unreachable;
  - exempting any member that implements an interface member, whatever base declares the name, which admits the static-type shadow §8.1 refuses (the hand-written `Serialize` row's shape);
  - a §22.6 tie-break ranking a class's own-typed `Equals` above `Object`'s inherited member (composition). §22.6 ranks no implicit conversion above another, and a tie-break keyed on one member name would be the only exception, for a shape the declaration avoids.

  Kernel: no contact. Body-locality: declaration-local. **Compiler (tracked, [#5669](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5669), probe first):** `checkHidingAndOverride` seeds its frontier from `t->baseTypes` (`src/sema/TypeResolution_Checks.cpp:6797–6803`), which never holds `Object`, so `Object`'s members take no part in the check. The overloads are therefore already accepted, and the plain same-signature spelling probably is too, which this ruling rejects. Nine tests flip (above). `l2_9_0003`, `s18_5_0007` and `s18_5_0008` stay `pass` and now have a rule to cite.
- **§28.8.1, the code-generation reference §7.3, proposal 0143 — a `finally` restoration satisfies K9.2, and the 0143 example is corrected (clarification and editorial).** The v0.328 example `var t := move h.Slots; _ := a[0]; h.Slots := t;` put an inline-array indexer access between the move and the restoration. §28.8.1 lists that access as throwable, with no constant-index carve-out, so the example had an unrestored exception edge (K9.2) and could not compile. The read now sits in a `try` whose `finally` restores the field: in the reference pair, and in proposal 0143 §1.1, §5 and §7. The reference's note says a slot read through an inline-array binding needs the restoration in a `finally`.
  - **The sentence.** §28.8.1 states what the path rule and §31.2 already compose to. A restoration in a `finally` satisfies the rule when every throwable expression between the move and the store lies in the `try`'s protected block, because §31.2 runs the `finally` on every exit edge of the block, the exception edges included. The store into the moved-from location is non-throwable.
  - The condition is sufficient, not necessary: a throwable in a `catch` arm also exits through the `finally`. The path rule stays authoritative, and nothing new is admitted.

  Verdict impact: none. Kernel: no contact (K9.2's path set and §31.2's exit edges). **Compiler:** the restoration analysis runs on the CFG, which expands `try`/`finally` into real blocks and exception edges (`src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:2733–2740`), so the shape is probably accepted. No test pins it; a probe-first pin is filed ([#5667](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5667)). [#5652](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5652)'s test specification copied the uncompilable probe and gets a comment.
- **§28.14 *The method-reference formation bar*, the code-generation reference §4.4, proposals 0133 and 0140 — the remedy is the direct call, not a lambda (ruling; [#5665](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5665)).** The bar's last sentence offered `lambda(g) => xs.Add(g)` as the remedy for a rejected `xs.Add` at `Array<() -> int>`. That lambda's body is rejected for every argument, capture-free ones included. `g` is a plain function-typed parameter, which:
  - contributes itself (§28.3 provenance clause 3);
  - is call-bounded (§28.14);
  - is refused by every collection slot (§28.3 *Function-typed holders*).

  No function value can forward an arbitrary argument into a set-erasing position: a plain function type announces no retention (K2.4), which is the bar's own ground. The sentence now says so and names the direct call at each site, `xs.Add(f)`, as the remedy. The code-generation reference is corrected in place, proposal 0140's quotation of it is corrected, and proposal 0133's two remedy sentences carry a superseded note (composition).

  **Declined** (one `rejected` row): every function-value spelling (`lambda(g)`, `lambda(scoped g)`, a `ref`-forwarding lambda). The reopening bar is a function-type form that announces its parameter's retention. Kernel: no contact (K2.4 is the ground, unchanged). Verdict impact: none; the body checks already rejected the lambda. **Compiler:** it rejects the lambda at a field-held `xs` (`lambda_own_param_call_bounded_1432.store_into_field_collection_rejected`, `tests/ownership/lambda_own_param_call_bounded_1432_test.cpp:131`) and accepts it at a local `xs` (`store_into_local_collection_accepted`, `:393`). That is the delta [#5518](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5518) already tracks, and the test flips when #5518 lands. [#5515](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5515) listed "the lambda remedy (run)" among its tests to add and gets a comment: the lambda is a reject.

### v0.331 changelog (v0.330 → v0.331)

**The borrow-flow matrix, decided under the owner's delegation.** A borrow-flow matrix audit crossed nine kinds of value (rows R1–R9: an owned class or interface value, a borrowed class or interface reference, a borrow-bearing record, a borrow-bearing inline array, a choice that holds borrows, a span, a capture-bearing function value, a bare type-parameter value, and a runtime-managed control) with thirteen destinations (columns C1–C13: an instance field, a static, a collection slot, a conversion to `Object` or an interface, a `ref`/`out` location, a return, a closure capture, a type-argument substitution, an async frame, an iterator frame, a pattern, `as` or aggregation binding, a domain crossing, and a `scoped` storage-bounded admission). It asked of each of the **117 cells** whether the documents decide where the value may go and on what guarantee. 85 cells were decided. **32 were open** (21 ambiguous, 7 missing, 4 in conflict), and they reduce to **10 root causes**, B1–B10, filed as [#5674](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5674)–[#5683](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5683). The cells, their rules, notes, counterexamples and cross-checks are published as [the borrow-flow matrix](https://claude.ai/artifact/2jv3zELseER5TmmUbFLoXx). On 2026-10-08 the owner directed: "Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them." This revision decides all ten root causes under that direction. Each decision is a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`), and each that removes a stated admission or adds a mechanism went through a proposal, which graduates here. The decisions:
- **Proposal [0148](proposals/0148-captured-holds-borrows-value-contributes-its-sources.md)** (a captured value that holds borrows contributes the sources of the borrows it carries): [#5677](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5677), root cause B4, fifteen cells.
- **Proposal [0149](proposals/0149-frame-locals-and-span-carried-borrows.md)** (frame locals and span-carried borrows in the consume-site freeze): [#5679](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5679), root cause B6.
- **Proposal [0150](proposals/0150-no-task-over-a-value-type-that-holds-borrows.md)** (no `Task<T>` over a value type that holds borrows): [#5674](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5674), root cause B1.
- **Proposal [0151](proposals/0151-static-stores-admit-only-static-sources.md)** (static stores admit only static-storage sources): [#5676](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5676), root cause B3.
- **Rulings, no proposal:**
  - [#5675](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5675), B2: an `as` at `Object` is a set-erasing position;
  - [#5678](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5678), B5: `Domain.Spawn`'s and `Parallel`'s plain rows admit no class but `string` and `Type`;
  - [#5680](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5680), B7: the storage admission's static bound is on the source;
  - [#5681](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5681), B8: an `async` body's result `return` is a marker-free consume;
  - [#5682](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5682), B9: a non-`await` borrow return in an `async` `Task<T>` body is rejected.

The critics' blocking findings were these:
- `T1`:
  - The lane measured zero flips for 0148. Four pinned accepts flip on the sink route: each returns a closure over a parameter-sourced span holder, which carried the empty set and now carries the parameter. The shape was unsound, because the caller's copy carries the empty set (provenance clause 4) and can outlive the argument. The flips are recorded, and §9.7's capture bullet now names the sink rule.
  - A method reference bound to a value receiver that holds borrows (`var f := pair.First; return f();`) was uncounted, though formation captures the receiver by copy (§27.6). Provenance clause 2, the method-reference bullet and the frame contribution now count it.
  - An `as` or typed pattern at a generic body's own type parameter (`V := f as T` in `class Box<T>`) carried a capture-bearing closure into a bare-`T` field, the generic twin of #5675. It is now a set-erasing position at the declaration.
- `T2`:
  - The draft froze a frame local's sources only while the local had a later use. A suspended enumerator's disposal runs its pending `finally`, which may read a span over a disposed source (§29.7). The frame's own disposal (explicit, `using var` scope end, or auto-drop) now counts as a use.
  - K5.9 named a span local and a frame local only. A span held in a record, inline-array or choice local, or captured by a live closure, is equally flagless. K5.9 now names every holder K5.5 traces.
  - Stdlib §4.14/§4.15 and rationale §5.15 read as making a span read flag-checked, which would make K5.9 unnecessary. Proposal 0149 now weighs that reading as option F, and the contradiction is filed ([#5707](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5707)).
- `T3`:
  - The lane classed #5674 as a ruling. It removes an admission three texts state (§30.5's "copyable value type … produced as today", §30.11's listing comment, stdlib §6.6), so it is a design change. Proposal 0150 records it, and its declines are `declined-at-proposal` rows.
  - The lane's survey said the `Task` family was the only standard-library generic retaining an unconstrained `T` without a stated rule. That is false: the value-copy members (`ToArray`, `Sorted`, `AddRange`, `CopyTo`, …) copy carried borrows inside exempt bodies. This changes the ground for declining a general rule, not the decision, and the family is filed ([#5693](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5693)).
  - `T3`'s and `T4`'s code-generation reference §7.6 insertions shared an anchor, so one order failed to apply. `T3`'s is re-anchored.
  - The drafted §30.14 bullet rejected the plain spawn rows "at a class type". Spec §30.14 reads `Type` as a class, and the stdlib declares `class String`, so `Domain.Spawn(Work, typeof(X))` would have been rejected against stdlib §6.8's own comment. `string` and `Type` are carved out.
- `T4`:
  - 0151's new bullet said a static property admits "exactly three operands", one of them a fresh value, which the preceding bullet's fresh-store error rejects. The rule is now a restriction on the borrow side only.
  - Two remedies offered `return move _item;`, a terminal field move, which §28.8.1 rejects on its own return edge. They are replaced.
  - The §30.1 sentence said that under `Task<T>` "a borrow is rejected", against Pattern A kinds 2 and 3 (`return await` over a source produces a borrow). The `return await` chain is excepted.
  - The `T3`/`T4` anchor collision above, from `T4`'s side.

- **`TaskCompletionSource<Pair>` and `Task.FromResult<Pair>` become errors** at a `Pair` that holds a borrow, and so does any written `Task<Pair>`, `Task<[2]Item>` or `Task<IReadOnlySpan<int>>`, at the declaration. `TaskCompletionSource<CancellationToken>` and a borrow-free record (`record Pt(X: int)`) stay admitted. Publish borrow-free data, or use `OwningTaskCompletionSource<Item>` for the object. Measured reach: zero.
- **A static holds only what is always live.** `Register(tx: ChannelSender<T>) _tx := tx;`, `Init(t: Task<Config>) _cfg := t;` and `Gate._m := m;` from a plain parameter are rejected at the store. A fresh value, `null`, `move m` from an owned binding and a bare read of another static (`Other._shared`) stay admitted. A borrow reached *through* a static (`T.f.g`, `T.P.Peek()`) is not static storage. Measured reach: zero.
- **Lazy-query and enumerator locals freeze their sources against move and reassignment, not mutation.** `var q := xs.Where(f); pool.Add(move xs); … q …` and `xs := new Array<int>();` under a live `q` are compile errors. `xs.Add(1)` under a live `q` stays admitted. Because a bound frame's disposal is a use, §29.11's recommended `using var q := xs.Where(f);` keeps `xs` frozen to the end of its scope even after `q` is consumed. Enumerate through an unbound call (`for var x in xs.Where(f) do … end;`) or dispose the frame before the transfer. Measured reach: zero.
- **Disposing a collection under a live span is a compile error.** `var s := xs.AsSpan(); xs.Dispose(); Console.WriteLine(s[0]);` is rejected at the `Dispose()`, and so is `_ := xs;`. Dispose after the span's last use. A record whose carried borrows are object references keeps the unfrozen posture, since every read through it hits the flag. Measured reach: zero; the five `Dispose()`-after-last-use sites in `consume_site_freeze_span_1726_test.cpp` and `consume_site_freeze_span_reassign_1741_test.cpp` stay accepted.
- **Every new rejection in this revision is ahead of the compiler**, except the direct plain-row `Domain.Spawn` call at a class, which it already rejects (#600). Nine trackers are filed (Migration, below).

- **§28.3's closure bullet (provenance clauses 1 and 2, the method-reference bullet), *Deferred-activation callees*, §28.14 (the captured-source sentence; *v1 admission bounds* item 1), §9.7 (the capture bullet), Appendix C.3, rationale §5.25, the code-generation reference §7.2 — a captured value that holds borrows contributes the sources of the borrows it carries (design change, [proposal 0148](proposals/0148-captured-holds-borrows-value-contributes-its-sources.md); [#5677](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5677); root cause B4).** Provenance clause 1 named no value-typed capture, and two passages said such a capture "contributes nothing". So a closure over a span, a borrow-bearing record or inline array, or a choice that holds borrows carried the empty set wherever the set was read rather than at the closure's escape:
  - `var f := lambda() => s; return f();` returned a window over a freed array with no flag (R3–R6 × C6);
  - a returned task or iterator frame rode the capture past its sources (R3–R6 × C9, R3–R5 × C10);
  - §28.14's admission neither tested nor froze the carried sources (R3–R6 × C13).
  - **The rule.** The capture contributes the sources of the borrows the value carries: the count *The sources an argument contributes* item 3 gives the same value as an argument, and the consume-site freeze gives a live local of that type. In a generic body it is read per instantiation (§9.7's generic-body paragraph). A captured value that carries no borrow (a value type that holds none, a null-source value, a `string`) still contributes nothing, and a captured `CancellationToken` is excepted at a frame as an argument one is. A method reference bound to such a receiver is counted the same way, its receiver being captured by copy (provenance clause 2).
  - **The sink rule.** Such a closure has a non-empty set, so returning or storing it is rejected whatever its sources are, a parameter's included, as for a closure over a class-typed parameter since v0.307. Four pinned tests flip (above).
  - Bound 1 keeps its headline ("a capture contributing no borrow source is exempt") and corrects its enumeration.

  **Declined** (three `rejected` rows): rejecting every such capture (option C), which forbids the in-place invocation and the in-scope lazy query that §9.7 and stdlib §4.16 admit; a route list in §9.7's capture bullet (option D), the closure-specific list the closure bullet forbids, which reopens at the next route; and a sinks-only count (option E), which leaves the counterexample. Kernel: derivation (K2.2 + K2.4); axiom A11 amended (bound 1's enumeration), headline kept. Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked, [#5697](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5697), probe first):** the capture gate `isBorrowableType` (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:3719`) answers false for every record, inline array, choice and bare type parameter, at both set-reading sites (`deferredActivationCaptureSources`, `:17398`; `checkScopedAdmission`, `:21540`). Whether the return check reads `return f()`'s set through a traced lambda local is unsettled by reading.
- **§28.3 *Set-erasing positions* and provenance clause 5, Appendix C.3, rationale §4.2, the code-generation reference §4.4 and §7.2 — an `as` at `Object` is a set-erasing position (ruling; [#5675](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5675); root cause B2).** The set-erasing list reached its positions "by implicit conversion" only, while §9.7's borrow-erasing twin named the `as` and the typed-pattern binding. `f as Object` over a capture-bearing `f` met no function-value rule, since the holders key on the static type `Object`. It carried the closure into a field (`_o := f as Object`), a collection, a storing `Object` parameter and a `ref` location (R7 × C1, C3, C4, C5), and the read-back `_o as () -> int` ran it over dead captures (R7/C11).
  - **The rule.** The `as` is a set-erasing position in its own right, rejected at the conversion as a box is, whatever then holds the result. Inside a generic body, an `as` or typed-pattern binding whose target is one of the body's own type parameters is a set-erasing position at the declaration (`T1`'s critique, B3).
  - **The other direction (clause 5).** A function value narrowed from `Object`, or from a value of bare type-parameter type, by `as` or a typed pattern carries the empty set: every function value at `Object` is capture-free by construction.
  - The one over-rejection is `(f as Object).ToString()`, while `f.ToString()` stays admitted. It is negligible and accepted for one rule.

  **Declined** (two `rejected` rows): tracking the set through the `Object`-typed result (the v0.329 `Object` local row in function-value form), and rejecting the `as` for capture-free function values. Kernel: derivation (K2.3 + K2.4). Body-locality: local. **Compiler:** no set-erasing check exists; the `as` route joins [#5514](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5514) (noted there, and on [#5650](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5650) for the generic route).
- **§28.3 *The consume-site freeze* (*Frame locals*; *Span-carried borrows and the site-announced kills*), K5's conjunct (ii) and clauses 3, 5 and 9, K6.4, the consume table's reading note, §29.4, Appendix C.3, rationale §5.1, the code-generation reference §5 and §7.2 — a frame local is a live borrow of its carried sources, and a span-carried borrow freezes the site-announced kills (design change, [proposal 0149](proposals/0149-frame-locals-and-span-carried-borrows.md); [#5679](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5679); root cause B6).** K6.4 said frame-held borrows are invisible to K5 and cited §30.1's settlement clause as their obligation, but that clause is a task's, and its backstop is the flag. A synchronous iterator may take a span (v0.317), and its frame carries the span's source, while a span reads its buffer window with no per-access check (§9.7). So `var it := Each(xs.AsSpan()); sink.Take(move xs);` then enumerating `it` had no static check, no recorded clause and no backstop (R6/C10). And `var s := xs.AsSpan(); xs.Dispose(); s[0]` was admitted by K5(ii)'s "exactly two recorded shapes", against §28.3's "every other consume" (the matrix's side finding S1). Two derivations close both:
  - **Frame locals (K5.5).** A live local holding an iterator or enumerator frame or a lazy query (the `for` desugaring's `__source` included) counts as a live local borrow of every source the frame carries, transitively, as a live closure value does. Its own disposal is a use, because a partially-consumed frame's disposal runs its pending `finally` (§29.7). A `move`, transfer or reassignment of a carried source under it is frozen; the site-announced kills of a carried *object* borrow stay unfrozen under the flag.
  - **Span-carried kills (K5.9).** A site-announced kill of a binding is frozen while a span-carried borrow of its value survives it in any holder the freeze traces: a span local; a record, inline-array or choice local that carries one; a live closure that captures one; a live frame local. The kill's flag never reaches a span read.
  - **Tasks.** K6.4 keeps a task local untraced, with the reason: its carried borrows are held under the recorded settlement clause, under §30.1's bans on a holds-borrows parameter and on a caller-sourced holds-borrows local across a suspension.
  - The consume table's reading note, K5's clause 3 and §28.3's "Unborrowed reassignment" sentence count three shapes. Rationale §5.1's v0.180 record gains the second exception to its decline of freezing `Dispose()`: #4413's decline of a third shape, and the v0.180 record, both rested on the backstop's presence, which a span window does not have.

  **Declined** (one `rejected` and three `declined-at-proposal` rows): the status quo, with no backstop of any kind for a span-carried borrow; a span-only frame trace, which keys K5.5's holder list on flag presence for one holder kind, with zero measured sites separating it; tracing task locals, which would turn §30.1's recorded abandonment and domain-transfer residuals into rejections (reopening bar: a span-carried source entering a task frame with no static rule); a K4.3 trust clause for the frame's span sources, with no backstop to name. The parameter ban stays declined (v0.317). Option F, making span reads flag-checked, is weighed and not taken here; it is filed ([#5707](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5707)), and would withdraw K5.9 if decided for the check. Kernel: derivations (K2.1 + K2.2 + K5.5; K5(ii)). Body-locality: local. **Compiler (tracked, [#5698](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5698)):** `checkConsumeFreeze` (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:13079–13160`) walks alias locals and span/record locals only, so a minted frame local carries no `source`. `markDisposedByName` (`:12145–12149`) runs the §28.14 freeze only, never the consume-site query. The frame's argument scan still covers reference-typed arguments only (v0.317; noted on [#5485](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5485)).
- **§28.14 *Class- and interface-typed `scoped` parameters* (the no-quiescence bullet), K5.7, Guide 01 §5 — the storage admission's static bound is on the source; a slot read through it keeps K5.6's posture (ruling; [#5680](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5680); root cause B7).** The scoped-construction bullet said the guarantee "is fully static with no residual trust" and the backstop "defense-in-depth only". It also admitted arguments sourced at `this` or a parameter whose referent a field overwrite disposes: a field read, a getter result, a capture of one (`using var r := new Reader(scoped _s); _s := new Stream(); r.Next()`). §28.3 *Scope* and K5.6 leave that referent to the runtime-checked posture (R2/C13, R7/C13).
  - **What is static.** The source's life: declared-before admission, the freeze and reverse-order disposal make the binding, parameter or `this` outlive the bounding object.
  - **What is not.** A class- or interface-typed borrow of a slot's current value keeps K5.6's posture under this admission, as under any other: the displaced object is flagged, and a later access through the stored borrow is K4.1's deterministic fault in checked mode. No K4.3 clause is recorded, and the trust-admission report stays silent.
  - K5.7's "a runtime flag is not an admissible backstop" is scoped to its subject, the captured binding. Guide 01 §5 says the same, and `s28_3_0091`'s `rule:` header is refreshed (verdict unchanged). The span-carried slot route is not claimed backstopped (`T2`'s critique, F7) and is filed ([#5706](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5706)).

  **Declined** (two `rejected` rows): narrowing the admission to local sources, which rejects form 3's sibling-field idiom (`_reader := new StreamReader(scoped _stream)`) and every parameter-sourced holder for a posture no narrowing removes; and a reported K4.3 clause, since the posture is flag-backstopped. Kernel: K5.6 + K4.1, already stated. **Compiler:** matches. `this`-derived sources are admitted with no freeze and parameters are frozen (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:21596–21640`). No tracker.
- **§30.5 (a new producer row), §30.10, §30.11, §9.7, Appendix C.6, stdlib §6.6 and §6.7, the code-generation reference §5.6 and §7.6 — no `Task<T>` over a value type that holds borrows (design change, [proposal 0150](proposals/0150-no-task-over-a-value-type-that-holds-borrows.md); [#5674](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5674); root cause B1).** §30.1's rejection of a value type that holds borrows as a result keys on the `async` modifier. So the non-`async` producers, `TaskCompletionSource<T>.SetResult`/`TrySetResult` and `Task.FromResult<T>`, retained a borrow-bearing record, inline array, choice or span in a task's result slot with no bound and, for a span, no backstop (§3.6 rule 2 exempts stdlib bodies; R3–R6 × C8).
  - **The rule.** §30.5 gains a producer row beside the move-only one. A value type that holds borrows (a T declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` read as the span it boxes) is admitted by no row. `Task<T>` over it is a compile error at the declaration, wherever the type is formed: a written `Task<Pair>`, and the instantiations `TaskCompletionSource<Pair>`, `Task.FromResult<Pair>` and `Task.WhenAll<Pair>`, explicit or inferred.
  - It is an instantiation-site rule in §3.6 rule 2's sense, re-read through a user generic (`Fwd<Pair>`, R8/C8).
  - `CancellationToken` is excepted on A10's footing, its result carrying §30.8's obligation that the source outlive every token observing it, with §28.2's backstop.
  - The ground is §30.1's own (K2.1 + K6.1). The rule is stated at the type rather than at the three retaining members, so `FromException<Pair>`, `FromCancelled<Pair>` and a `Task<Pair>` field fall under one sentence, as for move-only T.

  **Declined** (four `declined-at-proposal` rows): the status quo; a K4.3 trust clause for the retention (no flag on a span window); a member-level rejection leaving `Task<Pair>` declarable (two rules where one suffices, for a type no producer completes with a value); and a general §3.6 rule over every retaining stdlib member. The last fails because the second retention family, the value-copy members of the borrowing collections and LINQ (`ToArray`, `AddRange`, `Fill`, …), copies into a collection the caller holds and wants source propagation, not rejection; it is filed ([#5693](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5693)). No recorded decline is contradicted; the v0.274 `EventSource<T>` row is distinguished (that restriction was drawn from §30.1, this one is stated). Kernel: derivation (K2.1 + K6.1). Body-locality: local, decided at the type's formation site and per instantiation; no callee body is read. **Compiler (tracked, [#5699](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5699)):** the only check, `checkAsyncSignatureBorrowBearing` (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:18936–18963`), runs only when `isAsync_` (`src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:545–551`). The stated class-T rejection of `TaskCompletionSource<T>` is unenforced too (rule case `l6_6_0001`, banked `fail`).
- **Stdlib §6.8 and §6.12, spec §30.14's call-site list, Guide 04 §5, the code-generation reference §5.6 and §7.6 — the plain spawn rows admit no class but `string` and `Type` (ruling; [#5678](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5678); root cause B5).** `Domain.Spawn`'s plain `arg: A` and plain `R` rows, and `Parallel`'s value-element rows, constrained by `sendable, notnull`, admitted a sealed class. A borrow of a sendable class therefore crossed a domain without the move §30.14 requires (`Domain.Spawn<Counter>(Bump, c)` with `Bump(c: Counter)`, R2/C12; the same through `class Fan<T> where T: sendable, notnull`, R8/C12).
  - **The rule.** These rows carry the instantiation-site rule §3.6 rule 2 names for a stdlib type: `notnull` there means a sendable value type, `string` or `Type`. Any other class instantiation, explicit, inferred or through a user generic's substitution, is a compile error at the call site naming the `owned` row. "The `where` clauses state the full requirement" is dropped from both sections, and §30.14's call-site list states the rule.
  - It is a ruling, not a clarification: the matrix recorded both cells as conflicts, and §30.14's "class-typed arguments are `owned` and are moved", its "`R`: sendable non-class", and stdlib §6.8's "Value-typed, string or Type result" decide it. The dropped sentence was v0.274's sendability rewrite and decided nothing about class admission.
  - Stdlib §4.19's sharing idiom now declares `ScanLow(owned h: Shared<FrozenArray<double>>)`, which it relied on without stating (`T3`'s critique, F9).

  **Declined** (one `rejected` row): `where A: sendable, value`, which drops `string` and `Type`, while §14.2 has no non-class constraint. **Compiler:** the direct case is already rejected (#600, `src/sema/ExprTypecheck_Calls.cpp:13830–13856`); the generic-forwarder face is tracked ([#5700](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5700)), and `Parallel`'s is noted on [#3557](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3557).
- **§28.3 *Static stores of a class- or interface-typed value* (new) and the property-store bullet, §22.12, K4.3, Appendix C.3, rationale §12.15, the code-generation reference §7.6 — a static holds only what is always live (design change, [proposal 0151](proposals/0151-static-stores-admit-only-static-sources.md); [#5676](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5676); root cause B3).** §28.3's property-store bullet sent a static store to the field-store bullet, whose residual admitted a parameter- or receiver-sourced borrow under K4.1's backstop. A static is reachable from every domain, so the source's owner disposes in one domain while another reads the static. Neither the flag (read in the disposing domain) nor the domain clause (which names a transfer or consume, of which a static store makes none) orders that race. K4.3's recorded set had no static-held clause, and §28.3's own always-live claim for static reads was false under the admission (R2/C2).
  - **The rule.** A class- or interface-typed **borrow** stored into a non-`owned` static field (a mutable static rule 2 admits, or a `static readonly` in its static initialization) or into a static property other than through `set(owned)` is admitted only when static-storage-sourced: a bare read of a `static` field or of `T.P`, not a member reached through one (`T.f.g`, `T.P.Peek()`). Every other borrow is a compile error at the store.
  - Fresh values and `null` are admitted where they were. The remedies are the existing idioms: `new`, `move m` from an owned binding, `Other._shared`.
  - K4.3 states that no static-held clause exists, with a parenthetical for a borrow stored into a field of an object a static references, which stays the field-held residual under §22.12 rule 4's confinement.

  **Declined** (four `declined-at-proposal` rows): the status quo; a recorded K4.3 static-held clause (a clause needs a backstop, and across domains there is none); rejecting the static-sourced borrow too (process-lived storage never disposes a displaced referent, §22.13, so it cannot dangle); a warning (the hazard is rule 4's violation class, not form (iii)'s). Kernel: K4.3 gains one sentence; no new clause. Body-locality: store-local. **Compiler (tracked, [#5702](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5702), probe first):** `src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:15340–15350` exempts static targets from the §28.6 path, and no store check reads a parameter, receiver or capture source at a static target, so `_m := m;` is accepted today.
- **K3.2's Position cell, §30.1, §30.5 kind 1 and Pattern B, the code-generation reference §4.2 — an `async` body's result `return` under `OwningTask<T>` or a class- or interface-typed `Task<T>` is a marker-free consume (ruling; [#5681](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5681); root cause B8).** K3.2 named `Task`-family returns "in a non-`async` body" only, K3.13 says an unmarked read never consumes, and §30.5 kind 1 asked for "an owned expression". So `var c := new Conn(); return c;` under `OwningTask<Conn>` was in no row (R1/C9).
  - **The rule.** The result operand is K3.2's position: consumed marker-free, the binding moved-from, the task (kind 1) or the awaiter (Pattern B) owning the result. Kind 1's operand list names a fresh producer or a named owned binding of the body. A `move` of an owned field there is §28.8.1's terminal move, rejected (`T4`'s critique, C2).
  - By §28.3's one-spelling rule, `return move c;` there is the redundant marker, an error like every marker at a marker-free position (rationale's v0.260 decline of the symmetric reading).

  Kernel: K3.2's Position cell widens; no new row. **Compiler (tracked, [#5703](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5703)):** the unmarked spelling is accepted and consumes (`src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:8995`; `async_pattern_a_borrowed_identifier_return_4311`). The marked spelling is accepted by an explicit `!isAsync_` carve, which this ruling removes; one test flips (above).
- **§30.5 *No fourth kind* (new), §30.1, §28.3's callee-side item 1, Appendix C.6, the code-generation reference §7.6 — a non-`await` borrow return in an `async` `Task<T>` body is rejected (ruling; [#5682](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5682); root cause B9).** §28.3 admitted a receiver-sourced return from an instance method, while §30.5 enumerated three Pattern A result-slot kinds, none a borrow. `public async method GetAsync(): Task<Item> return _item;` fitted neither text (R2/C9).
  - **The rule.** There is no fourth kind. In an `async` body (method or lambda) whose return type is `Task<T>` for a class or interface T, a `return` whose operand is a borrow and not `return await` is a compile error at the return site, for a trivial-dispose class as for any other. The kinds are read off the operand's ownership state, not the class's disposal ceremony (K1.6).
  - **Why not a slot.** Kind 1 would have the task's teardown dispose an object it never owned, and kinds 2 and 3 chain through a *task*. The awaiter's borrow is sourced at the task location, so nothing would tie it to the object's owner.
  - **Remedies:** a fresh owned value (or a named owned binding, kind 1); `return await` an admitted task source; or a synchronous property. `null` under a nullable T stays admitted, and a runtime-managed operand (a `string`, a box under `Task<Object>`) is no borrow. §28.3's callee-side item 1 excludes `async` bodies, and §30.1's sentence excepts the `return await` chain (`T4`'s critique, C3).

  **Declined:** a fourth, borrow slot kind, since `Task<T>` announces no source set (K2.4) and no awaiter could bound it. Kernel: no contact (K1 + K2.4). **Compiler (tracked, [#5704](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5704)):** rejected already at a non-trivial-dispose class and at the builtin collection heads (#4285, #4311, #4463). Admitted at a trivial-dispose class, at an interface T and at `Object` by `isAsyncPatternAClassResultType`'s `isNonTrivialDisposeClass` gate (`src/ownership/Ownership.cpp:14395–14418`; `src/common/OwnershipFacts.cpp:240`), which this ruling removes. Two lit lines flip (above).

Meanwhile §9.7 read a value declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` as the span and kept a borrow-bearing record return type admissible at every member kind (R6/C6's `IReadOnlySpan` part).

A static method returning `xs.AsSpan()` over its parameter is rejected at the return.
  - The asymmetry with row 4's static class rejection is §9.7's own: a box of a value carries no disposal obligation, and its borrows are bounded per return expression.

### v0.332 changelog (v0.331 → v0.332)

**The borrow-flow matrix re-run, decided under the owner's delegation.** The borrow-flow matrix that v0.331 decided was re-run over the v0.331 text: the same nine kinds of value (rows R1–R9) and thirteen destinations (columns C1–C13), every deciding passage re-located and re-quoted, and every decided cell in R3–R8 attacked again with the new rules' edges (frozen sources, carried captured sources, static-source stores, `Task<T>` over a value type that holds borrows). Of the **117 cells**, 96 are decided and **21 are open** (17 ambiguous, 2 missing, 2 in conflict): 22 of v0.331's 32 open cells are confirmed decided, 10 stay open, and 11 cells v0.331 had decided were opened by the new text, eight of them by one root cause (#5688). The re-run also added **7 route cells** for the routes the first run had no cell for (the standard library's copying members, a span over a field slot's current value, a method-local collection of spans or frames, an iterator frame over a parameter-sourced span in an owned field, a field-slot span under a storage-bounded callback), all 7 missing. The open cells reduce to the questions v0.331 filed ([#5687](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5687)–[#5696](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5696), [#5706](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5706), [#5707](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5707)) and four the re-run filed ([#5708](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5708)–[#5711](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5711)). With the four questions v0.330 filed and left open ([#5666](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5666), [#5668](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5668), [#5670](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5670), [#5671](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5671)), these were every open spec issue: twenty. The cells, with their rules, notes, counterexamples and previous status, are published as [the borrow-flow matrix](https://claude.ai/artifact/2jv3zELseER5TmmUbFLoXx). On 2026-10-08 the owner directed: "Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them." This revision decides all twenty under that direction, each as a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`); each that removes a stated admission or adds a mechanism went through a proposal, which graduates here. The decisions:
- **Proposal [0152](proposals/0152-captured-binding-union-over-assignments.md)** (a captured binding is counted by every assignment to it): [#5688](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5688), twelve cells.
- **Proposal [0153](proposals/0153-span-reads-are-flag-checked.md)** (span reads are flag-checked): [#5707](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5707), with the four span routes it closes as rulings under it, [#5706](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5706), [#5691](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5691), [#5710](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5710) and [#5709](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5709), and the editorial fix [#5692](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5692).
- **Proposal [0154](proposals/0154-no-async-event-payload-that-holds-borrows.md)** (no `AsyncEventSource<T>` over a value type that holds borrows): [#5711](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5711).
- **Proposal [0155](proposals/0155-class-own-typed-equals.md)** (a class's own-typed `Equals`: the hash pairing, and `=` at a subclass operand): [#5668](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5668) and [#5670](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5670).
- **Rulings, no proposal:**
  - [#5687](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5687): a holds-borrows binding an `async` lambda captures is a local of its body under §30.1;
  - [#5690](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5690): a task minted by invoking an `async` lambda excepts a captured `CancellationToken`, as a frame does;

- **Span reads become flag-checked in checked mode, and K5.9 is withdrawn one revision after it landed.** A read or write through a buffer- or array-backed span, or through an `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` over one, is a member access on the backing `OwningBuffer<T>` or `Array<T>`, as the stdlib's declared indexer bodies already said. - **§28.3's closure bullet (provenance clauses 1 and 6), §27.5, §9.7 (the capture bullet), Appendix C.3, rationale §4, the code-generation reference §4.4 and §7.2 — a captured binding is counted by every assignment to it (design change, [proposal 0152](proposals/0152-captured-binding-union-over-assignments.md); [#5688](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5688); twelve cells, R2–R7 × C6/C7).** Provenance clause 1 read a captured binding's source at the closure's formation. But captures share one cell (§27.5), the local-scope bullet admits a same-block reassignment from a later-declared source, a slot store re-points a captured inline array, and an assignment in a lambda body is invisible to the enclosing flow analysis. So:
  - a stored closure over a `null`-initialized `Item?`, a null-source `Pair`, `[1]Item?` or `Ref.None` read a disposed `using var`;
  - a returned `a.Select(f)` over a reassigned captured span read a freed local array;
  - a stored closure over a capture-free `g` called a later capture-bearing one;
  - `g(); return s;` after `var g := lambda() => do s := zs.AsSpan(); end;` returned a freed window through the binding's own return.
  - **The rule.** A captured binding has one source set wherever it is read: the union over its initializer and every assignment to it in the declaring body and in every lambda body that captures it, compound assignments, stores into its own storage (an inline-array slot, a settable record member) and a `ref` or `out` location's post-call set included. It is read at the closure's formation, at the binding's own reads, at a frame's capture-set contribution and at §28.14's admission. Where the sets depend on one another through captures, they are the least sets that satisfy the clause. A binding no lambda captures keeps its reaching-assignment set.

  **Declined** (four `declined-at-proposal` rows): the status quo (A); a freeze on the captured binding after formation, inside every capturing lambda body (C), which keys a freeze on formation where K5 keys on liveness and bars re-pointing at a longer-lived source; rejecting in-lambda assignments with the union over the declaring body only (D), two rules where one serves; a flow-sensitive union cut at formation (E), three sets for one cell. The union's over-rejection is a family (an assignment counted against a read it cannot reach), measured at zero and remedied by a second binding. Kernel: derivation (K2.2 + K5.5). Body-locality: local. Measured reach: zero; the 152 reassigned captured bindings in `tests/` are counters, capture-free lambda locals, owned bindings or already-rejected rows. **Compiler (tracked, [#5718](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5718), probe first):** a frame's capture-set contribution is read at the lambda literal, and a reassigned lambda-typed local "contributes NOTHING (conservative admit)" (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:17330–17333`); `checkClosureEscapesOnReturn` (`:5150`) reads the captures' state at the literal.
- **§30.1 (*Borrow-bearing record locals across suspension*), Appendix C.6, K6.4, the code-generation reference §7.6 — a holds-borrows binding an `async` lambda captures is a local of its body (ruling; [#5687](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5687); R3/C9–R5/C9 and R6/C9's `async` leg).** §30.1 did not say whether an enclosing local captured by an `async` lambda and used after the lambda's own `await` is "a local" of that body.
  - **The rule.** It is, live there as §28.3's liveness reads a local, through a closure the body forms over it included. Its borrows are sourced in the enclosing scope, which the lambda's frame does not own, so it never meets the frame-resident condition, and a use of it after one of the body's own suspension points is rejected at the suspension point. A `CancellationToken` is exempt; an assignment to the binding is not a use. Read it before the first suspension, or copy borrow-free data out of it there (`var first := s[0];`). The minted task still carries the capture's sources (provenance clause 4).
  - K6.4's reason for leaving task locals untraced stays true, so proposal 0149 option D's reopening bar is not met.

Every other span member that reads or writes a slot (search, equality, the bulk members, the byte and bit accessors) reaches the slot the same way; the span's own components (`Start`, `Length`, `IsEmpty`, `Slice`) touch no storage. Their rejections are now a stipulation of regime uniformity, not a soundness ground, which the deferral records. Where a recorded trust clause carries such a value after a statically admitted step (a frame, a method-local collection, a span over a slot's current value), the clause's backstop reaches a span read as it reaches any member access.

### v0.333 changelog (v0.332 → v0.333)

**The borrow-flow matrix's third run, decided under the owner's delegation.** The borrow-flow matrix was run a third time, over the v0.332 text: the same nine kinds of value (rows R1–R9) and thirteen destinations (columns C1–C13), every deciding passage re-located and re-quoted, and every decided cell in R3–R8 attacked again at the edges of v0.332's new rules (the captured-binding union, flag-checked span reads, the value-copy store rule, terminal field moves, the class `Equals` pairing). Of the **117 cells**, **114 are decided** and **3 are open** (2 ambiguous, 1 in conflict): of the 21 cells the second run left open, which v0.332 decided, 20 are confirmed decided and R6/C9 stays open on its interface leg, and two cells the second run had decided were opened, R6/C4 by a route no earlier run tried and R6/C10 by the iterator face of the gap that keeps R6/C9 open. All **7 route cells** are decided. The three open cells reduce to two questions the run filed: R6/C4 is [#5726](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5726) (an `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` reaches `Object` through a covariant return slot or interface variance, with no conversion written), and R6/C9 and R6/C10 are [#5715](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5715) (§30.1's and §29.4's frame rules name value types that hold borrows, not a local declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>`). The run also filed [#5727](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5727), an editorial defect in §28.3's *Set-erasing positions*. With the four questions the v0.332 critics filed and left open ([#5713](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5713), [#5714](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5714), [#5716](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5716), [#5717](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5717)), these were every open spec issue: seven. The three runs are recorded, non-normatively, under [`research/borrow-flow-matrix/`](research/borrow-flow-matrix/README.md): every cell with its verdict, deciding text, note, counterexample and status change. Under the owner's 2026-10-08 direction ("Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them."), this revision decides all seven, each as a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`); each that removes a stated admission or chooses a design went through a proposal, which graduates here. After this train every cell of the matrix is decided, pending a fourth run. The decisions:
- **Proposal [0156](proposals/0156-span-interface-retyping-is-borrow-erasing.md)** (a retyping of `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` is a borrow-erasing conversion): [#5726](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5726), cells R6/C4 and R8/C4.
- **Proposal [0157](proposals/0157-report-a-transfer-of-a-collection-held-source.md)** (the trust-admission report names a transfer of a collection-held source): [#5713](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5713).
- **Proposal [0158](proposals/0158-equals-ambiguous-type-not-hashable.md)** (a type whose `Equals` is ambiguous at its own operands is not hashable): [#5716](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5716).
- **Rulings, no proposal:**
  - [#5715](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5715): a local, parameter or capture declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` is read as the span it boxes at §30.1's and §29.4's frame rules (cells R6/C9 and R6/C10);
  - [#5714](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5714): a store into a record value's own storage adds the stored value's sources and is checked at the holder.
- **Editorial and clarification:** [#5727](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5727) (§28.3's set-erasing field sentence names the `Object` substitution) and [#5717](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5717) (the standard library's value-copy members are registered and marked where they are declared).

Four lanes:
- `V1`: proposal 0156 and #5727.
- `V2`: #5715 and #5714, with one editorial fix of its own (§28.3's property-store verdict names a borrow-bearing inline array).
- `V3`: proposal 0157 and #5717.
- `V4`: proposal 0158.

Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique, which applied **22 fixes**: `V1` 3, `V2` 6 (two further findings were informational and left as they stood), `V3` 6 and `V4` 7. The 81 edits (`V1` 15, `V2` 16, `V3` 34, `V4` 16) were applied as one sequence, and all 24 lane orders apply clean. A composition check added 11: 2 in the spec, and 9 in the proposals folder and the decline index (three of them correcting proposal 0157's citation of the code-generation reference).

The critics' substantive findings were these:
- `V1`:
  - **A run-time type test reopened R6/C4 one hop later.** 0156 keeps the conversion of a constructed type as a whole (`var o: Object := xs;` over `xs: IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlySpan<int>>`), and §12.7 answers `is` and `as` by conformance with §12.9's variance, so `o as IReadOnlyList<Object>` handed the spans out at `Object` with no conversion written. A run-time type test now does not succeed through such a variance (§12.9, §9.7).
  - §12.9's sentence keyed on a span type argument "in the source", which missed the likeliest route, a method-local `Array<IReadOnlySpan<int>>` converted to `IReadOnlyList<Object>`, and a class implementing `ISink<Object>`. The source is now read at its instantiation of the target's interface.
  - A dispatched generic method converting `IEnumerable<T>` to `IEnumerable<Object>` under `where T: class` is newly rejected at its body (`class` admits interfaces, so it never establishes "not `IReadOnlySpan<…>`"); it was missing from the Migration list.
- `V2`:
  - **§28.3's field-store bullet read literally against #5714's admission.** Its clause 1 ("a borrowed local may not be assigned to any field") would reject the issue's own same-block program, so the ruling would have read as relaxing a stated rejection. §9.7's sentence now says a member store is not a store into a field of an object: a record value is not an object, and the holder's rule bounds it, as at an inline-array slot.
  - The holder of `o.B.Item := e` with `o` a class local is `o`'s field `B`, not the chain's root; a `ref p.Item` argument and a compound assignment are member stores too. Appendix C.6's capture clause still read "such a type" as value types only. The code-generation reference's pair said "a block enclosing a source's", which rejected the admitted program; it now says "strictly encloses".
- `V3`:
  - The lane had left open a collection moved to a wider binding after a body-sourced store (`outer := move coll;`). The text decides it: §28.11's "provably outlives" list is read over the collection's fate in the body, as §9.7's `var ys := xs.ToArray(); return ys;` is, so the store is rejected. Proposal 0157's ground for not tracking retention was rewritten accordingly: retention is not body-local, since a callee handed the collection may `Remove` or `Clear` it.
  - The register's value-copy census missed `Parallel.Map`'s value- and frozen-element forms and `LinkedList<T>`'s `Add*` members (both now listed as not value-copy, with the reason), and its declaration count was 27, not 28.
- `V4`:
  - **§8.3 contradicted the new clause.** Its pairing paragraph said `=`, a comparer-less `Set<C>` and every use through a type parameter at `C` compare by an own-typed `Equals` declared "at `C` or `C?`", while clause (d) makes the `C?` form not hashable. §8.3 now says those uses are §22.6's ambiguity at `C?`, the obligation unchanged.
  - The remedy "declare equality on the element type" in the §14.2 register row and stdlib §4 does not exist at a `Point3`, which §12.2 forbids declaring `Equals(Point3)`; both now name the collection formed at the base. §9.2's diagnostic remedy was wrong for two of clause (d)'s three shapes and now names the candidates.
  - The ground that reading 1 "compares by `Equals(Point)` and hashes by the override" was dropped: such a `Point3` already breaks §8.3's hash rule, and the adopted `Set<Point>` remedy has the same mix. A re-scan found two `C?`-declared own-typed `Equals` sites, not one; neither flips.

**Outcomes the owner should see.**
- **`Set<Point3>` is rejected, against the issue's recommendation.** #5716 recommended that a comparer-less `Set<Point3>`, `Point3` deriving from a `Point` that declares `Equals(other: Point)`, compare by `Equals(Point)`. That is the ranking v0.330 declined and v0.332 declined again for `=`, relocated to §9.2, so 0158 takes the issue's other reading: `x.Equals(y)` at two `Point3`s is already §22.6's ambiguity, §12.2 already counts a use through a type parameter among such calls, and the type is now not hashable. `Set<Point3>`, `Dictionary<Point3, V>`, `where T: hashable` at `Point3`, an equality search over `Point3` elements and `=` through a type parameter at `Point3` are compile errors; form the collection at `Point` (it holds `Point3` values and compares by `Equals(Point)`) or pass a comparer. Measured reach: zero. The compiler counts every class hashable today and compares by the nearest `Equals` up the chain ([#5736](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5736)).
- **A type test changes its answer.** Under 0156, `o is IReadOnlyList<Object>` over an `Object` holding an `Array<IReadOnlySpan<int>>` is `false`, and `as` is `null`, where §12.9's variance made it succeed. It is the revision's one run-time change; measured reach zero.
- **The variance and function-type retypings of a span are compile errors.** `var v: IReadOnlyList<Object> := spans;`, `var up: (IReadOnlySpan<int>) -> Object := id;`, an `(Object) -> ()` value at an `(IReadOnlySpan<int>) -> ()` slot, and a method reference over a callee declaring `Object` at a span slot are rejected where written, with the direct conversion's diagnostic. Measured reach: zero. Since proposal 0153 the escape faulted at run time in checked mode; the rule restores the static posture.
- **An `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` local no longer crosses an `await` or a `yield return` on a caller-side source.** `var s: IReadOnlySpan<int> := xs.AsSpan(); await Task.Delay(10); return s[0];` over a plain parameter `xs` is rejected, as its `ArraySpan<int>` spelling always was; §9.7 already read the interface this way, and #5715 states it at the frame rules. Measured reach: zero.
- **A store into a record member is checked at the record's holder.** `var p := new Box(); using var it := new Item(); p.Item := it;` is admitted (the source is in `p`'s own block), and the same store with `p` declared outside `it`'s block is rejected at the store. The compiler today classifies every member store as a field store, so it probably rejects the admitted form (HYPOTHESIS, probe first, [#5734](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5734)).
- **Every new rejection in this revision is ahead of the compiler.** Five trackers are filed and six existing issues get notes (Migration, below).

A composition check over the union then fixed three seams:
- **0156 × #5715 (spec §9.7's interface paragraph).** `V2` widened the reading of a value declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` to every frame rule (§3.6's row, §30.1, §29.4, Appendix C.6); `V1` made a retyping that carries one to `Object` the borrow-erasing conversion. The paragraph's hub sentence, "a value that holds borrows reaches no other reference-typed position", is the sentence #5726 showed false by retyping, and it is where a reader of either rule starts. It now says "by a conversion or by a retyping that converts no value" and cites §12.9 and §27.1.1 beside §8.6. `V1` does not edit §3.6's row, so `V2`'s wording there stands alone: the retyping rule keys on the interface type, not on the holds-borrows property the row defines.
- **#5714 × Appendix C.3.** The ruling adds a compiler-enforced rule at §9.7's first bullet, and C.3 already carries its captured twin (proposal 0152's row counts "a record member" store). `V2` drafted no C row. C.3 now carries one beside the captured row: a record value held at a named location has one source set, a member store adds to it and is checked at the holder.
- **Proposal 0157's citation of the code-generation reference.** `V3`'s proposal and README row cited the report sentence it restates as the reference's "§5"; it is in §4.6 (*The diagnostics you will actually hit*), §5 being the standard-library index. Corrected in three places in the proposal and in the README row.

The other places two lanes touch read together unchanged:
- **0156 × #5715 at a substitution.** §30.1's parameter and result rule now names a type "declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>`, or substituted with it", and 0156's generic-body paragraph rejects a variant retyping at an instantiation substituting `IReadOnlySpan<…>`. Both are §3.6 rule 2's per-instantiation reading of the one interface reading §9.7 states.
- **0157 × #5715 and 0156.** The report's new transfer entry reaches an element that is "a value that holds such a borrow", which §9.7 reads to include an element declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>`; 0156 rejects only retypings of a collection of spans, not its stores.
- **0157 × #5714.** A member store into a record held in a collection slot is already a compile error (§23.5), so the holder rule and the report's collection entry never meet one store.
- **0158 × #5717 (stdlib §4).** `V3`'s register paragraph, *Value-copy members are stores*, lands just before `V4`'s edited *Equality search* paragraph; neither reads the other.
- **0158 × 0155.** §8.3's pairing obligation still holds at an own-typed `Equals` declared at `C?`: a call with a `C?`-typed argument selects it.
- **Appendix C.** C.1 carries 0156's two clauses (the generic-body variance and the retyping as the borrow-erasing conversion) and 0158's hashable sentence. C.3 carries the composition's #5714 row. C.6 carries #5715's two rows.
- **The code-generation reference.** Every new rule has a row or a *Looks right, is rejected* pair, with no pin in prose: 0156 a §7.3 pair; #5714 a §7.3 pair (placed after the move-only field callout, so 0156's pair follows the `Object`-boxing callout it extends); #5715 a §7.6 pair; 0157 the §4.6 report sentence, restated in place; #5717 the §7.2 note, which names the marks; 0158 two lines in each half of the §7.4 pair. #5727 needs none.
- **`scripts/check_docs.sh`** passes on the composed tree with this entry, the four version headers and the code-generation reference's three pin lines at v0.333: ANCHOR, VERSION, PIN, FENCE, FACTS, TABLE, SETS, REGISTER, STYLE and EXTRACT are clean (525 fragments, as at v0.332). The one CITATION advisory, `§4.12`, was already present at v0.332. `scripts/check_proposals.sh` passes (158 ↔ 158; live 48, graduated 110). `corpus.py lint --strict` is clean (2,315 cases), and `corpus.py check` finds the manifest up to date.

- **§9.7 (the borrow-erasing bullet and the interface paragraph), §8.6, §12.9, §27.1.1, §27.6, Appendix C.1; stdlib §4.16; rationale §4.2; the code-generation reference §7.3 — a retyping that carries an `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` value to `Object` or another interface is the borrow-erasing conversion (design change, [proposal 0156](proposals/0156-span-interface-retyping-is-borrow-erasing.md); [#5726](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5726); R6/C4 and R8/C4).** `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` is the one reference type read as holding a span's borrows, but it is an interface, so the language's identity-preserving retypings reached it. No span value is converted on any of these routes, so §9.7's borrow-erasing bullet had no site to fire at, against its own "reaches no other reference-typed position" and §8.6's "exactly two positions":
  - §27.1.1's covariant return slot turned a capture-free `(IReadOnlySpan<int>) -> IReadOnlySpan<int>` into a `(IReadOnlySpan<int>) -> Object`, and the invocation's `Object` result, sourced at a plain parameter, went into an `Object?` field under the field-store residual;
  - §12.9's variance did the same through `IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlySpan<int>>` to `IReadOnlyList<Object>`;
  - the contravariant faces (an `(Object) -> ()` value at a span slot, a user `ISink<in T>`) and a method reference formed over a callee declaring `Object` at a span slot carried the span into a parameter declared `Object`.
  - **The rule.** Each such retyping is the borrow-erasing conversion, a compile error where it is written, with the direct conversion's diagnostic and remedy: a covariant type argument or return slot that is the span type in the source and not in the target, a contravariant one that is the span type in the target and not in the source, composed positions included, the source read at its instantiation of the target's interface (so a local `Array<IReadOnlySpan<int>>` and a class implementing `ISink<Object>` are reached). A lambda literal's written parameter type and return-type ascription are named among the retypings. Converting the constructed type as a whole stays admitted (`IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlySpan<int>>` to `Object` converts the list reference), and a run-time type test does not succeed through such a variance, so that conversion cannot be narrowed back to reach it.
  - **In a generic body** (R8/C4), a variant conversion over a type parameter (`IReadOnlyList<T>` to `IReadOnlyList<Object>`), which §12.9 left unstated, is checked under §28.1's class-or-interface assumption, and its two conditions (a reference type; not `IReadOnlySpan<…>`) are requirements read at each instantiation (§3.6 rule 2). It is rejected where the substitution is a value type or `IReadOnlySpan<…>` and stands elsewhere; a function-type substitution is not re-checked. §27.1.1's slot conditions over a type parameter are read the same way, and a dispatched generic method decides the requirement at its body (§14.2). This also closes the unstated value-type route of R3/C4–R5/C4 (`IReadOnlyList<T>` at `T = Pair`).
  - It is a rejected conversion, not a missing type relation, so overload resolution treats it exactly as the direct conversion: at `M(IReadOnlyList<Object>)` beside `M(Object)`, a list of spans selects the variance overload and draws §9.7's diagnostic rather than silently selecting `M(Object)`.

It now names a function type or `Object`, nullable or not, with `b: Box<Object>` and a class deriving from `Box<Object>` as examples. No verdict moves; #5708's corpus case is already recorded.
- **§30.1 (the parameter and result rule; *Borrow-bearing record locals across suspension*, with #5687's capture sentence), §29.4, §3.6's holds-borrows row, Appendix C.6, the code-generation reference §7.6 — a local, parameter or capture declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` is read as the span it boxes at the frame rules (ruling; [#5715](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5715); R6/C9 and R6/C10, with R8/C9's and R8/C10's interface legs).** §9.7 reads a value declared at that interface as the span it boxes under "every rule of this specification" that reads a value that holds borrows, and names §30.1's frame rules among the positions where such a value is stored past its bound at no position. But §30.1's three rules and §29.4's iterator rule listed only value types, and §3.6's row read the interface "under" §9.7's obligations alone. So `var s: IReadOnlySpan<int> := xs.AsSpan(); await Task.Delay(10); return s[0];` over a plain parameter `xs` read as an interface-typed borrow held to settlement, and a synchronous iterator kept such a local across `yield return`, although the `ArraySpan<int>` spelling of each is rejected.
  - **The rule.** Each of those rules names the interface. A local declared `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` crosses a suspension point (`await`, `await using`, `await for`, or a `yield return` in an async or synchronous iterator) only where every borrow it carries has a frame-resident source: an owned local, a `using var`/`await using var`, or an `owned` parameter of the same body. An enclosing local or parameter so declared that an `async` lambda captures is #5687's local of the lambda's body. An `async` parameter, result or element type declared at the interface, or substituted with it, is rejected as a span is. §29.4 now names every value type that holds borrows, as §30.1 already did for synchronous iterators. Read the value before the suspension (`var first := s[0];`) or re-derive the view after it.
  - The universal sentence in §9.7 already decided the case (corpus `s9_7_0030` expects the `async`-parameter face rejected, and v0.329's 0146 corpus list names `async method F(s: IReadOnlySpan<int>)` among the rejects), so this is a ruling that makes the enumerations agree with it.
