Kernel: derivation (K2.1 + K6.1). Body-locality: local. Measured reach: zero; the only program in `tests/` with an `IReadOnlySpan` in an `async` or iterator body is `s9_7_0030`, which already expects a reject. **Compiler (tracked, [#5733](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5733)):** the across-suspension walk registers a candidate by `isBorrowBearingRecordOrSpan` (`src/ownership/Ownership_Checks.cpp:20114`, `:20200`; the `yield return` arm at `:20213`ff is the same walk), which names the four span records and user records but not the interface (`src/common/OwnershipFacts.cpp:1757–1771`, beside `isIReadOnlySpanType` at `:1788`); the `async` parameter check uses the same predicate (`Ownership_Checks.cpp:18920`, noted on [#5659](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5659)).
- **§9.7 (the first bullet), Appendix C.3, the code-generation reference §7.3 — a store into a record value's own storage adds the stored value's sources and is checked at the holder (ruling; [#5714](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5714); R3/C1–C3, R4/C1, R3/C6, R3/C9, R3/C10, and the adjacency notes of R2/C11 and R3/C11).** §15.1.2 stated the slot-store rule for an inline array, and proposal 0152 counted a store into a captured record's settable member "as a slot store does". No sentence said what `p.Item := it` does to an uncaptured record local's set, whether the store itself is scope-checked, or which rule a store at depth (`a[0].Item := it`) takes.
  - **The rule.** A record value held at a named location (a local or parameter, a field, an inline-array slot) has one source set, as an inline array has. A whole-value assignment replaces it. A **member store** (`p.Item := e`, `p.Slots[i] := e`, a compound assignment by its desugaring, a `ref` or `out` argument through such a chain) adds the sources of the borrows `e` carries, never removing one, and is checked as an assignment of the updated value to the location that holds it: the chain's root, or the field a class- or interface-typed hop reaches (`o.B.Item := e` is checked at `o`'s field `B`). A local or parameter takes the local-scope bullet; a class instance or static field admits the value only in the null-source form; a `ref` or `out` parameter is caller storage; an inline-array slot is §15.1.2's slot store into that array (`a[0].Item := e` adds to `a`'s one set). A member store is not a store into a field of an object under §28.3's field-store bullet, and a store beyond a class- or interface-typed hop inside the value (`p.Obj.X := e`) is that object's store. A captured binding counts the same store in its union (0152), so the captured and uncaptured readings now agree.
  - So `var p := new Box(); using var it := new Item(); p.Item := it; return p.Item!.N();` is admitted; `do using var it := new Item(); p.Item := it; end` with `p` declared outside is rejected at the store; and `p.Item := it; return p;`, `_b := p;` and `p.Item := param;` with `p` used after an `await` are rejected by the return bullet, the instance-field bullet and §30.1, reading the set.

  **Declined** (one `rejected` row): per-member source sets, under which a store replaces what the overwritten member carried, a new mechanism §15.1.2 declined for slots ("a slot store narrows no slot", recorded liftable) that would split the captured and uncaptured readings of one store. Kernel: derivation (K2.2's union at a store; K2.1 and K2.3 at the holder). Body-locality: local. Measured reach: zero; a type-aware sweep of `tests/` and the documents finds one member store through a record with a settable reference-typed member, `r.Val := 2`, an `int`. **Compiler (tracked, [#5734](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5734), probe first):** every member-target assignment is a field store (`Ownership_Checks.cpp:9562–9567`), so the admitted program is probably rejected as "stored into a field"; the across-suspension walk re-derives a candidate's residency only at an identifier target (`:20142`), so `p.Item := param` followed by an `await` and a use of `p` is admitted; the instance-field type leg runs only under `storeTargetIsClassField` (`:15305–15327`), so `_b.Item := param` on a field-held record is admitted.

They now say "record, choice or inline-array value". No verdict changes.
- **§28.3 *The trust-admission report*, §28.11 *Storing a borrow*; rationale §5.31; the code-generation reference §4.6 — the report names a transfer of a collection-held source (design change, [proposal 0157](proposals/0157-report-a-transfer-of-a-collection-held-source.md); [#5713](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5713)).** The report named a collection store only for a parameter-, receiver- or field-path-sourced borrow, while §28.11's collection-held clause reaches every admitted element. `coll.Add(item); sink.Take(move item);` over locals, and the span twin v0.332 made explicit, `coll.Add(xs.AsSpan()); sink.Take(move xs);`, carried the clause with no report line, so "a compilation unit that emits no report … carries no recorded trust clause" was false (for the class form since v0.307).
  - **The rule.** The register gains a transfer entry: an obligation-moving kill that sets no flag (the consume table's rows K3.1–K3.4, K3.6, K3.7 and K3.12) of an owned binding, a local or an `owned` parameter, where an admitted store has placed into a collection slot or an `OwningDictionary<K, V>` key slot an element that carries a borrow of it (directly, in a value that holds borrows, or in an iterator, enumerator or lazy-query frame), on a path from the store (anywhere in the body, for a store in a lambda body). It is reported at the transfer. The claim's exclusions name both flag-backstopped kills, the site-announced kills (K4.2) and a reassignment's drop-on-overwrite (K3.11). §28.11 says which site the report names for each source kind.
  - The entry speaks at the transfer, not the store: most body-sourced stores never meet a transfer, so a store-site entry would list every local collection a program builds. It does not ask whether the collection still holds the element at the transfer, since retention is not body-local; a line over an emptied collection is an over-report the audit can dismiss.

At two operands of a `Point3` deriving from `Point`, that call is §22.6's ambiguity, and §12.2 counts a use through a type parameter among such calls. But §3.6 counted every class hashable, so a comparer-less `Set<Point3>` was admitted with no member to compare by, and §9.2's closing sentence ("every **hashable** S … has a member for all three kinds") was false there.
  - **The rule.** A class or interface type at which `a.Equals(b)` over two operands of that type is §22.6's ambiguity has no member for §9.2's first kind and is not hashable: a class deriving from one that declares `Equals(other: Point)`, a class whose own `Equals` is declared at `C?`, and a class declaring `Equals(I)` for an interface it implements. `Set<Point3>`, `Dictionary<Point3, V>`, `OwningSet<Point3>`, `where T: hashable` at `Point3`, the stdlib equality search over `Point3` elements and `=` through a type parameter at `Point3` are rejected at their sites; §9.2's diagnostic names the candidates in place of a missing member. The second kind (`Equals(Object?)`) and `GetHashCode` are untouched, and §8.3's pairing obligation still holds at a `C?`-declared member, which a call with a `C?`-typed argument selects.
  - **The remedies.** Form the collection at `Point`, which holds `Point3` values and compares by `Equals(Point)`, or pass a comparer, in which the author binds the comparison at `Point` or at `Object?`. `Point3` cannot declare `Equals(Point3)`: §12.2 keeps the name blocked across the boundary.

### v0.334 changelog (v0.333 → v0.334)

**Three matrices and two simplification reviews, decided under the owner's delegation.** Three completeness matrices ran against v0.333, each filling every cell with its deciding text, a verdict and, where the text did not decide, a counterexample of at most 25 lines. The **borrow-flow matrix's fourth run** (nine kinds of value × thirteen destinations) left **2 of 117 cells** open (R3/C4 and R6/C4) and **2 of 10 route cells** (R6/C3·equality and R2–R6/C11·loopvar), all four on the equality search's first kind, a generic `as T` over a span and a span loop's iteration variable. The **disposal matrix's first run** (ten kinds of obligation holder × fourteen disposal paths) left **51 of 140 cells** and **6 of 16 route cells** open, and the **generics matrix's first run** (ten kinds of type argument × fourteen generic constructs) **61 of 140 cells** and **13 of 13 route cells**. A consolidation pass merged every open cell, across the three, into **55 root causes**: 47 filed as new issues ([#5744](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5744)–[#5790](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5790)) and 8 already open (the borrow-flow run's [#5739](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5739)–[#5742](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5742) and the four questions v0.333 filed, [#5728](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5728)–[#5731](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5731)); they were every open spec issue. The runs are recorded, non-normatively, under [`research/borrow-flow-matrix/`](research/borrow-flow-matrix/README.md), [`research/disposal-matrix/`](research/disposal-matrix/README.md) and [`research/generics-matrix/`](research/generics-matrix/README.md). Two simplification reviews ran beside them: one over the open findings, asking which could be closed by narrowing a feature rather than adding a rule, with each candidate's reach measured; and a retrospective over the fixes landed v0.316–v0.333, asking which rules those fixes had multiplied. Under the owner's 2026-10-08 direction ("Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them.") and the 2026-10-09 additions ("Please also resolve all findings autonomously"; "Simplifications look good so far"), this revision decides all 55, each as a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`), and lands three of the retrospective's consolidations. The owner's standing preference decided the close calls: **narrow a feature when its measured reach is negligible, rather than add another rule; where real code uses the feature, keep it and fix the rule.** Each decision that removes a stated admission or chooses a design went through a proposal, eleven in all, and each graduates here. The one decision the owner reserved to the critique was the holds-borrows posture ("Draft both, critic decides"): the retrospective proposed retiring the storage bans on a value that holds borrows, so that such a value is a borrow under the residual-trust regime a class borrow has; the critique kept the bans and closed the two routes by declaration, **soundness first**. Retiring them trades a compile-time guarantee for a checked-mode fault, undefined in an unchecked build, at every field, `async`, task-result and `Object` position, for programs nobody measured a need for, and `DECLINED.md`'s bar for that retirement (a measured program the source-field remedy cannot express) is still unmet; the kept form costs about 400 words, its three rules reach zero sites, and a route the enumeration may still leave is at worst the retirement's posture at that one position. The decisions:
- **Proposal [0159](proposals/0159-holds-borrows-posture.md)** (the holds-borrows posture, option (b)): [#5739](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5739), [#5740](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5740); borrow-flow R3/C4, R6/C4, route R6/C3·equality; generics R4/C12·eqsearch, R2/C6.
- **Proposal [0160](proposals/0160-class-own-typed-equals-is-the-object-slot.md)** (a class's own-typed `Equals` is the `Object` slot): the retrospective's R8, with [#5755](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5755) and [#5731](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5731).
- **Proposal [0161](proposals/0161-constraint-table-narrowings.md)** (no `Object` bound, no hashable function type, the owning family's element rule): [#5748](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5748), [#5756](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5756) part 3, [#5749](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5749).
- **Proposal [0162](proposals/0162-explicit-disposal-marks-the-holder-frees.md)** (explicit disposal marks, the holder frees; static owned storage disposed only at exit): [#5759](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5759), [#5758](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5758), [#5760](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5760), [#5785](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5785), [#5782](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5782).

Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique, which applied **57 fixes**: `W1` 7, `W2` 6, `W3` 8, `W4` 10, `W5` 8, `W6` 5, `W7` 6 and `W8` 7. Two critiques reversed a lane decision, both back to the issue's own recommendation: `W3`'s on the in-flight `DisposeAsync` window (#5758) and `W6`'s on `default(T)` (#5751). The 337 drafted edits (`W1` 34, `W2` 47, `W3` 62, `W4` 43, `W5` 43, `W6` 41, `W7` 27, `W8` 40) were applied as one sequence in the order `W4`, `W3`, `W8`, `W1`, `W2`, `W5`, `W6`, `W7`; the composition step dropped one of them and adjusted eight, and added 26 of its own: 2 in the spec (§28.2 and §9.4), 2 carrying a critique's remedy correction into Guide 05 and the code-generation reference, 6 settling the proposals' composition notes, 11 graduation status lines, and 5 in the proposals folder's two indexes. The rule corpus took 18 case edits (below).

The critics' substantive findings were these:
- `W1`:
  - **The generic-record face of #5739 stayed open.** The draft rejected `Equals(Object?)` on "a record that holds borrows", but a generic record is classified per instantiation, so `record Box<T>(V: T)` with a storing `override Equals(other: Object?)` was admitted at its declaration and `Array<Box<Item>>.Contains(new Box<Item>(it))` handed it a boxed `Box<Item>` borrowing `it`. The rule now reads at each instantiation at which the record holds borrows (`Box<Item>` rejected wherever named).
  - **The interface closure missed indirect implementation:** a user interface may extend `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` and a class implement that. The closure now names user interfaces.
  - The lane had rewritten three remedies reading "a class implementing the interface" as if they named the span interface; they name the target interface, and stand.
- `W2`:
  - **What the slot is to overload resolution was undefined,** and §3.6's residual clause (d) depends on it. §8.3 now says: to §22.6 the member is one candidate, applicable at every argument and an exact match at the parameter type of its nearest declaration in the receiver's chain (`Object?` where that is `Object`'s own or is spelled at `Object?`).
  - **§14.4 over-admitted at a general interface bound:** `OwningTask<T?>` is admitted exactly where `OwningArray<T>` is, under a constraint set that guarantees `class`; a record may implement `IShape`.
  - The precedent was misstated in four texts: an enum or a choice *rejects* the `Object?` spelling. The precedent is the own-typed member filling the slot.
- `W3`:
  - **The in-flight window rule could not be implemented as drafted.** The draft faulted an alias's access from the beginning of a direct `DisposeAsync()` while exempting the disposal's own accesses, but §28.2's checked test is a flag test on member entry and cannot tell the two callers apart. The flag now records two moments: the beginning drives idempotence; the completion is what checked mode faults on, and an alias's access inside the window is §28.2's program error on an intact block (the issue's recommendation).
  - `await using`'s completing `Dispose()` would have been a no-op under "a second call after either has begun"; it is now that disposal's own step. "Reclaims nothing" became "does not reclaim its receiver" (the cascade reclaims the owned fields). The holder list names the runtime's own holders (a `Shared<T>` value's last handle, an exception after its catch arm, a killed frame). The deferred release neither awaits nor blocks.
  - The `static owned readonly OwningArray<T>` idiom recommended a per-slot `move` with restoration, the same per-method window over static-reachable storage K9.4's ground rejects; the idiom is now the indexer store.
- `W4`:
  - **The straight-line window rejected most disposal-restored slot moves.** With the collection's disposal counted as a restoration and everything from the move to it straight-line, every program taking a slot of a body-local collection and using the element with any throwable before the collection died was rejected, about 170 gtest sites and the lane's own rewrites among them. A slot of a heap collection held by an owned local of the body, disposed rather than moved on every path, now keeps today's window.
  - **An unmeasured flip:** the compiler admits a throwable in a `try` whose `catch` arm restores the field (#3241 R2), and the window rejects it. One gtest row flips; the text names `catch` beside `finally`.
  - The #5750 sentence read over every earlier argument and would have rejected `d.Add(item.Id, move item)`; it is scoped to a borrow of the consumed binding. #5781's text said the call "completes by the exception", but a handler in the callee can catch it.
- `W5`:
  - **0165's depth bound left the narrowing route open:** `var reg := o as ((T) -> ()) -> ();` in a generic body reached a capture-free static function that invokes the body's inner lambda with a closure over its own `using var`. The bound now covers every type a generic declaration's bodies write.
  - **0165's value rule let a lambda's `return` through** (a selector building `(T) -> ()` values, an `async lambda`'s result); the rule now bars a `return`, a lambda's included. The draft's declaration-site ban on exported `(T) -> …` slots closed nothing the value rule does not, cost two lit programs and the callback-field idiom, and was dropped.
  - The extension-block desugaring would have made an explicit list count the block's parameters (`xs.OfType<int>()` needing two arguments); the block's parameters are bound by the receiver or qualifier, never by a list. #5764's assembly check now carries the edges of internal implementations of dispatched generic methods.
- `W6`:
  - **#5751's reading C′ reversed to reading A** on re-measurement: C′ (`null` at a reference substitution, typed `T?`) is sound only by rejecting `T?`-to-`T` flows, which rejects thirteen programs that zero-initialize through `T`, two of them lit acceptance pins; reading A flips four, each an instantiation of a `default(T)` body at a non-defaultable type.
  - 0166's copy demand listed an unmarked field read as a consumable operand; a storage read lends, and is now among the borrowed operands rejected at the instantiation.
  - One unedited passage stated the old trivial-dispose list (§28.9's API-surface paragraph); the 4803 test flips its needle rather than gaining a second ground.
- `W7`:
  - **0167 left a parameter with no holder** when the iterable's right was spent by a transfer to a query or callee that never enumerated it; the iterable now disposes the parameters wherever no enumerator was produced.
  - **0168 left a re-raised instance with no frame binding** (a synchronous helper reading `.Result`) whose capture would end the deferral while the faulted task still carried the instance; such an operand keeps its in-flight deferral until the faulted task's teardown.
  - **0168 composed unsoundly with 0162:** 0162 reclaims every class instance at its holder's release point, deferring only for a direct `DisposeAsync()`'s receiver, so an unsettled `using var t` would be reclaimed at scope end while its frame still wrote into it. 0168 now keeps the disposed task's block live until its terminal state.
- `W8`:
  - **The announcement-erasing definition narrowed.** "Every other position is announcement-erasing" closed the positive list proposal 0126 declined, reaching a lambda's `return`, the receiver of a member `Object` declares and an `if` arm. The definition is now the union of the two site lists, and a position on neither is not announcement-erasing.
  - Two statements whose only home was the register were restored: a span view's indexer-set writes the buffer it views, and the single-element stores list.

**Outcomes the owner should see.**
- **The holds-borrows bans stay; the critique chose option (b) over the retrospective's R5.** See the lead paragraph. Nothing is newly rejected or admitted in tests, the documents or either corpus.
- **v0.333's `Set<Point3>` rejection is withdrawn.** Proposal 0160 makes a class's own-typed `Equals` the implementation of `Object`'s `Equals` slot, as an enum's and a choice's already were, so `p = d` at a subclass operand, `Set<Point3>` and the equality search at `Point3` compile again and compare by dispatch. It also fixes the one wrong answer v0.333 kept: a `Set<Point>` holding `Point3` values compared them by the base's non-virtual member against the subclass's override. Proposal 0158's clause (d) shrinks to the `Equals(other: I)` shape. Measured reach: zero sites move; the compiler already compares by the nearest own-typed member.
- **Two subtractions, each reviewed under process §10.** §22.12 **form (iv)**, the mutable static owning-inline-array field, is retired (2 gtest programs, 2 lit files and 3 rule cases, all the form's own tests; rewrite: `static readonly` for a fixed pool). An explicit `Dispose()` of a **`static owned` field** is no longer admitted (zero sites).
- **v0.332's `finally`-placed restoration is withdrawn.** A restoration window admits no call, `await` or `yield return`; neither a `finally` nor a `catch` arm covers one. Its users were two rule cases written to exercise it (rewritten here) and one gtest row the compiler admits through a `catch` arm.
- **A re-iterable iterator with an `owned` parameter becomes single-consumption.** Five gtest programs that enumerate one bound result twice flip to rejected; 87 such iterators keep compiling.
- **`default(T)` at a reference substitution is now rejected.** The ruling on #5751 reads §17.11's closing sentence as written: `Make<Widget>()` over `return default(T);` is a compile error, and `default(T?)` is the spelling for absence. Four test programs flip.
- **Reassigning a maybe-consumed owned local is admitted.** The compiler's narrow #3967 rejection becomes an over-rejection: nine gtest rows flip to accept once the per-path drop flag lands.
- **A method reference over a generic method names its type arguments** (`xs.Select(Util.Id<int>)`), and `Environment.Exit` unwinds nothing.
- **Every new rejection is ahead of the compiler.** 29 trackers are filed and ten existing issues get notes (Migration, below).

The composition step resolved these seams:
- **Form (iv) is retired by 0162, and 0163 had argued for its window.** `W4`'s clause in §22.12's form-(iv) paragraph ("a window on a static slot is admissible …") is dropped: its anchor was inside the paragraph `W3` deletes, and with no static slot movable (K9.4) it has no subject. The form-(iv) item and the *Statics:* sentence are struck from *The vacated location*, and the K9.4-statics clause from the rationale's decline. Proposal 0163's composition notes record each.
- **§28.10's "every exit path" sentence.** `W4`'s return-slot sentence and `W3`'s process-termination parenthetical extend it; the merged text carries the parenthetical, then the return-slot sentence, then the existing bold lead.
- **§7.10.** `W5`'s *The copy demand.* paragraph and `W6`'s *Move-only substitutions and the copy demand* stated the same scope. `W6`'s paragraph now follows `W5`'s directly and opens "At a move-only substitution …", leaving the scope to `W5`'s.
- **0162 × 0168 at §28.2.** *The compiler-inserted free* names the second deferral beside the direct `DisposeAsync()` one: a `Task`-family value disposed before it settles stays live until its terminal state, the continuation's disposals first.
- **§9.4 × *The vacated location*.** §9.4's sentence on a read of a vacated field through an alias now points at §28.8.1's paragraph, which generalizes it (`W4`'s question 2).
- **0167's remedy in the guide and the reference.** `W7`'s critique restricted the re-enumeration remedy to a class-typed resource (a move-only argument cannot be lent: plain passing moves it) in the spec only; Guide 05's new bullet and the reference's §7.5 note now say "a class-typed resource" too.
- **The proposals folder.** Four `DECLINED.md` insertions anchored on a group heading opened a blank line inside the table; fixed in the sequence. `W8`'s three rows had landed in the `retired` group and move to `declined-at-proposal`. The README rows 0159–0169 move to *Graduated*, in number order.

The other places two lanes touch read together unchanged:
- **§9.2's record spelling (`W1` × `W2`).** `W1`'s rule (a record that holds borrows declares no `Equals(Object?)`) sits in the record clause; `W2`'s slot rule is about classes and edits no record text. A record is now the one kind whose own-typed `Equals` does not fill the slot (filed below).
- **Stdlib §4's equality search (`W1` × `W2`).** `W1`'s sentence (the search never boxes a value that holds borrows) precedes the remedy sentence, whose 0158 parenthetical `W2` deletes.
- **Stdlib §4.14 (`W1` × `W6`).** `W1` rewrites the span iteration sentence (a copy of the slot's value), `W6` the one-argument constructor's condition; disjoint.

The standard library's equality search boxed a record or span value into a user `Equals(Object?)`, which could store it (#5739). And `x as T` at `T = Object` handed out a concrete `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` value from a generic body, which is never re-checked (#5740).
  - **The rules.** `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` is closed to user implementations: a user class, record, choice or interface naming it in its interface list is a compile error, a user interface extending it included (stdlib §4.16). A record that holds borrows may not declare `Equals(Object?)`, `override` or plain; a generic record is judged at each instantiation at which it holds borrows (§9.2: rejected wherever `Box<Item>` is named). An `as` or typed-pattern binding at a type parameter over an `IReadOnlySpan<TElement>` operand is a requirement of the body's use of that parameter, read at each instantiation: at an `Object` or other-interface substitution it is the borrow-erasing conversion, and a dispatched generic method decides it at its body (§9.7, §12.7, §28.3).

Also declined: a hashable clause (e) (the issue's option (A)); the trust clause (`DECLINED.md` row 42, kept); rejecting the `as` at the declaration; banning `Equals(Object?)` on every record. Row 579 (proposal 0153's option E) is re-affirmed with its bar unmet; the user-declared borrow-view row is annotated (the stdlib interface is no longer a door to it).
  - Kernel: no new clause (the bans are K2.3 + K2.4's). Body-locality: local at a declaration, per instantiation for a generic record and the `as`. A `Set<Point>`'s `Point3` values were still compared by the base's non-virtual member against the subclass's override.
  - **The rule.** A class's own-typed `Equals` (at `C` or `C?`) and `override Equals(other: Object?)` are two spellings of one virtual member, and a class writes one; the own-typed member fills the slot, as an enum's and a choice's does. `=`, the comparer-less hash containers, the type-parameter path, `IEquatable<C>` and every `Object` surface reach it by dispatch. A subclass overrides it in either spelling, under §12.1's override-boundary rules. Through the slot, a non-`C` or `null` argument compares unequal. The own-typed spelling obliges `override GetHashCode()`, the declaring class's own. To §22.6 the member is one candidate, applicable at every argument and an exact match at its nearest declaration's parameter type.

Under the slot the two readings agree at every own-typed class.

- **§3.6, §14.2, §14.4, §27.7.1, Appendix C.1, C.4; the code-generation reference §7.9 — no `Object` bound, no hashable function type, and the owning family's element rule reads the underlying type (design change, [proposal 0161](proposals/0161-constraint-table-narrowings.md); [#5748](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5748), [#5756](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5756) part 3, [#5749](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5749); generics R2–R6/R9/R10 × C4, R6/C5, R6/C12, R7/C8, R7/C13).**

- **§28.2, §28.3 (K3.9, the unbound-temporary sentence), §28.4, §28.6, §28.12, Appendix C.3; rationale §5.28 — explicit disposal marks, the holder frees (design change, [proposal 0162](proposals/0162-explicit-disposal-marks-the-holder-frees.md) items 1 and 3; [#5759](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5759); disposal R1/C9, R3/C9, R4/C9, R6/C9).** §28.4's "reclaimed — immediately" and §28.12's "immediately after whichever logical-disposal path completes" had the language's own second `Dispose()` read a released block in an unchecked build: the cascade over an early-released field, drop-on-overwrite after dispose-then-assign, the per-slot pass after a discard, and the exit pass.
  - **The rule.** An explicit `Dispose()` or direct `DisposeAsync()` performs logical disposal only: it sets the flag and runs the class's cleanup, and does not reclaim its receiver. Every class instance's block is reclaimed exactly once, by the compiler-inserted free at its holder's release point, after logical disposal has completed. The release points are scope end, the K8 boundary, the overwrite, the containing object's teardown, the container's cascade or removing operation and the exit pass, and the runtime's own release where it holds the value (a `Shared<T>` value's last handle, an exception after its catch arm, a killed frame).
  - Where a direct `DisposeAsync()`, or a `Task`-family value disposed before it settles, is still in flight at the release point, the release is deferred to its terminal state and never blocks. §28.9's trivial-dispose free, §28.6's trivial-dispose carve and axiom A15's non-reclaiming disposal were this rule for three cases. `Make().Dispose()` is K3.9's consume, and the K8 boundary reclaims only.
  - Declined: a per-location released bit; the repeated call undefined in unchecked builds; vacating the slot at the call (the compiler's shape). Kernel: K3.9's disposal-moment column separates logical disposal from reclamation; no new clause. **Compiler (tracked, [#5830](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5830)):** the explicit-disposal site reclaims at the call and nulls the slot (`LlvmBackend_Calls2.cpp:5772–5810`).
- **§28.12, §28.2, Appendix C.3 — a second call after logical disposal has begun is a no-op; checked mode faults from its completion (design change, [proposal 0162](proposals/0162-explicit-disposal-marks-the-holder-frees.md) item 2; [#5758](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5758); disposal R1/C14, R2/C14, R4/C14).** "After either has run" now reads "after either has begun". The per-instance flag records the beginning of logical disposal: at the `Dispose()` call, at the direct `DisposeAsync()` call, or at `await using`'s scope exit before the body's first statement.
  - A later `Dispose()` is a no-op, and a later `DisposeAsync()` returns a completed task. The `Dispose()` the runtime issues to complete an `await using` or a direct `DisposeAsync()` is that disposal's own step.
  - The cascade and the base chain run once, immediately after logical disposal completes. An instance is logically disposed, the state checked mode faults on, once logical disposal has **completed**: the disposal's own accesses run on a live instance, and a member access through another alias while a direct `DisposeAsync()` is in flight is §28.2's program error, memory-safe inside the window and faulting from the terminal state on.
  - Declined: reading B under a trust clause; a joined second task; faulting an alias inside the window while exempting the disposal's own accesses (a member-entry flag test cannot tell them apart). **Compiler (tracked, same tracker):** one flag, set before the core, and a callee-side guard (`LlvmBackend_Setup.cpp:10884–10900`), so a destructor body's call to an instance method of `this` faults in checked mode today (code-read).

A `static owned` field read is now a borrow of K2's always-live source, and `Dispose()` or `DisposeAsync()` through it is the borrow error. Static owned storage admits no `move`, no slot store and no explicit disposal. Early shutdown is spelled with a `Close()` method, a `Locked<T>` registry or a `Shared<T>` handle. Declined: keeping the receiver and recording the race; admitting it per type. Measured reach: zero sites ([#5807](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5807)).
- **§22.12, §22.13, §11.7, §15.1.1, §15.3, §28.7, §28.11, Appendix C.3, C.11; rationale §12.15, §12.7, §12.14, A13; the code-generation reference §7.2 — §22.12 form (iv) is retired, and the `static readonly` form's slots are fixed (design change, a subtraction; [proposal 0162](proposals/0162-explicit-disposal-marks-the-holder-frees.md) item 5; [#5785](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5785), [#5782](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5782); disposal R9/C2, R9/C5, R9/C6, R9/C8, R9/C10, R9/C11, route R9/C12·repopulation).** Form (iv), the mutable static owning-inline-array field, sent slot stores, `move arr[j]` and restoration to §15.1.1 "unchanged". K9.4's ground rejects a per-method window over static state for a slot as for a field (four lanes found it). And a destructor run by the exit pass could re-populate a slot the pass had disposed (#5782).

  - Note (h)'s `static readonly` form is the one static owning inline array: disposed at exit, written once, with no slot store and no `move` through it (K9.4); a replaceable pool is a `static owned readonly OwningArray<T>` written through its indexer, or a `Locked<T>` registry.

- **§33.3, §28.10, §28.3; stdlib §2.4; the code-generation reference §5.2 — `Environment.Exit` unwinds nothing (ruling, option (a); [#5779](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5779); route R1–R8/C1·env-exit).** The call initiates the shutdown sequence without unwinding the calling thread. This is the abandonment rule applied to the caller, and a stated exception to §28.3's exactly-once claim and §28.10's every-exit-path promise, which do not reach a frame the process abandons rather than unwinds (every live frame at this call, a spawned domain's at `Main`'s completion, §22.13's abnormal conditions). - **§28.3, §28.7, §15.1.1, K8.1, §28.13, §28.4, §31.1, §35.4; stdlib §2.16, §4.5, §4.9 — eight disposal-order and displacement-scope statements stated rather than inferred (editorial, two of them rulings; [#5747](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5747); disposal R1/C12, R6/C6).**

  - An owning choice's payloads are disposed in declaration order (ruling: stated, not aligned to §28.4's reverse order; one value, established together; the compiler's order kept).
  - Stdlib §4.9's `Add` and `PopValue` sketches compare before `move chain.Next`. No verdict moves.

- **K9.2, §28.3 *Scope*, §28.8.1 (*Exception paths are not exempt*, the new *The vacated location*), §28.11, Appendix C.3; rationale §5.10; the code-generation reference §4.2, §7.2, §7.3 — the restoration window is straight-line and the vacated location is in the disposed state (design change, [proposal 0163](proposals/0163-restoration-window-straight-line.md); [#5775](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5775), [#5776](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5776); disposal R4/C5, R5/C5, R6/C5, R4/C6, R6/C6, R4/C10–R6/C10, R4/C11–R6/C11, route R4/C3·reentrant).** K9.2's window admitted a call under a restoring `finally` (v0.332, #5666), an `await`, a `yield return` and a constructor body, and said nothing about what such code observes at the vacated field or where a value it stores there goes. In `var t := move _r; try Poke(); finally _r := t; end;` with `Poke` storing into `_r`, the restoration "stores without disposal" and leaked the stored value.

A `yield return` is an exit of the window: its abandonment edge leaves the body (K9.2, §28.8.1's exit list and inventory; #5776). A slot of a heap collection held by an owned local of the body, disposed rather than moved on every path, keeps today's window: every exit edge passes the collection's disposal.

- **§28.3 *Bare-type-parameter returns* (the nested-slot exclusion replaced by three paragraphs), the announcement table's row 5, *Set-erasing positions*, §12.9, Appendix C.3; rationale §4.2; the code-generation reference §4.4, §7.2 — a type parameter sits in a function type at depth one only, and the function values a generic body forms over its type parameters never leave the body (design change, [proposal 0165](proposals/0165-function-types-over-a-type-parameter.md); [#5762](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5762), [#5763](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5763); generics R2/C1, R2/C2, R6/C1, R6/C2, R6/C7, R8/C1).** Proposal 0133's nested-slot exclusion and the `Task`-family exclusion were stated over a parameter's declared type, which left several routes open. - **§28.11 (the new *Value-copy members*), §9.7, §28.3 (the closure bullet, *Function-typed holders*, provenance clause 1, *The trust-admission report*); stdlib §4, §4.20, §5; rationale §4.2; the code-generation reference §7.2 — retrospective consolidation (clarification, [proposal 0169](proposals/0169-retrospective-consolidation.md); the retrospective's R7, R6 and R2).**
  - **The value-copy register is read off signatures.** §28.11 states three shapes:
    - a method, constructor or `static` factory returning an `owned` collection copies in the element values it takes from its receiver or arguments;
    - a borrowing-family collection's or a span view's method with no return copies into the receiver what it takes from an `IEnumerable<T>`, a read-only span over `T` or a bare `T`;
    - a method with no return taking a writable span over `T` copies into that span's storage.
  - It names the four members a shape reads that copy nothing: `Set<T>.IntersectWith` and `ExceptWith` remove, and `Span<T>`'s class-typed `MoveFrom` and `MoveTo` move. ### v0.335 changelog (v0.334 → v0.335)

**The three matrices re-run against v0.334, decided under the owner's delegation.** After the v0.334 train the three completeness matrices were re-run against the new text, every cell and route re-derived from it. The **borrow-flow matrix's fifth run** left **3 of 117 cells** open (R6/C4, R7/C4 and R8/C4, all on an `is` narrowing of a carrier that announces borrows) and **1 of 13 route cells** (R7–R8/C6·objmint). The **disposal matrix's second run** left **12 of 140 cells** and **6 of 22 route cells** open, and the **generics matrix's second run** **18 of 140 cells** and **5 of 20 route cells**. Every v0.333 root cause was confirmed closed; the open cells sit at the edges of the v0.334 rules, and a consolidation pass merged them into **19 root causes**, NR01–NR19: 13 filed as new issues ([#5832](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5832)–[#5844](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5844)) and 6 already open ([#5792](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5792), [#5796](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5796), [#5797](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5797), [#5798](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5798), [#5800](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5800) and [#5802](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5802), questions v0.334 filed). The runs are recorded, non-normatively, under [`research/borrow-flow-matrix/`](research/borrow-flow-matrix/README.md), [`research/disposal-matrix/`](research/disposal-matrix/README.md) and [`research/generics-matrix/`](research/generics-matrix/README.md). The train also took the five v0.334 questions no root covers ([#5793](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5793), [#5794](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5794), [#5795](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5795), [#5799](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5799) and [#5801](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5801)) and one issue from a triage of the spec issues filed since ([#5878](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5878): "first use" is undefined), with three one-sentence clarifications the triage proposed. Under the owner's 2026-10-08 delegation ("Please resolve and decide all known spec related issues. Do proposals for issues that need them."), the 2026-10-09 direction ("Please also resolve all findings autonomously") and the 2026-10-09 "Please proceed as you recommend", given after the re-runs, this revision decides all 25, each as a delegated ruling (process §8, `accepted (delegated)`). The standing preference decided the close calls again: **narrow a feature whose measured reach is negligible rather than add a rule; where real code uses the feature, keep it and fix the rule.** Four decisions change a stated rule or narrow a stated admission; each went through a proposal, and each graduates here. Four lanes drafted the decisions, each reviewed by an independent critic. The decisions:
- **Proposal [0170](proposals/0170-restoration-window-stable-holder-frozen-collection.md)** (the restoration window's holder and index are stable; a body-local collection's binding is frozen in its window): [#5833](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5833), [#5843](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5843), the `await using` face of [#5796](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5796); disposal R5/C5, R5/C10, R5/C11, route R5/C6·reindex.
- **Proposal [0171](proposals/0171-borrowed-owning-task-award-spends.md)** (a borrowed Pattern B award spends the task; no static is declared at `OwningTask<T>`): [#5834](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5834); disposal R7/C10, R9/C10.
- **Proposal [0172](proposals/0172-function-slot-keying-through-implementations.md)** (function-typed slots keep their keying through implementations, containers and `scoped` fields; a body's bare-`T` lend stays out of `Object`): [#5836](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5836), [#5798](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5798); generics R2/C2, R8/C7 and five routes; borrow-flow route R7–R8/C6·objmint.
- **Proposal [0173](proposals/0173-function-value-hash-agrees-with-equality.md)** (a function value's hash agrees with its equality; the function type stays not hashable): [#5792](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5792); generics R2/C12, R2/C5's function-value face.
- **Rulings, no proposal:**
  - ownership windows and reassignment: [#5832](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5832), [#5840](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5840), [#5796](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5796) (its scope-end and discard faces), [#5797](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5797), [#5799](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5799);

Each lane passed its author's adversarial pass and an independent critique, which applied **45 fixes**: `X1` 15, `X2` 13, `X3` 7 and `X4` 10. No critique reversed a lane decision. The 135 drafted edits (`X1` 34, `X2` 34, `X3` 25, `X4` 42) were applied as one sequence in the order `X1`, `X2`, `X4`, `X3`; the composition step dropped none, re-anchored four (the proposals folder's shared insertion points), and added 9 of its own: 2 settling the proposals' composition notes, 4 graduation status lines, and 3 in the proposals folder's two indexes. The rule corpus took one header refresh (below).

The critics' substantive findings were these:
- `X1`:
  - **0170's freeze over-reached and under-reached at once.** As drafted it froze every live local borrow sourced from the collection, element borrows included (`var e := xs[2]; e.Touch();` rejected), and it admitted a borrowing `for` over the collection, whose enumerator reads the vacated slot: a deterministic checked-mode fault where a compile error is available, the ground 0170 itself declines reading A alone on. The frozen set is now the borrows whose referent is the collection; a `for` is a passed borrow; a store at a new key of an `OwningDictionary` inserts and is a member call.
  - **#5797's field-read class was unsound as drafted:** "a getter with no body" also classified a read through an interface, `abstract` or `virtual` property, which dispatches to a possibly bodied getter. The class is now an auto-property the read resolves to statically. The reference's examples were also respelled (`_cache.Count` is bodied in stdlib §4.5's sketch; `var s := Some(move _r);` is not valid Bezel, §35.3 admitting the bare case only in a declared-result position).
  - Three passages the lane left unedited stated the old rule: *The vacated location*'s no-hole sentence covered only a checked-mode fault's location, not one a destructor's raise leaves vacated in both modes; §35.4 repeated note (g)'s `owned`-field reliance sentence; and a discard of a **field's** holder is not the restoration 0170 makes a discard of a collection or inline-array local.
- `X2`:
  - **The in-flight-advance pass (#5842) would have voided a live `TaskScope`.** It ran §29.7's pass, which takes §28.12's synchronous fallback for every `await using var`, at a frame suspended at an internal `await`, where the yield-liveness rule does not reach. The cleanups now run as on an exit edge of the body under the advance's own continuation, an `await using var` there awaiting its `DisposeAsync()`, and §30.7's early-abandonment sentence is scoped to a frame suspended at a `yield return`.
  - **Two unedited passages contradicted the decisions:** §30.11's source accounting ("an await through the borrow disposes the task") under 0171, and §22.13's "the process exit code is not changed by this pass" under #5841.
  - 0171's note (j) was counted in §22.12's residual; `OwningTask<T>` is a class type under rule 4's class-type sentence, and Appendix C.11, not C.3, carries it. Its remedy (`static readonly _conn: Task<Conn> := ConnectAsync();`) put an asynchronous value in a static initializer, which §22.13 excludes; it now names patterns (a)/(b)'s `Task<T>?` cache. The proposal's expected output was wrong (`Bad` throws before any `Res` exists, so `closed` is never printed), and #5800's four statements now agree on "a parameter whose declared type is or contains a type parameter".
- `X3`:
  - **0172 (D) left a hole through collections:** `var xs: Array<(Box<T>) -> T> := [lambda(b) => b.V]; return xs;` from a member declared `Object` reached a caller as a mint, since *Exported mint slots* reads declared types only. The value rule now bars a collection or inline-array slot, collection-literal elements and indexer stores included.
  - 0172 (A)'s pass restriction applied at every substitution, so `class S: IOwningList<Item>` could not hand `Sort`'s comparer to a private helper; it now applies only where the declaring slot is a route. The declined visibility rule for `scoped` fields was declined on the wrong ground: as stated it is unsound, since a nested type sees `private` members and holds a concrete instantiation (§11.6).
  - 0173's hash sentence copied §27.7.1's "static (or extension-method)" bullet, which is imprecise for a bound extension reference; the hash is now derived from exactly what the equality compares, right under either reading (the bullet's sharpening is filed). The #5835 sentence's "within the controlled block" now reads "wherever §7.4 establishes one", so every narrowing form is covered.
- `X4`:
  - **#5838's paragraph contradicted its own conformance relation:** it excluded "boxing" unqualified, and §5.1 calls a record's, enum's and primitive's interface conformance boxing. It now excludes boxing to `Object` and admits a value type conforming to an interface `U`.
  - **#5837's ruling left a consequence unstated:** in a dispatched generic method's body a second-kind use at a non-`Object?` argument is now an error at the body, whose remedy is an `Object?`-typed argument, not §14.2's `where T: hashable`.
  - **The *Set-erasing positions* rewrite dropped three sentences matrix cells quote**, one of them `X3`'s anchor; they are restored verbatim. #5878's definition swept in `const`s and enum constants, which §22.13 says trigger nothing, and its DECLINED ground was not so (a static read from an initializer is itself a static-member access); #5802 item 6's "plain parameter" narrowed an enumeration it meant to complete.

**Outcomes the owner should see.**
- **A borrowed Pattern B await no longer disposes the task.** Proposal 0171 deviates from #5834's recommended fix (deferring the in-place disposal when the fault escapes), which kept the success path disposing through a borrow. The award of a borrowed `OwningTask<T>` operand now spends it (§30.4's state) and the holder disposes it, which is what the compiler already does for a bound operand; it supersedes v0.190's #1785 parenthetical.
- **`Clear()` is no longer a restoration of a vacated slot.** Proposal 0170 deviates from #5833's recommendation to keep it with a vacated-tolerant cascade: the reference `Clear` is Bezel-written and reads the slot through a spelling the vacated state has no exemption for, and no program uses it as a restoration. Remedy: `PopAt`, then `Clear()`.
- **One test program flips.** Proposal 0172 (C) restricts invoking a `scoped` field to its declaring type's own bodies, through `this`; `lambda_test.cpp`'s `t._cb(10)` from `Main` is respelled through a method. No other program, corpus case or document changes verdict.
- **A function value's hash now agrees with its equality** (0173), adopting the hash definition proposal 0161 declined as option B1 ("a hash for a key nobody uses") on new evidence: the key is used, at `Object`. The function type stays not hashable, on the ground that survives.
- **`Environment.Exit` inside the exit pass ends the pass with its code** (#5841), and a type's **first use** is defined (#5878), a base's static initializer running when a derived construction reaches the base's constructor.
- **Every new rejection is ahead of the compiler** and measured at zero sites but the one above. 13 trackers are filed and 9 existing issues get notes (Migration, below).

- **§28.3 *State match on reassignment*, K1's explicitly-disposed state, §17.13, §28.3's exception-path list, §28.7, §15.3, §28.8.1's inventory; rationale §5.28 — the overwrite of an explicitly-disposed local is its release point (ruling, option (a); [#5832](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5832); disposal R1/C6, R1/C7, R1/C8, R1/C9, R6/C9).** v0.334 landed the #5768 ruling and proposal 0162 side by side, and they disagreed about `x.Dispose(); x := new Res();`: §28.3 said an explicitly-disposed LHS "displaces nothing", which left the logically disposed block with no release point once the explicit call no longer reclaimed, while §28.2 listed "the overwrite for a displaced value" among the release points and §28.7's liveness test counted the value live. The text now reads as 0162's composition note intended: a moved-from LHS displaces nothing; an explicitly-disposed LHS displaces a logically disposed value and the store is its release point — the no-op `Dispose()`, then the free (deferred to a direct `DisposeAsync()`'s terminal state, as §28.2 states) — on every path that reached it disposed, a maybe-consumed binding taking that per path. The three sentences that said scope-end machinery "skips" such a binding say the skip is the disposal's, not the free's; §15.3's per-slot pass frees a slot object a discard or an explicit `Dispose()` of the slot disposed; a store into an explicitly-disposed local is non-throwable in §28.8.1's inventory. No verdict moves. Declined: making the explicit kill of a local its own release point (it reopens #5759's alias hazard). **Compiler:** the free's placement is tracked on [#5830](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5830) and [#5810](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5810); the receiver slot is nulled at the call today, so the block is reclaimed there, not leaked.
- **§28.11 *The index is trackable, and the holder and index are stable*, §28.8.1 *The window is straight-line* and *The field-restoration rule*, K9's closing sentence, §15.3 *Local lifetime*, Appendix C.3; rationale §5.10; the code-generation reference §7.2 — the window's holder and index are stable, and a body-local collection's binding is frozen in its window (design change, [proposal 0170](proposals/0170-restoration-window-stable-holder-frozen-collection.md); [#5833](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5833), [#5843](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5843), the `await using` face of [#5796](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5796); disposal R5/C5, R5/C10, R5/C11, route R5/C6·reindex, the ·rebind face of R4/C5, R5/C5 and R5/C6).**
  - **The problem.** The one window 0163 left open to calls — a slot of a heap owning collection held by an owned local of the body — and the per-index tracking together let the restoring store land somewhere other than the slot the move vacated: a structural member on the collection (`var t := move xs[1]; xs.RemoveAt(0); xs[1] := t;` leaks the live third element), a closure- or `ref`-written index, `Clear()` reading the vacated slot it was listed to restore, and a rebound holder (`var t := move p._r; p := q; p._r := t;` restores `q`'s field and leaves `p`'s original with a hole checked mode never meets).
  - **The rules.** The index local is a §7.4 stable local the body does not reassign over the window, and the holder binding is held to a like bar: a store into it, a transfer of it (`move`, or a move-only value's unmarked transfer) or a `ref`/`out` argument naming it inside the window is a compile error at the site, naming the move. In the collection window the collection binding and the live local borrows whose referent is the collection (an alias, a span, a closure or frame carrying it) are frozen: no member call but the store at a vacated slot's own index and `coll.Dispose()`, no borrow passed, captured, yielded, stored or iterated; element borrows, slot reads, further slot moves and property reads stay admitted. A structural member reached through an untracked alias, or run by a task started before the move, reads the vacated slot as it moves it and faults in checked mode. The restorations are the same-index store and the destruction of the holder's value (a heap collection's disposal on every path, a discard of the holding local, an inline array's whole-value reassignment or discard); `Clear()` restores nothing. An `await using var` declared inside a straight-line window is rejected at its declaration, its scope end being a suspension.
  - **Declined** (six `declined-at-proposal` rows): reading A alone (a run-time, capacity-dependent fault where a compile error is available); a tested restoring store; `Clear()` kept with a vacated-tolerant cascade; the holding local's overwrite as a restoration (#5843's recommendation; zero sites); by-object holder tracking; the `await using` admission. Measured reach: zero sites newly rejected (787 raw-text and 505 program-text windows; re-measured by the critique over 395 windows).
- **§28.3 *The return slot* — a raise from any return-edge cleanup disposes the slot's value at the raise (ruling, reading A; [#5840](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5840); disposal route R1, R3, R6/C2·slot-moment).** The #5781 ruling disposed the value "when the exception leaves the `return` statement's scope", a moment already past when the raising cleanup belongs to an enclosing scope (an outer `using var`, an enclosing `try`'s `finally`). The value is now disposed at the raise, before every pending cleanup established before the `return` and before a handler's arm in the callee, so a callee handler finds no returned value to dispose; in the issue's program `closed 1` prints before `caught in callee`. Declined: reading the scope as the method body (a callee handler would leave the value undisposed). **Compiler:** the order is to be pinned by [#5809](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5809)'s probe.
- **§28.8.1 *The window is straight-line* and *The vacated location*, K9.2 — a raise from a disposal the window itself runs is admitted unrestored; a discard inside the window is throwable (ruling, reading 1, with proposal 0170 for the `await using` face; [#5796](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5796); disposal route R4–R6/C3·scope-end).** The inventory classifies expressions, while a block ending inside the window runs its locals' disposals there, and K9.2 counted only edges "raised by an intervening throwable expression". A destructor's raise at a scope end or a K8 boundary inside the window is now an admitted exception edge: it leaves the method with the location vacated, which is no hole — every later read faults in checked mode and is undefined unchecked, as for an explicitly disposed owned field. A discard `_ := y;` of an owned value inside the window is the author's own disposal there and is throwable, as K3.9's `Dispose()` row already is; a discard of the local holding the collection or inline array whose slot the window vacated is a restoration (0170), a discard of a field's holder is not. Declined: rejecting a scope-end disposal of a live local inside the window (reading 2, also zero sites; recorded); admitting the discard under the vacated state.
- **§28.8.1's inventory — an auto-property read is a field read, a bodied getter is a call, and a choice-case construction is not in the inventory (ruling, reading 2; [#5797](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5797)).** The inventory named field reads among the non-throwable forms and method calls among the throwable ones and said nothing of property reads. A read the compiler resolves statically to an auto-property (a getter with no body) is a field read; every other property or indexer read — a bodied getter, or one reached through an interface, `virtual`, `abstract` or `override` member, which cannot tell the two apart — is a call. A case construction (`Slot.Full(move _r)`), like `new`, classifies by its payload arguments alone. Declined: every property read a call (it rejects by another name the field-like reads 0163 admitted); every property read a field read (a bodied getter is author-written code that may raise inside the window).
- **§28.5, §22.12 note (g), §35.4 — `owned` on a field of owning-choice type is admitted-but-redundant (ruling; [#5799](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5799)).** §28.5's "Only fields whose type is a class type or an interface type may be `owned`" read as a rejection, against §15.3's field-placement rule, §28.1's type requirement (a move-only value type is admitted-but-redundant at every marked position), the banked `run` case `s35_12_0003` and an accepting gtest row. The modifier is admitted-but-redundant on an owning-choice field; the double-marking rejection stays with `[N owned]T` fields, whose marker is visible in the type; note (g)'s and §35.4's reliance sentences are reworded (the static rejection stands). Declined: rejecting the marker under the class-or-interface list; the double-marking error for choices.
- **§30.5, §30.9, §30.11, K4.2, §22.12 rule 4 and notes (i)–(j), Appendix C.11; rationale §12.15; the code-generation reference §4.3, §7.6 — a borrowed Pattern B award spends the task and disposes nothing; no static is declared at `OwningTask<T>` (design change, [proposal 0171](proposals/0171-borrowed-owning-task-award-spends.md); [#5834](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5834); disposal R7/C10, R9/C10).**
  - **The problem.** §30.5 had the await of a *borrowed* `OwningTask<T>` operand — a `using var`, a plain parameter, an `owned` field read, an owning slot, static storage — "still dispose the task implicitly", a K4.2 kill through a borrow neither proposal 0162 nor 0168 revisited. Timed as the await's "terminal act, after handling completes", it disposed the operand task and its fault instance at the capture §30.9's retention paragraph says keeps them live, and it disposed a `static owned readonly OwningTask<T>` in place where K9.4 and §28.6 reserve static owned storage for the exit pass.
  - **The rules.** The award of a borrowed operand **spends** the task and disposes nothing; the task stays its holder's, which disposes it as it disposes any task it holds, finding no result and disposing the fault instance then, so an escaping fault stays retained by borrow. The owned-operand kill (K3.5) is unchanged, and K4.2's closed kill set names it. `OwningTask<T>`/`OwningTask<T>?` is a compile error in §22.12's `static readonly` column as in the mutable one (note (j), on form (ii)'s single-award ground; rule 4's class-type sentence names the exception; the bare-parameter substitution is rejected at the instantiation under note (i)); a task an admitted static holds inside an object or collection stays admitted, its await the borrowed award. §30.11's completion-source accounting is aligned (the source's disposal is the task's one disposal). Supersedes the v0.190 #1785 parenthetical.
  - **Declined** (four `declined-at-proposal` rows): deferring the borrowed-operand await's disposal to the faulted task's teardown (#5834's option 1); rejecting the borrowed await in an `async` body unless every fault is handled; a compile error at an await over static owned storage; recording the await as K9.4's one in-place disposal. Kernel: derivation (K3.5 unchanged; K9.4 restored). Measured reach: no static of `OwningTask<T>` type in `tests/`, the documents or the rule corpus beyond the mutable form's two rejection pins.
- **§29.7 (the new *Disposal while an advance is in flight*), §30.7 — disposing an async enumerator while a `MoveNextAsync()` is in flight (ruling, option (c) re-cut; [#5842](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5842); disposal route R8/C11·inflight-advance).** §29.7 was written for a consumer that stops between advances: read at a frame suspended at an internal `await`, its pass completed the machine while the advance task never reached the terminal state 0168's continuation and 0162's block release wait for, and the operand's later completion resumed into a disposed frame. Such a disposal now neither waits nor raises: it begins the enumerator's logical disposal and returns, and the frame's disposal is deferred to the pending advance's settlement, where the body does not resume. Nothing the suspended `await` produced is awarded (an owned operand disposed with its result, a borrowed one left to its holder unspent); the cleanups active at that suspension point run as on an exit edge of the body under the advance's own continuation, an `await using var` there awaiting its `DisposeAsync()` rather than taking the synchronous fallback; the machine completes; the advance settles `false` (or faults with a cleanup's exception); the token is not consulted; and the enumerator's block is reclaimed at that terminal state. `await for` never disposes mid-advance, stated at §30.7, whose early-abandonment sentence is scoped to a frame suspended at a `yield return`. Declined: raising from the disposal, or awaiting the advance inside `DisposeAsync()`; resuming the body to its next suspension point first (the issue's letter, which runs user code after the consumer disposed and can reach a `yield return` nobody takes).
- **§33.3, §22.13, §28.3; stdlib §2.4; the code-generation reference §5.2 — `Environment.Exit` inside the exit pass ends the pass (ruling, reading 2; [#5841](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5841); disposal route R9/C1·exit-in-pass).** §33.3 made the call "callable from any domain", but the exit pass runs on a shutdown thread outside any domain, and a destructor or lazy static initializer it runs could call it with no stated effect, while "no event inside the pass changes" an exit code the call carries. The call now ends the pass where it stands: the process exits at once with its `code`, the calling frame is abandoned like any live frame, every static not yet reached is reclaimed, never disposed (§28.3's abandoned-frame waiver, extended by name to the frames live in the pass), and nothing already disposed is disposed again. §22.13's exit-time-fault paragraph names the call as the one event that changes the exit code, and an exception the pass had raised and not yet reported is not reported. Declined: re-initiating the sequence (a pass re-entered mid-way can dispose a static twice); a no-op or an error (it makes "it never returns" false and keeps a code the call replaces).
- **§29.8, §29.11, §15.3, §30.1; the code-generation reference §7.5 — a parameter typed by a type parameter is a move-only parameter per instantiation (clarification, gated as a ruling, reading 1; [#5800](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5800); disposal R8/C5, R6/C11, route R8/C1·generic-T; generics R5/C13).** Proposal 0167 keyed single consumption on an iterator method that "declares an `owned` or move-only parameter" and did not say whether a parameter typed by a type parameter counts when an instantiation substitutes an owning choice or an owning inline array. A parameter whose declared type is or contains a type parameter now counts at every instantiation whose substitution makes that type move-only (§3.6 rule 2): `Each<T>(x: T): IEnumerable<int>` mints a single-consumption iterable at `Each<Slot>` and a re-iterable one at `Each<int>`, the argument passed by value-move and discharged by the one enumerator (or the iterable, where none was produced); a generic `async` method's such parameter is discharged by its frame. The static check applies where a call site names such an instantiation, the run-time check inside a generic body calling at its own type parameter. Declined: keying on the declaration alone (reading 2: a re-iterable result would re-run the body over a moved-from argument).
- **§12.7 (*A narrowing converts nothing*), §9.7's borrow-erasing bullet, §28.3 *Set-erasing positions*; the code-generation reference §7.2 — a flow-narrowed carrier is read at its declared type where borrows are read (ruling, reading 1; [#5835](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5835); generics R2/C6, R4/C6; borrow-flow R6/C4, R7/C4, R8/C4).** Wherever §7.4 establishes a type narrowing, a use of the narrowed carrier at a position declared `Object`, an interface or a type parameter is read as the carrier's `as` at the narrowed type, and takes its verdict: `if s is Object then sink.Keep(s); end;` over a span is §9.7's borrow-erasing conversion, `if f is Object then sink.Keep(f); end;` over a capture-bearing closure is §28.3's set-erasing `as`, and the generic faces (`if x is T then _v := x; end;` over a span, `if v is Object then _o := v; end;` over `v: T`) are the per-instantiation requirements §9.7 states for the written `as`, which leave the class substitution admitted. The test and reads through the narrowing are unaffected, and a nullability narrowing needs nothing; §22.3's `ref`/`out` posture is the precedent. Declined: reading the narrowed type as the carrier's type at an erasing position (unsound); withholding the narrowing from such carriers (a second narrowing regime).
- **§28.3 (the announcement table's inheritance note and row 5; *Function values a generic body forms over its type parameters*; *Exported mint slots*; the new *Implementations and overrides read their function-typed parameters at the declaring signature*; *Set-erasing positions*' routes sentence), §28.14, §12.9, Appendix C.3; rationale §4.2; the code-generation reference §7.2 — the keying of a function-typed slot follows the declaration through dispatch, containers and `scoped` fields, and a body-formed bare-`T` lend stays out of `Object` (design change, [proposal 0172](proposals/0172-function-slot-keying-through-implementations.md); [#5836](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5836), [#5798](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5798); generics R2/C2, R8/C7, routes R2/C2·impl-slot, R6/C2·impl-slot, R6/C7·scoped-field, R8/C2·object-handout, R2/C2·object-handout; borrow-flow route R7–R8/C6·objmint).**
  - **The problem.** Proposal 0165 admitted a body-formed `(T) -> …` value into a function-typed parameter and a `scoped` field, and carved a plain parameter's declared type out of *Exported mint slots*, assuming every invoker reads the pre-substitution slot. A concrete implementation of `ISink<V>.Take(f: (V) -> ())` or `Put(f: () -> V)`, a caller's own `Array<(Box<T>) -> T>` slot and a caller invoking a public `scoped` field do not, and a capture-free `lambda(b: Box<T>) => b.V` reached a caller as a mint through `Object`.
  - **The rules.** (A) A method implementing or overriding a generic declaration reads a function-typed parameter that declaration spells over a type parameter at the declaring signature, in its body and at every call: its arguments at a bare slot are set-erasing, its invocation at a bare return slot is a row-5 lend, and, where the declaring slot is a route, it is passed only to slots declared at a type parameter. (B) The exported-mint carve-out is a parameter's own function type only. (C) A `scoped` field is invoked by its declaring type's own bodies only, through `this`. (D) A body-formed value with `T` at a return slot reaches no set-erasing position, no collection or inline-array slot and no variance. *Set-erasing positions*' routes sentence now names four routes.
  - **Declined** (six `declined-at-proposal` rows): the general keying at every invocation through a generic declaration; narrowing the value rule's pass; a visibility rule for `scoped` fields (unsound as stated: a nested type sees `private` members and holds a concrete instantiation); dropping the `scoped`-field exemption; a caller-side lend reading of a value narrowed from `Object`; an iterable exclusion at every parameter slot.
- **§27.7.1, §3.6 clause (e), §8.3's table, Appendix C.1; rationale §7.7; the code-generation reference §7.2; `DECLINED.md`'s 0161 option-B1 row annotated — a function value's hash agrees with its equality, and the function type stays not hashable (design change, [proposal 0173](proposals/0173-function-value-hash-agrees-with-equality.md); [#5792](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5792); generics R2/C5, R2/C12).** v0.334 left a function value's hash as `Object`'s identity hash, "which need not agree" with §27.7.1's equality, while §8.3 states the invariant as a must and `Object` keys a capture-free function value: `Set<Object>` held two evaluations of one static method's reference as one element or two, and `where T: hashable` at `Object` promised what a legal key broke. The hash is now derived from exactly what the equality compares — a lambda from its closure object's identity hash; a method reference from its method and, where the equality compares a receiver, that receiver's identity hash (never its `GetHashCode`) — so any two references the equality makes equal hash alike. Clause (e) keeps the function type out of the hashable set because a lambda equals only itself. Declined (two `declined-at-proposal` rows): an identity `Equals` on the `Object` surface (it splits `=` from `Equals`); a documented exception in §8.3 (it leaves the invariant false at a legal key). 0161's option-B1 row is annotated, not struck: its conclusion stands on the new ground.
- **§14.2 *Type-parameter bounds*; the code-generation reference §3.3 — `where T: U` is satisfied by subtyping only (ruling, reading A; [#5838](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5838); generics R1–R6, R8–R10/C4).** The table row said "assignable to the substitution for `U`", which §5.1 reads as every implicit conversion, while the paragraph listed identity, class derivation and interface conformance. The three relations are the definition: no other implicit conversion — boxing to `Object`, numeric widening, nullable wrapping, a variance-induced conversion — satisfies the bound, while a value type conforming to an interface substitution satisfies it by conformance. At `U := Object` the bound admits `Object` and the class types; at `U := long`, `long` alone; at a nullable `U`, nothing. Declined: §5.1 assignability (reading B, taken at v0.333 without a ground). 0161's decline of a bound *naming* `Object` is not reopened: this is a type-parameter bound's degenerate instantiation, which 0161 left in place.
- **§9.2 *Through a type parameter* — the second kind's ambiguity rejects the instantiation (ruling, reading A; [#5837](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5837); generics R1/C5, R2/C5).** A hashable class declaring an `Equals` at another type beside its own-typed slot made a generic `a.Equals(x)` at an argument converting to both §22.6's ambiguity, which the rejection clause named for the first kind only. The clause now names it for both kinds (an argument converting both to the other type and to the slot's parameter, matching neither exactly); the second kind's argument is read at its static type in the body; and `where T: hashable` promises the first kind, `GetHashCode` and the second kind at an `Object?` argument, so in a dispatched generic method's body a second-kind use at another argument type is an error at the body, whose remedy is an `Object?`-typed argument. Declined: reaching the slot (reading B); reaching the other-typed `Equals` (reading C).
- **§14.6 — an artifact carries every edge of its request graph to assembly (ruling, reading A; [#5839](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5839); generics R9/C14).** The v0.334 ruling carried the bodies §2.8.2 carries and the implementations' own requests, which misses an internal non-dispatched helper's edge that closes a cross-module cycle (a `private` helper calling an imported interface method a sibling module implements). An artifact now carries every edge its compilation holds, whatever the declaring visibility; edges are substitution-labelled requests, not bodies, and the whole graph cannot over-reject (a cycle needs mutual reachability). Declined: the listed edges only (reading B). The bodies an assembly-time monomorphization needs are a separate question (filed).
- **§22.7, §22.13 — a type's "first use" is defined (ruling, reading (a); [#5878](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/5878)).** The static constructor "runs once before the type's first use" with the term undefined, and the failed-state list named static-member accesses only. First use is the first time any of the type's code runs or any of its static state is read: a static-member access (a `const` or an enum constant, a compile-time value, is no static state), a run of an instance constructor (the base's too, when a derived class's construction chains to it — so `new D` initializes `D` first and the base when the chain reaches it), or a call of an instance member, whatever module declares the type. A permanently failed type raises `TypeInitializationException` at every later first-use form, an instance construction included. Declined: static-member access as the only trigger (reading (b), which the banked case `s22_7_0011` already contradicts), and an exemption for construction as a base (§22.13 runs a type's code only after its statics). **Compiler:** the imported-base construction path skips the base's initializer, the bug #5878 reported; it is carried to a new tracker.
